papers.t: Fluid‐Controlled Tidal Modulation of Aftershocks Following the 2022 M6.8 Luding Earthquake
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Earthquake Research Institute, University of Tokyo
The University of Tokyo
tk: This study investigates the tidal modulation of aftershocks following the 2022 M6.8 Luding earthquake, highlighting the role of fluids in controlling seismicity.
本研究揭示了2022年泸定地震余震的流体控制潮汐调制特征。
papers.ab: Aftershock sequences record how fault zones recover and weaken after earthquakes, but the roles of fluid migration and stress heterogeneity remain difficult to isolate. Earth tides impose predictable stress perturbations and thus provide a natural probe of faults near failure, although their signals are often obscured by aftershock clustering. Here we apply bootstrap‐based spatial spectral analysis to the 2022 M6.8 Luding earthquake sequence to resolve tidal sensitivity. We identify a systematic shift from a fluid‐rich region before the mainshock to the margins of the high‐slip zone, bypassing the rupture core. This pattern suggests coupled interaction between coseismic stress heterogeneity and postseismic fluid redistribution. Elevated pore pressure enhances sensitivity to weak tidal stress in high stress‐gradient regions, whereas permeability contrasts promote localized fluid accumulation and triggering. Our results show that tidal forcing can reveal where postseismic faults are closest to failure, offering an indirect window into fluid migration and fault‐zone weakening.

papers.t: From Individual Gathers to Source-Composite Inversion in Active MASW: A paired field comparison of 8kg hammer and gun acquisition protocols
tk: A paired field comparison of 8kg hammer and gun sources in active MASW shows no significant difference in resolved shear-wave velocity structure or depth of investigation.
主动源MASW中8kg铁锤与枪源的配对野外对比表明，两者在剪切波速度结构和探测深度上无显著差异。
papers.ab: In multichannel analysis of surface waves (MASW), the suitability of an active source is evaluated by its ability to generate coherent and continuous surface-wave dispersion over a usable frequency and wavelength range, as these characteristics influence the reliability of mode identification and the attainable depth of investigation. We present a hierarchical paired comparison of hammer and gun acquisition protocols using 13 matched source positions and identical 12-receiver geometry (5m spacing, 55m aperture and 30m nearest offset). All 26 SEG-2 gathers were processed individually using the same phase-shift imaging and automated ridge-extraction criteria, followed by independent manual fundamental-mode picking to verify the automatic interpretation before acceptance and inversion. The verified individual gathers were then combined through normalized common-offset trace stacking and normalized dispersion-image stacking for each source. Every gather yielded an accepted fundamental-mode path. At the individual-gather level, mean maximum usable wavelength was 30.14m for the hammer and 29.45m for the gun (gun minus hammer = −0.69m; 95% paired bootstrap interval −3.81 to 1.50m). The hammer contained a greater proportional 4.5–10Hz spectral fraction (0.967% versus 0.672%), but this exploratory contrast did not remain significant after Holm correction [14]. Source-composite curves spanned 21.0–46.0Hz for the hammer and 20.5–43.5Hz for the gun, with maximum wavelengths of 32.14 and 33.41m, respectively. The stacked gun-minus-hammer wavelength difference was 1.27m (paired spatial-bootstrap 95% interval −1.39 to 2.50m), equivalent to upper screening depths of 16.07 and 16.71m under a 0.5 wavelength convention. Fixed-layer conditional inversions produced overlapping shear-wave velocity intervals in all four model layers; gun-minus-hammer differences ranged from −17.6 to +14.1m/s and all 95% intervals included zero. Agreement between independently extracted trace-stack and image-stack curves was 7.16m/s for the hammer and 4.15m/s for the gun. These results show that source ranking is endpoint- and threshold-dependent: the hammer supplied more relative low-frequency energy, whereas the gun stack gave a slightly longer wavelength, but neither a reliable depth advantage nor a distinct velocity structure was resolved. The proposed individual-to-stack consistency framework, strengthened by manual verification of automated modal picks, provides a reproducible way to prevent source-energy observations from becoming unsupported claims of deeper MASW investigation

papers.t: Source Representation and Earthquake-Ocean Coupling in Tsunami Generation by the 2020 Samos Normal-Faulting Earthquake
tk: Fully coupled 3D simulations of the 2020 Samos earthquake show that instantaneous Okada sourcing can underestimate tsunami crests compared to time-dependent sources.
萨摩斯地震模拟表明瞬时Okada源会低估海啸波峰高度。
papers.ab: The 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos normal-faulting earthquake produced damaging ground shaking and a destructive local tsunami. We construct a three-dimensional kinematic rupture model from a finite-fault inversion and use its shear stress changes to inform two dynamic rupture models. We initialize a non-linear shallow-water tsunami simulation with instantaneous Okada displacement and source one-way linked simulations with evolving seafloor deformation from the kinematic and dynamic rupture models. Fully coupled three-dimensional earthquake-tsunami simulations resolve rupture and elastic, acoustic, and gravity waves together. The coupled sea surface wavefield contains the developing tsunami, dispersive oceanic Rayleigh waves, first-mode ocean acoustic waves, and signals consistent with dispersive Scholte waves. We track crests and troughs over time as the respective means of the most extreme 0.1 percent of positive and negative sea surface height anomalies. For each time-dependent source, following transient seismo-acoustic waves, the one-way linked and fully coupled models agree within 0.10 m on both metrics from 50 to 360 s in water deeper than 100 m. At 6 min, all models share a leading drawdown with trough metrics near -0.5 m, whereas the instantaneous Okada source yields a crest metric of 0.35 m, compared with 0.5–0.6 m for time-dependent sources. Instantaneous sourcing, common in hazard assessment, may therefore underestimate tsunami crests from moderate normal-faulting earthquakes. The preferred dynamic rupture source captures the main tsunami periods at Syros, with larger tide gauge mismatches elsewhere. At Samos, full coupling resolves the early near-source seismo-acoustic wavefield, whereas time-dependent one-way linking provides an efficient estimate of the large-scale tsunami.

papers.t: Transformational Faulting: The Case of Quartz‐Coesite
in: Heidelberg University
University of Pavia
Université Paris Sciences et Lettres
École Normale Supérieure - PSL
Laboratoire de Géologie de l’École Normale Supérieure
Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESY
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Géosciences Rennes
Université de Rennes
tk: Deformation experiments on novaculite demonstrate that large volume changes during the quartz-coesite transition can solely drive transformational faulting and high-pressure brittle failure.
柯石英-石英相变实验表明，仅体积变化就能驱动相变断裂并诱发高压脆性破裂。
papers.ab: Transformational faulting in olivine has been widely invoked as a possible triggering mechanism for deep‐focus earthquakes, yet its dynamics remain debated. It is unclear whether it requires the combined effects of heat release, volume change and mechanical strength contrast, or whether it can be triggered by any one of these alone. Here, we tested if transformational faulting can be caused solely by a large volume change, through deformation experiments on novaculite during the quartz‐coesite transition. Under sluggish reaction kinetics, acoustic emissions and microstructural observations indicate strain localization and fault plane formation. Under fast kinetics, deformation was distributed and associated with fewer, lower‐magnitude events. b ‐values of ∼1 and ∼3 reflect these two regimes. Our results provide the first evidence of transformational faulting during the quartz‐coesite transition, suggesting that volume change is the primary driver of brittle failure at high pressure, broadening the range of mineral transitions generating deep and intermediate‐depth earthquakes.

papers.t: Spatially Variable Attenuation and a Localized Deep Stress-Drop Anomaly in the 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule Aftershock Sequence
in: Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris, Université Paris Cité, 1 rue Jussieu, Paris, France, 75005
Université Gustave Eiffel, 5 bd Descartes, Champs-sur-Marne, France, 77420
GFZ
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University, 116th and Broadway, New York, USA, 10027
Institut des Sciences de la Terre, Université Grenoble Alpes, 1381 Rue de la Piscine, Gières, France, 38610
tk: Generalized inversion of Maule aftershock spectra reveals highly variable attenuation and a localized high stress-drop anomaly in the deep slab.
对茂莱余震谱的广义反演揭示了空间可变的衰减及深部板片局部的强应力降异常。
papers.ab: We invert horizontal S-wave Fourier acceleration spectra between 0.5 and 25 Hz from 7,637 earthquakes in the 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule aftershock sequence to estimate source, path, and site terms in south-central Chile using a nonparametric generalized inversion technique. The dataset contains 95,515 event-station records from 117 stations during the first 10 months after the mainshock. To account for propagation heterogeneity, we divide crustal and slab-related earthquakes separately into spatially coherent clusters and invert each one independently. We use 100 randomized clustering iterations to evaluate the variance of the recovered terms. Relative site responses remain stable across these iterations, with site amplification above a factor of 10 at 2–4 Hz at some stations. Effective attenuation varies markedly across the rupture area, with Q0 values of 36–159 and frequency exponents of 0.35–1.4. Crustal clusters generally have lower Q0 and stronger frequency dependence than slab-related ones. We fit the recovered source spectra with an ω² model and obtain well-resolved source parameters for 6,279 events. Stress-drop distributions overlap between crustal and slab-related earthquakes, with median values of 2.93 and 2.76 MPa, respectively. For Mw ≥ 3, corner frequency scales approximately as M0^(−1/3), broadly consistent with self-similarity. Stress drops are systematically higher in a slab-related seismicity band between 42.5 and 52.5 km depth, with a median of 6.3 MPa. These results show that accounting for spatially variable propagation is important for interpreting source variability. The empirical model provides a basis for regional ground-motion characterization and for tracking postseismic fault evolution across the Maule rupture zone.

papers.t: Memory-Efficient Deep-Learning-Matching Full Waveform Inversion for Field-Scale Datasets
in: Bureau of Economic Geology, Jackson School of Geosciences , The University of Texas at Austin, TX ,
tk: Decouples the CNN automatic differentiation graph from the physical wave solver to enable memory-efficient, cycle-skipping-resilient deep-learning-matching FWI on field-scale marine seismic datasets.
通过解耦CNN自动微分与物理波动方程求解器，实现了内存高效且抗周波跳跃的深度学习匹配全波形反演。
papers.ab: Summary Classical full waveform inversion (FWI) is sensitive to kinematic inaccuracies in the initial velocity model, converging to local minima due to cycle skipping when low-frequency data are absent. The recently developed deep-learning-matching FWI (DLM-FWI) framework mitigates this by dynamically bridging the phase gap between synthetic and observed data, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) within the inversion loop as a robust kinematic preconditioner. However, because standard deep learning (DL) automatic differentiation (AD) engines scale poorly to large-scale wave equations, deploying DLM-FWI on practical field-scale data has been computationally prohibitive. To overcome this, we introduce a memory-efficient, hybrid computational workflow that interfaces the Flux machine-learning ecosystem with the Julia Devito Inversion framework (JUDI) finite-difference library. By decoupling the network’s AD graph from the physical solver and evaluating the chain rule strictly in the data domain, we avoid storing massive spatiotemporal wavefield histories. After verifying that this decoupled architecture maintains resilience to source-wavelet mismatch and ambient noise on the Marmousi2 synthetic model, we apply the workflow to the Mobil AVO Viking Graben Line 12 marine dataset to evaluate its practical scalability. Compared to classical L-BFGS FWI, the field-scale DLM-FWI results exhibit robust convergence, mitigation of shallow cycle-skipped artifacts, and geologically coherent structural continuity. This study addresses the gap between small-scale synthetic DL studies and field-scale 2D implementations, demonstrating that physics-guided matching strategies can be deployed in practice to improve FWI robustness on complex field datasets.

papers.t: Stepover of Strike-Slip Faults and Overpressured Fluid Favor Occurrence Short-Term Foreshocks: Insights from the 2021 Yangbi Foreshock–Mainshock–Aftershock Sequence, China
in: State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting, Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China
Geophysics Department, School of Earth Sciences, Yunnan University, Kunming, China
tk: Fault stepovers and deep overpressured fluids promote short-term foreshocks, potentially enhancing earthquake predictability.
断层阶区与深部超压流体共同促进了前震发生，有助于提高地震预测性。
papers.ab: This study comprehensively and in detail analyzed the spatial and temporal distributions of earthquakes, tidal responses, focal mechanisms, rupture directions, coseismic stress transfer, and stress field characteristics associated with the Mw 6.0 Yangbi earthquake that occurred in May 2021. This earthquake constitutes a typical foreshock–mainshock–aftershock sequence, monitored by permanent and dense temporary seismic networks. Detailed and precise hypocenter determinations revealed complex and previously unknown seismogenic fault structures located several kilometers away from the well-documented active faults in the region. The foreshocks were found to be closely associated with both the main fault and the conjugate faults surrounding a fault stepover. Notably, the onset timing of three foreshock episodes and the occurrence time of the mainshock were clearly coincident with the peak of dilational volumetric tidal strain, indicating a potential tidal triggering effect. By synthesizing findings from other research teams, this study proposes that the Yangbi earthquake foreshock swarms were the result of the combined effects of deep overpressured fluids, transitional slow-slip events, and cascade triggering. Among these factors, deep fluids are inferred to have served as the initial driver and the most critical controlling factor. Similar to the Haicheng earthquake, for which a successful short-term and imminent prediction was issued, the Yangbi earthquake likewise demonstrates that tectonic complexity (primarily stepovers in this case) and the action of deep overpressured fluids facilitate the occurrence of short-term and imminent foreshocks, thereby potentially enhancing earthquake predictability.

papers.t: Rapid transient uplift driven by active slab tear, southern Calabria, Italy
in: University of Oregon
The University of Texas at Arlington
University of Basilicata
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
INGV Sezione di Palermo
Royal Holloway University of London
University of Bologna
tk: Luminescence dating of high-elevation marine terraces in Calabria reveals rapid uplift (~12 mm/yr) driven by an active Ionian slab tear.
卡拉布里亚高海拔海成阶地测年揭示了板块撕裂驱动的快速抬升。
papers.ab: Southern Italy preserves a well-studied record of deformation and uplift related to migrating oblique collision, trench retreat, and tearing of subducted ocean slabs. However, the surface expression of these processes is incompletely understood due to a lack of reliable ages for marine terraces >200 m above sea level (masl). Here we use luminescence methods to date shallow marine sands from terraces ~ 100 to 1,000 masl in southern Calabria and interpolate the results with regional surface mapping. Burial ages overlap across the full range of sampled elevations with a weighted mean of 118.8 ± 8.7 thousand years before present (ka). These ages, combined with map data and fault-zone morphology, indicate that the terraces are erosional remnants of a single, once-continuous deformed surface. Calculated uplift rates vary from 12 mm yr-1 and throw rates on active normal faults are 0.8–4.2 mm yr-1. We infer that rapid post-120 ka uplift is an ongoing isostatic response to an active tear in the Ionian slab, consistent with recent geophysical observations and predictions of geodynamic models. These results have important implications for assessment of geohazards in southern Calabria and northeast Sicily, one of the highest seismic risk areas in the Mediterranean region.

papers.t: Inversion of Arctic Landfast Sea Ice Properties Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on Ice
in: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, 98 Water St, MS #9, Woods Hole, United States [US]
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, 266 Woods Hole Rode, Woods Hole, MA, United States [US]
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, 266 Woods Hole Road, Falmouth, MA, United States [US]
tk: This study presents the first DAS observations on Arctic landfast sea ice, using active and passive wavefields to invert for ice thickness, Young's modulus, and compressive stress.
本文首次利用冰上分布式声学传感（DAS）观测，反演了北极固定陆缘冰的厚度、杨氏模量和压应力。
papers.ab: Arctic landfast sea ice is subject to mechanical forcing from winds, waves, currents, and interactions with drifting ice. However, the resulting wavefields and their effects on the mechanical properties of the ice remain difficult to characterize using existing in situ and remote-sensing observations due to limited spatial and temporal coverage. Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) of fiber optic cable offers dense spatial sampling and continuous temporal coverage that can complement these approaches. We present the first DAS observations on Arctic landfast sea ice, using a 2-km-long armored fiber-optic cable installed at the snow-ice interface on ice near Utqiaġvik, Alaska for two weeks in spring 2025. The DAS recorded various signal types, including controlled hammer-generated signals and ambient flexural-gravity (FG) waves. We apply Bayesian dispersion-based inversions of the observed guided-wave modes to estimate ice properties. Hammer-generated waves yield estimates of Young's modulus and ice thickness of 5.4 GPa and 0.98 m, respectively; the inferred thickness agrees with independent field measurements. Directional beamforming of the L-shaped cable segment indicates a dominant FG-wave arrival direction from offshore with an effective Young's modulus of 0.6 GPa and compressive stress of 0.6 MPa. The lower effective modulus is consistent with previous reports of reduced effective moduli inferred from FG waves. The compressive stress shows a positive correlation with squared wind speed (r=0.37), indicating sensitivity to wind-related changes in the ambient wavefield. These results demonstrate that DAS can complement existing observations of sea-ice wavefields and mechanics, while highlighting the need to characterize its coupling and directional response.

papers.t: Variations in dv / v Susceptibility to Earthquake Shaking Along the Alaska Subduction Zone
in: Rice University
tk: Active volcanoes in Alaska show the highest susceptibility to earthquake-triggered seismic velocity drops, concentrated in shallow hydrothermal systems.
阿拉斯加活动火山区对地震动引起的波速下降最敏感，且集中在浅部。
papers.ab: Earthquake‐triggered decreases in relative seismic velocity ( dv / v ) of the crust have been reported for many events, but regional variations in dv / v susceptibility to shaking are not well understood. Here, 14 Alaskan earthquakes with Mw 6.8–8.2 are consistently analyzed with single‐station coda‐wave interferometry. For peak ground velocities (PGV) >1 cm/s, significant dv/v drops are found for ∼40% of seismometers, with a moderate linear correlation coefficient of −0.3 between dv / v and PGV. Sites in the highest susceptibility decile, indicated by the largest dv / v drops per unit PGV, are all located near active volcanoes: Akutan, Makushin, Shishaldin, Pavlof, Katmai, and Augustine. Some Cook Inlet basin sites are among the largest decile of dv / v drops but have lower susceptibility due to amplified PGV. Frequency‐dependence of dv / v indicates concentration of velocity changes at <500 m depth, consistent with hydrothermal systems and weakly consolidated volcanic rocks influencing heterogeneous and high susceptibility near volcanoes.

papers.t: Seismic Evidence of the Transition from Debris Flow to Hyperconcentrated Flow at Mount Rainier, USA
in: Department of Earth and Planetary Science, University of California Davis, Davis, California, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Geological Hazards Science Center, Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.
Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oregon, Eugene, Oregon, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Volcano Science Center, Cascades Volcano Observatory, Vancouver, Washington, U.S.A.
Mount Rainier National Park, National Park Service, Washington, U.S.A.
Department of Geological Sciences, California State University San Bernardino, San Bernardino, California, U.S.A.
tk: Seismic recordings of a Mount Rainier debris flow reveal a transition to hyperconcentrated flow, marked by an elongated signal onset and an increase in peak frequency.
雷尼尔山泥石流的地震记录揭示了其向超高浓度流的转变，表现为信号起伏变缓和主频升高。
papers.ab: Debris flows are a seasonal hazard in Tahoma Creek in Mount Rainier National Park, Washington, United States. We present seismic recordings spaced every 100–200 m along the path of a debris flow triggered by a glacial outburst on 15 August 2023. These recordings capture changes as the debris flow deposits ∼24,000 cubic meters of material along an ∼800 m stretch of channel, approximately 2.5 km from the glacial source. As the flow deposits material, the seismic signal onset shape associated with the debris flow snout recedes, resulting in an elongation of the delay between the signal onset and the peak amplitude from 100 to 300 s. In parallel, the peak frequency increases by more than 20 Hz, and energy below 20 Hz fades, indicating deposition of larger particles and changes in sediment concentration within the flow. We interpret these changes to correspond to the transition from debris flow to hyperconcentrated flow, a distinction based on sediment concentration by volume and on rheological criteria such as yield strength. We find that the frequency content of the seismic signal depends on grain size and sediment concentrations within the flow, among other factors, complicating the starting assumptions of many physical models of debris flows.

papers.t: Identify Potential Source Regions in the Nankai Trough Using Spatial Clustering Techniques
in: Hubei Subsurface Multi-Scale Imaging Key Laboratory, School of Geophysics and Geomatics, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan, China
Institute of Earthquake Forecasting, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China
tk: Integrates b-value, slip-deficit rate, and cumulative slip deficit using self-organizing maps to identify four potential earthquake source regions along the Nankai Trough.
利用自组织映射方法整合b值与滑移亏损数据，识别出南海海槽四个潜在地震源区。
papers.ab: Identification of potential source regions, pinpointing where large earthquakes are most likely to occur, is fundamental to seismic risk assessment. Previous results often suffer from significant uncertainties due to the limitations of individual observations. To address this issue, here we apply the self-organizing map method to the Nankai trough, which has been considered to have high-seismic potential. By integrating multisource observations (b value, slip-deficit rate [SDR], and cumulative slip deficit [CSD]), we cluster regions of low b value, high SDR, and large CSD to delineate potential source regions. We identify four potential earthquake sources along the Nankai trough. Among them, the Tokai segment shows the highest potential for generating earthquakes in the near future. Using pre-2011 observations, the identified source regions agree well with the rupture zone of the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-Oki earthquake, validating the reliability of this approach.

papers.t: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
in: International Research Institute of Disaster Science, Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan.
Advanced Institute for Marine Ecosystem Change (WPI-AIMEC), Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan.
Graduate School of Science, Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan.
Pacific Geoscience Centre, Geological Survey of Canada, Natural Resources Canada, Sidney, British Columbia, Canada.
School of Earth and Ocean Science, University of Victoria, Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.
Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology, Yokohama, Japan.
Earthquake Research Institute, University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan.
tk: Seafloor and onshore geodesy show that the Tohoku megathrust has rapidly relocked to pre-earthquake levels despite ongoing viscoelastic relaxation.
海底和陆地大地测量表明，尽管存在粘弹性松弛，东北大地震断层已快速恢复到震前锁定状态。
papers.ab: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

papers.t: Differentiated Rift Rupture and Apparent Northward Earthquake Ordering in Southern Tibet Revealed by the 2025 Mw 7.0 Dingri Earthquake and Its Preceding Events
in: Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences
Nanjing University
tk: The 2025 Mw 7.0 Dingri earthquake reveals contrasting along-rift rupture behaviors and an apparent northward earthquake ordering in southern Tibet's rift system.
2025年定日地震揭示了藏南裂谷差异破裂特征与向北的地震序列。
papers.ab: North–south‐trending rifts in southern Tibet accommodate active east–west extension, but how normal‐faulting rupture varies with rift development remains unclear. Here we use Synthetic Aperture Radar observations to investigate the 2025 Mw 7.0 Dingri earthquake in the southern Xainza–Dinggye rift. Our rupture model shows that the 2025 earthquake ruptured multiple segments and likely triggered three meter‐scale slope failures within surface‐rupture gaps at the rift margin. Together with preceding Dingri events, our results reveal contrasting along‐rift coseismic rupture behavior: larger, shallower, and more complex slip in the higher‐elevation, narrower northern Dengmo Co rift, but smaller, deeper slip in the lower, wider southern half‐graben. Combined with other geodetically constrained normal‐faulting sequences across southern Tibet, these observations show an apparent northward ordering along certain rift segments. Our study provides new insight into the relationship between long‐term rift development and earthquake rupture behavior in the southern Tibetan rift system.

papers.t: How do faults recover after giant earthquakes?
in: Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Indiana University, Bloomington, IN, USA.
tk: This perspective discusses how long-term geodetic monitoring of postseismic deformation reveals the mechanisms of fault recovery and relocking following giant earthquakes.
本文探讨了如何通过长期大地测量监测来揭示大地震后断层恢复与锁定的机制。
papers.ab: Long-term monitoring reveals how a fault relocks for a future earthquake after a massive rupture

papers.t: Apparent Velocity Extraction from Quadrupole Acoustic Logging While Drilling: CNN-Based Moveout Regression
tk: A lightweight CNN regresses moveout from quadrupole logging-while-drilling waveforms, achieving 25x faster processing than traditional methods for real-time downhole deployment.
提出轻量级CNN回归随钻声波测井时差，速度提升25倍。
papers.ab: Acoustic logging while drilling (LWD) provides formation shear-wave velocity in real time during drilling, supporting geosteering and geomechanical evaluation. Shear-wave velocity is currently extracted by slowness–time coherence (STC) processing, which relies on a grid search for the global extremum; its hard decision is prone to dense outlier spikes in multi-event wavefields, and its computational burden is unfavorable for downhole real-time evaluation. We propose a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) that regresses the inter-receiver moveout directly from array waveforms; five-fold cross-validation on a synthetic dataset yields a median relative velocity error of 2.51% ± 0.16%. The numeric and image-inversion domains, with either a threshold mask or an Attention U-Net segmentation mask, give consistent velocities, with differences between mask methods of ≤0.6%, and 2.5–4.5 kHz band-pass filtering brings the two domains into convergence. As a control, supervised regression labeled by a measured STC log attains per-gather r = 0.72 over the full well interval under random splitting, but r drops to 0.20 under depth-blocked cross-validation that removes near-neighbor leakage, delimiting the applicability boundary of this proxy route. Inference is a single deterministic forward pass, the model occupies only 266 KB, and it runs approximately 25× faster than vectorized STC, making it suitable for edge deployment.

papers.t: Empirical Relationships Between Ground Motion Intensities and JMA Seismic Intensity Scale
tk: Presents a new three-parameter empirical model relating ground motion parameters to JMA seismic intensity, reducing basis risk for parametric earthquake insurance.
提出新型三参数经验模型预测JMA烈度，降低地震保险基差风险。
papers.ab: There is a growing appetite for parametric Japanese earthquake insurance products that use Japanese Meteorological Agency seismic intensity, IJMA, triggers. However, most earthquake risk models used to price these contracts do not compute IJMA directly, instead relying on conversions that introduce additional basis risk. Here, we present empirical parameterisations of IJMA as a function of all combinations of moment magnitude, hypocentral distance, peak ground acceleration (PGA), and spectral acceleration (Sa(T)) at 0.2, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 s, derived from earthquake risk model outputs. Parameterisations are fitted using ridge regression applied to 21,354 ground motion recordings from 112 Japanese earthquakes spanning January 1997 to December 2025. A parsimonious three-parameter model — combining PGA, Sa(0.3 s), and Sa(1.0 s) — outperforms a previously published parameterisation, substantially reducing both uncertainty and bias. When applied to a synthetic parametric insurance portfolio exposed to 25 years of Japanese seismicity, this parameterisation yields a measurable reduction in basis risk. These results support more reliable and transparent pricing of parametric earthquake insurance products.

papers.t: Detecting the Oceanic Moho Using Teleseismic P‐Wave Coda Autocorrelations of Ocean Bottom Seismograph Records
in: Sun Yat-sen University
tk: This study demonstrates the detection of the oceanic Moho by applying autocorrelation analysis to teleseismic P-wave coda recorded by ocean bottom seismographs.
本研究利用海底地震仪记录的远震P波尾波自相关分析成功探测了海洋莫霍面。
papers.ab: Although active‐source seismic methods can image the oceanic Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho) at high resolution, their high cost motivates passive approaches using OBS, for which receiver functions (RF) are often complicated by instrument tilt, azimuthal misalignment, sedimentary layers, and water‐column reverberations. Here we apply teleseismic P‐wave coda autocorrelation to hydrophone data from OBS to image the oceanic Moho. Compared with vertical‐component data, hydrophone data provide a simpler interpretation because they avoid P‐to‐S conversions and are dominated by reflected and transmitted P‐wave energy. By analyzing autocorrelation results from 22 long‐period and 24 short‐period stations in the NoMelt experiment, we identify a Moho reflection with a TwTT of ∼2.56 s and resolve lateral variations in crustal TwTT that are smoothed out in the radially averaged representations of global velocity models. Combined with previous studies and model tests, this longer‐than‐expected crustal TwTT suggests that a crust‐mantle transition zone may exist beneath the NoMelt region.

papers.t: The pioneering CO2 test injection project at Trüllikon, Switzerland: insights from multiphase hydro-mechanical modeling
in: ETH Zurich
University of Bern
tk: Multiphase hydro-mechanical modeling of the Swiss CITru CO2 injection project shows that the 10,000-tonne injection remains safe, with pressure and stress changes well below fault reactivation thresholds.
瑞士CITru二氧化碳注入项目的多相流固耦合模拟表明，1万吨注入量安全，压力与应力变化远低于断层活化阈值。
papers.ab: Multiphase hydro-mechanical modeling was used to assess the pilot CO2 test injection at Trüllikon, northern Switzerland (project CITru), a pioneering project which aims to inject 10,000 tonnes into the Muschelkalk aquifer at ∼ 1100 m depth over two years. A site-specific geological model (4 × 4 × 2.3 km3) was constructed around the Trüllikon well (TRU1-1) using local and regional 3D seismic data and implemented in one-way coupled TOUGH3-FLAC3D simulations for three different reservoir permeability scenarios. In all scenarios, the supercritical CO2 plume migrates up-dip and predominantly northward along the inclined reservoir-caprock interface, where it becomes trapped in a small anticline before dissolving into the pore water in the longer term (thousands of years). The CO2 approaches the nearby Neuhausen Fault but never reaches it. For the lowest permeability scenario (most probable case), maximum pressure changes of 0.7 MPa and 0.25 MPa are simulated at the Neuhausen and Trüllikon faults, respectively, which is below estimated fault reactivation thresholds. Coulomb failure stress changes incorporating mechanically-induced elastic stresses remain below 0.05 MPa on both faults, indicating that injection-induced compression stabilizes them. Moreover, displacements and strains simulated in the overlying sealing formations are minimal (∼ 1 mm). In a hypothetical industrial-scale scenario (250,000 tonnes)—unlike CITru—the CO2 plume crosses the nearest branch of the Neuhausen Fault during the injection period and reaches the Trüllikon Fault within decades. Our results will directly support future planning and risk assessment within the CITru project and are likely to be useful for future onshore pilot, demonstration, and industrial-scale CO2 storage projects.

papers.t: Reliability of Bootstrap-derived stress uncertainty bounds in focal mechanism inversion
in: Institute of Disaster Prevention , Sanhe Hebei 065201 ,
Hebei Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics , Sanhe Hebei 065201 ,
Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration , Beijing 100081 ,
tk: This study evaluates Bootstrap-derived stress uncertainty bounds in focal mechanism inversion, showing they are heavily influenced by fault geometry and the true stress shape ratio.
本研究评估了震源机制解应力反演中Bootstrap不确定性边界的可靠性，发现其受断层几何和真实应力比控制。
papers.ab: Summary Earthquake focal mechanisms provide important constraints on the crustal stress field. In stress inversion based on focal mechanism data, each mechanism contains two nodal planes, whereas the actual seismogenic fault plane is often difficult to identify. Consequently, Bootstrap resampling with random nodal plane selection is widely used to estimate uncertainties in stress inversion results. However, the reliability of these uncertainty bounds remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluate the reliability of this approach using synthetic experiments and real fault-slip datasets. The results show that the reliability of Bootstrap-derived uncertainty bounds is jointly controlled by fault geometry and the true stress shape ratio (R). When seismogenic faults are distributed on both sides of the maximum compressive stress axis, the uncertainty bounds of principal stress orientations generally encompass the true solutions, whereas the uncertainty bounds of R may exhibit systematic biases depending on the true R value. By contrast, when faults occupy only one side of the fault space, the uncertainty bounds of both stress orientations and R may deviate from the true values. Further analysis indicates that this behavior reflects variations in the kinematic consistency between auxiliary-plane slip and the stress field under different R conditions, causing the influence of misselected nodal planes on inversion results to vary systematically. These findings highlight the importance of correctly identifying seismogenic fault planes and provide important implications for the interpretation of stress inversion uncertainties in practical applications.

papers.t: SeidarT: an open-source full-waveform seismic and electromagnetic wave propagation modeling toolbox demonstrated in snow and ice
in: University of Maine (Orono, United States of America)
tk: SeidarT is an open-source FDTD toolbox for modeling elastic and electromagnetic wave propagation in heterogeneous, anisotropic, and attenuating media, with applications in cryospheric geophysics.
SeidarT是一款开源FDTD工具箱，用于模拟非均匀、各向异性和衰减介质中的弹性波与电磁波传播。
papers.ab: We present SeidarT , an open-source, community-driven software package for full-waveform finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) modeling of elastic and electromagnetic wave propagation in heterogeneous, anisotropic, and attenuating media. SeidarT natively incorporates full-tensor anisotropy (all 21 stiffness coefficients), frequency-independent attenuation through a generalized Q formulation, and unified treatment of both seismic and electromagnetic wave physics on a simple Cartesian grid. The software prioritizes accessibility and extensibility by combining the computational efficiency of Fortran with the user-friendly scripting capabilities of Python. Model construction leverages an intuitive image-based geometry workflow and JSON project files, eliminating the need for complex mesh generation while allowing flexible specification of arbitrary stiffness or permittivity tensors, material distributions, and boundary conditions. We implement the Convolutional Perfectly Matched Layer (CPML) with explicit tuning strategies adapted for anisotropic media, and provide automatic stability checking via the Courant-Friedrichs-Lévy and wavenumber-bandlimit criteria. The software is validated against analytical solutions for elastic wave propagation and empirically constrained through comparison with ground-penetrating radar and seismic field observations in snow and ice. We document the physical property parameterizations for ice and snow as functions of temperature, pressure, and liquid water content, and provide multiple material homogenization schemes (Hill average, Gassmann substitution, Self-Consistent Approximation) to accommodate variable porosity and fluid saturation regimes. SeidarT is designed to lower economic and technical barriers for scientists, engineers, and students integrating sophisticated wave-physics simulations into workflows spanning cryospheric research, environmental monitoring, subsurface characterization, and civil infrastructure assessment. The open-source development model on GitHub and PyPI encourages community contributions and iterative improvements, positioning SeidarT as a versatile platform for advancing both fundamental understanding and applied geophysical imaging.

papers.t: Data and results: Periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault
in: University of California, Berkeley
tk: This dataset and model release provides Sentinel-1 InSAR stacks, GNSS data, and PyLith slip models characterizing periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault.
该数据集和模型发布提供了Sentinel-1 InSAR、GNSS及PyLith滑移模型，用于表征海沃德断层的周期性慢地震。
papers.ab: Overview. Data products and model files for Lindsay and Bürgmann, Periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault. The code is archived separately (below). The deposit holds the three rebased OPERA DISP-S1 Sentinel-1 displacement stacks over the Hayward Fault (2016 to 2026), the inputs the analysis reads, the PyLith slip-model files, and every product and figure of the analysis. Every number in the paper is in outputs/registry.csv and outputs/paper_numbers.md (in outputs.zip), with the notebook and section that computes it. Files 09156_stack.nc.part*, 09157_stack.nc.part*, 11115_stack.nc.part*: rebased OPERA DISP-S1 stacks, frames 09156 and 09157 (ascending, track 35) and 11115 (descending, track 42), netCDF, split into 600 MB parts. inputs_external.zip: the external inputs the notebooks read (fault trace and 100 m crossings, USGS creepmeter and alignment-array records, GHCNd rain). Other published datasets the notebooks read are cited. gnss_velocity.zip: GNSS station tables, the GNSS-InSAR tie, the tied velocity mosaics. aperture_sweep.zip: the cross-fault aperture sweep. models_inputs.zip, models_3d_sfsvm.zip.part*, models_homogeneous.zip: PyLith meshes, spatial databases and output points; for each run used, the points, fault and elastic_info outputs, parameters and G matrix; homogeneous (CSI) Green's functions. sensitivity.zip: sensitivity tables and L-curves. outputs.zip, figures.zip: all notebook products and the number registry, all figures (paper figures under paper/). The executed notebooks, with all their outputs, are in the code release. extension_check_2026-10-30.zip: the bridging check behind the forecast: Sentinel-1 from December 2025 to 30 October 2026 processed from OPERA CSLC-S1 with Dolphin 0.42.5 and the DISP-S1 settings (scripts, environment, configurations, Dolphin time series, the step check and its result). README.md, MANIFEST.csv, CHECKSUMS.md5: file descriptions, the contents of every zip, checksums. Rejoin split files with cat .part* > . Open Research and Software. OPERA DISP-S1 (doi:10.5067/SNWG/OPL3DISPS1-V1) and TROPO-ZENITH (doi:10.5067/SNWG/OPL4TROZEN-V1) products are public from NASA ASF DAAC. The USGS San Francisco Bay region 3D seismic velocity model v26.0 is doi:10.5066/P13AEJFI. Processing uses opera-utils 0.25.4, MintPy 1.6.3, PyLith 5.0.2 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21909051) and CSI (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14170821). Code: github.com/Dani-Lindsay/TulePond_DISP, archived at release v1.0.0 (the paper's run), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23934127. Acknowledgements. We thank the data providers: NASA JPL OPERA, ASF DAAC, USGS, NOAA NCEI and the Nevada Geodetic Laboratory. The forecast in this deposit was issued and archived on 4 November 2026, conditioned on data through 24 October 2026.

papers.t: Deep Learning Based Interference Suppression Method for Surface Wave Detection Using Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) Drilling Noise
in: State Key Laboratory for Tunnel Engineering , Shandong University, Jinan, China
Geotechnical and Structural Engineering Research Center, Shandong University, Jinan, China
School of Future Technology, Shandong University, Jinan, China
School of Qilu Transportation, Shandong University, Jinan, China
tk: A deep learning convolutional autoencoder with transfer learning suppresses body-wave and inter-trace interference in TBM drilling noise to improve surface-wave dispersion extraction.
利用深度学习与迁移学习抑制TBM钻掘噪声干扰并提取面波频散。
papers.ab: Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs), characterized by superior advancement rates and integrated operational sequences, have emerged as the predominant construction methodology for urban subsurface tunnel development. However, TBMs are less capable of coping with faults, isolated rocks, and other adverse geological conditions common to shallow urban subsurface. This has led to serious challenges in the safe construction and disaster prevention of urban subsurface tunnels. Due to the strong energy and large amplitude of surface waves, analyzing them provides an effective way to characterize the subsurface and ensure the safety of urban shallow tunnel construction. Inspired by the seismic-while-drilling method, surface-wave detection using tunnel-drilling noise has been widely applied due to its advantages of real-time detection and non-invasiveness. However, it is difficult to remove the body-wave interference signals brought about by factors such as the excitation mode of the seismic source, which in turn affects the subsequent extraction of the dispersion curves. Thus, we analyze the three main types of interference signals present in tunnel drilling noise-based surface-wave data, and a synthetic dataset incorporating realistic field interference signal characteristics is constructed. Then, we achieve the suppression of interference signals by constructing a special convolutional self-encoder that pays attention to the morphological features of the signal. Besides, a transfer learning method is proposed to suppress the inter-trace interference due to irregular acquisition and to make the method directly applicable to field data. The results of synthetic and field data processing show that the proposed method has good denoising capability and exhibits higher accuracy in subsequent dispersion-curve extraction.

papers.t: Seismic Resolution Enhancement Using a Transformer by Fusing Local and Global Attention
in: Shandong Province Key Laboratory of Intelligent Oil & Gas Industrial Software, China University of Petroleum (East China), Qingdao 266580, China
School of Geosciences, China University of Petroleum (East China), Qingdao 266580, China
tk: A dual-attention transformer (Seis-DAT) is developed to enhance seismic resolution by fusing local window-based self-attention and global channel attention.
开发了融合局部与全局注意力的Transformer方法以提高地震分辨率。
papers.ab: High-resolution seismic data is crucial for accurately characterizing thin reservoirs and small-scale faults, providing the foundation for lithology and fluid identification. However, image super-resolution techniques based on deep-learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks, are fundamentally constrained to local receptive fields. Such architectures struggle to capture the long-range spatial dependencies required to model continuous seismic events, often leading to oversmoothed results or structural artifacts. To address this problem, we develop a dual-attention transformer termed Seis-DAT. The core of Seis-DAT is a dual-attention transformer block that integrates window-based self-attention to capture local textures with channel attention to provide a global receptive field. This design enables the model to learn local details and global geological trends, ensuring both fidelity and structural consistency in the reconstructed results. To mitigate the scarcity of high-quality labeled data, we construct a large-scale synthetic dataset incorporating complex faults and folds. Furthermore, a composite loss function combining the ?1 loss and multiscale structural similarity loss is employed to dynamically balance pixel-level accuracy and structural integrity through a linear weight scheduling strategy. Synthetic tests demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index measure values than conventional comparative methods. Applications to real seismic data show that Seis-DAT generates clearer seismic events with enhanced lateral continuity, thereby improving seismic data resolution.

papers.t: TulePond_DISP: code for Periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault
tk: A code repository and dataset for modeling and forecasting periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault using OPERA DISP-S1 InSAR data and PyLith.
一个用于利用OPERA DISP-S1 InSAR数据和PyLith建模与预测海沃德断层周期性慢地震的开源代码库。
papers.ab: Code for Lindsay and Bürgmann, Periodic slow slip events on the Hayward Fault (in preparation). This release is the state of the code for the paper's run. The executed notebooks (01–15) hold every output, and every number in the paper is registered with the notebook and section that computes it. Data and results: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23850500. It contains the rebased OPERA DISP-S1 stacks, the external inputs, the PyLith model files, the sensitivity tables, and all products and figures. Forecast: notebook 13 issues the forecast of the next Tule Pond slow slip event (forecast_statement.txt). It was issued and archived on 4 November 2026 and is conditioned on no event through 24 October 2026. To reproduce: see README.md for the environment (environment.yml), setting the data root (TULEPOND_DATA_DIR), and running ./run_all.sh. Licence: MIT (code). The data in the Zenodo record are CC BY 4.0.

papers.t: Sensitivity Kernels for Earthquake Coda-Correlation Wavefield Features and Applications to Global Seismology
in: Research School of Earth Sciences, Australian National University , Canberra 2601 ,
ETH Zürich Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, , 8092 Zürich ,
tk: Develops a forward modeling framework and adjoint-based sensitivity kernels for earthquake coda-correlation features to enable deep Earth tomography.
开发了地震尾波相关特征的前向模拟框架，并利用伴随方法推导了用于深部地球成像的敏感性核。
papers.ab: Summary Seismic coda-correlation methods have revealed numerous body-wave-like features in globally stacked correlograms, offering new opportunities to constrain the structure of Earth’s deep interior. Unlike the common assumptions about the diffuse ambient noise field that enable reconstruction of surface waves, earthquake coda-correlation features arise from cross-terms in reverberating body waves of common slowness that share a subset of propagation legs. However, quantitative interpretation of these features for tomographic imaging has been hindered by the lack of distributed sensitivity kernels relating observed correlation signals to Earth heterogeneities. Here, we develop a forward modeling framework for the earthquake coda-correlation wavefield that bypasses conventional cross-correlation of late-coda waveforms. Our approach simulates correlation features directly by treating the time-reversed generating wavefield as a distributed source throughout Earth’s interior. The forward-modeled correlograms reproduce features obtained through conventional stacking with a significantly improved signal-to-noise ratio. Building on this framework, we derive finite-frequency traveltime banana-doughnut sensitivity kernels using adjoint methods, which quantify how correlation time measurements of correlation features depend on perturbations in P-wave velocity, S-wave velocity, and density. We compute sensitivity kernels for prominent correlation features (P*, ScS*, K*, and others) at station separations ranging from 30° to 180°. The kernels reveal extensive sampling of Earth’s mantle, outer core, and inner core, with spatial-sensitivity patterns fundamentally different from those of classical body-wave tomography. For antipodal station pairs, correlation features exhibit strong sensitivity throughout the deep interior, including regions poorly sampled by traditional seismic phases. Our results confirm that correlation features form through constructive interference of body-wave pairs with similar slowness, rather than representing Green’s functions between station pairs. This work establishes the theoretical foundation for coda-correlation tomography, enabling future three-dimensional imaging of Earth’s internal structure with unprecedented sampling of the deep interior. The sensitivity kernels provide a pathway to exploit the wealth of information contained in earthquake coda for high-resolution mantle and core tomography.

papers.t: Shallow Slip Deficit: An Intrinsic Property of Continental Earthquakes, Slightly Enhanced by Fault Maturity
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Université Côte d'Azur
Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur
Géoazur
Institut de Recherche pour le Développement
Centre d'Études et d'Expertise sur les Risques, l'Environnement, la Mobilité et l'Aménagement
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
Université Paris Cité
tk: Shallow slip deficit is an intrinsic property of continental earthquakes, only slightly enhanced by fault maturity.
浅部滑移亏损是大陆地震的固有特征，仅受断层成熟度轻微增强。
papers.ab: A depletion of earthquake slip in the shallow crust (shallow coseismic slip deficit, or coseismic SSD) has been observed on <30, Mw ≥ 6 continental earthquakes, and attributed to the immaturity of the ruptured faults. We question the factors that contribute to the coseismic SSD. We built the largest earthquake source model database available to date, with 1078 models providing coseismic SSD estimates on 163 Mw ≥ 6, various slip mode, continental earthquakes worldwide since 1990. We also built a database providing their fault maturity parameters (initiation age, net displacement, length, slip rate). Our combined earthquake‐fault analysis reveals that coseismic SSD of continental earthquakes, whatever their slip mode, is primarily controlled by the relation between their magnitude and peak slip depth, and, to a much lesser extent, by the fault maturity. A model where earthquake slip produces zero stress drop on the shallow velocity strengthening fault section reproduces the data well.

papers.t: FA-Agent: An extensible multimodal agent framework for first-arrival picking in mountainous seismic data
tk: FA-Agent is an extensible multimodal LLM agent framework that automates first-arrival picking in noisy mountainous seismic data by emulating human processing workflows.
FA-Agent是一个基于多模态大模型的智能体框架，通过模拟人工流程实现山区地震初至拾取。
papers.ab: First-arrival traveltimes underpin near-surface velocity modeling and static corrections, but in low signal-to-noise mountainous land data the first arrival is often weak, intermittent, and masked by strong direct waves and noise. Energy-based pickers then pick later arrivals or noise, and deep-learning pickers usually require retraining for a new survey. Because erroneous picks bias first-arrival tomography, many difficult zones are still inspected and corrected manually. We present FA-Agent, an agent framework for first-arrival picking built on a multimodal large language model. It combines a model that performs visual recognition and makes decisions, tools that process the data, and skills that carry experience of processing mountainous data. The framework is open and extensible: new pickers, denoising methods, and quality-control tools can be added, and new experience can be written into the skills. It is restricted neither to mountainous data nor to a particular model. Emulating a seismic data processor, the agent first surveys the whole gather to find zones needing attention, then examines them in enlarged views, and finally keeps, corrects, or removes the initial picks. On semi-synthetic gathers with known first arrivals and real mountainous noise, the agent picked the first arrival with high accuracy where it was clearly visible and removed the picks where it was invisible and could not be judged. Applied to randomly sampled gathers from a mountainous survey, it corrected picks onto weak first-arrival branches and removed picks where no first arrival could be confirmed, and it performed well on the most difficult data. Cases reviewed by experts are added to the skills automatically, so the agent improves with use, and a locally deployed model keeps confidential data on site. FA-Agent can thus become an essential component of future automated seismic data processing workflows.

papers.t: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
tk: An analytical framework for semidiurnal thermotidal torque on rocky planets models atmospheric tides and Lamb-wave resonances, matching general circulation model simulations.
本文提出了岩石行星半日热潮汐力矩的解析框架，模拟了大气潮汐与兰姆波共振。
papers.ab: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of the thermotidal torque on the tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising the star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the role of resonantly excited Lamb waves requires clarification due to its potential impact on Earth's length of day (LOD) during the Precambrian. Building on a previous work, which provided a fully analytical formulation of the atmospheric tidal response of rocky planets, we apply this framework to isentropic and isothermal atmospheres. We perform a comprehensive functional analysis of the resulting torque and compare the analytical predictions with numerical solutions from earlier general circulation model (GCM) studies. The analytical model agrees well with GCM results, accurately capturing the frequency dependence of tidal torque both for paleo-Earth and present-day Earth. More generally, the solutions capture the torque peak near synchronous rotation and the amplification associated with Lamb-wave resonance. Near resonance, the GCM results exhibit a stronger braking torque than accelerating torque. This asymmetry is reproduced by allowing tidal heating to lag behind insolation. The agreement with GCM spectra suggests that thermal tides in the benchmark simulations are driven predominantly by an indirect thermal forcing characterised by a substantial time delay, in contrast to the direct absorption of sunlight that dominates semidiurnal tides on present-day Earth.

papers.t: Scaling of Seismic Ground Motions Generated by Human Crowds
in: Department of Earth and Planetary Science, Faculty of Exact Sciences, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel
tk: Seismic ground motions from human crowds scale linearly with the logarithm of crowd size, with energetic protests producing stronger scaling than routine activities.
人群地震地动随人群规模对数线性缩放，且受集体行为影响。
papers.ab: Human activities generate seismic ground motions that dominate the high-frequency (>1 Hz) seismic spectra in urban environments. Although vehicular and train traffic have been widely studied, the seismic signature of large pedestrian crowds remains less well quantified. Here, I analyze seismic recordings from dense urban networks in Japan and combine them with observations from outdoor gatherings in the United States and Israel to characterize crowd-generated seismic signals. Through clustering analysis of ground motions recorded by the dense Metropolitan Seismic Observation Network in the Tokyo metropolitan area, I identify distinct temporal and spatial patterns associated with vehicular traffic. I then examine 385 outdoor gatherings in the United States and 300 schools in Tokyo, together with observations from the 2021 Meron pilgrimage in Israel, a 100,000-person event that resulted in a deadly crowd crush. Crowd-generated seismic energy is strongest in the 1–2 Hz band, consistent with human walking frequencies. Distance-corrected seismic amplification factors scale approximately linearly with the logarithm of crowd size across five orders of magnitude but form two distinct populations: energetic outdoor protests produce larger distance-corrected amplification factors and stronger scaling than routine student activity in Tokyo schools, suggesting that crowd-generated seismic excitation depends on collective crowd behavior. This relationship provides a framework for using seismic observations to detect and characterize large human gatherings in urban environments.

papers.t: Active tectonics of the Bodrum Peninsula and seismicity following the 2017 Mw 6.6 Bodrum-Kos earthquake: kinematic analysis and definition of the Bodrum Fault Zone, Western Anatolia
in: Afyon Kocatepe University
Dokuz Eylül University
tk: This study defines the Bodrum Fault Zone by analyzing active tectonics, fault kinematics, and post-2017 seismicity following the Mw 6.6 Bodrum-Kos earthquake.
该研究结合2017年地震余震与断层运动学，定义了博德鲁姆断裂带。

papers.t: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
tk: A process-based hydrological catchment model, CaRT+, matches or exceeds the accuracy of deep-learning LSTM models across hundreds of catchments on three continents.
物理过程驱动的流域水文模型CaRT+在三大洲数百个流域上的模拟精度达到了深度学习LSTM模型的水平。
papers.ab: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.

papers.t: Seismic evidence for double slab tears at the Neo-Tethyan subduction–collision transition
tk: Seismic imaging reveals double slab tears at the Neo-Tethyan subduction-collision transition, shedding light on the geodynamics of continental collision.
地震成像揭示了新特提斯俯冲-碰撞过渡带的双板片撕裂，为大陆碰撞动力学提供了新见解。

papers.t: From Seafloor Deformation to Sea-Surface Displacement: Tsunami Generation Over Variable Bathymetry
in: San Diego State University, 5500 Campanile Dr., San Diego, CA, United States [US]
tk: This study derives a generalized Kajiura transfer operator for tsunami generation over arbitrary 3D bathymetry, accounting for slope effects and global volume consistency.
该研究推导了适用于任意三维海底地形的广义Kajiura海啸激发转换算子，考虑了坡度效应并保持了全局体积一致性。
papers.ab: Tsunami source models commonly convert seafloor deformation into an initial sea-surface displacement with the classical Kajiura filter, which is exact for an ocean of uniform depth. Yet earthquake source regions often span trenches and continental slopes where water depth varies on the same scales as the deformation. We derive the corresponding transfer for arbitrary smooth, submerged, single-valued three-dimensional bathymetry. Seafloor motion enters through the bottom-normal forcing $q=U_z+ abla h\cdot\Uh$, and the exact rapid-source response is $\eta=\opC q$ with $\opC=\opB^{-1}$, a nonlocal operator determined by the actual bathymetry. This is not obtained by simply replacing $H$ with $h(\xh)$ in $\sech(KH)$: slope enters the exact bottom boundary condition, and spatially varying bathymetry couples the response globally. Exact wedge and three-dimensional seamount tests reveal a clear hierarchy. Local water depth controls the dominant attenuation and broadening, gentle slopes add a mainly phase-like correction, and surrounding geometry produces a smaller but genuinely nonlocal redistribution that local formulas cannot always improve. A 2011 Tohoku-Oki application shows the same hierarchy for realistic bathymetry and demonstrates that the full solution restores global volume consistency. The operator also appears in $\eta_{tt}+g\opG\eta=\opC q_{tt}$, making generalized Kajiura transfer the rapid-source limit of a single time-dependent generation framework rather than an independent initialization rule.

papers.t: Shallow lunar fractures dominate the long-lasting seismic coda
tk: A novel model using random vacuum fractures in the shallow lunar crust successfully explains the long-lasting lunar seismic coda through total reflection.
提出一种浅表随机真空裂隙模型，通过全反射机制完美解释了月震长尾余震的成因。
papers.ab: Lunar seismic records are characterized by long-lasting spindle-shaped coda, which has long been considered to be caused by strong velocity contrasts in a continuous-medium lunar crust; however, simulated waveforms could not well match the observation even with unrealistically strong velocity contrasts, demonstrating its mechanism still unsolved. Here we propose a novel model of coda wave generation with random fractures in the lunar crust, where vacuum fractures prevent seismic wave propagation as insulating boundaries, causing strong persistent reverberation in terms of total reflection among fractures. Our model can easily reproduce the typical characteristics of observed Apollo data even using a limited number of simplified fractures in homogeneous matrix, with envelope correlations over 0.9, much higher than previous studies. Numerical simulations suggest that fractures in the uppermost ~1 km of the crust may dominate lunar seismic scattering. This model enables us to investigate the shallow lunar fracture system using seismic data and to suppress seismic coda for detecting critical phases reflected from deep interiors.

papers.t: Depth-Dependent Extension and Flexural response of Lithosphere to enormous sediment loading in the Bangladesh: Clues to uplift of Shillong Plateau
in: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Pune, Unknown, Pune, Maharasthra, India [IN]
Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Pune, Pune, Unknown, Pune, 411008, India [IN]
tk: 3D gravity inversion and flexural backstripping reveal depth-dependent lithospheric thinning, magmatic underplating, and sediment-loading-induced uplift of the Shillong Plateau in Bangladesh.
3D重力反演与挠曲回剥揭示了孟加拉国岩石圈减薄、岩浆底侵及沉积负载导致的希隆高原隆升。
papers.ab: The Bangladesh is comprising up to 20 km of sedimentary deposits over the lithosphere and surrounded by India-Asia collision zone. Thus, deciphering the crustal architecture is essential for understanding the tectonic evolution. The sparse broadband seismic stations have provided estimates of Moho depth, however, the regional-scale variation in Moho topography remains poorly constrained. In this study, we performed a 3D gravity inversion constrained by seismically-derived Moho depth, to better delineate the crustal structure and thinning factor of the region. The inverted Moho depth beneath the Bangladesh varying from 22 – 32 km and exceed 32 km in the adjacent regions, while crustal thickness is less than 22 km in the Bengal Basin. The west-east lithospheric structure shows that the lithospheric thinning preceded crustal thinning in the northern Bangladesh, whereas in southern Bangladesh they occurred synchronously. Gravity modelling and stretching factors derived from tectonic subsidence support the presence of 5–8 km of magmatic underplating beneath the volcanic rifted margin in Bangladesh. 3D flexural backstripping analysis reveals that onshore Bengal Basin thermally subsided 5 – 7 km and adjacent region experienced a tectonic uplift < 2 km. The plume-related magmatism combined with prolonged sediment loading produced ~ 1 km of uplift of Shillong Plateau and remaining topography is generated by slip on the major thrust faults during the late Cenozoic shortening. Our findings highlight the key factors shaping the present-day crustal structure and topography of northeastern India.

papers.t: Lagrangian Irreversibility in Stratified Turbulence
tk: This study investigates how stable stratification affects Lagrangian power statistics and temporal asymmetry in homogeneous Boussinesq turbulence.
本研究探讨了稳定分层如何影响齐次布辛涅斯克湍流中的拉格朗日功率统计和时间不对称性。
papers.ab: Stable stratification reorganizes turbulence, suppressing vertical motion and altering the balance between vortical and strain-dominated flow structures. How these changes affect the temporal asymmetry of kinetic-energy exchange along fluid-particle trajectories remains incompletely understood. Using direct numerical simulations of homogeneous Boussinesq turbulence, we investigate Lagrangian power statistics across four local velocity-gradient topology classes and three nonzero stratification strengths, with an unstratified reference case. With increasing stratification, the global power variance decreases while the standardized skewness becomes more negative, indicating enhanced asymmetry despite weaker fluctuations. Conditioning on local topology reveals distinct responses: axial-strain-dominated regions exhibit the most negative total-power skewness at all stratification strengths, whereas biaxial-strain-dominated regions change sign from positive to negative under stratification. Horizontal and vertical component powers also respond differently, revealing directional dependence. Among the dynamical contributions to power, the pressure contribution, nearly symmetric in the unstratified case, becomes more negatively skewed with increasing stratification. Energy-conditioned pressure statistics further indicate altered pressure-mediated energy redistribution. Finally, tracer persistence-time distributions exhibit exponential tails, with time scales that differ across topology classes and respond differently to stratification. Increasing stratification is thus accompanied by three concurrent changes: enhanced asymmetry of Lagrangian power, modified energy redistribution by pressure, and altered temporal sampling of local flow structures by tracers. These co-occurring signatures characterize the response to stratification, though their causal relations remain to be established.

papers.t: New Scalar Measures of Geodetic Strain and Moment Rate from Kinematic Mode Decomposition: Application to the Southwestern United States
tk: Proposes new scalar measures of geodetic strain rate and seismic moment rate based on fault kinematics, showing significant differences in mixed-style deformation zones.
提出基于断层运动学的新大地测量应变率和矩释放率标量度量方法。
papers.ab: Scalar representations of geodetic strain rate tensors are widely used to characterize crustal deformation and, in seismic hazard assessment, to convert strain rate to expected seismic moment rate. Existing scalar definitions of shear strain rate, total strain rate and deformation style are not defined consistently and, because they depend on eigenvalues that carry both dilatation and shear, cannot be read as a partition of mixed-strain deformation. We propose definitions motivated by fault kinematics. The strike-slip strain rate (e_s), derived from the shear on zero-length-change orientations, is twice the geometric mean of the principal strain rate magnitudes and zero when both share a sign. The total strain rate (e_t) is the explicit sum of and the absolute dilatation (); except for uniaxial strain it exceeds the Frobenius norm (e_f), by up to a factor sqrt(3). The style parameter equals the fractional dilatational contribution in mixed-strain deformation and is extended to classify deformation in which both principal strain rates share a sign. We also propose a moment rate (M_split) that releases the strike-slip and dilatational contributions on separate strike-slip and dip-slip faults; for Andersonian dips it exceeds the minimum moment (M_min) by up to 37% for mixed-faulting settings. An application to southwestern U.S. geodetic strain rates shows that the 37% maximum difference is not a corner case: in the 53% of the area where each of the strike-slip and dilatational contributions is at least a quarter of the total strain rate, M_split exceeds M_min by 34%. The southwestern U.S. example demonstrates that these differences can be regionally significant, with moment-rate estimates differing by tens of percent in mixed-style deformation zones.

papers.t: Toward quantitative soundscape monitoring with low-cost recorders: application to the Venice Lagoon
in: University of Padua
tk: This study evaluates the feasibility of using low-cost HydroMoth recorders calibrated against a reference hydrophone for quantitative underwater soundscape monitoring in the Venice Lagoon.
本研究评估了使用与参考水听器校准的低成本HydroMoth记录仪在威尼斯潟湖进行定量水下声景监测的可行性。
papers.ab: Underwater noise in shallow coastal lagoons arises from both natural and anthropogenic sources and is shaped by complex environmental factors. High-quality hydrophones provide precise measurements but are often limited in spatial coverage and deployment duration due to cost and logistical constraints, whereas low-cost acoustic sensors allow flexible observational networks but frequently exhibit sensor-to-sensor variability and are typically used qualitatively. Here, we present a practical framework to demonstrate that low-cost recorders can provide quantitative insights in shallow lagoon environments. A spatially distributed array of three HydroMoth sensors (Open Acoustic Devices, UK) was deployed across multiple sites in the Venice Lagoon, recording continuous acoustic data over full diel cycles. Using a co-located reference-calibrated hydrophone and a straightforward calibration workflow, recorded signals were converted into absolute sound pressure levels (SPL, dB re μPa), enabling comparisons across sensors and sites. Analyses revealed marked day-night differences and spatial heterogeneity across monitoring sites. We also found that simultaneous recordings made by the three HydroMoth units at the same location slightly differ from one another, and this discrepancy could not be entirely suppressed by calibration. Our results show that, despite some important limitations, low-cost sensors can provide frequency-limited, semi-quantitative acoustic measurements, supporting large-scale, quantitative soundscape monitoring. By enabling spatially distributed and cost-effective measurements, this approach supports scalable monitoring of underwater noise pollution in complex transitional coastal systems, contributing to ongoing efforts in marine environmental assessment and management.

papers.t: Hydration at the base of the mantle transition zone by ancient subductions in Asia
papers.j: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
in: State Key Laboratory of Precision Geodesy, School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China
Mengcheng National Geophysical Observatory, University of Science and Technology of China
National Key Laboratory of Ecological Safety and Sustainable Development in Arid Lands, Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography, Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
tk: Maps water content at the mantle transition zone base by combining mineral physics and seismic observations, revealing ancient subduction-driven hydration beneath Asia.
结合矿物物理与地震学观测，重建了亚洲下方古俯冲带引起的幔源过渡带底部水分富集。
papers.ab: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine–Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol–Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth’s deep water cycle.

papers.t: Train Vibrations Reveal Internal Changes in a High-Speed Railway Viaduct System through Dispersion-Change Patterns of a Fast Guided Wave
in: Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China, Beijing, Chaoyang District,, Beituchengxi road, 19, Beijing, China [CN]
Peking University, Unknown, Beijing, China [CN]
Institute of Geophysics China Earthquake Administration, Unknown, Beijing, China [CN]
Southern University of Science and Technology, 1088 Xueyuan Avenue, Nanshan District, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China [CN]
Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Unknown, Beijing, China [CN]
Peking University School of Earth and Space Sciences, Unknown, Beijing, China [CN]
Institute of Geology and Geophysics Chinese Academy of Sciences, No.19 Beitucheng Western Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, Select a State, China [CN]
Peking University, Geophysics Department, Peking University, Beijing, China [CN]
tk: Seismic interferometry of high-speed train vibrations reveals diurnal temperature and multi-day groundwater effects on a railway viaduct's guided-wave dispersion.
利用高铁振动干涉测量揭示温度和地下水对高架桥导波色散的影响。
papers.ab: High-speed trains generate highly repeatable seismic vibrations, whose changes are expected to reveal how railway infrastructure changes over time. From a dense array and 28 days of trains, we use seismic interferometry to extract a fast guided wave along the viaduct hour by hour. The wave travels at about 3000 m/s with a single S-shaped branch, and its dispersion has two change patterns: a diurnal cycle of up to 4% that reverses near 7 Hz, and a 0.6% multi-day change. Fitting attributes the diurnal cycle to the resonance frequency and the coupling parameter, both tracking air temperature.The multi-day change can come from the waveguide velocity and coincides with an irrigation-driven groundwater fall. Together, these observations indicate that the viaduct system is locally resonant, and the frequency pattern identifies which internal parameter of the system has changed. This offers a new seismological means for monitoring railway bridge health.

papers.t: The width beyond a static arrest point predicts which static arrests span the fault
tk: The subcritical width beyond a static arrest point on a fault predicts whether a static arrest will dynamically span the entire fault.
断层亚临界宽度可预测哪些静态停止的破裂会发生动态贯通。
papers.ab: Population models treat a static arrest as the end of the rupture, although some of those arrests span the fault in a fully dynamic calculation. This paper tests whether the static crack itself shows which ones. A static stress-intensity criterion and a fully dynamic rupture were compared on 180 new random stress fields on one 120 km antiplane fault with linear slip weakening.
