The predictor is the subcritical width, the extra distance one crack tip must be extended, with the other tip held fixed, before the static stress intensity factor returns to its critical value. Two logistic models were fitted on 52 earlier antiplane ruptures, 10 of which span the fault. One uses the static arrest length alone and the other adds the width. Both were applied unchanged to the 158 new ruptures that the static criterion stops. Of the 158, 24 span the fault dynamically. Adding the width raises the probability that a spanning rupture ranks above an arrested one from 0.880 to 0.956, a gain of 0.076 with a 95% interval from 0.037 to 0.126. The test and the required gain were fixed before the new fields were drawn. Halving the grid spacing along strike left the outcome of all 158 ruptures unchanged. On 120 earlier ruptures on the same fault, the static criterion and the dynamic rupture disagreed 22 times, and all 22 were static arrests that spanned the fault. Population models and induced earthquake estimates that use the static balance make that error in one direction. The width read from the static crack can rank which of those static arrests should be run dynamically first, at the correlation length tested here. At a correlation length 1.78 times longer, a width threshold flags 19 of 38 spanning ruptures and a length threshold flags 34, so that ranking is not shown to carry over. The test covers antiplane rupture, one correlation length, three stress amplitudes, and linear slip weakening.

papers.t: Phase-field modeling of hydraulic fracturing across propagation regimes
in: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
University of California, Berkeley
tk: A phase-field numerical model is developed to simulate hydraulic fracture propagation across different physical regimes.
该研究开发了一种相场数值模型，能够模拟跨越不同物理机制的水力压裂裂缝传播。

papers.t: Seismogenic fault geometry of the Taiwan suture zone from arc-continent collision to the collision-subduction transition
in: National Chung Cheng University
National Cheng Kung University
tk: Delineates the 3D seismogenic fault geometry of the Taiwan suture zone, revealing structural transitions from arc-continent collision to subduction.
刻画台湾缝合带三维断层几何，揭示弧陆碰撞向俯冲的过渡特征。
papers.ab: We investigate the three-dimensional seismogenic architecture and along-strike evolution of the Longitudinal Valley (LV) suture zone in eastern Taiwan, where arc–continent collision between the Philippine Sea Plate (PSP) and Eurasian Plate progressively evolves into northward subduction of the PSP. Using seismic waveforms recorded by CWASN, BATS, and TSMIP between 1991 and 2024, we apply a machine-learning phase picker to obtain internally consistent P- and S-wave arrivals and relocate all events with a nonlinear probabilistic location algorithm and a 3-D velocity model of Taiwan. This procedure yields a more complete and structurally coherent earthquake catalog, allowing us to image the geometry of major fault systems and their relation to tomographic velocity and Vp/Vs anomalies. The relocated seismicity and tomography show that the west-dipping Central Range Fault (CRF) and east-dipping Longitudinal Valley Fault (LVF) and interaction change systematically from south to north. In the southern collision segment, the CRF is steep and bounds a strong, uplifted Central Range block, whereas the LVF is a moderately to steeply east-dipping fault localized beneath the Coastal Range. Northward, the CRF dip shallows and truncates the shallow LVF, producing a structurally complex interaction zone. In the northern transition to subduction, LVF-related seismicity deepens into a near-vertical, high-Vp/Vs structure accompanied by a west-dipping back-thrust, together defining the western boundary of the descending Philippine Sea Plate. We further document a high-angle left-lateral strikeslip fault within the suture zone that is active mainly in the southern LV but remains confined to the Central Range. Finally, a high-velocity, low-Vp/Vs block beneath the Southern Longitudinal Trough is interpreted as remnant forearc crust. Together, these results provide a unified seismological framework for the structural evolution of Taiwan’s suture zone from collision to incipient subduction.

papers.t: GeoSim: Benchmarking Multi-Field Neural Operators for Geodynamics
tk: GeoSim is a 2D mantle-plume simulation benchmark for evaluating multi-field neural operators, revealing a scalar-velocity prediction gap.
GeoSim是一个二维地幔柱模拟基准数据集，用于评估多场神经营算子并揭示了标量与速度场预测差距。
papers.ab: Learning reliable surrogates for geodynamic models requires benchmarks that resolve coupled fields and temporal stability. We present GeoSim, a benchmark of high-resolution two-dimensional mantle-plume simulations generated with I2VIS, comprising 237 trajectories across two parameter regimes, with six coupled fields, physical timestamps, and trajectory-level splits. GeoSim defines short-window prediction and autonomous rollout, and evaluates representative neural operators field by field. Across models, we observe a pronounced scalar--velocity gap: scalar fields are reconstructed accurately while velocity errors remain large, and short-window accuracy does not imply stable rollout. We also evaluate MFGNO (Multi-Field Graph Neural Operator), a joint multi-field graph baseline designed for this benchmark; on GeoSim-Plume1, under a fixed per-field objective, it reduces horizontal and vertical velocity errors by 58.4% and 38.5% relative to an independent-field graph baseline, while an explicit field-difference input shows no measurable benefit at this scale. GeoSim provides a reproducible benchmark for field-wise diagnosis and long-horizon evaluation of geodynamic surrogates.

papers.t: Extracting and Characterizing Near-Fault Effects from Strong Motion Observations of the 2022 Chishang Earthquake Sequence
tk: A new three-component baseline correction method for strong-motion data successfully extracts near-fault effects, including permanent displacements and velocity pulses, from the 2022 Chishang earthquake sequence.
提出一种三分量强震动基线校正新方法，成功提取了2022年池上地震序列的近断层效应。
papers.ab: Accurately characterizing near-fault ground motions, particularly permanent tectonic displacements and velocity pulses associated with rupture directivity, is essential for seismic hazard assessment and infrastructure design. However, conventional ground-motion processing can distort or remove these characteristics. This study extends existing baseline correction methods by synchronously processing all three components of strong-motion recordings to preserve near-fault effects. The proposed methodology is applied to 59 recordings from the 2022 M 6.5 Guanshan foreshock and M 6.9 Chishang mainshock in Taiwan. Comparison with nearby Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations demonstrates that the method reliably captures the amplitude and orientation of permanent tectonic displacements. Analysis of the processed recordings reveals pronounced velocity pulses and permanent displacements, with the largest peak-to-peak velocities concentrated along the direction of rupture propagation. A classification framework is also introduced to distinguish fling-step pulses from dynamic velocity pulses. The results indicate that fling-step pulses typically occur early in the ground shaking, whereas dynamic pulses span a broader temporal range. Furthermore, the spatial distribution and orientation of near-fault effects are consistent with bridge damage documented during post-earthquake reconnaissance. The resulting dataset provides ground-motion time histories that preserve near-fault characteristics for seismic hazard assessment and engineering applications.

papers.t: Controls on the deformation and reorientation of mafic enclaves during magma mingling: A computational study
tk: Level-Set simulations of mafic enclave deformation show that enclave shape reflects the flow regime rather than directly measuring finite strain.
模拟表明岩浆混合中基性包体形状反映流体机制而非直接测量有限应变。
papers.ab: Mafic microgranular enclaves in granitic plutons record magma mingling, and their shapes are often interpreted as a record of the flow that deformed them. We investigate how a dense, low-viscosity droplet deforms in a lighter, much more viscous host under shear and gravity, using 96 two-dimensional Level-Set simulations. The viscosity ratio ($μ_r$) spans $10^{-6}$ - $10^{-3}$, the capillary number ($\mathrm{Ca}$) ranges from $10^{6}$ to $8\times10^{9}$, the Bond number ($\mathrm{Bo}$) takes values of $3.5\times10^{6}$ and $9.8\times10^{6}$, and the Reynolds number ($\mathrm{Re}$) remains below $10^{-2}$, with a fixed density contrast ($Δρ$) of $400~\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Two broad regimes identified- sinking and non-sinking which spread over six outcomes like sinking, edge, mid and multiple break-up, rotation, and retraction. The ratio $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$ separates sinking from shear-dominated behaviour near unity, although the transition spans a range of $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$ values that shifts with confinement. In the shear-dominated regime, a lower viscosity ratio promotes stretching. Multiple pinch-off occurs mainly at viscosity ratios of $10^{-6}$ - $10^{-5}$, rotation occurs only at the higher vertical confinement, and retraction occurs only at the lower vertical confinement. The strain at maximum stretch averages 1.1 - 1.4 and increases with $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$, with a stronger increase at higher confinement. The orientation of the major axis decreases by approximately $10^\circ$ per unit strain and is lowest for rotating droplets. Because the capillary number exceeds conventional critical values for breakup for droplets, breakup is interpreted in terms of accumulated deformation rather than capillary stability alone. Enclave shape therefore reflects the flow regime and is not a direct measure of finite strain.

papers.t: Amplified transport variability in granular slope flows near the critical angle
tk: Numerical simulations show that granular transport variability is highly amplified near the critical angle, requiring stochastic models to capture the wide distribution of outcomes.
数值模拟表明，临界角附近的颗粒坡面流输运变率显著放大。
papers.ab: Mechanical disturbances such as seismic shaking can set a granular slope in motion. Understanding the resulting transport before arrest is important for predicting topographic change, assessing landslide hazards and controlling powder flows in industrial processes. Experiments show that smaller disturbances can trigger avalanches and larger areas are mobilized as slopes approach their stability limit. Yet how much transport varies between events under the same macroscopic conditions and forcing remains unclear. Here we use numerical simulations to show that transport variability is amplified near the critical angle. We apply identical basal pulses to static granular layers with the same macroscopic conditions but different initial particle configurations. Although the mean transport increases approximately in inverse proportion to the angular distance from the critical angle, the standard deviation increases even faster and can exceed the mean. Thus, identical forcing can produce widely different transport amounts. Deterministic constitutive laws that assign a unique response to given macroscopic conditions cannot capture this variability. We introduce fluctuations into the energy balance to develop a stochastic model that captures the main features of the broadening transport distribution. These results show that assessing transport near the critical angle requires considering its distribution, not just its mean, and motivate constitutive descriptions that incorporate fluctuations.

papers.t: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for rapid pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting: the case of Forlì, Italy
tk: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator (GINO) surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP enables rapid, accurate pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting and ensemble simulations.
基于几何信息神经算子的代理模型实现了快速高精度的洪涝预测。
papers.ab: Physically based two-dimensional hydraulic models are too slow for real-time inundation forecasting and large ensembles. We present a time-dependent geometry-informed neural operator (GINO) surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for the municipality of Forlì (Italy), severely affected by the May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods. The surrogate is designed for an operational setting in which only river stage gauges and rain gauges are available. A reproducible pipeline turns public regional observations into a physically based training set: each river inflow is driven by the first stage gauge downstream of it through a calibrated water-surface boundary condition, and rain enters as SCS-CN effective rainfall. The surrogate is an autoregressive GINO trained on 216 simulations of 24 observed events with scaled forcing. It predicts volume-conserving polygon-mean depths on an exposure-based Voronoi mesh of 659 nodes, with a 20 min step over 72 h. The surrogate is tested on 38 independent observed events that it never saw during training. On these events it reaches a critical success index (CSI) of 0.934 at 0.05m and 0.844 at 0.3 m, a depth RMSE of 0.008m and an $R^2$ of 0.984 for maximum-depth maps. On one NVIDIA A10G GPU a 72-h forecast takes 1.7 s instead of 55 s with LISFLOOD-FP, and a 50-member ensemble, computed in a single batched rollout, takes 6.2 s instead of about 46 min, which makes probabilistic flood forecasting practical. These results show that neural-operator surrogates can deliver accurate pluvial-fluvial flood forecasts driven by river stage for operational early warning.

papers.t: Combining Seismic Scalograms and Phase Detection Probabilities to Improve Generalization of Deep Learning Classification of Local Explosions and Earthquakes
in: Department of Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences, Rice University, Houston, Texas, U.S.A.
Department of Earth Science and Environmental Change, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, Illinois, U.S.A.
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, California, U.S.A.
tk: Combining seismic scalograms with phase detection probabilities in a two-branch CNN improves the generalization of local earthquake and explosion classification across different regions.
结合地震时频图与震相检测概率的双分支CNN提高了本地地震与爆炸分类的泛化能力。
papers.ab: Deep learning models can help mitigate the need for analyst intervention in seismic classification of local earthquake and explosion signals, but optimizing model performance across multiple localities is challenging. Here, we seek to advance multilocality classification through hyperparameter optimization, evaluation of training data selection, and incorporation of phase pick probabilities from a pre-existing deep learning model into the new source type classification models. One-branch and two-branch convolutional neural network model designs are tested with 16 local data sets, each containing earthquakes and shallow borehole explosions observed by the same receivers. The one-branch model uses a conventional input of time–frequency scalograms and the two-branch model adds vector inputs of P-wave and S-wave probabilities output from a pre-existing phase picking model, which are increasingly available in modern event detection workflows. Hyperparameters for the one- and two-branch models were optimized by a guided search algorithm. For in-distribution data tests spanning all 16 data sets, the two-branch model’s single-station balanced accuracy (95.7%) slightly outperforms the one-branch model (94.7%). In addition, the optimized two-branch model is simpler, with about half as many model parameters and faster convergence in training. Relative performance of the two-branch model increases for out-of-distribution tests (using a locality held out from training), with an average increase in single-station balanced accuracy from 84.4% to 87.6% across 16 held out localities. The two-branch model also substantially outperforms P/S amplitude ratio discrimination accuracy by 14% on average for out-of-distribution tests. The results suggest that the added context from phase detection probabilities, which are a common by-product of event catalog building, can provide an efficient means to improve generalization of event-type classification models when applied to new regions.

papers.t: Time for an Updated Macroseismic Scale
in: United States Geological Survey
Applied Technology Council
Natural Resources Canada
University of British Columbia
University of Victoria
Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction
Global Earthquake Model
tk: This paper advocates for replacing outdated macroseismic scales like MMI with the modern International Macroseismic Scale of 2025 (IMS-25).
本文呼吁使用现代的2025国际烈度表（IMS-25）取代陈旧的麦加利地震烈度表。
papers.ab: We believe that macroseismic scales are not static, but they should instead be updated based on new experimental observations."-Tosi et al. (2015) Macroseismology plays a crucial role in earthquake hazard and risk analyses, linking past earthquake occurrences and impacts with those of the present and future.The popularity of internet-based community contributions and the use of intensities for communicating seismic hazards, early warning, and impacts to the public have all bolstered the use of macroseismology beyond its traditional utility in characterizing sources and shaking from historical and modern earthquakes (Wald et al., 2023).Nevertheless, many modern approaches for collecting building damage data and assigning macroseismic intensities suffer limitations.Many countries do not or no longer routinely collect such data, and even after significant and catastrophic earthquakes, building damage data are often not collected or shared systematically, nor are field-based macroseismic intensities professionally assigned.Here, we describe how the International Macroseismic Scale of 2025 (IMS-25, Grünthal et al., 2026) could be used to replace other macroseismic intensity scales.For example, the United States, Canada, and other nations still use variations of the modified Mercalli intensity (MMI) scale (Wood and Neumann, 1931) for assigning macroseismic intensities.At nearly 100 yr old, the MMI scale predates most modern building types.It says nothing about single-or multiunit wood-frame buildings, the predominant type of residential structure in the United States and Canada, whose damage is a particularly important indicator of shaking intensity.Reliance on the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) "Did You Feel It?" (DYFI; Quitoriano and Wald, 2020) for domestic intensity data collection limits its accuracy at higher, damaging intensity levels, where attention to building type is requisite.The MMI and some of its widely used variants are often poorly documented; there is neither an official version, nor is it even clear which version of the scale was employed in many studies (Musson et al., 2010;Musson and Cecić, 2002).The MMI scale is consistent with-but is more limited than-the 1998 European Macroseismic Scale (EMS-98, Grünthal, 1998).The new IMS-25 (Grünthal et al., 2026) builds on EMS-98-a well-documented, modern scale already widely used in Europe and well beyond.Those currently employing EMS-98 need not 1.U.

papers.t: Strategies for Multiscale Seismic Monitoring in Alaska
in: Alaska Earthquake Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, Alaska, U.S.A.
Now at, Departmnet of Earth, Environmental and Planetary Science, Rice University, Houston, Texas, U.S.A.
tk: The Alaska Earthquake Center rebuilt its acquisition and processing systems using parallel cloud/on-premises infrastructure and multi-scale association pipelines to balance real-time response and catalog quality.
阿拉斯加地震中心重建了其数据获取与处理系统，通过云端/本地双轨制和多尺度关联管线平衡实时响应与编目质量。
papers.ab: Earthquake monitoring balances competing demands. Organizations must track small-scale seismicity visible on perhaps just a handful of sensors while assessing large earthquakes recorded globally. They must deliver authoritative information within seconds, while curating a research-grade catalog over decades. They need to remain operational precisely when communications, power, or cloud infrastructure may be degraded. These challenges are in tension and are particularly acute in Alaska. The region comprises 5%–10% of global seismicity. Station spacing varies by two orders of magnitude. Earthquake depths range from above sea level to below 200 km. A substantial fraction of seismicity occurs offshore and is essentially out of network. In late 2025, the Alaska Earthquake Center completed a ground-up rebuild of our acquisition, analysis, and product dissemination systems. We address the challenges above with a series of major design choices. Parallel on-premises and cloud-based deployments provide mostly independent paths for producing information. Detection algorithms are tuned to capture the full range of phase arrivals, whether they originate in our mission region or elsewhere in the world. Multiple association pipelines accommodate the wide range of station densities and tolerances for latent data. Together, they handle teleseismic earthquakes that spread arrivals across the region, routine in-state events, and in-state earthquakes large enough to benefit from using data from far outside our area of responsibility. Finally, we balance response time and event quality with a catalog workflow that allows the highest-quality real-time solutions to be published automatically, while lesser-quality events are held for review by the on-call seismologist, or for postprocessing during the final steps of catalog curation. Though our implementation is tailored to Alaska and remains a work in progress, our hope is that these strategies can help inform networks facing similar competing demands.

papers.t: Seismic study of soda straws exposed to nearby blasting vibrations
tk: Shorter soda straw stalactites are more vulnerable to high-frequency blasting vibrations than longer ones due to resonance, requiring a strict peak particle velocity limit.
共振使短钟乳石更易受爆破破坏，需设定2.4mm/s的振动阈值。
papers.ab: This study aims to protect an exceptional population of soda straw stalactites from vibrations generated by nearby rock blasting activities. The Choranche Cave, located in the Vercors region of France, hosts thousands of remarkably slender soda straws, reaching several meters in length while measuring approximately 0.5 cm in diameter. These speleothems are particularly susceptible to vibrations because of their structural fragility and potential for dynamic amplification. Our analyses revealed that their fundamental natural frequencies fall within the frequency range of nearby blasting-induced vibrations, typically spanning tens to hundreds of hertz. To assess the effects of blasting, we combined in situ vibration measurements, laboratory-based material characterization, and dynamic two-dimensional finite element simulations to estimate the loads experienced by the soda straw population. The results indicate that resonance can amplify the induced loads by a factor of five. Consequently, shorter soda straws (0.1--1 m) were found to be more vulnerable to blasting-induced vibrations than longer speleothems (>1 m), despite the greater weight and inertial forces associated with the latter. Based on simulations of several blasting tests, we established an allowable peak particle velocity (PPV) threshold of 2.4 mm/s within the cave. Subsequent blasting operations were conducted in compliance with this limit, successfully protecting the soda straw population from damage. We also investigated the dynamic response of soda straws to regional earthquakes. In contrast to blasting-induced vibrations, the lower-frequency content of earthquake ground motions preferentially excites resonance in longer speleothe

papers.t: Mapping rockfall hazard and detecting precursory damage in rock slopes with passive seismic: Lessons from the La Praz case-study
tk: Passive seismic monitoring using HVSR amplitude and peak-frequency variations successfully characterized rockfall hazards and detected precursory damage before a major slope collapse.
利用HVSR振幅和峰值频率变化进行被动源地震监测，成功预警了岩崩灾害并检测到崩塌前的先兆损伤。
papers.ab: Repeated passive seismic surveys were conducted over more than a decade on the unstable La Praz rock slope in Savoie, France, which involved an estimated rock volume of approximately 13,000--15,000 m${}^3$. The final survey took place two months before the complete collapse of the slope in August 2023. The amplitude of the Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratio at the peak frequency (*aHVSR(fp)*) was used to distinguish stable and unstable areas and identify fractures associated with significant mechanical decoupling. Rock compartments were also classified according to their rockfall hazard. The compartments most susceptible to failure exhibited the highest *aHVSR(fp)* values, ranging from 26 to 157, compared with values of 7.5--19 in intermediate-hazard areas and 2.7 in the adjacent stable rock mass. The main HVSR peak frequency (*fp*) exhibited distinct decreases of 15%, 14%, and 11% in three unstable rock compartments before the collapse. These reductions substantially exceeded the range of environmentally induced resonance-frequency fluctuations observed at the site and commonly reported in the literature as a limitation of this method. The frequency decreases were interpreted as indicators of progressive damage extending into the rock slope. Notably, these changes were detected exclusively in the three compartments identified as the most susceptible to failure, which also exhibited the highest *aHVSR(fp)* values. This study demonstrates, for the first time, the potential of passive seismic monitoring to reveal progressive in-depth damage within a complex, heterogeneous, and highly fractured rock slope. The findings highlight the value of combining HVSR amplitude and peak-frequency variations to characterize unstable rock compartments and identify potential precursors to catastrophic slope failure.

papers.t: Damage Assessment of Supporting Pillars in an Underground Cave Using Joint Inversion of Electrical Resistivity and P-wave Velocity, Burgundy (France)
tk: Joint inversion of electrical resistivity and P-wave velocity improves the spatial resolution and consistency of damage assessment for underground cave supporting pillars.
联合反演电阻率与P波速度，提升了地下洞穴支柱损伤评估分辨率。
papers.ab: This study presents an integrated approach combining seismic refraction tomography and electrical resistivity tomography to evaluate the structural integrity of supporting pillars in an underground cave in Burgundy, France. A three-phase petrophysical joint inversion (P-JIv) was performed using a finite-element model on an unstructured triangular mesh. Compared with independent inversions, the joint inversion improved spatial resolution and enhanced the consistency between the two geophysical methods. The results revealed distinct zones of electrical resistivity and P-wave velocity, reflecting variations in rock fracturing and weathering. The geophysical interpretations showed strong agreement with visual inspections and borehole logs. Furthermore, rock porosity and water content were estimated from the P-JIv results. Finally, an automated clustering procedure was used to establish a proxy indicator of pillar integrity, enabling the prioritization of cave reinforcement measures.

papers.t: Original Insights Into Rock Slope Damage Processes Until Collapse From Passive Seismic Monitoring
tk: Passive seismic monitoring of a rock slope reveals a 24% decrease in resonance frequency before collapse, highlighting alternating brittle damage and ductile sliding phases.
对岩体滑坡的微震监测发现崩塌前共振频率下降24%，揭示了脆性损伤与塑性滑移的交替演化。
papers.ab: We conducted passive seismic monitoring of the unstable La Praz rock slope (approximately 14,000 m${}^3$) in the French Alps over a period of more than 10 years. During the six months preceding collapse, we observed a pronounced 24% decrease in the slope's fundamental resonance frequency ((f\_0)), indicating a reduction in the overall stiffness of the rock mass. Joint analysis of (f\_0) variations and slope deformation revealed alternating phases dominated by sudden brittle damage and more ductile behavior, potentially involving sliding. Seismic monitoring identified damage processes that were either ambiguous or undetectable through surface deformation measurements alone, while also highlighting critical periods of intensified damage. Although some of these periods coincided with identifiable external triggers, such as intense rainfall events, others could not be clearly linked to external forcing. These findings demonstrate the potential of passive seismic monitoring to provide insights into the internal structural condition of unstable rock slopes at depth. Combining surface deformation measurements with seismic tracking of rock mass stiffness could therefore improve the identification and characterization of active slopes undergoing progressive damage, contributing to the development of more effective slope monitoring systems.

papers.t: Nonergodic Path Effects from 3D Ground-Motion Simulations of an M 8 Ryukyu Earthquake in Eastern Taiwan
in: Earthquake Disaster & Risk Evaluation and Management Center (E-DREaM), National Central University, Taoyuan, Taiwan
Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of California, Berkeley, California, U.S.A.
Department of Civil Engineering, National Chung Hsing University, Taichung, Taiwan
tk: 3D finite-difference simulations of a potential M 8 Ryukyu earthquake reveal that rupture directivity, velocity, and 3D crustal structures control nonergodic path effects in eastern Taiwan.
三维有限差分模拟表明，破裂方向性、速度和三维地壳结构控制着台湾东部的非各态历经路径效应。
papers.ab: The Ryukyu subduction zone offshore eastern Taiwan possesses significant seismogenic potential, exemplified by the 1920 earthquake. However, the scarcity of near-field observations leaves the ground-motion characteristics of such mega-earthquakes poorly constrained, limiting the reliability of seismic hazard assessments. This study investigates long-period ground-motion characteristics of a potential M 8 Ryukyu earthquake using large-scale 3D ground-motion simulations. We simulated an M 8 scenario earthquake using characterized source models based on the “Recipe” procedure and conducted 3D finite-difference simulations for 192 source–velocity-model combinations, incorporating variations in hypocenter location, rupture velocity, asperity distribution, two tomographic velocity models, and topography. Varying the Gaussian source time function (STF) duration in postprocessing expands the dataset to 1728 scenarios. Synthetic waveforms were generated at 4950 virtual stations, producing more than 8.5 million synthetic ground-motion records, and analyzed using RotD50 spectral accelerations (SAs) at periods of 1.0, 3.0, and 5.0 s. Results indicate that rupture directivity and rupture velocity dominate the spatial variability of long-period ground motions, with parameter sensitivity exhibiting strong spatial nonuniformity across the study region. Calibration against the empirical CH20 ground-motion model (GMM) suggests Gaussian STFs of 2, 6, and 8 s provide the most consistent spectral representation for SA at 1.0, 3.0, and 5.0 s, respectively. The nonergodic path terms (δP2P) derived from two alternative velocity models, which capture the path effects of the deep 3D structure (VS≥2.4 km/s), reveal spatially consistent features, including a persistent amplification zone near Hualien linked to the Longitudinal Valley low-velocity structure, a deamplification belt along the Coastal Range and Central Range high-velocity material, and a frequency-dependent amplification in the Ilan Plain attributable to deeper crustal focusing or trapping rather than near-surface site effects. The workflow established here provides a transferable framework for refining GMMs and advancing nonergodic seismic hazard assessments in data-sparse subduction environments.

papers.t: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
tk: DeepWaveRL introduces a self-supervised reinforcement learning framework for full-waveform inversion that optimizes velocity models using only scalar rewards, bypassing forward operator gradients.
DeepWaveRL提出了一种自监督强化学习框架，仅利用标量奖励优化全波形反演，无需前向算子梯度。
papers.ab: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. A global scalar reward is computed based on data misfit for each prediction and used to weight policy gradients. Thus, learning proceeds without accessing the gradients from the forward operator. Given the indirect and coarse supervision signals, we further identify key strategies to stabilize learning and mitigate the spatial credit assignment bottleneck. Experimental results show that, despite relying entirely on a single scalar reward, DeepWaveRL achieves competitive performance compared to supervised and self-supervised baselines. These findings suggest that our framework offers a flexible and complementary learning paradigm for the FWI research community.

papers.t: Unraveling Stress and Energy Variations Through Spectral Analysis of Seismic Sources in the East Anatolian Fault Zone (Türkiye)
in: Department of Earth, Environmental and Life Sciences - DISTAV, University of Genoa, Genoa, Italy
Helmholtz Center for Geoscience - GFZ, Potsdam, Germany
National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics – OGS, Trieste, Italy
Physics Department “Ettore Pancini”, University of Naples Federico II, Naples, Italy
tk: Spectral decomposition of ~10,000 earthquakes along the East Anatolian Fault Zone reveals self-similar scaling and distinct spatial patterns of stress-drop and scaled-energy anomalies.
对东安纳托利亚断裂带约万次地震的谱分解表明，应力降与辐射能量异常呈现出不同的空间分布特征。
papers.ab: We present a spectral decomposition applied to nearly 10,000 earthquakes (ML 2.0–5.5) recorded along the East Anatolian Fault Zone (EAFZ) between January 2019 and February 2024, focusing on spatial and temporal variations in source parameters surrounding the 6 February 2023 seismic doublet. Results indicate that M0–fc scaling is consistent with approximate self-similarity, with nearly constant stress drop Δσ across the analyzed magnitude range. The observed linear relationship between M0 and radiated energy Er demonstrates the internal consistency of the estimated source parameters, although this relationship alone should not be interpreted as evidence of stable energy partitioning. Despite the structural segmentation of the EAFZ, Δσ remains statistically similar across the Nurdağı and Sürgü segments, indicating no clear segment-scale difference in Δσ within the analyzed dataset. To investigate spatial variations across fault segments, we examined normalized stress-drop and scaled-energy anomalies (Δσ* and E˜r*, respectively) as proxies for mechanical heterogeneity and scaled radiated energy. Δσ* exhibits relatively smooth spatial variations, whereas E˜r* shows more localized variability. These distinct spatial patterns may reflect differences in the sensitivity of the two parameters to stress conditions and local structural or mechanical heterogeneities. Our results indicate that small-magnitude earthquakes encode meaningful insights into fault segmentation and stress evolution, providing a multiscale perspective on rupture mechanics. These observations can enable detailed segment-level analyses and offer a transferable framework applicable to other tectonically complex fault systems, improving our understanding of earthquake physics and mechanical heterogeneity in strike-slip environments.

papers.t: Teleseismic P -Wave Attenuation Along the East African Rift System: Strong Attenuation Within the Main Ethiopian Rift
in: Sustainable Earth Systems Science, University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson, Texas, U.S.A.
School of Earth and Sustainability, Northern Arizona University, Flagstaff, Arizona, U.S.A.
Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, University of California, Riverside, Riverside, California, U.S.A.
Now at, EarthScope Consortium, Washington, D.C., U.S.A.
tk: Teleseismic P-wave attenuation along the East African Rift reveals strong attenuation localized to the Main Ethiopian Rift, suggesting a thin layer of partial melt.
沿东非裂谷的远震P波衰减测量显示强衰减局限于埃塞俄比亚主裂谷，表明存在局部熔融薄层。
papers.ab: Remarkably strong anomalies in seismic properties of the mantle beneath the East African rift are plausibly explained by elevated mantle potential temperatures and/or the presence of partial melt. Previous studies have attributed strong attenuation to elevated temperatures that possibly extend as deep as the mantle transition zone. Although petrologic work clearly infers elevated temperatures, the ∼140°C anomaly is less than at many other hotspots. The anomalies in seismic velocity are stronger than can be explained by this modest excess in temperature, and hence additional mechanisms such as melt are often invoked. We measure the attenuation of a large dataset of teleseismic P phases stretching from the Arabian Platform to the Kaapvaal craton to constrain the nature of seismic anomalies beneath this plate boundary. Anomalies in attenuation are modest along our nearly 6000 km long profile, with the strong exception of the Main Ethiopian Rift (MER). We show that the anomalies in seismic velocity and attenuation beneath the Afar Depression and MER are jointly explained best by a relatively thin layer of high attenuation, akin to other regions of rifting, which we attribute to either “pre-melting” relaxation or an effect of an in situ melt phase. Because our data are path-integrated, thickness and QP trade off directly, and a thicker, more weakly attenuating region spread over hundreds of kilometers is an admissible end member. The opposite occurs further south—rifting occurs along the edges of the Tanzania craton and beneath Lake Malawi without strong attenuation, including beneath the Turkana Depression where the asthenosphere conditions must differ from the MER.

papers.t: Deep Learning-Based Probabilistic Earthquake Forecasting Along the Tan-Lu Fault Zone Using Multiparameter Seismicity Features
in: China Earthquake Networks Center, Beijing, China
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China
Institute of Earthquake Forecasting, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China
China University of Geosciences, Beijing, China
tk: A deep learning framework using probability-transformed seismicity parameters improves probabilistic earthquake risk-ranking along the Tan-Lu fault zone compared to raw parameters.
基于概率转换多参数地震活动性特征的深度学习框架提升了郯庐断裂带的地震风险排序预测能力。
papers.ab: Here, we develop a supervised framework for identifying probabilistic earthquake-risk states in the central and southern Tan-Lu fault zone and adjacent areas of eastern China using multiple catalog-derived seismicity features and a deep learning approach. Using the China Earthquake Networks Center catalog from 1979 to 2025, seven seismological parameters (b, M, η, D, Mf, N, and Rm) were calculated for ML≥2.0 earthquakes. These parameters were transformed into probability-based time-series features and used as inputs to an enhanced long short-term memory model with dual-task learning and dropout regularization. The model was trained using data from 1979 to 2020 and evaluated on an independent testing period from 2021 to 2025. Training was repeated using five predefined random seeds, and same-date predicted probabilities were averaged with equal weights. In the broad study area, the seven-parameter probability-transformed ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.650 and average precision (AP) = 0.297, compared with 0.535 and 0.258 for the raw-parameter ensemble; the no-skill AP baseline was 0.209. Input-feature ablation showed that the full seven-parameter model outperformed models using N alone or N together with b. Comparison with an epidemic-type aftershock sequence model indicated that the relative performance of statistical and data-driven models depends strongly on the forecasting task. Although elevated scores were not restricted to labeled pre-earthquake windows and the separation between positive and negative score distributions weakened in the independent test period, the continuous scores retained some ranking information. Accordingly, the model output is interpreted as a continuous risk-ranking score rather than as a deterministic forecast of earthquake occurrence on any specific date. Probability-based representations of multiple catalog-derived seismicity parameters, combined with deep temporal modeling, may provide a useful complementary approach to regional identification of pre-earthquake risk windows.

papers.t: Characterizing landslide dynamics from time-lapse time domain induced polarization and ground-based imaging: a case study of the MontGombert landslide (French, Alps)
tk: Combining time-lapse induced polarization with electrical resistivity tomography effectively delineates unstable landslide volumes and estimates seasonal permeability variations.
结合时序激发极化与电阻率成像可有效圈定滑坡并估算渗透率变化。
papers.ab: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) is widely used to investigate landslide morphology and dynamics. Landslide behavior is strongly influenced by clay content, pore pressure, and the spatial distribution of permeability. However, conventional direct current (DC) resistivity methods have limited capacity to characterize permeability, as materials with low electrical resistivity may exhibit either high or low permeability depending on their clay content and the relative contributions of surface and electrolytic conduction. Induced polarization (IP) offers a valuable complementary approach for investigating the petrophysical properties of geological materials. Despite its potential, IP has been rarely applied to landslide studies and has not yet been widely used for landslide monitoring. This study investigates the added value of IP measurements alongside conventional DC resistivity for landslide characterization and monitoring. Three time-domain induced polarization (TDIP) surveys were conducted at different time steps on an active landslide in the French Alps. Time-lapse inversions of resistivity and chargeability were performed, and spectral IP parameters were derived using Debye decomposition. The results were then compared with surface displacement estimates obtained from optical image processing. The findings demonstrate that TDIP is particularly valuable for delineating unstable volumes within the landslide. The geophysical results show strong agreement with independent measurements from piezometers and inclinometers. Furthermore, applying an empirical relationship between IP parameters and permeability enables the spatial distribution of permeability within the landslide to be estimated, as well as its seasonal variations. Overall, this study highlights the potential of combining IP and DC resistivity measurements to improve the characterization of landslide properties and support the monitoring of their temporal evolution.

papers.t: A spatial autocorrelation method for estimating Rayleigh-wave attenuation coefficients from microtremor array measurements
tk: A new spatial autocorrelation (SPAC) method estimates Rayleigh-wave attenuation coefficients from microtremor array measurements using an attenuation-aware formulation and a heptagonal array.
提出一种基于衰减感知空间自相关（SPAC）和七边形台阵估算微动瑞利波衰减系数的方法。
papers.ab: The velocity and attenuation structures of near-surface soils play an important role in controlling earthquake ground motions. While numerous passive techniques have been developed for estimating velocity structure, practical methods for estimating attenuation from microtremor array measurements remain limited. We developed a spatial autocorrelation (SPAC) method for estimating Rayleigh-wave attenuation coefficients using an attenuation-aware formulation of the SPAC coefficient. A theoretical analysis of directional aliasing showed that attenuation estimation requires denser azimuthal sampling than conventional phase-velocity estimation, motivating the use of a regular heptagonal array. The method uses a two-stage procedure in which initial estimates of phase velocity and the attenuation coefficient are obtained using a first-order approximation and then refined by fitting the complex SPAC coefficient. Synthetic data analyses demonstrated that the proposed method can recover attenuation coefficients under ideal conditions and clarified how directional aliasing, record length and sensitivity to attenuation affect the estimates. Comparison with a beamforming-based method showed that the proposed method is less sensitive to wavefield directionality and can be applied at longer wavelengths relative to the array size. The method was further validated using microtremor-like waveforms generated by independent P--SV wave-propagation simulations. Finally, a preliminary application to field microtremor records yielded attenuation coefficients that were broadly consistent across array sizes and with values expected from existing empirical attenuation relationships. These results demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method to passive estimation of Rayleigh-wave attenuation.

papers.t: Environmental seismology: What can we learn on earth surface processes with ambient noise?
tk: A comprehensive review of environmental seismology demonstrating how ambient seismic noise can monitor subsurface thermal variations, groundwater levels, and landslide stability.
本文综述了利用背景噪声监测地下温度、水位及滑坡稳定性的进展。
papers.ab: Environmental seismology investigates mechanical vibrations generated by external processes or influenced by phenomena originating outside the solid Earth. It encompasses interactions between the solid Earth and other environmental systems, including the cryosphere, hydrosphere, and anthroposphere, as well as the specific sources of seismic vibrations associated with these systems. This field also examines how environmental factors, such as temperature fluctuations and hydrological variations, affect seismic wave propagation. Recent advances in data-processing techniques, combined with increased computational capabilities and the growing density of seismic sensor networks, have enabled novel observations and contributed to the emergence of environmental seismology as a distinct research field. This article reviews how subtle changes in the Earth's subsurface can be detected and interpreted through variations in seismic wave propagation induced by external environmental processes, with applications to geomechanics, hydrology, and natural hazard assessment. In particular, we demonstrate how ambient seismic noise can be used to monitor: (1) thermal variations in the subsurface, within buildings, and in rock columns; (2) the temporal and spatial evolution of groundwater levels; and (3) changes in the rigidity of the material forming a landslide, with particular emphasis on the reduction in rigidity that may precede slope failure.

papers.t: Complex slab geometry related to multiple intermediate-depth seismicity clusters in NW South America
in: Industrial University of Santander
Universidad Nacional de Colombia
tk: Relocated intermediate-depth seismicity in northwestern South America reveals a highly complex slab geometry and multiple distinct earthquake clusters.
重新定位的西北南美洲中源地震揭示了复杂的板块几何结构及多个地震群。

papers.t: A stochastic sampling-filtering framework for probabilistic reconstruction of paleo-earthquake ruptures
in: Institute of Geophysics China Earthquake Administration, No.5,, Minzu University South Road, Haidian District,, Beijing, China [CN]
tk: A stochastic sampling-filtering framework probabilistically reconstructs paleo-earthquake ruptures from sparse geological data, accounting for non-unique timing and geometry.
该研究提出了一种随机采样-过滤框架，用于从稀疏地质观测中概率性地重建古地震破裂。
papers.ab: Reconstructing paleo-earthquake ruptures from sparse geological observations is inherently non-unique because evidence of past surface ruptures is commonly preserved only at isolated sites. We develop a stochastic sampling-filtering framework that represents this ambiguity as an ensemble of rupture scenarios consistent with geological, chronological, and mapped fault constraints. Candidate ruptures are sampled in timing, center position, and length and retained only when they satisfy these constraints. Applied to the Yanzhi Shan Fault, the framework identifies eight rupture-age density modes and a persistent southeastward trend in the spatial density of admissible ruptures. Criteria-based enumeration yields broadly similar first-order temporal concentrations, while prior-sensitivity tests show that filtering reduces differences among ensembles generated from contrasting priors. These results indicate constraint-induced convergence rather than prior-distribution independence. The framework therefore extracts observation-supported statistical rupture patterns while preserving uncertainty associated with non-unique rupture timing and geometry.

papers.t: The Thermodynamic Limit of Asthenospheric Circulation: The Characteristic Timescale of Plate Tectonics
in: Independent Researcher, Unknown, Xuchang, Henan, China [CN]
tk: The paper proposes a thermodynamic, kinematic, and dynamic framework showing that plate tectonics timescales converge to ~280 Myr, anchored by the dry peridotite solidus.
本文提出热力学、运动学和动力学框架，证明板块构造特征时间尺度收敛于约2.8亿年。
papers.ab: This paper proposes that the peridotite solidus (about 1300°C, dry conditions) is the thermodynamic anchor and negative-feedback target of plate tectonics. To distinguish different physical quantities, we define a thermally equivalent thickness to be heated, km; a kinematic return-channel thickness, km; and a dynamic effective return thickness, . Using and a mantle heat flux of about 0.07 W/m² as inputs, the thermodynamic path yields 282.5 Myr (baseline km; about 263–282.5 Myr for 80–100 km, all on the order of 2.6–2.8 × 10⁸ yr); the kinematic path yields about 278 Myr (thickness ratio about 1:2.5; if the more conservative 1:2 is used, 222 Myr, a lower-bound estimate biased short). The standard dynamic estimate is 233.6 Myr (global mean trench–ridge distance km; trench–ridge horizontal temperature difference K). The 600 K corresponds to about 700°C at the trench and about 1300°C at the mid-ocean ridge; it is the maximum temperature difference when the trench temperature is at its lower limit, so 233.6 Myr is a lower-bound estimate biased short. After confining-pressure correction by the overlying lithosphere, the dynamic estimate is about 283 Myr (confining-pressure factor , Pa·s; rounding to 1.77 gives about Pa·s, which does not affect the conclusion). If a high-end member within the literature range is adopted, the confining-corrected estimate is about 259 Myr, close to 282.5 Myr (about 8% lower) and near the lower edge of the 260–285 Myr convergence range. The three paths converge on about 260–285 Myr, centered at about 280 Myr; the standard dynamic value of 233.6 Myr and the kinematic 1:2 value of 222 Myr are lower bounds biased short. Using actual trench–ridge distances, the Pacific is about 318 Myr, Nazca about 179 Myr, Africa about 337 Myr, and South America about 300 Myr (standard viscosity); with confining-pressure correction, each plate time is multiplied by about 1.21. Asthenospheric viscosity is exponentially sensitive to temperature; the model implies that only about 20–50 K of temperature adjustment beneath each plate is needed for the circulation time to trend toward the statistical center of about 280 Myr. This adjustment is a theoretical mechanism hypothesis and is subject to dispersion from three-dimensional flow and other disturbances: about ±20–30 Myr within a single plate and about ±70–90 Myr as systematic differences between plates. The deviation output of the three-equation framework diagnoses four situations: shortened effective heating path (with lateral outflow), overdue retention, non-initiation of circulation, and three-dimensional flow. In reality, new trenches can be triggered incidentally on transform faults/fracture zones and truncate the original circulation; however, because the asthenosphere between the mid-ocean ridge and the trench has already been preheated, the ridge does not die immediately but enters a decay phase. Therefore, most systems do not complete even one full cycle, and a few complete at most two or three. Temperature (about 1300°C) is the invariant anchor; time (centered at about 280 Myr) is its response—the thermodynamic metronome of plate tectonics.

papers.t: Constraining incoming-plate upper mantle hydration at Cascadia, Alaska, and Nankai: distinguishing mineral-bound and free water using Vp and Vs
in: University of Oregon, 2272 Patterson St, Eugene, OR, Us
University of Oregon, 1272 University of Oregon, NULL, Eugene, United States [US]
University of Oregon, Unknown, Eugene, United States [US]
University of Oregon, 1272 Cascade Hall, Eugene, OR, United States [US]
tk: A new rock-physics framework uses joint Vp and Vs constraints to distinguish mineral-bound water from free water in subducting upper mantles.
利用Vp和Vs区分俯冲上地幔结合水与游离水的岩石物理框架。
papers.ab: Seismic velocity is widely used to estimate water stored in subducting upper mantle, but the same velocity reduction can result from very different combinations of serpentinization and fluid-filled porosity. We develop a rock-physics framework that treats serpentinization as modification of the solid matrix and crack porosity as a separate fluid reservoir, while explicitly accounting for uncertainty in crack geometry. For single Vp or Vs observations, absolute water contents remain strongly nonunique, whereas relative velocity differences provide more robust hydration contrasts. When Vp and Vs are available together, their combined behavior restricts the crack geometries that can explain the observations, providing stronger constraints on water partitioning. Applications to Cascadia, Alaska, and Nankai reveal substantial differences in how water is stored in the incoming mantle: propagator wakes in Cascadia are more hydrated than surrounding mantle; Semidi permits appreciable serpentinization, whereas Shumagin’s very low velocities require little serpentinization and only trace water in very thin cracks; and Nankai data are consistent with appreciable free water in thicker fractures with only moderate serpentinization. These results show that low mantle velocity does not uniquely imply high water content and that distinguishing structurally bound from crack-hosted water is important for assessing water transport into subduction zones.

papers.t: PKPPcP–PcPPKP Splitting: Observations, Modeling, and Implications for 3‐D Earth's Mantle Heterogeneity
in: School of Earth and Space Sciences University of Science and Technology of China Hefei China
Berkeley Seismological Laboratory Department of Earth and Planetary Science University of California Berkeley CA USA
State Key Laboratory of Geodesy and Earth's Dynamics Innovation Academy for Precision Measurement Science and Technology Chinese Academy of Sciences Wuhan China
tk: PKPPcP–PcPPKP splitting observations and numerical simulations reveal that current 3-D mantle tomography models underestimate deep mantle heterogeneities like LLVPs and subducted slabs.
PKPPcP-PcPPKP分裂观测与数值模拟表明，现有的三维地幔层析成像模型低估了LLVP和俯冲板块等深部地幔非均匀性。
papers.ab: Seismic body waves provide valuable insights into the interiors of the Earth, the Moon, and Mars. By analyzing their waveform characteristics, we can effectively reveal deep seismic velocity structures and associated dynamic processes. For the Earth, incorporating various body waves helps improve the ray path coverage and therefore the resolution of seismic imaging. For other planets with limited data, identifying seismic phases beyond the main P and S arrivals can provide critical insights into the picture of the deep interior. PKPPcP and PcPPKP phases propagate along the major arc of the great circle path, and are theoretically degenerate—arriving simultaneously—in a 1‐D spherical Earth model. Their splitting offers a unique opportunity to resolve 3‐D mantle heterogeneity, yet this potential remains under‐explored. Here we compile a global data set of high‐quality PKPPcP waves from 94 large events. Using PKKP ab as a reference phase, we quantify the observed PKPPcP–PcPPKP splitting and evaluate it against predictions from 3‐D mantle tomography models. Mantle tomography models generally underestimate the observed splitting, but the spatial correlation suggests that the observed splitting is linked to large‐scale structures in the deep mantle. We further analyze the features of PKPPcP travel time sensitivity kernels and conduct numerical simulations with various heterogeneous models. The simulations indicate that large‐scale velocity anomalies, such as large low‐velocity provinces and high‐velocity subducted slabs, are the primary contributors to PKPPcP–PcPPKP splitting. Our results highlight both the potential and the limitations of the PKPPcP phase in imaging 3‐D mantle heterogeneities.

papers.t: Missing Seismic Data Reconstruction Using Low‐Frequency Structure‐Guided 3D Diffusion
in: Key Laboratory of Earth Exploration and Information Technology of Ministry of Education, College of Geophysics Chengdu University of Technology Chengdu China
College of Geophysics Chengdu University of Technology Chengdu China
tk: A low-frequency structure-guided 3D conditional diffusion method is proposed to reconstruct missing 3D seismic data by combining low-frequency structural constraints with deep generative modeling.
提出一种低频结构引导的三维条件扩散方法，用于重建缺失的三维地震数据。
papers.ab: In field seismic acquisition, consecutively missing traces, local acquisition gaps and large‐scale sampling incompleteness commonly arise from complex near‐surface conditions, acquisition‐geometry constraints, receiver failures and field obstacles, which can degrade detailed imaging. Compared with scattered dead traces, consecutively missing traces interrupt the lateral coherence of reflection events over a wider spatial range, making event continuation, fault‐boundary continuity and thin‐bed response recovery more difficult. Conventional prediction filtering, transform‐domain interpolation and low‐rank completion methods usually rely on local linearity, sparsity or low‐rank assumptions. Under strongly nonstationary structures and wide missing‐trace bands, these assumptions can lead to oversmoothing, boundary mismatch and high‐frequency loss. Deep‐learning methods have improved the non‐linear representation capacity of reconstruction models, but slice‐wise 2D modelling does not fully exploit 3D spatial correlation, whereas existing 3D methods often suffer from high training cost, long sampling chains and insufficient stable structural constraints. To address these issues, we propose a low‐frequency structure‐guided 3D conditional diffusion method for seismic data reconstruction. The method first extracts stable low‐frequency components from an incomplete 3D seismic volume and completes the long‐wavelength structure within the missing‐trace band by combining 3D structure‐tensor dip estimation, event‐oriented low‐frequency interpolation and reliability‐weighted fusion. The completed low‐frequency volume preserves the dominant reflection geometry, long‐wavelength phase trend and 3D horizon distribution and is used as a structural condition for subsequent full‐band recovery. The reconstruction problem is then formulated as a 3D conditional diffusion process constrained by the low‐frequency structure, in which a 3D U‐Net denoiser progressively restores mid‐ and high‐frequency reflection details during reverse sampling. To adapt the model to the spatial organization of 3D seismic wavefields, the volumetric convolutional feature extractor supports an optional lightweight 3D attention module to strengthen local waveform information and structural associations across the missing‐trace band along the time, inline and crossline directions. The experiments include tests with consecutively missing traces using the SEG C3 synthetic data and a controlled test with artificially removed traces in a prepared field‐data volume. Ablation tests and comparisons with 3D tensor completion, slice‐wise 2D diffusion and 3D U‐Net show that the completed low‐frequency structural condition reduces the structural ambiguity inside missing‐trace bands and enables the diffusion model to recover high‐frequency details while preserving event continuity, phase consistency and amplitude compatibility. By combining low‐frequency structural modelling, 3D wavefield continuity and conditional posterior generation, the framework provides a feasible route for high‐fidelity reconstruction of seismic data with wide missing‐trace bands.
