papers.t: Deep structure and tectonic controls of the Majiaoba area inferred from gravity and magnetic data by multicriteria-evaluation-driven adaptive focusing inversion
in: College of geophysics 1 , , ,
tk: Gravity and magnetic inversions in the Majiaoba area reveal deep mafic intrusions, suggesting widespread Late Permian to Early Triassic magmatism along the western Yangtze Block.
重磁反演揭示马角坝地区深部基性侵入体，表明扬子地块西缘存在广泛的晚二叠世至早三叠世岩浆活动。
papers.ab: The Majiaoba area, on the northwestern margin of the Longmen Mountains within the Sichuan Basin, exposes a complete Silurian–Triassic succession. Silurian–Devonian strata are widespread, Carboniferous–Triassic formations are well developed, and metamorphic or igneous rocks are rarely exposed at the surface. With the exception of the weakly magnetic Lower Triassic Feixianguan Formation, most units are essentially nonmagnetic. Despite this, the region exhibits high-amplitude magnetic anomalies (up to approximately 10³ nT) whose genesis remains uncertain, and basin-scale magnetic highs in central–western Sichuan are commonly ascribed to rifting, even though their driving mechanisms and lateral continuity are debated. Two high-precision profiles across Majiaoba were acquired, and gravity and magnetic data sets were inverted independently using a minimum-support, adaptive iterative focusing algorithm selected under multicriteria evaluation, yielding high-resolution images of subsurface structure beneath both lines. Rock-magnetic measurements on Feixianguan samples, combined with the inversion results, revealed a pronounced vertical offset between the principal magnetic source and the surface-exposed reddish mudstone–shale of the Feixianguan Formation. Along profile L2, a closed high-susceptibility body was resolved at approximately 400–600 m depth. The anomaly pattern was inconsistent with a purely shallow sedimentary origin and was best explained by mafic (diabase) intrusions. At the regional scale, the deep magnetic source was interpreted as a product of sustained activity related to the large-scale magmatic episode along the western margin of the Yangtze Block during the Late Permian, with magmatism in the northern Longmen Mountain segment plausibly persisting into the Early Triassic (Feixianguan time). Considering gravity–magnetic anomaly patterns across northwestern Sichuan, the magmatic system was likely widespread rather than local in extent.

papers.t: Crustal and lithospheric mantle thinning variations beneath the East African Rift System
tk: The study reveals that lithospheric mantle necking precedes crustal necking along the East African Rift System, with varying decoupling between the eastern and western branches.
研究表明东非裂谷带的岩石圈地幔颈缩先于地壳颈缩，且东西分支呈现出不同的解耦特征。
papers.ab: Knowledge gaps remain regarding strain localization mechanisms that may initiate the transition to late-phase rifting and break-up along active rifts hosted in thick continental lithosphere. Here, we conduct a multiscale study of the East African Rift System (EARS) using one of the highest-resolution seismic tomography models of Africa, along with a comprehensive compilation of lithospheric structure models from active- and passive-source seismic studies. We estimate mantle temperatures and the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary using this model. Combined with estimated crustal thicknesses, we estimate the thinning factors of the crust and lithospheric mantle, as well as the deformation decoupling parameter, defined as the ratio of the lithospheric mantle to the crustal thinning factors. Our results reveal intriguing magnitudes of lithospheric mantle necking beneath both the eastern (magma-rich) and western (magma-poor) branches. However, the eastern branch ubiquitously exhibits commensurate crustal and lithospheric mantle thinning, whereas the western branch exhibits a complex mix of segments with coupled-thinning and those with significantly decoupled thinning. We note the key influence of inheritance, lithospheric foundering and delamination, and melt-induced ductile strain on decoupling of lithospheric thinning. The dearth of necked crust and the common occurrence of necked lithospheric mantle along the EARS suggest that necking of the lithospheric mantle probably precedes crustal necking along evolving rifts, which, where observed, manifest a weakened lithosphere primed to progressively transition to the later phases of continental extension.

papers.t: Quantifying Posterior Uncertainty in Array‐Based Surface Wave Tomography: A Hybrid Strategy Combining Bootstrap and Resolution Matrix
in: Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Exploration Technology Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
Department of the Earth and Space Sciences Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geophysical High‐resolution Imaging Technology Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
Qingdao Institute of Marine Geology China Geological Survey Qingdao China
tk: A hybrid uncertainty quantification strategy combining bootstrap resampling and resolution matrix correction is proposed to reliably estimate posterior uncertainties in array-based surface wave tomography.
提出一种结合自助法重采样与分辨率矩阵修正的混合不确定性量化策略，用于可靠评估阵列面波断层成像的后验不确定性。
papers.ab: Array‐based surface wave tomography has significantly enhanced the resolution of crustal imaging; however, rigorous quantification of posterior uncertainty in these regularized inversions remains a critical challenge. Conventional statistical methods, such as raw bootstrap resampling, often underestimate uncertainties in data‐sparse regions due to the dominance of regularization terms. This underestimation creates an artificial precision that risks misinterpreting inversion artifacts as robust structural features. To address this, we propose a hybrid uncertainty quantification strategy tailored for regional‐scale dense arrays, integrating data‐driven bootstrap resampling with model‐based resolution matrix correction. By utilizing the resolution matrix to explicitly debias the bootstrap variance, our approach provides a first‐order uncertainty metric for identifying and down‐weighting poorly constrained model estimates in the inversion's null‐space while retaining sensitivity to data inconsistencies in well‐resolved regions. We applied this workflow to ambient noise data from the ChinArray‐Himalaya project, extracting multimodal dispersion curves via the frequency‐Bessel (F‐J) transform. The derived hybrid uncertainty metric serves as a quantitative validity mask, successfully delineating reliable imaging regions for both fundamental and higher‐order modes, thereby facilitating objective, automated quality control for large‐scale data sets. Semi‐synthetic robustness tests further demonstrate that, unlike analytical or raw bootstrap methods, the hybrid strategy reliably distinguishes among data gaps (null‐spaces) and data conflicts. Ultimately, incorporating this resolution‐corrected uncertainty to weight subsequent 1D shear wave velocity inversions significantly suppresses regularization artifacts, laying a robust statistical foundation for constructing physically reliable 3D structural models.

papers.t: Do Shallow Slip Deficits Reflect Fault Structural Maturity or Modeling Choices? A Comparative Analysis of Tibetan Strike‐Slip Earthquakes
in: TRE ALTAMIRA Vancouver BC Canada
School of Earth and Ocean Sciences University of Victoria Victoria BC Canada
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting Institute of Geology China Earthquake Administration Beijing China
tk: This study evaluates whether shallow slip deficits in Tibetan strike-slip earthquakes are physical signatures of fault maturity or artifacts of geodetic modeling choices.
本研究评估了青藏高原走滑地震的浅部滑移亏损是断层成熟度的物理特征还是大地测量建模选择的人为假象。
papers.ab: InSAR‐constrained finite fault slip models are often used to characterize fault geometries and slip distributions of large continental earthquakes. A common feature of these models is a decrease in slip near the surface, commonly expressed as a percentage shallow slip deficit (SSD). This often does not seem to be accommodated interseismically and its causes are still debated, with some studies attributing large deficits to off‐fault deformation along structurally immature faults. We explore this hypothesis through a survey of ten, well‐documented strike‐slip earthquakes from the Tibetan Plateau which occurred on faults that sample a wide spectrum of structural maturity. We collate published SSD values and also compute our own, modified “effective shallow slip deficit” based on the total (on‐ and off‐fault) surface offsets from optical imagery, where available. For the 2021 7.4 Maduo and 2022 6.6 Menyuan earthquakes, we assess the consistency of 10–13 independently modeled slip distributions by comparing them with each other. Slip models vary the most in the uppermost 1 km and around fault bends and other geometrical complexities, leading to large ranges in SSD of 0%–88% (for Maduo) and 0%–51% (for Menyuan). This highlights the need to scrutinize slip models carefully before considering shallow slip deficits. The influence from modeling choices, together with factors such as fault roughness and near‐surface geology, obscures any simple relationship between shallow slip deficits and fault structural maturity for large strike‐slip earthquakes on the Tibetan plateau.

papers.t: Seismic depth imaging using combined dual-element data sets for geologic carbon storage investigations in Thorning, Denmark
in: Department of Earth Sciences 1 , , ,
tk: A combined landstreamer and nodal 2D seismic imaging workflow enhances velocity model building and prestack depth migration for carbon storage site characterization in Denmark.
结合陆地拖缆与节点双数据源的二维地震成像工作流，显著提升了丹麦碳封存场地的速度模型构建与深部成像分辨率。
papers.ab: The success of seismic depth imaging in sedimentary basins affected by salt tectonics depends as much on the illumination of complex geologic targets as on the ability to transform mere data into images that are considered to be an accurate structural description of the earth. Achieving this level of precision on land is by no means simple. This study proposed a tailored depth imaging workflow that combined novel landstreamer and nodal 2D seismic data sets acquired for geologic carbon storage site investigations above the Thorning salt pillow in Denmark. The dual-element configuration provided dense near-offset coverage alongside long-offset recordings, thereby enhancing the resolution of the shallow velocity field and improving illumination of near-surface and deeper reflectors. The combined processing workflow addressed differences in geometry, amplitude, phase, and statics between the two data sets. Early-stage merging of these data sets transformed the two partial views into a single, unified image, thereby providing the basis for prestack depth migration of the combined data. The resulting depth image delineated a fault system along the southwestern margin of the Gassum Formation reservoir and deformed suprasalt strata with high resolution. Subtle structural discontinuities were identified in the overburden, and Quaternary paleovalleys were observed in the shallow subsurface, with implications for seal integrity and groundwater systems. The combined data enabled improved velocity model building and enhanced imaging of key geologic boundaries and structures from the shallow subsurface to depths exceeding 5 km. These findings demonstrated the potential of combining dual-element land data and tailored processing workflows for high-resolution imaging in structurally complex onshore environments.

papers.t: Widespread On‐Fault Geologic Evidence for Variable Mode Coseismic Slip to the Trench in Cascadia
in: U.S. Geological Survey Pacific Coastal & Marine Science Center Santa Cruz CA USA
Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute Moss Landing CA USA
U.S. Geological Survey Woods Hole Coastal & Marine Science Center Woods Hole MA USA
Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys Anchorage AK USA
tk: High-resolution marine geophysical data reveal widespread, variable-mode Holocene coseismic slip reaching the trench along the Cascadia frontal thrust fault zone.
高分辨率海洋地球物理数据揭示了卡斯卡迪亚前缘冲断带广泛存在且模式多样的全新世近沟槽同震滑动。
papers.ab: Investigating the geologic record of near‐trench coseismic strain release is critical for estimating the slip distribution and tsunamigenic potential of future large subduction zone earthquakes. However, the style and extent of upper plate coseismic deformation offshore in subduction zones is poorly constrained. To address this knowledge gap, we integrate shipborne multichannel seismic and multibeam data with targeted autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) bathymetry and chirp data to resolve the updip limit and mode of coseismic slip along the frontal thrust fault zone in central and southern Cascadia. Detailed fault mapping and characterization reveals four distinct styles of Holocene deformation along the frontal thrust fault zone, including fault propagation folding, imbricate thrusting, breakthrough thrusting, and frontal erosion through widespread mass wasting. Joint interpretation with crustal‐scale seismic data shows that these variations in near‐surface deformation style are clearly linked to changes in megathrust geometry and accretionary mode at depth. Additionally, AUV data provide abundant on‐fault geologic evidence for discrete and episodic near‐surface deformation, including primary fault and fold scarps, bending moment fault scarps, punctuated growth strata, and discrete single event fault offset, that we consider to be predominantly coseismic. The widespread distribution of Holocene active, likely coseismic, frontal thrust deformation presented in this study highlights the potential for variable mode coseismic slip to the trench in Cascadia. These results provide an unprecedented view into the shallow megathrust structure and heterogeneity in Cascadia that is critical for estimating earthquake and tsunami hazard impacts locally and for understanding shallow megathrust slip behavior globally.

papers.t: A method for thermochemical full-waveform inversion: integrating mineral physics and seismology
tk: A new full-waveform inversion framework directly inverts seismic waveforms for mantle temperature and composition by integrating mineral physics and adjoint-state gradients.
提出一种结合矿物物理与伴随梯度的全波形反演新框架，可直接反演地幔温度和化学成分。
papers.ab: Seismic imaging of the Earth’s interior has steadily improved in the past 40 yr. Full-waveform inversion (FWI) has been the most recent driver of global and local tomography. Although mineral physics experiments link seismic properties to temperature, pressure and composition of the mantle, direct integration of seismic observations and thermodynamic calculations has not yet been achieved. This work illustrates a framework that integrates FWI techniques with mineral physics to directly invert seismic waveforms for mantle temperature and chemical composition. The forward model is based on interpolation of pre-calculated tables of mantle properties, namely density and P- and S-wave speeds. The inverse problem is formulated as an optimization problem. The gradient of the objective function with respect to temperature and composition is computed using the chain rule which allows us to split it into independent seismic and thermodynamic parts. For the seismic part, the gradient is computed with the adjoint method. For the thermodynamic part, gradients of the pre-calculated tables are obtained by analytically deriving the interpolation function, while accounting for the pressure–density coupling, under the assumption of hydrostatic loading. As a proof of concept, we applied this approach on 2-D synthetic models containing thermal and compositional anomalies where P–SV elastic wave propagation is simulated. The optimization problem is solved using the L-BFGS algorithm. We mitigate the trade-off between the effect of temperature and composition by applying a linear transformation to the model parameters before carrying out the minimization and then transforming back once a solution is found. The proposed framework enables the integration of diverse geophysical data sets as well as the incorporation of additional information on the potential origin of certain mantle anomalies based on petrological constraints, which are crucial to tackle the non-uniqueness of the inverse problem.

papers.t: Reevaluating Large‐Scale Deformation Precursors of Great Subduction Earthquakes: Insights From Satellite Gravity and GNSS Data
in: The Ohio State University
University of California, Berkeley
tk: A rigorous statistical reevaluation using GRACE gravity and GNSS data finds no evidence of large-scale deformation precursors prior to the Tohoku and Maule earthquakes.
利用GRACE重力和GNSS数据的严格统计评估表明，东北和茂莱地震前不存在大尺度形变前兆。
papers.ab: Validating the controversial hypothesis that precursory gravity changes arise from sudden acceleration of subducting plates potentially triggering great earthquakes is of paramount importance. To rigorously evaluate proposed precursors for the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku and 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule earthquakes, we develop a statistical framework that enables (a) robust assessment of their statistical significance, (b) characterization of temporal evolution, and (c) integrative analysis across multiple GRACE gravity solutions with differing error characteristics. Additionally, we test the precursor hypothesis using independent GNSS‐measured surface displacements within a physically consistent framework. Our results show no evidence supporting the proposed precursor in either alternative GRACE solutions or high‐precision GNSS observations. The anomalous gravity changes previously interpreted as earthquake precursors are indistinguishable from solution‐specific data errors or other non‐tectonic signals, lacking evidence for tectonic origin.

papers.t: High Resolution Focal Mechanisms and Stress Field Orientation in Southern Italy From Short‐Term Dense Arrays
in: University of Naples Federico II
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences
RWTH Aachen University
ETH Zurich
Swiss Seismological Service
National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics
University of Sannio
tk: Machine learning and a dense seismic array in Southern Italy resolve 289 low-magnitude focal mechanisms, revealing a stable normal-faulting stress field with seasonal hydrological modulations.
利用密集台阵和机器学习，研究解析了意大利南部289个低震级震源机制，揭示了受水文载荷调制的正断层应力场。
papers.ab: Understanding fault geometry and mechanics is key to interpreting the seismotectonic setting of a region. We analyze data from a 1‐year dense seismic array deployment in Southern Italy to infer focal mechanisms and stress field from low‐magnitude earthquakes using machine‐learning techniques. We derive 289 focal mechanisms, including nearly all events with , yielding a data set comparable to that obtained from 6 years of conventional monitoring. The retrieved mechanisms are consistent with the orientation of the main tectonic structures, and the stress field, inverted from the principal fault planes, indicates a dominant normal faulting regime. We illustrate that dense monitoring enables investigation of spatio‐temporal characteristics of the stress field, showing homogeneity at ∼20 km spatial scale and temporal stability of principal stress orientations. Furthermore, seasonal variations in the stress ratio are observed, that could be modulated by hydrological loading.

papers.t: Acoustic-gravity wave driven traveling ionospheric disturbances: Analytical modeling and application to 2025 Kamchatka earthquake GNSS data
in: Harbin Institute of Technology
Heilongjiang Institute of Technology
University of Science and Technology of China
Chengdu University of Technology
China Earthquake Administration
tk: Presents an analytical framework for acoustic-gravity wave-driven ionospheric disturbances, successfully modeling coseismic TEC perturbations from the 2025 Kamchatka earthquake.
提出声重力波电离层扰动解析框架，成功模拟堪察加地震TEC响应。
papers.ab: We present an analytical framework for ionospheric ion velocity and density perturbations driven by acoustic-gravity waves generated by seismic sources. Neutral motions are computed using a horizontally layered model, and ion responses are obtained from the linearized frequency-domain momentum and continuity equations, including neutral-ion collisions and geomagnetic effects. Simulations show that ion motion undergoes an altitude-dependent transition from a collision-dominated regime to a magnetically controlled regime, producing strong anisotropy. We further show that total electron content (TEC) disturbances are strongly controlled by the geometry between the Line-of-Sight and the wavefront. A case study of the 2025 Kamchatka earthquake demonstrates that the modeled TEC perturbations reproduce key observational features, including Rayleigh-wave and gravity-wave arrivals. These results provide new insights into seismic-ionospheric coupling and support analytical modeling of coseismic TEC responses.

papers.t: Tectonics on Early Earth Driven by Earth's Changing Shape During Tidal Recession of the Moon
in: School of Earth Sciences University of Bristol Bristol UK
Division of Geological and Planetary Sciences California Institute of Technology Pasadena CA USA
tk: Tidal recession of the Moon and Earth's slowing rotation changed Earth's shape, driving polar extension and equatorial convergence that shaped early crustal tectonics.
月球潮汐退行和地球自转减速改变了地球形状，驱动了两极张裂与赤道汇聚，塑造了早期地壳构造。
papers.ab: Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early‐Earth dynamics: rotation. Earth after the Moon‐forming impact was rapidly rotating with its rotation rate slowing significantly during the first tens of millions of years after the impact as the Moon tidally receded. Using planetary structure and tidal evolution calculations, I show that the initially distorted structure of Earth would likely have led to significant latitudinal variations in primary crustal thickness. Further, the subsequent changes in Earth's shape in response to its slowing rotation rate could have driven extensive tectonic activity and modulated the response of the crust to other forces. There was extension of the crust in polar regions and convergence in the equatorial regions at rates potentially comparable to those forming the Himalayas today in high‐angular momentum scenarios. Depending on the rheology of the earliest crust, such motions could have led to burial of hydrated and weathered surface material, extensive volcanism, and degassing of Earth's interior. Phase changes due to increases in internal pressure could have led to delamination of parts of the crust, producing early mantle heterogeneities. Hydrated secondary melting of the crust and the production of evolved magmas could explain the emergence of a diversity of rock types within tens of millions of years of Earth's formation.

papers.t: Porting Deep-Learning Phase Pickers from TensorFlow to PyTorch for SeisBench Without
in: University of Texas at Austin
tk: Presents a four-step workflow to convert TensorFlow-based deep-learning phase pickers to PyTorch for SeisBench integration without retraining, preserving original weights and numerical behavior.
提出一种无需重训练即可将TensorFlow深度学习震相拾取器转换为PyTorch的四步工作流，并集成至SeisBench。
papers.ab: SeisBench has become the premier open-source library for accessing pretrained deep-learning seismic phase pickers through a unified Python interface. Because SeisBench distributes models exclusively in PyTorch, phase pickers originally developed in TensorFlow must be converted to PyTorch before integration into the library. Although retraining is possible, doing so produces new learned weights that can alter the numerical behavior and picking characteristics of the original model while demanding substantial time and compute. We present a four-step workflow for converting static TensorFlow/Keras phase pickers to PyTorch that preserves original model weights without retraining: (1) architectural alignment, (2) weight extraction and layout transformation, (3) explicit parameter mapping, and (4) staged validation from intermediate activations through waveform traces and phase picks. We demonstrate the workflow by converting the Earthquake Compact Convolutional Transformer (EQCCT), a production phase picker used by the Texas Seismological Network, from TensorFlow to PyTorch. Across 100,000 STEAD and TXED waveform windows, CPU and GPU mean absolute errors remained between 1.46 × 10^(-9) and 1.82 × 10^(-9) with TF32 disabled. Detection decisions at thresholds of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 were identical on both devices, while argmax locations agreed for all but one CPU P-wave window, which differed by one sample. The converted EQCCT models are now available in the main SeisBench repository as EQCCTP and EQCCTS. This workflow serves as a reference for integrating TensorFlow-based seismic phase pickers into SeisBench by converting their original weights into a PyTorch-compatible format while preserving their operational behavior. Validation in this study is limited to EQCCT.

papers.t: Effective elastic properties of weakly cemented sandstone considering grain lateral displacement
in: State Key Laboratory of Deep Oil and Gas 1 , , ,
School of Geosciences 2 , , ,
Xinjiang Oilfield Company 3 , , PetroChina , ,
MSU-BIT-SMBU Joint Research Center of Applied Mathematics 4 , , ,
tk: A revised contact cement theory incorporates grain lateral displacement to accurately predict shear-wave velocities and VP/VS ratios in weakly cemented sandstones.
引入颗粒侧向位移修正接触水泥理论，提高弱胶结砂岩波速预测精度。
papers.ab: Predicting shear-wave velocities in weakly cemented sandstones remains challenging. The widely used contact cement theory (CCT) often overestimates shear-wave velocities even when P-wave velocities are well predicted. To address this issue, the CCT was revisited. It was found that the effects of grain lateral displacement on shear-wave velocities were neglected in the CCT. Because grain lateral displacement couples with the tangential displacement of cement, it can strongly affect shear-wave velocities. This effect was captured by solving a system of coupled integral equations that link the two types of displacements. The resulting formulation enabled more accurate estimation of the tangential stiffness of grain–cement assemblies and, consequently, of the shear moduli and shear-wave velocities. Application of the proposed approach to weakly cemented sandstones showed that grain lateral displacement markedly reduced tangential stiffness, leading to lower shear moduli and shear-wave velocities and thus an increased VP/VS ratio. Comparisons with ultrasonic measurements on synthetic shaly sandstone samples demonstrated that incorporating grain lateral displacement significantly improved agreement with the experimental results. The present formulation is primarily applicable to dry, weakly cemented, quartz-dominated sandstones with small grain–cement contact regions, for which the low grain Poisson’s ratio and elastic half-space approximation are appropriate. Within these applicable conditions, the proposed approach offers considerable potential for improving the seismic characterization of weakly cemented sandstone reservoirs.

papers.t: Inversion of elastic properties of stratified layered media using elastic direct waveform inversion
in: Tianjin University 1 , ,
University of Houston 2 , , ,
tk: The elastic Direct Waveform Inversion (eDWI) scheme reformulates global non-linear inversion into localized recursive inversions, avoiding local minima and parameter coupling in stratified media.
弹性直接波形反演通过局部递推避免了局部极小值和参数耦合。
papers.ab: Conventional gradient-based elastic full-waveform inversion methods encounter challenges associated with local minima and trade-offs in multiparameter inversion. To address these issues, a new method was developed, called the elastic direct waveform inversion (eDWI) scheme. By explicitly enforcing the time-space causality of the wavefield, eDWI converted, without loss of information, the global iterative nonlinear inversion problem into a sequence of localized recursive inversions performed from shallow to deep depths. The method was tested on two numerical examples for stratified layered elastic media with a plane-wave source and a point source. The stiffness matrix method was used to decompose and extrapolate wavefields into up/down-going P and S wavefields, and specific P-to-P and P-to-S reflection events were used for the localized recursive inversion. Numerical examples showed that the new approach did not need a global initial model, avoided local minima, and addressed parameter coupling issues. It automatically used multiples and maintained efficacy even without low-frequency content in the recorded seismic data. The new inversion approach may find a wide range of imaging and sensing applications using seismic and other waves.

papers.t: Ground Truth of Surface Rupture and Very-Near-Fault Ground Motion from Video, Seismic and Field Data
in: Graduate School of Science
University of Tokyo
tk: Validates surface rupture and near-fault ground motion using security camera footage, seismic records, and field data, revealing two distinct velocity pulses.
利用监控视频、地震记录和野外数据验证了熊本地震的近断层地表破裂与强震动，并揭示了两个速度脉冲。
papers.ab: Seismic radiation and dynamic faulting have rarely been observed concurrently, limiting observational constraints on earthquake rupture processes and seismic hazards. Here we report the first directly validated observation of both surface rupture and strong-motion generation captured by a security camera and independently corroborated by nearby seismic records and field measurements during and after the 2026 Kumamoto, Japan, earthquake. Image-retrieved displacement time series matched nearby seismic records. We further find that the very-near-fault ground motion comprised two velocity pulses generated by subsurface and surface fault rupture, respectively, with comparable amplitudes (~1 m s -1 ) and durations (~1 s). The pulse characteristics may reflect the depth-dependent variations in seismic velocities and stress conditions across a sedimentary cover overlying the basement rock. These observations provide rare constraints on the coupling between dynamic faulting and seismic radiation, offering new insights into earthquake source physics and seismic hazard assessments near faults.

papers.t: Muography Simulations for Carbon Capture and Storage Monitoring
tk: A two-stage workflow and geometric filtering reduce muography simulation times 700-fold for monitoring carbon capture and storage reservoirs.
双阶段工作流与几何过滤将碳封存监测的宇宙线缪子成像模拟速度提升了700倍。
papers.ab: Muography can monitor CO2 storage through reservoir density changes, but site-scale simulations are costly: reservoirs can be deep and borehole detectors are small. We address both with two approaches. First, a two-stage workflow splits the kilometer-scale simulation: a fast code transports muons through the overburden, and a general-purpose Monte Carlo code through the reservoir and detectors. Second, a geometric filter at the source keeps only muons whose direction and position let them reach the detectors, within a margin for multiple scattering, and a range cut removes those with too little energy. Both are available in the UCMuon simulation suite for muon generation, filtering and transport. At a deep (800-1000 m) and a shallow (65 m) CO2 storage site, each approach reduces the computing time about 700-fold, and the filtered simulation gives the same hit rate as a full one, as long as the margin exceeds the muons' sideways scattering drift.

papers.t: Denoising Teleseismic Data for Deep Earth Studies Using a Supervised Deep‐Learning Auto‐Encoder: A Case Study of Diffracted Waves From ULVZs
in: Institut für Geophysik Universität Münster Münster Germany
James Cook University Douglas QLD Australia
Department of Geosciences Utrecht University Utrecht The Netherlands
Research School of Earth Sciences The Australian National University Acton ACT Australia
Institut für Kernphysik Universität Münster Münster Germany

tk: A supervised deep-learning auto-encoder trained on 1D synthetics and real noise effectively denoises teleseismic Sdiff waves, revealing new ULVZ structures.
利用深度学习自编码器对超低速带衍射波去噪，发现新深部结构信号。
papers.ab: Seismic noise, particularly the microseism generated by the oceans, is a fundamental limitation on using short period (1–10 s) teleseismic data to study the deep Earth. Deep learning auto‐encoders have proven effective at denoising seismic data in other applications. Here, we provide a demonstration of their potential for improving the quality of deep Earth seismic data, using S diff post‐cursors generated by ultra‐low velocity zones (ULVZs) as a case study. We present a computationally efficient and accessible workflow, utilizing a supervised learning process with 1D synthetics and real, global seismic noise. This workflow does not require real teleseismic signals, which are limited in number and quality, and is computationally efficient, not requiring expensive 3D spectral‐element simulations. We present a series of example applications, finding the denoiser to be effective at removing noise and extracting S diff signal despite having not been trained with real teleseismic signals. Furthermore, we provide recommendations on how performance could be improved, including demonstrating transfer learning as an efficient and effective way to improve extraction of specific signals. Lastly we apply denoising to seismic data sampling known ULVZs, identifying previously unreported short‐period signals from several different ULVZs and obtaining observations of the Hawaiian ULVZ along a novel source‐receiver geometry from the East Pacific Rise to Japan, which is perpendicular to previous ray paths. These observations reveal previously undocumented frequency‐ and azimuth‐dependent S diff waveforms associated with ULVZs, demonstrating that denoising can expand observational constraints on deep Earth structure.

papers.t: Full-depth velocity model building and imaging in ultradeepwater regions: A case study on an OBS/streamer joint 2D survey data set acquired in the northern South China Sea
in: State Key Laboratory of Marine Geology 1 , , ,
School of Geosciences 2 , , ,

tk: An unsupervised seismic denoising method is developed by integrating implicit neural representation as a prior within the PnP-ADMM optimization framework.
提出结合隐式神经表示与PnP-ADMM的无监督地震异常噪声压制方法。
papers.ab: Deepwater basins have become major targets for commercial oil and gas exploration. However, as exploration advances into ultradeepwater basins, technical challenges become increasingly severe, as exemplified by the Liwan Sag in the northern South China Sea (SCS). The rugged seafloor terrain and great water depth degrade seismic imaging quality and increase uncertainties in drilling and geologic interpretation. Conventional towed-streamer reflection seismic data provide dense reflection information, but are limited by relatively narrow observation angles and limited offset coverage. By contrast, ocean-bottom seismometer (OBS) data provide first-arrival traveltimes at larger offsets, thereby complementing the limited offset coverage of streamer data. In this study, joint OBS and towed-streamer observations from the Liwan Sag were collated and preprocessed to obtain seismic data with an improved signal-to-noise ratio for velocity model building over the full depth range. An integrated workflow with three stages was established: seawater velocity model building, subseafloor background velocity model building, and subseafloor velocity refining. The resulting velocity models were evaluated using traveltime fitting, migration image quality, and common image gather (CIG) flattening, and were then used for imaging in the depth domain and geologic interpretation of the survey line. This case study provided a practical workflow that integrated seismic data preprocessing, full-depth velocity model building, and stratigraphic imaging for ultradeepwater seismic exploration.

papers.t: General Solution Scaling Relations in Linear Elastic Dynamic Rupture Models
in: Scripps Institution of Oceanography University of California, San Diego La Jolla CA USA
Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences University of California, Riverside Riverside CA USA
Center for Earthquake Research and Information (CERI) The University of Memphis Memphis TN USA
In Human Resources LLC Menifee CA USA
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences Ludwig‐Maximilians‐Universität München Munich Germany
tk: This study mathematically proves the generality of solution scaling in linear elastic dynamic rupture models across various fault geometries, medium complexities, and friction laws.
该研究数学证明了线性弹性动态破裂模型缩放关系的普适性。
papers.ab: Dynamic rupture models have been widely used to enhance our understanding of earthquake processes and associated hazards. A commonly held insight among modelers is that if the initial stress, rheological parameters, and space and time coordinates are scaled by certain factors in a specific manner, the solution will scale accordingly and remain similar. While this principle has been applied in numerical simulations, particularly to optimize parameter studies and interpret results through non‐dimensionalization, its general applicability to more complex modeling scenarios has not been rigorously established. In this study, we provide a proof of the generality of solution scaling in linear elastic dynamic rupture problems using a boundary integral equation formulation. We demonstrate how dynamic rupture solutions, including slip and traction evolution, scale with initial stress, fault rheology parameters, space and time coordinates, and elastic medium properties. The proof holds under arbitrary complexity in fault geometry and medium velocity structure, as well as with heterogeneous on‐fault rheology parameters, provided that solution uniqueness is satisfied. We consider four types of fault rheology: linear slip‐weakening, rate‐and‐state friction, linear time‐weakening, and general composite rheology with different slip rate dependencies at different slip rates. Our results have practical implications for the design of large‐scale simulation campaigns and for interpreting laboratory dynamic rupture experiments. More broadly, our work provides theoretical support for widely used scaling practices in the dynamic rupture modeling community by establishing a mathematical foundation.

papers.t: Bayesian Calibration of Dynamic Models of Earthquake Sequences Using Observations From Past Large Earthquakes
in: California Institute of Technology Pasadena CA USA
tk: A Bayesian framework calibrates earthquake-cycle models using paleoseismic summary statistics, leveraging ensemble Kalman inversion and Gaussian-process emulation for efficient uncertainty quantification.
该研究提出了一种利用古地震统计数据校准地震周期动力学模型的贝叶斯反演框架。
papers.ab: Physics‐based models of the earthquake cycle could be used for time‐dependent hazard assessment. For such an application, their parameters must be calibrated so that simulated earthquake sequences reproduce the statistics of past earthquakes, including recurrence statistics and magnitudes. This is challenging because the dynamics are described by nonlinear partial differential equations, initial conditions are unknown, and records of past earthquakes are sparse, incomplete, and noisy. To address this challenge, we present a Bayesian inverse‐problem framework to infer heterogeneous parameters in an earthquake‐cycle model from observations of past large earthquakes. Rather than matching a time‐series of individual events, we exploit ergodicity (long‐term statistics independent of initial conditions) and invert for stationary, spatially distributed summary statistics of event timing and slip, including mean interevent times, coefficients of variation, burstiness, and average coseismic slip, which are quantities that can in principle be estimated from paleoseismic and historical records. Observational noise and event‐detection thresholds are explicitly accounted for in the construction of these statistics. The inverse problem is solved using a derivative‐free ensemble Kalman inversion method, and uncertainty quantification is enhanced by an emulate–sample strategy that leverages machine‐learning for surrogate modeling, in which a Gaussian‐process surrogate of the parameter‐to‐statistics map enables efficient MCMC sampling without further expensive forward simulations. Synthetic experiments with realistic data noise suggest that the model parameters can be inverted from statistical quantities observable from paleoseismology at a limited number of observation points. The framework provides a principled and computationally tractable method to calibrate earthquake‐cycle models, providing a foundation for forecasting.

papers.t: Deep magmatic plumbing system beneath Harrat Al-Madinah revealed by borehole seismic ambient noise interferometry
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: The University of Tokyo
King Abdulaziz University
National Research Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics
tk: Borehole ambient noise autocorrelation reveals six crustal reflectors, including the Conrad and Moho, mapping the deep magmatic plumbing system beneath Harrat Al-Madinah.
井下背景噪声自相关揭示了麦地那火山区下方的六个地壳反射面，描绘了深部岩浆通道系统。
papers.ab: Ambient seismic noise interferometry is increasingly used for crustal imaging, but its application to intraplate volcanic systems remains limited because seismic networks are often sparse, ambient-noise sources are variable, and strong scattering in volcanic terrains makes stable reflectivity retrieval challenging. We analyze 70 days of continuous borehole seismic records from the VORiSA network in Harrat Al-Madinah, western Saudi Arabia, to investigate the crustal structure beneath a large basaltic volcanic field. Eight three-component seismometers deployed at approximately 120 m depth provide stable recordings with reduced near-surface noise. We apply conventional autocorrelation and phase autocorrelation with phase-weighted stacking (PAC–PWS) to the vertical component. Conventional autocorrelation provides an amplitude-preserving reference based on linear correlation and stacking, whereas PAC–PWS reduces the influence of amplitude fluctuations and emphasizes phase-coherent arrivals. Their combined use allows evaluation of reflector consistency across complementary processing schemes. The results identify six principal reflectors above approximately 50 km depth. These include boundaries corresponding to the Conrad discontinuity at approximately 22 km and the Moho at approximately 38 km, consistent with previous seismic studies, as well as additional reflectors near 10 km, within the mid-crust at 10–25 km, and near 46–47 km. Comparison with magnetotelluric imaging suggests that several mid-crustal reflectors may be associated with conductive zones interpreted as possible magma reservoirs. These results indicate that borehole ambient-noise autocorrelation, supported by complementary phase-based processing, can provide useful constraints on crustal structure beneath intraplate volcanic regions.

papers.t: Novel Data‐Driven Receiver Function Clustering and Analysis Along the Alaska‐Aleutian Volcanic Arc
in: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa Honolulu HI USA
University of California, Davis Davis CA USA
U.S. Geological Survey, Alaska Volcano Observatory Anchorage AK USA
Earth and Planets Laboratory Carnegie Institution for Science Washington DC USA
tk: A novel data-driven clustering method using receiver functions reveals first-order crustal magmatic architecture and magma storage complexity across 16 Aleutian arc volcanoes.
基于接收函数聚类的新方法揭示了阿留申火山地壳岩浆系统的复杂性。
papers.ab: Constraining magma storage and transport through the entire crust at a variety of arc volcanoes is essential to understand how subduction parameters may influence these processes. However, constraints throughout the crust are often limited to volcanoes that either fortuitously have properties that illuminate the entire crustal system, or volcanoes where high‐resolution geophysical imaging has been performed. Seismic receiver functions (RFs) offer sensitivity to the whole crust independent of local seismicity distribution using a few instruments. However, near volcanoes, they are often complex, requiring detailed analysis and potentially non‐unique velocity model solutions. Here, we introduce a novel, data‐driven method to identify and map RF variability using spectral clustering and kernel logistic regression. We apply it to 16 volcanoes in the Aleutian arc, enabling systematic comparisons of RF patterns without need for detailed velocity modeling. We observe that a subset of these volcanoes has RF variability that is spatially well‐separated in the crust, while others appear to have minimal spatial organization. Based on comparisons with previous results, we find that the former tends to occur at volcanoes with relatively simple magma storage systems, and the latter at volcanoes with complex, multi‐layer storage. This suggests that our technique reveals first‐order variability in crustal magmatic architecture. Furthermore, the ability to recover spatially coherent RF patterns shows no clear correlation with along‐arc subduction parameters but instead appears associated with edifice morphology. This work establishes a systematic framework for comparing arc volcanic structure and a foundation for future RF velocity modeling, extendable to other heterogeneous settings.

Understanding how the basin formed has important implications for the India–Seychelles breakup and the evolution of the western Indian Ocean. Despite its geodynamic significance, the nature of the basin and its crust remain uncertain, with differing views on its origin ranging from a stretched continental crust to pre‐Paleogene oceanic crust. In this study, we reexamine existing geodynamic models using new geochemical and Sr–Nd–Pb isotopic data obtained from the igneous basement recovered during the International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 355. The new data from the basaltic crust show that it formed from mid‐oceanic ridge basalt‐like magmas derived primarily from the depleted asthenospheric mantle, with a minor contribution from the subcontinental lithospheric mantle (

papers.t: Mechanical Decoupling Across the Deep Megathrust Boundary
in: Research Center for Prediction of Earthquakes and Volcanic Eruptions Graduate School of Science Tohoku University Sendai Japan
Department of Earth and Planetary Science The University of Tokyo Tokyo Japan
Earthquake Research Institute The University of Tokyo Tokyo Japan
Independent Researcher Tokyo Japan

tk: High-frequency moment tensor inversions in northeast Japan reveal a sharp stress rotation across the deep megathrust, indicating a weak, mechanically decoupled plate boundary at 60 km depth.
日本东北深部大断裂带两侧应力方向发生急剧旋转，表明在60公里深度存在极弱的机械解耦板块边界。
papers.ab: We examine stress and strength across the deep subduction plate boundary at ∼60 km depth offshore northeastern Japan, near the downdip seismic limit of the megathrust. High‐frequency (2–5 Hz) moment tensor inversion of ∼2,000 M 2–3.5 earthquakes, integrated with existing catalogs, increases the number of focal mechanisms by more than a factor of six, enabling detailed mapping of the stress field near the interface. The results reveal an abrupt, kilometer‐scale stress contrast across the interface: downdip‐compressional stress in the upper slab persists to within ∼2 km of the megathrust, whereas the immediately overlying plate is under nearly strike‐parallel compression, producing a ∼90° rotation of maximum compression over only a few kilometers. Because the principal stress axes remain nearly parallel or normal to the interface, this geometry implies very low shear traction on the deep megathrust: only ∼11% of the maximum shear stress in the underlying slab. In absolute terms, the estimated megathrust shear stress is only ∼108 MPa even assuming hydrostatic pore pressure within the slab (slab maximum shear stress, ∼0.98 GPa; μ ′ = 0.07), and decreases to ∼11 MPa for a weaker slab sustaining a maximum shear stress of 100 MPa (pore‐pressure‐to‐lithostatic‐pressure ratio, 0.93; μ ′ = 0.006). These results indicate that the deep megathrust is a weak, aseismically shearing fault zone that mechanically decouples the slab and overriding plate, allowing large unbending‐related stresses in the slab to coexist with strike‐parallel compression in the overriding plate.

papers.t: South of the 2016 rupture termination: Geodetic constraints on coseismic slip of the 2026 M7.1 Kumamoto Earthquake
in: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan, Kitasato 1, Tsukuba, 3050811, Israel [IL]
Geospatial Information Authority of Japan, 1 Kitasato, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan [JP]
tk: Geodetic and strong-motion data constrain the coseismic slip of the 2026 M7.1 Kumamoto earthquake, revealing how fault geometry and structural heterogeneity controlled the rupture.
利用大地测量和强震数据约束了2026年M7.1熊本地震的同震破裂，揭示了断层几何与结构非均匀性对破裂的控制作用。
papers.ab: The July 28, 2026, M7.1 Kumamoto earthquake occurred on the Hinagu Fault zone in southwest Japan, near the southern termination of the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake sequence. We investigated coseismic deformation from Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data and inferred a two-segment fault source model to examine the spatial relationship among coseismic slip, structural heterogeneity, and the 2016 rupture extent. The 2026 main slip was located south of the southern termination of the 2016 rupture, with a peak of right-lateral slip at shallow depth near the hypocenter, while a normal-slip component was concentrated at greater depth near a fault bend. Slip decreases toward the southwest, where weak slip remains at shallow depth on the southwestern segment; cross-validation tests and a strong-motion waveform inversion supported its robustness. Changes in slip characteristics occur near the fault bend and independently identified contrasts in seismic velocity and geological structure.

papers.t: Crustal structure beneath the Kivu Rift and Virunga Volcanic Province, Western Rift, Africa
in: Department of Earth, Environment, and Planetary Sciences
Northwestern University
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences
Tulane University
Goma Volcano Observatory
tk: Receiver function analysis reveals crustal thinning and localized magmatic modification beneath the Kivu Rift and Virunga Volcanic Province.
接收函数揭示了基伍裂谷与维龙加火山区下方的地壳减薄与岩浆改造。
papers.ab: Magmatism can substantially modify continental crust during rifting, yet the distribution of melt and intrusive additions to the crust is often difficult to resolve, particularly in rift sectors where volcanism is spatially localised. Unlike the Ethiopian and Eastern rift sectors of East Africa, volcanism in the Western Rift is concentrated in a few spatially isolated volcanic provinces, raising questions about where magma is stored and how it interacts with fault-controlled extension during the early stages of rifting. We use teleseismic Ps receiver functions (RFs) from the Kivu Rift sector (networks 7G, YA, and KV) to constrain crustal thickness, bulk P-to-S wave velocity ratio (κ), and the character of intracrustal and Moho impedance contrasts across the Kivu Rift that includes the Virunga and South Kivu volcanic provinces. We combine H–κ stacking, 1-D receiver function waveform inversion, and forward modelling to map lateral variations in crustal structure. Crustal thickness varies systematically with tectonic setting: the thinnest crust occurs at stations within the rift (∼28–34 km), whereas thicker crust (mid-30s to low-40s km) characterises the flanks and the broader province. Elevated κ values and increased waveform complexity are concentrated around the Virunga Volcanic Province, consistent with mid- to lower-crustal modification by mafic intrusions and/or melt–fluid effects. We also assess whether topographic variations are isostatically compensated after accounting for the dynamically-supported broad plateau uplift. The thinner crust within the fault-bounded basin confirms extension by a mean stretching factor of ~1.23, locally reaching ~1.32 where crust thins to ~28 km, but the basin–flank elevation contrast is smaller than expected from crustal thinning alone, suggesting that lower crust and/or sub-crustal density variations are important. Together, these observations indicate that the crust beneath the Kivu Rift sector is felsic in composition, has magmatic modification localised to the Virunga Volcanic Province, and crustal stretching is comparable to other Western Rift sectors with deeper basins.

papers.t: 3‐D Plate Interaction Beneath the Active Taiwan Orogen Revealed by Source‐Side Seismic Tomography: Implications for Slab Breakoff and Orogenic Evolution
in: Institute of Earth Sciences Academia Sinica Taipei Taiwan
Department of Geosciences National Taiwan University Taipei Taiwan
Institute of Oceanography National Taiwan University Taipei Taiwan
tk: Source-side teleseismic tomography reveals the 3-D geometry of subducting plates beneath Taiwan, supporting a slab breakoff model.
源侧远震断层成像揭示了台湾下方俯冲板块的三维几何结构，支持板块断裂模型。
papers.ab: We employed an unconventional teleseismic tomographic inversion method, referred to as source‐side teleseismic tomography (SSTT), to enhance the resolution of 3‐D P‐wave velocity (Vp) structure beneath the active Taiwan orogenic belt down to a depth of ∼400 km. Unlike traditional teleseismic tomography, which uses travel‐time residuals from teleseismic events to local stations, we utilize travel‐time residuals from local earthquakes to distant stations. This method significantly increases the spatial sampling of ray paths at mantle depths due to the substantially larger number of local events distributed at depths and along subduction zones compared to the limited number of broadband stations confined to the surface. Our findings reveal detailed 3‐D geometry and interaction of the subducting Eurasian Plate (EP) and Philippine Sea Plate (PSP) beneath Taiwan. In the south, the high‐Vp anomaly, interpreted as the subducting EP, descends eastwardly down to a depth of 400 km at approximately 123°E longitude. Moving from central to northern Taiwan, the EP steepens and becomes detached at depths of 200–300 km. This slab detachment progressively widens northward, and extends beneath the northward‐dipping PSP. The detached EP segment beneath the PSP indicates its prior subduction location beneath the southern Ryukyu and supports the slab breakoff model rather than the lithospheric tear model. This newly derived model resolves the intricate 3‐D plate interaction between the EP and PSP that drives complex spatiotemporal tectonic processes of the Taiwan orogen, and demonstrates the efficacy of SSTT in enhancing mantle imaging in Taiwan and other seismically active regions.

papers.t: The 2025 Mw 7.7 Myanmar Earthquake: Finite Fault Versus Point Source in Modeling Coseismic Ionospheric Disturbances
in: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Via Manzoni 93, Rome, Ravenna, Italy [IT]
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Unknown, Rome, Italy [IT]
Université Paris Cité, Institut De Physique Du Globe De Paris, CNRS, 39 Rue Hélène Brion, Batiment Lamarck A, Paris, France [FR]
Université Paris Cité, Institut de physique du globe de Paris (IPGP), CNRS UMR 7154, Unknown, Paris, France [FR]
tk: Modeling coseismic ionospheric disturbances using a finite-fault source significantly improves arrival time and amplitude predictions compared to a point-source model.
相比于点源模型，使用有限断层源模拟同震电离层扰动能显著提高到达时间和振幅的预测精度。
papers.ab: Coseismic ionospheric disturbances (CIDs), observed in the total electron content (TEC) measured by Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers, are often interpreted with a point source at the epicenter. We present a three-dimensional forward model that propagates the acoustic pulse from an extended rupture to the ionosphere and returns synthetic slant TEC along each observed line of sight. The source is a moment-weighted distribution of sub-sources along the fault, each radiating at its own rupture time. Rays are traced through a moving, stratified atmosphere into the far field, with absorption and ray-tube spreading; the neutral motion is projected onto the geomagnetic field, and the electron-density perturbation follows from the three-dimensional continuity equation. We apply the model to the 28 March 2025 Mw 7.7 Myanmar earthquake, which ruptured more than 400 km south of the epicenter along an almost straight fault, ideal for isolating the effect of rupture geometry. We compare finite-fault and point-source predictions with CID arrivals identified on 249 satellite-receiver arcs. The model reproduces the shape of the disturbance and its broadening with distance. The finite fault almost halves the median timing error of the point source (202 s against 383 s) and moves the strongest response toward the southern arcs, where observed amplitudes peak. Arrival times and amplitudes are ordered by distance from the fault rather than from the epicenter, which biases epicentral travel-time analyses. Misfits that grow with distance, common to both sources, point to the modeled propagation and to Rayleigh-wave-induced arrivals in the far field.

papers.t: Marine Sediment Imaging With Distributed Acoustic Sensing Offshore Central Chile
in: Université Côte d’Azur Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur CNRS IRD Géoazur Valbonne France
tk: This study combines DAS-based ambient noise interferometry, earthquake scattering, and spectral resonance to image high-resolution marine sediment structures and faults offshore Chile.
本研究结合DAS背景噪声干涉、地震散射和谱共振技术，高分辨率成像了智利近海的海洋沉积结构与断层。
papers.ab: In subduction zones, shallow crustal faults accommodate part of the tectonic deformation and modulate the distribution of marine sediments. The interplay between active faults and sedimentary basins influences seismic hazards and submarine landslides, making imaging these structures essential to constrain their geometry, physical properties, and contributions to regional geodynamic processes. Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) offers an opportunity to passively image offshore sediments at high spatial resolution by converting submarine telecom cables into dense seismic arrays. DAS enables ambient seismic noise tomography with a hundred‐meter resolution, revealing detailed velocity structures with strong impedance contrasts and localizing diffracting structures, such as faults and basin edges. In this study, we combine different imaging techniques that rely on both ambient noise and earthquake records from over 2 years of continuous DAS data to investigate marine sediment structures offshore central Chile. We first analyze the scattered wavefields in earthquake recordings to locate structures of strong impedance contrast along the cable at sub‐kilometer scales. We then apply autocorrelation and cross‐correlation of ambient noise to associate those features with faults and basin edges that both produce scattering patterns. Finally, we analyze high‐resolution power spectral density to investigate the relationship between high‐frequency resonances, shallow sedimentary deposits, local attenuation, and basin‐edge effects, and we validate our interpretations using numerical simulations. Together, these methods reveal sedimentary accumulations within basins and fault‐related structures, consistent with regional geological constraints, demonstrating the ability of DAS to resolve fine‐scale structures and its potential for studying offshore faults, sediment dynamics, and site effects.

papers.t: A Unified Joint Inversion Framework of Surface Wave Dispersion Data With Teleseismic and Local Body Wave Traveltimes: Methodology and Applications to Dense Arrays
in: State Key Laboratory of Precision Geodesy School of Earth and Space Sciences University of Science and Technology of China Hefei China
Hefei National Laboratory University of Science and Technology of China Hefei China
Mengcheng National Geophysical Observatory University of Science and Technology of China Mengcheng China
Anhui Provincial Key Laboratory of Subsurface Exploration and Earthquake Hazard Prevention University of Science and Technology of China Hefei China
School of Earth Sciences and Engineering Sun Yat‐sen University Zhuhai China
tk: A unified joint inversion framework integrates surface wave dispersion with teleseismic and local body wave traveltimes to improve crustal and lithospheric imaging using dense arrays.
该研究提出了一个结合面波频散与远震及地方震体波走时的统一联合反演框架，以提升密集台阵的成像精度。
papers.ab: We develop a unified joint inversion framework that integrates traveltimes from teleseismic body wave, local body wave, and surface wave data to construct 3‐D Vp and Vs models. The method builds upon a joint inversion framework based on the direct surface wave tomography (DSurfTomo) and local body wave double difference tomography (tomoDD), and is extended by incorporating the teleseismic station‐pair double difference differential times within a regional teleseismic inversion framework. This enables full exploitation of the complementary sensitivities of different data types, allowing the construction of a unified regional model spanning a broader depth range from the upper crust to the upper mantle. We validate the proposed method by applying it to both synthetic tests and real data inversions using realistic array configurations. We first apply it to the southern California plate boundary region, where extensive seismic observations are available, and the resulting 3‐D lithospheric‐scale Vp and Vs model is consistent with previous studies, thereby validating the feasibility of the proposed approach. The method is subsequently applied to the Weifang array in the Tanlu Fault Zone (TLFZ), demonstrating its effectiveness for small‐scale temporary dense arrays. By using teleseismic body wave data, the method enables the construction of a unified model with an extended depth range, revealing flexibility across different array scales and highlighting its potential to enhance the utilization of small‐scale temporary dense array data sets. The construction of a unified model provides important constraints for linking tectonic processes with the underlying geodynamic mechanisms.

papers.ab: Giant Antarctic tabular icebergs travel northward until they disintegrate and melt.Tracking their movement and state is challenging because remote sensing is sporadic. Combining a close-by seismic station and evidence from the SWOT KaRIn SSHA and MODIS True Color imagery, we achieved daily reconstruction of the A-76a iceberg's late-stage evolution (March-July 2023). Seismic spectrograms revealed bursts, harmonic tremors, and a micro-tsunami signal, with locations validated by satellite images. Bursts were associated with iceberg fracturing, tremors with seafloor scraping and collisions, and a micro-tsunami with capsizing. This study demonstrates the value of integrating remote sensing and seismic data to monitor iceberg dynamics. It is the first to observe a micro-tsunami with SWOT that generates a seiche-like signal on the 37-km-distant II.HOPE station. This approach astutely combines the strengths of continuous seismic monitoring and large-area satellite imaging to monitor this massive tabular iceberg.

papers.ab: Seismic data offer a unique window into planetary interiors. Here, following a note from Russell et al. (2026), we provide further analysis to solidify our identification of a seismic phase detected by the InSight mission as one which interacts with a basal mantle layer (BML) on Mars (Samuel et al., 2023a). We show that other mantle discontinuities or other seismic structures invoked in the aforementioned note are unlikely to produce this seismic signal. We further illustrate how our proposed layered structure is compatible with other available geophysical observations and geodynamical constraints, and can be used to make inferences about Martian evolution.

papers.ab: Metals are essential to the success of the energy transition, but the discovery rate of deposits has been in decline. Innovative new methods of exploration are required. In recent years, ambient noise tomography (ANT) using passive seismic wavefields recovered from the background noise recorded by seismometers has gained increasing popularity as a tool in mineral exploration. Many studies have demonstrated its efficacy in mapping the local geologic structure of mineral deposits but have been limited to depths of a few hundred meters to a few kilometers and have focused on small lateral scales. The application of ANT for district-scale (tens of kilometers) exploration has remained untested. In this study, a network of 30 Sercel WiNG microelectromechanical system (MEMS) accelerometers was deployed along an approximately 50-km NE-SW line through the Kansanshi copper (Cu)–gold (Au) mine. The Kansanshi mine is the third-largest copper mine in Africa, with a resource of 982.3 Mt of Cu (using a cut-off grade of 0.2% TCu) and 0.11 g/tonne of Au as of December 2023. Here, the study showed that ANT performed with cost-effective MEMS accelerometers can identify a significant body of metal-source sediments beneath Kansanshi, with a thickness of multiple kilometers, as well as structures consistent with the expulsion of mineralizing fluid through focused zones. These results demonstrated that ANT using MEMS accelerometers would be a valuable tool for district-scale mineral exploration of greenfield sites.

in: University of Oslo
Cardiff University
University of Maryland, College Park
Institut polytechnique de Grenoble
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

Université Savoie Mont Blanc
tk: Reviews how fluid pressure controls frictional instabilities across rock and ice, highlighting three rheological regimes governed by fluid overpressure length scales and transport time scales.
综述了流体压力对岩石和冰川摩擦不稳定的控制作用，提出了三种流变机制。
papers.ab: Slip instabilities leading to earthquakes, landslides, and glacier surges may be triggered by high fluid pressures at the slipping interface. High fluid pressures may, however, also suppress instability because of large nucleation length-scales in overpressured systems. We review geological, glaciological, and rock mechanical observations and highlight two key scales that control fluid pressure-enabled frictional instabilities: (1) the length scale over which fluid overpressure is maintained, and (2) a time scale defined by relative rates of deformation propagation and fluid transport. These scales are also dependent on rheological regime, and we suggest three end-member regimes: (1) brittle-localising (BL) regimes where deformation and fluid flow localise to discrete interconnected structures; (2) brittle-delocalising (BD) regimes where deformation and fluid flow are distributed over a broad region, and instability typically stabilised by fluid diffusion; and (3) transiently brittle (TB) regimes where in dominantly viscous rock or ice, fluid pressure may induce a transient frictional rheology that is typically delocalised and stabilised by dilatant hardening. In the BL regime, fluid overpressure can be sustained over a sufficient length scale to enable the nucleation and propagation of frictional instabilities. In the BD and TB regimes, however, fluid-driven instabilities tend to be suppressed, confined to local areas of overpressure, or rate-limited by fluid diffusion, because deformation delocalises in the bulk and/or dilatant hardening limits slip propagation. The three regimes can also be applied to glaciers, where viscous flow of ice competes with frictional sliding on the glacier base—here, sustained and interconnected high water pressure at the glacier base is commonly invoked as promoting frictional instability. In both rock and ice, these concepts imply that fluid-driven frictional instabilities are limited to areas where fluid overpressured patches can be interconnected, and therefore highlight the key role of fluid pressure heterogeneity in development of slip instabilities.

papers.ab: The 2025 M w 6.6 Sanriku-Oki earthquake occurred in a region where slow fault-slip phenomena coexist with ordinary earthquakes. We estimated its source process and investigated relationships of the slip model with seismic and aseismic activity. Joint inversion of S-net seismic and pressure-gauge records revealed a main slip region northeast of the epicenter, with a maximum slip of 1.2 m. Within this region, the rate of increase in cumulative tremor counts gradually decreased, while intervals between tremor bursts increased, possibly reflecting the long-term evolution of postseismic deformation following the 2011 Tohoku earthquake. The average stress drop within the main slip region was 1.4 MPa, which may reflect low effective normal stress associated with low confining pressure and elevated pore-fluid pressure. The spatial coexistence of slow and fast fault-slip phenomena may reflect heterogeneous frictional properties under such a low effective normal stress.

papers.t: Reinforcement learning-based task-aware denoising for ambient and instrument noise in DAS seismic data
in: College of Communication Engineering 1 , , ,
tk: A reinforcement learning-based task-aware denoising model (RL-TAD) adaptively suppresses multitype noise in DAS data by selecting region-specific filtering actions.
基于强化学习的自适应任务感知模型，有效抑制DAS多类型噪声。
papers.ab: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) offers advantages such as low cost, high sampling density, and minor geologic structure identification. However, although highly sensitive fiber-optic sensors effectively capture valuable data, they also introduce complex noise fields containing simultaneous interference from heterogeneous sources, such as ambient vibrations, instrument system noise, and optical artifacts. This complex mixture is termed “multitype noise,” which significantly degrades data quality and intensifies spatiotemporal variation features, posing great challenges for data denoising. Although existing machine learning (ML)-based denoising networks enhance performance by increasing depth or complexity, insufficient attention to multitype noise features limits interpretability. Such architectures are inherently rigid, failing to dynamically adapt to the evolving statistics of new noise types. To handle complex multitype noise in DAS seismic data, a reinforcement learning-based task-aware denoising (RL-TAD) model was proposed. This model decomposed multitype noise suppression into adaptive dominant-noise suppression by region. Under RL-TAD, the asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C) agent was aware of denoising tasks in each data region and formulated visualizable and interpretable filtering policies. These policies guided filtering action selection from the action space for targeted dominant-noise suppression. The region-aware filtering policy aligned with the regional consistency of DAS seismic data in time and reduced computation. The action space took multiple lightweight task-specific denoising networks as efficient filtering actions. Filtering actions can be flexibly adjusted for different noise types. Synthetic and field applications demonstrated that RL-TAD effectively suppressed multitype noise, accurately recovered signal details, and easily adapted to new noise types via fine-tuning.

papers.t: Inverting Debris Flow Basal Impact Forces from Seismic Waveforms via Deep Learning
in: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Potsdam, Potsdam, Germany [DE]
University of Potsdam
Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research WSL
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China
tk: LSTM and xLSTM models successfully invert debris-flow basal impact forces from seismic waveforms, enabling accurate force and volume estimation.
利用LSTM和xLSTM模型从地震波形中高精度反演泥石流底部冲击力。
papers.ab: Debris flows usually generate large basal impact forces because of their gravity-driven nature and moving mass, posing catastrophic threats to mountain communities. This basal impact force is a key parameter for understanding debris-flow dynamics and offers insights for hazard mitigation. However, developing cost-effective and easy-to-maintain approaches to measure or estimate this force remains challenging. While theoretical models have been developed to invert basal impact force from seismic signals, data-driven deep learning approaches offer greater flexibility and scalability, yet their performance for this task remains underexplored. Here, we train a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model and an eXtended LSTM (xLSTM) model to invert basal impact force from debris-flow seismic signals. Formulating the inversion as a regression task, we used 2019 seismic and impact-force data from seven debris-flow events at Illgraben (Switzerland) for training and validation. The 2020-2023 dataset, comprising 21 events, was used to evaluate the trained models and empirical relationships between basal impact force and physical properties. The xLSTM performs similarly to the baseline LSTM across metrics, including root mean squared error and peak inverted basal impact force. Peak-force estimates achieve a mean absolute percentage error of ≤ 5%, equivalent to ≤10 kN. Using xLSTM, we further find a strong correlation (Pearson's r = 0.867) between observed debris-flow volume and cumulative inverted impact force, supporting volume estimation without direct flow measurements. This work provides insights into using seismic signals to estimate debris-flow physical properties, supporting seismic-based early-warning systems that extend beyond event detection to characterize event magnitude and impacts.

tk: Integrates geological mapping, LiDAR, trenching, and vintage seismic reflection to show how inherited crustal structures controlled fault reactivation and evolution in New Zealand's Nelson Thrust Belt.
结合地质填图、LiDAR、探槽与反射地震数据，揭示了新西兰纳尔逊冲断带中继承性地壳结构对断层活化的控制作用。
papers.ab: The Nelson Thrust Belt (NTB) is a contractional structure within the Australian crust, northwest of the Pacific-Australian plate boundary in the northern South Island of New Zealand. Its structure and evolution record the influence of faults inherited from Paleozoic–Early Mesozoic terrane assembly and Late Cretaceous to Eocene rifting. We integrate revised regional mapping, LiDAR imagery, trench and borehole observations, and reinterpreted vintage seismic reflection lines to reconstruct how inherited fabric controlled fault localization and reactivation. The NTB comprises three principal fault groups, F1–F3, in decreasing order of structural elevation, and a local frontal splay, F4. Geometry, reverse ​reactivation, and association with syn- to late-rift deposits indicate that F2 and F3 are inverted normal faults. Fault inversion began in the Late Miocene and continued through the Pliocene–Pleistocene, but activity on F3 ceased earlier than on F2. F1 is a low- to moderate-angle thrust fault that truncates the underlying structures out of sequence. Together, these relationships suggest a long-term break-back transfer of deformation, while Late Pleistocene–Holocene seismic rupture of the major faults indicates that multiple structures were reactivated within overlapping earthquake cycles. The NTB provides a test case for recognizing how inherited crustal heterogeneity controlled long-term fault evolution and distributed active deformation in a contractional belt where modern subsurface imaging is limited.

papers.t: Heterogeneity at Current Rupture-length Scales Governs Multi-fault Earthquake Dynamics
in: School of Science, University of Tokyo, 7-3-1 Bunkyo-4 ku, Hongo, Tokyo, Japan, 113-0033
tk: Analytical modeling reveals that earthquake rupture dynamics are primarily governed by stress-drop heterogeneities at scales comparable to the current rupture length.
理论推导表明，地震破裂动力学主要受与当前破裂长度相当的应力降非均匀性尺度控制。
papers.ab: Stress-drop heterogeneity is widely recognized as an important control on rupture dynamics of multi-fault earthquakes, yet the influence of its scale dependence remains poorly understood. This study derives analytical expressions for the stress intensity factor and static energy release rate for ruptures propagating through heterogeneous stress-drop distributions in Mode II and III. This solution can approximate the effects of the non-planar fault geometry in Mode III. For a single-wavelength heterogeneity, the effect on rupture energetics is described by a dimensionless response function, involving the Fresnel integrals, that reaches its maximum when the heterogeneity wavelength is comparable to the current rupture length. The influence of both shorter- and longer-wavelength heterogeneities decays away from this characteristic scale. Extending the analysis to self-similar multi-wavelength heterogeneity demonstrates that the dominant contribution to rupture energetics always arises from wavelength components comparable to the rupture length, while shorter-wavelength effects are progressively averaged out due to the integral nature of the energetics. This scale-specific property is inherited by rupture arrest conditions, rupture velocity, and fault slip rate through the energy balance and stress intensity factor. The slip-pulse solution in the current model implies that the characteristic wavelength controlling rupture behavior is correlated with the seismogenic-layer thickness. These results imply that unresolved short-wavelength heterogeneity contributes only weakly to the dynamics of large earthquakes, providing a physical explanation for the reproducibility of large-scale rupture processes in dynamic rupture simulations. The theory suggests that uncertainty in earthquake rupture dynamics is intrinsically scale-dependent and that observational constraints on mechanical structures at scales comparable to the rupture dimension are most important for improving the forecastability of large-earthquake rupture scenarios.
