in: Department of Geophysics, State Key Laboratory of Deep Earth Exploration and Imaging, College of GeoExploration Science and Technology, Jilin University, Changchun, Jilin, China
Heilongjiang Earthquake Agency, Harbin, China
tk: Fine-tuning pretrained deep-learning pickers on regional Northeast China data significantly improves P-phase picking for deep-focus earthquakes, while S-phase picking remains challenging.
微调预训练深度学习拾取器显著提升了中国东北深震的P波拾取性能，但S波拾取仍具挑战。
papers.ab: Pretrained deep-learning phase pickers are now widely used in earthquake monitoring, but their transferability to deep-focus earthquakes recorded by regional seismic networks remains poorly constrained. We evaluate three SeisBench pretrained pickers, PhaseNet, EQTransformer, and generalized phase detection (GPD), using manually picked Northeast China deep-focus earthquake records. The fine-tuning set contains 1638 manually picked arrivals (875 P and 763 S arrivals) from 29 events during 2008–2022, 400 noise windows, and data augmentation applied to S-phase waveforms. The blind test uses 660 analyst-reviewed arrivals from four 2023–2025 events recorded by 135 stations, including 86 stations not used during fine-tuning. At validation-selected thresholds and a ± 1.0 s matching tolerance, fine-tuned PhaseNet, EQTransformer, and GPD yield P-phase F1 scores of 0.893, 0.673, and 0.350, respectively, and S-phase F1 scores of 0.315, 0.377, and 0.252. At a stricter ±0.5 s tolerance, the corresponding P-phase F1 scores are 0.758, 0.601, and 0.195, and the S-phase F1 scores are 0.243, 0.283, and 0.154. Post hoc blind-test F1-optimal thresholds are retained only as upper-bound estimates. Record-level bootstrap intervals, matching-tolerance tests, and leave-one-event-out analyses show that PhaseNet P-phase picking improves most clearly. In contrast, S-phase picking remains the primary empirical limitation. One event located near the edge of the source–station geometry strongly affects the pooled performance metrics for S-phase picking. We therefore interpret this result as an illustrative case suggesting possible sensitivity to source–station geometry, rather than as evidence for a general event-level pattern.

papers.t: A Unified Quadratic Scaling Relation Between Potency and Local Earthquake Magnitudes for −1.8 ≤ M L ≤ 7.5
in: Department of Earth and Space Sciences Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
Nevada Seismological Laboratory University of Nevada Reno NV USA
Department of Earth Sciences University of Southern California Los Angeles CA USA
tk: A unified quadratic scaling relation is proposed to link seismic potency and local magnitude across a wide range from -1.8 to 7.5.
提出了一个适用于-1.8至7.5震级范围的地震势与地方震级统一二次定标关系。
papers.ab: Quantifying earthquake size across scales requires linking physical source parameters to empirical magnitude measures, especially for microearthquakes where attenuation, scattering, and instrumental limitations complicate source characterization. We combine regional results with near‐source observations from the Tony Creek dual Microseismic Experiment, dense nodal data from Ridgecrest, and regional broadband data from San Jacinto to extend potency–magnitude scaling to local‐magnitude . Bayesian spectral inference yields robust potency estimates across seven potency magnitude units and nine units. The combined data sets follow a continuous quadratic relation . Synthetic modeling shows that source scaling, attenuation, and the finite Wood–Anderson passband can produce similar nonlinearity, although rupture‐scaling differences may also contribute. Despite sensitivity to observational and regional factors, the independent data sets are broadly consistent with the established quadratic relation, supporting it as a general empirical scaling over the investigated size range.

papers.t: Patch Interactions on a Heterogeneous Fault Drive Nearby Slow and Fast Earthquakes
in: Graduate School of Science Kyoto University Kyoto Japan
Faculty of Science Shizuoka University Shizuoka Japan
tk: Numerical modeling of a heterogeneous fault demonstrates how interactions between different frictional patches can simultaneously drive both slow slip events and fast earthquakes.
异质断层上的斑块相互作用模拟表明，不同摩擦性质斑块的耦合可同时驱动慢地震与快地震。
papers.ab: Tectonic tremor and repeating/regular earthquakes off Iwate in the shallow Japan Trench occur episodically and in spatially overlapping areas, implying a common aseismic driver. We investigate how small aseismic slip triggers events across multiple slip‐rate regimes using fully dynamic earthquake‐cycle simulations governed by rate‐and‐state friction. Along‐fault heterogeneity is imposed by alternating velocity‐weakening (VW) and velocity‐strengthening (VS) patches, and events are classified based on peak slip velocity . A single VW patch produces only aseismic events, whereas a multi‐patch heterogeneous model generates sub‐seismic slip and earthquakes, often nearly synchronous across VW patches. Inter‐event transient slip in VS patches raises stress during subsequent VW nucleation. Transitions in and rupture properties are controlled by subtle stress differences between nucleating VW patches and surrounding VS patches. This mechanism provides a simple physical explanation for why slow and fast earthquakes can emerge from interacting fault patches with spatial overlap and close temporal proximity.

papers.t: Reply to comment on “Insights into a neoproterozoic paleosubduction zone in the NW Borborema province from magnetotelluric data” by Aires et al.
in: Universidade Federal do Oeste do Pará
Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP)
Universidade Federal do Ceará
Universidade de Brasília
tk: The authors defend their magnetotelluric interpretation of a Neoproterozoic paleosubduction zone in the Borborema Province against criticisms regarding petrological and anomaly interpretations.
作者回应了对其利用大地电磁数据解释博博雷马省新元古代古俯冲带的质疑。
papers.ab: We thank the opportunity to respond to the Comment by Aires et al. (2026) on the tectonic interpretation of Braga et al. (2026) for the northwestern Borborema Province. The Comment argues that recent studies by the authors were not considered in our discussion and questions evidence for ultrahigh-pressure metamorphism, exhumation mechanisms, and the interpretation of the C1 conductive anomaly. We clarify that the studies cited in the Comment present an alternative interpretation of regional metamorphic evolution and that the article used as the main basis for questioning coesite was published after submission of our manuscript. We emphasize that much of the Comment focuses on reevaluating petrological, spectroscopic, and geobarometric interpretations from previous studies. These data were neither generated nor reanalyzed by Braga et al. (2026), but were incorporated into the discussion because they derive from peer-reviewed studies established in the regional literature. We demonstrate that the reinterpretation of coesite is based on samples and analytical domains different from those originally analyzed and therefore does not constitute a direct reanalysis of the identified inclusions. Petrological and geobarometric constraints do not justify a regional exclusion of the HP–UHP record. Regarding exhumation, alternative mechanisms, including crustal channel flow, may represent late stages in the evolution of the collisional orogen rather than mutually exclusive solutions. More importantly, these interpretative differences do not affect magnetotelluric result of Braga et al. (2026): C1 is a robust west-dipping crustal conductive anomaly, consistently recovered in 3D inversions. Its geometry is compatible with a paleosubduction-related structure along the eastern margin of the Santa Quitéria Continental Magmatic Arc. The origin of the anomaly and its electrical response do not depend solely on the volumetric abundance of graphite, but mainly on connectivity and continuity along grain boundaries and foliation. These characteristics were discussed and substantiated in our manuscript.

papers.t: Relative and calibrated stress-drop catalog for 2015–2024 Ridgecrest, California earthquakes from spectral-ratio asymptotes.
in: Stanford University
Columbia University
tk: A relative and calibrated stress-drop catalog for the 2015–2024 Ridgecrest, California earthquake sequence, generated using a spectral-ratio-asymptote graph inversion method.
基于谱比渐近线图反演方法构建的2015–2024年加州Ridgecrest地震序列相对与校准应力降目录。
papers.ab: Relative and calibrated stress drops for the Ridgecrest earthquake sequence from the spectral-ratio-asymptote graph inversion of Knudson, Shaw, Ellsworth & Beroza. Preferred configuration: k_nn = 8, 1.5 km edge cap, adaptive LF band, P+S combined, relay threshold M2.3, slope weight W = 0.25 (Table 1 of the paper). One row per event in the inversion graph. Columns: event_id SCSN event identifier origin_time_utc origin time (ISO 8601, UTC) from the SCEDC relocated catalog latitude, longitude degrees; depth_km in km (GrowClust location where available) catalog_magnitude SCSN catalog magnitude; magnitude_type: l = ML, lr = Mlr, w = Mw, blank = no type recorded (1-D/3-D located events) location_method gc = GrowClust (Trugman & Shearer 2017), 1d = Hypoinverse, 3d = SIMULPS growclust_relocated True if GrowClust relocated the event (nbranch > 1) role dual-band (M2.5-4.0, both LFL and HFL solved; the reported population), relay (M2.3-2.5, in the LFL block and additionally admitted to the HFL block to connect it; excluded from reported statistics), LFL-only (M 4.0) hf_group main = connected to the main high-frequency group (1961 dual-band events); disconnected = one of the 24 groups whose level relative to the main population is undetermined (their relative values are internal to the group) n_pairs number of spectral-ratio pairs involving the event (graph degree) mean_pair_separation_m mean 3-D separation of the event's pairs, metres LFL_rel, HFL_rel relative low- and high-frequency levels, log10 units (Eqs. 23-25; each block is zero-mean over the dual-band population) SD_rel_log10 relative log10 stress drop, 1.5*HFL_rel - 0.5*LFL_rel (Eq. 26); dual-band only SD_log10_MPa, SD_MPa calibrated stress drop (Brune model, k = 0.37, beta = 3.5 km/s; Section 6.3); calibration constant C = 6.75 for stress drop in Pa sigma_jackknife per-event uncertainty from the delete-20% pair jackknife, log10 units sigma_bootstrap per-event uncertainty from the station bootstrap, log10 units Catalog and waveforms: Hauksson et al. (2012) relocated catalog, 1981-2024 GrowClust extension distributed by the SCEDC; waveforms and parametric data from the Caltech/USGS Southern California Seismic Network (doi:10.7914/SN/CI) stored at the SCEDC (doi:10.7909/C3WD3xH1).

papers.t: Three‐Dimensional Resistivity Imaging Constrains Crustal Heterogeneity Beneath the 2010 Yushu Ms 7.1 Earthquake Rupture
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research
Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics
National Institute of Natural Hazards
Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences
tk: 3-D magnetotelluric imaging reveals that crustal resistivity transitions and a shallow conductor beneath the Yushu earthquake zone influenced rupture segmentation and aftershock distribution.
三维大地电磁成像表明，玉树地震区地壳电阻率过渡带和浅部导体影响了破裂分段与余震分布。
papers.ab: The 2010 Yushu (eastern Tibetan Plateau) Ms 7.1 strike‐slip earthquake ruptured unilaterally toward the southeast but left a hypocentral segment without mapped surface rupture, followed by a two‐stage reorganization of aftershocks. We present a 3‐D electrical resistivity model from 70 quality‐controlled magnetotelluric sites acquired shortly after the event. Alternative data‐component inversions, 2‐D/3‐D comparisons, and anomaly‐focused forward tests identify the best‐resolved features. A conductive mid–lower crust beneath the Qiangtang block abuts more resistive Bayan Har crust. The mainshock and early aftershocks lie near upper‐crustal resistivity transitions, while a broad shallow conductor extends beneath and beyond the hypocentral surface‐rupture gap. The late conjugate swarm extends into a sparsely sampled sector. The underlying electrical structure is therefore not well resolved. The results indicate that crustal heterogeneity may have influenced rupture segmentation and early aftershock redistribution, whereas the relation to the late swarm requires denser observations.

papers.t: The impact of an in-situ stress gradient on the growth of a fluid-driven frictional rupture
tk: This study models fluid-driven frictional rupture growth along a fault with an in-situ stress gradient, revealing asymmetric up-dip acceleration.
该研究揭示了原位应力梯度导致流体驱动破裂向上倾方向非对称加速。
papers.ab: Models of injection-induced aseismic slip commonly assume uniform in-situ stresses along the fault, and thus predict rupture growth symmetric about the injection point. We relax this assumption and account for linear variations with depth of the resolved shear and effective normal tractions. We consider a planar fault with constant friction under plane-strain conditions, subjected to fluid injection at constant overpressure. Vanishing stress intensity factors at both rupture tips yield two coupled equations for the up-dip and down-dip tip positions. We solve them semi-analytically and compare the results with numerical simulations. The stress gradient notably breaks the self-similarity of the uniform-stress solution. Growth is then governed by two parameters. The first is the fault-stress injection parameter $\mathcal{T}$, ratio between the initial distance to failure at the injection point and the effect of the fluid overpressure. The second is the ratio of the diffusion length $\sqrt{4αt}$ to a stress-gradient length scale $L_c$, namely the initial distance to failure at the injection point divided by its gradient along the fault. Growth is symmetric at early times. In the marginally pressurized regime, rupture lags behind the pressure front and the relative asymmetry grows as $1.1\,(4αt/L_c^2)^{1/2}$. The up-dip tip then accelerates markedly compared to the down-dip tip. In the critically stressed regime, rupture outpaces diffusion by a factor of order $1/\mathcal{T}$, and the relative asymmetry grows as $\sim 0.34\,(4αt/\mathcal{T}^2L_c^2)^{1/2}$. The up-dip tip reaches $\sim L_c$ earlier, and the ratio of up-dip to down-dip rupture lengths remains below two.

papers.t: Dynamic Rupture and Ground-Motion Simulations of Potential Earthquakes on the Jinqianghe–Maomaoshan Fault in China Constrained by Geodetic Interseismic Locking
in: High Performance Computing Department, National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, Shenzhen, China
Department of Earth and Space Sciences, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geophysical High-resolution Imaging Technology, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China
Key Laboratory of Earthquake Forecasting and Risk Assessment, Ministry of Emergency Management, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China
School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
tk: Constrains dynamic rupture and ground-motion simulations of the Jinqianghe–Maomaoshan fault using geodetic interseismic locking, revealing high seismic hazard.
利用大地测量锁合约束金强河-毛毛山断裂破裂模拟，揭示高地震风险。
papers.ab: Physics-based dynamic rupture and ground-motion simulations provide critical constraints for seismic hazard and risk assessment. However, their reliability is limited by the poorly constrained initial stress conditions on faults. To address this issue, we constrain the initial stress distribution in our simulations using geodetic estimates of interseismic locking distribution and slip deficit rate (from Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar and Global Positioning System). We apply this geodetically constrained stress framework to the Jinqianghe–Maomaoshan (JQH–MMS) fault system located within the Tianzhu seismic gap. Scenario dynamic rupture simulations indicate that the fault can generate an earthquake, which would produce peak ground motions exceeding intensity XI on the Chinese Seismic Intensity Scale, highlighting the high seismic risk in the region. To evaluate the impact of our approach, we compared simulated dynamic rupture processes and kinematic ground motions from models with and without geodetically constrained initial stress. The results demonstrate that the locking-derived stress model significantly affects rupture propagation and extent. It also provides a physically grounded framework for seismic risk assessment and mitigation.

papers.t: DETECT: seismological data from multiple dense arrays deployed across the Irpinia fault system in southern Italy
in: University of Naples Federico II
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences
National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics
CNR-IMIOT – Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche - Istituto di Metodologie Integrate per l’Osservazione della Terra
National Research Council
University of Sannio
University of Turin
INGV Osservatorio Vesuviano
University of Salerno
University of Genoa
INGV Osservatorio Nazionale Terremoti
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
École Supérieure d'Électronique de l'Ouest
tk: Presents a 5.2 TB open-access seismological dataset from 20 dense arrays deployed across the active Irpinia fault system in southern Italy.
介绍了意大利南部Irpinia断裂带DETECT项目的5.2 TB密集台阵地震数据集。
papers.ab: We present a large seismological dataset (https://geofon.gfz.de/doi/network/ZK/2021) composed by continuous recordings from 200 temporary stations (seismic network ZK, 10.14470/MX7576871994), which operated continuously for approximately one year in the Southern Apennines (Southern Italy) as part of the DETECT experiment. The dataset is compliant with the seismological standards for the archiving of data and metadata, and with standardized tools for disseminating them, e.g., the International Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks (FDSN) web services. The data set was collected during the DETECT experiment in the Irpinia area (southern Italy), which is one of the regions with the highest seismic hazard in Italy. From August 2021 to August 2022, a constellation of 20 seismic arrays, with a total of 200 seismic stations, was installed above the fault segments responsible for the M 6.9, 1980 Irpinia earthquake, the strongest and most destructive seismic event in Italy in the last fifty years. Each seismic array had a maximum aperture of ~2 km and was composed of one broad-band sensor, one short- period sensor with 1 Hz and eight 4.5 Hz natural frequency geophones. Data and metadata were managed in accordance with the GIPP/GEOFON policy using SeisComP (Helmholtz Centre Potsdam – GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences and GEMPA GmbH, 2008) and the final archive size is approximately 5.2 TB. In this contribution, we provide details on how to download waveform data and station metadata, as well as information on data availability and quality.

papers.t: A fully convolutional neural network to classify UXOs using multicomponent electromagnetic induction data
tk: A sequential fully convolutional neural network classifies unexploded ordnance directly from multicomponent electromagnetic induction data, bypassing physics-based inversion with comparable accuracy.
提出一种双阶段全卷积神经网络，直接从多分量电磁感应数据中分类未爆炸物，无需物理反演。
papers.ab: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance relies on electromagnetic induction (EMI) methods to detect and classify buried and submerged metallic objects, but the standard classification workflow requires physics-based inversion and manual expert review. We present a fully convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies UXO directly from multicomponent time-domain EMI data, bypassing the inversion step entirely. The CNN uses a segmentation-like architecture that preserves the spatial dimensions of the input and outputs a high-resolution classification map suitable for generating a diglist. Two CNNs are used in sequence: the first detects anomalies due to metallic objects and characterizes the spatially correlated noise present in the preprocessed field data; the second performs multi-class classification using synthetic training data augmented with that noise. A physics-based parameterization of the clutter class is used to train the network to discriminate clutter from UXO across a broad range of object types. We validate this approach on two field datasets acquired with the UltraTEMA-4 system at the Sequim Bay marine test site. On a calibration grid with 21 seeded objects, the CNN detects all UXOs and discriminates two out of four clutter objects. On an independent blind grid with 35 seeded objects (17 UXOs, 18 clutter), the CNN detects and classifies all UXOs and achieves a false-positive count comparable to that of the physics-based inversion approach. We see the two methods as complementary: once trained, the CNN classifies rapidly and with minimal supervision, making it well suited as a fast first-pass tool or as an independent check on physics-based results.

papers.t: Enhanced Melt Supply Promotes Near‐Symmetric Oceanic Crustal Accretion at the Ultraslow Eastern Gakkel Ridge
in: State Key Laboratory of Submarine Geoscience Second Institute of Oceanography Ministry of Natural Resources Hangzhou China
tk: Enhanced melt supply at the ultraslow eastern Gakkel Ridge promotes near-symmetric, magma-dominated oceanic crustal accretion, contrasting with magma-poor asymmetric accretion elsewhere.
超慢速扩张的东加克尔脊由于熔体供应增强，促进了近对称的岩浆主导型地壳增生。
papers.ab: Variations in melt supply can shift slow and ultraslow ridges between magmatic and tectonic accretion modes, but whether this effect persists at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge remains unclear. The eastern Gakkel Ridge provides a critical test because it spreads at only ∼6–10 mm/yr yet shows anomalously strong magmatism. We reconstruct sediment thickness and residual basement across the Eurasian Basin using seismic constraints and time‐dependent sedimentation models for the poorly constrained eastern Nansen Basin. Most of the western Eurasian Basin shows deep residual basement and variable flank asymmetry, consistent with magma‐poor ultraslow accretion. Eastward, residual basement becomes progressively shallower and more symmetric. In the eastern Nansen Basin, shallow residual basement persists even under maximum sedimentation, indicating sustained crustal thickening on both conjugate flanks since ∼45 Ma. These results show that enhanced melt supply can shift oceanic crustal accretion toward a near‐symmetric, magma‐dominated mode even at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge.

papers.t: A Neural Network Approach for Quality Control and Interpretation of Single-Station Microtremor Measurements
in: Dipartimento di Fisica e Astronomia, Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna, Bologna, Italy
MoHo srl, Venice, Italy
tk: A feed-forward neural network classifies single-station microtremor H/V spectra into seven categories, providing an automated, robust alternative to traditional SESAME quality control guidelines.
开发了一种前馈神经网络，可对单台微动H/V谱进行七类自动分类与质控。
papers.ab: Single-station ambient noise measurements, analyzed through the horizontal-to-vertical (H/V) spectral ratio, are widely applied in seismic hazard assessment and in stratigraphic reconstructions of the subsurface. In mining exploration and other applied geophysics contexts, large-scale surveys often involve hundreds of measurements to support preliminary bedrock mapping. Under these conditions, there is a strong need for tools that can rapidly evaluate the quality of collected data and guide users—expert or not—in their interpretation. To address this need, we developed and trained a supervised feed-forward neural network to classify different sections of microtremor spectra into seven categories: normal, 1D resonance, 2D or 3D resonance, artifact, velocity inversion, data requiring cleaning, and malfunctioning sensor. The training dataset comprised 3000 examples from over 20 yr of field measurements in diverse geological and environmental settings, processed with consistent windowing, smoothing, and spectral normalization procedures. By analyzing both the individual spectral components and the H/V curve within selected frequency intervals, the neural net produces a probability-based classification for each interval, which can be aggregated into a synthetic quality assessment—accept, reject, or reanalyze—based on predefined criteria. Testing on unseen data yielded an accuracy of about 80%–82%, with the main classification challenge being the distinction between 2D/3D resonances and artifacts due to their spectral similarities. The neural net proved robust to changes in instrument type, analysis window length, and smoothing parameters. This approach offers an alternative to fixed-threshold guidelines such as the SESAME (2004) criteria.

papers.t: Subsurface Deformation and Recovery From the Ridgecrest Mw 7.1 Earthquake Revealed by P ‐Wave Velocity Time‐Lapse Tomography
in: School of Earth Sciences Yunnan University Kunming China
State Key Laboratory of Tibetan Plateau Earth System, Environment and Resources Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) Beijing China
Tongji University Shanghai China
tk: This study uses time-lapse P-wave tomography to image subsurface deformation and post-seismic recovery following the Ridgecrest Mw 7.1 earthquake.
该研究利用P波速度时序断层成像揭示了Ridgecrest地震的震后恢复。
papers.ab: We investigate co‐ and post‐seismic P ‐wave velocity ( V p ) changes following the July 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest strike‐slip earthquake using time‐lapse tomography from 50,345 P ‐wave arrivals (2011–2024). Co‐seismically, V p changes correspond to the volumetric strain change lobes of the earthquake, increasing in compressional zones and decreasing in tensional zones. Post‐seismically, V p changes exhibit a reverse pattern, suggesting ongoing subsurface recovery. Notably, the Coso volcanic field, although distal to the rupture, shows significant co‐seismic velocity reduction and rapid post‐seismic recovery, likely indicating fluid migration or poroelastic effects. These results reveal the complex mechanical and hydrological responses to co‐seismic stress changes and provide important insights into post‐seismic healing processes. Our findings offer robust seismic evidence for the response of material properties to crustal deformation, contributing to improved understanding of structure changes in the earthquake process.

papers.t: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors?
in: ETH Zurich
Swiss Seismological Service
Institute of Geophysics
Boston University
Los Alamos National Laboratory
tk: Evaluates seismic foundation models, finding that current self-supervised objectives redistribute rather than universally improve downstream performance, acting more like feature extractors than true foundation models.
评估地震大模型，发现当前的自监督目标仅重新分配而非全面提升下游任务性能，使其更像特征提取器。
papers.ab: Earthquake sequences are stochastic on two separated timescales: the seismic waves of any individual earthquake propagate over seconds to minutes, while the earthquakes themselves arrive as a sparse, self-exciting occurrence process, with inter-event intervals from seconds to months. Respecting both scales in one training objective is the open challenge. Foundation models (FMs) for seismic waveforms instead import their learning targets from audio and vision, where every target is computed from a single fixed-length window. Such a window holds one realization of the wave propagation (an earthquake trace), never the occurrence process that decides when earthquakes happen. We develop nine model designs sharing one Mamba encoder-decoder, trained on a fixed corpus of 3M windows, varying the self-supervised objective, quantization bottleneck and mixer; the two key comparisons are architecture-matched, varying the objective alone. Each checkpoint is evaluated frozen on three downstream tasks. Varying the target redistributes downstream skill rather than raising it, and no checkpoint wins everywhere. Adding masking pressure to our strongest classifier re-specializes it rather than making it a generalist: it gains 6.9 points of few-shot P-wave picking precision and loses 9.6 points of few-shot classification accuracy. By the standard imported from language and vision, these models are feature extractors rather than FMs. Controls on capacity, architecture, and domain proximity do not explain why skill moves rather than rises. Against task-specific baselines the advantage is regime-dependent: our checkpoints beat them few-shot on classification and ground-motion prediction, and trail them on full data. We argue the binding constraint is the target, and that settling the question requires a learning target defined across events, the timescale that makes seismicity stochastic in the first place.

papers.t: Forward-Backward Map Matching for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
tk: A forward-backward algorithm on factor graphs improves airborne magnetic anomaly navigation accuracy and provides a reliable entropy-based uncertainty metric.
基于因子图的前向-后向算法提高了航空磁异常导航精度，并提供了可靠的熵不确定性度量。
papers.ab: Airborne magnetic anomaly navigation provides a passive, unjammable alternative to Global Navigation Satellite Systems positioning by matching magnetometer measurements against a lithospheric magnetic anomaly map. Existing map-matching algorithms either assume a Gaussian posterior (extended Kalman filter), require Monte Carlo sampling (particle filter), or discard posterior uncertainty in favour of a single optimal path (Viterbi algorithm). Here we formulate map matching as inference on a chain-structured factor graph and solve it segment by segment using the forward-backward algorithm, which yields a discrete posterior over candidate positions and its Shannon entropy $H_t$ at time $t$. Over the \texttt{Renfrew\_395} map, $10^3$ synthetic trials yield a median position error of $32.7$ m, $91\%$ below the median inertial drift of $362$ m. On these trials and $10^3$ flight paths, the median error is $43\%$ below the extended Kalman filter and particle filter. Across these paths, a threshold on segment-level entropy detects $47\%$ of segments with errors above two map cells and $94\%$ of those above three, at a $10\%$ false-alarm rate. The foregoing results indicate that $H_t$ provides a truth-free diagnostic of map-conditioned navigation ambiguity.

papers.t: Advancing global crop simulations with differentiable modelling
tk: A new differentiable global gridded crop model enables efficient parameter calibration, yield loss attribution, and management optimization using automatic differentiation.
一种新型可微全球作物模型利用自动微分实现了高效的参数校准与优化。
papers.ab: Global gridded crop models (GGCMs) are crucial for assessing the performance of food producing systems, for example under climate change or their contribution to environmental challenges. However, systematic calibration of their parameters remains a long-standing challenge. Persisting uncertainties in these parameters propagate into future crop projections, thereby affecting and potentially biasing food security assessments. Here we present a fully process-based differentiable GGCM implementation that offers a fundamentally new approach to parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, yield loss attribution, and management optimization. Using automatic differentiation, we optimize selected model parameters against site-scale carbon and water flux observations, reducing normalized root-mean-square errors at held-out sites by 24.8-36.2% compared to the default state-of-the-art model. Without calibration against yield data, the optimized model better captures detrended yield anomalies across 61.2-64.3% of global crop area and reduces low-yield errors by 3.4-43.5% for wheat, rice, maize and soybean. It also ranks among the best performers in comparison with GGCMI Phase 3 models. Future simulations show that calibration reduces the projected end-of-century rice production increase from 55.1% to 22.1% under SSP5-8.5. Parameter ensembles further reveal that parameterizations with comparable historical skill can produce markedly different future production responses. Beyond calibration, differentiability enables the attribution of crop losses under extreme events and supports the design of adaptive crop management strategies. For the 2018 European drought, we identify spring heat and water limitation as major contributors to wheat yield losses and develop more effective irrigation strategies for mitigating simulated regional yield losses.

papers.t: Syvä-Suomi: Illuminating the Finnish lithosphere with geophysical arrays
in: Geological Survey of Finland, Vuorimiehentie 5, Espoo, Finland
Department of Geosciences and Geography
University of Helsinki
Institute for Geophysics
Polish Academy of Sciences
tk: Syvä-Suomi is Finland's national-scale geophysical initiative, starting with a nationwide magnetotelluric survey, to build a digital twin of the Finnish lithosphere.
Syvä-Suomi是芬兰的一项国家级地球物理计划，旨在通过大地电磁测量构建岩石圈数字孪生。
papers.ab: The continental lithosphere preserves the record of tectonic evolution while hosting resources and structures of major scientific and societal importance. In Finland, lithosphere has been investi-gated through numerous geological and geophysical surveys, but differences in spatial coverage, acquisition and resolution limit their integration into a consistent national-scale representation. Global initiatives have shown that the modern way to image the lithosphere is systematic, at national or even continental scale, with uniform coverage and standardised acquisition, an approach that is more effective, more economical and more environmentally sustainable. Syvä-Suomi is Finland’s contribution to this movement, at unprecedented resolution, and the foundation of a digital twin of the Finnish lithosphere into which decades of legacy geophysical data and complementary geoscientific data and models can be integrated. The initiative is intended to be multiphysics, opening with a nationwide long-period magnetotelluric survey and designed to grow through further geophysical methods. Past, present and future observations can then be assimilated into a single representation of the subsurface, maintained and updated continually. A national model can support applications in resources, energy, infrastructure, geological waste disposal and geohazards, while advancing understanding of Fennoscandian tectonic evolution. The multidisciplinary scope of the initiative also makes it a training ground for the next generation of geoscientists, data scientists and AI researchers in Finland and beyond.

papers.t: Systematic Evaluation and Development of Long-Period Coda Moment Magnitude (Mwo) for Large Earthquakes
in: State Key Laboratory of Deep Earth and Mineral Exploration and Hebei Hongshan National Observatory on Thick Sediments and Seismic Hazards, School of Earth and Space Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, China
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Ludwig-Maximilians-University, Munich, Germany
tk: This study systematically evaluates and improves the long-period coda moment magnitude (Mw0) method, extending its robust applicability to earthquakes with Mw >= 7.5.
本研究系统评估并改进了长周期尾波矩震级方法，将其推广至Mw>=7.5。
papers.ab: The coda moment magnitude (Mwo) has recently been proposed based on the long-period and long-lasting coda energy of large earthquakes. In this study, we perform a systematic evaluation of the Mwo method on its robustness and applicability using a large dataset of 132 large earthquakes from January 2000 to March 2023. The results demonstrate that the Mwo is in general agreement with the moment magnitude (Mw) from the Global Centroid Moment Tensor, with the former being slightly larger. For relatively smaller events (Mw<8.3), the residual between the Mwo and Mw increases with decreasing magnitude. Further synthetic tests indicate that the background noise (or the signal-to-noise-ratio) is the primary factor for the deviation of Mwo for smaller events. After comparing different approaches, we propose an empirical relationship to correct the Mwo for events with Mw<8.3. Examination of other potential influences reveals a minimal impact, showing the robustness of the corrected Mwo and the enhanced Mwo method retains the advantages of potentially capturing a broader portion of the seismic energy release. Its stability has been shown to be largely insensitive to variations in epicenter location and the number of stations and to be only mildly sensitive to changes in source focal mechanisms and depth of hypocenter. Furthermore, the improved method is applicable to earthquakes with Mw≥7.3 when a sufficient number of high-quality coda measurements is available, with the recommended and more robust operational range being Mw≥7.5, thereby extending its capability for accurate magnitude determination of large earthquakes.

papers.t: 4D sensitivity kernels for infrasound atmospheric propagation: considering the need and impact of time dependent observation operators for acoustic wave observations in data assimilation methods
tk: This paper presents an adjoint-based method to compute 4D sensitivity kernels for infrasound propagation in a time-varying atmosphere, improving atmospheric data assimilation.
本文提出了一种计算时变背景大气中微声传播4D敏感核的方法，显著提升了大气数据同化效果。
papers.ab: The long range propagation of acoustic waves in Earth's atmosphere is sensitive to winds and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Thus, infrasound observations have a strong potential to improve numerical weather models by data assimilation methods. However, because acoustic waves propagate slowly, the atmospheric parameters can change during the propagation of the acoustic waves. This change of atmosphere properties is usually not taken into account by infrasound simulation tools which generally assume stationary atmosphere models. In order to close this modeling gap, we present here a method to compute the linear sensitivities of infrasound observables to atmospheric parameters varying both in space and time. We show that adjoint based methods can easily handle this computation of 4D sensitivity kernels, also called time variable observation operators in the data assimilation community. Then, we discuss the capabilities of various data assimilation methods to handle such observation operators. We demonstrate that only variational methods with data assimilation windows longer than the propagation duration of the long range infrasound can accommodate these observations, as well as their ensemble counterparts. Finally, we demonstrate the benefit of assimilating such long range infrasound observations, and we quantify the relative impact of linear approximation of observation operators and stationary approximation of the atmosphere model by assimilating propagation time observations of circumnavigating Lamb waves in Lorenz'96 low-order model. The results of this data assimilation experiment demonstrate that the time variability of atmospheric parameters should be taken into account even for infrasound propagation times limited to 2 or 3 time steps of the atmosphere model.

papers.t: PKIKPPKIKP Versus PKiKPPKiKP : A New Pair of Seismic Phases for Mapping the Earth’s Inner Core
in: University of Bucharest, Bucharest, Romania
National Institute for Earth Physics, Măgurele, Romania
Marine Science and Technology College, Zhejiang Ocean University, Zhoushan, China
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Potsdam, Germany
tk: Introduces PKIKPPKIKP–PKiKPPKiKP differential travel times near 90° as a new seismic phase pair to probe the Earth's inner core structure with minimal mantle path effects.
引入PKIKPPKIKP–PKiKPPKiKP差分走时对，用于高精度探测地球内核结构并减少地幔不均匀性的影响。
papers.ab: The Earth’s uppermost inner core (IC) is a critical boundary region where thermal, compositional, and mechanical interactions between the liquid outer-core and solid IC influence solidification processes and the geodynamo. Previous studies relied primarily on PKIKP–PKiKP seismic phases recorded at epicentral distances of 130°–142°. Here, we introduce a complementary approach by analyzing PKIKPPKIKP–PKiKPPKiKP differential times near 90° from deep earthquakes. These rare, multiply reflected phase pairs sample the IC on both descending and ascending paths and share similar trajectories, minimizing the influence of mantle heterogeneity. We measure their differential arrival times via waveform cross correlation in the 0.7–2 Hz frequency band and compute residuals with respect to synthetic seismograms that account for earthquake source mechanisms. These residuals are directly sensitive to P-wave velocity anomalies in the IC. In addition, we identify a new small set of PKIKPPKIKP and PKPbcPKPbc arrivals near 60°, which could support future studies of deeper IC regions. Statistical analysis using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria favors a single-parameter isotropic model, suggesting that the observed residuals can be explained without introducing additional anisotropy. Our results highlight the untapped value of rare, multiply reflected core phase pairs in probing Earth’s deep interior.

papers.t: Seismic Discrimination of Natural and Anthropogenic Events Near Atlanta, Georgia, USA
tk: A machine-learning-assisted workflow searches 14 years of seismic data near Atlanta, discriminating 2,181 events to reveal dominant quarry-blast activity and localized rock exfoliation signals.
利用机器学习工作流检索亚特兰大14年地震数据，识别并鉴定了2181个采石场爆破与自然地震事件。
papers.ab: Distinguishing small earthquakes from anthropogenic seismic sources is important for accurate fault characterization and seismic hazard assessment, yet remains challenging in regions with sparse seismic networks and frequent quarry activities. Around Atlanta, Georgia, only a small number of local natural earthquakes and one operator-confirmed quarry blast in July 2026 are reported in regional USGS catalogs in recent years. Here we use three cataloged earthquakes and the 2026 quarry blast as references to search 14 years of continuous seismic and pressure records at a nearby permanent station N4.Y52A. Based on a machine-learning-assisted workflow, we identify 2,181 impulsive events with clear seismic arrivals, associated pressure disturbances, and reliable particle-motion measurements. Most of them occur during weekday working hours and exhibit repeated source-distance and directional patterns that correspond to known quarry areas, indicating that the detected population is dominated by quarry-blast activity. The search also recovers smaller earthquake candidates and short event sequences with more ambiguous origins, demonstrating that waveform similarity or occurrence time alone cannot determine source type. As an independent case study, we reassess signals previously associated with a 17 July 2023 spontaneous rock exfoliation event at Arabia Mountain. The previously associated regional signal is more consistent with quarry activity, whereas subsequent exfoliation events in 2024 produced highly localized signals recorded only by a near-source dense array but not clearly at N4.Y52A. These results demonstrate that improved seismic detection must be accompanied by independent seismic, acoustic, spatial, and direct observational constraints for reliable source identification.

papers.t: Present-Day Soil Gas Geochemistry Along the 1975 Ms 7.3 Haicheng Earthquake Rupture Zone: Fault-Controlled Migration Five Decades after the Earthquake
in: Liaoning Earthquake Agency, Shenyang, China
China Earthquake Networks Center, Beijing, China
Institute of Earthquake Forecasting, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China
tk: Soil gas geochemistry along the 1975 Haicheng earthquake rupture zone reveals persistent fault-controlled deep fluid migration five decades post-event.
1975年海城地震破裂带的土壤气体测量表明，震后50年仍存在断裂控制的深部流体运移。
papers.ab: Although substantial gas emissions from postearthquake rupture zones have been documented, their underlying mechanisms, sources, and fault-related migration pathways remain uncertain. Here, we present a systematic tectonogeochemical survey across the surface rupture zone of the 1975 Ms 7.3 Haicheng earthquake, northeast China. A total of 233 sampling sites were established for soil gas concentration measurements, among which nine were further selected for carbon isotope analysis. Synchronous in situ measurements of Rn, CO2, and H2 concentrations were performed at all sites to elucidate the spatial coupling between soil gas concentration anomalies, seismic activity, and fault structures. The results indicate that soil gas concentrations along the rupture zone remain higher than those in background areas 50 yr after the Haicheng earthquake. The peak concentrations of Rn, CO2, and H2 reach 376.60 kBq/m3, 9.98 vol.%, and 1292.00 ppm, respectively, implying distinct geochemical anomalies along the fault zone. The carbon isotope results reveal that the contribution of deep-derived CO2 ranges from approximately 5% to 12%, indicative of the potential upward migration of deep crustal fluids. According to the analysis of gas emission-controlling factors, fault offset, persistent small-to-moderate seismicity, and deep fluid activity are likely the primary controls on these geochemical anomalies. Furthermore, the pronounced H2 anomalies and unique geological conditions of the Haicheng area may be useful for regional geochemical screening of fault-controlled gas migration. In conclusion, this study provides a representative case for understanding decadal-scale postseismic gas migration and its primary controls along the rupture zone of a major continental earthquake.

papers.t: Spatial Colorimetric Mapping of pH and Dissolved Carbon during Convective Dissolution of CO{\_2}: Constraints from Domain, Geometry, and Indicator Mix on Measurement Reliability
tk: This paper evaluates the reliability of spatial colorimetry for mapping pH and dissolved CO2 during convective dissolution across different domains, geometries, and indicator concentrations.
该研究评估了空间比色法在不同介质、几何和指示剂浓度下测量CO2溶解的可靠性。
papers.ab: Quantifying the dissolution and buoyancy-driven transport of CO2-rich water is critical to understanding solubility trapping mechanism in geologic storage. Analog-fluid density driven convection experiments do not represent CO2 dissolution chemistry or the aqueous CO2 density-concentration monotonic relationship. X-ray tomography does not provide enough contrast to directly measure dissolved CO2. Spatial colorimetry provides an inexpensive method to map pH and estimate total dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) via carbonate equilibrium assumptions. However, the effects of experimental conditions such as domain (free fluid and porous), geometry (2D and 3D), and indicator mix concentration on the reliability of pH and CT measurements remain unexplored. We evaluated how these factors affect the reliability of measurements using two different colorimetric models (hue and spherical coordinates (θ and φ)). Hue was reliable in all domains whereas θ-φ was reliable in free fluid. Lower indicator mix concentration increased the chromatic sensitivity at low pH in free fluid; however, it did not produce sufficient color contrast for pH calibration and mapping in the porous domain. In the porous domain, θ-φ calibration was 33 times more susceptible to noise than hue. Temporal pH noise was less than 0.01 units; spatial noise changed domain-mean CT by 0.6-4.4{\%}. Both models were able to resolve CO2-rich plumes in free fluid; however, θ-φ had sharper plume boundaries than hue. The temporal evolution of CO2 dissolution resolved by the color models agreed more in 2D than 3D. These findings provide a reliability framework for studying subsurface dissolution and mixing of CO2.

papers.t: On dependence of the source deactivation factor on the magnitude of main earthquake shock
tk: Clarifies a phenomenological method to calculate the source deactivation coefficient from aftershocks using 'proper time', showing its inverse relationship with mainshock magnitude.
基于“固有时间”计算震源去激活系数，其与主震震级呈反比。
papers.ab: We have discovered an inverse relationship between the earthquake source deactivation coefficient and the magnitude of the main shock. Recently, this pattern was confirmed through an analysis of earthquakes in the Central Himalayas (Poudel et al., 2026). On the one hand, independent confirmation of a previously unknown pattern strengthens our confidence in the relevance of the phenomenological theory of aftershocks, upon which we have based our method for processing and analyzing aftershocks. On the other hand, Poudel et al. (2026) presented our method in a distorted manner. Poudel et al. mistakenly believe that our method is based on a modified Omori law. Both circumstances provide an occasion and a basis for a simple and clear explanation of the essence of our approach to the study of aftershocks. First and foremost, our approach to the problem is diametrically opposed to Omori approach. Omori law and its modification, proposed by Hirano and Utsu, describe the decay of aftershocks. In contrast, we formulated and solved the inverse problem. The essence of the inverse problem lies in the need to calculate the source deactivation coefficient based on aftershock observation data, without making any prior assumptions regarding the law governing the decay of aftershocks. A crucial concept in our theory is the rather complex notion of the proper time of a source. Proper time differs radically from astronomical time. The paper describes the continuous and discrete representations of proper time. This paper is methodological in nature and may prove useful to researchers studying the dynamics of an earthquake source following the formation of a main rupture within the rock mass. Keywords: earthquake source, main shock, relaxation, deactivation coefficient, proper time, inverse problem.

papers.t: Estimating urban subsurface models using metro seismic signals
in: School of Earth and Space Science and Technology, Wuhan University , Wuhan, Hubei 430072 ,
tk: Proposes a metro seismic interferometry workflow using stationary-phase zone analysis to reconstruct high-quality empirical Green's functions for urban subsurface imaging.
提出基于驻相区分析的地铁地震干涉法，实现高精度城市地下成像。
papers.ab: Summary Traffic-induced seismic waves provide valuable signals for characterizing the subsurface structures. The operation of metro systems generates powerful, broadband, and repetitive seismic signals that propagate in the urban subsurface. This repeatability mainly arises from scheduled metro operations on fixed tunnel routes with similar metro wagons, speed, and weights. Unlike other traffic signals that are generated by vehicles running on the free surface, the metro operates in subsurface tunnels. The use of metro-induced signals for the estimation of the subsurface model, however, remains unexplored. This paper proposes a metro seismic interferometry workflow for urban subsurface characterization. We analyse the characteristics of metro signals and derive a formula for the stationary-phase zone (SPZ) analysis of metro sources. Empirical Green’s functions (EGFs) are estimated by selecting segments of metro signals when the metro is in the SPZ. We performed a field study in Wuhan, China, by deploying a seismic survey line approximately 70° to a metro line. The EGFs reconstructed from multi-component metro seismic signals show distinct Rayleigh and Love waves. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the EGFs is further improved by stacking multiple metro events. The SNR and the accuracy of the dispersion curves estimated from the EGFs with SPZ analysis are much higher than those obtained without SPZ analysis, demonstrating the validity of our proposed method. The comparison with dispersion curves obtained from road traffic signals shows the reliability of the proposed method. In addition, the EGFs also contain abundant guided P waves with high SNR, enabling the reconstruction of the P-wave velocity model. This work shows that utilizing metro seismic waves provide a powerful, efficient, and cost-effective approach for the estimation and monitoring of urban subsurface models.

papers.t: SEQNet: A Multiscale Feature Attention and Global Feature Aggregation Network for Seismic Waveform Denoising
in: China Earthquake Networks Center, Beijing, China
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting, Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China
tk: SEQNet improves seismic waveform denoising by integrating multiscale feature attention and global feature aggregation, balancing waveform fidelity and contrast enhancement.
SEQNet通过整合多尺度特征注意力和全局特征聚合，提升了地震波形去噪的保真度。
papers.ab: Deep-learning denoising is increasingly used for earthquake monitoring, and time–frequency mask-reconstruction models such as DeepDenoiser have shown strong potential for seismic waveform recovery. However, many existing approaches still rely on U-Net-like backbones, leaving the contribution of denoising-specific architectural design insufficiently isolated. Here, we introduce SEQNet, an architecture-focused seismic waveform denoising model that integrates multiscale feature attention (MFA) and global feature aggregation (GFA) into a phase-sensitive time–frequency mask-reconstruction framework. MFA refines encoder features through multiscale context and attention, whereas GFA incorporates bottleneck-level global summaries before decoding. Using paired event–noise waveforms from INSTANCE and STEAD with physical-event-level separation, matched ablation experiments identify MFA as the most strongly supported architectural contribution, while the aggregate effect of GFA is smaller and metric-dependent. Compared with DeepDenoiser and representative conventional methods, SEQNet shows a more favorable reference-based waveform-fidelity profile, whereas DeepDenoiser often produces stronger event-to-pre-event contrast. Trace-level analysis further shows that contrast enhancement and waveform fidelity can disagree on the same records, and a four-day continuous Lushan aftershock test examines downstream phase-picking behavior in continuous data. These results show that targeted architectural modifications can improve waveform-oriented seismic denoising and that module attribution should distinguish waveform fidelity from contrast enhancement.

papers.t: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
in: University of Oslo
The University of Texas at Austin
University of Texas Institute for Geophysics
tk: Self-supervised embeddings of continuous borehole measurements outperform expert lithological labels in predicting sediment physical properties.
自监督钻孔物理测量嵌入比专家岩性标签能更好地预测沉积物性质。
papers.ab: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. We train an self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged properties (bulk density, magnetic susceptibility, natural gamma radiation, and red, green and blue reflectance) across 236,963 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder that has a heteroscedastic Gaussian decoder and learnable mask tokens. The embeddings separate geologist-assigned lithologies as well as a variant trained with those labels, and increasing the weight on the labels degrades reconstruction while leaving classification unchanged. The labels are recoverable from the measurements geologists use to assign them, so training on them adds nothing. Lithological categories compress continuous measurements into classes, and compressing them discards what the measurements record about the processes that produced the rock. The embeddings also predict physical properties that were absent from training, on boreholes the model has never seen. While depth should account for this since sediments compact with burial, it does not. On held-out boreholes depth alone reaches a median $R^2$ of -0.02, against 0.20 for the embedding.

papers.t: A flexible regularization for magnetic vector inversion with petrophysical, structural, and sparsity constraints
tk: A new magnetic vector inversion regularization incorporates petrophysical, structural, and sparsity constraints without coordinate-aligned artifacts.
一种引入物性、结构和稀疏约束且无坐标伪影的磁矢量反演新方法。
papers.ab: Magnetic vector inversion (MVI) is widely used because it can account for both induced and remanent magnetization by inverting for a magnetization vector model. This flexibility comes at the cost of nonuniqueness, since the number of unknowns is three times that of scalar inversion, and prior information can be required to make the result geologically useful. Recent work has applied sparse norms to the vector model, but many of the other tools for incorporating prior information within scalar inversions remain either unavailable for a vector model or unavailable without introducing artifacts or significant nonlinearity. We introduce a vector regularization, formulated in Cartesian coordinates, that generalizes existing sparse Cartesian formulations. We formulate the smallness term to admit a Cartesian reference model, from susceptibility and oriented remanence, and a magnitude reference model, from unoriented remanence or total magnetization. Because a nonzero magnitude reference model makes the Hessian of the smallness term indefinite, we derive its eigendecomposition analytically and modify the eigenvalues so that standard conjugate-gradient solvers can be applied. We formulate the smoothness term to penalize changes in both the direction and magnitude of magnetization. It is independent of the choice of Cartesian basis, so sparse norms can be applied without coordinate-aligned artifacts, and it admits arbitrary preferred smoothing directions through a rotated gradient operator. We demonstrate the method on synthetic data from a folded body with spatially variable magnetization direction, where each form of prior information improves the recovered model. We then apply it to airborne magnetic data over the DO-27 kimberlite, where incorporating petrophysical measurements yields a model more consistent with the measured properties and the geologic model inferred from drilling.

papers.t: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
tk: Self-supervised embeddings of marine sediment physical properties outperform expert lithological labels in predicting unseen physical properties, demonstrating that categorical labels discard valuable continuous information.
自监督海洋沉积物物性嵌入在预测未知物性上优于专家岩性标签，表明分类标签丢弃了连续测量信息。
papers.ab: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. We train an self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged properties (bulk density, magnetic susceptibility, natural gamma radiation, and red, green and blue reflectance) across 236,963 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder that has a heteroscedastic Gaussian decoder and learnable mask tokens. The embeddings separate geologist-assigned lithologies as well as a variant trained with those labels, and increasing the weight on the labels degrades reconstruction while leaving classification unchanged. The labels are recoverable from the measurements geologists use to assign them, so training on them adds nothing. Lithological categories compress continuous measurements into classes, and compressing them discards what the measurements record about the processes that produced the rock. The embeddings also predict physical properties that were absent from training, on boreholes the model has never seen. While depth should account for this since sediments compact with burial, it does not. On held-out boreholes depth alone reaches a median $R^2$ of -0.02, against 0.20 for the embedding.

papers.t: Super-resolution method based on a Transformer: a novel solution for improving the quality of stacked or migrated seismic data
in: Northeast Electric Power University, Key Laboratory of Modern Power System Simulation and Control and Renewable Energy Technology (Ministry of Education), Jilin City, China
Jilin University, College of Instrumentation and Electrical Engineering, Changchun, China
tk: A novel Transformer-based super-resolution method (SDST) simultaneously performs denoising, interpolation, and frequency extrapolation on stacked or migrated seismic data.
提出一种基于Transformer的超分辨率方法，可同时对叠后或偏移地震数据进行去噪、插值和频率外推。
papers.ab: Seismic data obtained after stacking or migration typically exhibit low dominant frequency, sparse spatial and temporal sampling, and may retain a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) even after stacking. To enhance the resolution of seismic data, we propose a deep learning-based single-step super-resolution (SR) method that simultaneously performs denoising, interpolation, and frequency extrapolation. We design a seismic data super-resolution Transformer (SDST) to extract and fuse local and global features from low-resolution seismic data, with particular emphasis on the amplitude characteristics and spatial continuity of effective events (e.g., horizons, folds, faults). Edge information from the input data is extracted using the Canny algorithm and used as a mask to generate an edge map, which is then concatenated with the raw data to form a two-channel input, thereby improving amplitude preservation and noise suppression. The SDST backbone comprises residual groups containing Swin Transformer layers which capture features within windows while reducing the computational cost of self-attention by restricting attention to finite-sized windows. Pixel shuffle layers are employed to efficiently upsample the output feature maps from the SDST backbone, thereby enhancing the details of geological structures. In addition, upsampling the input data through a skip connection helps preserve the output amplitudes, particularly for weak events. We prepare 3-dimensional (3D) synthetic seismic volumes with complex geological structures, half of which contain a mixture of strong- and weak-amplitude events. 2-dimensional (2D) slices are then randomly selected from these volumes to construct training datasets that better approximate the characteristics of field data for supervised learning. Numerical tests on both synthetic and field data from different exploration regions demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method.

papers.t: Detection of seismic events via cluster analysis of trimmed spectrograms
in: Department of Physics, University of Alberta, Edmonton, AB, Canada
tk: CATS is a transparent seismic event detection method using cluster analysis of trimmed spectrograms and the B-E-DATE noise estimator.
CATS是一种基于修剪谱图聚类分析的透明地震事件检测方法。
papers.ab: Due to the growth of data volumes in monitoring seismicity, automation is crucial to fully use the information content. Seismic event detection is the first step in processing, aimed at reducing the amount of data by extracting intervals with seismic activity. At the same time, interpretability remains important for justification and quality control of the detected events, especially when multiple candidate events are to be triaged. A novel seismic event detection technique based on cluster analysis of trimmed spectrograms (CATS) is presented. It uses an automatic noise estimator, B-E-DATE, and cluster filtering in the time-frequency domain. CATS workflow is fully transparent, offering a framework for comprehensive quality control. Evaluated on the benchmark dataset TXED, CATS showed competitive performance compared to traditional and deep learning methods by showing high recall, precision, and F-scores. Furthermore, CATS can be extended to multi-station processing and employed directly for denoising without requiring any extra parameters, and its outputs can be utilized for phase-picking and event classification.

papers.t: Magnetic Topological Evolution and the Predictive Role of Winding-flux-based Masked PILs in Extreme Solar Flares from AR13664 and AR13842
tk: This paper analyzes magnetic topological evolution and winding-flux-based masked polarity inversion lines to predict extreme solar flares from active regions.
该研究分析了磁拓扑演化和基于绕转磁通的极性反转线，以预测极端太阳耀斑。
papers.ab: Using vector magnetogram data from the Helioseismic Magnetic Imager (HMI) on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present detailed case studies of precursor activity in Active Regions (ARs) 13664 and 13842, which produced several intense flares. We examined the spatiotemporal evolution of key magnetic topological parameters, including winding, helicity, winding-flux-based masked polarity inversion lines (PILs), and PIL gradients, from the precursor to the post-flare phases. The temporal evolution of the winding flux showed a significant enhancement during the precursor phase, and this trend was consistent across the seven X-class and five M-class flares (>= M5.0). The spatial distribution of both raw and Gaussian-smoothed winding-flux enhancement is co-located with flare footpoint regions of highly twisted core fields, as indicated by the photospheric magnetic topology. The winding-flux-based masked PILs that persisted around the flare locations showed a significant increase in strength and area during the precursor activity. These masked PILs spatially coincide with regions likely hosting non-potential core magnetic fields associated with the observed flares. Furthermore, the gradient of strong PILs extracted from the ARs was positively correlated with flare-associated locations and typically increased several hours (approx. 3-5 h) before flare onset. By imposing a gradient threshold on strong PILs, we isolate magnetic regions repeatedly associated with flare initiation, providing useful constraints in regimes where current flare-forecasting models remain uncertain. Therefore, the combined analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of different magnetic topological parameters enhances our understanding of intense solar flare forecasting and the identification of potential triggering sites, thereby contributing to improved space weather prediction frameworks.

papers.t: Comment on essd-2026-513
in: University of Turin
University of Naples Federico II
Institute of Geosciences and Earth Resources
National Research Council
Institute for Agricultural and Forest Systems in the Mediterranean
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
Istituto per il Rilevamento Elettromagnetico dell'Ambiente
tk: A high-resolution 3D crustal model of the Southern Apennines is constructed by integrating geological, geophysical, and petrophysical data, validated with independent borehole and receiver function data.
通过整合地质、地球物理和岩石物理数据，构建并验证了南亚平宁山脉的高分辨率三维地壳模型。
papers.ab: The Southern Apennines in Italy represent a geologically complex and seismically active region shaped by the ongoing convergence between the African and Eurasian plates. In this study, we present a high-resolution 3D crustal model of the Southern Apennines, parameterized on a 5 × 5 × 1 km³ grid and constructed through the systematic integration of geological, geophysical, and petrophysical data. The considered dataset includes laboratory velocity measurements (vp) under different pressure and temperature conditions, stratigraphic well logs, seismic tomography (vp), and geophysical models from inversion of gravimetric and magnetic data. Pressure- and temperature-dependent corrections were applied to P-wave velocities derived from regional seismic tomography, enabling us to delineate key intra-crustal boundaries, including the top of the Mesozoic limestones, the base of the Mesozoic sedimentary succession, the onset of the felsic crystalline basement, and the deeper transition to mafic, gabbroic lower-crustal units, within a 3D volume extending down to the Moho discontinuity. This modelling strategy ensures full internal consistency across spatial scales and tectonic domains, and is validated using independent borehole data, receiver functions, and other geophysical interpretations. The resulting 3D volume offers a robust framework for investigating crustal architecture and supports applications in geophysical modeling and seismic hazard assessments. All datasets are openly accessible under FAIR principles, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and interdisciplinary reuse of the results.

papers.t: Geophysical characteristics of a fossil transform plate boundary; case of the Central European Variscides
in: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
TU Bergakademie Freiberg
tk: Integrates 2D seismic reflection and potential-field data to characterize the fossil Gondwana–Laurussia transform plate boundary, identifying distinct high- and low-strain crustal domains.
结合二维地震反射和位场数据，揭示了中欧华力西造山带中化石转换板块边界的深部地壳结构特征。
papers.ab: Crustal-scale strike-slip zones within transform plate boundaries, as imaged by seismic reflection profiles, commonly appear as low-reflectivity zones in the crust and at the Moho, often overprinted by younger deformation phases. To investigate the geophysical characteristics of fossil strike-slip plate boundaries and assess whether features formed during the initial strike-slip stage are preserved at depth, we study the Gondwana–Laurussia plate boundary zone in Central Europe. We integrate two-dimensional seismic reflection and potential-field data with surface geological information and constraints from basement wells. Based on geophysical characteristics, we subdivide the Saxo-Thuringian Zone, south of the Gondwana–Laurussia boundary zone, into three domains. The northwestern and southeastern domains display high-amplitude, continuous reflections and are interpreted as high-strain domains. The northwestern domain is further interpreted as a strike-slip-dominated region overprinted by late Variscan shortening, analogous to structures exposed in the northwestern Bohemian Massif and the Mid-German Crystalline Zone. In contrast, the Central-domain displays low–amplitude, discontinuous reflections and is interpreted as a low-strain domain bounded by high-strain domains. Although our geophysical observations are dominated by late Variscan compression that overprinted the strike-slip phase, they retain characteristics that allow the identification of a fossil transform plate boundary zone.

papers.t: Distribution model of fault locking and slip rate in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau under joint constraints of GNSS, InSAR, and leveling data
in: Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics
Lanzhou University
China Earthquake Administration
Nanjing University
tk: This study jointly inverts GNSS, InSAR, and leveling data to construct a high-resolution fault locking and slip rate model for the northeastern Tibetan Plateau.
该研究联合GNSS、InSAR和水准数据，构建了青藏高原东北缘高分辨率的断层锁定与滑移速率模型。

papers.t: Unified Explanation of Long-Period Ground Motion Using the Basin Sloshing Index (BSI): A Dimensionless Analysis of Large-Scale Sloshing Phenomena in Sedimentary Basins
tk: Introduces the Basin Sloshing Index (BSI) as a dimensionless framework to unify the explanation of long-period basin shaking and whole-Earth free oscillations.
引入盆地晃动指数（BSI）这一无量纲框架，统一解释盆地长周期震动与地球自由振荡。
papers.ab: This study introduces a new dimensionless index, the Basin Sloshing Index (BSI), to provide a unified explanation for long-period ground motion and persistent shaking observed in large sedimentary basins. Inspired by fluid sloshing dynamics, BSI is defined using three fundamental parameters—the basin scale L, seismic wavelength λ, and attenuation factor Q —and takes the simplified form: BSI=2πQ(L/λ) Applying representative values for the Kanto Basin yields BSI ≈ 12,500 (≈10⁴), indicating an extremely high level of inertial dominance comparable to strongly resonant fluid sloshing systems. This high BSI naturally explains key features of long-period ground motion in the Kanto Basin, including amplification in the 5–10 s band, double peaks, prolonged shaking exceeding 100 s, and sensitivity to distant earthquakes, all of which arise as consequences of dynamic flattening. Using the analogy of cake batter in a baking pan (BSI ≈ 12,500), the study illustrates that solid Earth behaves fluid-like in the long-period regime, enabling intuitive understanding of basin-scale resonance. Furthermore, dynamic flattening induced by repeated deep large earthquakes may have contributed to maintaining the anomalously flat geomorphology of the Kanto Basin for over one million years, a process that can be quantitatively interpreted through BSI. Finally, the free oscillation of the Earth following great earthquakes—characterized by BSI ≈ 2,500—is shown to lie on the same dimensionless “worldline” as basin-scale sloshing, suggesting that BSI provides a unified framework applicable continuously from basin-scale dynamics to whole-Earth oscillations.

papers.t: Nucleation process of laboratory earthquakes induced by dual-well injection
in: China University of Geosciences (Beijing)
Air Force Engineering University
tk: This study investigates the nucleation process of laboratory earthquakes induced by dual-well fluid injection to understand the mechanics of induced seismicity.
本研究通过双井注水诱发实验室地震，探讨了诱发地震的成核过程与机制。

papers.t: Assessing Basin Amplification and Rupture Directivity Effects Using Physics-Based Ground Motion Simulations in Wellington
tk: Physics-based simulations in Wellington show that dynamic fault ruptures generate distinct spatial patterns of basin amplification compared to point sources.
惠灵顿物理强震动模拟表明，动力破裂显著改变了盆地放大的空间分布。
papers.ab: Near-surface velocity structure plays a crucial role in modulating ground motion, and, in turn, contributes to seismic risk. However, a complete understanding of the basin effect is limited, owing to the paucity of detailed shallow basin structure, geological structures and near-field seismic sources. In this study, we perform physics-based simulations of ground motions incorporating the sedimentary low-shear velocity layers in the Wellington basin to evaluate the fundamental characteristics of regional seismic responses. We simulate ground motions of frequency up to ~2 Hz for intermediate-size earthquakes around Wellington, then validate acceleration time series and spectral amplitude ratio against GeoNet strong motion records. After that, we simulate potential dynamic ruptures of Mw> 7 earthquakes on the Wellington Fault, investigating the impact of rupture directivity effects on basin amplification. Our models demonstrate distinct ground intensity patterns arising from dynamic fault ruptures, rather than from distant seismic point sources, revealing significant spatial variation in basin amplification.

papers.t: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters
tk: The paper benchmarks empirical, machine-learning, and deep-learning models for satellite-derived bathymetry in turbid waters using a leakage-free validation design.
该研究在无泄漏验证下评估了浑浊水域中卫星反演水深的多模型性能。
papers.ab: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is often proposed as a low-cost complement to multibeam surveys of ports, but its accuracy is seldom measured on an area the model has never seen. We test SDB in the turbid, shallow and tidal waters of the Abu Dhabi coast against 285,619 multibeam soundings from twelve surveys at six port areas, reduced to Lowest Astronomical Tide. The Stumpf ratio, the Lyzenga transform, a monotonic gradient-boosted tree model (LightGBM) and a U-Net ensemble were trained on 72 Sentinel-2 images and tested in transfer to an unseen site and with local control (about 20% of a site's soundings, spatial blocks beyond a 225 m buffer). The validation design changed the result more than the model: the same LightGBM model gave 0.57 m RMSE under a random pixel split, 1.30 m under spatial blocks and 1.66 m at an unseen site. In transfer the Stumpf ratio (1.45 m) was not beaten by LightGBM, the U-Net or Lyzenga. With local control a hybrid of the tree output and the band ratio reached 1.11 m over 0-11 m, 67% of pixels within the IHO S-44 Order 2 tolerance and a conformal 95% interval with 95% observed coverage; in clear water it reached 0.29-0.53 m. The seabed could not be read beyond 11 m, and summer images were five to six times more turbid than winter ones. ICESat-2 ATL24 agreed with the surveys to 0.25 m after a depth-dependent offset was removed. A 60 m reconnaissance mosaic of 17,200 km2 of the UAE coast, calibrated cell by cell on ICESat-2 without any vessel survey, reached 1.42 m RMSE on held-out blocks over half of the product. Sentinel-2 SDB with about a hundred control depths per image is a usable reconnaissance and change-monitoring tool in these waters to about 10 m; it does not meet S-44 Order 1 without local control, and accuracies from random splits should not be taken as operational accuracy.

papers.t: Integrating rapid 3D structural validation into interpretation: forward modelling of the Katnook Graben, Otway Basin
tk: A rapid 3D kinematic forward modeling method integrates structural validation into early-stage seismic interpretation, reinterpreting the Katnook Graben as a shallow-detached crestal collapse structure.
一种快速三维运动学前向建模方法将构造校验融入早期地震解释，将Katnook地堑重新解释为浅部脱耦的脊部塌陷构造。
papers.ab: Structural validation of a prospect is invariably applied after the interpretation is finished, by restoring one or two key lines in 2D or, rarely, by a full 3D restoration that needs finished horizons and a specialist. The authors propose that a simple 3D kinematic forward model, built in minutes using a few explicit structural rules, fully restorable and scaled onto the mapped horizons, is a highly effective way of building structural validation into the early stages of interpretation. The rules are taken from the published literature and built into a software module, referred to herein as the rules module. The rules module is made available together with the crestal collapse graben solution used in this paper. The structural rules are those of the published literature: (1) fault-parallel flow, (2) slip decaying towards the fault tips and (3) syn-rift deposition to a datum. The fourth rule is that any accommodation problem arising when using them in a restorable forward model is flagged to the user. The resolution of the accommodation problem is a decision made by the user as part of the model build. Where the hangingwall of a listric fault cannot be carried over a bend in the fault without strain, that resolution is a crestal collapse graben. How the graben scales with slip is part of scaling the model onto the data, and it may differ between geological provinces. The method is tested here on the Katnook Graben of the Penola Trough, the main gas province of the onshore Otway Basin, which the authors interpreted twenty years ago as bounded by a basement-rooted, thick-skinned fault and its antithetic.
