The dip of the listric Hungerford Fault and its top basement cutoff are taken from 2D regional sections and the geometry of the graben from 3D interpretation. With these inputs the authors' model fits the mapped thickness of the base Laira to top Crayfish growth interval along dip to within about 120 m, roughly 10% of the 1.2 km by which the interval thickens along dip. It also reproduces the proportions of the syn-tectonic thickening into the graben. The detachment depth is projected and two parameters are fitted, namely the proportion of the slip pre-dating the base Laira horizon and the keystone throw. No basement fault beneath the graben is needed to account for the mapped geometry. Thus the authors now interpret the Katnook Graben as a crestal collapse graben, detached within the sedimentary fill and formed as a consequence of the large displacement on the listric Hungerford Fault. This has important implications for fault seal integrity risk in the area. The model also implies that the mapped basement, poorly imaged and broken by faults carried down from the reservoir level, can reasonably be re-interpreted as a simpler and less faulted surface. The value of the approach lies in structural validation carried out while the horizons are still being picked. Several structural ideas can be tested against the fault geometry, the growth pattern and the isopachs within hours, and the scenario that survives carries a structural history into trap definition, charge timing and volumetric uncertainty. The method is at an early stage of development. The purpose of this paper is to outline a new method and demonstrate its usefulness at prospect scale for reducing structural risk and the associated risk to fault seal.

papers.t: Interaction between seismic and aseismic slips along the Mendocino oceanic transform fault offshore northern California
in: Chinese University of Hong Kong
tk: This study investigates the interaction between seismic and aseismic slip along the Mendocino oceanic transform fault to understand fault mechanics offshore northern California.
本研究探讨了加州近海门多西诺洋脊转换断层上地震与无震滑动的相互作用。
papers.ab: Aseismic slip plays an important role in the earthquake cycle. On oceanic transform faults (OTFs), the majority of fault slip occurs aseismically which makes OTFs a natural laboratory to study the physical mechanism of aseismic slip and its interaction with seismic rupture. In this study, we apply state-of-the-art methods to analyze the aftershock sequences of three Mw > 6.5 earthquakes on the Mendocino OTF offshore California, including the 1994 and 2024 Mw 7.0 earthquakes, which are one of the largest OTF earthquakes so far. Compared with similar-magnitude continental strike-slip earthquakes, these large Mendocino OTF earthquakes have an order of magnitude fewer aftershocks, suggesting limited inter-event stress triggering. Nevertheless, their aftershock zones expanded with logarithmic time substantially beyond the co-seismic rupture zones, likely reflecting propagating aseismic slip transients. This behavior suggests that low-seismic-coupling segments can host aseismic slip transients triggered by earthquakes in neighboring high-seismic coupling segments while limiting the propagation of these seismic ruptures. In addition, the aftershocks of the 1994 and 2024 Mw 7.0 events, together with abundant background seismicity and previously identified repeating earthquakes, surround the rupture zones of the 2024 Mw 7.0 event and a Mw 6.1 earthquake in 2021, which suggests heterogeneous embedding of seismic slip patches within a predominantly aseismic slip zone in the eastern Mendocino OTF. Our observations reveal heterogeneous slip behavior and complex interaction between seismic and aseismic slips along the Mendocino OTF possibly due to variation in fault zone serpentinization and/or fluid-filled porosity.

papers.t: Ground-motion simulation of multi-segment ruptures on the Alpine-Marlborough fault system
tk: Hybrid broadband simulations of multi-segment Alpine-Marlborough ruptures reveal strong northward directivity and basin amplification in Wellington, posing hazards comparable to local sources.
混合宽频模拟表明阿尔卑斯-马尔堡多断层破裂给惠灵顿带来显著灾害。
papers.ab: The Alpine Fault (AF) is the major plate boundary crustal structure in New Zealand (NZ), producing large-to-great (M7-8+) earthquakes approximately every 300-500 years, and has long been a focal point for earthquake resilience in NZ. This study advances prior AF ground-motion modelling by considering multi-segment ruptures that initiate on the AF and rupture northward onto structures in the Marlborough Fault Zone (MFZ), resulting in ground shaking of consequential amplitudes for the upper South Island and Lower North Island, including Wellington city. From the 2022 NZ National Seismic Hazard Model (NSHM), three multi-segment rupture geometries including the Wairau, Clarence, and Hope fault structures in the MFZ are obtained, together with their scenario rupture rates. Hybrid broadband simulations using a multi-segment kinematic source description and a 3D NZ crustal velocity model are performed. Three rupture realizations per geometry are considered to compare the effects of kinematic rupture randomness with those of the different geometries. To provide comparisons with the prior ground-motion simulations used for public outreach in the AF8 programme, we also simulated the segmented M7.9 Alpine Fiordland-to-Kelly rupture geometry of Bradley et al. (2017a), adopting the same southern hypocentre location in all rupture scenarios, enabling examination of differences due to eight years of advancements in kinematic rupture and crustal velocity modelling. Results illustrate strong northward directivity and basin response, with the largest Wellington amplitudes resulting from the Alpine-Wairau and Alpine-Clarence scenarios -- peak ground accelerations of approximately 0.1 g, comparable to those observed during the 2016 Kaikōura earthquake; in aggregate, these Alpine-MFZ ruptures have a likelihood similar to the conventionally-considered Wellington Fault and Hikurangi subduction sources.

papers.t: On-Fault Parameters and Fault Connectivity Control Synthetic Earthquake Catalogs and 30-Year Rupture Probabilities in RSQSim Simulations of the Eastern San Francisco Bay Area
tk: RSQSim simulations of the San Francisco East Bay demonstrate that fault connectivity and frictional parameters significantly control synthetic earthquake catalogs and 30-year rupture probabilities.
RSQSim模拟表明断层连通性和摩擦参数显著影响合成地震目录及30年破裂概率。
papers.ab: The faults in the Eastern San Francisco Bay Area in California have long been known as a source of seismic hazard. This potential for large earthquakes, paired with high population density and economic activity leads to high seismic risk in the Bay Area. In this study we utilize the physics-based earthquake simulator RSQSim to generate synthetic earthquake catalogs for the San Francisco East Bay. We run a suite of models with different fault connectivity and on-fault parameters. We compare the model catalogs with UCERF3 probabilities and paleoseismic data. We find that initial on-fault assumptions of friction, weakening and connectivity shape the resultant catalogs. Firstly, we find that all our catalogs have b-values greater than 1, with models with uniform velocity-weakening and strong coseismic weakening having the lowest b-values (~1.4). The b-values are higher (1.5~1.8) for models with velocity-neutral and velocity-strengthening patches. However, if only fitting Mw 5 and greater, all model b-values fall within ~1.0-1.2. Secondly, we observe connected faults leading to more multi-segment slip events for the Hayward and Calaveras faults. We also observe good agreement between the RSQSim models and the UCERF3 Time-Independent and Time-Dependent probabilities of Mw 6.7 or greater events on the Hayward and Calaveras faults, within the maximum and minimum probability bounds. Models without velocity-strengthening yield time-independent 30-year probabilities of 22.4-28.9% for the Hayward and 13.3-20.5% for the Calaveras and time-dependent probabilities of 17.3-42.2% and 12.5-25.3% respectively. Finally, we compare model results to the mean recurrence intervals at three paleoseismic sites using a Welch’s t-test. For all but three models (all of which have uniform velocity-weakening friction) we can reject the equality of the mean recurrence rate between the paleoseismic data at Tyson Lagoon and the model catalog at the 95% confidence level, motivating future work exploring the full spectrum of fault slip.

papers.t: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
in: State Key Laboratory of Geological Processes and Mineral Resources, School of Earth and Planetary Sciences, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan 430074, China.
Institut für Geologie und Mineralogie, Universität zu Köln, Zülpicher Str. 49b, 50674 Köln, Germany.
State Key Laboratory of Deep Geothermal Resources, School of Sustainable Energy, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan 430074, China.

Hubei Key Laboratory of Petroleum Geochemistry and Environment, YU-CUGW Joint Research Center on Deep Earth and Surface Dynamic Coupling, College of Resources and Environment, Yangtze University, Wuhan 430100, China.
School of Environment, Earth and Ecosystem Sciences, The Open University, Walton Hall, Milton Keynes MK7 6AA, UK.
Research School of Earth Sciences, Australian National University, Canberra 2601, Australia.
State Key Laboratory of Isotope Geochemistry, Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guangzhou 510640, China.
State Key Laboratory of Geological Processes and Mineral Resources, School of Earth Resources, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan 430074, China.
tk: Primitive basalts from the North China Craton reveal distinct chalcophile-element signatures inherited from subducted continental crust in the metasomatized lithospheric mantle.
华北克拉通原始玄武岩揭示了交代地幔中继承自俯冲大陆地壳的独特亲铜元素特征。
papers.ab: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

papers.t: A Low-Cost Tool for Communicating the Time-Critical Feasibility of Near-Field Tsunami Evacuation: A Proof of Concept in Viña del Mar, Chile
in: Programa de Doctorado en Geografía, Instituto de Geografía, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, Santiago, Chile
Instituto de Geografía, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Valparaíso, Chile
tk: A low-cost tool combines drill GPS tracks with tsunami inundation simulations to evaluate and visualize time-critical evacuation feasibility in Chile.
该研究结合演练GPS轨迹与海啸淹没模拟，评估并可视化了智利海啸疏散的时间可行性。
papers.ab: Near-field tsunamis can leave coastal communities with only minutes to reach safe areas, so how quickly people begin moving after the earthquake shaking is critical to evacuation success. Static evacuation maps do not represent this time dependence, whereas more complex evacuation models can be data-intensive, costly, or difficult to scale. We introduce a simple, low-cost tool that combines Global Positioning System (GPS) tracks recorded with mobile applications during evacuation drills with tsunami inundation modeling. As a proof of concept, we apply the tool in Viña del Mar (central Chile), where a large tsunami is expected and evacuation is particularly challenging because of the long distances required to reach safe areas. We analyzed 119 GPS trajectories collected during drills between 2022 and 2026 and compared them with simulated inundation for a plausible subduction earthquake scenario. For illustration, each trajectory was evaluated under three departure times measured from the earthquake origin time: 0 min (T0), 8 min (T8), and 12 min (T12). T0 represents immediate evacuation, T8 departure when a warning is issued, and T12 departure when the tsunami is already reaching the coast. A trajectory was considered feasible if the participant completed the evacuation before being reached by the simulated inundation. Of the 119 trajectories, 100 were feasible under T0, 49 under T8, and only 3 under T12, showing how strongly evacuation success depends on when people begin moving. Most trajectories followed 13 main evacuation corridors. Feasibility varied sharply among corridors, even between neighboring routes within the same departure scenario. By overlaying the trajectories on the advancing inundation, the approach produces intuitive videos that make the consequences of delayed departure visible to residents, authorities, and decision-makers. Inexpensive and easily replicable, the method complements detailed evacuation modeling and may be particularly useful in tsunami-prone communities with limited resources, supporting evacuation awareness, preparedness, and risk communication.

papers.t: QR-Based Coherence Analysis for Seismic Signal Detection in Dense Arrays
in: Colorado School of Mines , Golden, Colorado ,
tk: A novel QR decomposition-based algorithm efficiently approximates array coherence to enhance seismic signal detection and data management in dense seismic arrays.
提出一种基于QR分解的新算法，高效近似台阵相干性，提升密集台阵的地震信号检测效率。
papers.ab: Summary Emerging sensing technologies across the physical sciences and engineering, including arrays of many sensors, have revolutionized the ability to collect high-resolution, large-scale datasets continuously. Although these advances have opened up new possibilities for scientific discovery, public data archives of some communities struggle to accommodate the sheer volume of larger datasets, and research teams face growing difficulties in efficiently exploring, transferring, visualizing, and interpreting the data at scale. These challenges are particularly pressing in the geophysics and seismology communities, which have encountered data that are several orders of magnitude larger in recent years. Array coherence, which relies on the similarity between sensor pairs within an array to analyze coherent signals, is effective in enhancing the detection of weak or emergent signals in noisy environments. In this study, we show how array coherence can be leveraged to effectively manage a surplus of data and serve as a robust method for signal detection and identification of regions of interest for further analysis. We present a novel algorithm that employs a QR decomposition to efficiently approximate array coherence and enhance the time resolution of detected signals, providing more precise signal detection. We demonstrate the utility and efficiency of this algorithm on data from a continuously recording, dense seismic array, allowing us to identify candidate seismic events and reduce the amount of data that require further transfer and analysis.

papers.t: Relationship between Meteorological Parameters and Temporal Variations of Microseismic Processes at the Belarusian Antarctic Research Station
tk: High-frequency microseisms (0.5–1.0 Hz) at the Belarusian Antarctic station correlate with northward wind speed, showing a 14-hour lag and Rayleigh-wave dominance.
白俄罗斯南极站的0.5-1.0 Hz高频微震与北向风速显著相关，存在14小时滞后且以瑞利波为主。
papers.ab: This study involved an analysis of seismic data acquired in the surrounding area of the Belarusian Antarctic research station “Mount Vechernyaya” in February, 2023 to identify a possible relationship between the seismic noises and local meteorological parameters. Probability density functions of power spectral densities histograms were constructed using the ObsPy framework based on the source seismograms. Separate power spectral densities were also extracted for each time window for the more detailed analysis. In addition to the main peak of the secondary microseisms, some noticeable peaks can be identified in the range of 0.5-1.0 Hz on individual spectral power density graphs at certain time intervals. These peaks can be attributed to the so-called high-frequency microseisms that are often due to the coastal zone waves. The intensity of these peaks shows a significant correlation with the northward wind speed projection, with the correlation coefficient reaching its maximum at a time shift of 14 hours and can reach 0.51 for the horizontal components and 0.45 for the vertical component. The conducted polarization analysis shows the dominance of Rayleigh waves in the wave pattern of oscillations in the range of 0.5-1.0 Hz.

papers.t: Dual scaling regimes and entropy transitions in the morphometric evolution of stratovolcanoes
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
University College London
Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas
Fundación Miguel Lillo
Royal Holloway University of London
tk: Statistical analysis of 392 stratovolcanoes reveals dual power-law scaling and entropy transitions, indicating a shift from highly variable small volcanoes to morphometrically constrained larger systems.
对392座复式火山的统计分析揭示了双重幂律标度与熵变，表明火山从高变异性向形态受限的生长模式转变。
papers.ab: Stratovolcano morphology reflects the influence of magma supply, composition, eruptive style, tectonic setting, and erosion. Morphometric parameters such as height, volume, slope, and ellipticity capture the influence of these processes during volcanic growth. Here, we present a statistical-physics-based analysis of 392 stratovolcanoes from seven volcanic zones, examining frequency-size distributions of these four morphometric parameters to assess whether scale-invariant patterns describe stratovolcano growth. All parameters exhibit heavy-tailed behaviour characteristic of power-law distributions. However, the data are better described by dual scaling relationships. Log-log plots reveal distinct linear segments separating abundant, morphologically variable small-to-intermediate volcanoes (sub-population 1) from rarer and more similar, large volcanoes (sub-population 2). Shallow slopes in the log-log plots reflect high dispersion, whereas steeper slopes associated with larger volcanoes indicate reduced dispersion. Using thermodynamic entropy and its information-theoretic extension (Shannon entropy), we quantify dispersal and variability within volcanic zones, providing a measure of morphometric and size spreading, complementing scaling exponents, and revealing a systematic transition between sub-populations. Sub-population 1, represented by a high-entropy regime, transitions to a low-entropy phase found in sub-population 2. This transition may reflect the evolution of volcanoes toward more morphometrically constrained systems. Together, dual power-law and entropy-scaling relationships indicate non-uniform volcanic growth across scales. These results provide a comparative framework for quantifying morphometrical variability among volcanic zones and indicate that stratovolcano growth is governed by scale-dependent transitions between variable and mechanically constrained growth regimes.

papers.t: Fault gouge composition controls preparatory processes and recurrence of laboratory earthquakes: From time-Predictable failure to aseismic slip
in: University of Memphis
tk: Fault gouge composition controls the transition from predictable stick-slip to stable aseismic slip, altering preparatory processes and recurrence predictability in laboratory earthquakes.
断层泥成分控制了实验室地震从可预测粘滑向稳定无震滑动的转变。
papers.ab: Fault zone heterogeneity takes several forms, such as surface roughness, lithological variations, and the intermixing of mineral phases with contrasting frictional properties within the fault core. Each is thought to affect earthquake nucleation and arrest, yet their effects on preparatory processes before failure and on earthquake recurrence remains insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted direct shear experiments on binary mixtures of soda-lime glass beads and quartz powder, systematically varying the gouge composition from 100 to 0 wt% glass beads at 313 ± 15 kPa normal stress. Frictionally contrasting phases are intermixed at the grain scale, making the mixtures spatially homogeneous but compositionally heterogeneous. Homogeneous glass beads, as one end member of the gouge mixtures, produce quasi-periodic stick-slip with pronounced pre-failure dilation, late-stage rapid slip acceleration, and time and slip predictable recurrence. In contrast, compositionally mixed gouges accelerate more gradually and exhibit shorter dilational phases with small amplitudes. Furthermore, preparatory slip starts earlier in the interseismic period and evolves towards an intermittent critical stress state prior to failure, which is associated with increasing deviation from time-predictable recurrence and a growing fraction of aseismically accommodated slip. The transition from stick-slip to stable sliding occurs within a narrow compositional range (80–85 wt% glass beads), with peak slip velocities differing by approximately 3.8 orders of magnitude between the two regimes. These results demonstrate that gouge composition strongly affects preparatory processes, and predictability of stick-slip recurrence in the laboratory and potentially in nature.

papers.t: Relocated Earthquake Hypocenters and Finite-Fault Slip Distributions for the 2021 Mw 7.0 Miyagi-Oki Earthquake Sequence
in: Tohoku University
The University of Tokyo
University of Michigan
tk: This dataset provides relocated hypocenters, centroid locations, and finite-fault slip distributions for the 2021 Mw 7.0 Miyagi-Oki earthquake sequence.
该数据集提供了2021年Mw 7.0宫城冲地震序列的重定位震源、质心位置及有限断层滑动分布。
papers.ab: This dataset contains relocated hypocenter and centroid locations (Figure 2) and finite-fault slip distributions (Figure 4) associated with the 2021 Mw 7.0 Miyagi-Oki earthquake and surrounding events. The data accompany Yoshida et al. (2026), Geophysical Research Letters, https://doi.org/10.1029/2026GL125835. File descriptions and units are provided in the README.

papers.t: Widespread non-double-couple earthquakes revealed by a dense seismic network in Tottori, Japan
in: Earthquake Research Institute, University of Tokyo
The University of Tokyo
Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Kyushu University
Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University
tk: A dense seismic network in Tottori, Japan, reveals widespread non-double-couple earthquake mechanisms, suggesting complex faulting or fluid involvement.
日本鸟取密集地震台网揭示了广泛存在的非双力偶地震，表明了复杂的断裂过程或流体作用。
papers.ab: Understanding how small earthquakes rupture in fault systems is central to revealing the physical processes that govern faulting in the Earth’s crust. These events are commonly assumed to be dominated by simple shear slip, producing earthquake sources that can be described by classical double-couple models. This assumption underpins many interpretations of seismicity but has rarely been tested using comprehensive source representations for large numbers of small events. Here we demonstrate that small earthquakes in a well-instrumented fault system systematically depart from double-couple behavior. By applying full earthquake source inversions to thousands of events recorded by a dense seismic network in western Japan, we identify widespread non-double-couple rupture patterns that cluster spatially and exhibit combined shear and opening motions. These observations indicate that non-double-couple processes are a common feature of small-earthquake rupture rather than rare anomalies. Our findings suggest that fluid-related processes, structural complexity and rock damage within fault zones could influence earthquake nucleation and rupture growth. These findings provide further insights into the complexity of small earthquakes in fault systems and their implications for earthquake rupture physics.

papers.t: Autogenic initiation of basin-scale salt tectonics
tk: Seismic data and numerical modeling show that Southern North Sea salt tectonics were initiated autogenically by diagenetic gypsum-to-anhydrite conversion rather than tectonic forces.
地震数据与数值模拟表明，北海南部盐构造是由石膏-硬石膏成岩转变自发启动的。
papers.ab: Salt structures typically form due to the post-depositional flow of salt driven by differential loading, gravity gliding, or shortening, with the internal architecture of the evaporite treated as a passive strain marker. Using ~26,000 km² of 3-D seismic reflection data and 34 wells from the Southern North Sea, we show that the earliest regional deformation of the Southern Permian Basin salt giant (Zechstein Supergroup) was instead autogenic. The synclines of the first salt-cored folds overlie ridges of intrasalt gypsum that converted to anhydrite at the end of the Lopingian. Triassic onlap and truncation show that these folds formed immediately after salt deposition, long before Paleogene–Neogene shortening, and their curvilinear, unoriented pattern follows neither the sub-salt fault grid nor the dip of the detachment, as allogenic mechanisms would predict. Numerical experiments show that the density contrast created by the conversion suffices to make the ridges founder into the underlying halite, depressing the depositional surface above them into lows that Triassic sediments then filled. A significant component of Southern Permian Basin salt tectonics may therefore be autogenic in origin, with the distribution of the related structures being fixed by depositional mounding and diagenetic reactions within the evaporite rather than by regional, plate-driven stresses. Regional tectonism subsequently amplified these structures, which nonetheless retain the distribution imposed within the evaporite.

papers.t: Three-dimensional geometric modeling of the Gulang–Zhongwei fault, northeastern Tibetan Plateau: implications for the seismic hazard assessment
in: Tianjin University
Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration
China Earthquake Administration
Hainan Earthquake Administration
China Petroleum Pipeline Engineering (China)
tk: This study constructs a 3D geometric model of the Gulang–Zhongwei fault to evaluate its seismic hazard.
本研究构建了古浪—中卫断裂的三维几何模型并评估了其地震危险性。

papers.t: Development of a Combined Detection and Relocation Workflow (TM2DD) to Characterize Escalating Hydraulic Fracturing Induced Seismicity in the Karnes Trough Fault Zone of the Eagle Ford Shale Play, Texas
tk: Develops and applies the TM2DD workflow to detect and relocate hydraulic fracturing-induced seismicity in Texas, revealing distinct fault segment behaviors and geometry.
开发并应用TM2DD工作流重定位德州水力压裂诱发地震，揭示断层分段特征。
papers.ab: On January 30, 2025, an M4.7 earthquake shook the Eagle Ford Shale, Texas, the region's second M4 event in under eighteen months. Unlike much of the central United States, where induced seismicity stems from wastewater disposal, most of the earthquakes in the Eagle Ford are linked to hydraulic fracturing (HF) (Fasola et al., 2019; Fasola & Brudzinski, 2023). If HF-induced, the 2025 event would be the largest such earthquake in the United States, amid seismicity increasing in both magnitude and frequency. The seismicity appears to be associated with mapped normal faults in the Karnes Trough Fault Zone (KTFZ), but its detailed pattern and relationship to HF operations remain poorly characterized. This study leverages ~5 years of continuous TexNet recordings (~25 km station spacing) to better detect and locate this seismicity. We have developed a workflow (TM2DD) that integrates multistation template matching with automated per-template correlation thresholds, refines phase arrivals via template-detection cross correlation, and applies double-difference relocation using a local 1-D velocity model. This expands the detected catalog by 17.5-fold, with relocations revealing that the 2023 M4.0 and 2025 M4.7 sequences ruptured adjacent fault segments with 15-20 degree differences in dip angle. In addition, the larger event occurred at the deeper extent of the seismically active zone. All detected sequences correlate tightly in space and time with active HF wells within 3.5 km, with the deeper 2025 event showcasing mainshock - aftershock behaviour, whereas the shallower 2023 sequence is swarm-like. These results indicate that HF-induced seismicity in the KTFZ can propagate along adjacent, connected fault systems as nearby operations continue, with deeper segments potentially hosting larger, mainshock-dominated ruptures.

papers.t: 3D inversions of magnetic and gravity data for the Yaouré region, Ivory Coast: a greenstone belt characterization
tk: 3D gravity and magnetic inversions characterize the density and magnetic susceptibility of the Yaouré Greenstone Belt, mapping key structures and lithotypes under low magnetic inclination.
利用三维重磁反演表征了科特迪瓦亚乌雷绿岩带的密度和磁化率，揭示了低磁偏角背景下的关键构造与岩性。
papers.ab: We carried out 3D inverse modeling of full tensor gravity gradiometry data, its derived products (Tz and Tz residual), and magnetic data to recover the density and magnetic susceptibility distributions of the Yaouré Greenstone Belt in Ivory Coast, West Africa. The study area presents significant challenges: it lacks well-defined stratigraphy and structural measurements, and it lies close to the magnetic equator, where the magnetic inclination is low. Inverted models were analyzed using isosurfaces and histogram curves to characterize physical properties distribution and highlight geophysical sources. We extracted vertical slices through the 3D inverted models across significant mapped structures and lithotypes, and measured magnetic anomaly dips within these sections to create an artificial structural map. We identified positive and negative density contrasts as well as magnetic susceptibility sources in the region that correlated with mapped surface geology. Our results revealed that sedimentary and volcano-sedimentary rocks in the region present higher susceptibility than some intrusions, contrasting with their comparatively lower density. The 3D inverted models provided insights of some mapped structures, such as major faults, that may act as physical property boundaries. Ranking magnetic susceptibility and density contrast of geological units alongside the structural map offers a systematic first approach to maximizing the value of geophysical inversions. This integration may serve as a petrophysical or geological constraint when prior information is limited for subsequent inversions, acting as useful information for starting or reference models.

papers.t: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
tk: GeoAgent is a contract-constrained LLM agent system that automates complex seismic data processing workflows using Madagascar's command-line tools.
GeoAgent是一个受合同约束的LLM智能体系统，实现地震数据处理流程的自动化。
papers.ab: Large language models (LLMs) can drive scientific software through function calling, but free-form tool use is fragile on long, data-dependent processing chains. Models omit arguments, invent units, feed the previous artifact into the wrong input, and report completion without a verifiable product. We present GeoAgent, an agent system for seismic data processing built on Madagascar's roughly 1{,}965 command-line programs. GeoAgent exposes 54 operator agents (51 generated from a declarative specification), retrieves from an index of 1{,}937 operators, and encodes the processing flow as a nine-stage state graph. Four explicit contracts---named artifacts, input resolution, parameter takeover, and artifact validation---move everything the graph can determine out of the model's discretion. A deterministic geometry tool parses the self-describing SPS/RPS/XPS and SEG-Y headers, cross-checks eight consistency conditions, and reproduces the reference shell recipe exactly. The system runs in containers with session- and task-level isolation, bounded execution, and defenses against silent failures. On a 2-D land dataset, the nine-stage pipeline completes in about six to eleven minutes and yields a verified artifact at every stage, while retrieval reduces per-turn tool context from about 12k to 2k tokens. We report the design, deployment experience, and motivating failure modes.

papers.t: Modelling wide-swath altimeter observation-error correlations with a regularised diffusion operator
tk: A regularised diffusion-based correlation operator is proposed to model large-scale observation-error correlations for wide-swath altimeters in ocean data assimilation.
提出正则化扩散算子以模拟海洋同化中的高度计误差相关性。
papers.ab: Unaccounted-for observation-error correlations have long been known to be detrimental to the quality of atmospheric and ocean analyses produced by data assimilation (DA) systems. While progress has been made over the past decade on modelling inter-channel error correlations, modelling spatial error correlations remains a challenge for large datasets. Common strategies for mitigating the harmful effects of spatial error correlations, such as variance inflation or data thinning, prevent the extraction of valuable small-scale information from the observations. With the emergence of new sources of high-resolution observations, such as those from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath altimeter, the need to address this limitation of DA systems has become increasingly pressing. To do so, we consider a diffusion-based observation-error correlation operator, extending previous work on modelling correlated errors in conventional nadir altimeter data. When observation-error correlation length scales are large, the original method can suffer from an excessive sensitivity of the inverse correlation operator to small-scale perturbations. Since actual estimates of observation-error correlations from SWOT suggest the presence of large length scales, a more robust formulation of the method is required. We present a regularised formulation of the diffusion-based correlation operator that eliminates this excessive sensitivity while preserving computational efficiency. We describe the implementation of the operator for a mesh constructed from SWOT observation locations and demonstrate its application in a global ocean DA system. To validate the new formulation, we perform DA experiments with simulated SWOT observations. These experiments confirm that the regularised correlation operator provides an effective, robust and practical approach for representing wide-swath altimeter observation-error correlations in operational ocean DA systems.

papers.t: A static arrest criterion classifies some fault-spanning ruptures as arrested
tk: Dynamic rupture simulations show that static arrest criteria can incorrectly predict the arrest of ruptures that actually span the entire fault.
动态破裂模拟表明，静态停止准则会错误地预测本可贯穿断层的破裂发生停止。
papers.ab: A static arrest length and a fully dynamic rupture are compared, one rupture at a time, for 60 antiplane and 60 in-plane cases on one 120 km fault with linear slip weakening and one correlation length of the initial stress. The standard deviations were fixed before those ruptures were drawn. The comparison tests the rule, used to build earthquake populations, that a rupture stops where its static energy release rate falls below the fracture energy and that this rule decides which ruptures span the fault. In 22 of the 120 cases the two calculations disagreed on whether the rupture spanned the fault, and in all 22 the static criterion predicted arrest while the dynamic rupture spanned the fault. All 22 still spanned the fault when the spacing along strike was halved. Where both stopped, the dynamic length was longer in 41 of 42 antiplane cases and 38 of 40 in-plane cases, and the median ratio was 1.08 in each mode. The in-plane values depend on the grid across the fault: with half the nodes, the in-plane median ratio was 0.99 and seven of the twelve in-plane disagreements remained. Three-dimensional rupture and other slip-weakening distances were not tested.

papers.t: How to quantify discrepancies between arbitrary polarization states ? Unifying geometrical insight and full-waveform inversion of polarization observables
in: Opera Applied-geophysical research group , Pau ,
Formerly: IFSTTAR , Bouguenais ,
Univ. Grenoble Alpes , ISTerre, F-38058 Grenoble ,
BRGM (French Geological Survey) ,
tk: Introduces a Poincaré-sphere-based geodesic metric to quantify polarization discrepancies and demonstrates its superior performance in multicomponent full-waveform inversion.
引入庞加莱球测地线度量量化偏振差异，并应用于多分量全波形反演。
papers.ab: Summary Polarization observables have long been used to infer properties of the Earth, but the geophysical literature has not explicitly addressed the problem of a general metric for comparing arbitrary polarization states (independently of specific application contexts). To address this question, we first introduce a geometrical representation of polarization based on the Poincaré sphere. This framework allows us to derive a novel polarization discrepancy criterion, defined as the geodesic length between two polarization states represented on the Poincaré sphere. We establish, both analytically and geometrically, the relationship between this intrinsic metric and the main classes of polarization metrics (based on polarization angles, ratios and cross-products). Then, we examine the advantages and limitations of various polarization-based misfit functions from both fundamental and geophysical perspectives. On the fundamental side, we theoretically compare the different misfit functions in light of a few qualitative criteria. From a geophysical perspective, we extend the conventional multicomponent FWI method for inverting the discussed polarization-based criteria. With a simple numerical experiment, we show that misfit functions based on intrinsic and extrinsic distances (PoincarÃ© and normalised cross-product misfit functions, respectively) produce superior inversion results compared to all other polarization-based misfit functions. More generally, inverting polarization observables with a suitable metric can be beneficial for a wide range of geophysical problems, from source estimation to the quantitative imaging of Earth properties based on different types of physical fields (such as seismic or electromagnetic waves).

papers.t: T-phase detection within spectrograms of hydroacoustic data from the Arctic Ocean
tk: An automated Regions of Interest (ROI) spectrogram detector successfully identifies earthquake-generated T-phases in Arctic hydroacoustic data with minimal computational resources.
一种基于时频图感兴趣区域（ROI）的自动检测器成功识别了北极水听器数据中的地震T相。
papers.ab: Microseismicity in the Central Arctic remains understudied due to its remoteness from land stations. Hydrophone arrays can be used to detect earthquakes from their T-phases, components that propagate in water. This approach can provide a valuable alternative to traditional recording systems and improve the monitoring coverage. However, manual annotations of T-phases are a time-consuming process, and more automatic approaches are needed. Recent studies in T-phase detection consider machine learning techniques, but these methods are computationally intensive and sensitive to training data. In this study, an automated detector is presented utilising a Regions Of Interest (ROI) algorithm on spectrograms, requiring minimal parameter tuning and computational resources. The detector was applied to acoustic data recorded along the Nansen Basin from September 2019 to August 2020 during the CAATEX experiment. The ROI detector correctly identified 82 out of 96 manually labelled events across all moorings, with the majority of false detections linked to the presence of flow noise within hydrophones. The algorithm also characterised spectro-temporal properties of T-phase signals, with energy focused between 3 and 50 Hz, peaking at around 20 Hz. This method is robust against the varying underwater background noise conditions encountered and aids in studying the complexities of the T-phase signal structure.

papers.t: Conditional Mean Flows for Frequency-Domain Scattered Wavefield Generation
tk: A conditional mean flows model generates accurate frequency-domain scattered wavefields in a single step, outperforming multi-step diffusion models in efficiency and generalization.
引入条件平均流模型，实现高效、单步的频域散射波场生成与泛化。
papers.ab: Frequency-domain wavefield modeling underpins seismic imaging and inversion, where repeated Helmholtz solutions become costly as velocity models, source locations, and frequencies vary. Neural operators learn mappings between physical fields, and their accuracy can decline outside the training distribution. Diffusion models learn wavefield distributions and generally require repeated sampling evaluations to produce accurate fields. A conditional mean flows model is introduced for complex scattered-wavefield generation. The analytical background wavefield serves as a condition alongside the velocity model, supplying spatially organized information about the source location and frequency. Learning the scattered wavefield avoids the point-source singularity in the target and supports generalization across these physical conditions. The model estimates the average transport velocity over a finite interval connecting Gaussian noise to the scattered field. This representation captures the accumulated displacement and permits both full-interval one-step generation and interval-partitioned sampling. Trained on OpenFWI, the model is evaluated on in-distribution and out-of-distribution velocity structures, frequency generalization, and inference efficiency. In most evaluated settings, one-step mean flows sampling achieves lower wavefield error than multi-step diffusion. Because each sampling step requires another network evaluation, accurate one-step generation also reduces inference time. These results indicate that mean flows can provide accurate and efficient frequency-domain scattered-wavefield generation.

papers.t: Inverting ground displacement to resolve traction changes on fractures in a 3D heterogeneous crust
in: The Lyon University, Université Jean Monnet , Institut Camille Jordan, F-42023 Saint-Etienne ,
Université Clermont Auvergne , CNRS, IRD, OPGC, Laboratoire Magmas et Volcans, Clermont-Ferrand F-63000 ,
tk: A new adjoint-based inversion method using XFEM resolves variable traction changes on fractures in 3D heterogeneous crusts from InSAR and GNSS data.
一种基于XFEM和伴随状态的新反演方法，可利用InSAR和GNSS数据解析三维非均匀地壳中裂缝的牵引力变化。
papers.ab: Summary Over the past few decades, InSAR and GNSS have significantly improved the monitoring of volcanic and tectonic processes by providing frequent, high-resolution measurements over large areas. To track magma transport and better understand the seismic cycle, these data are typically analyzed using kinematic solutions that model fractures as dislocations within an elastic, homogeneous half-space. Such simplifying assumptions can lead to inaccuracies when estimating the location and strength of subsurface sources. To address these limitations and determine more physically meaningful quantities - such as stress vectors rather than dislocations - we propose a new method for inferring variable pressure or traction changes on fractures, through the inversion of noisy InSAR or GNSS ground displacement data. These fractures may represent faults or magma intrusions embedded in a three-dimensional, heterogeneous crust with prominent topography. Our approach is based on a fictitious domain method inspired by the extended finite element method (XFEM), which is particularly well-suited for modeling fractures that need not conform to volume meshes. The inversion framework minimizes a cost function comprising the misfit between modeled and observed displacements, along with two regularization terms applied to both the tractions and their gradients. We present an inversion algorithm based on the forward and adjoint problem. The method is reformulated for InSAR data, which is challenging due to missing data, measurement noise, and the projection of displacements into Earth-satellite line-of-sight (LOS) directions, resulting in an incomplete displacement field. A corresponding adaptation for GNSS data is also introduced. Synthetic tests demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method even with a single LOS observation, or in the presence of spatial gaps and noise, as well as with few GNSS data. They show that, neglecting heterogeneities in the inversion may bias the distribution of pressure and their amplitude. Regularization parameters are determined using either L-curve analysis or a compromise function, both providing reliable results. We confirm that log-log L-curves, and not lin-lin L-curves, are required for appropriate regularization selection. As source depth or noise levels increase, the method favors stronger regularization, yielding smoother solutions. We apply the method to the May 2016 intrusion and eruption at Piton de la Fournaise, where InSAR and GNSS data are available for the beginning and end of the intrusion and eruption. Using a homogeneous elastic medium, the results agree well with those from a previous boundary element study, that assumed a homogeneous medium and pressurization over a circular portion of a dike. Inversion results for a heterogeneous elastic medium show greater complexity in the pressure distribution within the dike, but remain consistent with our previous findings. Furthermore, by inverting traction changes rather than pressure changes, we identify a shear displacement at depth–interpreted as a flank slip occurring simultaneously with the magma intrusion.

papers.t: Estimating the Ice Thickness and Water Depth of a Frozen Lake Using Flexural Waves Recorded by Distributed Acoustic Sensing
in: Institute of Seismology, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland
Institut des Sciences de la Terre, Université Grenoble Alpes, Grenoble, France
tk: Wind-generated flexural waves recorded by DAS on a frozen lake are used to estimate ice thickness and water depth, demonstrating cryospheric monitoring capabilities.
利用光纤分布式声学传感（DAS）记录的风成弯曲波估算冰厚和水深，展示了冰冻圈监测潜力。
papers.ab: Characterizing the physical properties of frozen lakes, such as ice thickness and water depth, is essential for diverse applications, including ice safety assessment and climate change monitoring. Typically, these properties are measured through labor-intensive field surveys, limiting their spatial and temporal coverage. Alternatively, frozen lake environments can be investigated using seismology. Seismic waves propagating on floating ice travel at velocities that depend on physical properties of the ice–water system, including the elastic properties and thickness of the ice and the water depth. Because seismic waves are frequently generated and can propagate through entire lake systems, they have greater spatiotemporal coverage than field measurements. In this study, we investigate the use of wind-generated flexural waves recorded by a distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) system to infer ice thickness and water depth along a 1000 m fiber-optic cable installed on Lake Pääjärvi, southern Finland. We detect flexural waves in the 0.01–0.5 Hz frequency band, measure their phase-velocity dispersion curves, estimate ice thickness and water depth along four cable intervals, and compare the estimates with field measurements and the lake bathymetry. The ice-thickness estimates are comparable to field measurements, with differences ranging from 2% to 34%, whereas the water-depth estimates underestimate bathymetry values by 22%–60% while resolving the increasing water-depth trend along the cable. We find that water-depth estimates tend to become less robust as the water depth increases because the measured dispersion curves lack sufficiently low wavenumbers to resolve the water column. We illustrate that flexural waves can refract toward the shore as they approach shallow water. This effect must be considered when estimating true phase velocities from apparent velocities measured along the cable to avoid bias in the estimated ice thickness and water depth. Our results demonstrate the potential of DAS to leverage ambient signals for monitoring frozen lakes.

papers.t: Spatiotemporal Characterization of the Shallow Subsurface Using Dense-Array Ambient Noise Tomography at Cape Modern, Utah
in: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, California, U.S.A.
Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, U.S.A.
tk: Dense-array ambient noise tomography at Cape Modern, Utah, reveals spatially heterogeneous, frequency-dependent shallow subsurface velocity changes driven primarily by seasonal thermoelastic forcing.
犹他州Cape Modern的密集台阵微动断层成像揭示了由季节性热弹性力驱动的空间非均匀、频散的浅表速度变化。
papers.ab: We deployed 500 seismic nodes across 257 locations at Cape Modern, Utah, over several months to characterize temporal velocity variations in the shallow subsurface using ambient-noise tomography. Because of the nature of ambient noise and minor changes in the sensor locations, the available ray paths were modified during the acquisition. A Voronoi tessellation-based path resampling strategy mitigated azimuthal bias from heterogeneous station distributions, achieving quasi-uniform ray-path coverage. Spatial mapping of velocity changes reveals lateral heterogeneity in the evolution of relative velocity change (dv/v), with velocity perturbations varying across the study domain and spatial patterns reflecting underlying variations in material properties and subsurface structure. Analysis of continuous data systematically reveals dv/v decreases followed by gradual recovery, with frequency dependence (0.5–1.2 s) indicating a shallow subsurface origin. Integration with environmental monitoring identified thermoelastic forcing as the dominant mechanism, with calculated velocity change variation matching observations (0.6% for 25°C seasonal variation). The 90–100-day delay between air temperature and velocity response aligns with thermal diffusion timescales. At shorter periods (0.5–0.8 s), high-velocity regions showed rapid recovery (60–95 days), whereas low-velocity zones exhibited extended recovery (90–130 days), reflecting thermal conductivity differences. The absence of systematic correlation at longer periods (0.8–1.2 s) indicates thermal decoupling of deeper intervals. This study demonstrates the monitoring capability of a dense array for spatially resolving heterogeneous subsurface thermoelastic responses.

papers.t: Enhanced full-waveform inversion through Fourier MLP and cosine-similarity optimization: A neural tangent kernel and multiscale loss approach
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Sinopec (China)
SINOPEC Exploration & Production Research Institute
tk: FED-FWI combines Fourier feature mapping, a composite optimal-transport/wavelet loss, and cosine-similarity optimization to mitigate cycle skipping and accelerate convergence.
FED-FWI结合傅里叶MLP与混合损失，缓解周期跳跃并加速收敛。
papers.ab: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful tool for high-resolution subsurface imaging, but its practical use is limited by cycle skipping, strong sensitivity to the initial velocity model, and high computational cost. This study proposed a Fourier-enhanced dynamics FWI (FED-FWI) framework that combined three components within a recurrent neural network formulation of the forward problem. First, Fourier feature mapping was applied to the coordinate inputs of the multilayer perceptron (MLP) that parameterized the velocity model, which enriched the neural tangent kernel spectrum and improved the representation of sharp velocity contrasts. Second, a composite misfit coupled an optimal transport term, which was robust to phase shifts, with a wavelet-domain term that enforced multiscale consistency; the two terms were adaptively balanced by exponential moving average weighting according to their smoothed relative magnitudes, and the resulting coefficient was not required to vary monotonically with iterations. Third, an optimizer that modulated the update magnitude according to the cosine similarity between successive gradients suppressed oscillatory updates and stabilized convergence. The framework was implemented with automatic differentiation, so the adjoint equations need not be derived manually. Starting from a linear initial model that spanned 1200–4800 m/s, without prescribing a known, fixed velocity for the shallow water layer in the initial model, FED-FWI recovered the Marmousi II model with a structural similarity index of 0.804 and a mean squared error of 0.075, compared with 0.626 and 0.212 for optimal transport FWI and 0.695 and 0.134 for Sobolev-norm FWI; it also attained the shortest convergence time of the methods compared while requiring less than 200 MiB of additional graphics processing unit memory. Ablation tests indicated that each component contributed to this improvement, and two salt-model experiments showed that the principal salt geometry was recovered under strong velocity contrasts. The results indicated that FED-FWI improved inversion quality when initialized with the linear velocity model considered in this study.

papers.t: First Results of Calculation of the Dayside Magnetopause Reconnection Rate with TRACERS
tk: This study presents the first calculations of the dayside magnetopause reconnection rate using ion dispersion data from the TRACERS satellite mission.
本研究首次利用TRACERS卫星任务的离子色散数据计算了日侧磁层顶重联率。
papers.ab: Quantifying the rate of reconnection remains a key challenge in the study of geomagnetic storms. In this study, we present the first results from the new Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites (TRACERS) mission to calculate the reconnection rate from dispersed ion populations measured in the cusp, using previously developed methodology. We study ion dispersion events in two storms. During the first storm, which occurred on September 30, 2025, 21 dispersion events were identified in TRACERS 2 ion data as a combined result of geospace dynamics and the spacecraft cusp encounters. Throughout this time when ion dispersion was detected by TRACERS , the reconnection rate is calculated and is shown to track reasonably well with another measure of geomagnetic activity, the Cross Polar Cap Potential (CPCP) as obtained by the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN). The dispersions are correlated with the smoothed CPCP, and a correlation of $r^2=0.62$ was found using the dispersions from the onset and main phase of the storm. The correlation disappears when including dispersions from the recovery period. The distribution of reconnection rates throughout this storm lies generally between 0.1 - 1.5 mV/m, slightly lower than previous reconnection rates calculated with DMSP, but consistent with in-situ observations made with Polar. In this work, we also apply a previously developed automatic identification algorithm for ion-energy cusp dispersion to TRACERS, with the intent that it may serve as a tool for future statistical analysis as the data volume becomes too large to manually review.

papers.t: Tibetan Plateau-Scale Kinematics Revealed in a Single Event: The Mw 7.1 7 January 2025 Tingri Earthquake
in: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Science Center, Moffett Field, California, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Geologic Hazards Science Center, Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.
tk: The 2025 Mw 7.1 Tingri earthquake ruptured two distinct fault systems, demonstrating how a single event can partition discrete and diffuse deformation to reproduce long-term Tibetan Plateau kinematics.
2025年廷里Mw 7.1地震破裂了两个不同的断裂带，揭示了单次地震如何分配离散与弥散变形。
papers.ab: The 7 January 2025 Mw 7.1 Tingri earthquake ruptured the southern Xainza–Dinggye rift in the Tibetan Plateau, ∼200 km north of the Himalayan frontal thrust system. This rift lies in a network of discrete normal and strike-slip faults that accommodate gravitational collapse and lateral extrusion of the Plateau with overall India–Eurasia convergence. Subpixel image correlation and coseismically shifted digital elevation model differencing of high-resolution (∼0.5 m) satellite optical imagery reveal the full 3D coseismic displacement field of the earthquake. Rupture occurred on two west-dipping faults: the Lagoi fault in the north, cutting through mountainous terrain at relatively high elevation (∼5500 m) within granitic–gneissic rocks, and the Dingmu Co fault in the south, bounding a lower elevation (∼4200 m) basin within Tethyan metasedimentary rocks. Northern deformation consists of coherent, block-like oblique hanging wall subsidence with left-lateral slip (>2 m). Southern deformation is more distributed, with comparable magnitudes of subsidence and northwestward translation accommodated along a series of hanging wall faults. Footwall rebound is minimal and occurs over shorter distances than observed in the long-term landscape record. Between these domains, a ∼5–10 km wide east–west transition zone absorbs diffuse north–south contraction (∼1 m) and right-lateral motion (∼1.5 m), above a concave-up along-strike curved fault imaged by aftershocks that may direct slip toward its deepest center. Collectively, these observations indicate the control of topographic stresses, lithology, fault geometry, and a weak lower crust in partitioning discrete and diffuse deformation during a single earthquake, reproducing Plateau-wide kinematic patterns typically inferred from geodetic and geomorphic observations over much longer timescales.

papers.t: Direct tsunami wavefield sensing on submarine telecom cables enables coastal wave height forecasting
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Université Côte d'Azur
Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur
Géoazur
Institut de Recherche pour le Développement
Centro Sismológico Nacional
University of Chile
tk: Submarine telecommunication cables are utilized for direct tsunami wavefield sensing, enabling real-time coastal wave height forecasting.
利用海底商业光缆进行海啸波场直接传感，实现了沿海波高的实时预测。
papers.ab: Detecting tsunamis in the open ocean before they reach the coast is critical for saving lives, yet open-ocean observations remain sparse and costly. Submarine telecommunication cables span many tsunami-prone regions and can be instrumented with distributed sensing, but their tsunami sensitivity remains uncertain. Here we report observations of the transoceanic tsunami generated by the Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake on 29 July 2025, obtained through distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on a 400-km telecommunication cable array offshore Chile. After suppressing background and instrumental noise, we recover coherent tsunami signals along hundreds of kilometres of cable despite maximum open-ocean amplitudes of only ~ 4 cm. The recovered signals agree with tsunami simulations, while revealing spatial variability in cable sensitivity. Converting DAS strain to water elevation empirically, we reconstruct the tsunami wavefield and predict coastal tide-gauge records where constrained by high-fidelity cable segments, providing 5 to 15 minutes of warning time before the tsunami arrives at the coast. These results demonstrate the viability of an end-to-end tsunami warning system based on existing submarine cables.

papers.t: Evaluating New Earthquake Forecasting Models: Against a Strong ETAS Benchmark, Not an Underimplemented One
in: The Institute of Statistical Mathematics, Research Organization of Information and Systems, Tokyo, Japan
Department of Statistical Science, The Graduate University for Advanced Studies (SOKENDAI), Tokyo, Japan
tk: Proposes the POGA framework to ensure new earthquake forecasting models are evaluated against properly optimized, strong ETAS benchmarks rather than under-implemented ones.
提出POGA框架，以确保新型地震预测模型与优化充分的强ETAS基准进行对比。
papers.ab: New earthquake forecasting models are increasingly reported to outperform established models such as the epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model. However, the scientific meaning of such improvements depends critically on how the benchmark is constructed. I use the term “under-implemented ETAS” for a benchmark that is unnecessarily restricted, weakly optimized, or otherwise disadvantaged, and propose the Parity of information, Optimization, Generality, and Assessment (POGA) test as a simple framework for assessing model comparisons. The purpose is not to protect ETAS from competition, but to ensure that improvements over established models are scientifically interpretable. A strong benchmark makes victory harder, but also reveals what a new model has genuinely learned that its competitor could not.

papers.t: From rifting to collision: deep closure of a Wilson cycle during the Archean–Paleoproterozoic transition at the Carajás-Bacajá boundary, Amazonian Craton
tk: This study reconstructs a complete Archean-Paleoproterozoic Wilson cycle at the Carajás-Bacajá boundary, detailing rifting, subduction, collision, and post-collisional collapse.
该研究重建了卡拉雅斯-巴卡雅边界完整的太古宙-古元古代威尔逊循环。
papers.ab: The Carajás-Bacajá boundary preserves complementary archives of continental rifting, passive-margin development, subduction, collision and post-collisional exhumation across the Archean-Paleoproterozoic transition. We present whole-rock lithogeochemistry, Sm-Nd isotopes, U-Pb zircon geochronology and thermobarometry from the Vila Santa Fé-Rio Preto association, a mafic-felsic granulitic assemblage tectonically above the Buritirama succession. Rio Preto-type mafic granulites define a comparatively juvenile pole, whereas arc-modified felsic orthogneisses have negative εNd at ca. 2.10 Ga, TDM ages of ca. 2.44-2.46 Ga and Archean inherited zircon. U-Pb zircon records lower-crustal melt growth at 2097 ± 19 and 2093 ± 25 Ma, followed by granulite-facies recrystallization, migmatization and charnockitic to enderbitic melt generation between 2073 ± 3 and 2067 ± 7 Ma. Thermobarometry constrains a 9-10 kbar, 760-800 °C granulitic root, followed by hydrated decompression at 7-8 kbar and 690-710 °C; Carajás-side amphibolite records ca. 700-720 °C. Structural, geophysical and 40Ar/39Ar constraints define southwest-verging stacking of Bacajá lower crust over Buritirama and northern Carajás between ca. 2.10 and 2.05 Ga. Published data extend the reconstruction backward. A 2549 ± 5.9 Ma A2-type granite and proximal ca. 2.55 Ga detritus date rift initiation; upward provenance broadening, seawater-like carbonate chemistry, positive pre-ore δ13C and later manganese accumulation record margin maturation and sediment starvation. Apparent Paleoproterozoic detrital ages in Buritirama are reproducible by low-discordance Pb loss from Archean zircon. The same correction applies to the Novolândia granulite belt, whose sedimentary protoliths carry a 3.32–3.18 Ga Paleoarchean provenance peak, 2.75 and 2.55 Ga magmatic populations and a rift-type granite crystallized at 2567 ± 22 Ma with 2744 ± 21 Ma inheritance, identifying the far side of the closed ocean as a detached fragment of the Carajás margin. Bacajá arc magmatism at ca. 2.21-2.13 Ga and coeval fluid-assisted re-equilibration in Carajás define upper- and lower-plate responses consistent with slab-pull extension. Decompression, rapid cooling and the unconformable Águas Claras basin, whose basal marine interval is exposed at Azul and Serra Pelada, record collapse and renewed marine transgression. The direct result is the Rhyacian collisional stack; the full Wilson cycle is the integrated model that explains the ordered regional evidence.

papers.t: Computational and experimental study of multi-grain-size sediment transport and sorting process
tk: A coupled large-eddy simulation and multi-grain-size sediment transport model is developed and validated to predict riverbed deformation and particle sorting.
该研究开发并验证了耦合大涡模拟与多粒径泥沙输移的模型，用以预测河床变形和颗粒分选。
papers.ab: Successful prediction of the interaction between turbulent flows and river ecosystems is essential for flood management, development of mitigation strategies, and infrastructure protection. Natural riverbeds consist of bed materials of multiple grain sizes that interact with turbulence differently, leading to spatial classification of particle sizes. Such particle sorting processes can only be captured by models capable of handling multiple grain sizes. We present a numerical framework that couples large-eddy simulation with a multi-grain-size sediment transport module to track multiple grain size classes, their local fractions within the bed-load layer, and bed evolution. A laboratory experiment was conducted in a flume with multi-size bed material to examine sediment particle redistribution and sorting. Measured sediment grain size distributions and bed elevations were used to validate the numerical framework. The results of the multi-grain-size sediment transport model for bed deformation were then compared against those of a uniform sediment transport model, demonstrating that the former reduces the prediction errors relative to the experimental measurements from 37.98 to 3.83 percent for maximum scour depth and from 48.35 to 11.54 percent for maximum deposition height. The validated numerical framework was also applied to large-scale meandering rivers with multi-grain bed material, simulating their bed deformation and sediment sorting. The simulation results revealed the formation of particle sorting patterns in meandering rivers, with coarser and finer sediment particles accumulating near the erosional depression (scour) and depositional (point bar) regions, respectively. These findings support the coupled framework's ability to predict sediment particle sorting and highlight the importance of representing bed material heterogeneity in numerical modeling of meandering rivers.

papers.t: Robust clustering of variable-duration seismic waveforms using an incremental dynamic time warping framework
tk: A new unsupervised clustering algorithm using incrementally buffered Dynamic Time Warping groups variable-duration seismic waveforms without requiring fixed window lengths.
基于增量动态时间规整的无监督算法，可对变长度地震波形聚类。
papers.ab: Different geophysical processes generate characteristic seismic waveforms. Identifying similar waveforms therefore helps to distinguish between different source mechanisms and to monitor seismic activity in settings ranging from volcanoes and glaciers to urban environments. In many applications, however, the seismic event types are unknown and no labelled training data is available. Then, unsupervised clustering is necessary. Most existing approaches require all input vectors to have the same length, which in seismology translates to a fixed event window. However, seismic signals can differ considerably in duration: This may require events to be cropped or padded to a common length, which may lead to a loss of important waveform characteristics. Furthermore, the approaches commonly rely on extensive feature engineering or machine-learned representations, which often require hyperparameter tuning and can reduce the physical interpretability of the resulting clusters. In addition, many clustering algorithms require the number of clusters to be specified a priori, limiting their flexibility when analysing previously unknown datasets. This study introduces Incrementally Buffered Dynamic Time Warping Clustering, a new unsupervised clustering algorithm that operates directly on seismic time-series data using a small number of physically interpretable parameters. The method is based on Dynamic Time Warping and is particularly suited to noisy and continuously active seismic environments, where overlapping signals and imperfect event catalogues are common. The buffered and incremental structure of the algorithm explicitly identifies outliers and allows new clusters to form during incremental updates, enabling continuous monitoring without reclustering the entire dataset. The algorithm is evaluated on a labelled volcano-seismic dataset, where it achieves a clustering accuracy of 69.39 per cent, comparable to previously published supervised approaches. A second application to Antarctic icequake data demonstrates its ability to identify meaningful waveform groups in a setting with limited prior knowledge of event types. These results show that the newly introduced clustering algorithm provides an interpretable and scalable framework for clustering large seismic datasets while retaining direct access to waveform similarity in the time domain.

papers.t: Comparisons of tsunami inundation for homogeneous and heterogeneous earthquake sources at selected sites for the Cascadia Subduction Zone
tk: Modeling heterogeneous earthquake sources for Cascadia shows that tsunami inundation limits and hazard thresholds extend further inland than traditional homogeneous models.
模拟卡斯卡迪亚非均匀震源表明海啸淹没范围比传统均匀模型更深。
papers.ab: Tsunami hazard severity — especially tsunami inundation depth — is related to the tsunami’s source mechanism. Traditionally, homogeneous earthquake rupture sources have been used as the source mechanism for tsunamis generated in the Cascadia Subduction Zone for regional hazard assessment. We show with 200 heterogeneous earthquake rupture sources how tsunami inundation hazards change for three sites located along the Cascadia Subduction Zone when the assumption of homogeneous slip is relaxed. Our results indicate that the tsunami inundation limit extends further inland compared to homogeneous sources. We also note that the 1-in-2475-year exceedance threshold extends further inland for heterogeneous earthquake rupture sources compared to official tsunami evacuation lines and the American Society of Civil Engineers tsunami design zone.

papers.t: Stabilizing seismic source inversion by accounting for P-wave picking uncertainty: A waveform-shift covariance approach
tk: A new waveform-shift covariance approach incorporates P-wave picking uncertainty into seismic source inversion, significantly improving the stability and accuracy of inferred earthquake rupture models.
将P波寻相不确定性纳入协方差矩阵，显著提高了震源反演的稳定性。
papers.ab: In seismic source inversion using teleseismic P waves, P-wave arrival times are picked from observed waveforms and used to adjust their timing relative to the predicted arrivals. However, uncertainty in the picked arrival times remains after this correction. Picking errors shift the entire waveform and produce temporally correlated waveform errors. If these errors are not properly accounted for, small differences in arrival-time picks may substantially alter the inferred source models and contribute to discrepancies among analysts. In this study, I propose a waveform-shift covariance approach that approximately constructs the component of the data covariance matrix associated with P-wave picking uncertainty from observed waveforms and a probability distribution of time shifts. I incorporate this approach into potency density tensor inversion (PDTI) and compare it with a conventional approach that neglects picking uncertainty, using 125 synthetic waveform datasets that differ only in picking errors. Relative to the conventional approach, the proposed method reduces the normalized model root mean square error (RMSE) by approximately 0.09 and reduces the variability among inferred source models across datasets to less than 40% of that for the conventional approach. Although the normalized data RMSE is comparable between the two approaches, the normalized model RMSE for individual datasets is concentrated within 0.32–0.36 for the proposed method, whereas it spans 0.35–0.50 for the conventional approach. These results show that incorporating P-wave picking uncertainty into the data covariance matrix yields more accurate and stable source models, even though the proposed and conventional approaches fit the observed waveforms similarly well. Application to real earthquake data with uncertain P-wave picks suggests that neglecting the data error structure may lead to overfitting in the conventional approach. Accounting for picking uncertainty changes how waveform discrepancies are weighted in the inversion, reducing the tendency to interpret waveform-shift errors as source complexity. These findings underscore the importance of returning to a basic principle for reliable estimation of earthquake rupture processes: interpreting source signals in observed data requires an understanding of not only the signal structure but also the error structure.

papers.t: Deep Earthquake Swarm near the Moho: Implications for Fluid-Driven Reactivation of a Pre-existing Fracture Network
in: Bosai Kagaku Gijutsu Kenkyujo, Unknown, Ibaraki, 3-1, Tennodai, Tsukuba, Japan [JP]
Bosai Kagaku Gijutsu Kenkyujo, Unknown, Japan [JP]
tk: Relocation and moment-tensor analysis of a deep Moho earthquake swarm in Japan reveal fluid-driven reactivation of a pre-existing heterogeneous fracture network.
莫霍面深源地震群分析表明深部流体驱动了预存裂隙网格的活动。
papers.ab: A deep earthquake swarm has continued beneath northern Yamaguchi, southwestern Japan, near the Abu Monogenetic Volcano Group since February 2025. We investigated its spatiotemporal evolution and source processes using hypocenter relocation and moment-tensor analysis. Relocated hypocenters are concentrated at depths of approximately 25-35 km and exhibit distinct geometries evolving with time, including inclined planar structures in the south and a relatively horizontal structure in the north. Several episodes show diffusion-like hypocenter migration, with apparent diffusivities of 0.12-4.57 m 2 /s. Moment-tensor solutions are diverse and include significant non-double-couple components, while locally clustered events often show similar or nearly reversed mechanisms. These observations suggest that fluid-pressure perturbations associated with deep fluids propagated through a pre-existing heterogeneous fracture network, sequentially reactivating locally favorable structures. The swarm highlights transient deep fluid related seismicity near the Moho beneath a region without recent surface volcanism.

papers.t: Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution
tk: A neural network model predicts the spatial distribution of high-latitude decameter ionospheric irregularities using SuperDARN/SECIRA radar and space weather data.
该研究利用SuperDARN/SECIRA雷达和空间天气数据，构建了预测高纬度十米级电离层不均匀体空间分布的神经网络模型。
papers.ab: This paper describes an approach to constructing nowcast and forecast predictive models for the occurrence of high-latitude decameter ionospheric irregularities based on SuperDARN and SECIRA radar data and space weather parameters. The method relies on self-learning pattern recognition in the dynamics of space weather parameters, that influence the irregularities formation. The proposed approach is a data-driven, multiscale method in which the spatial distribution of irregularities is approximated using a neural network of an original architecture, inspired by graph neural networks. The model was trained and tested using data from 11 radars during the period 2010-2025 (SuperDARN: CVW, ICE, ICW, INV, PGR, PYK, RKN, SAS, STO; SECIRA: EKB, MAGW). It is shown that the model achieves optimal performance when using geomagnetic coordinates MLT,MLAT. The optimal set of parameters for the best nowcast and forecast over studied set of parameters is a combination of geomagnetic and solar disturbance indices ($a_{p}$, $K_{p}$, $AE$, F10.7) from ground-based observations, and satellite-measured solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field parameters ($P_{sw}$, $E_{sw}$, $\widetilde{B_{z}}$, $T_{sw}$). Hourly mean values for all the parameters were used in the analysis. The results indicate that acceptable forecast quality is achieved with a lead time of up to 7-9 hours, with the highest quality reached for nowcast (zero lead time). It is shown that the parameters $\widetilde{B_{z}}$ and F10.7 are significant for nowcasting only and can be neglected for other lead times. It is shown that $AE$ and $T_{sw}$ are significant for mid-term forecast (\textgreater 2hours ahead) and can be neglected for short-term predictions. Statistical relationships between the maximum latitude of the equatorial boundary of the irregularities and space weather parameters are also discussed.

papers.t: From seafloor morphology to fault architecture: Three-dimensional reconstruction and segmentation of the offshore Carboneras Fault Zone (Alborán Sea)
in: Barcelona Center for Subsurface Imaging, Institut de Ciencies del Mar - CSIC, Passeig Marítim de la Barceloneta, 37-49, Barcelona, 08003, Barcelona, Spain, 08003
Geociencias Barcelona - CSIC, Lluís Solé i Sabarís, s/n, Barcelona, Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain [ES], 08028
Facultat de Ciències de la Terra, Universitat de Barcelona, Martí i Franquès, s/n, Barcelona, Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, 08028
tk: Integrates multibeam bathymetry and multichannel seismic reflection data to reconstruct the 3D geometry and segmentation of the offshore Carboneras Fault Zone.
结合多波束水深与多道地震反射数据，重建了阿尔沃兰海卡沃内拉斯断裂带的三维几何结构与分段特征。
papers.ab: The Carboneras Fault Zone (CFZ) is one of the most active structures of the Alborán Sea, and together with the Al-Idrissi Fault, forms part of the Trans-Alborán Shear Zone (TASZ), which accommodates ongoing Africa-Eurasia convergence. Despite its tectonic significance, the offshore geometry and segmentation of the CFZ remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate multibeam bathymetry, high-resolution multichannel seismic reflection data, and three-dimensional (3D) structural modelling to reassess its offshore architecture. Our results show that the offshore CFZ forms a deformation corridor exceeding 110 km in length, comprising five principal and seven subsidiary fault segments. Individual segments range from 6.48 to 41.1 km in length and strike between N46º; and N79º. Interpretation of nine stratigraphic horizons, from the Tortonian acoustic basement to the seafloor, enabled the reconstruction of a 3D geological model of the fault system. Along-strike variations in deformation style, uplift, and segmentation allow subdivision of the CFZ into northeastern, central, and southwestern sectors. Structural complexity is greatest in the central sector, where fault branching, pressure ridges, a sag pond, and flower structures define a deformation corridor up to 4.1 km wide, and where uplift and accommodation contrasts between structural highs and fault-controlled depocentres are strongest. This complexity coincides with the transition between the dominant NE-SW-striking segments (N46º-N59º) and the more easterly southwestern segments (~N79º).
