Our findings refine previous models by resolving the 3D geometry, segmentation, and along-strike variability of the offshore CFZ, providing new insights into fault localization, tectonic inheritance, tectono-sedimentary evolution, and constraints for seismic-hazard assessment.

papers.t: A 400 Myr subduction memory in the mid-ocean ridge source
tk: Mantle hydration modeled over 410 Myr reveals that subduction water signatures can persist in the mid-ocean ridge source for up to 400 Myr.
过去4.1亿年的板块重建模型表明，俯冲水分特征可在洋中脊地幔源区保留长达4亿年。
papers.ab: The upper mantle sampled by mid-ocean ridges carries the volatile imprint of past subduction, but the global distribution of hydration through time and how long that imprint survives mixing and melt extraction are poorly known. We investigate the history of mantle hydration by calculating where and when hydration occurred using a plate reconstruction model of subducted water over the past 410 Myr. We compare model results to present-day mantle hydration based on H₂O/Ce in ~1,340 mid-ocean ridge basalt (MORB) glasses from ~1,050 sites. Estimated hydration ages vary by region: ~120 Ma for the Arctic, ~320 Ma for the northern Mid-Atlantic Ridge (NMAR), ~220 Ma for the mid-latitude Mid-Atlantic, and ~380 Ma for the southern Mid-Atlantic (SMAR). Most Pacific ridges show no evidence of hydration. Globally, MORB derived from mantle with a modeled hydration age has a higher median H₂O/Ce than MORB from mantle with no modeled water delivery (249 versus 200). Neither hydration age nor duration affects H2O/Ce in present-day MORB. Agreement between model and data is particularly strong in the North Atlantic and Arctic. Here, hydrated mantle remained largely undisturbed until the post-130 Ma westward migration of North America. Subduction signatures may remain detectable as long as 400 Myr after hydration, well beyond the lifetime of the plate configuration that produced them.

papers.t: Bayesian Co- and Postseismic Slip Model of the 2023 Mw 7.8 and 7.7 Türkiye–Syria Earthquake Doublet from Geodetic Data
in: Seismological Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, California, U.S.A.
Now at, Université Grenoble Alpes, Université Savoie Mont Blanc, CNRS, IRD, Université Gustave Eiffel, ISTerre, Gières, France
Now at, Department of Geophysics, Stanford University, Stanford, California, U.S.A.
Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, California, U.S.A.
tk: A Bayesian geodetic inversion of the 2023 Turkey-Syria doublet reveals that postseismic afterslip surrounds coseismic rupture zones, leaving a persistent seismic gap between the Erkenek and Pütürge faults.
贝叶斯大地测量反演表明2023年土耳其双震的余滑包围了同震破裂区，且存在未破裂地震空区。
papers.ab: On 6 February 2023, an earthquake doublet occurred in the East Anatolian fault zone (EAFZ), producing significant surface displacements and causing extensive damage in Türkiye and Syria. The EAFZ is known to be spatially complex, with multiple segments, fault stepovers, and fault-bend structures. How such fault complexities modulate the co- and postseismic distribution of fault slip remains an important question. We use Sentinel-1 and Advanced Land Observation Satellite-2 Synthetic Aperture Radar-derived pixel offset measurements and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) static offsets for the two events to constrain the distribution of coseismic slip along both strands of the EAFZ. We constrain the postseismic slip distribution using Sentinel-1 interferograms and GNSS time series. We adopt a Bayesian framework to explore the solution space, relying solely on physically justifiable prior information without employing artificial regularization. We account for both observational errors and epistemic uncertainties due to imperfect knowledge of the regional elastic structure and orientation of the fault plane. We find that elastic afterslip mostly surrounds the areas of coseismic rupture. However, the geodetic data sets that span the postseismic period cannot be explained solely by elastic afterslip. We also confirm the potential seismic gap on the boundary between the Erkenek and Pütürge faults, across which neither coseismic nor postseismic slip occurs in the periods considered here.

papers.t: Fitful but sustained rupture of the 2026 Mw 7.6 Venezuela earthquake
tk: The 2026 Venezuela earthquake was a single Mw 7.6 event with a fitful, variable-speed rupture that overcame a historical stress barrier to cause severe damage.
2026年委内瑞拉地震是一次单次Mw 7.6事件，其变速破裂克服了历史应力屏障并造成严重破坏。
papers.ab: The devastating 2026 Venezuela earthquake was cataloged as a doublet of \Mw~7.2 and 7.5 events. Combining NISAR and ALOS-2 Synthetic Aperture Radar data, teleseismic source imaging, and ensemble Kalman inversion of multiple moment tensors and dynamic rupture simulations, we show that the 2026 Venezuela earthquake was instead a single \Mw~7.6 event with variable rupture speed and seismic moment release. The earthquake rupture went through episodes of acceleration and deceleration, including a pronounced slow-down around the rupture area of the 1967 \Mw~6.6 Caracas earthquake. Stress transfer from the partially arrested front and a trailing slip pulse enabled the rupture to break through this stress barrier and release ~26% of the seismic moment beneath the coastal cities of Playa Grande and Caraballeda, where damage was most severe. Such fitful ruptures enhance high-frequency seismic radiation and challenge conventional methods for characterization of large earthquakes.

papers.t: HypoNet Nankai PS: rapid hypocenter determination for the Nankai Trough using physics-informed neural networks with three-dimensional P- and S-wave velocity models
tk: HypoNet Nankai PS extends a PINN-based hypocenter determination framework to include both P- and S-wave travel times in a 3D velocity model of the Nankai Trough.
HypoNet Nankai PS将基于PINN的震源定位框架扩展至南海海槽3D速度模型下的P波和S波走时。
papers.ab: Rapid and accurate hypocenter determination based on three-dimensional (3D) seismic velocity models is essential for seismic monitoring in subduction zones, yet it remains computationally demanding. HypoNet Nankai, a hypocenter determination package that uses physics-informed neural network (PINN) travel-time inference for a realistic 3D P-wave velocity model of the Nankai Trough subduction zone, was designed to address this problem, but supported only P-wave arrival times. Here, we present HypoNet Nankai PS, which extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times. We first constructed an S-wave velocity model from the existing P-wave model using empirical conversion relations for marine sediments and the crust. Because the resulting S-wave velocity structure has lower velocities and therefore considerably steeper travel-time gradients, the original PINN training procedure designed for the P-wave velocity structure was insufficient. We therefore revised the training procedure by reconsidering the distribution of collocation points, the NN architecture, and the optimizer. Benchmark comparisons with the fast marching method showed that the revised approach substantially reduced the root-mean-square deviations for both P- and S-waves compared with the original algorithm. Recovery tests using synthetic earthquakes were also performed. When applied to 223 earthquakes recorded by DONET stations off the Kii Peninsula, the system yielded hypocenters generally consistent with the JMA catalog beneath the network, suggesting that the 3D velocity model captures travel-time variations accommodated by JMA's 1D model and station corrections. Farther seaward, the estimated hypocenters were substantially shallower than those in the JMA catalog and were located in the oceanic crust and uppermost mantle, consistent with previous relocations that used DONET data and 3D velocity models.

papers.t: Coseismic rock slope deformation at different failure stages - towards assessing the likelihood of high hazard avalanching failures
in: Geotest Ag
University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand [NZ]
Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research WSL, Birmensdorf, Switzerland [CH]
GNS Science, Lower Hutt, New Zealand [NZ]
Wsp
Oregon State University College of Forestry, Corvallis, Oregon, United States [US]
tk: Proposes the Translational Slope Deformation Index (TSDI) to link coseismic slope displacement to the likelihood of catastrophic rock avalanche transitions.
提出平移边坡变形指数（TSDI），将地震滑坡位移与发生灾难性崩塌的概率联系起来。
papers.ab: Landslide hazard is the probability of occurrence of an event of a given magnitude in a specific area and time period. The failure mechanism of the mass, and displacement needed to transition the hillslope from metastable to failure are fundamental inputs for coseismic landslide hazard analyses. In closely-jointed rock mass, joint-step-path failure mechanisms evolve with increasing rock-mass displacement. Three main stages have been hypothesized; incipient, transitional and avalanching. Investigating and characterizing these failure-stage transitions is critical for quantifying coseismic landslide hazard as the hillslope-specific scale. However, little is known about the magnitudes of rock mass displacement associated with these transitions. This study aims to quantify the hillslope displacement magnitudes required to transition a rock mass to failure. These thresholds are based on remote sensing measurements of displacement and derived estimates of normalised translational slope displacement (TSDs) - used as a proxy for rock mass deformation or strain - for six coseismic landslides situated in closely-jointed greywacke. Our results show that for a rock mass to transition from metastable to failure - the rock avalanche stage - requires TSDs greater than 5%, where the amount of TSD required varies with the hillslope angle. We propose an empirically-derived “translational slope deformation index” (TSDI); a function of the translational angle of displacement and normalised displacement along it. This novel tool could provide the link between the permanent slope displacements estimated using analytical methods, to the likelihood that a slope will transition into a more mobile, hazardous rock avalanche, during earthquake shaking.

papers.t: Controlled-Source Seismic Imaging of the Cascadia Margin Off Oregon: Implications for Hydration and Dehydration Processes of the Shallow Juan de Fuca Slab
in: Department of Geology and Geophysics
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

Auburn University
tk: Wide-angle seismic traveltime tomography offshore Oregon reveals shallow slab dehydration and fracturing of the Juan de Fuca plate at 12-15 km depth.
俄勒冈近海宽角地震走时成像揭示了胡安·德富卡板块在12-15千米深处的浅部脱水与破裂。
papers.ab: Three profiles of wide-angle seismic traveltime data offshore Oregon are analyzed to determine two-dimensional compressional-wave velocity structure. Tomographic imaging of the Juan de Fuca (JdF) plate reveals a porous, hydrated upper crust and a dry lower crust and uppermost mantle. The accretionary prism is imaged as a wedge of lower-velocity material oceanward of Siletzia, a high-velocity block in the upper plate. Seismic velocity boundaries within the prism align with previously identified kinematic discontinuities, including the static backstop of Siletzia and the transition between active (oceanward) and non-active (landward) wedge deformation. As the JdF plate interacts with and subducts beneath Siletzia in Central Oregon, the JdF crust fractures and releases pore water into the overlying wedge by 12-15 km depth, as evidenced by coincident localized velocity reductions in the slab and wedge and the seafloor seeps. Dewatering along this 100-km segment leaves the JdF plate generally dry as it enters the mantle. Localized slow-velocity anomalies suggest locally increased hydration, potentially consistent with evidence for water input farther down-dip in the subduction system.

tk: The 2021 Luxian earthquake triggered a multi-year, spatially shifting release of thermogenic shale gas, demonstrating methane's utility as a tracer for post-seismic subsurface connectivity.
泸县地震引发了空间迁移的甲烷释放，可示踪震后地下连通性演化。
papers.ab: Following the September 2021 M S 6.0 Luxian earthquake in China's Luzhou shale-gas field, soil methane enrichment shifted between fault zones and the epicentral area. We combine 4 surveys during 2021–2026 with 2021 isotopes, seismicity, shallow geophysical structure, and mechanical calculations to examine this redistribution. Concentration–carbon-isotope covariation (ρ = 0.61; n = 14) supports a thermogenic contribution compatible with regional shale gas. Enrichment was concentrated on the anticlinal flanks in 2021, weakened in 2023, peaked centrally in 2024, and shifted northwestward in 2026. Localized buried slip and heterogeneous Coulomb stress changes favor selective adjustment of existing pathways. We interpret the sequence as rapid shallow release, episodic deeper replenishment, and a later northwestern response associated with local seismicity. Methane thus provides a geochemical tracer of evolving subsurface connectivity, guiding monitoring of fossil methane escape after strong earthquakes.

papers.t: Interseismic Locking on the Main Himalayan Thrust From Viscoelastic Earthquake-Cycle Models With a Nonstationary Locked-Creeping Boundary
in: Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, Indiana University Bloomington, 1001 East 10th Street, Bloomington, IN, Bloomington, IN, United States, 47405-1405
GEOMAR Helmholtz-Zentrum fur Ozeanforschung Kiel, Wischoffstraße 1-3, Kiel, IN, Germany [DE]
tk: Viscoelastic earthquake-cycle models of the Main Himalayan Thrust show that nonstationary locked-creeping boundaries concentrate moment accumulation and transition rapidly to full creep.
结合粘弹性地震周期模型的喜马拉雅主推覆断层反演表明，非稳态锁固-蠕滑边界使矩累积更加集中。
papers.ab: Interseismic locking on the Main Himalayan Thrust (MHT) governs where crustal strain and seismic moment accumulate, yet published locking inversions vary substantially with assumptions about fault boundary and coupling kinematics. We combine Himalayan Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements with a viscoelastic earthquake-cycle model that includes interseismic viscous flow in the lower crust and mantle and an approximation for gradual migration of the locked−creeping boundary on the MHT. We invert baseline length-change rates and evaluate 20 model configurations that vary fault-block kinematics and lower-crustal and mantle viscosity structure. Across the ensemble, strong locking is concentrated above mid-crustal ramp segments, whereas uncertainty peaks near ramp transitions and along the downdip edge of locking. Increasing lower-crustal and mantle viscosity shifts the inferred locked zone farther downdip. Inferred strongly negative process zone stressing rates along the bottom boundary of locking across much of the margin suggest up-dip propagation of creep into the locked zone. A stationary end-member with zero process zone stressing rate fits the data more poorly and distributes moment accumulation broadly across the interface from the surface to ∼45 km depth, producing a gradual transition from locking to full creep. In contrast, the nonstationary solutions concentrate nearly all moment accumulation within the locked zone and exhibit a rapid transition to full creep outside it, yielding locked-zone moment accumulation rates roughly twice those inferred from the stationary model. These results refine Himalayan moment-budget estimates and highlight how rheology and boundary dynamics influence geodetic coupling inferences.

papers.t: Deep-Slab Earthquakes Illuminate the Crust Beneath Campi Flegrei
in: Universita degli Studi di Napoli Federico II Dipartimento di Fisica Ettore Pancini, Complesso Universitario Monte S. Angelo, via Cinthia, Naples, Italy [IT]
Universita degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, Unknown, Naples, Italy [IT]
tk: Adapts receiver-function analysis using regional deep-slab earthquakes to image the crustal structure and magmatic sill beneath the Campi Flegrei caldera.
利用区域深源地震的接收函数分析，首次精细成像了坎皮佛莱格瑞火山下方的地壳结构与岩浆房顶界。
papers.ab: Constraining the crust beneath Campi Flegrei is critical for understanding its magmatic system, but the resolution of local-earthquake tomography decreases with depth. Here, we adapt receiver-function analysis to intermediate- and deep-focus earthquakes within the Ionian slab beneath the Tyrrhenian Sea, recorded by the dense Campi Flegrei seismic network at regional distances. Deep sources provide steep P-wave incidence, while relatively short source–receiver paths reduce high-frequency attenuation receiver functions are corrected for finite-distance moveout and modelled using ray-theory simulations and global optimization. Synthetic tests assess the resolution of the method. The preferred model identifies a prominent interface at 7.7±0.4 km depth, associated with a low-velocity, high- layer, and a deeper discontinuity at 21.7±0.9 km, interpreted as the Moho. The 7.7 km interface is consistent with the top of the magmatic sill identified by the 2001 active-source experiment. No additional shallow discontinuity is required by the data within the resolution of the method.

papers.t: Rupture elongation for buried earthquakes suggests directionally structured heterogeneity in fault stress and strength
in: Department of Earth and Space Sciences
Southern University of Science and Technology
Department of Earth Sciences
University of Southern California
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geophysical High-resolution Imaging Technology
Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Exploration Technology

tk: Rupture aspect ratios of buried earthquakes, analyzed alongside 3D dynamic simulations, suggest that directionally structured heterogeneity in fault stress and strength controls rupture elongation.
结合埋藏地震破裂长宽比观测与三维动力学模拟，揭示断层应力和强度的方向性非均匀性控制了破裂延伸。
papers.ab: Finite-fault attributes, such as rupture elongation in buried earthquakes, may reflect the spatial organization of fault stress and strength. We quantify rupture elongation using rupture aspect ratio (RAR), derived from the spatial second seismic moment of slip for 51 screened finitefault models spanning 𝑀𝑤 4.45–7.43 whose ruptures neither reach the surface nor span the seismogenic thickness. Observed RARs range from 1.02 to 1.59, with a median of 1.18 and a pronounced upper tail toward elongated ruptures. We then use three-dimensional boundaryintegral dynamic rupture simulations to determine how heterogeneous fault properties modify rupture geometry. Homogeneous self-arresting models reproduce the nearly circular RAR range but fail to reach the most elongated ruptures. Introducing directional heterogeneity in initial stress and frictional properties broadens the simulated RAR distributions and generates substantially greater elongation. Across the tested parameter ranges, initial-stress amplitude and directional structure exert the strongest influence on RAR. Several heterogeneous parameter combinations are compatible with the observed high-RAR subset, showing that similar rupture geometries can arise from different fault states. The RAR distribution therefore provides a statistical, rather than deterministic, constraint on classes of directionally structured fault states. Together, the observations and simulations establish a quantitative framework for evaluating candidate directional organizations of fault stress and strength from the RAR statistics of buried ruptures.

papers.t: Quantifying the Threat: A Bayesian Probabilistic Framework for Heavy Metal Health Risks among Children in the Densu Basin, Ghana
tk: A Bayesian probabilistic framework quantifies cumulative heavy metal health risks for children using groundwater samples from Ghana's Densu Basin.
该研究利用贝叶斯概率框架评估了加纳Densu流域儿童的地下水重金属健康风险。
papers.ab: Groundwater in Ghana's Densu River Basin remains a key domestic water source, but multi-metal contamination threatens children's health. Previous deterministic hazard index assessments provide limited treatment of uncertainty, co-exposure, and spatial variability. This study applies a Bayesian probabilistic framework for non-carcinogenic risk assessment using 94 groundwater samples and measurements of Fe, Mn, Ni, Pb, Cd, and As. A Bayesian regression model propagates parameter uncertainty and accounts for contaminant co-occurrence. Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo is used for posterior inference, while inverse distance weighting generates spatially continuous risk surfaces. Pb, As, and Cd dominate cumulative risk. Posterior predictive results indicate that approximately 31% of sampling sites have a probability greater than 0.5 of exceeding a hazard index (HI) of 1. The risk surface is highly heterogeneous, with a posterior mean of 0.372 and a standard deviation of 0.416. High-risk zones often reflect moderate co-exposure rather than extreme contamination by a single metal. The framework provides uncertainty-aware, spatially explicit information to support groundwater monitoring, risk mitigation, and public health planning in data-limited regions.

tk: Shear-wave splitting in the Central India Tectonic Zone reveals asthenospheric mantle flow aligned with plate motion alongside fossilized lithospheric fabrics from ancient orogenies.

papers.ab: This study presents shear wave splitting (SWS) estimates for core-refracted SK(K)S phases utilizing data from nine seismic stations in the Central Indian Tectonic Zone (CITZ) that were temporarily operational between July 2023 and July 2025. The CITZ was formed during the Mesoproterozoic orogeny in central India, resulting from the collision of the northern Bundelkhand Craton with a jumble of South Indian cratons. We used transverse energy minimization methodology to ascertain the SWS parameters, the fast polarization directions (FPDs) and splitting delay times ( δ t ). A total of 129 high-quality SWS measurements were obtained from 87 earthquakes ( M >5.5) at epicentral distances between 84–145° for SKS phases and 84–180° for SKKS phases. The mean δ t s at each seismic station ranges from 0.7 to 1.4 s, demonstrating the upper mantle heterogeneity in the study region. Most stations show NE-SW FPDs, aligning with the Absolute Plate Motion (APM) of the Indian plate. Ray-piercing-point spatial coherency analysis suggests that 200–250 km is a promising average depth of anisotropy, indicating that the primary source of the observed SWS measurement is mantle flow at asthenospheric depths, rather than frozen lithospheric fabric. tk: Calibrates a local magnitude scale for Taiwan using station- and interval-specific corrections, incorporating a moment magnitude proxy to prevent saturation.
基于台湾地表和井下台网校准地方震级，引入矩震级代理以解决大震饱和问题。
papers.ab: Local magnitude (ML) must remain consistent as a seismic network combines surface and borehole installations and changes its recorded responses. It can also underestimate large earthquakes. We calibrate an ML scale for Taiwan from more than eight million Wood–Anderson amplitudes at 188,109 earthquakes and 873 stations, with a separate correction for every instrument and for every interval over which its response was unchanged. In calendar year validation experiments, estimating corrections while excluding the test year reduced the median dispersion among all station magnitudes by more than 50% and reduced the misfit to moment magnitude by 21%. We also derive an amplitude magnitude MA and adjust it for saturation, and the reported magnitude changes from ML to the adjusted value when MA exceeds 5.5. The adjustment improves agreement for the largest earthquakes of the calibration set, although they are few. The equations and three correction tables allow the scale to be applied across the calibrated network.

papers.t: OWL: Open Wave Library for seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion in acoustic and elastic media
in: Earth and Environmental Sciences Division, Los Alamos National Laboratory , Los Alamos, NM 87545 ,
Pennsylvania State University Department of Geosciences, , University Park, PA 16802 ,
tk: OWL is an open-source, high-order finite-difference framework for 2D/3D seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion in acoustic, elastic, and anisotropic media.
OWL是一个用于声波、弹性波及各向异性介质地震波模拟与全波形反演的开源高阶有限差分框架。
papers.ab: Summary Seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI) are important tools for investigating subsurface structures and properties. Open-source seismic modeling and inversion tools enable researchers to test new methods, reproduce published results, and use waveform data to characterize the subsurface. However, building flexible FWI workflows still requires substantial effort to integrate wave solvers, misfit functions, and inversion algorithms. We introduce the Open Wave Library (OWL), an open-source framework that integrates these capabilities for local- to exploration-scale modeling and FWI. We implement high-order finite-difference solvers for 2D and 3D isotropic acoustic, isotropic elastic, and general anisotropic elastic media. We combine curvilinear meshes and local refinement to represent topographic elastic free surfaces, and use complex-frequency-shifted multi-axial perfectly matched layers to support stable simulations in strongly anisotropic media. For FWI, we implement conventional waveform, correlation, and adaptive waveform misfits to accommodate different waveform characteristics and degrees of cycle skipping. We also develop two objectives based on generalized dynamic time warping: one penalizes the estimated time shifts, while the other measures amplitude differences after warping. We regularize the time-shift estimates and use a common warping function across components for multi-component data. We compute adjoint-state gradients using source wavefields reconstructed from stored boundary values. We accelerate modeling and inversion through shot-level parallelism, distributed-memory domain decomposition for 3D models, and OpenMP shared-memory parallelism. We assess solver accuracy and numerical consistency through unit tests and comparisons with spectral-element solutions. Through sensitivity-kernel studies and synthetic and field data examples, we demonstrate the complementary behavior of the misfit functions and the applicability of OWL to heterogeneous, anisotropic, and topographic models. OWL assumes negligible Earth curvature and is not intended for regional- or global-scale simulations. Our current implementation runs on central processing units (CPUs); support for heterogeneous computing architectures, viscoelasticity, and coupled acoustic–elastic media remains for future development. With OWL, we provide an extensible platform for methodological research and reproducible seismic modeling and inversion.

papers.t: CURIE: A continental-scale probabilistic magnetotelluric reference model of USArray data for the contiguous United States
in: University of Houston Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, , Houston, TX ,
Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences, Massachusetts Institute of Technology Department of Earth, , Cambridge, MA ,
Southern University of Science and Technology Department of Earth and Space Sciences, , Shenzhen ,
University of Houston Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, , TX ,
tk: CURIE provides a continental-scale probabilistic 1D magnetotelluric reference model of the contiguous US using physics-driven normalizing flows to quantify resistivity uncertainties.
CURIE利用正则化流构建了美国本土概率性一维磁共振参考模型。
papers.ab: Summary Magnetotellurics (MT) provides critical constraints on Earth’s electrical conductivity structure and thereby illuminates lithosphere and mantle processes. The EarthScope USArray MT program provides a unique opportunity to investigate large-scale tectonic and compositional variations across the contiguous United States (U.S.). However, uniform MT interpretation is hindered by data quality and the computational and initialization demands of 3D inversion. To provide a physically consistent and uncertainty-aware continental-scale baseline, we develop CURIE (continental U.S. 1D resistivity inference ensemble), comprising two complementary probabilistic reference model ensembles obtained by independently inverting the Zxy and Zyx components from 1773 MT stations using unsupervised, physics-driven normalizing flows. For each station and mode, CURIE provides posterior resistivity distributions, uncertainty estimates, and predicted MT responses. We assess the 1D assumption using filtered data misfit, mode differences, and phase tensor skew and ellipticity. Most stations yield filtered misfits below 4, indicating that 1D models reproduce the dominant responses. Low phase-tensor skew and ellipticity broadly coincide with low-misfit regions across the Interior Plains and the Intermontane Plateaus, whereas elevated indicators and misfits along tectonic and continental margins identify areas where 1D interpretation requires greater caution. At shallow depths, CURIE recovers resistivity patterns associated with major geological provinces; at mid- to lower-lithospheric depths, it resolves the broad contrast between the tectonically active western U.S. and the stable eastern craton. Differences between the Zxy and Zyx results along the Pacific and Gulf coasts, and in Florida further reflect orthogonal sensitivities to conductivity gradients and indicate 3D structural orientations, with some near-coast misfits influenced by the coast effect. The resulting dataset provides a continent-wide probabilistic reference that offers a first-order view of the U.S. electrical structure while supporting data quality assessment, identification of potential 3D effects, and development of initial or reference models for future 3D inversion and geodynamic interpretation.

papers.t: Imaging the Magnetic Structure of Izu-Oshima Volcano Using Observation-Mesh Decoupled 3-D Magnetic Inversion with Self-Demagnetization
in: State Key Laboratory of Marine Geology
Tongji University
Earthquake Research Institute
University of Tokyo
Center for Environmental Remote Sensing
Chiba University
tk: A new 3D magnetic inversion framework incorporating self-demagnetization and observation-mesh decoupling successfully images the shallow magmatic and hydrothermal systems of Izu-Oshima volcano.
提出一种结合自退磁和观测网格解耦的3D磁反演框架，成功成像了伊豆大岛火山的浅部岩浆与热液系统。
papers.ab: High-resolution airborne magnetic surveys are increasingly used to image shallow volcanic structures, but interpretation remains challenging in basaltic volcanoes where strongly magnetized lava, shallow intrusions, and hydrothermally altered rocks coexist beneath rugged topography. In such settings, conventional linear formulations can be unreliable because self-demagnetization modifies internal magnetization, and finite-element response evaluation may depend on the observation mesh. We develop a self-demagnetization-aware magnetic inversion framework based on a hybrid finite-element and volume-integral formulation. The finite-element solution resolves the susceptibility-dependent internal magnetic field, whereas the volume-integral operator evaluates the external magnetic anomaly from the resulting magnetization distribution at arbitrary airborne observation points. This separation avoids refinement around dense flight-line observations and suppresses mesh-dependent local-gradient artifacts. An analytical ellipsoid benchmark verifies that the formulation reproduces the response of a high-susceptibility body and provides stable sensitivities for inversion. Application to unmanned autonomous helicopter magnetic data from Izu-Oshima volcano reveals a heterogeneous susceptibility structure beneath the summit caldera. The recovered model images a shallow magnetic layer associated with recent volcanic products and a deeper low-susceptibility domain consistent with hydrothermal demagnetization. Around Mt. Mihara, the susceptibility distribution separates crater-fill lava, laterally distributed buried magnetic bodies, and demagnetized zones that cannot be resolved from the map-view magnetic anomaly alone. Comparison with existing electrical constraints supports a coupled shallow magmatic and hydrothermal system. These results show that self-demagnetization-aware inversion of high-resolution magnetic data can image lava accumulation, shallow magma emplacement, and alteration-related demagnetization in basaltic volcanic systems.

papers.t: Coupling Subsurface and Geomorphic Constraints to Decipher Fault Evolution: Insights from the South Gulf of Evia rift, Central Greece.
in: Department of Earth Science and Engineering
Imperial College London
National Observatory of Athens
Institute of Geodynamics
Department of Geology and Geoenvironment
National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
tk: This study integrates vintage 2D seismic reflection data and river profile geomorphology to reconstruct the million-year to Holocene evolution of active normal faults in Central Greece.
本研究结合复古二维地震反射与河流地貌分析，重建了希腊中部活动正断层百万年来的演化历史。
papers.ab: Understanding the temporal and spatial scales over which normal faults grow and interact is crucial for constraining seismic hazard in regions of active faulting such as Central Greece, where destructive earthquakes have been widely documented. In principle, subsurface and geomorphic datasets should provide complementary insights into fault evolution, allowing fault growth and interaction to be resolved across millennial to million-year timescales, a broader range than can be achieved using either method alone. However, the expression and evolution of normal faults in the subsurface and landscape have generally been explored independently of one another. We focus on the South Gulf of Evia active rift system in Central Greece, where several active normal faults bounding the southern rift margin have recently been mapped, including the Nea Palatia, Kalamos and Varnavas Faults. The availability of both geomorphic and seismic reflection data makes this an ideal natural laboratory to reconstruct their growth and evolution. We present new interpretations of vintage 2D seismic reflection data for the first time since their acquisition in the 1980s, including a new offshore age model for the eastern basin, which indicates that linkage of the two Varnavas Fault segments likely occurred between ca. 12–245 ka. These subsurface constraints are integrated with analyses of tectonic knickzones preserved in river long profiles, providing insights into early fault evolution over 10 5 –10 6 years. We propose fault initiation times for two end member bedrock erodibility scenarios for the Nea Palatia, Kalamos and Varnavas Faults. By applying a coupled landscape and basin analysis we reconstruct fault evolution from million-year to Holocene timescales and provide a proof of concept for the use of this integrated workflow to decipher the evolution of faults over contrasting and interconnected timescales in active rifts. Highlights A new offshore seismic-stratigraphic age model for the South Gulf of Evia Vintage 2D seismic reflection data reveals recent fault evolution over the past ca. 245 kyrs Fault initiation and early interaction recorded by river profiles over 10 5 -10 6 yr timescales Coupled landscape-basin approach resolves fault evolution over Holocene to million-year timescales

papers.t: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
tk: Machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations reveal the phase equilibria of ammonia-hydrogen mixtures, suggesting ammonia rain may occur in Uranus and Neptune.
机器学习分子动力学模拟揭示了氨-氢相平衡，表明天王星和海王星中可能存在氨雨。
papers.ab: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known. We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation. The critical temperature increases with pressure, from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa, and we find no phase separation at 3000 and 4000 K up to 100 GPa. The slope of the critical curve decreases substantially between 0.3 and 30 GPa, and the curve nearly flattens above about 30 GPa and 2000 K, where molecules begin to give way to atomic species. The coexistence curves are asymmetric with an ammonia-rich critical composition. For the expected envelope compositions, the phase boundary lies close to, and intersects, published thermal profiles of Uranus and Neptune, implying ammonia may be raining out in these planets today. In contrast, in warm sub-Neptunes such as TOI-270 d, ammonia and hydrogen are likely miscible in all proportions. Together with previous studies, our results suggest that silicates, water and ammonia separate from hydrogen in sequence as planets cool, with implications for their compositional, thermal and structural evolution.

papers.t: 3D Attenuation Tomography of the Pampean Flat-slab Subduction Zone
in: Michigan State University, 288 Farm Lane, East Lansing, MI, United States [US]
Michigan State University, Unknown, East Lansing, MI, United States [US]
University of Costa Rica, Unknown, San Pedro, Costa Rica [CR]
Department of Geosciences, University of Arizona, Unknown, Tucson, Arizona, United States [US]
New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology, 801 Leroy Pl, Socorro, New Mexico, United States [US]
tk: The first regional 3D attenuation models of the Pampean flat-slab subduction zone reveal strong lateral variations in crustal and mantle attenuation, highlighting hydration and fracturing patterns.
首次构建的潘帕斯平俯冲带三维衰减模型揭示了地壳和地幔的强侧向非均匀性及脱水特征。
papers.ab: The Pampean flat-slab subduction zone (29°–32°S) in the south-central Andes is characterized by a volcanic gap, strong crustal deformation, and a heterogeneous lithospheric mantle, yet the distribution of deformation and hydration remains incompletely resolved. Here we present the first regional 3D attenuation models of this system, derived from P- and S-wave spectra of local earthquakes using a transdimensional Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo tomography approach that quantifies model uncertainties. The resulting models reveal strong lateral variations in attenuation across both the crust and lithospheric mantle. In the continental crust, elevated attenuation is concentrated in the Precordillera and adjacent regions, spatially correlating with major tectonic boundaries and previously mapped fault systems, suggesting that small-scale heterogeneity and fracturing play a primary role. In contrast, lower attenuation in the eastern Sierras Pampeanas is consistent with comparatively less deformed crust. In the lithospheric mantle, attenuation patterns vary systematically along strike. Low attenuation in the western segment is consistent with a relatively cold and dry mantle, whereas higher attenuation above the flat slab may reflect increased hydration and/or the presence of fluids. Farther east, moderate attenuation is compatible with a more depleted and relatively dry lithosphere, while increased attenuation near the transition to steeper subduction may be associated with higher temperatures and possible partial melting in a re-established mantle wedge. Attenuation anomalies within the flat slab itself further suggest enhanced fracturing of the subducted Juan Fernández Ridge.

papers.t: Global Mantle Flow and the Development of Seismic Anisotropy in the Lower Mantle
in: California Institute of Technology, 1200 E California Blvd, Pasadena, CA, United States [US]
tk: Lower-mantle seismic anisotropy records both present-day mantle flow and historical subduction-driven deformation.
下地幔地震各向异性记录了现今地幔流及历史俯冲累积变形。
papers.ab: Seismic anisotropy provides a direct observational constraint on mantle flow in Earth's lowermost mantle. However, mineral fabric that generates anisotropy develops progressively and can preserve a memory of past deformation, rather than simply reflecting present-day flow. Here we investigate this memory by coupling 3-D global thermochemical convection models (with plate reconstruction consistent kinematic boundary conditions) since 230 Ma with mineral texture evolution while making forward predictions of the seismic signal. Models reproduce first-order present-day lower-mantle thermochemical structures, and piles with a relatively small intrinsic density excess and a high bulk modulus produce seismically observed edge morphologies of large low velocity provinces (LLVPs). The computations generate observed global patterns of D′′ anisotropy, including rapid variation of radial anisotropy across pile boundaries, with stronger anisotropy outside and generally weaker anisotropy inside the piles. At large scales, predicted fast polarization directions broadly follow present-day mantle flow, whereas regional departures reveal the influence of accumulated deformation history. Along the eastern margin of the African LLVP, calculations along observed SKS-SKKS ray paths reproduce key features of the regional splitting pattern, consistent with deformation associated with Tethyan subduction. The predicted anisotropy is sensitive to mineral rheology: Weakening associated with the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition localizes deformation near the core-mantle boundary and produces a strong depth dependence to the anisotropy, consistent with that observed beneath the western Pacific. Together, these results show that present-day seismic anisotropy records both the current mantle flow field and its geological history, providing constraints on long-term mantle dynamics and lowermost-mantle rheology.

papers.t: Dual Reverse Time Migration: Efficient Least-squares Imaging with Multiple Scattering in Dual Space
tk: Dual RTM reformulates least-squares imaging in the dual space to efficiently reconstruct multiple scattering and reduce computational costs using a source-independent Hessian.
双重逆时偏移在对偶空间重构多重散射，利用源无关海森矩阵降低计算成本。
papers.ab: Least-squares reverse time migration (LSRTM) estimates a broadband reflectivity image by iteratively minimizing the data misfit. Despite its superior imaging performance over conventional reverse time migration (RTM), LSRTM is fundamentally limited by the first-order Born approximation and incurs a high computational cost due to the iterative solution of a source-dependent model-space Hessian. We propose dual RTM, a seismic imaging framework that reformulates the inverse problem in the dual space, where the optimization variable is the scattering information of all orders, rather than being limited to the first-order scattering of the Born approximation. Unlike LSRTM, which directly estimates the reflectivity model, dual RTM reconstructs the missing scattering data (dual variable) through a fixed-point iteration governed by the full wave equation, enabling the recovery of higher-order scattering and multiple reflections without repeated background velocity updates. Furthermore, dual RTM replaces the source-dependent model-space Hessian with a source-independent data-space Hessian. A hybrid time--frequency formulation enables this Hessian to be assembled and inverted once in the Fourier domain as an offline preprocessing step, reducing the online computational cost of each dual iteration to that of a single RTM application. Numerical experiments on challenging synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that dual RTM suppresses acquisition footprints, improves amplitude fidelity, and enhances deep imaging where primary reflections alone provide insufficient illumination. These results establish dual RTM as an efficient bridge between conventional RTM/LSRTM and nonlinear waveform inversion for high-resolution large-scale seismic imaging.

papers.t: Solid–Fluid Hydraulic Stress Contrast as a Plate Driving Force: A Conceptual Lithosphere–Asthenosphere Coupling Model and Order-of-Magnitude Estimates
tk: Proposes a lithosphere-asthenosphere coupling model where hydraulic stress contrast between solid and fluid-like layers drives plate motion.
提出一种岩石圈-软流圈耦合模型，利用固液介质间的液压应力差驱动板块运动。
papers.ab: The driving force of plate motion remains a central unsolved problem in solid Earth science. This study develops a conceptual, testable framework of lithosphere–asthenosphere coupling that asks whether the contrast in hydraulic stress transmission between the solid lithosphere and the partially molten asthenosphere can supply a distributed horizontal driving force for plate motion. The framework rests on two elementary mechanical premises: in a solid elastic medium under gravitational loading, the horizontal stress is approximately one-third of the vertical stress for a Poisson ratio near 0.25; whereas in a fluid or fluid-like medium, pressure is transmitted almost isotropically, so that the horizontal stress approaches the vertical stress. At an effective depth of about 70 km, the resulting horizontal normal stress contrast reaches the order of Pa. This paper quantitatively discusses two questions bearing on the physical plausibility of the mechanism. The first is the initial melt trigger: overpressure from closed-volume expansion driven by mantle thermal anomalies, reduction of the minimum principal stress by basal tensile stress, and stress concentration at pre-existing microstructures can act together to nucleate the first microfractures. The second is the mechanical feasibility of compressional offset at convergent boundaries: in a gravity field, the minimum principal stress is nearly vertical; when horizontal compression exceeds rock strength at a local weak surface, shear sliding on the fracture surface preferentially occurs along the vertical component, causing one plate front to move downward or overthrust. The model predicts a horizontal compressional stress of about 500–1500 MPa. This exceeds the critical buckling stress of the lithosphere, about 55–600 MPa, by factors of about 11–27; therefore, compressional offset and downward displacement are mechanically feasible. Trench formation requires a large, young, thin, and relatively uniform oceanic lithosphere, together with the dynamic condition of being “unable to move” or “blocked”; large-scale trenches do not form within continental lithosphere. These conditions are most easily satisfied beneath the thin lithosphere of the early Earth, which provides a quantitative mechanical basis for a multi-plate, small-scale, fast-cycling Archean tectonic style. The model further explains the evolution from discrete magmatic intrusions to linear rifting at mid-ocean ridges, the compressional-offset coupling between ridges and trenches at convergent boundaries, and the possibility that asthenospheric return flow is opposite to plate motion. From ridge to trench, the oceanic plate may gradually shrink rather than maintain a constant area. In the reference scenario, the global driving force is about N, and the mechanical power is about 11 TW; under conservative parameters, the estimates remain of order N and several TW. This study does not exclude a role for slab negative buoyancy, lithospheric cooling, or mantle convection in the present plate system. Rather, it proposes a possibly underestimated distributed pressure-transmission mechanism and sets out predictions that can be tested against seismic anisotropy, the thermal structure of subduction zones, and numerical modelling. The model is offered as a hypothesis with explicit falsification conditions and a well-defined scope. Its central inference can be refuted by a single class of observation: if global thermobarometric statistics for mantle xenoliths show that the pressure anomaly beneath mid-ocean ridges cannot be accounted for by the thermal expansion relation—that is, if a pressure deficit persists beyond the thermally induced density deficit—the model fails. Future work should give priority to the systematic compilation and joint inversion of the global xenolith thermobarometric database.

papers.t: Emergent Sparsity: How Many Effective Variables Survive Coarse-Graining in AlphaEarth Embeddings?
tk: The paper shows that the effective dimension of AlphaEarth embeddings decreases significantly under coarse-graining when analyzed using nonlinear beta-VAEs.
非线性分析表明AlphaEarth嵌入维度随空间粗粒化显著降低。
papers.ab: AlphaEarth encodes each 10 m land pixel as a 64-component vector intended to support diverse global mapping tasks. Yet many scientific applications work at coarser spatial supports, for which fewer than 64 effective variables may suffice. We ask whether these vectors can be reorganized into ranked global nonlinear coordinates, how many suffice at a chosen reconstruction accuracy, and whether that number decreases with spatial scale. We thus describe effective dimension as a two-control surface over tolerance and spatial scale, rather than one intrinsic number. At each scale, a $β$-VAE scan with a common architecture produces a rank--distortion envelope, giving the smallest retained count achieved within the scanned family at each reconstruction tolerance. At 3% validation tolerance, this number falls from 24 to 7 when the scale is increased from 10 m to 78.9 km, whereas the corresponding PCA rank falls only from 46 to 38. Repeating the analysis on unit-norm targets preserves this trend.

papers.t: Spec2VEC: Interpretable Spectral Representations of Planetary Signals in Vector Spaces
tk: Spec2VEC is an interpretable, unsupervised representation learning framework that extracts physics-informed textural and spatial features from spectrograms for planetary and exotic seismic signal classification.
Spec2VEC是一种可解释的无监督表征学习框架，用于行星和奇异地震信号分类。
papers.ab: The application of machine learning to planetary geophysics is frequently bottlenecked by a scarcity of labeled data and the complexity of non-stationary seismo-acoustic signals. While deep learning offers powerful feature extraction, it requires massive datasets that are rarely available for phenomena like Martian quakes or deep-ocean volcanism. Consequently, researchers often rely on unsupervised machine learning or hand-engineered features that are typically impoverished or hard to interpret. To resolve this, we introduce Spec2VEC, a framework that transforms parameter-dependent TFRs into a robust, interpretable, and high-dimensional vector space. Spec2VEC treats spectrograms not merely as energy distributions but as structured, textured images, and extracts physics-informed, dataset-agnostic features without requiring massive training loops. The framework systematically extracts a feature vector using two novel pathways: (1) a Textural path that utilizes Hilbert space-filling curves to map 2D spectral patterns into 1D sequences for advanced information-theoretic analysis (e.g., permutation entropy, fractal dimension); and (2) a Spatial path driven by PDFSI (Probabilistic Distribution Fitting for Signal Identification), a novel probabilistic pre-conditioning engine that quantifies spatial connectivity by dynamically separating coherent signal modes from stochastic noise. We validate this feature space on a comprehensive benchmark of complex synthetic wavefields and two real-world examples: an Exotic Seismic Events Catalog (ESEC) and a Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) dataset. Spec2VEC provides objective features for information discrimination and enables highly accurate classification of the diverse geophysical signal classes present in the ESEC catalog. Furthermore, application on the high data volume DAS dataset confirms its computational efficiency and domain-agnostic capability to isolate anomalous seismic arrivals from background noise. Ultimately, Spec2VEC bridges the interpretability of classical signal processing with the discriminative power of modern representation learning, providing a reliable, interpretable foundation for automated discovery across the geosciences. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggag430

tk: InSight detected the first long-period thermospheric acoustic wave on Mars from the S1094b impact, enabling kinetic energy estimation via atmospheric normal mode modeling.
InSight首次探测到火星撞击产生的长周期热层声波，并估算了撞击能量。
papers.ab: We report the detection by the InSight seismometer of a long-period infrasound wave detected about 5.8 hr after the S1094b impact on Mars, on December 24th, 2021. This is the first observation of a long-period ( T > 10 sec) infrasound signal associated with an impact on Mars. This signal can be modeled by atmospheric normal mode summation and is a long-period thermospheric wave, refracted above 150 km altitude, whose low frequency reduces very strongly the expected attenuation of Martian atmosphere CO2 molecular relaxation. Waveform inversions provide an estimate of the kinetic energy of the S1094b impactor in the range of 1-3 10^13 J (2.4-7.2 kT TNT equivalent), in agreement with previous estimates based on the crater diameter. Most of the excitation is likely related to energy deposition during atmospheric entry and not to the surface explosion. The S1094b event is now associated with three different observations: seismic, infrasound and crater formation, enabling future multi-messenger inversions to better estimate the impactor velocity, mass and density.

papers.t: Permafrost augmented simulation and forecast using hybrid modeling through spectral neural networks
tk: A hybrid modeling framework combining numerical cryohydrogeological simulations with spectral neural networks enables fast, stable, and data-assimilated forecasting of permafrost dynamics.
结合数值冰冻圈水文模拟与谱神经网络的混合框架实现了快速稳定的多年冻土预测。
papers.ab: Purpose - Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study investigates the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a critical gap in the existing literature related to high computation times and energy costs of the simulations. Methodology - A numerical cryohydrogeological study on water and energy transfer in a forested, continuous permafrost site has been conducted using parallel high-performance computing to simulate the permafrost dynamics. The numerical results reasonably replicate the measured soil temperature profiles and the dynamics of infiltrated waters. This work uses a spectral network to achieve a fast, reliable, and stable surrogate model for the simulations to forecast over long periods of time. The surrogate is also enhanced by assimilating experimental data through the development of a hybrid modeling framework. Findings - The proposed approach improves the physical simulation while maintaining the stability of the dynamic model over long periods of time. The results reveal that the proposed hybrid modeling remains stable in integration and forecasting. The final hybrid solution demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation accuracy when tested against a test set of measurements. Predictions of the permafrost behavior in the coming decade are later made based on the CMIP6 climate change scenarios. Originality - This research offers a novel perspective on permafrost modeling that extends the current understanding of its behavior under different climate change scenarios. It shows a higher-than-expected temperature increase of the permafrost. Moreover, the stable forecasting of climate change effects is demonstrated.

papers.t: Why Bandung heard the September 2026 Anak Krakatau eruption and Jakarta did not: eruption timing, ray tracing and search-interest evidence, compared with April 2020
tk: Atmospheric ray tracing and Google search data explain why the 2026 Anak Krakatau eruption's acoustic booms bypassed Jakarta but reached Bandung.
大气射线追踪与搜索数据解释了2026年喀拉喀托火山声音传播的选择性。
papers.ab: During the night of 4–5 September 2026, residents of the Bandung area, 240–300 km from Anak Krakatau, reported repeated booms and rattling windows, while Jakarta, 150 km from the volcano, reported almost none. The Indonesian meteorological agency (BMKG) first judged the volcano too distant and the winds unfavourable, then attributed the booms to the eruption. We test the volcanic explanation with three independent lines of open evidence. Timing: the volcanological agency (PVMBG) recorded continuous eruption tremor from 23:07 WIB on 4 September to 00:04 WIB on 6 September, and Darwin VAAC advisories show the ash column rising from about 2 km to 13.7–15.2 km between 23:20 and 01:10 WIB; the booms, reported from about 23:30 to 05:00 WIB, fall within this high-intensity phase and are consistent with atmospheric travel times. Propagation: ray tracing through ERA5 extended upward with the HWM14 wind and NRLMSIS atmosphere models, with 200 random gravity-wave realisations, returns sound to Bandung in 88 % of ensemble members at the eruption hour and in 84–97 % in every hour of the reported window, mostly through eastward winds near the stratopause (about 55–60 km), whereas Bogor (11 %), Jakarta (3 %) and Serang (0 %) lie in a shadow zone; with a windless upper atmosphere the shadow zone persists but the return to Bandung is thermospheric, a path along which absorption would leave only sub-audible infrasound. Search behaviour: all 26 cities with measurable Google search interest in “dentuman” (boom) lay 206–371 km from the volcano, with 96 % of the interest at 200–300 km, while every large city within 200 km showed none; searches for “krakatau” instead declined with distance from the volcano and peaked a day later. Applied to a 2025 meteor of known location, the same measure placed 96 % of “dentuman” interest within 100 km of it. For the April 2020 eruption, whose volcanic origin PVMBG rejected in favour of thunderstorms, eastward stratopause winds also favoured returns, at about 150–210 km; 70 % of “dentuman” interest lay at 100–200 km, and rain within thunder range of Jakarta was light during the reported booms, although a thunderstorm had passed close to Jakarta about two hours earlier. A matched-control analysis of eleven boom reports shows that low-level acoustic ducts occur on most nights and cannot by themselves explain when booms are heard. Long-range sound and infrasound from sustained explosive eruptions, returning beyond a shadow zone, explain both episodes, the 2020 case with less certainty.

papers.t: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints
in: Harvard University
University of Chicago
Tulane University
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
Columbia University
tk: A physics-informed neural operator reveals scale-dependent limits and an accuracy ceiling in recovering Greenland ice loss from sea level fingerprints.
物理信息神经算子揭示了从海平面指纹恢复格陵兰冰盖流失的尺度相关限制。
papers.ab: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.

papers.t: Rare Synchronization Among Recurring Earthquakes
in: Department of Earth and Planetary Science University of California, Berkeley Berkeley CA USA
Miller Institute for Basic science Berkeley CA USA

tk: This study investigates the rare phenomenon of synchronization among recurring earthquake sequences, shedding light on fault interaction and triggering mechanisms.
该研究探讨了重复地震序列之间罕见的同步现象及断层相互作用。
papers.ab: Earthquakes are notoriously irregular, yet occasionally neighboring faults rupture in close succession, repeatedly, as if synchronized. Over successive cycles, differences in recurrence intervals, overall irregularity and external stressors should all drive neighboring faults out of phase. We propose that synchronization emerges only when fault interaction is phase dependent and exceeds the accumulated misalignment. The competing effects are quantifiable from the geometry of neighboring faults, yielding a conditional existence prediction for synchronization that we test first against simulations and then observations. Among repeating earthquake families in the central San Andreas Fault, the overall prevalence of synchronized pairs decays rapidly with increasing separation, tracking their stress transfer. Among neighboring megathrust segments in the 1000‐year historical record for Japan, the same threshold identifies segments in Nankai and Hokkaido as uniquely poised for synchronization. This work offers a mechanistic basis for earthquake synchronization and, more broadly, shows how interaction shapes earthquake recurrence.

papers.t: Shallow Poroelastic Hydrothermal Deformation at Changbaishan Volcano Before the 2020 Unrest Revealed by Sentinel‐1 InSAR Time Series
in: Lab of Volcano and Earthquake Research School of Geosciences and Info‐Physics Central South University Changsha China
Department of Earth Sciences University of Geneva Geneva Switzerland
WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF Davos Switzerland
Climate Change, Extremes and Natural Hazards in Alpine Regions Research Centre CERC Davos Switzerland
tk: InSAR time series reveal shallow poroelastic hydrothermal compaction at Changbaishan volcano prior to its 2020 unrest, driven by H2O-CO2 mixture discharge.
InSAR时间序列揭示了长白山火山2020年活跃前由H2O-CO2混合物排放引起的浅部孔隙弹性热液压实。
papers.ab: Ground deformation of dormant volcanoes provides critical insights into subsurface processes and potential hazards. Here we present Sentinel‐1 Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) time series (2015–2020) for Changbaishan volcano, the largest intraplate volcanic system in East Asia. We detect persistent subsidence of up to 3.5 mm/yr on the eastern flank of the summit prior to minor unrest in December 2020. Geodetic inversion locates the deformation source within a shallow hydrothermal system 2.7 ± 0.3 km beneath the summit. Constrained by independent CO 2 ‐flux estimates, poroelastic models reproduce the observed deformation and indicate sustained discharge of an H 2 O–CO 2 mixture with vapor–liquid separation occurring above the hydrothermal system. We infer that long‐lived, mixture‐driven poroelastic compaction might have dominated the background deformation during the observed period. These findings underscore the need to integrate geodetic and geochemical observations to improve hazard assessments of future unrest at Changbaishan and analogous volcanic systems.

papers.t: An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0
tk: SLEvolve v1.0 reformulates viscoelastic memory in GIA modeling as an exact recursive update, achieving up to 4,000-fold speed-ups for sea-level projections.
SLEvolve v1.0将GIA模型中的粘弹性记忆重构为精确递推更新，实现了高达4000倍的海平面模拟加速。
papers.ab: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. As these models are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet simulations, glacial-cycle calculations, and large ensembles, standard pseudo-spectral 1-D solvers face a steep computational barrier: they evaluate the viscoelastic response by explicitly re-summing every past load increment, scaling quadratically with time steps as $O(N^2)$. Here we show that this computational penalty is an artifact of algorithmic formulation rather than Earth physics. By exploiting the exponential form of the viscoelastic relaxation kernel, we reformulate the viscous response as an exact recursive update of a finite set of modal states, without re-summing the load history. This exact reformulation alone reduces the cost of a run to $O(N)$, yielding a 20.6-fold speed-up relative to a standard full-history 1-D GIA solver for a case study involving a 550-step Antarctic future sea-level projection. Implemented in our open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0, this formulation---combined with fewer, table-free and multithreaded spherical-harmonic transforms, improved file handling, and physics-inspired iteration starts---achieves an end-to-end speed-up of over three orders of magnitude (up to 4,000-fold) against the same 1-D GIA solver, reducing day-long simulations to under thirty seconds on a workstation. Beyond this solid-Earth application, SLEvolve illustrates how human-derived analytical reformulations can be combined with benchmark-harnessed AI-assisted engineering to modernize scientific software. In particular, Numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided the AI agents' implementation choices and helped reject ineffective optimizations.

papers.t: In Situ Observation of Pressure‐Enhanced Hydrous–Anhydrous Solid Solution in Lower‐Mantle SiO 2 –AlOOH Phases
in: Department of Earth and Space Science Osaka University Toyonaka Japan
Geodynamics Research Center, PIAS Ehime University Matsuyama Japan
Japan Synchrotron Radiation Research Institute Sayo‐gun Japan
tk: In situ high-pressure experiments show that SiO2 and δ-AlOOH form extensive CaCl2-type solid solutions, enhancing water storage capacity in the lower mantle.
原位高压实验表明SiO2与δ-AlOOH形成广泛的固溶体，增强了下地幔的储水能力。
papers.ab: Water plays a critical role in Earth's mantle dynamics and evolution, yet lower‐mantle storage mechanisms remain debated. δ‐AlOOH and SiO 2 phases have been independently proposed as high‐pressure water hosts. Here, we conducted in situ synchrotron X‐ray diffraction experiments with a multi‐anvil apparatus and sintered diamond anvils to investigate phase relations in the SiO 2 –AlOOH system up to 45 GPa and high temperatures. We found that SiO 2 and δ‐AlOOH form extensive, stable CaCl 2 ‐type solid solutions across a broad compositional range under lower‐mantle conditions. The solid‐solution extent increases strongly with pressure, indicating enhanced H 2 O storage in dense SiO 2 ‐rich phases and stabilization of SiO 2 ‐enriched AlOOH‐rich hydrous phases at greater depths. These results suggest that water released from less favorable peridotitic hosts during lower‐mantle transport can be redistributed into subducted crustal lithologies, where pressure‐stabilized complementary CaCl 2 ‐type phases serve as water hosts.

papers.t: Tracing Mantle Upwellings Beneath Changbaishan/Mount Paektu: New Insights From Transition Zone Discontinuity Structure
in: State Key Laboratory of Deep Earth Exploration and Imaging College of Geoexploration Science and Technology Jilin University Changchun China
School of Natural Sciences Birkbeck, University of London London UK
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting Institute of Geology China Earthquake Administration Beijing China
Department of Earth Sciences University College London London UK
tk: Receiver function imaging beneath Changbaishan reveals depressed transition zone discontinuities, suggesting mantle dehydration and localized upwelling through a slab gap drive intraplate volcanism.
接收函数成像显示长白山下方过渡带不连续面下凹，表明地幔脱水与板片空隙处的局部上涌驱动了板内火山活动。
papers.ab: Intraplate volcanism in Northeast Asia, located in a distant back‐arc setting, challenges conventional models of mantle convection and volatile cycling. Using receiver function data from over 300 broadband stations, we image the mantle transition zone (MTZ) beneath the Changbaishan/Paektu volcano. Our results show a modest 410‐km depression consistent with melt accumulation caused by slab dehydration and/or a hydrous MTZ, and a depressed 660‐km discontinuity linked to slab stagnation. Notably, lateral variations in the morphology of negative phases above the 410‐km discontinuity may reflect localized variations in upwelling rate and are associated with lateral heterogeneity of the underlying slab and localized uplift of the 660‐km discontinuity, suggesting focused upwelling through a potential slab lens/gap. These observations suggest that MTZ dehydration primarily drives regional intraplate magmatism, with potential lower‐mantle return flow locally enhancing this process, highlighting the critical role of the MTZ in controlling volatile transfer in deep subduction systems.

papers.t: Transform-to-thrust reactivation of a fossil back-arc spreading system: Evidence from marine magnetic anomalies in the East Sea (Japan Sea)
in: Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology
Pusan National University
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
Université Paris Cité
tk: Marine magnetic anomalies reveal that the Ulleung Basin's fossil transform boundary is reactivating as the modern Ulleung Major Thrust under compression.
海洋磁异常表明郁陵盆地的古转换边界正受压活化为现代冲断带。
papers.ab: Transform faults contain rheological weaknesses that can be reactivated into either divergent or convergent boundaries, depending on tectonic stress regime. While rifting triggered from transform fault is well documented, geophysical evidence demonstrating compressional reactivation of fossil transform boundaries, and the lithospheric controls that govern it remains poorly understood. The East Sea (Japan Sea), a back-arc system at the junction of the Eurasian, Pacific, North American, and Philippine Sea plates, offers an ideal setting to understand this process. However, the tectonic origin and opening history of its southeastern part, the Ulleung Basin, have remained controversial due to thick sedimentary cover and previously ambiguous magnetic signatures. Here we show that the Ulleung Basin underwent seafloor spreading between 20–17 Ma, and that its paleo-transform boundary is currently reactivating into a thrust system. Using a newly compiled high-resolution marine magnetic anomaly map and two-dimensional forward modeling, we identify coherent ENE-WSW trending magnetic lineations (Chron C6An.1n–C5Dn), indicating a past half-spreading rate of 20 km/Myr. Furthermore, we identify the western margin of the basin as the East Korean Fracture Zone, a fossil transform boundary that spatially coincides with the modern Ulleung Major Thrust indicating that the rheological weakness of this transform fault has facilitated its compressional inversion under E-W tectonic stress regime. These results provide a kinematic framework linking the back-arc opening of the East Sea to its Late Cenozoic inversion, and document a rare example of transform-to-thrust reactivation in a continental back-arc setting.

papers.t: Early warnings of earthquakes
tk: A comprehensive overview of the methodologies, challenges, and future prospects of earthquake early warning systems.
对地震预警系统的关键方法、面临挑战及未来前景的系统性综述。
papers.ab: Earthquakes are among the most destructive natural hazards. As populations in seismically active regions grow, the need for effective risk mitigation strategies is more urgent than ever. In that regard, earthquake early warning systems are a key component to reduce the impact of seismic shaking.

papers.t: Bayesian Geophysical Inversion using Stein Mixture Variational Inference for Multimodal or Complex Solutions
tk: Introduces Stein Mixture Variational Inference (SMVI) to efficiently resolve complex, multimodal posterior probability density functions in Bayesian geophysical inversion.
引入斯坦混合变分推断（SMVI）方法，高效解决贝叶斯地球物理反演中的多峰或复杂后验不确定性问题。
papers.ab: Bayesian geophysical inversion provides a probabilistic framework to estimate subsurface properties, in which uncertainties are represented by a so-called posterior probability density function (pdf). Estimating this pdf is computationally challenging when it is high dimensional or complex, particularly if it may be multimodal. We introduce Stein mixture variational inference (SMVI) for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion with multimodal or complex posterior solutions. The method combines parametric variational inference with Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD). In SMVI, the posterior pdf is approximated by a mixture (sum) of distributions, in which component distributions are optimised jointly using the SVGD update rule. This construction combines computational efficiency with the flexibility to represent a range of plausible Earth models and allows components to be updated in parallel. Here, SMVI is first tested on two synthetic seismic inverse problems, demonstrating that SMVI can recover non-Gaussian, complex and multimodal posterior solutions accurately and efficiently. Then, we apply SMVI to real seismic data by performing Love wave tomography of the British Isles, and obtain inversion results that are consistent with previous Monte Carlo solutions. Around the East Irish Sea sedimentary basins, SMVI captures bimodal uncertainty associated with ambiguity in basin boundary locations, revealing alternative subsurface structures compatible with the observations. These results indicate that SMVI generalises various previous variational methods, and provides a practical and effective framework for quantifying complex uncertainties and supporting geological interpretation of seismic images.

papers.t: Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints
tk: A physics-informed neural operator quantifies the scale-dependent limits of recovering Greenland ice loss from sea level fingerprints.
利用物理信息神经算子量化了从海平面指纹恢复格陵兰冰盖流失的尺度相关极限。
papers.ab: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.

papers.t: An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0
in: Harvard University
tk: SLEvolve v1.0 reformulates viscoelastic GIA modeling using an exact recursive update of modal states, reducing complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) and accelerating simulations up to 4,000-fold.
SLEvolve v1.0通过模态状态的精确递归更新重构了粘弹性GIA建模，将复杂度降至O(N)并实现高达4000倍的加速。
papers.ab: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. As these models are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet simulations, glacial-cycle calculations, and large ensembles, standard pseudo-spectral 1-D solvers face a steep computational barrier: they evaluate the viscoelastic response by explicitly re-summing every past load increment, scaling quadratically with time steps as $O(N^2)$. Here we show that this computational penalty is an artifact of algorithmic formulation rather than Earth physics. By exploiting the exponential form of the viscoelastic relaxation kernel, we reformulate the viscous response as an exact recursive update of a finite set of modal states, without re-summing the load history. This exact reformulation alone reduces the cost of a run to $O(N)$, yielding a 20.6-fold speed-up relative to a standard full-history 1-D GIA solver for a case study involving a 550-step Antarctic future sea-level projection. Implemented in our open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0, this formulation---combined with fewer, table-free and multithreaded spherical-harmonic transforms, improved file handling, and physics-inspired iteration starts---achieves an end-to-end speed-up of over three orders of magnitude (up to 4,000-fold) against the same 1-D GIA solver, reducing day-long simulations to under thirty seconds on a workstation. Beyond this solid-Earth application, SLEvolve illustrates how human-derived analytical reformulations can be combined with benchmark-harnessed AI-assisted engineering to modernize scientific software. In particular, Numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided the AI agents' implementation choices and helped reject ineffective optimizations.

papers.t: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

University of Chicago
Tulane University
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
Columbia University
