papers.t: State of Stress in Subduction Zone Forearcs: Influence of the Mantle Wedge Corner and Serpentinization
in: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences University of Minnesota Twin Cities Minneapolis MN USA
tk: This study investigates how the mantle wedge corner and serpentinization influence the state of stress in subduction zone forearcs.
本研究探讨了地幔楔角和蛇纹石化如何影响俯冲带前弧的应力状态。
papers.ab: We investigate the role of the elasticity and density of the forearc mantle wedge corner on the stress distribution in the forearc region of subduction zones, using numerical quasi‐2D lithospheric deformation models for the Cascadia, Nankai, NE Japan, and Costa Rica subduction zones. We incorporate the forearc mantle wedge corner as an elastic domain within the overriding lithosphere with physical properties that reflect reported degrees of serpentinization. In the models, we also incorporate reported values of effective friction coefficient ( μ ) and the downdip extent of frictional coupling (DoC) for the four subduction systems. Our models predict horizontal deviatoric tension in the wedge and the overriding crust in Cascadia and Nankai due to the buoyancy and elasticity of the wedge corner and relatively low DoC and μ . In NE Japan and Costa Rica, the plate coupling force dominates over the effect of the mantle wedge corner, resulting in horizontal deviatoric compression.

papers.t: Volatile Conduits Beneath Vulcano Island (Italy) Revealed by High‐Resolution Nodal Local Earthquake Tomography During Volcanic Unrest
in: Department of Earth Sciences University of Geneva Geneva Switzerland
Instituto Volcanológico de Canarias (INVOLCAN) Puerto de la Cruz Spain
Invert SA Echichens Switzerland
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Sezione Roma 1 Rome Italy
tk: High-resolution local earthquake tomography using a dense nodal network reveals fluid- and gas-dominated conduits and reservoirs beneath Vulcano Island during its 2021 unrest.
节点地震断层扫描揭示了火山岛活跃期的流体与气体通道。
papers.ab: Understanding shallow magmatic and hydrothermal systems at active volcanoes is essential for interpreting unrest and forecasting eruptions. We present the first high‐resolution three‐dimensional , , and models of Vulcano Island, Aeolian Islands, Italy, derived from a dense nodal seismic network. During 1 month of acquisition in 2021, coinciding with volcanic unrest, we detected and picked 1749 local earthquakes. Tomographic results reveal pronounced velocity anomalies, including high Vp / Vs ratios beneath Lipari and Vulcano, compatible with fluid‐rich zones, and low Vp / Vs anomalies compatible with gas‐ or vapor‐dominated reservoirs within the shallow magmatic–hydrothermal system. A deeper low anomaly coincides with hypocentral depths of very‐long‐period seismic events, suggesting a genetic relationship between fluid accumulation, pressure buildup, and very‐long period seismicity. These results significantly improve travel‐time tomography resolution and provide new insights into the geometry, fluid distribution, and structural controls of Vulcano's upper plumbing system, with important implications for volcanic monitoring and planning strategies.

papers.t: Seasonal variation of earthquake source characteristics of the long-duration Palghar swarm, western India
in: National Geophysical Research Institute
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research
tk: This study investigates the seasonal variations in earthquake source parameters of the long-duration Palghar swarm in western India, highlighting the role of monsoon-induced fluid recharge.
该研究探讨了印度帕尔加尔地震群震源特征的季节性变化及流体作用。
papers.ab: A swarm sequence initiated in November 2018 in the Palghar region near the western coast of India, and continued with high intensity for two years. About 8300 earthquakes were found with horizontal and depth uncertainties of ≤1.5 km after relocation. The earthquakes were distributed along two narrow N-S oriented clusters, separated by ~5 km. We performed time-domain regional waveform full moment tensor inversion to compute focal mechanisms of the 33 M L ≥ 3.5 earthquakes, followed by stress inversion. Source parameters for 28 of these events were estimated from frequency spectra analysis. The focal mechanisms indicate dominant normal faulting along steeply dipping, N-S-oriented nodal planes, with high non-DC components (~42%). Stress inversion also reveals a normal-faulting regime, in contrast to the regional India-Eurasia compressive stress regime. The Palghar swarm has been previously linked to rainfall, and our results also show contrasting earthquake source properties during the post-monsoon period, when cumulative rainfall is highest, compared to summer. During the post-monsoon period, the strikes are strictly N-S, slips are ~−100°, and a pure normal-faulting regime is observed, accompanied by increased non-DC components and reduced static stress drops. In contrast, during the summer season, oblique-normal faulting occurs along NNE-SSW-oriented planes, with slip angles reduced to about −65°. We infer that pure normal faulting induced by vertical rainwater load during the post-monsoon transitions to a combination of regional convergent stress regime and vertical loading due to remnant water during summer, resulting in oblique normal faulting. This interplay possibly sustains the rain-induced swarm.

papers.t: Onset of Thrusting at ca. 23 Ma in East Kunlun Mountains, Northern Tibet, Recorded by Syntectonic Strata
in: State Key Laboratory of Loess Science Institute of Earth Environment Chinese Academy of Sciences Xi'an China
Xi'an Institute for Innovative Earth Environment Research Xi'an China
Faculty of Ocean Science and Technology Kobe University Kobe Japan
tk: Magnetostratigraphic dating of growth strata in the East Kunlun Mountains constrains the onset of major thrusting to ca. 23 Ma, linked to lower crustal flow.
东昆仑山生长地层古地磁定年表明冲断作用始于约23 Ma，与下地壳流有关。
papers.ab: The timing of Cenozoic deformation in the East Kunlun Mountains, northern Tibet, is crucial for understanding plateau growth but remains disputed due to the scarcity of direct chronological constraints on specific tectonic structures. Here, we present a high‐density‐sampling magnetostratigraphic record from the Xiaohongshan section, interior of the East Kunlun Mountains, where growth strata directly constrain syndepositional thrust activity. Correlation with the geomagnetic polarity timescale, supported by ostracod biostratigraphy, dates the section to 25.7–17.5 Ma and places the onset of growth strata at ca. 23 Ma, marking the initiation of major thrust faulting. We propose that this thrust deformation was triggered by the northward flow of weakened lower crustal material from the Hoh Xil Basin, which was obstructed by the rigid lithospheric keel of the Qaidam Basin, leading to upper crustal shortening and surface uplift. Our results provide a direct temporal link between deep lithospheric processes and surface tectonics in northern Tibet.

papers.t: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
in: Isotope Laboratory, Department of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Washington, Seattle, WA 98195, USA.
Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA 02138, USA.
Department of Earth and Environmental Science, Rice University, Houston, TX 77005, USA.
tk: Mg isotope signatures in arc magmas reveal that up to 50% of their Mg budget originates from deep, water-saturated melting at the base of the mantle wedge.
弧岩浆的镁同位素特征表明，其多达50%的镁源自地幔楔底部的深部饱水熔融。
papers.ab: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

papers.t: Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment based on submarine active faults and their possible interactions in the sea of Japan
in: Tohoku University
National Chung Hsing University
International Research Institute of Disaster Science, Tohoku University
Chulalongkorn University
tk: This study evaluates probabilistic tsunami risks for a coastal power plant, highlighting the significant impact of coupled submarine active faults.
本研究评估了日本海沿岸电厂的海啸风险，强调了耦合断层的影响。
papers.ab: The Sea of Japan coastal areas have experienced tsunami damage caused by submarine active seismic faults. Large uncertainties remain regarding seismic activity of these faults and the following tsunami. Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment (PTRA) enables the evaluation of tsunami risk accounting for such uncertainties. In this study, the tsunami risks of a thermal power plant located in Joetsu on the Sea of Japan coast were evaluated using PTRA based on submarine active faults, including coupled faults, across the Sea of Japan. The results indicate that coupled fault models had large impacts on risk levels, especially for severe damage states. For the most severe damage state, the median expected annual probability of experiencing this damage state among the structures increased by 154% when coupled fault models were considered. In addition, the risk levels varied depending on the structures, even within the same site. The spatial distribution of tsunami risk revealed that structures with high risk levels existed not only along the coast but also inland. The findings of this study provide practical insights into reliable tsunami risk assessment, which are useful for the development of disaster resilience measures, especially for infrastructure.

papers.t: An Innovative Approach for Estimating Coseismic Surface Uplifts Using Ionospheric Observations From Remote GNSS Stations: First Application for the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake
in: Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (DST) Navi Mumbai India
CSIR‐National Geophysical Research Institute Hyderabad India
AcSIR‐Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research Ghaziabad India
Hokkaido University Sapporo Japan
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
Wadia Institute Himalayan Geol. Dehradun India
Survey of India Dehradun India
tk: This study presents a novel method to estimate coseismic surface uplifts using remote GNSS ionospheric observations, applied to the 2025 Myanmar earthquake.
利用远程GNSS电离层观测估计同震地表隆起的新方法。
papers.ab: The M w 7.7 Myanmar earthquake on 28 March 2025 ruptured ∼480 km of the Sagaing Fault. Its fault slip distribution remains poorly constrained by three‐dimensional surface displacement data due to sparse GNSS‐coverage near the fault. Satellite‐based synthetic aperture radars capture meters of right‐lateral displacements but isolating vertical crustal movements from these measurements is challenging. We present a new way to map vertical displacements distributed along the fault using ionospheric total electron contents (TEC) variability measured by GNSS stations located >300 km away from the epicenter along the India‐Myanmar border. We identified three distinct peaks in the TEC time‐series. The arrival times and amplitudes of these peaks are used to determine the positions and relative strengths of three acoustic wave sources. These results are compared with slip distribution inferred from seismological observations. The study demonstrates the capability of this innovative‐approach to constrain coseismic uplifts indirectly using ionospheric data at remote GNSS stations.

papers.t: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
tk: InSight seismic event S0976a is identified as a deep crustal strike-slip marsquake in Valles Marineris, demonstrating ancient fault reactivation under contemporary planetary stresses.
InSight探测到的S0976a地震是发生在水手号峡谷的深部地壳走滑型火星震，证实了古老断裂的活动性。
papers.ab: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

papers.t: Bayesian Geophysical Inversion using Stein Mixture Variational Inference for Multimodal or Complex Solutions
in: University of Edinburgh
tk: Stein mixture variational inference (SMVI) is introduced to efficiently resolve complex, multimodal posterior probability distributions in Bayesian geophysical inversion, demonstrated on Love wave tomography.

papers.t: Active hazardous slow faults drive drainage evolution in the Atacama Desert
tk: Extremely slow-slip faults in the hyperarid Atacama Desert drive drainage reorganization and represent an underestimated seismic hazard capable of generating M6.1–6.8 earthquakes.
阿塔卡马极慢断层重塑水系演化，具M6.1-6.8级地震危险。
papers.ab: The Atacama Desert of the Central Andean forearc is the driest non-polar region on Earth, where extremely low erosion rates preserve geomorphic markers over Myr timescales. Between 19°S and 20°S, subtle Quaternary east-vergent reverse faults deform the west-sloping landscape and disrupt drainage development. This setting provides a unique opportunity to investigate fault evolution, uplift thresholds for drainage reorganization, and the seismic significance of slow faulting in hyperarid landscapes. We investigated two faulted interfluves, Pampa de Tiliviche (~19.5°S) and Pampa de Soga (~19.75°S), using geomorphic mapping and cosmogenic ¹⁰Be dating of displaced alluvial surfaces, channels, and terraces. We constrained fault geometry, reconstructed fault-driven incision histories, and quantified uplift and slip rates. Faulting in interfluves started after ~2.6 and ~5 Ma, while warped terraces and riverbeds record accelerated faulting since ~330 and ~35 ka, respectively. Simplified fault geometries yield maximum long- and short-term uplift/slip rates of ~0.011 and ~0.3 mm/yr. Numerical landscape-evolution models incorporating measured rates reproduce observed geomorphic patterns and constrain the uplift rate-catchment area ratio governing drainage reorganization. Observations and modelling indicate that tectonic uplift outpaces fluvial incision in hyperarid landscapes when drainage networks with small catchment areas cannot restore channel-bed slope modified by slow uplift. Regional consistency in fault geometry, distribution, and associated microseismicity suggests these counter-slope faults form an active forearc system capable of generating M6.1–6.8 earthquakes. Our results show that extremely slow faulting can substantially reorganize drainages in hyperarid landscapes and that Quaternary faults commonly considered inactive may represent an underestimated seismic hazard.

papers.t: Inherited lithospheric weakness enabled rapid stress transmission across Tibet
in: Tianjin University
University of Bologna
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
Chinese Academy of Sciences
Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences
tk: K-Ar dating of the Altyn Tagh Fault reveals that inherited lithospheric weaknesses enabled rapid, long-distance stress transmission across Tibet during the India-Asia collision.
阿尔金断裂带的K-Ar定年表明，继承性岩石圈软弱带促进了印度-亚洲碰撞过程中应力的快速远距离传递。
papers.ab: The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict. K–Ar dating reveals >110 Myr of episodic Altyn Tagh Fault activity, beginning at ~115 Ma along a Cretaceous lithospheric weakness. Reactivation at ~56 Ma records rapid India–Asia collisional stress transmission >1500 km into the continental interior.

papers.t: Nascent Alaskan-Aleutians slab gap formed after late Miocene subduction of the extinct Kula-Pacific spreading ridge
in: University of Arizona, Unknown, Tucson, United States [US]
The University of Arizona, Unknown, Tucson, United States [US]
University of Colorado-Boulder, Unknown, Boulder, United States [US]
Michigan State University, Unknown, East Lansing, United States [US]
Michigan State University, Unknown, East Lansing, MI, United States [US]
Kansas State University, 108 Thompson Hall - Department of Geology, Manhattan, KS, United States [US]
tk: Integrates P-wave tomography and plate reconstructions to show that the Alaskan-Aleutian slab gap formed from subducting the extinct Kula-Pacific spreading ridge.
结合断层成像与板块重建，揭示阿留申板块空隙源于熄灭洋中脊的俯冲。
papers.ab: Globally, numerous modern and ancient examples of active spreading-ridge subduction ‘slab windows’ are documented, whereas definitive examples of extinct spreading-ridge subduction are lacking or controversial. Published high-resolution P-wave tomography of southwest Alaska and the eastern Aleutians reveals an unmistakable >1000 km-long slab gap, expressed as a low-velocity anomaly within the subducted Pacific slab at depths of ~200–500 km between ~158.5°W and 168°W. We unfold the Pacific slab and integrate it into a quantitative plate-reconstruction model, demonstrating that the slab gap aligns with the extinct Kula-Pacific mid-ocean ridge that became inactive at ~40 Ma. Initial subduction of the extinct Kula-Pacific ridge after ~8 Ma was concurrent with documented Aleutian Trench arc and Kodiak Island forearc exhumation at ~7–5 Ma. The nascent extinct Kula-Pacific ridge slab gap may explain uplift of the Bristol Bay and St. George basins, slab-edge magmatism at the Quaternary Hayes volcano, and intraplate mafic volcanism at the Pribilof volcanoes. The modern slab gap may partially control the limit of deep Benioff seismicity along the Alaska-Aleutian margin, including the westward-shallowing Benioff zone beneath the Aleutians. We infer that the slab gap continues another >1000 km westward into tomographically less-resolved regions beneath the central-western Aleutians and likely terminates near the remnant Kula-Pacific spreading ridge around the Near Islands, explaining the origin of a previously recognized slab “portal” in this region. Our reconstruction arguably provides the archetypal example of extinct spreading ridge subduction – a separate class of ridge-trench intersection that is distinct from active ridge subduction.

papers.t: Rupture Process and Seismogenic Mechanism of the 2023 Mw 6.0 Jishishan Earthquake: Insights from Joint Inversion of InSAR, GNSS, and Tele-Waveforms
in: School of Land Resource Engineering, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming, China
College of Geoscience and Surveying Engineering, China University of Mining and Technology-Beijing, Beijing, China
tk: Joint inversion of geodetic and seismic data reveals the 2023 Jishishan earthquake was a thrust-dominated rupture on the Lajishan fault system.
联合大地测量与远震波形揭示积石山地震逆冲破裂特征。
papers.ab: On 18 December 2023, an Mw 6.0 earthquake struck Jishishan County, Gansu Province, China, rupturing a segment of the Lajishan fault system along the northeastern margin of the Tibetan plateau. To characterize the seismogenic fault geometry and the spatiotemporal evolution of the rupture, we developed a joint inversion framework that integrates Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) coseismic displacements, and far-field seismic waveforms. The fault geometry was constrained through a nonlinear inversion based on coseismic InSAR deformation. Using the optimal fault geometry, we performed a kinematic finite-fault inversion that jointly incorporates InSAR line-of-sight displacements, static GNSS offsets, and seismic waveforms to resolve the rupture process. Our results show that the rupture was mainly concentrated at depths of 5–12 km, with a maximum slip of ∼30 cm. The estimated seismic moment is 1.0×1018 N·m, corresponding to Mw 5.94. The total rupture duration is ∼20 s. Regional interseismic GNSS velocities and strain-rate fields indicate that the event occurred within a compressional tectonic regime and was dominated by thrust faulting with a minor strike-slip component, providing insights into tectonic loading and seismogenesis within the Lajishan fault system. Coulomb stress calculations further suggest that stress transfer from the mainshock may have contributed to the subsequent aftershock activity. Our results provide constraints on the rupture behavior and tectonic loading of the Lajishan fault system and improve our understanding of seismogenesis along the northeastern margin of the Tibetan plateau, with implications for regional seismic hazard assessment.

papers.t: Thermo-viscous feedback in heat transport through fracture-matrix systems with finite thermal capacity
tk: A reduced semi-analytical model describes thermo-viscous feedback in geothermal fracture-matrix systems with finite thermal capacity.
提出描述有限热容裂隙-基质系统热粘性反馈的半解析模型。
papers.ab: In geothermal systems, injected fluid flows along preferential fracture pathways and exchanges heat with matrix blocks. Reduced models often neglect temperature-dependent viscosity and assume unlimited matrix storage, although the thermal capacity accessible to the flow is finite. This work analyzes thermo-viscous feedback in a planar fracture-matrix system where viscosity controls discharge through the integrated hydraulic resistance, while finite capacity enters through an effective single-timescale memory fixed by initial uptake and total capacity. The reduced model gives parsimonious semi-analytical predictions with physically based parameters, verified against the nonlinear solution. A perturbation hierarchy separates matrix storage from the hydraulic response it induces, while an exponential velocity reconstruction preserves the exact terminal discharge and bounds front-moment errors within the front-moment limit model. At fixed pressure difference, heating accelerates and broadens the front, whereas cooling delays and sharpens it. The terminal discharge depends only on the endpoint viscosity ratio, while matrix uptake, storage and contrast determine its approach time. At fixed rate, viscosity alters only the pressure drop, not the thermal response. Finite thickness controls the transition to capacity-limited equilibration, and strong matrix uptake collapses the isoviscous response onto a two-variable similarity surface.

papers.t: Shallow seismic damage and structural inheritance at the onset of faulting
tk: Analysis of an immature fault in the Bedretto Underground Laboratory reveals how pre-existing mylonitic anisotropy confines seismic damage and guides early-stage fault propagation.
地下实验室研究揭示了预存结构各向异性对早期断层地震损伤的控制作用。
papers.ab: Faults accommodate shear motion in the upper crust through brittle deformation like fracturing and cataclastic flow. The width of the embrittlement, the lateral extent of the fault, and the grain size distribution within the fault core seem to scale with shear displacement, though scaling laws have large uncertainties. Inherited structures may drive strain partitioning, restrict damage extension, and either favour or hinder seismic slip propagation. It is difficult to explore these features in natural faults since delicate structures such as crackle breccias and gouges are reworked during exhumation, overprinted during multiple deformation cycles, and altered by surface weathering. The Bedretto Underground Laboratory represents a unique chance to study the structure of immature faults at depth, whose pristine structures are hardly preserved elsewhere in the field. The exceptional exposure allowed for a detailed analysis of a fault zone named Waterfault, which exploited the pre-existing fabrics of a mylonitic shear zone in the Rotondo granite. The limited extension of the damage zone and the scarce presence of cataclastic products indicates that the fault's activity was short-lived, possibly stemming from a single slip event. The presence of pulverised rocks, restricted to the hanging-wall side, suggests that faulting was produced during the propagation of a low magnitude earthquake. The pre-existing mylonitic fabrics provided a strong mechanical anisotropy, which confined the damage zone and favoured the lateral extension of the fault. We argue that the WF structures illustrate the onset of faulting along pre-existing anisotropies, revealing their role in the partitioning of energy and strain.

papers.t: Dataset and Results for: Spatiotemporal evolution of shallow seismic velocities associated with the 2024 East Rift Zone eruption at Kīlauea Volcano
tk: This dataset provides spatiotemporal seismic velocity changes at Kīlauea Volcano before the September 2024 eruption, derived from ambient noise interferometry using nodal and permanent networks.
基拉韦厄火山2024年喷发前的背景噪声时空速度变化数据集。
papers.ab: This dataset contains seismic velocity change estimates derived from ambient noise interferometry for Kīlauea volcano, Hawaii, during the period of volcanic unrest preceding the September 2024 East Rift Zone eruption near Nāpau Crater. The data were computed using continuous vertical seismic recordings from a dense temporary nodal array and the permanent network of the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory. Relative seismic velocity changes were estimated from ambient noise cross-correlations and subsequently inverted to obtain spatially distributed velocity change fields through time. The dataset includes time series of relative seismic velocity changes, spatial inversion results, and associated metadata describing station pairs, processing parameters, and inversion settings. The velocity change fields resolve spatial and temporal variations associated with magma transport, dike intrusions, and deformation processes at the summit and in the East Rift Zone of Kīlauea. These data support the analysis presented in "Spatiotemporal evolution of shallow seismic velocities associated with the 2024 East Rift Zone eruption at Kīlauea Volcano" (A. Rohnacher, N. Bennington, M. Bagnardi, S. Wiemer, F. Lanza).

papers.t: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP): Towards standardisation of global glacier projections
tk: GlacierMIP4 establishes a standardised experimental protocol for global glacier evolution models to improve projection comparability up to the year 2300.
GlacierMIP4为全球冰川演化模型制定了标准化实验方案，以提高至2300年投影的可比性。
papers.ab: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP) provides an international framework for the coordinated evaluation and comparison of global glacier evolution models and their projections of glacier change. Its fourth phase, GlacierMIP4, updates previous global glacier projections through a standardised experimental design. For the first time, the protocol includes simulations extending to 2300 and an overshoot scenario for a subset of climate projections and requires monthly output of individual mass-balance components such as melt, accumulation and refreezing, in addition to annual results for glacier mass and area. While permitting model-specific approaches to calibration and other aspects of model implementation, the protocol prescribes common atmospheric forcing data, inventory boundary conditions, and reporting conventions to enable consistent analyses of inter-model differences. Here, we describe the GlacierMIP4 experimental protocol, including the simulation domain, initialisation, atmospheric forcing, and standardised output requirements. More broadly, we emphasize the need for standardised terminology, units, sign convention and file formats in global glacier modelling to improve the traceability, interoperability, and comparability of results, and recommend this protocol as a blueprint for future global glacier modelling studies.

papers.t: Comment on egusphere-2026-1415
in: Scuola Superiore Meridionale
University of Naples Federico II
University of Bari Aldo Moro
tk: An Exponentially Modified Gaussian distribution models volcanic eruption size uncertainty, showing that observed volume distributions are compatible with an underlying power-law.
采用指数修饰高斯分布模型考虑喷发量不确定性，证实其实际分布符合幂律规律。
papers.ab: Forecasting the size of a future volcanic eruption in densely populated areas is a key aspect of volcanic hazard and risk assessment. Estimates of the next eruption's size for both long- and short-term forecasts are typically based on the sizes of past events. Using the erupted volume as a proxy for eruptive size, forecasts are often obtained from the sampling of a power-law distribution. Notwithstanding, the distribution of the measured/inferred erupted volume of past eruptions often appears markedly different from a power-law. Here, we consider how the uncertainty on the volume of past eruptions may affect the shape of a hypothetical power-law distribution. The goal is to understand if the distribution of real data is compatible with an Exponentially Modified Gaussian distribution (EMG) that includes both the power-law and the uncertainty on the observed volumes. We apply this method to two large high-risk calderas, Campi Flegrei, Italy, and Taupo, New Zealand, but it can be potentially applied to any volcano. We find that the EMG distribution provides a good statistical fit to both volcanoes' eruptive records, supporting the use of a power-law distribution for forecasting the volume of the next eruption.

papers.t: Shift and Increase in Tidal Modulation of Seismicity in the Ridgecrest Fault Zone Before and After the 2019 Magnitude 7.1 Earthquake
in: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University, Palisades, New York, U.S.A.
Dipartimento di Geoscienze, Università di Padova, Padova, Italy
Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts, U.S.A.
tk: Seismicity in the Ridgecrest fault zone shifted from stress-controlled to stress-rate-controlled tidal modulation and increased in strength prior to the 2019 Mw 7.1 earthquake.
Ridgecrest断层地震在2019年大震前转为应力率控制且调制增强。
papers.ab: We studied the tidal modulation of the rate of seismicity in the Ridgecrest, California area between 2008 and 2024, thus including the 2019 Mw 7.1 earthquake. We combined machine-learning-enhanced earthquake detection and location with a novel methodology to characterize tidal modulation. We identified significant modulation of seismicity in the Ridgecrest fault zone and in the neighboring regions, the Coso volcanic field and the Garlock fault, but tidal modulation in the fault zone exhibits a unique temporal evolution. Modulation in the fault zone shifts, around 2014–2015, from a stress-controlled regime where peak seismicity occurs at peak tidal stress to a stress-rate-controlled regime where peak seismicity occurs at peak tidal stress rate. In contrast, peak seismicity in Coso and along the Garlock fault consistently occurs at peak tidal stress throughout time. Moreover, the strength of tidal modulation in the fault zone increases before the 2019 Mw 7.1 earthquake, unlike in its surroundings. A possible interpretation based on experimental and theoretical work suggests that some characteristic frictional time scale (the nucleation time or the critical period of the fault) becomes shorter than the dominant tidal period after 2015. This change implies that the fault loading rate increases, which may be accompanied by a decrease in effective normal stress. Reduced effective stress, fault zone resonance, or increased mechanical compliance could cause the increase in modulation strength. We propose that these changes manifest a preparation phase before a large earthquake.

papers.t: Local Distance Seismic Source Discrimination in the United Kingdom Using P/S Amplitude Ratios and Machine Learning
in: AWE Blacknest, Reading, United Kingdom
British Geological Survey, Earthquake Seismology, The Lyell Centre, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
tk: High-frequency network-averaged P/S ratios combined with machine learning effectively discriminate small-magnitude earthquakes, explosions, and mining-induced events at local distances in the UK.
结合高频台网平均P/S比与机器学习，可有效识别英国近距离小震级地震、爆炸及矿震。
papers.ab: Seismic source discriminants comparing earthquakes and explosions have been validated for large-magnitude events (local magnitude, ML>3.5) detected at regional and greater distances (>350 km). However, there is less evidence that existing seismic source discriminants apply to small-magnitude seismic events (ML≤3.5), which are predominantly detected at local distances (≤350 km). In this study, we investigate the performance of a P/S amplitude ratio discriminant for 210 small-magnitude seismic events in the United Kingdom (UK). High-frequency (> 8 Hz) network-averaged P/S ratios can discriminate between earthquakes and explosions, whereas low frequencies (2–4 Hz) can separate offshore explosions and quarry blasts. We derive a path and site amplitude correction model that reduces P/S ratio distribution variability, but using discrimination metrics we show that simple across-network averaging is the most important step to allow effective discrimination. We also applied a machine learning classification model, previously trained to discriminate earthquakes and explosions in France, to our dataset. The model demonstrates high classification accuracy, likely due to similarities between geology and seismic sources in France and the UK. When the predictions from the convolutional neural network are combined with high-frequency P/S ratios, we are able to distinguish other seismic sources, such as longwall mining-induced earthquakes. These results suggest that P/S ratios can be considered a useful seismic source discriminant at local distances across the UK, and network-averaging sufficiently accounts for non-source factors.

papers.t: DiffSpecMatch: Differentiable Waveform Inverse Design with Configurable Optimization Modules for Response-Spectrum Matching of Ground Motions
tk: DiffSpecMatch uses differentiable SDOF dynamics and configurable optimization to match ground-motion response spectra while preserving engineering-relevant waveform characteristics.
DiffSpecMatch利用可微单自由度动力学和可配置优化模块，实现了满足工程约束的地震动反应谱拟合。
papers.ab: Response-spectrum matching is an underdetermined waveform inverse problem in which spectral compatibility must be achieved without uncontrolled changes in other engineering-relevant ground-motion characteristics. This study formulates the problem as differentiable waveform inverse design using a fixed SDOF dynamics engine and configurable optimization modules. An envelope-guided parameterization defines the correction waveform, while a hard projection enforces zero correction-induced terminal velocity and displacement. Differentiable SDOF responses then provide gradients for waveform optimization. Spectral fidelity and Arias-intensity accumulation are treated as adaptive objectives. Spectral feasibility, PGA, total Arias intensity, and displacement-path requirements are incorporated as constraints. The differentiable spectrum operator agrees with an exact solution of the equation of motion to within 0.002%. The complete five-damping configuration achieves a maximum spectral error of 5.00% over 375 ordinates. On a common benchmark, maximum errors of 2.61% and 8.47% are obtained for single- and multi-damping matching, respectively, while retaining the additional waveform constraints. Three-component applications further show that different engineering acceptance requirements can be accommodated through module reconfiguration without changing the forward dynamics.

papers.t: Surface mass removal can induce extremely shallow earthquakes despite nominally stable friction: the case of the 2019 Mw 4.9 Le Teil, France, earthquake.
tk: Surface mass removal from quarrying can induce extremely shallow, destructive earthquakes like the 2019 Mw 4.9 Le Teil event, even on faults with nominally stable friction.
采石场地表质量移除可在名义上稳定的摩擦条件下诱发极浅层地震。
papers.ab: # Repository Overview This repository contains the aerial imagery and digital elevation data used to estimate surface mass removal, together with figure-generation scripts and processed numerical simulation data associated with the manuscript: *Surface mass removal can induce extremely shallow earthquakes despite nominally stable friction: the case of the 2019 Mw 4.9 Le Teil, France, earthquake.* The repository is organized into two compressed archives: 1. `aerial.tar.gz` — aerial imagery and digital terrain data used to estimate surface mass removal.2. `archive_FIGURES.tar.xz` — plotting scripts, processed simulation data, and auxiliary files required to reproduce the figures presented in the manuscript. ## 1. Aerial Imagery and Digital Elevation Data: `aerial.tar.gz` This archive contains two subdirectories: ### 1.1. `etat_major/` This directory contains historical maps from the SCAN État-major® 40K product. The product is generated by georeferencing and tiling scanned État-major maps at a scale of 1:40,000. The original maps were drawn in the nineteenth century, based on surveys conducted between 1825 and 1866. They were subsequently supplemented by partial updates, including the addition of railway lines, through 1889. These historical maps provide information on the landscape before modern surface modifications and are used in the analysis of surface mass removal. ### 1.2. `LIDAR/` This directory contains digital terrain model (DTM) data derived from the classified point clouds acquired through the French national high-definition LiDAR (HD LiDAR) program. The point-cloud acquisition density is at least 10 laser pulses per square meter, decreasing to 5 pulses per square meter at altitudes above 3,200 m. The DTM is derived from points classified as ground, water, and virtual points in the HD LiDAR point cloud. These data provide information on the modern terrain and support the estimation of surface mass removal. ## 2. Figure Scripts and Processed Simulation Data: `archive_FIGURES.tar.xz` This archive contains the scripts and processed data needed to reproduce the figures presented in the manuscript. The numerical simulations were performed using BEM2D, an open-source two-dimensional boundary element method code. The BEM2D source code is maintained separately and is available from its official GitHub repository: https://github.com/esopaci/BEM_2D.git Examples and instructions for running simulations of the type used in this study are available in the `examples/QUARRY_LOADING/` directory of the BEM2D repository. ### 2.1. Repository Structure The archive is organized into one directory for each manuscript figure: - `Figure01/`- `Figure02/`- `Figure03/`- `Figure04/`- `Figure05/`- `Figure06/`- `Figure07/`- `Figure08/`- `Figure09/` Each directory contains the files required to generate the corresponding figure, including, as applicable: - plotting scripts;- processed numerical simulation data or the subsets of simulation outputs needed for plotting; and- auxiliary files required by the scripts. For figures that include maps, the corresponding directories also contain Generic Mapping Tools (GMT) scripts and any required auxiliary files. The archive provides the processed simulation outputs needed to reproduce the published figures without rerunning the complete numerical simulations. ### 2.2. Numerical Simulations The numerical simulations were performed using BEM2D. To reproduce the simulations, users should: 1. Obtain the BEM2D source code from the GitHub repository.2. Compile the code following the instructions in the BEM2D documentation.3. Consult and adapt the examples in `examples/QUARRY_LOADING/` to reproduce the simulation configurations described in the manuscript. The processed simulation data included in `archive_FIGURES.tar.xz` were generated using this workflow. ### 2.3. Figure Generation Each figure directory contains one or more scripts for generating the corresponding manuscript figure from the data stored in that directory. For figures involving maps, the accompanying GMT scripts should also be executed. The scripts are intended to facilitate figure reproduction using the archived data, without requiring the numerical simulations to be rerun. ### 2.4. Software Requirements Depending on the figure and the desired level of reproduction, the following software may be required: - **BEM2D:** to rerun the numerical simulations.- **Generic Mapping Tools (GMT):** to generate maps for figures that use GMT.- **Additional software or libraries:** as specified in the individual plotting scripts. Users should consult the relevant script headers and documentation for specific software dependencies and execution instructions. ### 2.5. Reproducibility Workflow To reproduce the manuscript figures, the recommended workflow is: 1. Extract `archive_FIGURES.tar.xz`.2. Navigate to the directory corresponding to the figure of interest.3. Execute the plotting scripts using the processed data provided in that directory.4. For figures containing maps, execute the accompanying GMT scripts as required. To rerun the numerical simulations, users must additionally obtain and compile BEM2D and configure the simulations according to the manuscript and the examples provided in the BEM2D repository. ## Notes on Reproducibility The figure archive contains processed simulation outputs and the data required for figure generation, rather than the complete set of raw simulation outputs. These archived files are intended to enable reproduction of the published figures without rerunning the full numerical models. The BEM2D implementation is maintained separately in its GitHub repository. The aerial imagery and digital terrain data used to estimate surface mass removal are provided in `aerial.tar.gz`. 10.6084/m9.figshare.34475100

papers.t: Spatiotemporal evolution of shallow seismic velocities associated with the 2024 East Rift Zone eruption at Kīlauea Volcano
in: ETH Zurich
Swiss Seismological Service
United States Geological Survey
Hawaiian Volcano Observatory
Cascades Volcano Observatory
tk: Monitors shallow seismic velocity changes ($dv/v$) at Kīlauea Volcano during the 2024 East Rift Zone eruption using ambient noise interferometry.
利用背景噪声干涉法监测基拉韦厄火山2024年东裂谷带喷发期间的浅部地震波速度变化。
papers.ab: Dense temporary seismic nodal arrays offer new opportunities for ambient noise interferometry, enabling spatially resolved imaging of subsurface processes at scales inaccessible to permanent networks. Here we demonstrate this potential in a volcanic setting, exploiting the 2024 unrest at Kīlauea volcano, . By inverting velocity changes across 2667 station pairs from both a temporary nodal deployment and the permanent Hawaiian Volcano Observatory network, we reconstruct the full spatio-temporal evolution of the unrest, capturing the pre-, co-, and post-eruptive sequence. The resulting velocity changes are validated against Global Navigation Satellite System and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar measurements, and conceptual volumetric strain models. Within our study period, we find no significant influence of precipitation and instead we identify three primary mechanisms driving velocity changes: magma reservoir dynamics, including inflation/deflation at the summit reservoirs, dike intrusions indicating down-rift magma transport, and transient changes related to earthquake rupturing. While disentangling effects of overlapping deformation sources remain challenging, our seismic velocity anomalies from distinct processes closely mirror independent geodetic observations. This close alignment indicates that, in the absence of strong environmental influences, high-resolution spatio-temporal velocity changes determined using dense networks can guide interpretations of subsurface strain in regions where geodetic measurements lack sufficient resolution.

papers.t: Progressive oxidative weathering raised sub-arc mantle fugacity on the Archaean Earth
tk: Sulfur spectroscopy of Archaean zircon-hosted apatite inclusions reveals that sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity increased between 3.4 and 3.0 Ga due to progressive oxidative weathering.
硫光谱分析表明太古代弧下地幔氧逸度因氧化风化而增加。
papers.ab: In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. Here we use sulfur K-edge micro-X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy to measure the relative abundances of S 6+ , S 4+ and S 2− in apatite inclusions hosted by geochemically characterized and dated zircons from sub-arc sanukitoid magmas that span 3.4 billion years of Earth’s geological history. The sub-arc mantle shows marked increase in oxygen fugacity between 3.4 and 3.0 billion years ago (Ga). It is substantially more oxidized than unaltered ambient upper mantle, a characteristic that cannot be explained by fractionation, degassing or intrinsic mantle processes. We propose that progressive oxidative weathering enhanced the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled to mantle wedge sources, establishing feedback between subduction of surface materials and incrementally oxidized arc magmatism. Early subduction involving inorganic oxidation and ‘whiffs’ of oxygen between 3.4 and 2.7 Ga may have regulated an early increase in fugacity of the sub-arc mantle before the Great Oxidation Event, matching similar conditions to the modern Earth by 2.1 Ga.

papers.t: Reinvigorating the wavelet transform: A versatile topol for modern seismic imaging
in: bp, Houston, USA
bp, Aberdeen, UK
tk: Embedding wavelet transforms directly into FWI and LSM workflows improves convergence, image quality, and parameter decoupling.
将小波变换直接嵌入FWI和LSM流程可提高收敛速度并实现参数解耦。
papers.ab: Recent advances in ocean-bottom node acquisition and GPU-enabled computing have established inversion-based methods such as Least-Squares Migration (LSM) and Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) as key tools for high-resolution seismic imaging. However, extending these workflows to higher frequencies and multi-parameter settings introduces persistent challenges, including noise amplification, slow convergence, high computational cost, and severe parameter cross-talk. This study revisits wavelet transform methods as an integral component of the imaging process rather than a pre- or post-processing tool. Exploiting their multiscale, localized, and directional characteristics, we embed wavelet representations directly within inversion workflows to improve scalability, efficiency, and image quality. Applications include wavelet-domain gradient conditioning, adaptive image-domain LSM via Hessian filtering, and practical Hessian-based preconditioning for FWI. We further extend this framework to multi-parameter FWI through a wavelet-domain block Hessian inversion strategy, enabling explicit decoupling of parameter sensitivities without relying on conventional heuristics such as reparameterization or staged inversion. Results from synthetic and field examples, including the Atlantis dataset, demonstrate accelerated convergence, enhanced image fidelity, and substantial reduction of cross-talk. These results position the wavelet transform as a scalable and unifying toolkit for next-generation inversion-driven seismic imaging.

papers.t: Shallow magma ponding and degassing beneath Mt. Etna summit craters inferred from a multi-parameter study
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
INGV Osservatorio Etneo
tk: A multi-parameter study of Mt. Etna combines geochemical, seismic, and thermal data to track shallow magma ponding and degassing dynamics.
结合多参数观测揭示了埃特纳火山浅部岩浆积聚与脱气动力学。
papers.ab: Effective monitoring of active volcanoes relies on the integrated analysis of multidisciplinary datasets to constrain magma migration and its temporal evolution. Here, we present a multidisciplinary study, which combines plume geochemical data, volcano-seismic signals and thermal satellite data, to gain insights into the magmatic processes in Mt. Etna's shallow plumbing system. The multiparametric study enables assessing magma ponding, convection and degassing dynamics, with particular emphasis on halogen gas emissions. Halogen and sulphur emission rates provide constraints on magma residence efficiency and the steadiness of the magma supply in the shallow system. From January to May 2023, persistent thermal anomalies, low infrasound activity, stable volcanic tremor, and sustained halogen and sulphur degassing indicate a steady-state degassing regime and efficient magma rejuvenation at shallow levels. From late May 2023, an increase in SO₂ emissions without a corresponding increase in HCl emissions, alongside enhanced infrasound activity, increased tremor amplitude, and sporadic thermal anomalies, point to a decoupling between deep gas ascent and magma ascent within the main conduit. These observations suggest that halogen flux monitoring, owing to the high solubility of halogens in silicate melts, provides a sensitive indicator of changes in the magma supply rate and near-surface magma residence time in basaltic volcanic systems.

papers.t: Structural Geothermal Plays in the Lower Carboniferous Limestone, East Midlands, UK: Insights from Legacy Geophysical Data
tk: Integrates legacy 3D seismic, gravity, and magnetic data to characterize structural controls and define geothermal plays in the UK East Midlands.
利用遗留地震与重磁数据表征了英国东米德兰兹地热储层结构。
papers.ab: Lower Carboniferous Limestone (LCL) is a promising geothermal target in Britain, but uncertainty in subsurface structure and permeability limits resource assessment. Here, we use the Welton area of the East Midlands, where legacy hydrocarbon exploration data provide detailed subsurface coverage, to investigate the controls on LCL geothermal prospectivity. We integrate 3D seismic reflection, well, gravity and aeromagnetic data with gravity forward and inverse modelling to characterise the geometry and structural evolution of the LCL. Seismic interpretation reveals a heterogeneous reservoir partitioned into a western rift-bounding fault corridor, an eastern relay system and a northern fault-intersection zone, together with fault-tip and segment-linkage structures. Seismic-stratigraphic relationships record late Carboniferous reactivation of this inherited extensional architecture, expressed by localised LCL doming and erosion, Namurian absence and onlap, and onlap within the lowermost Westphalian. These relationships indicate variable inversion and possible weathering or palaeo-karst development on uplifted LCL highs. Gravity and magnetic lineaments reproduce and extend seismic-scale structural trends, while source-depth estimates indicate that parts of the fault network were localised above deeper inherited fabrics. Gravity modelling shows that plausible LCL density variations alone cannot explain the observed gravity field, requiring deeper or unmodelled density heterogeneity. The integrated results define three conceptual structural geothermal plays: a fault-damage-zone play, a relay/linkage play and a fault-intersection play. These settings may favour secondary permeability through fracturing, augmented by inversion-related deformation and possible palaeokarst development, although present-day transmissivity remains unconstrained. This study demonstrates how legacy seismic and potential-field datasets can support geothermal targeting in structurally complex carbonate reservoirs.

papers.t: The Gannon Storm: Citizen science observations during the geomagnetic superstorm of 10 May 2024
tk: This study utilizes citizen science observations to analyze auroral characteristics and technological disruptions during the extreme geomagnetic storm of 10 May 2024.
本研究利用公民科学观测数据分析了2024年5月10日极端地磁暴期间的极光特征和技术干扰。
papers.ab: The 10 May 2024 geomagnetic storm, referred to as the Gannon Storm in this paper, was one of the most extreme to have occurred in over 20 years. In the era of smartphones and social media, millions of people from all around the world were alerted to the possibility of exceptional auroral displays. Hence, many people not only witnessed but also photographed the aurora during this event. These citizen science observations, although not from scientific instruments operated by observatories or research groups, can prove invaluable in obtaining data to characterise this extraordinary event. In particular, many observers saw and photographed the aurora at mid-latitudes, where ground-based instruments targeting auroral studies are sparse or absent. We created an online survey and circulated it within networks of aurora photographers to collect observations of the aurora and disruptions in technological systems that were experienced during this superstorm. We obtained 696 citizen science reports from over 30 countries, containing information such as the time and location of aurora sightings, observed colours and auroral forms during the geomagnetic storm. We supplemented the obtained dataset with 186 auroral observations logged in the Skywarden catalogue by citizen scientists. The main findings enabled by the data collected through these reports are that the aurora was widely seen from locations at geomagnetic latitudes ranging between 30° and 60°, with a few reports from even lower latitudes. This was significantly further equatorward than predicted by auroral oval models. The reported auroral emission colours, predominantly red and pink and intense enough to reach naked-eye visibility, suggest that the auroral electron precipitation contained large fluxes of low-energy (< 1 keV) particles. (...)

papers.t: A 3D Finite-Element Workflow for Mapping Earthquake Nucleation Tendency Under Tectonic Loading in Embedded Frictional Fault Systems
in: School of Earthquake Science and technology, University of Emergency Management, Langfang, China
Hebei Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics, Langfang, China
Langfang Key Laboratory of Earth Exploration and Information Technology, Langfang, China
School of Geophysics and Geomatics, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan, China
Institute of Geophysics, Department of Earth Sciences, ETH Zurich, Switzerland.
tk: A 3D finite-element workflow maps relative earthquake nucleation tendency on frictional faults under tectonic loading without preassigning initiation points.
提出一种无需预设起裂点的三维有限元断层地震成核趋势评估方法。
papers.ab: Dynamic-rupture simulations commonly prescribe rupture initiation, which complicates assessment of where instability would preferentially localize for a given fault geometry and tectonic loading. We present a 3D finite-element workflow that maps relative nucleation tendency on embedded frictional fault systems without preassigning an initiation point. Faults are represented as frictional contact interfaces within an elastic volume. Gravity is retained in both branches to provide the depth-dependent normal-stress background and stable contact closure on embedded frictional interfaces. The workflow employs paired branches on the same undeformed geometry with an identical mesh: a gravity-only quasi-static baseline and a gravity-plus-tectonic branch that differs only by a small displacement boundary condition. Each quasi-static state is transferred to a short implicit transient analysis on the same undeformed mesh under the same gravity and compatible boundary constraints. Slip may occur through the contact-state transition from sticking to sliding in the transient stage. We define the onset slip s(x) as the slip accumulated over the first N dynamic increments (default N = 1) and use the differential onset slip Δs(x) between the paired branches as a single-event indicator of nucleation tendency. Timestep tests over Δt=0.001–0.05 s identify the same peak node, and 1–2 km meshes give consistent localization at 15–16 km depth; coarser 3–4 km meshes shift the peak to 3–5 km depth, whereas the thresholded high-slip footprint remains resolution dependent.

papers.t: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
tk: Combining remote sensing and 3D dynamic rupture modeling, this study shows that the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake's slip, helix-shaped geometry, and supershear speed were predictable from pre-event observations.
结合遥感与三维动态破裂模拟，研究表明2025年曼德勒地震的滑动、几何及超剪切速度可由震前观测预测。
papers.ab: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

papers.t: Components of Variability in Ground-Motion Model Derived from Distributed Acoustic Sensing
in: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Potsdam, Germany
Institute of Geosciences, University of Potsdam, Potsdam, Germany
Institute of Environmental Science and Geography, University of Potsdam, Potsdam, Germany
Institute of Earth Sciences, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan
tk: Presents the first regional, partially nonergodic ground-motion model for DAS, incorporating cable coupling, orientation, and channel correlation.
提出首个基于DAS的区域半非遍历性地震动模型，考虑了耦合、方向及通道相关性。
papers.ab: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) allows meter-scale measurements along kilometer-scale fiber-optic cables, offering new opportunities to develop ground-motion models (GMMs) that resolve spatial variations in ground motion. However, developing GMMs from DAS measurements remains challenging because DAS observations are influenced by DAS-specific nonergodic components not present in seismometer-based measurements, including cable coupling and orientation. Moreover, channel correlation in DAS measurements can lead to biased uncertainty estimates of ground-motion variability when DAS channels are treated as independent stations; therefore, configuring correlation is essential for the reliable development of DAS-based GMMs. Here, we present the first regional, partially nonergodic DAS-based GMM using strain-rate data from a 400-channel array in Hualien City, Taiwan. We compile a dataset of peak strain rates and Fourier amplitudes (0.1–10 Hz) from 77 earthquakes (3.2≤Mw≤7.1, 45.75≤Rhypo≤170.80 km). Building upon classical seismometer-based GMMs, we extend the variability framework to consider (1) cable coupling associated with installation and environment types and (2) cable orientation. We further model (3) channel correlation inherent to DAS measurement principles and array geometry using Matérn kernels parameterized by both along-fiber channel and Euclidean distances. The resulting DAS-based GMM achieves magnitude–distance scaling comparable with classical GMMs, while allowing decomposition of ground-motion variability. We observe that the cable-coupling component exerts a broadband effect on ground motions and emerges as a dominant, frequency-dependent source of within-event variability. The orientation component captures frequency-dependent DAS directional sensitivity related to cable orientation and wavefront azimuth, and accounts for only a small portion of the variability. Introducing channel correlation substantially reduces channel-related standard deviations. Overall, our findings demonstrate that DAS-derived ground motions require a fundamentally different framework from classical seismometer-based GMMs, emphasizing the importance of deployment metadata and correlation modeling and providing a foundation for next-generation seismic hazard assessments using dense fiber-optic sensing.

papers.t: NetArray, a New Seismic Array Methodology with Example Implementation for Earthquake Early Warning
in: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Tel-Aviv University, Tel Aviv, Israel
tk: NetArray unifies network and array methods by accounting for wavefront curvature, improving source location and depth estimation for out-of-network earthquakes.
NetArray通过考虑波前曲率融合了台网与台阵方法，提高了台网外地震定位与深度测定的精度。
papers.ab: Accurate seismic source location remains challenging when earthquakes occur outside or near the edges of seismic networks. Standard network methods require favorable azimuthal coverage and suffer from severe distance–depth trade-offs, whereas conventional array approaches assume planar wavefronts and are restricted to distant sources. Here, we introduce NetArray, a methodology that unifies network and array approaches within a single framework. Based on a planar–radial decomposition of interstation delays, NetArray relaxes the plane-wave assumption to explicitly account for wavefront curvature. This yields a semianalytical, velocity-model-independent cost function that jointly constrains back azimuth, epicentral distance, and horizontal slowness. After the slowness vector and epicentral distance are resolved, a velocity model is used to constrain source depth, avoiding the distance–depth trade-off inherent to network methods. Synthetic tests demonstrate that NetArray notably improves back-azimuth accuracy relative to standard array methods at distances up to several times the array aperture while providing reliable estimates of epicentral distance and depth. Compared with conventional network approaches, NetArray yields more stable solutions for out-of-network sources and provides explicit minimum and maximum distance bounds for uncertainty estimation. Application to a virtual array in the Mendocino Triple Junction region highlights NetArray’s potential for earthquake early warning systems: using a limited number of stations, the method successfully mitigates the offshore distance overestimation inherited in network approaches. These results demonstrate that NetArray provides a robust, unified framework for real-time and offline seismic source location.

papers.t: Acoustic modeling of low-frequency seismic sources in transition zones: state of the art and challenges
in: Sercel, France
Stanford University / Sercel, US
POEMS (CNRS-INRIA-ENSTA), Institut Polytechnique de Paris, France
Department of Geophysics, Stanford University, US
tk: This paper reviews acoustic modeling methods for low-frequency marine seismic sources, highlighting challenges in shallow-water transition zones.
本文评估了浅水过渡带中低频海洋地震震源的声学模拟方法与挑战。
papers.ab: Low-frequency marine seismic sources are becoming increasingly important for enhancing deep-target illumination and improving the stability of broadband imaging, particularly for Full-Waveform Inversion and quantitative imaging. This study investigates the modeling of a large-volume low-frequency marine source designed to radiate energy down to about 1 Hz. Unlike conventional air guns, this source operates in a distinct physical regime, generating a much larger bubble and a longer oscillation period. In deep water, field observations show that spherical lumped-parameter models already provide a robust first-order description of its acoustic signature. Because the Tuned Pulse Source (TPS) behaves as a single, nearly omnidirectional point source, it produces a simpler and more controlled wavefield than conventional air-gun arrays, creating favorable conditions for precise source characterization and predictive modeling. In shallow-water and transition-zone environments, the larger bubble size, stronger hydrostatic pressure gradients, buoyancy, and free-surface interaction motivate a more refined representation of source dynamics. These effects are expected to influence the low-frequency signature, particularly through stronger coupling between the source pulse and surface ghost reflections. The paper therefore evaluates the range of applicability of conventional spherical source models for such configurations and identifies the conditions under which higher-fidelity approaches can further improve source characterization. It also highlights the potential of Boundary Element Methods (BEM) to capture non-spherical bubble dynamics and more complex boundary interactions, while addressing the associated mathematical and numerical challenges. Overall, the study establishes a physics-based framework for progressively improving TPS modeling in shallow-water settings and supports future experimental validation in transition-zone applications.

papers.t: A Positive Flower Structure Uncovered by InSAR Images of the 2025 Mw ∼6 Afghanistan Earthquake Sequence
in: Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geodynamics and Geohazards, School of Earth Science and Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, China
Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory, Zhuhai, China
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Potsdam, Germany
tk: InSAR observations of the 2025 Afghanistan earthquake sequence reveal conjugate thrust faults reactivating a positive flower structure under the control of the Konar fault system.
InSAR观测揭示2025年阿富汗地震序列由科纳尔断裂带控制的走滑正花状构造复活所致。
papers.ab: On 31 August 2025 (UTC), an Mw 6.0 shallow thrust earthquake struck the southern Hindu Kush region of Afghanistan, followed by a largest aftershock (Mw 5.6) on 4 September. This earthquake sequence caused widespread damage and unusually high casualties. To investigate the seismogenic structure, we utilized Sentinel-1 Terrain Observation with Progressive Scans Synthetic Aperture Radar data for Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar processing to derive the coseismic deformation fields of both the mainshock and aftershock. The results show that the maximum cumulative deformation reached 24.2 cm in the ascending track and 17.0 cm in the descending track in line of sight, with consistent trends moving toward the satellites. The optimal earthquake slip model reveals a set of conjugate thrust faults, including the mainshock segment F1 (north-dipping, peak slip ≈ 1.11 m) and the aftershock segment F2 (south-dipping, peak slip ≈ 0.99 m). Integrating the regional fault network with these newly resolved faults, we interpret the earthquake sequence as the reactivation of a positive flower structure, which is likely controlled by flexural bending processes of the Konar fault system, the major tectonic boundary of the local crustal block. A Coulomb failure stress change (ΔCFS) analysis shows that the mainshock had effective triggering effects on the following sequence. Meanwhile, positive ΔCFS has also been loaded in the bend segment of the Konar fault through the earthquake sequence, highlighting this region as a locus of elevated seismic hazard potential for future.

papers.t: Uncertainty quantification-driven shear wave velocity prediction using a spatiotemporal Bayesian neural network
in: Key Laboratory of Marine Geology and Metallogency, First Institute of Oceanography, MNR, Qingdao 266061, China
Laboratory for Marine Geology, Qingdao Marine Science and Technology Center, Qingdao 266237, China
College of Earth Sciences and Engineering, Shandong University of Science and Technology, Qingdao 266590, China
tk: A spatiotemporal Bayesian neural network predicts shear wave velocity and quantifies epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties using reservoir logging data.
提出一种时空贝叶斯神经网络，利用测井数据预测剪切波速度并量化不确定性。
papers.ab: Shear wave velocity (Vs) is a key parameter used for seismic data processing and evaluating oil and gas reservoirs. Conventional logging and machine learning methods are hampered by the provision of fixed Vs predictions, which limits their capacity to effectively quantify the uncertainty of predictions. Therefore, we propose a spatiotemporal Bayesian neural network (STBNN), which exploits the advantages of ensemble learning methods in processing logging data and Bayesian methods in modeling uncertainty. STBNN facilitates both accurate Vs predictions and a robust quantification of uncertainty. We initially perform a feature selection on logging data to identify logging-sensitive attributes as input features, and employ Monte Carlo dropout, a Bayesian approximation method, to determine both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. These uncertainties are integrated into the STBNN framework, which reduces prediction uncertainty and enhances accuracy. Subsequently, we assess the model using a logging dataset derived from actual oil reservoirs, and evaluate its generalizability. The trained STBNN model is applied to an untrained exploration area to predict Vs and its associated uncertainties. Finally, we assess the influence of sample size on network epistemic uncertainty and devise a practical mitigation strategy. The results reveal that compared with spatiotemporal neural network and empirical models, the STBNN model achieves a higher accuracy of prediction. We establish that prediction uncertainty is primarily attributable to epistemic uncertainty, with higher uncertainty observed in areas with limited data. This prediction uncertainty can be effectively reduced by increasing the diversity of sample data. The proposed method delivers excellent Vs prediction results, whilst minimizing the risk of errors in the interpretation of logging.

papers.t: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
tk: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake's complex rupture dynamics, including depth-dependent supershear propagation, were successfully modeled using pre-event observations and 3D dynamic rupture simulations.
结合震前观测与三维动力学破裂模拟，揭示了2025年缅甸曼德勒M7.8级地震的复杂破裂动力学特征。

Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone.
