papers.t: Building and calibrating a 3Di subgrid flood model for Hanoi, without a surveyed terrain model, drainage data, or rain gauges
tk: A 3Di subgrid flood model for Hanoi was built and calibrated using repaired DEMs, satellite rainfall, and crowdsourced depth observations under severe data constraints.
在严重缺乏数据的情况下，利用修复的DEM、卫星降雨和众包深度观测构建并校准了河内3Di子网格洪水模型。
papers.ab: Urban hydrodynamic flood models typically rely on a surveyed terrain model, an explicit pipe drainage network, and rain gauge measurements, none of which were available for the inundation following Typhoon Matmo in My Dinh and Tay Mo, Hanoi, on 7 October 2025. The present study addresses this issue by documenting the construction and calibration of a 32.8 km^2 3Di subgrid model under severe data constraints, demonstrating how unmonitored catchments can be simulated using openly accessible sources. Specifically, a 1 m digital elevation model was systematically repaired for river and lake bathymetry, unsurveyed water bodies, road underpasses, and an excavation pit to re-establish essential overland flow paths. In addition, assigned infiltration rates across land-cover classes were utilized to stand in for the unrecorded subsurface sewer system, while half-hourly satellite precipitation from the IMERG Late product provided rainfall forcing for a closed two-dimensional domain. Model calibration was conducted against eight crowdsourced depth observations. The simulation results demonstrated that six observation points retained surface water and were closely aligned with the reported values within 2.2 cm. However, two peripheral locations along Tay Mo Road and Road 70 remained completely dry in the model. Because all eight points were utilized during parameter adjustment and no independent validation dataset was withheld, this correspondence reflects a calibration fit rather than an unconstrained predictive test.

papers.t: Rapid Rupture Mapping of Potential Tsunamigenic Earthquakes in the Southwest Pacific Using Regional Seismic Arrays
in: School of Environment, University of Auckland, Auckland, New Zealand
Earth Science New Zealand, Wellington, New Zealand
Department of Physics, University of Auckland, Auckland, New Zealand
School of Earth and Environment, University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand
tk: Optimizing regional seismic array backprojection using the MUSIC algorithm provides rapid, reliable rupture extent constraints for large Southwest Pacific earthquakes to improve tsunami early warnings.
优化区域地震台网的MUSIC回溯投影成像，可快速准确约束西南太平洋大地震破裂范围，提升海啸预警能力。
papers.ab: Rapid spatial characterization of rupture in tsunamigenic earthquakes (Mw≥7.5) is critical for improving tsunami early warning capabilities, particularly for sparsely instrumented regions. We investigate how regional array seismology can be optimized for such settings by enhancing real-time rupture imaging. Using the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) backprojection technique, we evaluate regional array processing performance with the New Zealand broadband seismic network in the Southwest Pacific. Performance is assessed using synthetic earthquakes spanning a range of magnitudes (Mw 8.5–9.1), rupture lengths, directivities (unilateral and bilateral), and source–array geometries (epicentral distances and back azimuths). Results show that the New Zealand seismic network can reliably constrain rupture extent for large regional tsunamigenic earthquakes, with an average rupture length error of less than ∼15%. Earthquake magnitude primarily governs the optimum processing parameters (frequency band and time window length), whereas source–array geometry ultimately limits the rupture imaging quality that can be achieved. Integrating MUSIC-derived rupture extents into tsunami warning workflows generally improves agreement with reference tsunami forecasts compared with magnitude-based scaling alone, demonstrating the value of rapid spatial rupture constraints as a complement to magnitude and ocean observations. These findings provide practical guidance for parameter selection in real-time rupture imaging and highlight the potential of MUSIC-based array processing for rapid characterization of large tsunamigenic earthquakes.

papers.t: Basin-scale organization of groundwater and surface water during the monsoon season: Hydrochemical and isotopic insights from the Brahmaputra River Basin, Northeast India
in: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati
University of California, Berkeley
Georgia Institute of Technology
tk: This study investigates the basin-scale interaction of groundwater and surface water in the Brahmaputra River Basin using hydrochemical and isotopic tracers during the monsoon.
该研究利用氢氧同位素和水化学示踪剂探讨了季风期雅鲁藏布江-布拉马普特拉河流域地下水与地表水的盆地尺度相互作用。
papers.ab: Study region The Indian sector of the Brahmaputra River Basin (BRB). Study focus We co-evaluated groundwater (GW) and river water (RW) across the Indian BRB using a synoptic monsoon-season survey (July 2022; n = 83; 36 GW, 47 RW). Hydrochemistry, stable isotopes (δ²H, δ¹⁸O), water-quality indices, and principal component analysis (PCA) were interpreted within a geomorphic–hydrogeological framework to resolve solute-acquisition processes, water-quality controls, and setting-dependent GW–RW relationships. New hydrological insights for the region GW–RW organization varied systematically with geomorphic setting and subsurface storage. Monsoon-season RW was comparatively dilute and carbonate-weighted, consistent with rapid routing and preferential expression of carbonate-derived solutes during high flow, whereas GW recorded greater solute accumulation, stronger silicate-weathering signatures, and widespread cation exchange. Stable isotopes showed pronounced GW–RW separation in low-gradient alluvial settings, where GW integrated recharge across broader spatial and temporal scales, but greater correspondence in mountainous settings characterized by shorter flow paths and limited storage. PCA independently reproduced this setting-dependent hydrochemical structure. Glacier- and snow-fed rivers preserved depleted high-elevation signatures that were progressively modified by downstream mixing. Drinking-water suitability was constrained principally by Fe, Mn, and Al, with As and NO₃⁻ contributing locally, whereas irrigation suitability was broadly favorable. Exceptional antecedent rainfall coincided with multi-constituent enrichment in two Himalayan tributaries, demonstrating that event-scale perturbations can locally disrupt basin-scale river-water patterns.

papers.t: Data from: Mitigating flood risk amplified by localized land subsidence in China's Greater Bay Area through targeted levee heightening
tk: This dataset supports the assessment of flood risk and targeted levee heightening in China's Greater Bay Area under land subsidence and sea-level rise.
该数据集支持评估地面沉降影响下大湾区的防洪风险与堤防加高策略。
papers.ab: This study presents a refined assessment of inundation risk in the Guangdong-Hong k, China. By leveraging high-resolution relative local land subsidence, sea-level rise, and demographic projections, we evaluated future coastal land loss and flood exposure.

papers.t: Investigating the control of subsurface structures on rainfall-induced ground instability using integrated geophysics and remote sensing in Jixi, China
tk: This study integrates multi-source geophysics and remote sensing to reveal the subsurface structure and evolutionary mechanism of the Jixi landslide.
本研究整合多源地球物理与遥感数据，揭示了鸡西滑坡的演化机制。
papers.ab: Landslides are common geological hazards worldwide, often associated with by heavy rainfall. Jixi City, located in southeastern Heilongjiang Province, experiences frequent rainstorms from July to September. Long‑term unregulated quarrying has destroyed vegetation and reduced slope toe stability in the area. In early August 2023, Typhoon Doksuri increased rainfall. The Jixi landslide occurred on August 10 following this heavy rainfall. This study integrates aeromagnetic data, electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), multi‑temporal satellite and UAV remote sensing, borehole data, and surface displacement monitoring. Aeromagnetic anomalies support a magnetically quiet basement without deep magmatic activity. ERT 2D and quasi‑3D inversions, calibrated by six boreholes, reveal a three‑part electrical structure: a shallow discontinuous high‑resistivity landslide deposit, a continuous low‑resistivity slip zone interpreted as mudstone with elevated moisture content and fault fracture zones, and a deeper blocky high‑resistivity slip bed. Steeply dipping low‑resistivity belts are interpreted as possible water‑bearing faults. Multi‑temporal images show progressive quarry expansion. Post‑landslide UAV orthophotos indicate that the main landslide body showed approximately 20 m of cumulative displacement toward the southwest between 2020 and 2023, with a fan‑shaped morphology exhibiting apparent retrogressive geomorphic characteristics. Surface monitoring from August 17 recorded horizontal displacements of 0.2–35.2 cm, with the dominant direction toward the southwest and elevation changes showing rear subsidence and frontal uplift. Boreholes support the transition from intact slip bed to fractured landslide mass. Based on these results, a possible evolutionary chain is proposed as an evidence‑supported interpretation: quarrying disturbance, typhoon‑induced rainfall infiltration, fault‑controlled water conduction, slip zone softening, and retrogressive sliding. The multi‑method approach provides cross‑scale constraints from regional background to shallow detailed structures, offering a scientific basis for post‑disaster identification, investigation, and mitigation of similar landslides.

papers.t: Phanerozoic perturbation of the mantle nitrogen cycle recorded by kimberlites
in: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
Williams College
University of Manchester
Carnegie Institution for Science
Earth and Planets Laboratory
tk: Nitrogen isotope analyses of kimberlites reveal that subducted, biologically-derived heavy nitrogen perturbed the subcontinental lithospheric mantle during the Phanerozoic.
金伯利岩氮同位素揭示显生宙生物源重氮对岩石圈地幔的扰动。
papers.ab: The surface nitrogen (N) cycle is dominated by biological activity, yet its impact on the deep N cycle is poorly constrained. Although recycled sedimentary N is observed in modern magmatic systems, it remains unknown when it first became identifiable in mantle-derived magmas and to what extent it affects the deep mantle N budget. Kimberlites provide a unique opportunity to study mantle N reservoirs because they may sample the subcontinental lithospheric mantle (SCLM), deeper plume-influenced sources, or both. Here, we present N isotope measurements of olivine-hosted fluid inclusions from 13 kimberlite pipes spanning eight cratons and emplaced from 14 ka to 558 Ma. Kimberlites with near-zero δ 15 N (+0.8 ± 1.1 ‰) are observed throughout the Phanerozoic, whereas isotopically heavier N (+5.3 ± 0.5 ‰) is only observed in kimberlites younger than 180 Ma. Elevated δ 15 N values correlate with K 2 O enrichment, indicating interaction with phlogopite-bearing, sediment-modified lithospheric mantle. K-poor kimberlites with plume-like Ne isotopes have δ 15 N and N 2 / 36 Ar consistent with a primordial deep mantle N reservoir. The emergence of 15 N-enriched signatures in Earth’s surface reservoirs is attributed to increased primary productivity and biomass burial following the Cambrian Explosion, which produced N-rich, isotopically heavy sediments that were subsequently subducted. We hypothesise that 15 N-enriched subduction signatures impacted metasomatic fluids that overprinted the SCLM during the Phanerozoic. These observations provide additional temporal resolution into the link between biosphere evolution and the deep N cycle.

papers.t: Geothermal implications of the lithosphere's thermal structure in northern Pakistan
in: University of Göttingen (Göttingen, Germany)
LIAG Institute for Applied Geophysics (Hanover, Germany)
tk: Thermal modeling of Northern Pakistan's lithosphere reveals that radiogenic crustal enrichment and rapid exhumation drive elevated heat flow and geothermal anomalies without active volcanism.
热模拟表明放射性富集与快速折返驱动了巴基斯坦北部的地热异常。
papers.ab: Conventional geothermal resources are typically associated with volcanically active plate boundaries, yet collisional orogens can also sustain elevated heat flow through radiogenic enrichment, crustal thickening, and rapid exhumation. Northern Pakistan, encompassing the Himalaya, Kohistan, and Karakoram terranes, hosts numerous hot springs aligned with major fault zones despite the absence of active volcanism. The origin of this anomalous heat remains debated, reflecting the lack of surface heat-flow measurements and limited geophysical constraints on the lithosphere. To address this gap, we apply 1D steady-state, 1D transient, and 2D advective-conductive thermal models with radiogenic heat production and exhumation-driven heat transport to the Nanga Parbat Massif, Kohistan arc, and Karakoram terrane. These models, in the absence of direct heat-flow measurements in the region, remain uncalibrated; however, they bracket a range of plausible thermal states. Steady-state models show a strong dependence of geotherms on crustal radiogenic heat production (RHP): in the NPM, upper-crustal enrichment (4–5 µW m −3 ) yields surface heat flow of 85–120 mW m −2 , whereas Kohistan produces lower values (50–85 mW m −2 ) due to its mafic-dominated crust. Karakoram yields intermediate heat flow (65–103 mW m −2 ), with RHP concentrated in the batholith and metamorphic complexes. These models also reveal that surface-derived RHP values cannot be extrapolated to the mid- and lower crust: doing so yields Moho temperatures inconsistent with petrological and geophysical constraints, implying redistribution of heat-producing elements during partial melting and differentiation. 1D transient models suggest that exhumation of 2–3 mm yr −1 in the NPM can further amplify geotherms, producing surface heat flow up to 220–250 mW m −2 and inverting deep geotherms at 20 km in exploratory end-member scenarios. 2D models capture the combined effects of radiogenic enrichment, exhumation, and rugged topography. Isotherms are compressed beneath valleys and expanded beneath peaks, with the strongest thermal anomalies localized in the NPM and Karakoram. Surface heat-flow patterns reflect these contrasts, ranging from ∼120 mW m −2 (moderate scenarios) to nearly 180 mW m −2 (fast exhumation). Péclet numbers ranging from below unity to greater than unity indicate that exhumation progressively increases the contribution of advective heat transport. Crustal differentiation indices calculated from the model-derived heat-flow estimates are consistent with strong upper-crustal enrichment of heat-producing elements in the NPM and Karakoram, indicating their redistribution during crustal thickening and partial melting. The models suggest that the region can sustain anomalously high heat flow through the interplay of RHP, exhumation, and crustal differentiation. For northern Pakistan, these results provide a physical basis for the widespread hydrothermal activity and indicate elevated subsurface temperatures in the NPM and Karakoram, identifying them as regions that warrant further site-specific investigation of reservoir properties and hydrogeological conditions.

papers.t: Input files and output time series for: Nonlinear Dynamics of Single Fault Earthquake Cycles
tk: A dataset of 55 three-dimensional earthquake-cycle simulations on planar faults with dip angles from 5° to 90° modeled using the HBI code.
基于HBI模拟的55个不同倾角三维断层地震周期数据集。
papers.ab: This dataset contains the input files and output time series from 55 three-dimensional earthquake-cycle models on planar faults with dip angles ranging from 5° to 90°. The models were performed with HBI (Ozawa et al., 2023). All models use the same friction parameters and initial conditions, so dip angle is the only parameter that varies between runs. Each model covers approximately 10,000 years of fault slip history. The archive contains the following files and directories: input/, which contains the HBI input file (.in) for each model; geometry/, which contains the fault mesh (.stl) for each dip angle; the parameter file; and monitor/, which contains the fault maximum/average output time series, recorded at every time step (refer to the HBI user guide for column info https://github.com/sozawa94/hbi).

papers.t: Probabilistic AI models outperform numerical weather prediction models on record breaking heat extremes
tk: Probabilistic AI weather prediction models outperform traditional numerical weather prediction models in forecasting record-breaking heat extremes when evaluated using fair probabilistic verification.
在采用公平的概率验证时，概率AI天气预报模型在预测破纪录极端高温方面优于传统数值天气预报模型。
papers.ab: AI weather prediction (AIWP) models have emerged as a key complement to physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, and now often outperform them on aggregate skill. Yet, several studies report that physics-based models still forecast extreme events better, in particular record-breaking extremes, based on the evaluation of deterministic forecasts. Here we evaluate heat extreme forecasts from probabilistic AIWP models over global land and show that they clearly outperform the ECMWF IFS ensemble, both raw and post-processed, including for record-breaking events, in all regions and at all lead times considered. AIWP models better forecast the occurrence and intensity of extremes, are better calibrated in the tail and miss fewer records. Station observations confirm these results. We argue that many reported AIWP limitations stem from unsuitable verification choices, specifically comparing deterministic forecasts that target different quantities. Instead, a fair evaluation of extremes necessitates probabilistic verification.

papers.t: Uncertainty quantification in time-lapse full-waveform inversion of vertical seismic profiling data: Contrasting the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Stein variational gradient descent methods
in: Department of Chemistry and Earth Sciences
Department of Earth Sciences
tk: Contrasts Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Stein Variational Gradient Descent for uncertainty quantification in 2D time-lapse full-waveform inversion.
对比HMC与SVGD在二维时移全波形反演不确定性量化中的表现。
papers.ab: Time-lapse full-waveform inversion (TL-FWI) is increasingly important in energy-transition applications, particularly for monitoring CO2 geologic storage. Because TL-FWI is highly nonlinear and baseline and monitor surveys commonly differ in acquisition, illumination, and noise conditions, uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable interpretation. Two promising Bayesian approaches are Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD), which represent the posterior in fundamentally different ways. HMC constructs the posterior through stochastic sampling with gradient-based proposals, whereas SVGD approximates it using a deterministically evolving particle ensemble. Here, the feasibility of 2D vertical-seismic-profile (VSP)-based TL-FWI using these two approaches under a matched computational budget was investigated. Both methods recovered the main injection-related velocity anomaly, but they expressed posterior uncertainty differently. Under this resource-limited comparison, HMC yielded uncertainty fields that remained comparatively diffuse and became increasingly difficult to interpret in deeper and off-well regions where illumination is weak. By contrast, SVGD produced uncertainty patterns that are more strongly organized by acquisition geometry, placing larger uncertainty more explicitly in poorly constrained regions, although this also caused the posterior means and profiles to inherit stronger illumination-shaped artifacts. These results suggested that the practical distinction between HMC and SVGD was not one of better or worse uncertainty quantification, but rather how limited computational effort was converted into posterior information. The preferred method was therefore budget- and objective-dependent. Specifically, HMC remained attractive when more exhaustive posterior exploration was computationally feasible, whereas SVGD provided a more scalable and practically interpretable route for rapid uncertainty assessment in TL-FWI monitoring applications.

papers.t: No Tremor Accompanying Subduction Zone Slow-Slip Events in the Lower Cook Inlet, Alaska
in: Department of Geoscience, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Madison, Wisconsin, U.S.A.
Now at, New Mexico Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources, Soccoro, New Mexico, U.S.A.
tk: The study finds no evidence of tectonic tremor accompanying slow-slip events in the Lower Cook Inlet, Alaska, suggesting episodic tremor and slip is not globally ubiquitous.
下库克湾慢滑移未伴随构造震颤，表明二者并非全球普遍共存。
papers.ab: Slow-slip events (SSEs) have been reported in the Cook Inlet segment of the Alaska–Aleutian subduction zone. Tectonic tremor, a repeating low-frequency signal, has been observed in the subduction zone in the Upper Cook Inlet (UCI) slow-slip zone, but thus far no studies have identified tremor in the Lower Cook Inlet (LCI) region. This study addresses whether or not tremor occurred in the LCI from 2015 to 2017, a time window that includes multiple SSEs. Two methods are used to search for tremor within continuous data from 34 broadband stations. The first approach utilizes envelope cross-correlations across an array of stations to identify clusters of seismic events. The second method tracks relative changes in the frequency content of seismic records over time at a single station. Neither approach provides evidence of events that can conclusively be identified as tectonic tremor. Subsequently, we consider whether tremor in the LCI might be masked by noise and basin effects by simulating seismograms of tremor-like signals. Stations within the basin have high noise levels that may interfere with visual verification of tremor, but methods that leverage cross correlations should identify tremor. The apparent absence of tremor in the LCI during SSEs supports the hypothesis that fundamental differences in subduction zone geometry, thermal state, sediment load, or other properties between the LCI, where the Pacific plate subducts, and the UCI, where the Yakutat slab is found, play a role in allowing or inhibiting tremor. This work underscores emerging evidence that coupled episodic tremor and slip is not globally ubiquitous.

papers.t: Along-Dip Variations in Triggering Among Low-Frequency Earthquakes in Shikoku
in: Department of Applied Physics, Tokyo University of Science, Tokyo, Japan
tk: A modified ETAS model reveals nonmonotonic along-dip variations in low-frequency earthquake triggering in Shikoku, with higher background fractions at both shallow and deep ends.
改进的ETAS模型表明四国低频地震触发呈非单调沿倾角变化，在深部和浅部边界背景比例均较高。
papers.ab: Deep low-frequency earthquakes (LFEs) exhibit unique occurrence patterns distinct from those of regular earthquakes, but the physical conditions governing their occurrence and the spatial variations in their activity remain poorly understood. Among various types of slow earthquakes, LFEs are detected as discrete seismic events by ordinary seismometers, and detailed analysis of their activity has the potential to provide important insights into the underlying mechanisms of slow earthquakes. Therefore, we analyze tectonic LFEs in Shikoku using an epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model to investigate spatial variations in seismicity. To account for spatial interactions inherent in spatially distributed seismicity, we modify the classic ETAS approach by incorporating a reference region surrounding the target region. The analysis reveals that the background seismicity rate correlates with the total seismicity rate. Furthermore, we focus on the background fraction, which is defined as the ratio of the background seismicity rate to the total seismicity rate. We find a relatively high background fraction at both shallower and deeper ends of the source region. This result indicates that the depth dependency of the seismicity is not a simple monotonic transition, from shallow periodic to deep continuous, but instead reflects a more complex pattern. At the down-dip end, triggering is likely suppressed because of the dominance of ductile deformation, which not only reduces the elastic stress level but also inhibits efficient stress propagation for triggering. In contrast, at the up-dip end, the proximity to the region of megathrust events, where no dislocation is either allowed or at least observed at interseismic periods, may also inhibit stress propagation, leading to a similar increase in the background fraction. These results suggest that spatial variations in both temperature–pressure conditions and frictional properties influence LFEs in a nonmonotonic manner along the dip direction.

papers.t: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes
tk: Ensemble spread in deep learning streamflow models provides good error ranking but severely underestimates predictive uncertainty during extreme hydrological events.
深度学习径流预测模型中的集合传播能很好地排序误差，但在极端事件中严重低估了不确定性。
papers.ab: Deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are increasingly used for operational streamflow forecasting, with ensemble spread providing a signal of predictive uncertainty. As climate change increases the frequency of hydroclimatic extremes, these models will increasingly operate under flow conditions that are rare in their historical records. We therefore evaluate whether ensemble spread remains informative under increasing flows, examining both its magnitude relative to error and its ability to rank errors. Prediction error is approximately $2\times$ the corrected spread at ordinary flows and up to $4\times$ at the highest flows, with the discrepancy increasing with flow (log-log slope $1.30$, 95% CI: $[1.20,1.41]$). Under-dispersion is strongest in observed extreme flows beyond the training record, reaching an $18\times$ discrepancy. This is pervasive and not explainable by conditional mean bias. Area Under the Sparsification Error, a standard distribution-free metric of uncertainty ranking, describing how well a model knows when it is uncertain, indicates near-oracle ranking for ensemble spread ($0.071$), yet ordering by predicted discharge alone nearly matches it. Informative uncertainty ranking can coexist with severe under-dispersion. In deployment, error ranking cannot be verified, yet the spread is available, and it is relied on as the uncertainty signal under increasingly extreme conditions, while systematically understating risk, most severely for the extreme events that matter most.

papers.t: Fault complexity of the 2010 Jiashian earthquake sequence, southwestern Taiwan, from enhanced earthquake catalog, seismic tomography, and focal mechanism inversion
in: Institute of Earth Sciences, Academia Sinica
Academia Sinica
National Central University
National Chung Cheng University
tk: This study investigates the complex fault geometry of the 2010 Jiashian earthquake sequence in southwestern Taiwan using an enhanced catalog, seismic tomography, and focal mechanism inversion.
利用地震目录、成像与震源机制揭示台湾甲仙地震的复杂断层结构。
papers.ab: The 2010 M L 6.4 Jiashian earthquake was a significant earthquake in the fold-and-thrust belt region in southwestern Taiwan, rupturing along the Chihshan Transfer Fault zone. In this study, we collected data from a temporary seismic network deployed after the mainshock to construct an aftershock catalog containing 2506 events, surpassing the event counts of previous studies, using deep-learning-based tools. The aftershocks are then relocated using the double-difference method and used as the input for a 3D seismic tomography inversion combined with regional travel time data. The alignment of the relocated earthquake sequence reveals the structure of the seismogenic fault, trending in the northwest direction and gently dipping to the northeast at a depth of 15 km to 25 km, with three clusters: Cluster 1 aligns with the mainshock's northwest propagation, while Clusters 2 and 3 emerge southwest and south, indicating subsidiary faults. The seismic tomography images also reveal the structure of the major Chaozhou Fault in the area as the boundary between contrasting velocity zones and the seismogenic zone characterized by low velocity and a high Vp/Vs ratio structure. We determined 329 new focal mechanism solutions by first-motion P-wave polarity inversion. The P-axes of the aftershocks are predominantly oriented northeast-southwest, with greater variability in the north-south and northwest-southeast directions for earthquakes with magnitudes less than 2. The results of this study reveal the complexity of the Chihshan Transfer Fault zone and southwestern Taiwan's seismotectonics.

papers.t: Fault Structure Derived From Long-Lasting Aftershocks After the 1905 Mw≥8 Tsetserleg-Bulnay Earthquake Sequence in Mongolia
in: CEA, DAM, DIF, F-91297 Arpajon, Arpajon, Ile de France, France [FR]
Université de Paris Cité, Institut de physique du globe de Paris, CNRS, 1 rue de Jussieu, Paris, 75005, Paris, France [FR]
Université Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier, IRAP, OMP, 14 Avenue Edouard Belin, Toulouse, Toulouse, France [FR]
Geosciences Azur, UMR 6526, 250 rue Albert Einstein, Valbonne, 06560, Valbonne, France [FR]
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory of Columbia University, P.O. Box 1000, 61 Route 9W, Palisades, Palisades, United States [US], NY 10964-1000
Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics, Ulaanbaatar, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia [MN]
tk: Microseismicity from a temporary network reveals that active seismicity in the Tsetserleg-Bulnay fault system represents long-lasting aftershocks of the 1905 Mw>8 earthquake sequence.
临时地震台网观测表明，蒙古杭爱地区当前的微震活动是1905年两次8级大地震的超长余震。
papers.ab: Slowly deforming continental regions (SDCRs) host large earthquakes with long recurrence intervals that limit direct observations, and therefore, our understanding of how strain accumulates and is released through the seismic cycle in these regions. Mongolia is an SDCR where large earthquake surface ruptures of the 20 th century are exceptionally well preserved. We investigate present-day microseismicity within the fault system responsible for the two Mw>8 Tsetserleg-Bulnay earthquake sequence in 1905, northwestern Mongolia, to constrain fault geometry and ongoing seismogenic processes at depth. Using 16 months of data from a temporary seismic network, we construct a catalog of 8,000 earthquakes with M L ≥-0.6. Seismicity delineates the three-dimensional geometry of the main and secondary faults, but is strongly heterogeneous across the system. Fault orientation within the regional stress field exerts a first-order control on microseismicity, while structural complexity modulates earthquake productivity locally. Several observations indicate that the ongoing activity represents long-lasting aftershocks of the 1905 sequence. First, earthquakes occur throughout the seismogenic crust, both along faults that ruptured in 1905 and on surrounding secondary structures. Second, the present-day rate is consistent with predictions based on the combined Omori and Gutenberg-Richter relations. Third, in agreement with the rate-and-state predictions, the slowly slipping Tsetserleg fault hosts abundant microseismicity compared to the 10-times-faster-slipping Bulnay fault, which accommodated the largest coseismic slip in 1905. These findings show that aftershock sequences can persist for more than a century in SDCRs and preserve key information about historical ruptures and the long-term behavior of such fault systems.

papers.t: Some generalizations of the tornado model
tk: The paper presents generalizations of a hydrodynamic tornado model based on convective instability and rotating convection to study vortex generation.
该研究基于对流不稳定性，提出了龙卷风流体动力学模型的推广。
papers.ab: A possible mechanism of tornado generation is associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability. The supercooled cloud-air mixture near the axis starts to descend and, due to the super adiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated near-surface air mass rises. The complete system of equations for full model includes equations for the stream function, for the azimuthal velocity component, and for the change in density. The refined model considers rotating convection within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics. The simplest model uses a separate equation for the stream function and can be applied to the initial stage of vortex generation. Within the framework of the simplest model, an analytical solution is combined from 8 linear dependencies by height. Rotation increases due to the conservation of angular momentum. Within the framework of the refined model, some unidirectional differential rotation arises, but it depends on boundary conditions (can be local). The full model studies the tornado development as rotating convection from the very beginning to the quasi-stationary stage. Velocity components increase in a coordinated manner. Two cases are considered: a single whirlwind and a two-eyed tornado. Radial flows converge towards the central part of the tornado near the earth surface, and there is an outflow from the "wall" to the axis and to the periphery near the top of the tornado. The maximum vertical velocity component is achieved at a certain radial distance at a certain height. The maximum azimuthal velocity component is achieved in the tornado "wall". Tornado generation criteria are discussed.

papers.t: MELVIS: An open-source web application for computing and modelling the viscosity of volcanic melts
tk: MELVIS is an open-source Python/Streamlit web application for computing and modeling volcanic melt viscosity using machine learning and artifact-free physical models.
MELVIS是一个开源网页应用，利用机器学习和物理模型计算与模拟火山熔体粘度。
papers.ab: The viscosity of volcanic melts governs magma transport, eruption dynamics, and a broad range of magmatic processes, so predicting it as a function of temperature, composition, and dissolved water content is central to physical volcanology. Yet no freely accessible tool integrates global machine-learning predictions, physically motivated viscosity equations, and composition-specific models calibrated to avoid nanocrystallization and water-loss artefacts — experimental biases that can lead conventional viscometry to overestimate melt viscosity. Nor can existing tools show how different assumptions about the dependence of melt fragility on dissolved water propagate into viscosity predictions at eruptive temperatures — a debated question with direct consequences for conduit-flow modelling and eruption-style assessment.,Here we present MELVIS (MELt VIScosity), an open-source web application built with Python and Streamlit. MELVIS comprises three integrated modules: (1) a viscosity calculator based on the artificial neural network of Langhammer et al. (2022), developed using a database of 3,482 measurements spanning basanite to rhyolite including hydrous compositions, with batch processing and TAS-based compositional classification; (2) a hydrous modelling module that parameterises the glass transition temperature Tg(H2O) and melt fragility m(H2O) under three alternative fragility–water relationships, making explicit how model assumptions propagate into viscosity predictions at eruptive temperatures; and (3) a library of seven composition-specific, artefact-free MYEGA models for key volcanic systems. All modules yield closed-form MYEGA parameterisations suitable for direct implementation in numerical eruption models.

papers.t: Geometric Filtering in Curved Fibre-Optic Sensing—I. Planar-Arc Response and a Deployment Decision Map
in: ETH Zurich
tk: Derives the analytical response of curved fiber-optic cables to seismic waves, establishing a decision map for DAS deployment design.
推导了弯曲光纤对地震波的解析响应，并建立了DAS部署决策图。
papers.ab: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) and integrated fibre-optic sensing (IFOS) measure an optical phase change that integrates axial strain along a fibre, whose path often bends and loops. We show how planar bending controls the angular and spectral sensitivity of this measurement, an effect we call geometric filtering. Separating the integrated strain into endpoint and curvature terms, we derive the exact plane-wave response of a circular-arc fibre as a Bessel series valid at any wavelength and opening angle. At long wavelengths the response of any fibre path follows from a geometrical tensor, the gauge average of the tangent dyad. It depends on the shape of the path but not on its size. Bending fills the broadside blind spot of a straight fibre to P waves and weakens its sensitivity to SH waves. For smooth, symmetric single-apex bends, the height-to-chord ratio sets the P-wave pattern: dipole-like below about 0.13 and nearly omnidirectional above about 0.46. A closed loop acts as an areal dilatometer: it senses P waves equally from every azimuth and is blind to SH waves at all wavelengths. At finite wavelengths the opening angle filters the Bessel orders. This limits the number of terms required and turns the gauge-length notches of a straight fibre into the Bessel rings of a closed loop. For a point source, the plane-wave response requires the source to be many wavelengths away, far compared with the fibre footprint, and beyond the footprint squared over the wavelength. The last condition defines a Fibre Fresnel Number. We condense these criteria into a Decision Map that selects the response model from fibre geometry, signal frequency, and source distance, and apply it to eight DAS and IFOS deployments. Fibre geometry is thus a design variable for geometric filtering: it can make a fibre segment selectively sensitive to certain azimuths and wavelengths. Preliminary version (v1). Part I of two companion papers; Part II treats helically wound cables. To be submitted to Geophysical Journal International.

papers.t: A smooth ocean-to-continent transition without transform faults: Evidence from new bathymetric and seismic data at the Eurasia Basin-Laptev Sea shelf junction
in: Lomonosov Moscow State University
Institute of Mineralogy, Geochemistry and Crystallochemistry of Rare Elements
Durham University
Russian Academy of Sciences
Institute of Oceanology. PP Shirshov Russian Academy of Sciences
Rosneft (Russia)
tk: New bathymetric and seismic data reveal a smooth ocean-to-continent transition without transform faults at the Eurasia Basin-Laptev Sea shelf junction.
新数据表明欧亚盆地与拉普捷夫海陆架间存在无转换断层的平滑过渡。

papers.t: Physics-based deep learning for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression
tk: A physics-guided, self-supervised deep learning framework using U-Net and adaptive matching filtering constraints for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression.
一种基于物理引导和自监督深度学习的海洋地震自适应多次波压制方法。
papers.ab: Surface-related multiple elimination (SRME) is an indispensable processing step in marine seismic exploration, comprising two main components: multiple prediction and adaptive subtraction. While the multiple prediction is theoretically data-driven and relies on the data itself, the adaptive subtraction step requires a fairly subjective manual control. Our approach introduces a purely data-driven and physics-based deep learning (PDL) algorithm for improving the adaptive multiple subtraction to significantly enhanced performance. There are two main innovations in the proposed deep-learning (DL) multiple subtraction approaches: first, being data-driven and self-supervised, which removes the dependence on inflexible label preparation and model training processes; secondly, being governed by the adaptive matching filtering (AMF) equation to guide the training process. The DL module serves as a strong regression filter analogous to the traditionally known AMF. We segment a moderately sized seismic profile and an initial multiple model into a large number of patches using a patching scheme for self-contained training. The number of patches is controlled by the patch size and the shift size to enable a sufficient number of training samples required by mainstream DL platforms. The patching-based self-training and regression approach, PDL, is inherently a non-stationary matching approach that aims to obtain a globally optimal matching from the initial multiple models to the input full wavefield data through iterative patching-based training. It is also closely connected with the non-stationary regression approach, which was developed almost two decades ago. However, the PDL approach achieves even stronger regression performance due to the backpropagation-based optimization mechanism in DL, and has shown significantly improved multiple subtraction performance over a number of examples.

papers.t: Data and code: Comminution, not localization, welds faults
tk: A dataset and code repository for 2000-year quasi-dynamic earthquake cycle simulations incorporating microphysically-derived gouge evolution on a heterogeneous fault.
包含2000年地震周期模拟的数据与代码库，引入了断层泥演化机制。
papers.ab: Code, input files and compacted outputs of the earthquake-cycle simulations of Chapter 6 of the doctoral thesis "How Faults Prepare to Fail" (ETH Zurich, 2026). The simulations follow 2000 years of seismic cycles on a 200-km periodic strike-slip fault with a heterogeneous normal stress (self-affine, ±30 % about 100 MPa). They use a modified version of the quasi-dynamic simulator QDYN in which the gouge layer of every fault element evolves by wear, localization and comminution, and sets the critical slip distance D_c and the evolution parameter b of rate-and-state friction through relations derived from a microphysical model. The deposit contains the 140 simulations of the study (the main set on two stress profiles, four sensitivity sets and a comparison set) and eight simulations that test the pressure-solution constant of the friction table. It also contains the solver, the friction-table generator, the analysis and figure scripts, and the per-cycle catalogues. Every figure and table of Chapter 6 and Appendix D of the thesis can be regenerated from these files. The README describes the contents, the data format and how to reproduce the results.

papers.t: 3D Broadband Ground-Motion Simulations of Cascadia Megathrust Earthquakes: Full-Margin Scenarios Incorporating Variable Magnitudes and Frontal Thrust Splay Faulting
in: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Science Center, Seattle, Washington, U.S.A.
Department of Earth and Space Science, University of Washington, Seattle, Washington, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Pacific and Coastal Marine Science Center, Santa Cruz, California, U.S.A.
Department of Geophysics, Kangwon National University, Chuncheon-si, South Korea
U.S. Geological Survey, Geology, Minerals, Energy, and Geophysics Science Center, Portland, Oregon, U.S.A.
tk: 3D broadband simulations of 36 Cascadia megathrust scenarios reveal that offshore hypocenters and basin-directivity interactions significantly amplify inland shaking.
3D宽频地震动模拟表明，卡斯卡迪亚俯冲带的离岸震源和盆地方向性效应会显著放大内陆震动。
papers.ab: Great megathrust earthquakes (∼Mw 8–9) that rupture along the Cascadia Subduction Zone pose significant shaking and tsunami hazards to the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Although these large earthquakes are documented in the geologic record, none have been recorded with modern instrumentation, complicating regional seismic hazard assessments. To improve constraints on seismic hazard estimates for future earthquakes, we develop 3D broadband (0–10 Hz) ground-motion simulations for 36 full-margin megathrust earthquake scenarios through the Cascadia Coastlines and Peoples Hazards Research Hub. These simulations expand on the M9 Project (Frankel et al., 2018; Wirth, Frankel, et al., 2018) by incorporating a broader range of rupture parameters—variable magnitudes, splay faulting, and geodetically informed slip distributions. Benchmarking these simulations against the Next Generation Attenuation Subduction (NGA-Sub) ground-motion models shows reasonable fits for non-basin sites, although simulations predict stronger shaking at short (0–2 s) and long (6–10 s) periods. NGA-Sub basin terms improve fits to synthetic shaking within the Seattle Basin but underpredict amplitudes by a factor of 2 at periods of 2–5 s. We also evaluate how rupture characteristics influence regional inland shaking variability and basin response in the Puget Lowlands. Larger magnitude scenarios generally cause stronger inland shaking due to farther inland extents of slip and larger strong-motion-generating fault patches but show little difference in basin amplification within the Puget Lowlands compared to smaller magnitude events. Along-dip hypocenter location strongly influences overall inland shaking, with offshore (updip) hypocenters generating on average ∼45% higher shaking at long periods (>6 s) compared to onshore (downdip) hypocenters due to rupture directivity effects. Offshore splay faults minimally affect inland shaking but alter offshore deformation important for coupled ground-shaking and tsunami scenarios. Finally, we show that rupture directivity increases amplification within the Seattle Basin through the generation and interaction of higher order mode surface waves, an effect of 3D basin geometry that cannot be captured using 1D approximations.

papers.t: Global Long-wavelength Body-wave Catalog (GLoBoCat) for Lower Mantle P and S Wave Travel Times
tk: GLoBoCat uses attention-based machine learning to build a massive, consistent catalog of lower-mantle P and S wave travel times spanning 2010–2023.
GLoBoCat利用注意力机制构建了下地幔P波和S波走时目录。
papers.ab: Travel times of long period body waves passing through the lower mantle reveal the deep seismic structure and forces shaping our planet . Manual methods measuring P and S wave arrivals produce travel time catalogs with high internal consistency, but have not kept pace with the rapid growth in waveform records. Here we use attention-based machine learning trained on prior manual datasets to develop a catalog spanning 2010-2023 which is consistent with previous catalogs and straightforward to update. The new catalog exceeds millions of measurements for P and S wave travel times and retains features of the previous datasets while improving coverage in the lower mantle, particularly for raypaths turning beneath the southern hemisphere. Comparing our measurements to short period travel times, we find the correlation is different for early versus late arrivals, and that this difference is larger for P waves than S waves. The change in slope we observe is opposite to that proposed for wave propagation effects and warrants further investigation into the origin of this apparent dispersion in Earth's lower mantle.

papers.t: Oblique Closure of Confined Oceanic Domains: Subduction Abortion or Microplate Formation
in: Sorbonne Universite, T 46-00, 4 place Jussieu, Paris cedex 05, France [FR]
Institut Universitaire de France
Institut des Sciences de la Terre Paris, ISTeP UMR 7193, Sorbonne Universite, CNRS-INSU, 75005, Paris, France [FR]
Sorbonne Universite - Campus Pierre et Marie Curie, 4 place Jussieu, Paris, 75005, France [FR]
Ecole Normale Supérieure, 24, rue Lhomond, Paris, 75, France [FR]
CNRS- ENS, 24 rue Lhomond, Paris, 75231, France [FR]
Universite Toulouse III-Paul Sabatier, Unknown, Toulouse, France [FR]
tk: Thermo-mechanical modeling reveals how lower-crustal rheology and obliquity control whether oblique subduction closure leads to subduction abortion or microplate formation.
热力学模拟揭示了地壳流变学和斜向汇聚如何控制俯冲中断或微板块形成。
papers.ab: Oblique terrane entry can reorganize subduction zones and isolate small oceanic domains, but the conditions controlling whether a second subduction develops remain poorly understood. We use 2D and 3D thermo-mechanical models to investigate the roles of lower-crustal rheology and obliquity. In 2D, both continental-type and arc-type terranes localize a secondary dipping boundary, with contrasting geometries. In 3D, obliquity forces slab bending in two directions and produces structural stiffening. Accretion of weak continental crust and associated topographic loading enhance this effect and abort secondary subduction, whereas stronger arc-type crust permits a short-lived triangular oceanic microplate to form. Continued consumption folds the initial slab at depth, providing an additional mode of accommodation of the classical double-subduction space problem. The Taiwan–South China Sea and Molucca–Mindanao systems illustrate these contrasting outcomes. Our results provide mechanical criteria for reconstructing vanished oceanic domains and their magmatic evolution.

papers.t: Craton delamination induces circum-supercontinent subduction
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry
tk: Craton delamination triggered by plume underplating or melt infiltration can initiate subduction at passive margins, driving the periodic cycle of supercontinents.
克拉通下部岩石圈剥落可弱化被动大陆边缘，从而诱发超大陆周缘的俯冲启动。
papers.ab: Over the past billion years, Earth’s large-scale tectonics have been dominated by the assembly and breakup of supercontinents Rodinia and Pangea. It is widely accepted that circum-supercontinent subduction and associated sub-supercontinent upwelling trigger supercontinent breakup. Yet, previous geodynamic simulations predicted that whole mantle convection would stabilize in a fixed, long-wavelength mode, with a common degree-1 pattern resembling a stable supercontinent. In contrast, geological records show that continental arcs rapidly formed along circum-supercontinent passive margins shortly prior to the breakup of Rodinia and Pangea, indicating successful subduction initiation and an evolving supercontinent cycle. Thus, it requires an additional mechanism for subduction initiation along circum-supercontinent passive margins beyond self-organizing mantle flow. Here, we propose a new mechanism for subduction initiation at the passive margin before supercontinent breakup, based on geological records and the recent finding that the cratonic lithospheric mantle comprises a buoyant upper layer, a weak mid-lithospheric discontinuity, and a dense lower layer. We demonstrate that perturbations, such as plume underplating or melt infiltration, could initiate delamination of the dense lower cratonic mantle lithosphere, while the remaining buoyant continent uplifts, weakening the nearby passive margin and decoupling the continental and oceanic lithosphere. Eventually, the enhanced density contrast across the former passive margin leads to the formation of a new ocean-continent subduction zone. We suggest that this new subduction initiation mechanism is a key driver of the periodic operation of supercontinent cycles, modulating Earth’s long-term tectonic evolution.

papers.t: Exact solutions produce a full picture of crack behavior in dynamic fracture
papers.j: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
in: Center for Nonlinear Dynamics, Department of Physics, The University of Texas at Austin
tk: This study uses particle-level exact analytical solutions to show that stable tensile cracks can exceed shear wave speeds, driven by dissipation and weak interfaces.
该研究利用粒子级精确解析解，表明耗散和微弱界面可促使稳定的张裂纹超剪切波速传播。
papers.ab: The theory of fracture normally describes cracks as propagating discontinuities in a continuous medium where stresses vanish on free crack faces. We describe cracks instead at the particle level and obtain more general analytical results than were available previously. Using dynamical crack solutions for widely varying dissipation and general isotropic elastic moduli, we construct a catalog of 100,000 crack solutions and from it a general picture of when cracks are stable. For our exactly solvable model of dynamic fracture, the surface wave speed sometimes sets an upper limit on crack velocity, as expected. However tensile cracks traveling faster than the shear wave speed are possible and their stability is enhanced when they travel along weak interfaces, when dissipation increases, and when system sizes are small. Our results reinforce a standard view that supersonic cracks require supersonic energy transport near the tip, but we show it can come from dissipation as well as hyperelasticity.

papers.t: The influence of a long-lived basal magma ocean on the coupled core-mantle evolution of Mars
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
Southern University of Science and Technology
Institute of Earth Sciences, Academia Sinica
Academia Sinica
ETH Zurich
Institute of Geophysics
tk: A long-lived basal magma ocean on Mars regulates core-mantle heat exchange, suppressing core cooling and inhibiting inner-core growth while promoting present-day mantle plumes.
火星底部岩浆洋调节核幔热交换，抑制内核生长并促进地幔柱活动。
papers.ab: Recent seismic observations suggest the presence of a basal molten layer above the Martian core that may represent a long-lived basal magma ocean (BMO). However, its influence on the coupled thermal evolution of the Martian mantle and core remains poorly understood. Here, we employ a two-dimensional mantle convection model coupled with parameterized thermal evolution models for the core and BMO to investigate the long-term interior evolution of Mars. Our results show that a long-lived BMO modifies core-mantle thermal coupling by regulating heat exchange between the core and mantle and maintaining elevated temperatures in the lowermost mantle. In particular, enrichment of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the BMO enhances deep interior heat retention, suppresses secular core cooling, inhibits inner-core growth, and promotes present-day mantle plume activity. We further find that reconciling a long-lived BMO with a present-day solid inner core requires both limited enrichment of HPEs within the BMO and relatively high core liquidus temperatures, which may be difficult to satisfy simultaneously. These results offer constraints on the thermal and magnetic evolution of Mars and highlight the importance of coupled mantle-BMO-core dynamics on Mars.

papers.t: Barriers, conduits, and seismic sources: Faults in subsurface CO₂ storage across scales
in: Heriot-Watt University, Research Avenie S, Edinburgh, EH1444AS, United Kingdom [GB]
State Supervision of Mines, Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy, Unknown, The Hague, Netherlands [NL]
Heriot-Watt University, Unknown, Edinburgh, United Kingdom [GB]
Newcastle University, Ridley Building, Newcastle upon Tyne, NE1 7RU, United Kingdom [GB]
Heriot-Watt University Institute of GeoEnergy Engineering, Unknown, Edinburgh, United Kingdom [GB]
Universiteit Utrecht, 4 Princetonianlaan, ESL, Utrecht, Netherlands [NL]
Heriot-Watt University, Unknown, Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom [GB]
Heriot-Watt University, Research Avenue S, Edinburgh, EH14 4AS, United Kingdom [GB]
tk: Synthesizes fault behavior in subsurface CO₂ storage, reviewing sealing capacity, leakage pathways, and induced seismicity mechanisms across multiple operational projects.
综述了地下二氧化碳封存中的断层封闭性、泄漏与诱发地震机制。
papers.ab: Geological CO 2 storage is transitioning from demonstration to industrial-scale deployment, and faults within and around storage complexes exert a first-order control on its safety and performance. Faults can compartmentalise reservoirs through across-fault sealing, provide pathways for vertical migration of CO 2 and brine across caprocks, and host induced seismicity when reactivated by pore-pressure, thermal and geochemical changes during and after injection. These behaviours are not independent in the sense that the same fault can seal hydraulically while remaining critically stressed, or slip without becoming transmissive, and its state can evolve over engineering to geological timescales. We synthesise structural geology, fault-seal analysis, geomechanics, geochemistry, modelling and the operational record from projects including Sleipner, In Salah, Decatur, Quest, Snøhvit, Aquistore and Gorgon. No measurable fault-related leakage from a storage complex has been documented at any saline-aquifer or depleted-gas-field project. Microseismicity on unmapped sub-seismic and basement structures is recurrent, and in 2026 two events above M L 4.0 near Quest became the first felt events at a storage project, provisionally attributed to injection and without effect on containment. Because the pressure and stress perturbation extends far beyond the CO 2 plume, the faults that host seismicity commonly lie beneath or outside the storage complex and loading there can peak after injection stops. We review across-fault sealing proxies and their CO 2 -specific uncertainty, fault-fracture network controls on leakage, induced-seismicity mechanisms, natural analogues, regulatory frameworks and post-injection behaviour, and identify five priority data classes and the coupled workflows needed to convert them into defensible risk envelopes.

papers.t: Structure-aware Bayesian full waveform inversion via diffusion-regularized Stein variational gradient descent
tk: This paper integrates a learned diffusion model as an implicit prior within Stein variational gradient descent to improve structural realism and uncertainty quantification in Bayesian FWI.
本文将扩散模型作为隐式先验引入变分梯度下降，提高了贝叶斯全波形反演的结构真实性与不确定性量化能力。
papers.ab: Full waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful tool for high-resolution subsurface model reconstruction, but it remains highly nonlinear and ill-posed, especially when the initial model is inaccurate or the acquired data are noisy and incomplete. Annealed Stein variational gradient descent (ASVGD) provides a particle-based Bayesian framework for FWI by approximating the posterior distribution with an ensemble of velocity models, thereby enabling uncertainty quantification beyond a single deterministic solution. However, conventional ASVGD-FWI commonly relies on simple handcrafted priors, such as Gaussian or smoothing assumptions, which are often insufficient to represent complex geological structures. To address this limitation, we introduce a learned diffusion model (DM) as an implicit regularization mechanism within the ASVGD-FWI framework. Instead of explicitly evaluating the diffusion prior density, the trained diffusion model acts as a learned geological projection operator that guides updated particles toward the distribution of plausible velocity models. In this way, the proposed method combines data consistency from FWI, posterior diversity from ASVGD, and structural realism from the diffusion prior. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the diffusion-regularized ASVGD-FWI produces more geologically consistent mean models, suppresses nonphysical artifacts, and yields uncertainty estimates that are more concentrated around structurally complex and poorly constrained regions. These results suggest that learned diffusion priors can effectively enhance Bayesian FWI by improving both inversion stability and the interpretability of posterior uncertainty.

papers.t: Multivariate phase-space interpretation of ensemble forecasts: A comparison of physical and AI models
tk: A phase-space framework compares physical and AI ensemble weather forecasts, showing that their uncertainty subspaces do not fully overlap despite similar error-representation performance.
该研究利用相空间框架对比了物理和AI天气预报集合，发现两者不确定性子空间未完全重合。
papers.ab: Ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF's Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-ENS) are compared using a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Within this framework, the uncertainty is interpreted as the linear subspace spanned by the ensemble members in phase space, from which various geometric properties are extracted. As revealed by the analysis, the error does not entirely lie in this subspace, but is reasonably well calibrated in all directions. Moreover, the framework allows to quantify that this subspace critically depends on the number of ensemble members, suggesting that the current setups only partially represent the uncertainty subspace. This phase-space interpretation furthermore allows a direct comparison of the error-representation patterns of AIFS-ENS and IFS by computing the principal angles between the subspaces: IFS and AIFS ensemble subspaces do not entirely overlap in phase space, even though they were shown to have similar abilities to represent the amplitude and the structure of the error.

papers.t: Global Structure-Constrained 4D prestack inversion
tk: The paper proposes a global 4D prestack seismic inversion method using multi-dimensional matrix multiplication and structural constraints to improve stability.
提出基于多维矩阵乘法和结构约束的全局四维叠前地震反演方法。
papers.ab: Prestack seismic inversion often suffers from inherent ill-posedness and is significantly affected by complex factors such as the wavelets, parameter coupling, heterogeneous media, fault displacements, and stratigraphic variations, making it difficult for the conventional inversion methods to accurately recover subsurface information. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a global inversion method based on multi-dimensional matrix multiplication to optimize the inversion results under structure constraints. This method first represents the inversion model as a four-dimensional tensor representing spatial and parameter dimensions. By performing multi-dimensional matrix multiplication operations in various directions of the model, a multi-dimensional tensor of observed data is effectively constructed. Secondly, multi-dimensional regularization are introduced. By analyzing the impact of different dimensional constraints on the inversion results, targeted parameter selection and adjustment are achieved, significantly enhancing the stability of the inversion process and effectively suppressing noise. Finally, stratigraphic and fault constraints extracted from seismic interpretation are incorporated to improve the geological coherence and reasonableness of the inversion results. Both synthetic and field data experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances the robustness of inversion in complex structural areas while maintaining high computational efficiency, validating its effectiveness in practical applications.

papers.t: Planar intrusions from a narrow, jet-like source in a linearly stratified ambient
tk: Direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions in stratified fluids reveal a three-phase evolution and show how three-dimensional mixing near the source enhances the effective volume flux.
线性分层介质中窄源平面侵入体的数值模拟揭示了其三阶段演化及三维混合效应。
papers.ab: We present two and three dimensional direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions injected from a continuously supplied, narrow source into a linearly stratified ambient at the level of neutral buoyancy. The evolution passes through three phases. A laminar leading vortex dipole first advances at constant speed with a varicose wave train behind it; the trailing jet then undergoes a sinuous instability whose initial growth rate and wavelength agree with inviscid unstratified planar-jet theory evaluated on the local jet; the flow finally relaxes into a buoyancy-controlled wedge whose area grows linearly in time. Three-dimensional simulations show that the transition remains organized by the planar instability, while three-dimensionality reshapes the near-source region into a slowly evolving, actively mixing zone that entrains an additional twenty to one hundred percent of the source flux depending on source width. Rescaled with this measured effective flux, the downstream intrusion collapses reasonably well onto the similarity solution for a wide-source intrusion.

papers.t: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
in: Stanford University
Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology
Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University
Kagawa University
RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project
Kyoto University
tk: This study uses Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to estimate heterogeneous fault friction and model spatio-temporal slip during the 2010 Bungo slow slip event.
本研究利用物理信息神经网络估算非均匀断层摩擦，并模拟了2010年丰后水道慢滑移事件的时空演化。
papers.ab: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan.

papers.t: A Multi-frame Analysis of Flow Reversal in Tidal Bore
tk: This study uses PIV and SPH simulations to show that tidal bore flow reversal classification depends heavily on the chosen frame of reference.
本研究通过PIV和SPH模拟表明，涌潮流量反转的分类很大程度上取决于所选的参考系。
papers.ab: A tidal bore is a nonlinear step like surge propagating on the top of a river counter-current. The scientific literature reports that the passage of the tidal front may induce local flow reversals and, in some cases, a global reversal of the river current. Here, combining Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) measurements and 2D numerical simulations based on a Weakly Compressible Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (WCSPH) method, we show that the flow classification of tidal bores must explicitly take into account the frame of reference. When the river flow does not reverse after the bore passing, this is a consequence of the perspective imposed by the background current (itself resulting from the previous tide and the natural river discharge toward the sea). Depending on the relative magnitudes of the river current and the velocity field induced by the bore, one may observe a global reversal, a local reversal (or both), or no reversal at all. When the tide is spatially inhomogeneous, with a tidal range that varies along the estuary rather than a simple step in water depth, transitions between bore types may occur during the bore passing.

papers.t: Along-strike stress delays the ordering of slip on a fixed-length fault
tk: Idealized 2D dynamic rupture simulations show that along-strike stress variations delay the time at which final earthquake slip order is established.
二维动力学破裂模拟表明，沿走向的应力变化会延迟最终地震滑动量顺序的确定。
papers.ab: The size of a large earthquake depends on how far the rupture runs and how much the fault slips. An early correlation with magnitude can appear while those two contributions are still mixed. Patches at both ends stop every rupture on a 120 km fault, so the length no longer varies and the early order is an order of slip. One background stress is a single value along the fault, and the other also varies along strike. Slip at 20 s is ordered by 2 s for 259 ruptures in the first case, and by 8 s (7-9 s) for 230 ruptures in the second. The extra seconds are not a slower rupture front. Where the stress varies along strike, stations beside the fault and around it show that order when the waves arrive. Stations ahead of the rupture do not lead the waves, and where the stress is one value, stations around the fault are later than the waves. The calculations are an idealized two-dimensional dynamic simulation, with one friction law and no field record.

papers.t: Event-Centric Earthquake Monitoring with a Multi-Station Transformer
tk: EQNet2 is a geometry-aware multi-station Transformer that jointly performs phase picking, association, location, and magnitude estimation, improving earthquake catalog completeness.
EQNet2是一种几何感知的多台站Transformer，可联合进行震相拾取、关联、定位和震级估计。
papers.ab: Earthquake catalogs underpin studies such as fault structure, earthquake processes and seismic hazard, and their value depends on being both complete and reliable. Machine learning has improved individual tasks of earthquake monitoring, but processing stations independently discards the consistency of arrivals across the network, and running tasks in sequence fragments the information describing each earthquake. We present EQNet2, a geometry-aware multi-station Transformer that jointly predicts phase arrivals, first-motion polarities, source location and magnitude, and the association of arrivals into events. On a Northern California test dataset and on continuous waveforms from Ridgecrest and the San Francisco Bay Area, EQNet2 recovers more weak arrivals, produces fewer false detections, and associates more picks into located events. Its learned attention links information across stations along time--distance patterns consistent with seismic moveout. As seismic networks grow denser, exploiting multi-station coherence and event-centric prediction offers a path to more complete and reliable catalogs.

papers.t: Evaluating Dynamic Viability of Finite-Fault Slip Models with Ensemble Kalman Inversion
tk: Couples Ensemble Kalman Inversion with 3D dynamic rupture simulations to evaluate the physical viability of finite-fault slip models, applied to the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake.
将集成卡尔曼反演与三维动态破裂模拟相结合，评估有限断层滑动模型的物理可行性。
papers.ab: Finite-fault slip models are widely used to infer earthquake rupture processes, yet they are inherently non-unique and do not guarantee physically consistent rupture evolution. Here, we develop a data-constrained framework that couples Ensemble Kalman Inversion (EKI) with large-scale 3D dynamic rupture simulations to efficiently evaluate the dynamic viability of finite-fault slip models. The framework explores initial shear stress conditions informed by slip models while constraining dynamic rupture scenarios with geodetic observations and the teleseismic moment-rate function. Applying this approach to 32 models of the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake, we identify 26 dynamically viable 3D rupture scenarios using $\sim$285 total forward simulations. Across the ensemble, both smooth and highly heterogeneous finite-fault slip models can be reproduced dynamically. Yet these models converge to three dynamic rupture families, characterized by crack-like, single-reactivation, or multiple-reactivation rupture styles. This convergence suggests that apparent finite-fault diversity may reflect a smaller set of dominant controls on rupture dynamics, including the level of prestress heterogeneity. Multiple-reactivation dynamic rupture models best reproduce the observed depth-dependent rupture behavior and moment-rate complexity. By contrast, large tsunamigenic slip near the trench and comparable partitioning of released strain energy between breakdown and radiated energy persist across dynamically viable models, despite differences in initial shear stress conditions and rupture style. These results show that finite-fault slip model heterogeneity can map onto a smaller set of dynamically viable rupture styles, preserving robust first-order features. Our EKI framework provides an efficient pathway for integrating observations with physics-based simulations and identifying dynamically consistent earthquake source models.

papers.t: Rapid Epicentral Distance and Magnitude Estimation via Collaborative Attention Network
in: Key Laboratory of Earthquake Engineering and Engineering Vibration, Institute of Engineering Mechanics, China Earthquake Administration, Harbin, China
Key Laboratory of Earthquake Disaster Mitigation, Ministry of Emergency Management, Harbin, China
Department of Security Products, HeNan Splendor Science & Technology Co., Ltd., Zhengzhou, China
tk: EEWCAN uses a collaborative attention network to rapidly estimate epicentral distance and magnitude from single-station seismic waveforms for earthquake early warning.
EEWCAN利用协同注意力网络，通过单台地震波形快速估计震中距和震级。
papers.ab: Rapid and reliable estimation of epicentral distance and magnitude are pivotal for damage assessment in earthquake early warning (EEW). However, conventional epicentral distance and magnitude estimation approaches for EEW rely primarily on manually defined features to construct empirical prediction equations. Meanwhile, many existing machine learning models focus solely on single tasks (either epicentral distance or magnitude estimation alone), neglecting the correlation and impact between epicentral distance and magnitude. In this study, we design a collaborative attention network (CAN) framework for EEW, named EEWCAN, which combines global and local attention mechanisms. In addition, we explore the feasibility of EEWCAN for estimating epicentral distance and magnitude from single-station data in the Japan region. EEWCAN integrates global and local attention mechanisms to automatically capture more critical features pertinent to epicentral distance and magnitude from seismic waveforms. The EEWCAN framework is composed of two models: the EEWCAN-Dis model for epicentral distance estimation and the EEWCAN-Mag model for magnitude estimation. Meanwhile, the epicentral distance estimated by the EEWCAN-Dis model is incorporated into the EEWCAN-Mag model. We trained and tested EEWCAN using seismic events recorded by the Kyoshin network in Japan, with waveforms serving as the input to EEWCAN. The test results demonstrate that, when data from 3 s after P-wave onset are used, EEWCAN can obtain reliable estimates of epicentral distance and magnitude, outperforming the baseline models. Furthermore, by incorporating the estimated epicentral distance information, EEWCAN enhances the reliability of magnitude estimation. This result demonstrates that our proposed method can provide a certain degree of reliability for epicentral distance and magnitude estimation in EEW.

papers.t: Reassessment of Focal Depths of Shallow Moderate-Sized Earthquakes in Mariana Subduction Zone with Short-Period Rayleigh-Wave Amplitude Spectra
in: Key Laboratory of Ocean Observation and Forecasting, Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Qingdao, China
Laboratory of Marine Geology and Environment, Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Qingdao, China
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China
Innovation Academy for Precision Measurement Science and Technology, China Academy of Sciences, Wuhan, China
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geodynamics and Geohazards, School of Earth Sciences and Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, China
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China
tk: Reassesses focal depths of shallow moderate earthquakes in the Mariana subduction zone using short-period Rayleigh-wave amplitude spectra, revealing significant catalog discrepancies.
利用短周期雷利波振幅谱重新评估马里亚纳俯冲带浅源中强地震的震源深度。
papers.ab: Focal depths provide vital information for seismogenic mechanisms and tectonic structures. Because of sparse seismic stations in the Mariana subduction zone, accurately determining the focal depth of shallow earthquakes is challenging. The amplitude spectra of short-period Rayleigh waves are highly depth sensitive and are applicable at local and regional distances with sparse seismic station coverage. In this study, we collect seismic data at local and regional distances in the Mariana region, and then use the optimal period of short-period Rayleigh-wave amplitude spectra to determine the depths of shallow moderate-sized earthquakes. The difference between our resolved depths and the Incorporated Research Institutions for Seismology (IRIS) results ranges from −12.5 to 17.5 km, whereas the difference between our resolved depths and the Global Centroid Moment Tensor (Global CMT) depths has a range of −7.5 to 12.5 km. To further verify the estimated source depth, we used depth phase modeling to constrain the source depth of the largest Mw 5.9 earthquake. The result of depth phase modeling (27.9 ± 0.3 km) is slightly larger than the depth of 24.4 ± 1.4 km using the optimal period method. In comparison, the estimated depth is quite different from the fixed values of 10 and 12 km in the IRIS and Global CMT catalogs, respectively. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this approach on shallow offshore earthquakes and the need to reassess the depth of earthquakes in the Mariana subduction zone.
