papers.ab: The North-Anatolian Fault (NAF) in the Sea of Marmara is characterized by varying mechanical behaviours and fluid manifestations along its path. In this study, we investigate an earthquake sequence including a Mw 4.6 earthquake that occurred on 2013 November 27 in the partially creeping section of the NAF in the Sea of Marmara. Using onshore and offshore seismic data from 2013 October to 2014 August, we document a sequence of highly similar events prior to this earthquake, occurring within a zone where repeating earthquakes, likely indicative of creep, have been previously identified. This sequence coincides with the recently proposed existence of a several months-long slow-slip event (SSE) propagating westwards along the main fault trace at a rate of ∼0.5 km d−1, based on the interpretation of onshore geodetic data and offshore surface sediment pore pressure data. The timings of a multiplet (i.e. highly similar events), mainshock and decreases in pore pressure measured within the fault valley are compatible with the hypothesis that the SSE impacted first the multiplet-mainshock sequence and then the subseafloor hydrological network within the fault valley. Models of the SSE as a slipping patch propagating westwards with a combination of right-lateral slip and tensile opening, show an increase in Coulomb stress of a few tenths of kPa at the position of the mainshock sequence. Despite limited calculated Coulomb stress transfer due to the SSE, our observations suggest that complex hydromechanical interactions exist between splay faults, such as those where the mainshock occurred, and the main NAF, and underline the interest of using multidisciplinary data to study relationships between fluids and fault deformation.

papers.t: Earthquakes and cluster dynamics during interseismic phases between the Northern and Central Apennines (Italy)
in: Dipartimento di Geoscienze, Università degli Studi di Padova , 35131 Padova ,
tk: Relocated seismicity and cluster analysis in the Apennines reveal that interseismic deformation is accommodated by a low-angle seismogenic layer and aseismic processes, influenced by crustal rheology.
亚平宁山脉间震期地震重定位与群集分析揭示了受地壳流变性控制的低角度地震带及无震滑动过程。
papers.ab: In the last 30 yr, the Northern and Central Apennines (Italy) have been affected by three main destructive seismic sequences: the 1997 Colfiorito (three events ML > 5.5), the 2009 L’Aquila (one event ML > 5.5) and the 2016–2017 Amatrice–Visso–Norcia (three events ML > 5.5). Several studies have analysed the spatiotemporal evolution and processes driving each sequence, focused more on the foreshock–main shock–aftershocks dynamics. Here, we focus on the 2018–2024 interseismic period, aiming to unravel the long-term seismogenic behaviour of this region. We first relocated the earthquake catalogue and identified clusters through a declustering algorithm. During this phase, background seismicity and most of the clusters were arranged in a 2–3 km thick low- angle layer. We found that (i) most clusters were driven by an aseismic process, (ii) the depth of both clusters and seismicity layer increased toward the southeast, (iii) the volume of clusters decreases to the southeast, (iv) the low-angle layer almost disappeared in the L’Aquila area. Comparing two interseismic phases (2011–2016 and 2018–2024), we found striking similarities with events occurring on same sites and characterized by both foreshock–main shock–aftershocks and swarm-like behaviour. In addition to this, the L’Aquila area was seismically more ‘silent’ compared to the norther sites during both interseismic phases. We propose that these different long-term seismogenic behaviours may reflect variation in the structure and rheology of the upper crust moving from the Northern to the Central Apennines. This highlights the important role of the structural inheritance in controlling how the active deformation can affect the interseismic period.

papers.t: Extensional tectonics and magma-driven seismicity across the Santorini–Amorgos basins, south-central Aegean Sea: insights from the 2025 earthquake swarm
in: Department of Geophysical Engineering, The Faculty of Mines, Istanbul Technical University, ITU Ayazağa Campus , Maslak 34469, Sarıyer, İstanbul ,
Department of Geophysical Engineering, Kocaeli University , Izmit 41001, Kocaeli ,
ALomax Scientific 320 Chemin des Indes , 06370, Mouans-Sartoux ,
Disaster Management Institute, İstanbul Technical University, ITU Ayazağa Campus , Maslak 34469, Sarıyer, İstanbul ,
tk: The 2025 Santorini-Amorgos earthquake swarm was driven by a NW-SE extensional tectonic regime and magma/fluid-induced tensile fracturing, as revealed by relocated seismicity and moment-tensor inversions.
2025年圣托里尼-阿莫尔戈斯地震群由西北-东南向伸展构造和岩浆/流体诱发的张裂隙机制共同驱动。
papers.ab: We examined source characteristics of the recent earthquake sequence that occurred in February 2025 between the volcanic fields of Santorini, Kolumbo, Anydros and Amorgos in south-central Aegean. This region lies within the volcanic back-arc domain of the Hellenic subduction zone in the Aegean Sea. During this period, the area experienced intense seismic activity (ten earthquakes 5.0 < Mw < 5.5), with earthquake magnitudes generally increasing towards Amorgos Island. The largest event was the Mw 5.4 earthquake on 2025 February 10, located northeast of Santorini. In this study, we first obtained 4869 earthquakes that occurred between 2024 January 2 and 2025 March 23. We then derived full moment-tensor (MT) solutions for 30 earthquakes (Mw ≥ 4.5) by inverting seismological data sets. In addition, principal stress orientations were calculated by stress tensor inversion to recognize the most recent crustal stress field in the region. The spatio-temporal distribution of the relocated aftershocks indicates that the seismic activity initiated beneath the Santorini and Kolumbo volcanic centres, and subsequently migrated northeastward towards Anydros and Amorgos. Most earthquakes occurred at shallow crustal depths of approximately 5–15 km. Stress-inversion results and the orientation of T-axes highlight a dominant NW–SE extensional regime that characterizes the combined effects of deep geodynamic processes and shallow crustal dynamics in the back-arc area of the Aegean. The full MT solutions reveal predominantly normal, oblique-normal and strike-slip faulting mechanisms, accompanied by significant non-double-couple (non-DC) components. These non-DC signatures strongly suggest tensile processes that are likely related to magma intrusion, fluid migration or hydraulic fracturing. We therefore conclude that the 2025 seismic sequence was largely driven by crack-opening mechanisms and fluid- or magma-induced activity within the crust, consistent with the broader structural framework and volcanic nature of the Santorini–Amorgos region. Overall, this study enhances our knowledge on tectonic characteristics of the 2025 Santorini–Amorgos earthquake activity, which is significant for evaluating and monitoring the potential hazards in the south-central Aegean region.

papers.t: High-resolution volcanic tremor localization via MLE-based iterative peeling interferometry
in: College of Artificial Intelligence, China University of Petroleum (Beijing) , Beijing 102249 ,
State Key Laboratory of Petroleum Resources and Engineering, CNPC Key Laboratory of Geophysical Prospecting, China University of Petroleum (Beijing) , Beijing 102249 ,
DER/CERENA, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa , Lisboa 1049-001 ,
China—Portugal Joint Research Institute of Climate and Energy, China University of Petroleum (Beijing) , Beijing 102249 ,
tk: An MLE-based iterative peeling interferometry method improves volcanic tremor localization resolution by adaptively whitening and sequentially stripping source responses.
提出一种基于最大似然估计的迭代剥离干涉成像方法，显著提升了火山震颤定位的空间分辨率。
papers.ab: Accurate source localization is critical for monitoring volcanic tremors, microseismic events and earthquakes. Compared to other source localization algorithms, waveform-based interferometric imaging exhibits superior robustness. It proves particularly effective when confronting weak signal phase signatures, noise interference and inaccurate velocity models. Despite shared methodological commonalities, high-resolution imaging and localization of volcanic tremors prove notably more challenging than other passive seismic tasks. This difficulty primarily arises from sparse monitoring networks, complex wavefield interactions with the subsurface and the indistinct phase signatures inherent in tremor signals. Consequently, waveform-based interferometric imaging tends to suffer from more severe blurring effects (i.e. poorer spatial resolution) when applied to volcanic tremor localization and compared against other application fields. To address these resolution limitations, we propose a maximum likelihood estimation-based iterative peeling interferometric imaging method. This approach synergizes the inherent noise robustness of interferometry with a rigorous iterative framework designed to deblur the source image. By constructing data-driven empirical wavelets and employing an adaptive whitening filter dynamically updated via the Sherman–Morrison formula, the method sequentially strips source responses from the residual wavefield. This adaptive procedure directly counters the energy smearing caused by sparse arrays, effectively suppressing sidelobe interference to achieve a highly focused source resolution. Synthetic tests based on the Katla scenario demonstrate that the proposed method yields significantly higher spatial resolution than existing techniques. Furthermore, it exhibits robust performance even under adverse array geometries, concurrent multisource interference and velocity model inaccuracies. Field application to the 2011 Katla data further validates this by recovering source locations consistent with known ice cauldrons.

papers.t: Addressing InSAR long wavelength errors enhances the reliability of GNSS and InSAR combined 3-D deformation estimation: methodology and application to the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake
in: Faculty of Geosciences and Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University , 611756
School of Geomatics and Urban Spatial Information, Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture , 100044
tk: A new combined adjustment model integrates GNSS and InSAR data while correcting for InSAR long-wavelength errors, significantly improving 3D co-seismic deformation estimates.
提出一种结合GNSS和InSAR的新平差模型，通过修正长波段误差显著提高了三维同震形变估计精度。
papers.ab: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) deformation measurements are susceptible to long wavelength errors, yet existing geometric and strain models for estimating 3-D deformation from combined Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and InSAR observations do not explicitly account for these errors. Neglecting long wavelength errors can substantially bias 3-D deformation estimates for large earthquakes. We therefore develop a combined adjustment model that introduces additional systematic parameters to represent InSAR long wavelength errors, defines these parameters using GNSS minimum constraints and optimizes the stochastic model of the heterogeneous observations through least-squares variance component estimation. We evaluate the model using synthetic tests and observations of the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake. In the synthetic tests, the proposed model constrained the datum deviation to below 1 mm, whereas the corresponding mean datum deviations obtained using the geometric and strain models were 5.40 and 3.80 m, respectively. Relative to the design values, compared with the geometric and strain models, the proposed model reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) for the East (E) and North (N) components by 98.63 per cent and 98.84 per cent, 93.65 per cent and 96.45 per cent, respectively. This indicates that the proposed model can effectively eliminate the interference of long wavelength errors on the 3-D deformation parameter estimation. We further applied the proposed model to the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake and compared the resulting deformation with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) coseismic displacement solution. Compared with the geometric and strain models, the proposed model reduces the MAE for the E, N and U components by 89.32 per cent and 89.27 per cent, 83.33 per cent and 85.25 per cent, 37.50 per cent and 82.14 per cent, respectively. Under the adopted fault geometric parameters, the proposed model also recovered candidate strike-slip components that were not resolved by the conventional models. Compared with the geometric and strain models, the proposed model reduces the MAE between forward modelled and JPL coseismic displacements for the E and N components by 98.36 per cent and 98.01 per cent, 95.45 per cent and 94.59 per cent, respectively. Overall, explicitly estimating InSAR long wavelength errors within a combined adjustment framework improves the numerical and physical reliability of GNSS-InSAR 3-D deformation estimation.

papers.t: Seismological constraints on subduction and suture zone architecture in the Central African Copperbelt
in: Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oxford , Oxford, OX1 3AN ,
Department of Earth Sciences, University of Durham , Durham, DH1 3LE ,
School of Earth Sciences, University of Bristol , Bristol, BS8 1RJ ,
Geological Survey Department, Ministry of Mines , Lusaka, P.O Box 31969 ,
tk: Joint inversion of receiver functions and surface waves reveals underthrusting of the Congo Craton beneath the Kalahari plate and lithospheric metasomatism beneath the Central African Copperbelt.
接收函数与面波联合反演揭示了刚果克拉通向萨拉哈里板块下方的俯冲及交代岩石圈特征。
papers.ab: Central Africa marks a major collisional zone of the Pan-African Orogeny, involving convergence of the Congo and Kalahari plates during Gondwana assembly ($\sim$600–500 Ma). This collision formed the Lufilian Belt and one of the world’s most significant metallogenic provinces—the Central African Copperbelt. However, the deep lithospheric architecture underpinning this mineral-rich region remains poorly understood. Fundamental questions persist regarding the role of subduction, convergence polarity and suture-zone geometry. We address this using broad-band seismic data collected across Zambia’s Pan-African orogenic belts to construct a lithospheric shear-wave velocity model via joint inversion of receiver functions and surface waves. Common conversion point stacking of P-to-S receiver functions further enhances imaging of subsurface discontinuities. Our results reveal pronounced crustal deformation below the central Lufilian Belt, where the Moho is deepest ($\sim$48 km) and most gradational, marking the suture zone during continent-continent collision. Elsewhere, Moho architecture is shallower and uniform despite protracted convergence, suggesting lower-crustal flow accompanying orogenesis smoothed crustal thickness contrasts. At mantle depths, thick (160–180 km), homogeneously fast velocity (4.5–4.74 km s−1) lithosphere delineates the unmodified Congo Craton margin. Further south, thinner lithosphere (140–150 km) contains a pervasive mid-lithospheric low-velocity zone (4.3–4.4 km s−1) at 50–80 km depth, interpreted as metasomatically modified Proterozoic lithosphere rich in easily-fusible phases emplaced during Pan-African subduction. This contrast in mantle wave speeds, together with southward-dipping Moho geometry and intracrustal structure, indicates underthrusting of the Congo beneath the Kalahari Plate. The spatial coincidence of mantle metasomes and zones of crustal reworking with critical mineral occurrences across the Copperbelt highlights their role in creating favourable conditions for mineralization in overlying sedimentary basins.

papers.t: Three-dimensional crustal seismic structure of southern mainland Portugal from combined local earthquake and active source tomography
in: Instituto Dom Luiz (IDL), Faculdade de Ciências, Universidade de Lisboa , 1749-016 Lisboa ,
Instituto Superior de Ciências da Educação da Huíla (ISCED-Huíla) , 230 Lubango ,
Instituto Superior de Engenharia de Lisboa (ISEL), Instituto Politécnico de Lisboa , 1959-007 Lisboa ,
Department of Earth Sciences, University of Cambridge , CB3 0EZ, Cambridge ,
tk: Presents high-resolution 3D P- and S-wave crustal velocity models of southern Portugal using local earthquakes and active-source data, revealing strong correlations with Variscan tectonic structures.
利用地震与主动源数据构建了葡萄牙南部高分辨率三维地壳速度模型。
papers.ab: We present P- and S-wave seismic tomographic models for southern mainland Portugal, specifically for the region south of the 39° N parallel. These models were obtained using local seismicity and wide-angle refracted and reflected seismic profiles, considering a spatial resolution of approximately 10 km in latitude and longitude, and 3 km in depth, the highest spatial resolution so far compared to previous models of similar or broader regional scope. The aim is to improve the understanding of continental seismicity and to correlate seismic heterogeneities with crustal tectonic structures. For this purpose, the fast marching method was employed to solve the forward problem, while subspace inversion was used for the inverse problem, both implemented within the Fast Marching Tomography package (FMTOMO). The resulting tomographic model shows a segmented crust between upper, middle and lower. Some of the seismic structures show orientations consistent with Variscan tectonic features, generally following a northwest–southeast direction within the Ossa-Morena and South Portuguese Zone. Contacts between major geological units are discernible and well delineated in the model. Within the Ossa-Morena Zone, a negative velocity anomaly was identified which may be related to a possible fractured zone between the Boa Fé Shear Zone and Ciborro–Aldeia da Serra Fault. In the South Portuguese Zone, the most pronounced velocity contrast is associated with the syenite intrusion of the Monchique Massif in the southwest, characterized by a positive velocity anomaly, extending down to 20 km depth. To the southeast, seismic activity may be related to the Alcoutim and Ribeira do Vascão Faults. These structures impose a velocity anomaly suggesting that they are near-vertical faults extending to the top of the lower crust. A good correlation is observed between seismicity, seismic anomalies and regional geology.

papers.t: A four-dimensional spatiotemporal misfit function for waveform inversion of distributed acoustic sensing data
in: Faculty of Exact Sciences, Tel-Aviv University , Tel Aviv, 6997801 ,
tk: A new 4-D spatio-temporal misfit function for DAS waveform inversion suppresses shallow scattering to improve deep imaging and mitigate local minima.
提出一种适用于DAS的4D时空目标函数，通过抑制浅层散射改善深部成像并减少局部极小值。
papers.ab: Standard full-waveform inversion (FWI) objective functions often struggle to resolve deep structures when data are dominated by localized near-surface scattering. To address this, we develop a 4-D time-frequency-space-wavenumber (TFXK) objective function that explicitly enforces spatial coherence, leveraging the dense sampling of distributed acoustic sensing. We derive the corresponding adjoint sources for both phase and envelope misfits. By suppressing localized scattering from shallow heterogeneities, the TFXK misfit shifts kernel sensitivity toward deeper, larger scale structural targets. Furthermore, this 4-D mapping smooths the objective function topology, mitigating local minima while improving inversion convergence, as demonstrated in a 2-D synthetic FWI example with strong shallow heterogeneity. The proposed idea of a spatiotemporal objective function is generalizable and can be adapted to other objective functions. We also show how it can accommodate curved fibre geometries via arclength parametrization, Local polynomial Fourier transforms, or a full vectorial wavenumber approach, depending on the complexity of the fibre layout. These mathematical extensions are necessary for applying the method to varied fibre geometries and low-frequency inversions. The foundational principles of our approach extend beyond optical fibres and can also be applied to structural inversions using traditional dense nodal arrays.

papers.t: Bayesian inversion of rate-and-state parameters from stable velocity step experiments on Quartz Gouge close to instability
in: Mechanical and Civil Engineering Department, California Institute of Technology (Caltech) , Pasadena 91125 ,
Seismological Laboratory, California Institute of Technology (Caltech) , Pasadena 91125 ,
Rock Deformation Laboratory, Department of Earth and Ocean Sciences, University of Liverpool , Liverpool L69 3GP ,
tk: A Bayesian inversion framework is developed to accurately infer rate-and-state friction parameters and their uncertainties from stable velocity-step experiments on quartz gouge.
该研究开发了一个贝叶斯反演框架，用于准确推断石英断层泥稳定速度步进实验中的速率-状态摩擦参数及其不确定性。
papers.ab: Accurate determination of rate-and-state friction parameters from experiments is crucial for physics-based modelling of the earthquake source. In this study, we develop a Bayesian inversion framework based on a spring-slider model of the experiment to infer rate-and-state frictional properties from stable velocity-step experiments of a fine-grained quartz gouge that is close to instability. The inversion framework infers frictional parameters with superior precision to conventional methods based on nonlinear least squares. We identify that logarithmic sampling of the characteristic slip $D_{\rm RS}$ is an essential step for accurate inversion. Testing the same gouge material under the same effective normal stress but different pore pressure additionally shows that the presence of pressurized pore fluids changes the inferred rate-and-state properties of the gouge material by increasing rate-and-state parameters a, b and $D_{\rm RS}$. The Bayesian inversion framework provides a valuable tool for inferring accurately rate-and-state parameters of realistic gouge materials close to instability, with a small and quantifiable range of uncertainty in cases where the steady-state behaviour quantified by $a-b$ can be constrained independently. We also find that the steady-state friction properties evolve over the course of the experiment, adding additional uncertainty to the rate-and-state parameter estimates but not altering the conclusion about significant differences between the rate-and-state parameters in the presence of fluids.

papers.t: Insights from more than a year of ongoing episodic lava fountaining at Kīlauea
in: US Geological Survey, Hawaiian Volcano Observatory, Hilo, HI, USA.
US Geological Survey, Cascades Volcano Observatory, Vancouver, WA, USA.
US Geological Survey, California Volcano Observatory, Moffet Field, CA, USA.
US Geological Survey, Volcano Hazards Program, Vancouver, WA, USA.
University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo, Hilo, HI, USA.
Earth Sciences New Zealand, Natural Hazards and Resilience Platform, Lower Hutt, New Zealand.
University of Hawaiʻi at Manoa, Honolulu, HI, USA.
University of Oregon, Eugene, OR, USA.
tk: A multiparameter record of Kīlauea's episodic lava fountaining reveals systematic correlations with summit inflation, enabling quantitative eruption forecasting.
基拉韦厄火山喷泉的多参数记录揭示了其与山顶膨胀的系统相关性，实现了定量喷发预测。
papers.ab: Episodic lava fountaining is rare globally, with only three occurrences from Kīlauea (Hawaii) since 1823. Beginning in December 2024, an eruption within the summit crater, Halemaʻumaʻu, has produced 54 fountaining episodes to date, each lasting typically for hours and separated by days to weeks. Although multiple mechanisms have been proposed, fundamental questions remain about how magma reservoir pressure, conduit permeability, and volatile exsolution control fountaining onset. We present a multiparameter record of episodic fountaining at Kīlauea using modern geochemical, geophysical, and geologic monitoring. These observations revealed systematic correlations between fountaining and summit inflation, enabling unprecedented quantitative forecasts. This eruption will provide new constraints on the timing, evolution, and processes driving episodic fountaining globally, and highlights Kīlauea’s role as a natural laboratory for studying volcanic processes.

papers.t: Conformal prediction for earthquake early warning: finite-sample coverage guarantees for prediction intervals of peak ground acceleration
in: Department of Geology, Gyeongsang National University , Jinju 52828 ,
Department of Geophysics, Kangwon National University , Chuncheon 24341 ,
tk: Conformal prediction methods, specifically conformalized quantile regression, provide reliable, finite-sample coverage guarantees for peak ground acceleration prediction intervals in earthquake early warning.
利用合规预测为地震预警PGA预测区间提供有限样本覆盖保证。
papers.ab: Earthquake early warning requires reliable uncertainty estimates from short initial waveforms. We evaluate split conformal prediction (CP) and conformalized quantile regression (CQR) for single-station peak ground acceleration using event-partitioned K-NET records. Each 3 s waveform is normalized by component while retaining amplitude scales measured before normalization. The convolutional neural network (CNN)–Transformer that retains amplitude information is more accurate and yields narrower intervals than the waveform-only ablation. At the nominal 90 per cent level, CQR attains 90.03 per cent coverage; raw quantile regression and split CP are also near nominal, whereas heteroscedastic deep ensemble and MC-dropout baselines are more conservative and wider. Event-cluster bootstrap and repeated event-level resplits support marginal-coverage stability, although performance degrades for rare large earthquakes. Upper-bound screening trades increased recall for more false alarms, so the intervals are an uncertainty-quantification and screening layer rather than a standalone alert system. Under exact exchangeability, conformal prediction supplies finite-sample marginal coverage; record-level exchangeability is not established for this event-clustered sample and event-conditional reliability is not guaranteed.

papers.t: Depth estimation of shallow low-frequency tremor by inversion technique using differential traveltimes between ocean bottom seismometers
in: Research Center for Prediction of Earthquakes and Volcanic Eruptions, Graduate School of Science, Tohoku University , Sendai 9808578 ,
Earthquake Research Institute, The University of Tokyo , Tokyo 1130032 ,
Regional Cooperation and Disaster Mitigation Research Center, Miyazaki Municipal University , Miyazaki 8808520 ,
tk: A new OBS-based relocation framework constrains shallow tremor depths in the Hyuga-nada subduction zone without prior depth constraints.
利用海底地震仪差分走时成功重定位日向滩浅部低频微震。
papers.ab: Low-frequency tremors (LFTs) provide important constraints on the mechanical and hydrological conditions of subduction plate interfaces, yet their focal depth distributions remain challenging to be resolved compared to those of fast earthquakes. In this study, LFTs in the Hyuga-nada region are independently relocated using earthquake location techniques with traveltimes by converting cross-correlation–derived arrival-time delays into pseudo-arrival times for each single station, without imposing a priori depth constraints. The resulting hypocentre distribution reveals systematic spatial patterns that are robust across multiple observation periods. Hypocentre locations are determined through a multistage relocation procedure, in which an initial maximum-likelihood location incorporating station correction terms is followed by a double-difference relocation using a 3-D velocity model. Only events meeting stringent quality thresholds on converted arrival counts, azimuthal gap and initial hypocentral depth uncertainty are retained. Location uncertainties are quantified at each stage using a Bayesian framework and jackknife resampling, which respectively characterize the probabilistic confidence of the solution and its robustness against the influence of individual stations and potentially biased converted arrival times. These steps are iteratively applied to refine source parameters, thereby improving depth resolution and overall location stability. The relocated LFTs are predominantly concentrated at shallower depths than fast earthquakes and are distributed along the plate interface. Comparison with seismic reflection profiles indicates that LFTs are generally distributed in the vicinity of strong reflective interfaces along the plate boundary, supporting previous interpretations that associate LFTs with mechanically weak, fluid-rich layers. The relocated tremor locations further show a clear spatial correspondence with a subducted seamount inferred from magnetic anomaly data, consistent with mechanical and hydrological contrasts associated with seamount subduction, particularly along the downdip flank, which may reflect stronger compression and enhanced fluid drainage. These results demonstrate that LFTs in the Hyuga-nada region are strongly controlled by the plate interface and structural heterogeneity. The relocation framework presented here provides a unified basis for integrated analyses of fast and slow earthquake processes in subduction zones.

papers.t: Structure, deformation history and seismic hazard of the active Hutubi anticline at the deformation front of the Northern Tian Shan
in: National Field Observation and Research Station (Xinjiang Pamir) for Intracontinental Subduction, State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting, Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration , Beijing, 100029 ,
Urumqi Institute of Central Asia Earthquake, China Earthquake Administration , Urumqi, 830000 ,
China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute , Beijing, 100011 ,
Petroleum Engineering Technology Research Institute of Jiangsu Oilfield Company, SINOPEC , Jiangsu, 225100 ,
tk: Reconstructing the Hutubi anticline's growth history reveals accelerated late Quaternary shortening and shows how tectonic deformation and gas storage operations jointly drive seismic hazards.
重建呼图壁背斜生长历史揭示了晚第四纪缩短加速，并阐明了构造变形与储气库注采如何共同影响地震危险性。
papers.ab: Industrial activities in active foreland fold-and-thrust belts complicate conventional seismic hazard assessment, yet how tectonic deformation and industrial perturbations affect fault stability remains poorly understood. The Hutubi underground gas storage facility, situated within the Hutubi anticline at the deformation front of northern Tian Shan, has experienced a marked increase in seismicity since the start of gas injection and extraction. Here, we integrate seismic-reflection interpretation, growth strata analysis, geomorphic surface survey and optically stimulated luminescence dating, and area-depth-strain analysis to reconstruct the structure and growth history of the Hutubi anticline and quantify its late Quaternary shortening rate. The Hutubi anticline is a detachment fold growing above an 8–9 km-deep detachment. The shortening and uplift rates of the anticline have undergone a marked acceleration, rising from long-term averages of ∼0.06 and ∼0.03 mm yr−1 for the Pliocene–0.4 Ma period to ∼1.1 and ∼1.3 mm yr−1 since ∼0.4 Ma, respectively. This acceleration, consistent with other foreland structures, reflects ongoing basinward propagation of the Tian Shan deformation front in the late Quaternary. Within this tectonic setting, we further modelled the Coulomb stress evolution on secondary faults within the anticline driven by tectonic deformation. Our results indicate that tectonic deformation drives secondary faults to the seismic triggering threshold over a decade, and governs where ruptures nucleate and how they propagate, consistent with relocated earthquake observations in previous studies. Given sustained late Quaternary activity and pronounced injection-extraction perturbations, the potential for moderate-to-strong earthquakes (∼Mw 5.3–7.0) on these faults cannot be ignored in the future. Thus, in active tectonic regions, seismic hazard assessments must incorporate deformation rates to accurately evaluate tectonic deformation and industrial perturbation effects on fault stability.

papers.t: Probabilistic source-type classification from seismic moment tensors
in: NORSAR , NO-2007 Kjeller ,
tk: A probabilistic framework maps seismic moment tensor posteriors onto the fundamental lune to classify source types with explicit uncertainties.
该研究提出了一种基于矩张量后验分布的概率源类型分类框架，可定量评估分类不确定性。
papers.ab: Seismic source classification often relies on a single best-fitting moment tensor and deterministic rules on source-type diagrams. This study formulates classification directly in terms of the posterior distribution of the moment tensor on the fundamental lune. Moment tensors from waveform inversion are mapped into a uniform $(v,w)$ source-type domain and used to build empirical source-type probability density functions $p(v,w)$. We evaluate five hypotheses ($\pm \mathrm{ISO}_{\mathrm{CAL}}$, DC, $\pm$CLVD) plus a residual baseline, where $\mathrm{ISO}_{\mathrm{CAL}}$ denotes a calibrated isotropic (ISO) kernel relative to the canonical ISO endmember. Classification probabilities $P(H_i)$ are obtained by integrating $p(v,w)$ against the hypothesis kernels; a residual probability $P_{\mathrm{residual}}$ is included as a sixth baseline (uniform) model that absorbs probability when the posterior is diffuse or poorly matched by the prototypes. The framework is applied to published regional moment tensor ensembles for 32 events, including 23 nuclear tests at the Nevada National Security Site and the Punggye-Ri, North Korea, test site, plus nearby earthquakes and collapses. Well-recorded underground nuclear tests yield tightly localized +$\mathrm{ISO}_{\mathrm{CAL}}$ probabilities with small $P_{\mathrm{residual}}$, while events recorded by sparse, complex source-receiver paths show broader probability vectors and larger $P_{\mathrm{residual}}$. Tectonic earthquakes map primarily to double-couple (DC) and compensated linear vector dipole (CLVD) hypotheses, while collapses map primarily to negative ISO (–$\mathrm{ISO}_{\mathrm{CAL}}$), with secondary CLVD in some events. The method is applicable wherever source-type posteriors are available, given a declared hypothesis family, and produces explicit hypothesis probabilities with uncertainty and a residual diagnostic that flags diffuse or weakly matched posteriors, and can feed directly into monitoring and decision pipelines.

papers.t: Q M1D: A 1-D model of shear attenuation in the mantle from differential body waves
in: Department of Geosciences, Utrecht University , NL-3584 CB ,
Research School of Earth Sciences, The Australian National University , Canberra, ACT 0200 ,
tk: Introduces QM1D, a new 1D mantle shear attenuation model built from over 90,000 differential S-ScS measurements using Bayesian inversion.
基于超9万条差异衰减数据和贝叶斯反演构建地幔1D衰减模型QM1D。
papers.ab: We introduce a new 1-D model of shear attenuation in the mantle ($Q_{\text{M1D}}$) constructed from measurements of differential attenuation of S and ScS body waves. We build a data set of over 90 000 measurements of $\delta t^{*}_{\text{ScS-S}}$ from seismograms with high-quality S and ScS waveforms from deep earthquakes between 20° and 75$^\circ$ epicentral distance from 1990 to 2024. To ensure that measurements are robust, we require that values of differential attenuation are similar between the instantaneous frequency matching and waveform matching methods. Using this data set, we perform a Bayesian inversion to construct 1-D profiles of mantle shear quality factor $Q_\mu$ and its uncertainties. Our data set has a high sensitivity to the mid-mantle (660–2000 km) corresponding to the turning depths of the S phases, which maps into lower uncertainty in the ensemble distribution at these depths. $Q_{\text{M1D}}$ suggests that the mantle is more attenuating than PREM on average; but, notably, that there is a strongly attenuating layer around 750 km depth and that there are weakly attenuating layers around 900 and 2000 km depth. Due to the source–receiver distribution for the phases, our data set has a sampling bias in the mantle around the edge of the Pacific which may not be representative of the whole mantle. The weakly attenuating zones in the mantle may correspond to a viscosity jump around 900 km depth and a further viscosity jump in the deep mantle around 2000 km depth, whilst the thin strongly attenuating layer may correspond to regions of slab stagnation caused by a potential thin layer of low viscosity beneath the mantle transition zone in the circum-Pacific region.

papers.t: Amplitude source location for volcanic earthquakes using source location-dependent amplification corrections: application to Izu Oshima volcano, Japan
in: Department of Geophysics, Graduate School of Science, Tohoku University , Sendai 980-8578 ,
Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation, Geological Agency, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources , Bandung 40122 ,
tk: A new source location-dependent amplitude correction method improves the accuracy of amplitude source location (ASL) for volcanic earthquakes in highly heterogeneous media.
提出源位置相关振幅校正方法，显著提高火山地震定位精度。
papers.ab: The amplitude source location (ASL) method has been widely applied to volcanic earthquakes that do not show clear wave onsets at active volcanoes. To reduce the effects of shallow velocity structures just beneath seismic stations, observed amplitudes are generally corrected by using seismic coda waves of regional earthquakes. However, even using such amplitude corrections, ASL may not accurately locate the source of volcanic earthquakes occurring in a strongly heterogeneous medium in volcanic regions. To overcome this limitation, we propose a source location-dependent amplitude correction method and introduce seismic velocity structure with a vertical gradient. We analyse 339 volcanotectonic earthquakes (VTs) recorded by eight seismic stations deployed across the Izu Oshima volcano edifice. Reference hypocentres are determined from manually picked P- and S-wave arrival times and used to evaluate the performance of the proposed amplitude-based method. We divide the VT data set into two subsets, which are used as reference and test data sets. The amplification factors, which are the ratio of observed to predicted amplitudes of known VTs, are calculated for the reference data set. The amplification factors are further interpolated onto a 2-D grid using the ordinary kriging method with an exponential variogram model and then replicated at each depth level of the 3-D grid. Using interpolated source location–dependent amplification factors, we correct the observed amplitudes of VTs in the test data set and estimate the source locations by minimizing the amplitude residual in a grid search scheme. We use the 8–16 Hz frequency band, a velocity gradient k of 0.33 s−1 and v0 1.5 km s−1, and a constant attenuation factor (Q) of 50. The obtained source locations show good agreement with the locations determined from P- and S-wave onsets. Median misfits are approximately 1.1 and 1.0 km in the vertical and horizontal directions, respectively. Meanwhile, the median misfits from conventional ASL are approximately 2.2 km vertically and 2.3 km horizontally, with the estimated location concentrated close to the summit. These results demonstrate that our proposed method substantially improves relocation consistency and reduces summit-ward bias.

papers.t: Kinematic and Mechanical Heterogeneity Along the Xianshuihe Fault Zone from Nine Years of Continuous Seismicity and a Crustal Velocity Model
in: State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting, Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, People’s Republic of China
Key Laboratory of Intraplate Volcanoes and Earthquakes, China University of Geosciences (Beijing), Ministry of Education, Beijing, People’s Republic of China
University of Emergency Management, Langfang, Hebei, People’s Republic of China
Urumqi Institute of Central Asia Earthquake, China Earthquake Administration, Urumqi, Xinjiang, People’s Republic of China
Earth Observatory of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, U.S.A.
tk: Machine learning seismicity analysis and 3D velocity modeling reveal pronounced kinematic and mechanical segmentation along the Xianshuihe fault zone.
利用机器学习与速度反演揭示鲜水河断裂带力学分段及强震危险性。
papers.ab: The Xianshuihe fault zone (XSHF), a major strike-slip system on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, is one of the most seismically active structures in China. However, the relationship between its kinematics and long-term seismic behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we utilize continuous seismic data from 2014 to 2022, employing machine learning to detect 12,534 events, and invert for a regional 3D velocity model. We further derive a fault locking model from Global Navigation Satellite System data and systematically analyze spatiotemporal seismicity patterns and statistical features. Results reveal pronounced segmentation in seismicity along the northern XSHF. Along with low b values and a southward shallowing of seismogenic depths, locking constraints delineate two primary zones of enhanced locking north of the Bamei region, which are embedded within a northern fault segment that remains predominantly locked as a whole. In the Bamei–Kangding segment, a releasing bend concentrates seismicity along the western and southeastern faults, with marked spatial variations in b values. Velocity and resistivity structures indicate that the extensional environment of pull-apart basins facilitates deep melt upwelling. Overall, the northern XSHF is progressively entering a locked state, with potential for Mw 6.8+ earthquakes, whereas the Kangding segment structural assemblage modulates regional compressive and strike-slip stress loading. These constraints help clarify aspects of seismic behavior and deformation in intracontinental block-margin strike-slip systems and may inform regional seismic hazard assessment.

papers.t: Escaping Geological Generative Prior Distributions in Bayesian Travel Time Tomography
tk: A new Bayesian model-space inversion method uses generative neural network manifolds as guides to reconstruct geological features that lie outside the network's prior distribution.
提出一种新型贝叶斯模型空间反演方法，利用生成网络流形作为引导，成功重建先验分布之外的复杂地质特征。
papers.ab: Solutions to geophysical inverse problems are generally non-unique, and greatly benefit from additional geological prior information. Generative Neural Networks (GNNs) are commonly used to parametrise such information, typically restricting solutions to a lower-dimensional latent space. The final inversion result is obtained by mapping the latent space parameters to the original higher-dimensional model space using the GNNs. However, solutions then remain confined to a low-dimensional geological generative manifold; if the true Earth model lies outside of this manifold, standard latent space inversion fails. We propose a Bayesian model space inversion method that uses the generative manifold as a guide to find the solutions that lie outside this manifold. We validate our approach in non-linear travel-time tomography experiments on both simple and more geological structures. By comparing our method with model space inversion using uniform prior probabilities and standard latent-space inversion, we demonstrate that the less informative uniform prior fails to constrain the solution, while the latent space approach fails when the true Earth model lies outside of the generative manifold. Conversely, our new model-space inversion method successfully recovers complex off-manifold geological features while maintaining low solution uncertainty.

papers.t: Variational Derivation of the Weak Form for Viscous Flows Involving Free Surfaces with Implications for Geodynamic Simulations
tk: The paper presents a variational derivation of the weak form for viscous Stokes flows with free surfaces, mathematically justifying commonly used gravity stabilization terms.
该研究通过变分法推导了含自由表面粘性流的弱形式，为重力稳定化项提供了数学基础。
papers.ab: Geodynamic simulations involve solving the Stokes equations, where boundary conditions play a crucial role in governing internal dynamics and surface topography evolution. A common approach is to model the interface in contact with air as a free surface. This interface is stress-free and deforms in response to internal force balances, which is essential for understanding processes ranging from rifted margins to subduction. However, a free surface can introduce instabilities and oscillations in the numerical solution, commonly known as the "drunken sailor" instability, forcing the use of small time steps. Geodynamic models therefore often employ stabilization terms based on the gravitational effect of free-surface motion. To date, these terms have been derived primarily on a heuristic basis. Here, we apply variational calculus to the energy-minimization formulation of incompressible Stokes flow. Using the Gateaux derivative, we derive the complete weak form for a deforming free-surface domain and show that the stabilization terms arise naturally from the free-surface assumption. We consider the linear-viscosity case and identify two boundary-integral contributions: one associated with internal viscous deformation and the other with gravitational body force. Two benchmark cases demonstrate the consistency of the derived formulation with previously proposed stabilization approaches. Our results provide a mathematical foundation for the commonly used gravity stabilization and identify an additional viscous boundary contribution.

papers.t: A Physics-Based Site-Specific Approach to Probabilistic Fault Displacement Hazard Analysis
in: Nuclear Risk Research Center, Central Research Institute of Electric Power Industry, Abiko, Japan
Nuclear Facilities Division, Taisei Corporation, Tokyo, Japan
Research Institute for Earth and Information Sciences, Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology, Yokohama, Japan
tk: A physics-based probabilistic fault displacement hazard analysis method is developed using numerical modeling and applied to the 2014 Northern Nagano earthquake.
提出了一种基于物理和数值模拟的概率断层位移危险性分析方法，并应用于2014年北长野地震。
papers.ab: In the existing probabilistic fault displacement hazard analysis (PFDHA), empirical equations derived from a database of previously observed surface earthquake faults are used. A physics-based PFDHA method was developed using numerical analysis instead of the empirical equations. The developed method was applied to the surface earthquake faults in the 2014 Northern Nagano earthquake. The method enables us to evaluate fault displacement hazard by considering information obtained from geological and fault surveys at important facility sites as an analytical model.

papers.t: Measuring rock strain with distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and cemented patch cables
in: Geophysical Institute, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) , 76187 Karlsruhe ,
Black Forest Observatory (BFO) , 77709 Wolfach ,
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences , Telegrafenberg, 14473 Potsdam ,
Institute of Geodesy, University of Stuttgart , 70174 Stuttgart ,
tk: Cementing DAS patch cables into concrete grooves provides highly accurate rock strain measurements, showing excellent agreement with traditional Invar wire strainmeters.
将DAS光缆用水泥固定在沟槽中可实现高精度岩石应变测量，与传统应变仪高度一致。
papers.ab: A rigid connection between the optical fiber and the rock allows to properly measure ‘rock strain’ with distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). We demonstrate this by running four interrogator units (IU) on a testbed with single-fiber patch cables being cemented into a groove in the concrete floor of Black Forest Observatory (BFO). The recorded signals are compared with the recordings of a calibrated Invar wire strainmeter array that has been continuously in operation for the last decades at a distance of about $350 \,\mathrm{m}$ to the testbed. In this way, we compare the ‘fiber strain’ against ‘rock strain’ at frequencies below 0.2 Hz. We investigate this on the background of a previous study with DAS cables unreeled on the floor and loaded down by sand and sandbags, where we found a significant loss of strain amplitude between rock and fiber. Waveform similarity for strong earthquake signals is high with typical values of the normalized correlation coefficient greater than 0.95. The strain amplitude measured by all four IUs is very consistent and by about 10 per cent larger than the strain measured by the strainmeters. We attribute this minor discrepancy to spatially varying strain–strain coupling caused by the local topography. At frequencies up to 14 Hz we make an intercomparison of IUs, showing no significant variation with frequency. The scatter of strain amplitude in between channels which are spatially near to each other in the same fiber route is about $\pm 10~\mathrm{ per~cent}$ in most cases. The variation of median values in between different IUs and earthquakes is less than $5~\mathrm{ per~cent}$. By subtracting the common mode noise, which is coherent along the fiber route, we lower the background signal level to an rms amplitude of $100\, {\rm pstrain}$ at 0.1 Hz and $5\, {\rm pstrain}$ at 1 Hz in a bandwidth of 1/6 decade for the best cases. This allows the detection of the marine microseisms during times of moderate amplitude level.

papers.t: Crustal shearing induced significant magmatic fractionation of Himalayan leucogranites
in: Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Arizona
University of Bucharest
The University of Texas at El Paso
tk: Crustal shearing plays a critical role in driving the magmatic differentiation and geochemical fractionation of leucogranites in the Himalayas.
地壳剪切作用显著促进了喜马拉雅淡色花岗岩的岩浆分异与地球化学分异过程。
papers.ab: Himalayan leucogranites, some of the best-known high-silica granites in the world, are associated with abundant rare-metal mineralization, particularly lithium pegmatites in the Higher Himalaya. Although structural deformation has been proposed to play a major role in magmatic fractionation, how it enhances this process remains poorly understood. Here, we examine the Gyirong leucogranite, a representative Higher Himalayan leucogranite adjacent to the South Tibetan Detachment System (STDS), through detailed analyses on minerals and whole-rock samples along the transect. Mineral microstructures reflect the granites experienced high-temperature melt-present deformation, with typical differential stresses of the STDS. Systematic geochemical variations are observed, with increasing Li, Rb, and Cs and decreasing La, Sr, and Zr toward the STDS, reflecting a clear magmatic fractionation trend. The muscovite compositional zonings indicate that fractionated melt is concentrated at the top of the pluton without magmatic recharge signatures. According to the systematic geochemical composition, we divide the Gyirong leucogranite into cumulate and residual melt parts. The calculated crystallinity of cumulate part is higher than the maximum packing fraction, reflecting deformation must play a role. Forward modeling shows that at least 200 kyr is required to achieve the observed geochemical profile, longer than the cooling duration estimated by thermal modeling. Thus, we propose that crustal shearing could increase the efficiency of crystal-melt segregation, leading to significant magmatic fractionation of high-silica granitic magmas over short periods of time. Such a process is intrinsically linked to the Himalayan uplift, providing a critical mechanism for rare-metal elements enrichment.

papers.t: Broad-band Rayleigh-wave imaging of railways using train vibrations
in: Formerly at Sercel and Mines Paris
Sercel , 27 Avenue Carnot, Massy Cedex 91341 ,
Mines Paris—PSL Research University, Centre de Statistique et Images , 35 rue Saint-Honoré, 77300 Fontainebleau ,
tk: Proposes an automated workflow using train-induced vibrations on a dense 2D array to construct high-frequency 3D Rayleigh-wave velocity models of railway near-surface structures.
利用列车振动与二维台阵构建铁路浅地表高频三维速度模型。
papers.ab: Passing trains act as correlated sources in both space and time, generating powerful waves that illuminate the near-surface below critical infrastructure. We propose an automated workflow for surface wave imaging below railway tracks that uses passing trains as the seismic source, in a context where train signals are far from an ideal isotropic source distribution. We exploit a dense 2-D seismic array situated a few meters from the tracks for 3-D imaging. To accommodate the complex moving source, we retain only correlations that form a limited angle with the moving train. This extends existing methods for a single line of receivers, either parallel or perpendicular to the tracks. We split the data into two cases, where the train is either far from or close to the acquisition setup. When the train is far from the array, sensor pairs mainly parallel to the tracks are important, while sensor pairs perpendicular to the tracks are decisive otherwise. In each case, the signals are time-windowed before computing the cross-correlations. Local dispersion panels are obtained through a Matched Field Processing algorithm. The dispersion curves are computed for various subsets of the array and referred to as patches. Extracting the dispersion curve of the surface wave below many patches results in a 3-D model of the Rayleigh wave phase velocity of the near-surface. Analysing correlations for trains both near and far from the array yields broad-band Rayleigh wave dispersion curves with high-frequency content (above 70 Hz), which is uncommon in passive methods. The velocity model is robust for wavelengths as short as 3 m and sensitive to soils at around 1 m depth, allowing to image what may be a thicker ballast layer formed by previous track settlement issues.

papers.t: Effects of groundwater level variations on seismic ground motion
in: Instituto de Ingeniería, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México , Mexico City 04510 ,
Department of Seismology, Centro de Investigación Cientíıfica y de Educación Superior de Ensenada (CICESE) , Ensenada, Baja California 22860 ,
State Key Laboratory of Deep Oil and Gas, China University of Petroleum (East China) , Qingdao 266580 ,
tk: This study models wave propagation in a saturated porous layer to show how groundwater level variations alter seismic ground motion amplitude and resonance.
该研究模拟了饱和多孔介质中的波传播，揭示了地下水位变化对地震动振幅和共振频率的显著影响。
papers.ab: The mechanical properties of Earth’s uppermost layers are seismically relevant because they can modify seismic waves as they pass through them. These properties may significantly modify the intensity of ground shaking during an earthquake. The relatively common presence of fluids in these layers raises the question of whether they can affect ground motion during earthquakes. In general, seismic ground motion results from the complex interaction of P and S waves within the subsurface, and it is certainly influenced by the presence of fluids. This work examines the effects of varying the groundwater level on seismic ground motion by studying the propagation of P and S waves through a saturated porous layer over an elastic half-space. Our results show that ground motion due to both types of incident waves is affected by the presence of water, with changes in amplitude and resonance frequency. These results highlight the importance of accounting for fluid saturation in both site characterization and site response.

papers.t: Kirchhoff migration of the shallow crustal discontinuities using local earthquake synthetic records in the Campi Flegrei Volcano, South Italy
in: Department of Geophysics, College of Geological Engineering and Geomatics, Chang’an University , Xi’an 710064 ,
Department of Physics “Ettore Pancini”, University of Naples Federico II , Naples 80126 ,
Institute of Geophysics, Polish Academy of Sciences , Warsaw 01-452 ,
ISTerre, Université Grenoble Alpes, CNRS , Grenoble Cedex 9 38058 ,
tk: A workflow combining synthetic local earthquake records and modified Kirchhoff migration with STV and PCA successfully images shallow crustal discontinuities in volcanic settings like Campi Flegrei.
提出一种结合合成局部地震记录与改进基尔霍夫偏移的火山浅表地壳不连续面成像工作流。
papers.ab: Understanding the complex subsurface structures of volcanic regions is crucial for hazard assessment and resource management. Traditional active seismic studies are normally limited for the exploration of shallower crustal structures using low-energy sources located at the Earth surface. While, using earthquake data, the deep seismic interfaces of the crustal structure can be imaged with high-energy and in-depth located sources. Here we propose a data simulating-processing-migration workflow for imaging the subsurface shallow crustal structure by earthquake synthetic signals. As a reference test-site for our study we used the Campi Flegrei caldera internal structure. Thanks to accurate earthquake locations now available in this area, we treat passive data like active data and employ advanced seismic imaging methods. For methodological assessment and improvement, we simulate 400 microearthquakes randomly distributed between 1 and 3 km depth in a vertically layered velocity structure and recorded by 13 stations. Exploiting the cylindrical symmetry of the vertically layered velocity model, we construct representative 2-D seismic sections by sorting synthetic source–receiver records as a function of source–receiver distance. This provides a controlled framework for identifying the different seismic phases and relating them to their corresponding reflecting interfaces prior to migration. Finally, we apply a modified Kirchhoff migration technique combining the Shifted Total Variation regularization and Principal Component Analysis to reconstruct images of subsurface structures. This workflow suppresses migration artefacts, enhances coherent events and extracts structural features that remain stable under model perturbations and noise contamination. The resulting images reliably recover major subsurface interfaces and provide a coherent and robust characterization of the subsurface structure.

papers.t: Shallow lithosphere structure in the North-Central region of the Gulf of California, Mexico, from seismic noise and earthquake tomography
in: Departamento de Sismología, División Ciencias de la Tierra, Centro de Investigación Científica y de Educación Superior de Ensenada (CICESE) , Ensenada, Baja California, 22860 ,
tk: This study constructs a 3D S-wave velocity model of the north-central Gulf of California using ambient noise and earthquake surface waves, revealing crustal thinning and geothermal anomalies.
本研究利用背景噪声和地震面波构建了加利福尼亚湾中北部三维S波速度模型，揭示了地壳减薄与地热异常。
papers.ab: The potential for geothermal resources and the tectonic activity of the north-central region of the Gulf of California, Mexico (GoC) offer a good opportunity to investigate the lithospheric structure of this region. We used 1 yr of ambient seismic noise and 11 shallow earthquakes recorded by the Gulf of California Broadband Seismological Network and stations from the Northwest Mexico Seismic Network and the National Seismological Service to estimate the 3-D S-wave velocity structure. We used surface wave traveltimes at short and long periods, and a two-stage tomography technique to retrieve an S-wave velocity model. We use coarse mesh of 16 × 40 cells with dimensions of 20×20 km in the horizontal direction and variable up to 60 km in depth. The absolute velocity model shows three areas in depth and significant lateral changes from the north to the centre of the GoC associated with crustal and upper-mantle structure. We observed variations in crustal thickness that would indicate a variable Moho depth in the northern GoC and a likely constant depth towards the centre of the Gulf. We identified low-velocity anomalies that could confirm the existence of a geothermal system in the north of the Gulf. The velocity models show relative changes associated with a heterogeneous lithosphere from the central region to the north of the GoC, which would indicate a transition from weak to stronger lithosphere. Velocity anomalies explain some of the tectonic differences between the north and the central GoC, as well as geophysical observations, including heat flow measurements and seismicity.

papers.t: Divergent responses of the Cyclades to large earthquakes: insights from Amorgos Island
in: Université Côte d’Azur, CNRS, Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur, IRD, CEREMA, Géoazur, Sophia Antipolis, 250 rue Albert Einstein , F-06560 Valbonne ,
Geology and Geoenvironment, National Kapodistrian University of Athens , Panepistimiopolis, 15784 Athens ,
tk: Geophysical investigations on Amorgos Island reveal stiff soil conditions and high-frequency attenuation, explaining its unexpectedly low damage during the 1956 Aegean earthquake doublet.
对阿莫尔戈斯岛的地球物理调查表明，坚硬地层和高频衰减减轻了其在1956年大地震中的震害。
papers.ab: On 1956 July 9, the southeastern Cyclades were struck by an earthquake doublet, consisting of an ∼Ms 7.4 main shock, the largest recorded in Greece during the instrumental era, followed shortly afterward by a twin earthquake of magnitude greater than 6.0. The sequence caused severe damage on Santorini, leading Greek authorities to declare the island a disaster area and triggered a major tsunami that affected much of the Aegean basin. Despite the historical significance of this catastrophe, ground-motion observations in the near-source region remain sparse and sometimes contradictory 70 years later, limiting our understanding of the rupture process and hindering reliable seismic hazard assessment. This is particularly true for Amorgos, located less than 30 km from the rupture zone, where available macroseismic evidence suggests unexpectedly low earthquake impacts. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted the first comprehensive geophysical investigation of Amorgos, combining passive and active seismic methods, including ambient vibration arrays and multichannel analysis of surface waves. Taking advantage of the remarkable seismic sequence that occurred between Santorini and Amorgos in early 2025, we further compared the seismic responses of both islands to a set of local crustal earthquakes with magnitudes greater than 3.2. Our results provide a geophysical characterization of the island’s main inhabited areas and reveal moderate to high near-surface shear- and compressional-wave velocities, consistent with the local geology and indicative of stiff soil conditions with limited amplification potential. Combined with the analysis of seismicity, these observations confirm the absence of site effects in Amorgos, in sharp contrast with the strong amplification and directivity observed in Santorini. Conversely, the permanent seismological station on Amorgos exhibits remarkably short-duration ground motions and a pronounced attenuation of high-frequency energy (> 6 Hz), corresponding to the frequency range of traditional Cycladic buildings. These findings offer a new perspective on the ground-motion pattern of the 1956 earthquake and suggest that the geological setting of Amorgos played a major role in mitigating earthquake impacts. However, the geophysical evidence does not account for the large spatial variability in the reported macroseismic intensities, raising questions about the reliability of the intensity assessments. More broadly, this study highlights the complexity of near-fault ground motions and demonstrates the relevance of integrated geophysical approaches for overcoming the limitations of macroseismic data sets and improving seismic hazard assessment.

papers.t: Earthquake hazards across the San Francisco Bay Area: a methodology for probabilistic seismic hazard analysis of strong shaking occurring anywhere in a region
in: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Science Center , Moffett Field, CA 94035 ,
Institute of Statistical Mathematics , 10-3 Midori-cho, Tachikawa-shi, Tokyo, 190-8562 ,
School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Nanyang Technological University , 50 Nanyang Avenue, Singapore 639798 ,
U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Science Center , Pasadena, CA 91106 ,
U.S. Geological Survey, Geologic Hazards Science Center , Pasadena, CA 91106 ,
NASA Ames Research Center , Moffett Field, CA 94035 ,
tk: Develops a probabilistic seismic hazard analysis methodology to estimate the probability of strong ground shaking occurring anywhere within a region, applied to the San Francisco Bay Area.
开发了评估区域内任意位置强震动概率的概率地震危险性分析方法。
papers.ab: Probabilistic seismic hazard analysis is commonly used to estimate the likelihood of ground motion exceeding a certain threshold, over a given time horizon, at a single location. This is different than knowing the probability that any location within a region will experience ground motion exceeding that threshold, information that would be useful for assessing short-term hazards from aftershocks or induced seismicity, guiding emergency managers’ response planning, identifying which areas an earthquake early warning system should alert, or even validating existing probabilistic seismic hazard models. In this paper, we develop a methodology for estimating ground motion hazard across a region, specifically determining the probability of ground shaking anywhere in that region exceeding a prescribed threshold. We benchmark the efficiency of several stochastic sampling algorithms; compare various spatial covariance models including a new spatial covariance model based on dense observations of shaking from aftershocks of the 2019 Ridgecrest, California earthquake sequence; determine the minimum required spatial discretization for estimating shaking hazard across a region and explore assorted computational efficiencies. With this new methodology, we then present a case study of seismic hazard across California’s San Francisco Bay Area, computing probabilities that somewhere in the Bay Area will experience peak ground acceleration exceeding 0.1g, 0.2g, 0.4g or 0.8g at least once over timescales of one to 30 yr. Finally, we use these results to explore the impacts on the estimated seismic hazard of short-term versus long-term earthquake rates, ground motion variability and source selection,.

papers.t: Deep learning-augmented earthquake catalog from a large-N array reveals seismogenic hotspots associated with moderate-rate saltwater disposal in Oklahoma’s Mississippi Limestone Play
in: Earth and Environmental Sciences Division, Los Alamos National Laboratory , Los Alamos, NM, 87545 ,
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory , Livermore, CA, 94550 ,
tk: A deep learning-augmented earthquake catalog from a dense array in Oklahoma reveals localized, low-magnitude seismic clusters strongly correlated with nearby moderate-rate saltwater disposal wells.
利用深度学习增强的密集台阵地震目录揭示了俄克拉荷马州与中等速率注水井密切相关的低震级地震群。
papers.ab: The central United States has experienced a surge in induced seismicity linked to wastewater injection, with Oklahoma as a key study area. While the broader effects of large-scale injection are well documented, the relationship between local injection activities and short-term seismicity fluctuations is less understood. Using deep learning and dense seismic monitoring, we developed an enhanced earthquake catalogue and identified four persistent, low-magnitude (${{M}_\mathrm{ L}} = \ - 0.69\ \rm to\ 2.83)$ seismic clusters within an active saltwater-disposal region. These clusters, several located near mapped faults, exhibit near-daily activity and provide case studies for examining local injection–seismicity dynamics. We find that injection histories for wells within approximately 8–10 km of the clusters generally exhibit stronger temporal correspondence with seismicity than those aggregated over larger spatial scales. Analysis of individual wells further identifies injection histories exhibiting comparatively strong short-term temporal correspondence with observed seismicity, independent of average injection rate or well distance. These relationships are interpreted as statistical associations within a pre-existing regional stress and pore-pressure state rather than evidence of direct hydraulic causality. Compared with higher-moment induced-seismicity cases, the detected clusters exhibit comparable patterns of cumulative seismic moment growth but at predominantly lower magnitudes. These low-moment sequences demonstrate how deep learning-augmented, high-resolution earthquake catalogues can reveal short-term variations in seismic response that are poorly resolved by conventional regional catalogues. Our results suggest that temporal similarity metrics may complement established injection rate and distance criteria by identifying individual wells for further evaluation in induced-seismicity monitoring and mitigation strategies.

papers.t: mhs: mollified Mindlin half-space Green's functions for triangular dislocation elements
in: Harvard University
tk: Introduces a singularity-free library for mollified Mindlin half-space Green's functions using regularized Stokeslets for triangular dislocation elements.
提出了一种基于正则化斯托克斯子方法的无奇异性半空间三角形位错格林函数计算库。
papers.ab: Mollified Mindlin half-space triangular-dislocation Green's functions, as matrices, for a homogeneous half space with no topography. Following Cortez's method of regularized Stokeslets, the point force is replaced by a smooth blob of width epsilon and the elastostatic equations are then solved exactly for that body force, so the kernels are singular nowhere and still satisfy the equations of static elasticity. A fault therefore has a finite width, and stress is defined on the fault itself, where classical dislocation theory returns a value that ordinary integration does not define. The free surface is carried by Mindlin image terms rather than by a meshed boundary, so nothing is solved: there is no linear system, no collocation on a boundary and no box truncation. The library builds the on-fault interaction matrices used in static stress transfer, rate-and-state and earthquake-cycle models. Known limitation: the free-surface traction condition is satisfied to O(epsilon^2) rather than exactly. Work in progress, developed with Claude.

papers.t: Perturbation-based implicit full-waveform inversion with improved optimization conditioning
in: College of Marine Geo-sciences, Ocean University of China , Qingdao 266100 ,
Key Laboratory of Submarine Geoscience and Prospecting Techniques MOE China, Ocean University of China , Qingdao 266100 ,
Shandong Provincial Geo-mineral Engineering Exploration Institute , Jinan 250014 ,
Laboratory for Marine Mineral Resource, Laoshan Laboratory , Qingdao 266100 ,
tk: A perturbation-based implicit FWI framework decomposes velocity into background and perturbation to reduce multi-scale gradient interference and improve convergence.
提出一种基于扰动的隐式全波形反演框架，通过分解背景与扰动改善优化条件。
papers.ab: Implicit full-waveform inversion (IFWI) has shown strong potential for seismic velocity reconstruction due to the implicit regularization of neural networks. However, conventional IFWI based on direct modelling represents multiscale structures within a unified parameter space, where gradients associated with different wavenumber components may interfere, leading to slow convergence and limited recovery of deep structures. To address this issue, we propose a perturbation-based IFWI framework that decomposes the velocity model into a fixed background and a learnable perturbation. This parametrization reduces multiscale gradient interference and improves optimization efficiency by restricting updates to the perturbation subspace. In addition, a coordinate normalization strategy is introduced to decouple spatial scale from the network frequency response, enabling stable optimization across different model sizes. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more stable convergence, improved structural resolution and more reliable deep recovery compared to direct modelling IFWI. The approach also shows strong robustness under challenging conditions, including inaccurate initial models, varying spatial scales and missing low-frequency data.

papers.t: Sedimentary layers enable extra-wide rupture jumps across extensional strike-slip stepovers
in: Shenzhen MSU-BIT University
Southern University of Science and Technology
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Geophysical High-resolution Imaging Technology
tk: Sedimentary layers can significantly increase earthquake rupture jump distances across extensional stepovers by trapping sediment-guided Mach waves that sustain favorable dynamic Coulomb stress.
浅部沉积层通过捕获引导的马赫波，显著增加了拉张型走滑阶区处的地震破裂跨越距离。
papers.ab: Fault stepovers commonly arrest earthquake ruptures, yet shallow sedimentary layers can substantially modify this behavior. We use three-dimensional spontaneous dynamic-rupture simulations to examine how sediment velocity, thickness, background stress, rupture regime, and fault burial affect critical jump distance across extensional and compressional stepovers. In the reference models, sedimentary layers strongly promote transfer across extensional stepovers under high-prestress conditions with supershear rupture. Sediment-guided Mach waves reflect between the free surface and sediment–bedrock interface and sustain favorable dynamic Coulomb stress at large fault-normal distances. The sediment effect is weaker and regime-dependent across compressional stepovers, where transfer is associated primarily with the stopping phase and may be inhibited after supershear transition. At the highest stress level, coexisting and merging Burridge–Andrews and free-surface-induced fronts accompany maximum extensional critical jump distances of 35 km in the low-velocity sediment model and 40 km in the higher-velocity model. These maxima are conditional on the reference stress and friction assumptions. Additional tests show that shallow stress and residual strength substantially change the absolute jump distance. Independent changes in main- and secondary-fault prestress distinguish source-side and receiver-side sensitivity. Fault burial suppresses near-surface supershear development and reduces the enhancement. The results identify a conditional mechanism for sediment-assisted rupture transfer and motivate including shallow structure and fault properties in physics-based assessments of multifault earthquake potential.

papers.t: Off-fault plasticity limits the speed of elongated earthquake ruptures
in: Massachusetts Institute of Technology , Cambridge, 02139 ,
Université Côte d’Azur , Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur, IRD, CNRS, Géoazur, 06560, Valbonne ,
tk: Off-fault plastic deformation limits the propagation speed of elongated, width-limited earthquake ruptures to realistic sub-Rayleigh velocities.
断层外塑性变形限制了长条形地震破裂的传播速度，使其保持在合理的亚瑞利速度范围内。
papers.ab: Conventional earthquake rupture models in elastic media with scale-independent dissipation predict rupture acceleration up to a limiting speed dictated by seismic wave speeds. However, most earthquakes are inferred to be significantly slower than these theoretical limiting speeds. Previous 2-D modelling shows that inelastic deformation of the material surrounding the fault can stabilize rupture propagation at velocities below the limiting speed, owing to scale-dependent dissipation due to the expansion of the off-fault inelastic zone with rupture length. An essential ingredient missing from such models is that large earthquake ruptures become elongated after they saturate the seismogenic width, which prevents a length-dependent growth of the off-fault dissipation zone. Here, we carry out a computational study of elongated ruptures with off-fault plasticity, with a particular focus on steady rupture speeds. We combine a 2.5-D (width-averaged) modelling approach and Mohr–Coulomb plasticity to simulate width-limited strike-slip earthquake ruptures propagating in an inelastic medium. We observe steady pulse-like ruptures propagating at speeds below the Rayleigh wave speed. Through a systematic parametric study, we characterize the dependence of the steady rupture speed on the initial fault stress, closeness to plastic failure and seismogenic zone width. Our simulation results show that off-fault plastic deformation allows the rupture velocity on long faults to saturate at speeds between 6.5 and 99 per cent of the Rayleigh wave speed, encompassing the common range of speeds of real earthquakes as well as those of tsunami earthquakes. Our results indicate that off-fault plasticity is a viable mechanism for achieving realistic earthquake rupture speeds, even on planar faults with homogeneous stress and strength. The model also provides insights on the factors controlling other earthquake source properties, including pulse width, peak slip velocity, inelastic off-fault deformation and inelastic zone width.

papers.t: Exploring new statistical metrics to evaluate the magnitude distribution of earthquake forecasting models
in: School of Earth Sciences, University of Bristol , Bristol, BS8 1QU ,
Global Earthquake Model (GEM) Foundation , Pavia 27100 ,
ETH , Zurich 8093 ,
GFZ German Research Centre for Geoscience , Postdam 14473 DE ,
School of Geosciences, University of Edinburgh , Edinburgh EH8 9YL ,
kw: collaboratory for the study of earthquake predictability
tk: Proposes a resampled M-test and a Multinomial Log-Likelihood score to decouple magnitude and rate evaluations in earthquake forecasting models.
提出重采样M检验和多项对数似然评分，以解耦地震预测模型中的震级与频度评估。
papers.ab: Evaluating earthquake forecasts is a crucial step in understanding and improving the capabilities of forecasting models. The use of specific metrics to assess the consistency between forecasts and data on one particular aspect of the process is important to understand which aspects of seismicity a model is failing to describe, and, consequently, highlight where new versions of the model should improve. This can be done effectively only by metrics unaffected by inconsistencies in other aspects of the process. The Collaboratory for the Study of Earthquake Predictability (CSEP), which organizes earthquake forecasting experiments around the globe, has developed different tests targeting different aspects of the process, such as the number N-test or the magnitude M-test, assessing (in)consistency between the observed and forecasted number and magnitude distributions of events, respectively. We find that the results of the recently proposed M-test for catalogue-based forecasts (composed of a collection of synthetic catalogues from the model) depend on the N-test, that is, the two tests do not isolate the desired aspects appropriately, rendering uninformative forecast results. Here, we address this problem using simulated data and provide a solution based on resampling of simulated catalogues. We implement this new M-test with resampling in the pyCSEP software toolkit, conduct two analyses using actual earthquake forecasts for Europe (1990–2015) and Switzerland (1933–1962, 1962–1992, 1993–2022) that provide inconsistent earthquake counts compared to observations, and analyse how the test results change using this proposed test. Lastly, we investigate alternative metrics, namely an unnormalized M-test, two Chi-square formulations, the Hellinger distance, the Brier score and a novel Multinomial Log-Likelihood (MLL) score, and compare them based on the ability to find (in)consistency between data and forecast in various synthetic scenarios.
