papers.t: Structure-Driven Methodology: An Emerging Cross-Domain Paradigm
tk: Proposes a structure-driven inversion paradigm that directly constructs solutions by exploiting intrinsic problem structures, contrasting with traditional iterative objective-driven search methods.
提出结构驱动反演范式，通过利用问题内在结构直接构建解，而非迭代搜索。
papers.ab: This article proposes and articulates structure-driven methodology as an emerging cross-domain paradigm. In contrast to the objective-driven paradigm that has dominated inverse-problem solving for over two centuries, structure-driven methodology advocates identifying and exploiting the intrinsic structure of a problem to construct the solution method directly, rather than approaching the solution through iterative search. Drawing on examples from the Liouville-variant Goldbach conjecture, the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, Noether's theorem, and the author's nearly four decades of geophysical inversion practice, the article illustrates the common logic of structure-driven thinking in number theory, pure mathematics, physics, and seismic imaging. The author also systematically proposes the Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI) paradigm, comprising Mathematical Structure-Driven Inversion (MSDI) and Physical Structure-Driven Inversion (PSDI). Structure-driven methodology does not negate objective-driven methodology but complements it: objective-driven is a general search strategy, whereas structure-driven is a custom direct strategy. The article concludes that the significance of this shift lies not only in efficiency gains but also in cognitive deepening---when facing complex problems, the first question is no longer ``how to solve the problem faster'' but ``what is the structure of the problem.''

papers.t: Coupled Sb-Hg isotopes reveal mixed basement and deeply recycled mantle-related metal sources for the South China antimony belt
in: China University of Geosciences
China University of Geosciences (Beijing)
State Key Laboratory of Geological Processes and Mineral Resources
McGill University
Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geochemistry
Juniata College
Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
Geophysical Survey
tk: Coupled Sb and Hg isotopes trace the metal sources of the South China antimony belt to Precambrian basement and recycled mantle reservoirs.
耦合锑-汞同位素揭示华南锑矿带的金属源自前寒武纪基底和深部循环地幔。
papers.ab: Understanding the sources of metals in hydrothermal ore systems is fundamental for improving exploration models. However, direct tracers of metal sources remain limited, especially for large, low-temperature deposits. Here we apply coupled antimony (Sb) and mercury (Hg) isotope analyses to Sb deposits from South China, the World’s largest antimony metallogenic province. The dataset reveals substantial variability in δ123Sb (−0.64 to +0.69‰), δ202Hg (−1.86 to +2.08‰), and Δ199Hg (−0.20 to +0.14‰). These data support a model involving two metal sources, namely a deep, recycled mantle-related reservoir and Precambrian basement metamorphic rocks. Our results demonstrate that coupled Sb and Hg isotopes provide a potentially powerful tool with which to identify the metal sources for Sb ore deposits, and that their application may help refine models for these deposits globally and help decode the dynamic interplay between Earth’s interior and crustal metal cycling. Coupled Sb-Hg isotope signatures from the South China antimony belt reveal that ore metals were sourced from both Precambrian basement rocks and a deep recycled mantle reservoir, demonstrating the utility of coupled Sb-Hg isotopes for tracing metal provenance, according to coupled Sb and Hg isotope analyses.

papers.t: RiptideRemix: A Toolboxfor Musical Synthesis ofMarine Acoustic Data
in: Oceanography
University of Washington
University of Hawaii
University of California, San Diego
Sound Data Science
Ocean Science Analytics
Ocean Networks Canada
University of Victoria
tk: RiptideRemix is an interactive educational toolbox that allows users to synthesize music by remixing marine acoustic and geophysical datasets.
通过混音海洋声学与地球物理数据创作音乐的科普工具箱。
papers.ab: For the 2025 Ocean Hack Week hosted at the University of Washington, we built the framework for an interactive dashboard allowing users to create new musical compositions by remixing marine sounds. Starting from a base library of typical ocean sounds, users can pull audio clips from publicly available acoustic and geophysical datasets. Incorporated datasets include Ocean Networks Canada (ONC), the NSF Seismological Facility for the Advancement of Geoscience (SAGE), OrcaSound, and the National Center for Environmental Information (NCEI). Currently, we pull audio clips from pre-processed libraries managed by these sources. Creators can then drag clips into a visual audio mixer, and change the pitch, speed, and repetition of a clip to form a “song,” which is also rendered as a waveform and spectrogram. A whimsical map diagram is generated when a song is completed, reflecting the varieties of sound sources combined in the piece. This project, representing a fusion of data science, acoustic processing, and fun, invites us to dive into the rich world of ocean soundscapes. Alongside the musical aspect of the project, there are several educational components. First, a thorough description of each dataset is provided, explaining the type of sensors and environment. Secondly, visualization of common waveforms and spectrograms explains general analysis of different signals, allowing the users to understand the scientific context behind the sounds they are hearing. From drag-and-drop music mixing to thorough explanations of seismic waves, there’s something for everyone here.

papers.t: Eigenwaves: Finite-frequency Eigenrays in Elastic Anisotropic Media
tk: The paper introduces Eigenwave theory, extending variational eigenray tracing to finite frequencies in heterogeneous anisotropic media using a trajectory-mechanics formulation.
本文提出特征波理论，将变分特征射线追踪扩展至有限频率。
papers.ab: The Eigenray method solves two-point boundary-value ray-tracing problems in heterogeneous anisotropic elastic media using a variational formulation based on the eikonal equation. Here, we extend the method to finite frequencies using the trajectory-mechanics formulation in which finite-frequency effects are represented by a frequency-dependent potential that couples phase and amplitude. We show that finite-frequency propagation can be described within the same variational framework through an equivalent effective medium, preserving the structure of the original method while introducing corrections to trajectories, phase, amplitudes, geometric spreading, wavefront curvature, and caustic behavior. The resulting Eigenwave formulation requires only local modifications of the ray velocity and its derivatives and reduces to classical ray theory in the high-frequency limit. Numerical examples involving multipathing and cusp caustics demonstrate accurate modeling of finite-frequency propagation effects. While ray-based amplitudes become unreliable near caustics, a phase-space (Maslov) treatment successfully reproduces finite-difference wavefield solutions. These results establish Eigenwave theory as a unified framework connecting ray theory and finite-frequency wave propagation in heterogeneous anisotropic media.

papers.t: Analysis of building seismic damage characteristics and topographic amplification effects of the 2026 Diebu Ms5.5 earthquake
tk: Integrates field surveys, seismic monitoring, and FLAC3D simulations to reveal how topographic amplification and slope deformation drove building damage during the 2026 Diebu Ms5.5 earthquake.
结合调查与模拟，揭示了2026年迭部地震地形放大对震害的控制机制。
papers.ab: On January 26, 2026, an Ms5.5 shallow-focus earthquake occurred in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province. The affected area lies within the alpine gorge of the Bailong River on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, a region characterized by rugged topography and complex geological conditions that are typically prone to topographic amplification of ground motion. To address how topographic and site conditions control ground-motion amplification and the resulting spatial distribution of seismic damage, this study selected Dianga Town in Diebu County—the area covered by the earthquake damage survey—as the study area. Field damage surveys, seismic station monitoring data, and FLAC3D three-dimensional numerical simulations were integrated to systematically reveal the relationships among ground-motion amplification, building damage, and slope deformation. Results indicate that the seismic intensity in the study area reached VI–VII on the Chinese seismic intensity scale. Ground-motion amplification was closely associated with the spatially non-uniform distribution of seismic damage: at steep cliffs, slope shoulders, and high-elevation sites, peak ground acceleration (PGA) amplification factors approached 2.0, and buildings at these locations experienced significantly more severe damage than those at other sites. Seismic loading also altered the shear strain distribution pattern of the slope, causing the zone of concentrated shear strain to redistribute and extend toward the residential area. Topographic relief, excavation-induced free faces, and elevation differences were identified as the primary factors contributing to topographic amplification in the studied alpine gorge; in particular, an elevation difference of only about 100 m produced pronounced differences in seismic damage. These findings qualitatively reveal the mechanism of ground-motion amplification and provide a scientific basis for seismic fortification and geological hazard mitigation in villages and towns within alpine gorge areas on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau.

papers.t: Tsangbu Ri slope failure triggers massive flash flood across the Himalaya and shakes the globe – the seismic observations
tk: Seismic observations from Nepal and China localize a massive Himalayan slope failure and preceding M2.5 event, demonstrating the potential of regional networks for early warning.
利用尼泊尔和中国的地震观测定位了喜马拉雅滑坡及前兆事件，展示了区域网络预警的潜力。
papers.ab: On 26 August 2026, a massive slope failure in the Himalaya caused a destructive flash-flood all along the Trishuli River. Here we report the first complete set of related seismic observations from Nepal and China. Using first-arrivals of high-frequency waveforms, we localize the main mass-movement and a nearby M2.5 seismic event shortly preceding it. The flash-flood increased seismic noise levels, persisting for hours. We report global seismic detections of the main event. Ultimately, we argue that a regional seismic monitoring network coupled with a signal detection and classification system would provide an early warning tool for future high-risk events.

papers.t: Bulk Viscous Resistance Principle: A Unified Physical Framework for Effective Resistance in the Lithosphere–Asthenosphere System
in: Independent Researcher
tk: Proposes the Bulk Viscous Resistance Principle to explain the ultra-low effective resistance of the lithosphere-asthenosphere system through melt-assisted distributed diffusion creep.
提出体粘性阻力原理，通过熔体辅助的分布式扩散蠕变解释岩石圈-软流圈系统的超低有效阻力。
papers.ab: The effective resistance coefficient of the lithosphere–asthenosphere system inferred from geodynamic inversions is 0.01–0.03, more than an order of magnitude lower than laboratory rock friction values (0.6–0.85). This paper proposes the Bulk Viscous Resistance Principle, demonstrating that plate resistance consists of two physically distinct components: rate-dependent viscous drag at the lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary (LAB), and rate-independent brittle friction at subduction trenches. This paper further decomposes the internal physical implementation mechanism of bulk viscous resistance and identifies a hierarchical relationship among three sub-mechanisms: (1) interface selection as the triggering mechanism, in which the system selects the interface with the minimum among multiple candidate interfaces; (2) creep accommodation as the primary accommodating mechanism, in which material between different interfaces accommodates deformation through diffusion creep shear, distributing motion within a bulk domain of finite thickness ; (3) melt spreading as an auxiliary mechanism, in which sliding shear stretches and spreads melt particles into melt films, replacing solid–solid contact with liquid–liquid contact. Based on the diffusion creep constitutive law, this paper derives an analytical framework for the bulk viscous resistance coefficient from first principles: where is in cm, is an effective material constant (dimension cm2 MPa-1 s-1, having absorbed the unit conversion of grain-size scaling), and is the equivalent creep layer thickness. Using a reasonable range of diffusion creep parameters (, ), this framework yields . In the pure solid limit (), achieving the mantle inversion value requires an equivalent creep thickness , far exceeding the Earth's scale—demonstrating that a purely solid mantle cannot produce the observed ultra-low resistance and must rely on melt-assisted diffusion. With standard melt-bearing parameters (), achieving the same value requires , which coincides with the upper limit of the global asthenospheric low-velocity zone (LVZ) thickness. This paper further points out that this is the equivalent thickness of the entire asthenosphere participating in distributed creep, rather than the thickness of a localized shear band at the LAB. Trench friction remains approximately constant (), because water in subduction zones is transient—absorbed into mineral structures before forming a persistent lubricating film, maintaining solid–solid contact. This value is consistent with serpentine friction experiments (0.3–0.5) and thermodynamic inversions. Plate motion occurs only when the driving force exceeds the constant trench friction (), establishing a velocity threshold; the velocity is then regulated by . This paper transforms effective resistance from a fitting parameter into a first-principles derivable physical quantity and provides six testable predictions.

papers.t: Understanding Earthquake Physics with On-Fault Observatories
tk: This paper advocates for a paradigm shift toward on-fault observatories and controlled fault activation experiments to directly measure earthquake physics.
本文倡导向断层原位观测站和受控断层激活实验转变，以直接测量地震物理过程。
papers.ab: Earthquakes often strike without warning. Current fault monitoring infrastructure is not sensitive enough to detect signals such as accelerating fault creep or dilation, which laboratory experiments and numerical models predict may precede large earthquakes. Here we argue that a paradigm shift is needed and technically achievable: from inferring faulting processes from a distance with surface arrays, to on-fault observatories (OFOs) that measure the processes directly on faults. And from accidental fault activation to controlled fault activation experiments. We discuss how the resulting observations could solve long-standing earthquake physics questions, and pave the way for more powerful earthquake risk mitigation strategies.

papers.t: Using Neural Operators to Enable Fast and Accurate Scientific Simulations
in: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
tk: This report explores the application of neural operators to accelerate and maintain accuracy in scientific simulations, particularly wave propagation.
该报告探讨了利用神经算子加速科学模拟（特别是波动传播）并保持其精度的应用。
papers.ab: This report was prepared as an account of work sponsored by an

papers.t: Peak ground acceleration underestimates narrow-band seismic amplification on mountain slopes
tk: PGA significantly underestimates narrow-band seismic amplification on mountain slopes compared to frequency-dependent spectral ratios.
PGA显著低估了山体边坡上的特定频率地震放大效应。
papers.ab: Topographic amplification is widely invoked to explain strong shaking and slope failure in mountainous terrain, yet direct field observations remain limited. Here we analyze 24 regional earthquakes recorded by a four-station strong-motion array spanning a ridge crest, a valley bottom, and two contrasting slope facets on a single ridge in central Japan. Peak ground acceleration (PGA) and frequency-dependent measures reveal markedly different representations of local seismic response. PGA ratios vary among events and are positively associated with epicentral distance; however, earthquake magnitude also increases with distance, so source-size and propagation-distance effects cannot be separated in this catalog. In contrast, the NS slope exhibits a persistent narrow-band station-to-valley Fourier spectral-ratio peak at 3.5–4.0 Hz that remains stable across events and processing choices. Absolute spectra confirm enhanced energy at the slope in this band, while also showing that a relative spectral depression at the valley reference contributes to the large ratio magnitude. Most importantly, the geometric-mean 5%-damped response-spectral ratio reaches 6.67 at 0.277 s (3.61 Hz), compared with a corresponding full-record geometric-mean horizontal PGA ratio of 1.13. These observations show that PGA can substantially under-represent frequency-specific elastic response on mountain slopes, while the responsible mechanism cannot be uniquely attributed to topography or near-surface structure alone.

papers.t: Fault or Not? Evaluating Himalayan Lineaments as Potential Multi-Hazard Controls in the Sikkim Himalaya (NE India)
tk: This study evaluates the seismotectonic role of geomorphic lineaments in the Sikkim Himalaya, finding earthquake clustering and a deep concentration of low-magnitude events at ~67.5 km depth.
本研究评估了锡金喜马拉雅地貌线状构造的地震构造作用，发现地震聚集及约67.5公里深处的低震级地震集中区。
papers.ab: The Sikkim region of northeastern India (87.5°E–90°E, 26°N–29°N) is forecast to host an Mw 8.4 or larger earthquake due to rupture along the Main Himalayan thrust (MHT). However, the 2011 Mw 6.9 Sikkim earthquake was notable for its lower-than-expected magnitude, strike-slip focal mechanism, and intermediate depth below the MHT. This event raised the possibility that some geomorphic lineaments in Sikkim may have a seismotectonic role. We examine Sikkim seismicity in relation to mapped lineaments and major Himalayan faults to test whether the lineaments may represent active, deep-seated strike-slip faults. Earthquakes cluster along some lineament traces and intersections, consistent with these zones acting as stress concentrators or rupture segment boundaries. Focal mechanisms reveal variable kinematics, with a dominance of oblique- and strike-slip motion, reflecting a complex interplay among inherited basement structures, Himalayan compression, and differential motion within the deforming Indian craton. An analysis of the best-located hypocenters reveals a clear concentration of lower magnitude (Mw 2–4) events at 67.5 ± 0.33 km depth (MSWD = 2.9; n = 69 events). Although such low-magnitude events are nondestructive, their recurrence suggests they may contribute to strain accommodation, a possibility that warrants further investigation when developing models for future seismic hazard.

papers.t: Temporal evolution and decline of seismicity associated with cyclic operations at the Serajeh underground gas storage, Iran
tk: Investigates induced seismicity at Iran's Serajeh gas storage, finding an 8-month lag with injection and a significant decline after four years.
研究伊朗Serajeh储气库诱发地震，发现其滞后注气8个月并在四年后显著减少。
papers.ab: Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. We investigate seismicity around the Serajeh UGS in central Iran by combining 29,781 deep-learning-based single-station earthquake detections, multi-station relocation, centroid moment tensor inversion, and operational records. The relocated hypocentres form a compact cluster near the Serajeh structure, primarily at depths of 3–8 km, overlapping with and extending below the 2.4–3.0 km storage interval. Independent comparison with relocated earthquakes confirms that S–P time at the nearby GHVR station provides a useful first-order proxy for local source distance. Cross-correlation between monthly gas injection and seismicity shows a distinct maximum at an offset of approximately 8 months. This feature is reproduced by the phase-randomized ReshuffleCorr analysis, while additional structure-preserving tests indicate that its global statistical strength and exact timing depend on the treatment of temporal variability. An objective change-point analysis identifies a marked decrease in seismicity centred on April 2015, nearly four years after storage operations began, and the decrease remains evident using a conservative magnitude threshold. Seismicity subsequently remains lower despite continued cyclic operations. The selected focal mechanisms show predominantly strike-slip to oblique source kinematics across pre-operational, operational, and post-operational periods. We interpret these observations as evidence for an evolving temporal and spatial association between storage operations and a pre-existing fault–reservoir system. These results highlight the value of integrating high-resolution seismic monitoring with independently constrained locations and operational records for seismic-hazard assessment at UGS sites.

papers.t: Rapid Source Characterization and Static Stress Transfer of the 24 September 2026 Mw 5.3–5.4 Şanlıurfa (Karaköprü–Hilvan) Earthquake, Southeastern Türkiye
in: University of Kirkuk
tk: The study performs rapid source characterization and Coulomb stress transfer modeling for the 2026 Şanlıurfa earthquake, highlighting the high uncertainty in early underconstrained solutions.
对2026年土耳其地震进行快速震源表征与库仑应力计算。
papers.ab: On 24 September 2026, a moderate earthquake occurred in southeastern Türkiye near the Hilvan–Karaköprü sector of Şanlıurfa Province. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) reported M 5.3 at 37.4736°N, 38.8612°E and 10 km depth, whereas the Disaster and Emergency Management Authority of Türkiye (AFAD) issued a rapid Mw 5.4 solution at a shallower and approximately 5.9 km displaced hypocenter. We present a rapid, reproducible first-hours source and static-stress analysis based on openly accessible waveform and station metadata. The downloaded study archive contains 32 MiniSEED waveform files, 199 SAC traces, 25 StationXML response files, and 25 station-geometry records within a 200 km acquisition radius. After response correction, P-arrival refinement, polarity quality control, and geographic deduplication, five weighted vertical-component first motions were retained. A transparent double-couple grid search yields a provisional oblique mechanism with nodal planes NP1 = 118°/66°/−50° and NP2 = 233.9°/45.6°/−145.3°. Although all five retained polarities are fit, the solution is demonstrably underconstrained: the maximum azimuth gap is 207.7° and 1,588 near-best solutions remain. Using an Okada elastic half-space, Mw 5.3 as a working moment-magnitude proxy, 3 MPa stress drop, effective friction 0.4, and a magnitude-scaled 6.36 × 3.18 km rectangular source with 0.173 m mean slip, we calculate alternative NP1 and NP2 Coulomb failure stress (ΔCFS) fields. After excluding the inner 5 km source-core region and retaining only cells where both nodal-plane scenarios exceed +0.01 MPa, two compact consensus-positive sectors emerge approximately 5–10 km west and east of the USGS epicenter. Each covers about 34 km2 and reaches a conservative scenario-overlap maximum near +0.05 MPa. By contrast, modeled ΔCFS at the centers of Hilvan, Şanlıurfa, Siverek, Bozova, Kâhta, and Adıyaman is much smaller than +0.01 MPa. An early AFAD ML 2.4 aftershock plots in a negative ΔCFS area under the source-plane receiver assumption, emphasizing that static stress maps are strongly dependent on receiver-fault orientation, source geometry, and rapid-location uncertainty. The immediate scientific priority is therefore dense near-source seismic monitoring, rapid relocation, regional moment-tensor inversion, InSAR/GNSS analysis, and fault-specific receiver-plane modelling—not deterministic prediction of the next earthquake. Same-day U.S. Geological Survey Did You Feel It? (DYFI) reporting had reached 8 community responses and community intensity V, providing preliminary evidence of moderate felt shaking but insufficient sampling for a stable spatial intensity-attenuation analysis.

papers.t: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
tk: This study utilizes GIS and Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis to identify optimal geothermal power plant sites in the Gulf of Suez, Egypt, using subsurface thermal and geological data.
本研究利用GIS和多准则决策，确定了埃及苏伊士湾地热电厂的最佳选址。
papers.ab: The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. In the context of escalating global energy demands, geothermal energy, defined as terrestrial heat extracted from the Earth’s crust through deep drilling and surface fluid transport, represents a viable pathway toward energy transition. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, environmental, and infrastructural parameters, each assigned relative weights commensurate with its significance. A robust correlation ( R = 0.975) was established between subsurface temperature and depth, yielding a mean geothermal gradient of 48.5 °C/km (R² = 0.9509) and affirming the reliability of the thermal model. The resulting suitability analysis demonstrates that the Gulf of Suez region possesses favorable conditions for the deployment of both Flash Steam and Binary Cycle power plant technologies. Along the eastern coastal corridor, localities including Hammam Faraun, Ras Sudr, and Abu Zenima were identified as suitable for Flash Steam systems at drilling depths of 3,000–4,000 m, corresponding to reservoir temperatures of 140–210 °C, while Binary Cycle systems are applicable at depths of 2,000–3,000 m with temperatures ranging from 100 to 160 °C. On the western coast, sites encompassing Ras Gharib, Ras Shukeir, Jabal al-Zeit, and Jabal Ataqa are technically viable for Flash Steam technology at depths of 3,000–4,000 m and temperatures of 140–210 °C, with supplementary Binary Cycle suitability observed at depths of 2,000–3,000 m and temperatures of 100–180 °C. Zones exclusively suited for Binary Cycle applications include Ayoun Moussa, Wadi Baaba, Wadi Feiran, and Wadi El-Tor to the east, and Zaafarana, Wadi Dara, and Wadi Araba to the west, at depths of 3,000–4,000 m with temperatures ranging between 100 and 160 °C and 100–155 °C, respectively. Northern portions of the study area, characterized by comparatively subdued geothermal gradients, are deemed appropriate for direct-use applications, including space heating, light industrial operations, and residential thermal supply.

papers.t: Spatially Organized Hillslope Weakening Localizes Retrogressive Thaw Slumps across the Tibetan Plateau
tk: The study proposes a Hillslope Weakening Field framework to explain why retrogressive thaw slumps cluster and localize under widespread permafrost warming on the Tibetan Plateau.
该研究提出了山坡弱化场框架，解释了青藏高原广泛多年冻土退化背景下热融滑塌的局部聚集机制。
papers.ab: Long-term permafrost warming on the Tibetan Plateau is continuously and broadly reshaping cold-region landscapes, and has produced numerous localized and clustered retrogressive thaw slumps (RTSs). However, the question why RTSs are highly localized and clustered under the widespread permafrost warming remains incompletely understood. To understand and explain the RTS localization and clustering, we propose the Hillslope Weakening Field (HWF), which represents the spatial distribution of relative hillslope weakening states jointly formed by multiple environmental conditions, including thermal conditions, moisture and soil properties, topographic setting, permafrost and ground-ice conditions, and land-surface cover. We examined the correspondence between the HWF and RTS spatial selectivity across seven study regions on the Tibetan Plateau. Positive HWF-RTS correspondence was observed in six of the seven regions, with consistently strong relationships in five. In these five regions, RTSs preferentially occurred on more strongly weakened hillslopes, with occurrence rates 3.35-5.09 times the regional background rate within the 10% most strongly weakened slope units. Moreover, high-weakening hillslopes were not spatially isolated but correlated and connected across the landscape. RTS-bearing slope units and their surrounding hillslopes showed higher weakening levels than RTS-unrecorded slope units and their surroundings, and the weakening contrast declined with distance. These results suggest that RTSs preferentially occur on more strongly weakened hillslopes and cluster where high-weakening states are spatially continuous and connected. Our findings show how spatial differences in hillslope weakening states can help explain why geomorphic responses to widespread permafrost warming are highly heterogeneous across permafrost landscapes.

papers.t: A Multivariable Approach to the Regional Calibration of the Galvez Davison Index across Mexico Climate Regimes
tk: This paper evaluates and regionally calibrates the Gálvez Davison Index (GDI) for convective favorability across Mexico's diverse climate regimes using ERA5 and CHIRPS data.
该研究利用ERA5和CHIRPS数据评估并区域校准了墨西哥不同气候区用于对流预测的GDI指数。
papers.ab: The Gálvez Davison Index (GDI) is a thermodynamic diagnostic designed to summarize convective favorability in the tropical regions, yet its transferability across complex terrain and heterogeneous hydroclimates remains uncertain. Here we assess the climatological behavior and precipitation relevance of the GDI over Mexico using ERA5 hourly fields and CHIRPS daily precipitation for 1981 to 2024. We characterize the seasonal cycle and spatial contrasts of GDI and evaluate its association with rainfall using grid point and regional Pearson and Spearman correlations between daily maximum GDI and daily precipitation. To introduce an independent convective proxy, we also quantify the relationship between hourly GDI and ERA5 outgoing longwave radiation (OLR). Event level discrimination skill is assessed with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) across regions and months. While GDI precipitation correlations are moderate and region dependent, GDI OLR coupling is consistently stronger, partly because OLR approaches a lower bound once deep convection develops, supporting its use as an intermediate proxy between thermodynamic favorability and rainfall. However, GDI values are systematically lower over elevated terrain because of the pressure level formulation of the index, which should be considered when interpreting the GDI over mountainous regions. ROC results indicate skill above random chance in nearly all region month combinations, with AUC frequently exceeding 0.75 during the core convective season. Building on these diagnostics, we propose a regionally calibrated GDI convective regime scale for May to October, adapted from the original GDI framework but recalibrated for Mexico using event conditioned distributions defined from OLR and precipitation and quantified with bootstrap uncertainty.

papers.t: GraphSplit: Sparse Double-Difference Earthquake Relocation From Synchronized Differential-Time Graphs
in: University of Iceland, Unknown, Reykjavik, Iceland [IS]
tk: GraphSplit decouples timing estimation from double-difference relocation using synchronized differential-time graphs, enabling highly efficient and robust relocation of massive earthquake catalogs.
GraphSplit通过分离双差定位中的时间估计与定位图，实现了海量地震目录的高效、鲁棒重定位。
papers.ab: Relative earthquake locations can reveal fault structure and improve earthquake accuracy, but large catalogs pose a new challenge, partly due to the massive underlying differential travel-time datasets. We introduce GraphSplit, which splits apart the graphs used to estimate relative timing from the graphs used to relocate earthquakes. The recently developed DDSync method fits one relative arrival-time potential per event, station and phase. GraphSplit uses these potentials to improve initial locations through a prelocation step and then constructs a sparse graph of neighboring earthquakes for a robust double-difference relocation. The timing estimates can therefore draw on many measured event pairs without requiring the data for each pair in every relocation update. In a known-location benchmark, GraphSplit gives the smallest depth error and second-smallest horizontal error among the compared methods, with better depth precision and similar horizontal precision to the evaluated hypoDD catalog. Field applications show robustness on real data. Prelocation and double-difference relocation progressively resolve narrow, branching structures in the Cahuilla swarm. In a station-sparse Guyana earthquake sequence, the central aftershock population develops a dip of approximately 30°, closer to independent mainshock and satellite radar constraints than the gently dipping starting locations. A full Ridgecrest relocation with 237,202 input events completes on an 18GB laptop in 2.26 hours, retaining 221,633 earthquakes. Requiring stronger timing-graph support removes local updates for over half of that population. Station-phase resampling reasonably describes conditional location variability. Splitting the timing estimation from relocation makes spatial connectivity and computational cost a controllable part of a large joint inversion.

papers.t: Propagation of Subduction Polarity Reversal Along Arc‐Continent Convergent Margin: Insights From 3D Geodynamic Simulations
in: National Key Laboratory of Uranium Resources Exploration‐Mining and Nuclear Remote Sensing East China University of Technology Nanchang China
Engineering Research Center for Seismic Disaster Prevention and Engineering Geological Disaster Detection of Jiangxi Province (East China University of Technology) Nanchang China
State Key Laboratory of Precision Geodesy School of Earth and Space Sciences University of Science and Technology of China Hefei China
tk: 3D geodynamic simulations show that subduction polarity reversal propagation requires a thermally aged and rheologically strong subducting lithosphere, whereas weak lithosphere leads to slab tearing.
三维动力学模拟表明，俯冲极性反转的传播需要高热龄和强流变性的岩石圈。
papers.ab: Subduction polarity reversal (SPR) driven by arc‐continent collision stands as a crucial process to establish new subduction zones throughout the Phanerozoic. Despite its inherent 3D nature, investigations of SPR along extensive arc–continent collision margins have largely been confined to 2D models, providing limited perspectives on the collision‐perpendicular propagation of SPR and the associated tectonic evolution. In this study, we establish a 3D numerical model to examine the geodynamic viability and tectonic responses of SPR propagation in the context of arc‐continent collision. Through systematic parameter testing, we demonstrate that the SPR propagation can only occur when the subducting lithosphere is both thermally aged and rheologically strong. In contrast, simulations involving young or rheologically weak lithosphere result in slab tearing or slab break‐off, thereby interrupting SPR propagation. Our study offers new geodynamic insights into how the extensive Vitiaz and Andaman–Sumatra trenches were initiated and why slab tearing occurs in the Philippine and Vanuatu subduction zones.

papers.t: Introduction to the Special Section on Advancing Physics-Based Ground-Motion Simulations for Seismic Hazard Applications
in: IIstituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Rome, Italy
Middle East Technical University, Ankara, Türkiye
University of Canterbury, Canterbury, New Zealand
The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan
U.S. Geological Survey, Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.
Politecnico di Milano, Milano, Italy
tk: This paper introduces a special section highlighting recent advancements, methodologies, and applications in physics-based ground-motion simulations for seismic hazard assessment.
本文介绍了关于地震危险性分析中物理强地面运动模拟最新进展的专题。

papers.t: The 24 June 2026 Venezuela Earthquake Sequence: A Multifault Mw 7.6 Supershear Rupture on the Boconó and San Sebastián Faults Constrained by Near- and Far-Field Observations
in: National Seismological Center, University of Chile, Santiago, Chile
Department of Structural and Geotechnical Engineering, School of Engineering, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, Santiago, Chile
Seismic Risk Program, University of Chile, Santiago, Chile
Department of Civil Engineering, Universidad Católica de la Santí­sima Concepción, Concepción, Chile
Caracas, Venezuela
Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Central de Venezuela, Caracas, Distrito Capital, Venezuela
Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Simón Bolívar, Caracas, Distrito Capital, Venezuela
Fundación Venezolana de Investigaciones Sismológicas, Caracas, Distrito Capital, Venezuela
tk: The 2026 Mw 7.6 Venezuela earthquake was a multifault, supershear rupture spanning the Boconó and San Sebastián faults, characterized by an unusually long 70-second duration.
2026年委内瑞拉Mw7.6地震是跨越双断层的超剪切破裂事件。
papers.ab: On 24 June 2026, northern Venezuela was struck by a large and destructive earthquake with a scalar seismic moment equivalent to Mw 7.6. A preliminary source inversion yields a finite-fault model with two distinct plane solutions, providing evidence that the rupture propagated across two fault segments: an initial rupture along the right-lateral Boconó fault system, followed by propagation onto the offshore San Sebastián fault (SSF). The duration of ∼70 s is approximately twice the value predicted by global scaling laws, consistent with an unusually extended or multisegment source process confirmed by a multiple point source W-phase analysis. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar surface deformation models support the two-fault rupture geometry. Critically, strong-motion recordings and backprojection analysis from Alaska, European, and western United States networks indicate that the rupture along the SSF reached supershear velocities of up to ∼ 5.5 km/s at distances of ∼50 km from the hypocenter. The event released strain consistent with the slip deficit inferred from regional Global Navigation Satellite System deformation data, which had accumulated to a potential Mw 7.6 equivalent along these faults. Only a few aftershocks are observed in the inferred supershear velocity zones of the fault plane.

papers.t: Velocity Model Building and Editing With Guided Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
in: Physical Science and Engineering Division King Abdullah University of Science and Technology Thuwal Saudi Arabia
tk: A unified framework using guided denoising diffusion implicit models (DDIM) is introduced for high-resolution seismic velocity model building and localized editing.
引入了一种基于引导去噪扩散隐式模型（DDIM）的速度模型构建与局部编辑统一框架。
papers.ab: Velocity‐model building is a fundamental component of seismic imaging workflows, yet they remain challenging inverse problems due to limited data coverage, strong nonlinearity, and the need to incorporate heterogeneous sources of information. Such information, like wells, can have a localized influence on the velocity model. In this work, we introduce a unified framework for velocity model editing and velocity model building that combines learned diffusion priors with structurally preconditioned inverse problem formulations. A diffusion model is trained on high‐resolution synthetic velocity models to learn a data‐driven prior, which is then exploited through Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models inversion and guided sampling. For localized velocity model editing, we integrate the diffusion prior with a structurally preconditioned Tikhonov inversion, enabling controlled modification of target regions while preserving the global characteristics of the background model. For full velocity model building, we formulate a well‐matching inverse problem augmented with imaging‐based regularization and solve it using a conventional least‐squares approach, the proposed Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model guided method, and Diffusion Posterior Sampling. Numerical experiments on synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that diffusion‐based approaches consistently recover sharper interfaces and higher‐resolution structures than classical least‐squares inversion. Field data applications on the Viking Graben data set further validate the robustness of the proposed framework for both editing and model building under realistic acquisition conditions.

papers.t: When Earthquakes Cross the Gap: Physics-Based Dynamic Modeling of Stepover Jumps in Normal Faults
in: Autorité de Radioprotection et de Sureté Nucléaire (ASNR), PSE-ENV/SCAN/BERSSIN, Fontenay aux Roses, France
Now at, University of Grenoble Alpes, Univ. Savoie Mont Blanc, CNRS, IRD, University of Gustave Eiffel, ISTerre, Grenoble, France
Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, La Jolla, California, U.S.A.
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität, München, Germany
tk: 3D dynamic rupture simulations of normal-fault stepovers reveal that geometric trade-offs, stress-shadowing, and dynamic effects control rupture propagation, which static Coulomb stress changes fail to fully predict.
三维动态破裂模拟表明，正断层阶区跳跃受几何权衡和应力遮蔽控制，静态库仑应力难以完全预测。
papers.ab: Understanding the mechanisms that enable earthquakes to jump across stepovers in fault systems is essential for improving seismic hazard assessment. Although many previous studies focused on strike-slip fault systems, the physics of rupture jumping across normal faults remains less investigated. In this study, we perform a series of 3D dynamic rupture simulations to explore the key factors that govern rupture jumps across normal-fault segments. By systematically varying critical parameters such as prestress levels, principal stress orientation, the distance between emitting and potentially triggered faults, and their relative positions, we identify conditions and dynamic effects that allow ruptures to successfully jump stepovers of up to 5 km. Our findings provide insights into why some dynamically triggered events propagate as self-sustained runaway ruptures, while others are rapidly self-arrested after nucleation. Our results highlight the trade-offs between the stress-shadowing effect, relative fault positioning, fault proximity, and stopping phases. For instance, fault geometry introduces a fundamental trade-off: closely spaced fault sections enhance rupture-jump potential, yet do not necessarily favor larger magnitudes. For very closely spaced faults, stress-shadowing suppresses slip and limits magnitude, whereas at larger gaps, where the shadow weakens, the rupture can grow and release more energy. Our simulations show that the largest magnitudes occur in configurations where the receiver fault lies on the hanging wall of the emitter fault at specific overlap and gap distances, highlighting the strong geometric control on multifault earthquake behavior for normal faults. Furthermore, the simulations reveal that the static Coulomb stress change approach, commonly used to predict rupture connectivity, does not fully capture the complexities of dynamic rupture processes across normal-fault systems: Dynamically jumping between normal-fault segments is more rare than static criteria would suggest.

papers.t: Earthquake Seismogram Denoising Across Time, Time‐Frequency, and Hybrid Domain Approaches
in: Institute of Geophysics ETH Zurich Zurich Switzerland
tk: A hybrid sequential deep learning model outperforms single-domain architectures in earthquake seismogram denoising, preserving sharp onsets while detecting low-SNR events.
混合序列深度学习模型在地震波去噪中优于单域模型，在检测低信噪比事件的同时保留了清晰的初至。
papers.ab: Deep learning earthquake signal denoisers commonly operate directly on waveform data or on time‐frequency representations, yet the impact of this design choice has not been systematically assessed under controlled conditions. Here we design and benchmark four comparable deep learning architectures to assess the effect of input data representation: a time‐domain denoiser, a time‐frequency denoiser–the Earthquake Seismogram (EQS) Denoiser–and two hybrid models processing both domains in parallel or sequentially. We evaluate waveform quality as a direct measure of denoising performance and assess the impact on signal detection and phase picking tasks using standard phase pickers. We further examine how denoising enhances signal onsets using a dedicated first‐motion polarity model, benchmark the best‐performing model against state‐of‐the‐art denoisers, and evaluate its generalization to out‐of‐distribution data. Our results show that the time‐domain model produces the most accurate waveforms at high signal‐to‐noise ratios (SNRs), but fails to detect event signals at low SNRs. The time‐frequency denoiser captures event signals down to lower SNRs but can introduce artifacts such as smeared onsets due to the time‐frequency binning. Hybrid models mitigate shortcomings of single‐domain approaches. The hybrid sequential model , which extends the EQS architecture, demonstrates strong signal detection at low SNRs while preserving sharp onsets, improving phase picking and extending first‐motion polarity determination to lower SNRs compared to raw or bandpass‐filtered data. Overall, surpasses benchmark models across every waveform and downstream task metric for both in‐ and out‐of‐distribution data, demonstrating that hybrid domain processing is a powerful strategy for accurate seismic denoising.

papers.t: A Seismic Crustal Stratigraphy on Mars Constrained by Seismic Waveforms and Receiver Functions
in: Laboratory of Seismology and Physics of Earth’s Interior, School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, ; Hefei, China
China Earthquake Networks Center, Beijing, China
Department of Geosciences, Stony Brook University, ; Stony Brook, New York, U.S.A.
tk: Constrains Mars' crustal stratigraphy using marsquake waveforms and receiver functions, revealing a low-velocity layer with negative shear-wave anisotropy on both sides.
利用波形和接收函数约束火星地壳层序，发现具负各向异性的低速层。
papers.ab: Seismic crustal stratigraphy of Mars is one of the key features that can be used to infer the internal composition of Mars and decipher the evolution of the planet. Here, we construct a detailed seismic stratigraphy of Mars from the source region of a marsquake (event S0235b) in Cerberus Fossae to the Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport landing site. Seismic velocity structures are constrained by waveforms recorded for event S0235b and receiver functions extracted from the seismic data of four quality-A marsquakes. The inferred crustal stratigraphy consists of four layers on the landing site and three layers on the source side. Models on the both sides have a low-velocity layer sandwiched between the high-velocity layers at the top and the bottom, with the low-velocity layer on the source side situated at a depth range of 2.7–4.3 km having an SH–SV shear-wave anisotropy of −16% and the low-velocity layer on the landing site situated at a depth range of 3.9–6.2 km having an SH–SV shear-wave anisotropy of −18%. The low-velocity layers overlay a layer with similar seismic velocities, but they are overlain by two distinct layers on the landing site and a single layer on the source side. The inferred crust–mantle discontinuity has a depth of 29.5 km on the source side and 23.0 km on the landing site. The major advancements of this study from the existing crustal-scale models include the discovery of the low-velocity layer sandwiched between the high-velocity layers and well-constrained both P- and S-wave velocities in the individual layers; both are attributed to the waveform data that are first employed in this study. Synthetic tests indicate that our model features are well resolved by the waveform data, and so are the differences from the existing models.

papers.t: Frequency- and Component-Dependent Topographic Effects in Alpine Valleys Using 3D Physics-Based Simulations
tk: 3D spectral-element simulations of the Swiss Rhône Valley reveal that Alpine topography systematically deamplifies horizontal ground motion while consistently amplifying vertical motion.
三维谱元模拟表明，阿尔卑斯地形系统性地减弱了水平地面运动并放大了垂直运动。
papers.ab: We present three-dimensional (3D) spectral-element simulations of seismic wave propagation in the Swiss Rhône Valley to quantify how realistic Alpine topography affects ground motion across frequency bands. The simulations incorporate a digital elevation model–based free surface topography representation, a 3D crustal velocity model, and geotechnically constrained near-surface layers. The simulations are performed for three local earthquakes (Mw 3.2–4.5) recorded in two different configurations: topographic and flat-surface with basin geometry preserved. Topo/flat spectral ratios reveal a systematic component asymmetry in the topographic response. At mountain sites sampled by a spatially uniform synthetic grid, horizontal motion is deamplified across the dominant low-to-intermediate frequency bands (median 0.80–0.97× at 0.05–0.50 Hz), whereas vertical motion is consistently amplified (1.16–2.32×). The real seismic network with preferential sites confirms the strong vertical amplification, whereas the horizontal regime yields weak deamplification (0.65–1.00×). Basin sites exhibit mixed horizontal response and strong vertical amplification, consistent with coupled topographic scattering and basin-wave interactions as well as excitation of the Rhône basin’s fundamental frequencies. The observed asymmetry is consistent with topography-induced mode conversion and constructive interference associated with Alpine ridge geometry. These results demonstrate that realistic surface topography can fundamentally redistribute seismic energy between motion components and that sparse observational networks may incompletely capture this behavior. Physics-based simulations with realistic relief and spatially unbiased receiver sampling therefore provide a complementary framework for seismic hazard assessment in mountainous terrain.

papers.t: Frequency- and Component-Dependent Topographic Effects in Alpine Valleys Using 3D Physics-Based Simulations
tk: 3D spectral-element simulations in the Swiss Rhône Valley reveal that realistic Alpine topography systematically deamplifies horizontal and amplifies vertical ground motion.
3D谱元模拟表明高山地形会减弱水平向并放大垂直向地面运动。
papers.ab: We present three-dimensional (3D) spectral-element simulations of seismic wave propagation in the Swiss Rhône Valley to quantify how realistic Alpine topography affects ground motion across frequency bands. The simulations incorporate a digital elevation model–based free surface topography representation, a 3D crustal velocity model, and geotechnically constrained near-surface layers. The simulations are performed for three local earthquakes (Mw 3.2–4.5) recorded in two different configurations: topographic and flat-surface with basin geometry preserved. Topo/flat spectral ratios reveal a systematic component asymmetry in the topographic response. At mountain sites sampled by a spatially uniform synthetic grid, horizontal motion is deamplified across the dominant low-to-intermediate frequency bands (median 0.80–0.97× at 0.05–0.50 Hz), whereas vertical motion is consistently amplified (1.16–2.32×). The real seismic network with preferential sites confirms the strong vertical amplification, whereas the horizontal regime yields weak deamplification (0.65–1.00×). Basin sites exhibit mixed horizontal response and strong vertical amplification, consistent with coupled topographic scattering and basin-wave interactions as well as excitation of the Rhône basin’s fundamental frequencies. The observed asymmetry is consistent with topography-induced mode conversion and constructive interference associated with Alpine ridge geometry. These results demonstrate that realistic surface topography can fundamentally redistribute seismic energy between motion components and that sparse observational networks may incompletely capture this behavior. Physics-based simulations with realistic relief and spatially unbiased receiver sampling therefore provide a complementary framework for seismic hazard assessment in mountainous terrain.

papers.t: Subsurface basin structure, seismic site conditions and earthquake damage: case study of the Gölbaşi basin, Türkiye
tk: This study integrates microgravity and SPAC ambient noise measurements to map the Gölbaşı Basin's subsurface structure, revealing a strong correlation between sediment thickness and 2023 earthquake damage.
本研究结合微重力和SPAC方法探测了Gölbaşı盆地结构，揭示了沉积层厚度与2023年地震震害之间的强相关性。
papers.ab: Gölbaşı (Adıyaman) Town, located within a basin along a left-stepping segment of the East Anatolian Fault Zone in Türkiye, experienced severe damage during the 6 February 2023 Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.6 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. Widespread liquefaction, ground subsidence, lateral spreading, bearing capacity failures and building collapses occurred, with their spatial distribution suggesting a strong association between basin geometry and ground motion amplification. This study investigates the subsurface geometry and sediment thickness of the Gölbaşı Basin using an integrated approach combining microgravity measurements and Spatial Autocorrelation (SPAC) analyses. A total of 120 microgravity measurements were conducted to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of low-density alluvial deposits, and two-dimensional gravity models were constructed along four profiles. Additionally, SPAC measurements at 20 locations yielded deep shear-wave velocity (Vs) profiles, from which Vs30 values were derived. Basin-depth proxies (Z 1.0 and Z 2.5 ) were subsequently estimated from Vs30 using empirical relationships. The basin contains up to approximately 700 m of unconsolidated sediments. Variations in sediment thickness and basin geometry produce significant lateral heterogeneity in seismic velocity and impedance contrasts across the basin. Areas underlain by the thickest sediments experienced the most severe structural damage. The results demonstrate a strong spatial association between sediment thickness, basin geometry, seismic site conditions, and the observed distribution of structural damage. A neighborhood-based Pearson correlation analysis revealed a very strong positive relationship between the severe-damage ratio and sediment thickness ( r = 0.905, p 2.5 ( r = 0.763, p = 0.017) and a strong negative correlation with Vs30 ( r = − 0.698, p = 0.037). Although the correlations with Z 1.0 and the gravity anomaly did not reach the 5% significance level, they exhibited similarly strong spatial trends. Given the limited number of neighborhoods analyzed ( n = 9), these results are interpreted as exploratory spatial associations rather than evidence of causal relationships. Nevertheless, the agreement among the gravity-derived basin geometry, SPAC-derived site parameters, and the damage analysis indicates that sediment thickness and subsurface basin structure were significant contributors to the spatial distribution of earthquake damage.

papers.t: The Role of Slab Folding in Modulating the Landscape Evolution of Ribbon Collision
in: School of Geosciences University of Sydney Sydney NSW Australia
BHP Pty Ltd Adelaide SA Australia
Department of Environmental and Life Sciences University of Newcastle Newcastle NSW Australia

tk: Slab folding modulates orogenic topography, while sediment loading controls regional lithospheric extension versus localized fault subsidence.
板块折叠调节造山带地形，且沉积载荷控制区域伸展与局部断层沉降。
papers.ab: We investigate how slab folding impacts the topographic evolution of collisional orogens and the sediment supply to the associated basins, under the effect of different erosion and sedimentation rates. Results show that when slab folding causes the steepening of the subducting slab, it enhances topographic growth in the orogen at rates between 0.008 and 0.310 mm/yr and increases the sediment thickness at rates between 0.05 and 0.3 mm/yr. The topographic growth depends on the erosion rate, which is up to 0.2 mm/yr in our simulations. In the basin, the sedimentation rate not only depends on the erosion rate in the orogen, but also on how efficiently sediments are transported to the basin. Results from a correlation test between the plastic strain and the cumulated sedimentation suggest that the load of sediments affects deformation at two different spatio‐temporal scales. The load caused by sedimentation rates of 0.3 mm/yr or more enhances the regional deformation that causes lithospheric extension in the basin. Conversely, the load of sedimentation rates below 0.3 mm/yr increases the localized deformation that causes tectonic subsidence in normal faults. These results highlight how erosion rates control the topography evolution of the orogen, and how sedimentation rates enhance regional deformation or/and localized tectonic subsidence in the basin.

papers.t: Effects of Microstructural Heterogeneity on the Macroscopic Spectrum of Elastically Accommodated Grain‐Boundary Sliding
in: Bullard Laboratories Department of Earth Sciences University of Cambridge Cambridge UK
tk: Numerical simulations show that a broad distribution of grain-boundary viscosities, rather than grain-size variance, broadens the elastically accommodated grain-boundary sliding attenuation peak into a wide background.
数值模拟表明，晶界黏度的宽分布（而非晶粒尺寸变化）使晶界滑动衰减峰变宽。
papers.ab: Elastically accommodated grain‐boundary sliding (EAGBS) is a plausible source of upper‐mantle seismic attenuation and dispersion, yet classical theory predicts a localized Debye‐like peak that is absent or only weakly expressed in dry olivine experiments. Here we test whether microstructural heterogeneity can explain this discrepancy using 2‐D finite‐element simulations on periodic Voronoi tessellations. We find that irregular grain geometry changes the baseline EAGBS response relative to the regular hexagonal benchmark, but increasing grain‐size variance alone produces only modest changes in modulus and peak height, with little spectral broadening. In contrast, a broad distribution of grain‐boundary viscosities progressively suppresses and broadens the Debye‐like loss peak into a weak background spanning a wide frequency interval. This broadening arises from the superposition of many localized relaxation processes with distinct characteristic timescales and motivates a reduced‐order 0‐D description of the aggregate response. These results suggest that the absence of a pronounced EAGBS peak in dry olivine does not necessarily imply the absence of EAGBS mechanism itself. If grain boundaries sample a sufficiently broad viscosity distribution, the macroscopic EAGBS contribution may appear experimentally only as part of a broad attenuation background, while still remaining relevant for upper‐mantle seismic attenuation and velocity dispersion.

papers.t: A modeling strategy for ground motion prediction equations based on relative importance analysis
in: Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration
tk: Proposes a new modeling strategy for ground motion prediction equations (GMPEs) using relative importance analysis to optimize parameter selection.
提出了一种基于相对重要性分析的地震动预测方程（GMPE）建模策略。
papers.ab: Existing studies typically present the modeling strategies of ground motion models directly, and there remains a lack of methods for determining such strategies in a quantitative manner. In this study, we developed a modeling strategy for ground motion prediction equations based on model relative importance analysis. The method first decomposes the contributions of the different components within the ground motion prediction equation to the model’s interpretability and then determines the modeling strategy for the prediction equation based on the contributions in ascending order. Strong motion data from the Next Generation Attenuation-West2 project in the western United States were analyzed as a case study, to which the new method was applied to determine the peak ground acceleration prediction equation for the rock sites. The results indicate that the strategy developed herein did not exhibit systematic bias in fitting, thereby demonstrating its validity and rationality. The ground motion prediction equations determined using the modeling strategy also accurately reflected the strong motion characteristics.

in: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences Jackson School of Geosciences The University of Texas at Austin Austin TX USA

tk: Full-waveform inversion of regional earthquakes reveals a 250-km-thick Arabian lithosphere underthrusting Eurasia, suggesting continental collision initiated at ~22 Ma.
全波形反演揭示阿拉伯岩石圈向欧亚大陆下插达250公里，表明碰撞始于约22 Ma。
papers.ab: Despite being one of the most recent major orogenic events, the timing of the Arabia‐Eurasia collision is still debated. Much of the discrepancy arises due to uncertainties over the amount of continental subduction of the Arabian passive margin and the timing of a hard collision of cratonic Arabian lithosphere with Eurasia. Subducted continental lithosphere and underthrusted cratons can be imaged using high resolution seismic tomography, which can be used to improve understanding of the tectonic history of the region. In this study, we perform a full waveform inversion of seismic wave velocity beneath the Turkish‐Iranian plateau, using regional earthquakes, which provide good horizontal and vertical resolution in the upper 500 km of the mantle. We use a normalized cross‐correlation misfit function, which fits both the phase and relative amplitude of multi‐path arrivals, allowing us to extract additional information from complex triplicated waves that provide relatively good coverage of the upper mantle. Our results reveal that 250 km thick Arabian lithosphere extends horizontally beneath Eurasia. When reconstructed back in time, these results indicate that continental underthrusting and collision initiated at ∼22 Ma, which is consistent with accelerated deformation observed at this time in the geological record.

papers.t: Ground Motions on Competent Rock Sites Have Low Aleatory Variability
in: Department of Earth Sciences, Western University, London, Canada
tk: Ground motions on competent rock sites in central and eastern North America exhibit significantly lower aleatory variability at frequencies ≤5 Hz compared to soil sites.
北美中东部坚硬岩石场地的地震动在低频（≤5 Hz）下的偶然不确定性显著低于土层场地。
papers.ab: The aleatory variability of response spectral amplitudes about the median values specified in ground-motion models is significantly lower for competent rock sites in central and eastern North America (CENA), in comparison to commonly assumed values derived from soil sites. Competent CENA rock is defined as sites with near-surface shear-wave velocity >800 m/s having measured site response peaks no greater than a factor of 3 in amplitude (0.5–30 Hz). At frequencies ≤5 Hz, the within-event aleatory variability for competent rock is ∼0.4 ln units at moderate magnitudes, compared to values of 0.5–0.6 reported for soil sites. Variability on rock sites increases at higher frequencies, exceeding that for soil sites at >15 Hz. Single-station total aleatory variability for competent CENA rock sites is ∼0.5–0.6 ln units from 1 to 10 Hz.

papers.t: Evolution of Scaled Energy During Earthquake Ruptures
in: Department of Earth Sciences University of Southern California Los Angeles CA USA
tk: Scaled energy during earthquake ruptures consistently peaks in the first 20%–30% of duration, decays, and slightly rises near arrest, with deep events showing highly energetic onsets.
地震破裂期间的标度能量在初期达到峰值，随后衰减并在接近结束时略有上升，深源地震表现出更强烈的起始。
papers.ab: Earthquake ruptures radiate seismic energy in complex ways, reflecting the interplay of fault heterogeneity and rupture dynamics. How the radiated energy evolves during rupture, and whether this evolution varies systematically with earthquake properties, remains poorly understood. Here we analyze more than 1,500 global earthquakes using moment‐rate functions to quantify the temporal evolution of scaled energy (the ratio of radiated energy to seismic moment in successive time windows), complemented by comparisons with dynamic rupture simulations. We find a consistent pattern across focal mechanisms, magnitudes, and depths: scaled energy is highest in the first 20%–30% of rupture duration, decays to a steady value several times lower, and increases somewhat again near rupture termination. Deep earthquakes show a robust more energetic onset than arrest across two independent data sets. This suggests deep earthquakes typically start energetically but arrest more gradually. Strike‐slip events show slightly higher values of initial scaled energy than thrust events, while deep earthquakes exhibit overall higher scaled energy. Dynamic rupture simulations with heterogeneous prestress and a hierarchical asperity model reproduce the energetic onset, decay, and late‐stage rise near arrest, underscoring the important roles of spatially correlated fault heterogeneity, proximity to failure, and rheology. The distinct energy evolution of earthquakes deeper than 550 km may reflect a different seismogenic mechanism than that of shallow earthquakes. The temporal evolution of scaled energy provides a new constraint on earthquake source physics, offering a diagnostic tool for evaluating rupture models and understanding both shallow and deep earthquake processes.

papers.t: Quantum spin regulates the catalytic cycle beyond binding energy
tk: The paper introduces an augmented Onsager operator framework to show how quantum spin regulates non-dissipative circulation in catalytic cycles.
论文提出增强翁萨格算子框架，揭示量子自旋对催化循环的调节作用。
papers.ab: Conventional catalytic descriptors evaluate symmetric, dissipative responses ($\mathcal{D}$), remaining blind to the antisymmetric, non-dissipative circulation ($\mathcal{L}$) associated with cyclic catalyst turnover. We address this by applying an augmented Onsager operator, $\mathcal{A} = \mathcal{D} + \mathcal{L}$, to catalytic interfaces. Through Onsager--Casimir parity rules, we show that electron spin governs this non-dissipative circulation within the reduced state space, as antisymmetric coupling necessitates a time-reversal-odd coordinate. We map these multi-physical couplings (Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical-Chemical-Electrical-Spin) using a Hasse diagram and introduce a basis-invariant Gateway number to quantify circulation relative to dissipation, thereby expanding standard one-dimensional volcano plots into a two-dimensional activity surface. Using metal--nitrogen single-atom sites on doped carbon as a model, published electronic-structure calculations supply the static response quantities from which both operator components can be constructed. Finally, we propose an explicitly falsifiable experimental test utilising magnetic field modulation near a spin-crossover to probe the effect of quantum spin on this non-dissipative regime.

papers.t: Fifty Years Later: Revisiting Viking 2 Seismic Signals Through InSight
in: SKLab‐DeepMinE MOEKLab‐OBCE School of Earth and Space Sciences Peking University Beijing China
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting Peking University Beijing China
The Viking Seismology Team Pasadena CA USA
Retired
tk: Reinterprets Viking 2's candidate seismic events using InSight's Martian seismicity framework, suggesting they represent either local high-frequency events, a distant tectonic marsquake, or an impact.
利用InSight火星地震背景重新解释了海盗2号的候选地震信号。
papers.ab: For nearly 50 years, the origin of the candidate seismic signals recorded by Viking 2 remained unresolved because of limited instrumental sensitivity, onboard observation, data compression, and the absence of Martian seismic context. Here we reconstruct the Viking seismic workflow and reinterpret the two Viking candidate events, recorded on sol 53 and sol 80, using the seismic context established by InSight. We show that the Viking seismometer was optimized for high‐spectral‐frequency seismic signals, consequently reducing its sensitivity to low‐spectral‐frequency events. If the original 10‐s S‐P travel‐time difference is correct, the inferred location of the sol 80 event overlaps the broad northern‐plains source region suggested for the seasonally recurrent high‐spectral‐frequency and 2.4‐Hz marsquake populations observed by InSight. Alternatively, if the first‐arrival phase represents a crustal conversion phase rather than a direct P wave, the sol 80 event corresponds to a distant tectonic (low‐spectral‐frequency or broadband) marsquake with an estimated moment magnitude of M W 4.6–4.8 or M W 4.9–5.1. A meteorite impact origin cannot be excluded either. The two Viking seismic signals decay more rapidly than typical InSight marsquakes, suggesting heterogeneity in the Martian attenuation structure. Together, these findings integrate Viking observations into the modern framework of Martian seismicity, illustrating how a legacy planetary data set can acquire renewed scientific implications when re‐examined in light of subsequent mission data.

papers.t: Geothermal gradient change during subduction recorded by ultrahigh-pressure eclogite
tk: Discovery of a young ultrahigh-pressure eclogite reveals a transition from a warm to a cold geothermal gradient during active subduction.
年轻超高压榴辉岩揭示了俯冲过程中从热到冷的温度梯度转变。
papers.ab: The subduction of crustal rocks to, and exhumation from, depths greater than 90 km in the stability field of the mineral coesite is known as ultrahigh-pressure metamorphism, widely regarded as evidence for cold subduction. This assumption stems from peak metamorphic conditions of ultrahigh-pressure rocks, which indicate low subduction gradients of less than 330 °C GPa −1 , but direct evidence for such a cold prograde evolution is lacking. Here we report the discovery of a young ultrahigh-pressure eclogite in eastern Papua New Guinea. We find (sub)micrometre-sized inclusions of coesite in intermediate growth zones of garnet crystals and zircon inclusions revealing a U–Pb age of approximately 4.4 million years. Petrographic observations and thermo-barometric methods show that the prograde subduction path was initially warm with an apparent average gradient of approximately 470 °C GPa −1 until a depth of about 45 km, before switching to a cold thermal regime with ultrafast subduction rates of greater than 60 mm yr −1 (vertical component). This change in geothermal gradients can be explained by shear heating and/or by formation during the non-steady-state phase of a young subduction zone. We propose that high geothermal gradients at shallow levels of deep subduction systems might be common, challenging the use of peak metamorphic conditions as indicator for subduction zone thermal structures.

papers.t: Scattering‐to‐Intrinsic Transition Governing Coda Attenuation in the US Continental Crust
in: Key Laboratory of Planetary Science and Frontier Technology Institute of Geology and Geophysics Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China

tk: S-wave coda attenuation in the US continental crust transitions from scattering-dominated at lower frequencies (1.5–3 Hz) to intrinsic-dominated at higher frequencies (6–12 Hz).
美国大陆地壳S波包络衰减在低频受散射主导，高频受固有吸收主导。
papers.ab: Seismic attenuation is a key indicator of crustal heterogeneity and energy dissipation, yet the physical mechanism of coda‐wave attenuation remains unclear due to the combined influence of scattering and intrinsic absorption. In this study, we analyze multi‐frequency S‐wave coda attenuation using the seismic recordings from USArray. Our results reveal that S‐wave coda attenuation exhibits pronounced frequency dependence, with distinct dominant mechanisms across different frequency bands. At lower frequencies (1.5 and 3 Hz), attenuation is primarily controlled by scattering associated with crustal heterogeneities and velocity contrasts, whereas at higher frequencies (6 and 12 Hz), intrinsic absorption becomes the dominant mechanism and exhibits a strong correlation with surface heat flow, consistent with temperature‐dependent viscoelastic dissipation. Comparisons with attenuation models derived from other seismic phases highlight their different sensitivities to depth and frequency, indicating that no single approach can fully capture the complexity of attenuation. These findings underscore the diagnostic value of multi‐frequency coda‐wave attenuation and highlight the importance of integrating various attenuation measurement methods to better constrain crustal heterogeneity and thermal state, with implications for improved crustal imaging and geodynamic interpretation.

papers.t: Subduction Recycling and Closure of the Paleo‐Asian Ocean in the Beishan Orogen: Constraints From the Niujuanzi Ophiolitic Mélange and Associated Intrusions
in: Guangxi Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution Control Theory and Technology College of Environmental Science and Engineering Guilin University of Technology Guilin China
Guangxi Key Laboratory of Hidden Metallic Ore Deposits Exploration College of Earth Sciences Guilin University of Technology Guilin China
National Key Laboratory of Ecological Security and Resource Utilization in Arid Areas Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography Chinese Academy of Sciences Urumqi China
tk: Geochronological and geochemical data from the Niujuanzi ophiolitic mélange constrain the Paleo-Asian Ocean's subduction, closure, and postcollisional transition in the Beishan Orogen.
北山造山带牛圈子蛇绿混杂岩的年代学和地球化学数据约束了古亚洲洋的俯冲、闭合及碰撞后转变。
papers.ab: Ophiolitic mélanges and associated intrusions provide key archives for reconstructing the evolution of ancient ocean basins and subduction‐related mantle modification. The Hongliuhe–Niujuanzi–Xichangjing ophiolitic mélange in the central Beishan Orogen preserves important records of the Paleo‐Asian Ocean, but the timing of oceanic subduction, terminal closure, and subsequent postcollisional reworking in the Niujuanzi remain debated. Here we integrate field observations, zircon U–Pb geochronology, whole‐rock and mineral geochemistry, and Sr–Nd–Hf–Pb isotopic data from the newly dated and geochemically characterized ophiolitic rocks and associated dioritic to granodioritic intrusions. Zircon U–Pb ages define three Paleozoic magmatic episodes: Early Silurian diorites at 435–427 Ma, Late Silurian ophiolitic gabbros at 423–418 Ma, and Early Devonian granodiorites at ca. 403 Ma. The diorites display continental arc‐like geochemical signatures and were derived from a lithospheric mantle source modified by slab‐derived fluids. The gabbros show N‐MORB‐like affinities with weak subduction‐related enrichment, consistent with formation in an SSZ setting. The granodiorites were generated mainly by partial melting of the ancient lower crust with minor mantle input, recording a transition to postcollisional extension. Silicate in situ Pb isotopes exhibit a temporal shift toward Indian MORB‐like signatures from the Early Silurian to Early Devonian, indicating progressive mantle source modification by recycled subduction components. These results demonstrate that the Niujuanzi basin remained active until the Late Silurian, closed by the end‐Silurian, closed during the latest Silurian to the earliest Devonian (ca. 418 Ma), and transitioned to postcollisional extension in the Early Devonian, providing a refined geodynamic model for the central Beishan Orogen.

papers.t: A Prompt Elastogravity Signal–Based Rapid Source Characterization Module for Tsunami Warning Support in Alaska
in: Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur, Université Côte d’Azur, IRD, CNRS, Géoazur, Valbonne, France
Nantes Université, CNRS, Laboratoire de Planétologie et Géosciences, Nantes, France
Alaska Earthquake Center, Geophysical Institute, University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, Alaska, U.S.A.
tk: A pseudo-real-time pipeline using prompt elastogravity signals and deep learning rapidly characterizes major Alaskan earthquakes within 90–120 seconds to support tsunami warnings.
基于瞬态弹性重力信号和深度学习的伪实时系统可在90-120秒内快速表征阿拉斯加特大地震，支持海啸预警。
papers.ab: State-of-the-art earthquake early warning systems relying on seismic waves tend to underestimate the magnitude of large earthquakes, which typically results in dramatic underestimation of tsunami forecasts. Systems relying on other types of data (W phase, Global Navigation Satellite System) may provide more reliable magnitude estimates for very large seismic events but at the cost of slower warning. Prompt elastogravity signals (PEGS) have shown potential to provide unsaturated magnitude estimates more rapidly than systems based on other data. In this study, we present the first fully automated pseudo-real-time implementation of a PEGS-based approach on the Alaska seismic network. We designed a continuous pipeline that combines an automatic detection module, a real-time waveform processing protocol, and a PEGS-based deep-learning model for rapid source characterization. To evaluate operational resilience, we conducted a 13-month continuous playback, alongside targeted testing of 42 moderate regional earthquakes and 37 major teleseismic events recorded between 2018 and 2025. By implementing a multiparametric alert criterion—requiring a stable Mw ≥7.8 inference, network consensus, and regional location—the system achieved a strict zero false-alarm rate. Crucially, the pipeline accurately tracked the magnitude and focal mechanism of three major regional earthquakes (the 2018 Mw 7.9 Kodiak, 2020 Mw 7.8 Shumagin, and 2021 Mw 8.2 Chignik events) within 90–120 s of their onset. Although highly robust to typical automated picking errors (± 2 s), comparative tests reveal that the system’s sensitivity limit is strictly bound to network density. We are presently running a real-time test system in partnership with the Alaska Earthquake Center. In addition to its validation against simulated real-time data presented in this study, the regular occurrence of Mw ≥7.8 earthquakes in the region offers a concrete possibility to test the system against real-time-acquired data in the next 2–4 yr.
