papers.t: Combining horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratios with empirical amplification functions to develop high resolution site amplification maps: Application to Sion, Switzerland
tk: This study combines ambient-noise HVSR with empirical amplification functions using canonical correlation and clustering to produce high-resolution site amplification maps for Sion, Switzerland.
本研究结合背景噪声HVSR与经验放大函数，在瑞士锡永实现了高分辨率场地放大图的绘制。
papers.ab: Site amplification significantly influences ground shaking intensity during earthquakes and is a key factor in seismic hazard assessment and microzonation. Traditional methods for mapping site amplification that use earthquake recordings often face challenges related to spatial resolution and capturing local soil heterogeneities. This study takes the advantage of Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratios (HVSR) obtained from ambient noise measurements to develop high-resolution site amplification maps. The proposed methodology combines HVSR clustering, canonical correlation analysis (CC), and geostatistical interpolation to predict site amplification across the area of Sion (Switzerland). Spatial patterns are modelled using kriging, and results are compared with independent hybrid standard spectral ratio (SSRh) amplification estimates. The results show consistent identification of strong amplification in the central part of the valley across all methods, highlighting the control of basin geometry on low-frequency site response. Among the tested approaches, CC provides the best overall agreement with SSRh in terms of spatial pattern and statistical performance (lower Root Mean Squared Error), although it systematically underestimates amplification values by up to a factor of ∼2.5. The Pearson correlation-based clustering approach produces smoother amplification fields and larger discrepancies at basin edges, with underestimation of up to a factor of ∼1.5 relative to SSRh. Despite differences in amplitude, all methods reproduce the main frequency-dependent behaviour, with low frequencies controlled by deep basin resonance and higher frequencies influenced by shallow structures. Validation against independent datasets indicates good consistency in spatial trends, while also highlighting limitations of statistical models in capturing extreme amplification in deep Alpine basins. Overall, the results demonstrate that combining HVSR-based methods with empirical amplification functions improves the spatial resolution of site response estimates. CC offers the most robust framework among the tested approaches, while HVSR clustering remains useful for rapid or data-limited microzonation. The study highlights the benefit of multi-method strategies for improving seismic microzonation in complex geological environments.

papers.t: Efficient Physics-Informed Ground-Motion Simulations with Reduced-Order Models: CyberShake Implications and High-Resolution Site Terms for Southern San Andreas Fault Earthquakes
in: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, University of California, San Diego, La Jolla, California, U.S.A.
Statewide California Earthquake Center, University of Southern California, Los Angeles, California, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Pasadena, California, U.S.A.
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Ludwig-Maximillians-Universität München, Munich, Germany
tk: A scientific machine learning reduced-order model based on proper orthogonal decomposition accelerates physics-based ground-motion simulations for seismic hazard analysis by a factor of 336.
基于本征正交分解的科学机器学习降阶模型将物理地震动模拟加速了336倍。
papers.ab: Recent advances in Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Analysis (PSHA) leverage physics-based ground-motion simulations to estimate seismic hazard, such as the CyberShake project. However, computational costs quickly escalate when performing PSHA for numerous faults or sites and can become prohibitively expensive. To reduce computational demands, CyberShake uses reciprocity and interpolates physics-informed corrections from simulations conducted at fewer locations, but the accuracy of these interpolations remains poorly quantified. To quantify the interpolation accuracy, we derive high-resolution, frequency-dependent site terms for southern California and compare them with interpolated site terms using the CyberShake approach. We accomplish this by performing a set of earthquake point-source simulations distributed along the nonplanar fault geometry for the southern San Andreas fault (SSAF) extending from Bombay Beach to Lake Hughes. Using SeisSol, we simulate three minutes of viscoelastic seismic wave propagation for these sources and store the horizontal-component Green’s functions for 480,000 sites. We then use a scientific machine learning approach based on interpolated proper orthogonal decomposition to construct an accurate reduced-order model of the Green’s functions to efficiently predict effective amplitude spectra (EAS) for finite-source rupture models of SSAF earthquakes. Using minimum curvature interpolation with tension, as used in CyberShake, we compare the interpolated site terms against our high-resolution site terms. We identify local discrepancies with EAS differing by up to a factor of approximately three. Furthermore, we identify locations where unexpectedly high or low ground motions are missed when using the interpolated dataset for these earthquakes. We estimate that our approach may be used within CyberShake to reduce the time-to-solution by a factor of 336 for the entire earthquake rupture forecast. Our analysis of physics-based site terms provides more insight into the seismic hazard due to SSAF ruptures and guides future developments by combining high-performance computing and reduced-order modeling techniques for PSHA.

papers.t: Geophysical identification of geo-morphologically indistinctive Miocene maar-diatreme volcanoes in Western Bohemia and their seismic amplification effect
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Charles University
Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Geophysics
University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice
Czech Geological Survey
tk: Geophysical methods identify hidden Miocene volcanoes in Western Bohemia, revealing their impact on seismic wave amplification.
地球物理方法识别了西波西米亚地区隐藏的中新世火山，揭示了其对地震波放大的影响。
papers.ab: This study uses ambient seismic noise processing methods as the primary tool to investigate suspected maar volcanic structures at Nežichov village and Sepuska hill in West Bohemia, Czechia. The research employs ambient seismic noise surveys, gravimetric surveys, electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), and numerical modeling to analyze these structures. At Nežichov, the ambient seismic noise survey identified fundamental mode amplification frequencies, with particle motion trends indicating a complex 3D resonance structure. The gravimetric survey revealed a negative anomaly, suggesting a volcanic breccia fill. ERT results showed low resistivity zones attributed to maar lake sediments, with a high resistivity intrusion dividing these zones. At Sepuska, similar methods identified fundamental mode frequencies, with a circular amplification distribution. The gravimetric survey indicated a negative anomaly, consistent with a maar structure. The study concludes that both Nežichov and Sepuska are likely maar volcanic structures, with complex subsurface features revealed through combined geophysical methods. These findings contribute to understanding the volcanic history and geological evolution of the Bohemian Massif.

papers.t: Tracing Orogenic Evolution From Multi‐Detrital Mineral Records: U‐Pb Geochronology and Trace‐Element Constraints From Glacial Diamictites
in: School of Earth Sciences Zhejiang University Hangzhou China
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences University of Waterloo Waterloo ON Canada
State Key Laboratory of Ecological Safety and Sustainable Development in Arid Lands Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography Chinese Academy of Sciences Urumqi China
School of Resources and Environmental Engineering Hefei University of Technology Hefei China
Department of Earth Sciences University of New Brunswick Fredericton NB Canada
Hubei Key Laboratory of Paleontology and Environmental Change (Wuhan Center of China Geological Survey) Wuhan China
Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences University of Hong Kong Hong Kong China
tk: This study integrates detrital apatite, rutile, and zircon records from glacial diamictites to reconstruct the Neoproterozoic tectonic evolution of the Yangtze Block.
本研究联合冰川杂砾岩中多种碎屑矿物重建了扬子陆块新元古代造山演化。
papers.ab: Integrating multiple detrital mineral systems provides a powerful framework for reconstructing source‐region tectonothermal evolution because different minerals record complementary aspects of magmatic and metamorphic processes. Glacial diamictites are particularly valuable for this approach because extensive glacial erosion can sample broad source regions and diverse crustal levels while minimizing chemical weathering and preserving unstable mineral phases. Here, we present integrated U‐Pb geochronological and trace‐element analyses of detrital apatite and rutile from Marinoan‐aged glacial diamictites of the Yangtze Block in South China and combine these data with existing zircon data sets. Detrital apatite records dominant mafic and I‐type magmatism between ∼970 and 650 Ma, with more evolved peraluminous signatures appearing at 850–820 Ma, broadly consistent with declining zircon εHf(t) values. Detrital rutile reveals dominant Neoproterozoic (∼970–790 Ma) and subordinate Paleoproterozoic (2.2–1.8 Ga) metamorphic signatures. Zr‐in‐rutile thermometry indicates temperatures of 480°C–980°C, including a distinct ∼950–820 Ma high‐pressure, low‐temperature population consistent with blueschist‐ to eclogite‐facies conditions. These data record major tectonic transitions within the Panxi‐Hannan orogen of the northwestern Yangtze Block, from an intra‐oceanic arc (970–880 Ma) to a continental arc (870–790 Ma), followed by regional extension after 790 Ma. The cessation of rutile and metamorphic apatite ages coincides with the onset of regional extension in the source orogen. The ∼950–820 Ma cold‐subduction signature expands the global record of Tonian low‐geothermal‐gradient metamorphism. Our results demonstrate that integrating multiple detrital mineral systems yields a more complete tectonic history than any single provenance proxy.

papers.t: Exploring the potential of distributed acoustic sensing for fish bioacoustics
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Géoazur
International University of Monaco
Scientific Centre of Monaco
Princess Grace Hospital Centre
Institut de Biologie Valrose
tk: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on a seafloor fiber-optic cable to detect, isolate, and localize fish sounds in marine environments.
本研究证实了利用海底光纤分布式声学传感（DAS）技术探测和定位鱼类声音的可行性。
papers.ab: Underwater soundscapes are critical indicators of marine ecosystem health, but traditional passive acoustic monitoring with hydrophones is spatially limited and logistically challenging for long-term observations. This study investigates the potential of distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) to overcome these limitations. A field trial was conducted using a bespoke fiber-optic cable deployed off the coast of Monaco, focusing on three sound-producing Mediterranean species: Ophidion rochei , Sciaena umbra , and Epinephelus marginatus , all known for their distinct acoustic signatures. DAS recordings reveal species-specific patterns consistent with documented behaviors, and are validated by co-located hydrophone recordings. Due to its high sensor density, DAS allows the isolation and localization of individual sounds over tens of meters. The results demonstrate that DAS can detect and locate fish sounds under real-world conditions, while also assessing ambient noise levels. The DAS setup in this experiment may not match the performance of conventional hydrophones, but the approach’s potential for dense, continuous, and low-maintenance monitoring, particularly where suitable fiber-optic infrastructure already exists, points to a promising complementary role in marine conservation in the context of climate change and biodiversity loss.

papers.t: High‐Resolution Body‐Wave Tomography of Kı̄lauea's Summit Magma Storage System From a Dense Passive and Active Source Experiment
in: Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science University of Miami Miami FL USA
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute Troy NY USA
U.S. Geological Survey Cascades Volcano Observatory Vancouver WA USA
U.S. Geological Survey Evergreen CO USA
U.S. Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory Hilo HI USA
U.S. Geological Survey Alaska Volcano Observatory Anchorage AK USA
tk: A dense hybrid passive-active seismic experiment at Kīlauea's summit resolves two distinct magma reservoirs at 1–3 km depth using high-resolution body-wave travel-time tomography.
结合密集节点和主动源的联合旅行时断层成像，揭示了基拉韦厄火山下方1-3千米深处的两个独立岩浆库。
papers.ab: Imaging magma storage beneath active calderas requires resolving crustal structure at scales comparable to those of individual reservoirs. To identify potential reservoirs beneath Kı̄lauea, Hawai'i, we conducted a hybrid seismic experiment at its summit for 37 days in 2023 that combined more than 1,800 three‐component nodal seismometers with 396 vibroseis source positions, yielding about 15 million ‐ and ‐wave arrivals. Joint inversion of earthquake and active‐source travel times yields three‐dimensional models of , , and within the upper ∼4 km beneath the summit relative to mean sea level, parameterized on a 500 m grid, within which the resolution tests demonstrate recovery of sub‐kilometer to kilometer‐scale structure. The models delineate two principal magma storage regions beneath Halema'uma'u and the south caldera, each on the order of 2 km across. Both reservoirs are expressed as localized zones of reduced and moderately reduced with locally elevated at depths of 1–3 km below sea level. The anomalies are laterally distinct at shallow levels but appear to merge within a broader zone of reduced velocities at depth. Surrounding higher‐velocity domains likely represent mechanically stronger intrusive complexes that confine magma storage. Spatial correspondence between seismic velocity anomalies and independently modeled geodetic deformation sources supports the interpretation that the imaged structures represent magma storage regions. These results demonstrate that dense nodal arrays combined with hybrid passive‐active tomography can resolve reservoir‐scale structure at active volcanoes and provide an improved framework for interpreting magma storage and transport beneath Kı̄lauea.

papers.t: A collection of video footage, marker files and event files of the 2021 Geldingadalir eruption (Iceland)
in: University of Potsdam
Earth Sciences New Zealand
Icelandic Meteorological Office
Iceland GeoSurvey
University of Iceland
University of Cambridge
Charles University
Czech Academy of Sciences
tk: This dataset provides video footage, marker files, and seismic/acoustic event files documenting the July 2, 2021 crater collapses and plumes of the Geldingadalir eruption.
该数据集包含2021年冰岛火山喷发塌陷事件的视频与地震声学数据。
papers.ab: The six-month-long Geldingadalir eruption in 2021 was characterised by different episodes of effusion, which changed several times during the eruption. On 2 July 2021, the eruptive crater drained for the first time, followed by several tephra-rich plumes. Several seismic and acoustic signals were also recorded, likely caused by inner crater collapses. These collapses may also have generated the tephra-rich plumes. This collection provides marker files containing the start and end times of the observed tephra-rich plumes and collapses. Additionally, we include a table showing the durations and widths of the collapses. We have provided event files for the eight largest seismic and acoustic events. This collection also contains 2 hours of video footage of early 2 July between 03:00 to 05:00, which is a merged video from two different webcams. The video was provided by mbl.is,a news portal in Iceland. Another video shows a few hours of the erupting volcano alongside a spectrogram of the seismic data.

papers.t: Broadband Multi-Aperture Passive Scholte-Wave Imaging Using Seabed Distributed Acoustic Sensing
in: Bureau of Economic Geology, The University of Texas at Austin, Austin, U.S.A.
tk: Passive Scholte-wave imaging using seabed distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on the Texas Gulf Coast provides broadband shear-wave velocity profiles down to 2 km depth.
利用德克萨斯湾海底分布式声学传感进行被动Scholte波成像，获得了深达2公里的剪切波速度剖面。
papers.ab: Shallow-water ocean forcing provides strong broadband passive Scholte-wave illumination along a seabed distributed acoustic sensing cable on the Texas Gulf Coast. We exploit this illumination through direct processing of the uncorrelated wavefield, long-duration frequency–wavenumber stacking, and a multi-aperture strategy that preserves high-frequency spatial localization while resolving low-frequency modes. Constant-wavenumber slices enable spatially consistent multimode tracking across successive array centers. The resulting dispersion spans approximately 0.3–4.5 Hz and supports 400 1D inversions along a 51 km cable segment. These profiles form a pseudo-2D shear-wave velocity model extending from the near seafloor to approximately 2 km depth. Broad shallow low-velocity intervals are consistent with softer incised-valley fill within stiffer Pleistocene deposits. The results demonstrate that existing seabed fiber infrastructure, when coupled with strong shallow-water passive illumination, can deliver broadband regional shear-wave imaging, whereas higher-frequency active sources remain necessary to resolve the uppermost several meters.

papers.t: Microgravity Measurements Spanning 2019–2022 Indicate No Change in Magma Supply or Storage During Kīlauea's Reawakening
in: U.S. Geological Survey, Cascades Volcano Observatory Vancouver WA USA
R&D Department of Seismology and Acoustics Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI) De Bilt The Netherlands
U.S. Geological Survey, Hawaiian Volcano Observatory Hilo HI USA
U.S. Geological Survey Volcano Hazards Program Vancouver WA USA
tk: Microgravity measurements at Kīlauea from 2019 to 2022 reveal a shallow mass increase but indicate no significant changes in magma supply or reservoir geometry.
微重力测量显示基拉韦厄火山浅部质量增加，但岩浆供应无显著变化。
papers.ab: After more than 2 years of quiescence following its major 2018 flank lava effusion and summit caldera collapse, Kīlauea, Hawaiʻi, returned to frequent eruptive activity in late 2020. Microgravity measurements from the summit region in 2019 and 2022 span this reawakening and indicate a gravity increase of up to hundreds of microgals near the center of the summit caldera. Much of this increase is caused by lava that partially filled the 2018 collapse pit. We accounted for this mass by differencing digital elevation models of the summit area to determine the geometry and amount of accumulated lava and its gravity contribution at each station in the network. The remaining gravity change is best approximated by a mass increase of 6.9 × 10 10 kg (5.1–23.0 × 10 10 kg at 95% credible interval) at a depth of 480 m (121–795 m at 95% credible interval) beneath the locus of the 2018 collapse. The modeled source depth reflects the combined impacts of magma accumulation in a reservoir known from previous geophysical studies to exist at about 1–2 km depth, intrusions between that reservoir and the surface, and mass accumulation in the heavily fractured caldera floor. The spatial and temporal patterns of subsurface mass accumulation during 2019–2022 imply that there were no significant changes in magma reservoir geometry or magma supply to the volcano in the years following the 2018 collapse.

papers.t: Radial‐Component Predominant‐Mode Inversion of Rayleigh Waves: Application to DAS‐Based Site Characterization
in: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering Utah State University Logan UT USA
tk: A new radial-component predominant-mode inversion framework for Rayleigh waves improves DAS-based near-surface shear-wave velocity profiling without requiring manual modal indexing.
提出一种径向分量优势模态反演框架，无需人工模态标记即可提高DAS近地表剪切波速度建模精度。
papers.ab: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a transformative technology for near‐surface site characterization. When a vertical source is activated along the fiber, DAS measures only the in‐line (radial) component of Rayleigh‐wave motion, whereas conventional surface‐wave methods primarily measure the vertical component. Dispersion data extracted from radial‐component waveforms may differ from those obtained from vertical‐component measurements, particularly under complex stratigraphic conditions. Hence, a component‐consistent forward problem is desired when inverting radial‐component DAS dispersion data to retrieve accurate shear wave velocity () profiles. This study presents a radial‐component predominant‐mode (RCPM) inversion framework designed for DAS‐based surface‐wave analysis that explicitly accounts for source–receiver directivity and modal sensitivity of the Rayleigh‐wave radial component. The proposed approach matches measured dominant radial dispersion trends with the theoretical mode exhibiting the maximum modal participation. As a result, the RCPM framework eliminates the need for explicit modal indexing, provides a component‐consistent interpretation of radial‐component dispersion data, and substantially reduces reliance on subjective analyst‐driven modal interpretations. The RCPM approach is systematically evaluated using three synthetic ground models and two field DAS data sets. The synthetic results demonstrate that modal energy distribution differs significantly between vertical and radial components in the presence of strong velocity contrasts and velocity reversals, and that conventional inversion approaches may misinterpret modal behavior, resulting in less accurate profiles. In contrast, the RCPM method consistently captures the correct modal response and yields reliable profiles. Application to two field DAS data sets further demonstrates good agreement between the inverted profiles and independent invasive borehole measurements.

papers.t: Quasi‐Global Search Behaviour of Large‐Step Gradient‐Based Optimization in Full Waveform Inversion
in: Physical Sciences and Engineering King Abdullah University of Science and Technology Thuwal Makkah Province Saudi Arabia
tk: Using large step lengths in gradient-based FWI optimization enables a quasi-global search behavior that mitigates cycle skipping by resolving shallow structures first.
在梯度类FWI优化中采用大步长可实现准全局搜索，通过先更新浅部结构来缓解周期跳跃问题。
papers.ab: Full waveform inversion (FWI) iteratively updates the velocity model by minimizing the difference between observed and simulated data. However, because FWI typically relies on gradient‐based local optimizers, it is prone to cycle skipping when the initial velocity model is inaccurate and low‐frequency data are absent. In such cases, the mismatch between simulated and observed data can exceed half a wavelength, causing the optimization to converge to local minima. Inspired by optimization strategies in machine learning, we employ gradient‐based optimizers with relatively large step lengths, beyond the traditional local optimization limit, to promote a quasi‐global search behaviour. This strategy allows the inversion to first approach the global minimum in the shallow subsurface, where the problem is more linear and convex, while deeper updates behave more like a global search. As iterations proceed, the improved shallow model gradually facilitates convergence at greater depths. Synthetic and field data experiments demonstrate that this approach can still produce accurate velocity models even in the presence of significant cycle skipping, highlighting an important property of the FWI loss topology related to the propagation of information from shallow to deep.

papers.t: OIB‐Type Garnet Amphibolites From the Xuerongzangbu Area, Central Lhasa Terrane, Tibet: Implications for Songduo Paleo‐Tethys Ocean Evolution and Permian Mantle Activity Along North Gondwana
in: National Key Laboratory of Earth System Numerical Modeling and Application College of Earth and Planetary Sciences University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
Department of Ocean Exploration and Technology Zhejiang Ocean University Zhoushan China
State Key Laboratory of Oil and Gas Reservoir Geology and Exploitation Chengdu University of Technology Chengdu China
School of Environment and Resource Southwest University of Science and Technology Mianyang China
tk: Geochemical and geochronological analysis of garnet amphibolites from the Central Lhasa Terrane reveals a Permian OIB-type protolith, tracking the evolution of the Songduo Paleo-Tethys Ocean.
藏中拉萨地块雪绒藏布石榴角闪岩揭示了二叠纪洋岛玄武岩原岩及松多古特提斯洋演化。
papers.ab: Whether the Songduo metamorphic belt represents an in situ Paleo‐Tethyan suture within the Lhasa Terrane or far‐traveled allochthonous high‐pressure slices, and how Permian mantle activity along the North Gondwana margin relates to subsequent Tethyan evolution, remain central questions in Tibetan tectonics. We investigated retrogressed garnet amphibolites from the Xuerongzangbu area of the Central Lhasa Terrane using petrography, mineral and whole‐rock geochemistry, Sr–Nd isotopes, SHRIMP zircon U–Pb geochronology, 40 Ar/ 39 Ar thermochronology, and phase‐equilibrium modeling. The rocks record prograde burial, peak high‐pressure amphibolite‐facies metamorphism, and fluid‐assisted retrogression during exhumation. Modeling of a weakly retrogressed Type I amphibolite yields peak conditions of 15.4–16.0 kbar and 600–660°C, whereas more strongly retrogressed Type II amphibolites preserve relict kyanite, high‐Si amphibole, phengite, and rutile. The amphibolites' OIB‐type trace‐element patterns, initial 87 Sr/ 86 Sr ratios of 0.7050–0.7057, ε Nd (t) values of −1.59 to +0.16, and Nd model ages of 0.97–1.08 Ga indicate derivation from an enriched intraplate mantle source with limited crustal contamination. Zircon U–Pb dating gives a protolith crystallization age of 271.0 ± 3.0 Ma, whereas hornblende and mica 40 Ar/ 39 Ar ages of 232.9–216.9 Ma record Late Triassic cooling and exhumation. Integrated with regional geological evidence, the protoliths are interpreted as seamount or ocean‐island basalts formed on the Songduo oceanic lithosphere. Together with regional Permian plume‐affinity mafic magmatism, these data suggest sustained mantle heating beneath North Gondwana and a possible temporal and geodynamic link between Songduo Ocean closure and the development of younger Tethyan branches.

papers.t: The Size of Greater India: Estimates by Comparing the Apparent Polar Wander Paths of the Tethyan Himalaya and the Indian Craton
in: Beijing Institute of Geological Survey Beijing China
Key Laboratory of Deep‐Time Geography and Environment Reconstruction and Applications of Ministry of Natural Resources Chengdu University of Technology Chengdu China

Frontiers Science Center for Deep Ocean Multispheres and Earth System Key Lab of Submarine Geosciences and Prospecting Techniques MOE College of Marine Geosciences Ocean University of China Qingdao China
School of Earth Sciences and Resources China University of Geosciences (Beijing) Beijing China
tk: A refined APWP-constrained approach using Monte Carlo simulations estimates the pre-shortening northern margin of Greater India, yielding a crustal shortening of approximately 880 km.
采用改进的APWP约束方法和蒙特卡洛模拟，估算出大印度板块地壳缩短量约为880千米。
papers.ab: The northern extent of Greater India is a critical, yet highly debated, parameter for reconstructing the India‐Asia collision. Previous paleomagnetic estimates, including the fill‐the‐gap and fixed great circle approaches, yield widely varying results, spanning from ∼200 to ∼3,000 km. These large discrepancies stem principally from two primary issues: the inherent uncertainties associated with both the Tethyan Himalaya (TH) and Indian apparent polar wander paths (APWP) based on paleomagnetic and geochronologic data, and India's complex kinematic history, particularly the large rotation in the Early Cretaceous followed by rapid northward translation in the Late Cretaceous. Because of limited data coverage from TH, discrete age‐matched comparisons between them compound these uncertainties. To address this, we introduce a refined APWP‐constrained approach that evaluates the TH paleomagnetic record as a temporal sequence. Assuming a coherent rigid attachment, this framework iteratively translates the TH northward, systematically quantifying the discrepancies between its restored paleomagnetic poles and the coeval poles expected from the updated Indian APWP while propagating uncertainties in both pole position and age using Monte Carlo simulations. Applying this to paleomagnetic data from the Jurassic–Paleocene units with age reassessment, we identify a statistically minimized discrepancy following a 7.9 ± 1.2° northward shift, which likely represents the pre‐shortening northern margin of Greater India. This optimal shift translates directly to a crustal shortening estimate of ∼880 km, consistent with geologic records of Greater India. This refined estimate provides a constraint for the India‐Asia collision and facilitates improved tectonic models of the Tibetan Plateau.

papers.t: A Sharp Melt‐Bearing Lithosphere–Asthenosphere Boundary Beneath the Korean Peninsula: Evidence From Teleseismic Receiver Functions
in: Research Center for Deep‐Surface Coupling of Earth Seoul Republic of Korea
School of Earth and Environmental Sciences Seoul National University Seoul Republic of Korea
tk: Teleseismic receiver functions reveal a sharp, melt-bearing lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary at ~70 km depth beneath the southern Korean Peninsula, indicating significant tectonic modification.
远震接收函数揭示朝鲜半岛南部约70公里深处存在一个含熔体的陡峭岩石圈-软流圈边界，表明其经历了显著的构造改造。
papers.ab: The lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary (LAB) provides key constraints on how continental lithosphere responds to tectonic processes. Located between the East Asian cratonic blocks and the western Pacific subduction system, the Korean Peninsula (KP) provides an important setting to examine continental lithospheric evolution, yet seismic constraints on its LAB structure remain limited. We use P‐ and S‐receiver functions to investigate crustal and lithospheric structure beneath the southern KP and adjacent volcanic islands. Beneath the southern KP, the LAB lies at ∼70 km depth and is marked by a sharp transition zone (V S ) reduction (7%–10%), most plausibly explained by partial melt near the LAB. Thermodynamic modeling predicts melt fractions near the LAB, consistent with independent estimates from V S reduction. These observations suggest that the southern KP represents the eastern continuation of a tectonically modified domain formed through long‐term subduction‐related thinning and removal of continental lithosphere. This modification varies laterally within the southern KP, where the southeastern block shows a deeper Moho, shallower LAB, and higher crustal P‐to‐S wave velocity ratio ( V P /V S ) than the northwestern block, indicating lithospheric overprinting by magmatic or thermal processes. Jeju Island retains inland‐like Moho and LAB depths, but shows complex V P /V S variations and a broad lithosphere–asthenosphere transition. In contrast, Ulleung Island exhibits a shallow Moho, low V P /V S , and an exceptionally shallow LAB, reflecting additional lithospheric modification associated with Miocene backarc extension. Our results link the present‐day lithospheric heterogeneity to the multi‐stage tectonic evolution of the eastern Eurasian margin.

papers.t: Earthquake Seismogram Denoising Across Time, Time-Frequency, and Hybrid Domain Approaches
tk: Benchmarks four deep learning architectures for earthquake seismogram denoising, showing that a hybrid sequential model combining time and time-frequency domains outperforms single-domain models.
评估了四种地震波去噪深度学习架构，表明结合时域和时频域的混合顺序模型性能最优。
papers.ab: Deep learning earthquake signal denoisers commonly operate directly on waveform data or on time-frequency representations, yet the impact of this design choice has not been systematically assessed under controlled conditions. Here we design and benchmark four comparable deep learning architectures to assess the effect of input data representation: a time-domain denoiser, a time-frequency denoiser–the Earthquake Seismogram (EQS) Denoiser–and two hybrid models processing both domains in parallel or sequentially. We evaluate waveform quality as a direct measure of denoising performance and assess the impact on signal detection and phase picking tasks using standard phase pickers. We further examine how denoising enhances signal onsets using a dedicated first-motion polarity model, benchmark the best-performing model against state-of-the-art denoisers, and evaluate its generalization to out-of-distribution data. Our results show that the time-domain model produces the most accurate waveforms at high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), but fails to detect event signals at low SNRs. The time-frequency denoiser captures event signals down to lower SNRs but can introduce artifacts such as smeared onsets due to the time-frequency binning. Hybrid models mitigate shortcomings of single-domain approaches. The hybrid sequential model (Formula presented.), which extends the EQS architecture, demonstrates strong signal detection at low SNRs while preserving sharp onsets, improving phase picking and extending first-motion polarity determination to lower SNRs compared to raw or bandpass-filtered data. Overall, (Formula presented.) surpasses benchmark models across every waveform and downstream task metric for both in- and out-of-distribution data, demonstrating that hybrid domain processing is a powerful strategy for accurate seismic denoising.

papers.t: Pre‐Eruptive Volatiles and Magma Storage Depth for the 2018 Eruption at Mount Veniaminof, Alaska
in: University of Nevada Reno NV USA
Now at Cornell University Ithaca NY USA
U.S. Geological Survey (Alaska Volcano Observatory) Anchorage AK USA
Virginia Polytechnical Institute Blacksburg VA USA
Bureau de Recherches Géologiques et Minières Orléans France
tk: Melt inclusion analysis of the 2018 Mount Veniaminof eruption reveals polybaric magma storage with modal depths of 100–200 MPa and no temporal volatile variations.
熔体包裹体分析揭示威尼亚米诺夫火山多压岩浆储集特征。
papers.ab: Mount Veniaminof is a frequently active, open‐system arc volcano on the Alaska Peninsula, part of the Alaska‐Aleutian arc. Mount Veniaminof's September–December 2018 eruption began with small lava flows and culminated in a larger explosive event in November that produced a 450 km long continuous ash plume—one of the volcano's most significant ash‐producing events in recently observed eruptions. A temporally constrained tephra record was sampled after the eruption. We present volatile element concentrations (H, C, S, Cl, F) from a total of 65 olivine‐hosted melt inclusions (MIs) across six tephra layers to assess potential variations in magma chemistry throughout the course of the eruption. No variation is observed in volatile concentrations across the tephra layers, and there is no correlation between volatile concentrations and the explosivity of eruptive pulses leading to the November explosive event. H 2 O concentrations within MI suggest moderately hydrous magmas up to 2.4 wt% H 2 O and a large range in CO 2 concentrations in the MI (14–2,180 ppm) from Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry and vapor bubble reconstructions. H 2 O and CO 2 measurements correspond to entrapment pressures up to 400 MPa (entrapment depths ∼15 km), but with modal storage around 100–200 MPa. H 2 O contents can be reconciled with previous microlite number density estimates using a polybaric storage history.

papers.t: First geophone and DAS test in the LUNA Moon analogue facility
a: Microgravity User Support Center, German Aerospace Center, Cologne, Germany
in: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)
Institut Supérieur de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace (ISAE-SUPAERO)
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences
tk: This paper presents the first seismic dataset from the LUNA Moon analogue facility, comparing DAS and geophone recordings in simulated regolith.
本文介绍LUNA月球模拟设施首个地震数据集，对比了DAS与检波器记录。
papers.ab: The temporary 4W network represents an initial seismic data set collected as an exploratory study in the 700m² regolith yard of the LUNA Moon analog facility jointly operated by DLR and ESA in Cologne, Germany. The facility opened at the end of September 2024 and provides a simulation environment to test hardware, commanding, procedures and operations for future planetary, and especially lunar, missions, including astronaut training in a controlled, standardized environment. In that capacity, it includes a permanent seismic broad-band station (DL.LUNAF) as well as 500 m of fibre-optic cable, containing single-mode, multi-mode and an engineered fibre, deployed in a grid-like pattern on the concrete floor below the regolith simulant. The regolith layer is generally about 60 cm thick, but extends up to 3 m deep in the 130m² deep floor area of LUNA. DAS data from this cable, using a Constellation fibre and corresponding interrogator, were obtained during three days in November 2024, partly overlapping with a geophone qualification campaign using 9 vertical-component geophones and one broad-band seismometer (Trillium compact 120 s), and used to obtain geolocations for the fibre channels. In addition to providing the first seismic characterization of LUNA, with implications for future seismic campaigns and the use of the facility to help interpreting data collected on the Moon, the measurements provide the opportunity to compare DAS and conventional seismic data for a dense, small-scale urban deployment at an indoor location. Recordings include hammer shots, road and airborne traffic, crane motion within the hall, and small rovers and people moving. Waveform data are available from the GEOFON data centre, under network code 4W. Waveform data are available from the GEOFON data centre, under network code 4W.

papers.t: GeoFWI3D: Large-scale 3D Velocity Model Dataset for Deep Learning-assisted Seismic Imaging
tk: GeoFWI3D is a large-scale, open-source dataset of 10,000 geologically diverse 3D velocity models designed to benchmark deep learning-assisted seismic imaging and full-waveform inversion.
GeoFWI3D是一个包含万个3D速度模型的开源数据集，旨在推动深度学习辅助地震成像与全波形反演。
papers.ab: We introduce GeoFWI3D, a large-scale open-source benchmark dataset of geologically plausible 3D subsurface models designed to accelerate deep learning (DL) assisted seismic imaging and full waveform inversion (FWI). FWI is a physics-driven, wave-equation-based optimization technique used in seismic imaging to estimate the subsurface properties. However, traditional FWI is highly non-linear, non-unique, and ill-posed. The iterative process often converges to local minima when the starting model is insufficiently accurate. Most importantly, 3D FWI is prohibitively expensive. With the advent of DL, a direct mapping between the shot gathers and subsurface properties can be established by training a network on realistic models. The primary bottleneck for such approaches is the lack of large-scale, realistic training datasets. GeoFWI3D addresses this gap with 10,000 geologically diverse velocity models at 96x96x96 resolution, spanning four structural complexity classes: pure stratigraphy, faulted networks, salt diapirism, and complex coupled fault-salt systems. Each model is accompanied by co-registered multi-modal labels including compressional velocity (Vp), zero-offset seismic reflectivity, relative geologic time (RGT), and semantic fault/salt masks. To facilitate systematic evaluation, we introduce benchmark tasks covering fault detection, joint salt body segmentation and chronostratigraphy prediction, FWI, wavefield and traveltime surrogates using neural operators, and generative modeling with a 3D diffusion model. We present baseline results for each task to establish reference performance metrics for future users. The dataset is publicly available under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

papers.t: Automatic Extraction of a Generalized Physics‐Based Feature From Time‐Lapse Active Source Ultrasonic Waveforms for Prediction of Shear Stress in Laboratory Friction Experiments
in: Department of Engineering Science and Mechanics The Pennsylvania State University University Park PA USA
Department of Computer Science and Engineering The Pennsylvania State University University Park PA USA
tk: A novel explainable generalized physics-based (XPG) machine learning model automatically extracts spectral features from ultrasonic waveforms to accurately predict shear stress in laboratory friction experiments.
提出一种可解释的广义物理特征（XPG）模型，能自动从超声波形中提取特征并准确预测实验室摩擦实验中的剪切应力。
papers.ab: Physics‐based handcrafted features, such as P‐wave amplitude derived from early parts of active source ultrasonic waveforms, successfully predict shear stress evolution. This study investigates whether feature extraction can be automated by leveraging full active source ultrasonic waveforms recorded during a laboratory friction experiment. We compare four models: handcrafted feature‐driven model (reference), convolutional neural network (CNN) model, explainable data‐driven (XDD) model, and a model with an explainable generalized physics‐based (XPG) feature. The reference model uses the spectral amplitude of the P‐wave packet calculated at center frequency, while the CNN relies on convolutional and pooling layers for feature extraction. The XDD model combines CNN feature extraction with long short‐term memory units and an attention layer to capture feature time history and significance. The novel XPG extracts a generalized spectral amplitude feature through a custom multilayer perceptron designed to learn linear combination of signals' spectral amplitudes without prescribing specific frequencies. Although CNN‐extracted features resemble handcrafted ones, both the CNN and XDD models underperform compared to the reference, while the XPG model outperforms all others. The attention mechanism in the XDD model highlights the importance of first P‐wave packet, whereas the XPG model also identifies later‐arriving shear wave packet as significant. The prediction improvement by inclusion of shear waves is physically intuitive; S‐waves have particle motion polarized in the direction of fault shear and are likely more sensitive to frictional state than P‐waves. This work demonstrates the value of incorporating domain knowledge into automatic feature extraction with potential applications in seismic data analysis.

该研究利用地方震波形探讨了苏门答腊俯冲带地壳地震各向异性的变化。

papers.t: Maximum earthquake magnitude unlikely to be controlled by subduction interface roughness
tk: Global analysis shows subduction interface roughness at 1–10 km scales does not control maximum earthquake magnitude or geodetic coupling.
全球分析表明，1-10千米尺度的俯冲界面粗糙度并不控制最大地震震级。
papers.ab: Understanding the controls on seismogenic behaviour at the plate interface in subduction zones is essential to assessing the hazard they pose. The interface topography, or roughness, is widely thought to be an important factor, yet how roughness influences earthquake magnitude is still debated. This debate persists because, generally, studies are limited to individual subduction margins, proxies for roughness are used rather than direct measurements and historical earthquake records are short. Here we show by analysing data from 15 subduction zones globally that there is no relationship between any interface roughness parameter we derive from observations and a proxy for maximum earthquake magnitude. Specifically, for each margin, we use seismic reflection profiles of the plate boundary fault to quantify its roughness at 1–10 km scales, and in the same locations we test whether geodetically constrained interface coupling is an indicator of earthquake potential in lieu of a longer historical record. This analysis shows a strong positive relationship between earthquake magnitude and interface coupling, and that roughness parameters are unrelated to maximum magnitude or coupling. Our findings challenge the prevailing hypothesis that subduction interface roughness is a predominant control on its seismogenic behaviour and imply that interface roughness measured over length scales up to 10 km should not be used to assess a margin’s seismic hazard.

papers.t: Unraveling the Evolution of Silicic Volcanism in a Distributed Volcanic Field: Insights From Harrat Khaybar, Western Saudi Arabia
in: Department of Geology & Geophysics College of Science King Saud University Riyadh Saudi Arabia
College of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Science Oregon State University Corvallis OR USA
Chemistry Division Los Alamos National Laboratory Nuclear and Radiochemistry Group Los Alamos NM USA

tk: Geochemical and isotopic modeling reveals that silicic magmas at Harrat Khaybar evolved via a two-stage assimilation-fractional crystallization process from basaltic parents.
地球化学与同位素模拟表明，哈拉特海巴尔的酸性岩浆通过两阶段同化-分数结晶过程演化而来。
papers.ab: Distributed basaltic volcanic fields commonly host minor but significant silicic magmas, the origin of which remains debated. At Harrat Khaybar (western Saudi Arabia; ca. 1.7 Ma to present), volcanic activity erupted compositions range from alkali olivine basalt to trachyte and comendite. Here, we integrate petrography, geochemistry, Sr–Nd–Pb isotopes, and petrogenetic modeling in the context of existing geochronology to investigate the origin of the silicic magmas. Geochemical data define continuous, non‐linear differentiation trends from basalt to comendite, accompanied by progressive incompatible element enrichment, increasingly negative Eu anomalies and increasingly radiogenic isotopic ratios; characteristics that cannot be fully explained by closed‐system processes alone. Radiogenic isotope systematics exclude bulk melting of Arabian crust, instead supporting assimilation–fractional crystallization (AFC). AFC modeling supports a two‐stage differentiation history: early basaltic evolution in the lower to middle crust dominated by olivine–clinopyroxene fractionation, followed by >90% feldspar‐dominated fractional crystallization in the upper crust coupled with minor assimilation ( r

本研究利用北安第斯弧辉石岩包体中的铼-锇和氧同位素，探讨了俯冲带中的地壳沉没与循环机制。

papers.t: Model‐Predicted Shear‐Wave‐Splitting Parameters in NE Japan: Comparison With Observations
in: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences University of Minnesota Minneapolis MN USA
Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences School of Science Institute of Science Tokyo Tokyo Japan
Earthquake Research Institute University of Tokyo Tokyo Japan
tk: This study models mantle wedge olivine CPO and shear-wave splitting in NE Japan, finding that while average fast directions match observations, predicted delay times are significantly overestimated.
本研究模拟了日本东北部地幔楔的各向异性，发现平均快向与观测一致但高估了延迟时间。
papers.ab: We model olivine crystal preferred orientation (CPO) and shear wave splitting (SWS) in the mantle wedge, using the results of a 3‐D numerical thermomechanical model for the NE Japan subduction zone. The model predicts a quasi‐2‐D trench‐normal (E‐W) mantle wedge flow pattern beneath Tohoku, given the trench‐normal subduction, but a more complex flow pattern beneath Hokkaido due to oblique subduction. The calculations of CPO in the mantle wedge indicate a predominantly E‐W fast axis beneath Tohoku, aligned with the mantle flow, but beneath Hokkaido the fast axis orientation changes laterally and with depth (ranging from approximately N‐S to E‐W) and is generally less aligned with the flow, especially near the base of the mantle wedge. The model calculations for vertical wave propagation yield location‐averaged fast directions consistent with observationally constrained station‐averaged fast directions: E‐W in Tohoku and N‐S in Hokkaido. However, the model significantly overestimates delay times in both study areas. Furthermore, model‐predicted fast directions from individual event‐station pairs cannot explain the variability in the observationally constrained fast directions for the same pairs even when the incidence angle and backazimuth are incorporated into the calculation instead of assuming vertical wave propagation. These discrepancies may reflect the impacts of simplifications in the model calculations and other factors, such as the anisotropy outside of the mantle wedge and data uncertainties.
