papers.t: Petrologic and geochemical characterization of the first year of the 2024–ongoing episodic Halema‘uma‘u eruption of Kīlauea (Episodes 1–39)
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: United States Geological Survey
Hawaiian Volcano Observatory
University of Hawaii at Hilo
Cascades Volcano Observatory
University of Oregon
Planetary Science Institute
University of Ottawa
University of California, Berkeley
tk: This study presents a petrologic and geochemical analysis of the first year of Kīlauea's 2024–ongoing episodic eruption, revealing shallow magma storage and new magma compositions.
本研究对基拉韦厄火山2024年起喷发的首年进行了岩石学和地球化学分析，揭示了浅部岩浆储集与新岩浆成分。
papers.ab: Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024 (and is ongoing at the time of this writing in 2026) with two consistently active vents in Halema‘uma‘u producing lava fountains ranging in height from 40 to 540 m. In the first year of the eruption (through December 24, 2025, episode 39), the U.S. Geological Survey's Hawaiian Volcano Observatory collected 178 samples for eruption monitoring purposes and used a subset of 80 for near-real-time geochemical analyses. Tephra, lava, and recycled lava lake ooze-out samples have been studied on inter-episode timescales using diverse microanalytical techniques, where research-scale investigations have proven to be advantageous pseudo-near-real-time techniques. Here we present a geochemical and petrologic overview of episodes 1–39 to better understand eruption dynamics and identify changes at Kīlauea following the 2018 summit caldera collapse. There are no significant intra-episode geochemical changes that might be related to variable fountain heights or episode durations, suggesting that eruption dynamics are instead primarily controlled by viscosity and conduit geometry changes throughout a single episode and between episodes. There is variable but clear influence of the still-molten lava lake interior on compositions of this eruption, including in tephra samples from lava fountains, indicating that the vent conduits are connected in some way at depth with the still molten passive lava lake core. Tephra glasses (7.0–7.8 wt% MgO) show cyclic changes in MgO that were decoupled from lava fountain heights and behavior in episodes 1–28 but positively correlated after episode 29. Additionally, whole-rock and glass compositions are enriched in minor elements such as K 2 O and TiO 2 compared to 2008–2023 summit eruptions, tracking the arrival of a new magma composition that may be related to the prolonged episodic eruptive behavior. Olivine-hosted melt inclusions from five episodes have ~0.35–0.43 wt% H2O, < 300 ppm CO 2 and < 1500 ppm S, with no significant variations between episodes. Melt and fluid inclusion barometry show that magmas driving these episodes are stored and sourced from the shallow 1–2 km Halemaʻumaʻu reservoir, as were olivine from the 2023 summit eruption. The ongoing episodic eruption also has higher bulk-rock MgO compared to the five previous summit eruptions (2020−2023) and the forsterite (Fo) content of olivine has varied systematically from 2015 to 2025 with the equilibrium olivine composition of the Halema‘uma‘u reservoir increasing from Fo 80.7 in 2015 to Fo 82.7 by 2025. We argue that the Halemaʻumaʻu reservoir is heating up because the rate of magma supply is outpacing effusion and cooling following caldera collapse in 2018.

papers.t: Combining Borehole Seismic Data and Deep‐Learning Methods to Monitor Seismic Sequences in the Istanbul‐Marmara Region, NW Türkiye
in: GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences Potsdam Germany
Free University Berlin Institute of Geological Sciences Berlin Germany
RWTH University of Aachen Aachen Germany
tk: A deep-learning and borehole-seismic workflow detects eight times more microearthquakes, revealing pre-mainshock clustering and waveform similarity changes in the Istanbul-Marmara region.
结合深井地震数据与深度学习，该研究显著提升了马尔马拉海微震监测能力。
papers.ab: The North Anatolian Fault Zone beneath the Sea of Marmara in NW Türkiye displays a 50% probability of an earthquake within the next decades. The proximity of the fault to the Istanbul megalopolis highlights the need for high‐resolution microseismicity monitoring to identify seismicity transients including pre‐mainshock clustering. We analyze six 4.0 M L 5.8 earthquake sequences in the eastern and central Marmara region from 2016 to 2023 and focus on the occurrence of seismicity immediately prior to the mainshocks. We combine borehole and surface seismic waveform data with deep‐learning phase picking, automated phase association, and non‐linear relocation to compile a comprehensive seismicity catalog. Compared with conventional processing, our workflow allows us to detect about eight times more events in time windows around the mainshocks in the area instrumented with borehole sensors. We then apply waveform cross‐correlation, refined location techniques, and template matching to quantify waveform similarity and characterize seismic activity preceding moderate events. We observe a strong increase in waveform similarity and decrease in inter‐event distance prior to a 2016 M L 4.5 event in the Çınarcık Basin, consistent with earlier results from manual processing, and identify additional highly similar events preceding the mainshock. The 2019 M L 5.8 Silivri sequence shows increased waveform similarity but more heterogeneous spatial clustering. We demonstrate that borehole seismic arrays are critical for resolving these subtle signals due to higher signal‐to‐noise ratios. Our workflow provides a robust basis towards near‐real‐time microseismic monitoring in the Istanbul‐Marmara region and systematically identifying seismicity transients and localization processes.

papers.t: Updating the geometry of the Saluki segment: Bayesian moment tensor analysis of the 2012 MW6.3 Palu, Indonesia, earthquake and implications for Coulomb stress transfer
in: Bandung Institute of Technology
Meteorological, Climatological, And Geophysical Agency
tk: This study performs a Bayesian moment tensor inversion of the 2012 Mw6.3 Palu earthquake to update the Saluki fault segment's geometry and analyze Coulomb stress transfer.
本研究对2012年Mw6.3帕卢地震进行贝叶斯矩张量反演，更新了Saluki断层几何并分析了库仑应力演化。
papers.ab: The Palu-Koro Fault System in central Sulawesi, Indonesia, is known to produce medium-to-large earthquakes, including the M W 6.3 event on August 18, 2012, and M W 7.5 event in 2018. However, the subsurface fault geometry, particularly its dip angle, remains poorly constrained, which may lead to an underestimation of stress transfer and inaccurate hazard assessments. In this study, we performed Bayesian moment tensor inversion on 19 focal mechanisms ( M W ≥ 3.8) from the 2012 M W 6.3 earthquake sequence to update the geometry of the Saluki segment within the Palu-Koro Fault System. The analysis yielded a dip angle of 83°±4.5°, a rake of 7.33°±5.52° (left-lateral strike-slip), and a 345.2°±3.87° strike (NNW-SSE). This geometry substantially influenced the Coulomb stress change calculations, producing a ∼ 300 kPa (3 bar) decrease in the maximum stress; however, polarity reversals in 12 of the 54 Saluki subfaults were observed in this study. The stress redistribution from the 2012 event predominantly affected the Saluki segment, along which gentle dips produced broader stress perturbations. Although the Palu-Saluki zone accumulated significant stress, the Makassar Strait segment (i.e., where the 2018 rupture occurred) exhibited limited seismicity after 2012, which suggests that its failure required additional stress contributions beyond the transfer that occurred in 2012. Nevertheless, These results underscore that even moderate adjustments to fault geometry (e.g., dip) can substantially influence stress interpretations and hazard assessments.

papers.t: Estimating Anisotropic Parameters in Vertically Transversely Isotropic Media Using Long‐Offset Traveltime Approximations
in: College of Instrumentation and Electrical Engineering Jilin University Changchun China
National Technology Innovation Center for Geophysical Exploration of Oil and Gas Zhuozhou China
CNOOC Research Institute Co., Ltd. Beijing China
National Engineering Research Center of Offshore Oil and Gas Exploration Beijing China
tk: A user-guided sequential workflow using high-accuracy long-offset traveltime approximations improves the estimation of anisotropic parameters in vertically transversely isotropic media.
该研究提出了一种基于高精度长偏移距走时近似的顺序参数估计工作流，提高了VTI介质中各向异性参数估算的可靠性。
papers.ab: Accurate estimation of anisotropic parameters in vertically transversely isotropic media is essential for reliable velocity modelling and seismic imaging in modern seismic exploration. However, long‐offset seismic data often exhibit pronounced nonhyperbolic moveout, which leads to strong coupling between background velocity and anisotropic parameters and reduces the stability of conventional estimation approaches. To address this issue, we implemented a user‐guided sequential parameter‐estimation workflow within the framework of the classical two‐step parameter‐decoupling strategy. Specifically, a high‐accuracy traveltime operator designed for long‐offset data is employed in place of conventional low‐order or fourth‐order nonhyperbolic moveout approximations and is integrated with a semi‐automatic moveout‐flattening and parameter‐selection procedure. Once the target reflection event, zero‐offset time, offset windows, vertical P‐wave velocity and candidate parameter ranges are specified, an objective‐function‐based grid search is used to select the optimal moveout parameters from the corrected reflection events. The resulting estimates of and are subsequently used to recover the Thomsen anisotropic parameters and . Numerical experiments on undulating layered models and applications to marine field reflection data demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively improves the reliability of anisotropic parameter estimation. The results indicate that the method provides an efficient and robust framework for estimating the anisotropic parameters of vertically transversely isotropic media and can offer reliable initial models for velocity model building and anisotropic seismic imaging under complex geological conditions.

papers.t: Slip-Informed Ground-Motion Models in Subduction Zones
in: Departamento Ciencias de la Tierra, Universidad de Concepción, Concepción, Chile
Departamento de Geología y Obras Civiles, Universidad Católica de Temuco, Temuco, Chile
Centro de Investigación, Innovación y Creación UCT (CIIC-UCT), Temuco, Chile
Departamento de Ingeniería Civil, Universidad de Concepción, Concepción, Chile
Departamento de Geofísica, Universidad de Concepción, Concepción, Chile
tk: Incorporating coseismic slip distributions and interseismic coupling into subduction-zone ground-motion models significantly reduces interevent uncertainty, especially for short-period spectral accelerations and megathrust earthquakes.
将破裂滑动分布和震间锁合引入俯冲带地面运动模型可显著降低不确定性。
papers.ab: Ground-motion models (GMMs) are fundamental tools for seismic hazard analysis but typically rely on simplified distance metrics that fail to capture the spatial heterogeneity of energy radiated during earthquake ruptures. In this study, we evaluate the performance of GMMs that incorporate rupture heterogeneity through slip distributions and interseismic coupling, comparing them to conventional formulations based on the minimum-distance metrics. We selected all interface events from the Next Generation Attenuation for subduction zone regions project database for which at least one coseismic slip model was available, resulting in 19 earthquakes (Mw>6.7) and approximately 1400 ground-motion records. From this dataset, we developed both traditional RRUP-derived GMMs and alternative GMMs that account for rupture heterogeneity through mean distance metrics (RP). Residual analyses demonstrate that slip-informed GMMs yield systematically lower interevent variability and reduced total uncertainty, with the interevent standard deviation (τ) decreasing by up to 30% globally. These improvements are most pronounced at short-spectral periods (T ≤ 1.0 s) and for megathrust earthquakes (Mw>8.1), in which τ drops by up to 50% relative to RRUP-based models. Strikingly, these localized performance peaks are particularly relevant for seismic engineering and hazard assessment. Furthermore, we evaluated the use of pre-event interseismic locking models as forward-modeling tools, finding remarkable consistency with coseismic slip-informed predictions. Although physically informed approaches introduce additional epistemic uncertainty due to source model parameter variability, they represent a critical step toward enhancing the physical realism and predictive capability of subduction-zone GMMs.

papers.t: Rupture and Associated Microseismicity Controlled by Fault Topography
in: State Key Laboratory of Coal Mine Disaster Dynamics and Control Chongqing University Chongqing China
Geofluids, Geomechanics and Geoenergy (3G) Research Group Chongqing University Chongqing China
Department of Earth and Space Sciences Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
Department of Energy and Mineral Engineering EMS Energy Institute and G3 Center Pennsylvania State University State College PA USA
Institute of Geophysics Polish Academy of Sciences Warsaw Poland
tk: Numerical simulations show that smoother faults promote extensive ruptures, while rougher faults limit rupture propagation and produce frequent microseismicity.
数值模拟表明较光滑断层易产生大地震，而粗糙断层限制破裂并产生频繁微震。
papers.ab: Fault topography exerts a key but poorly constrained control on rupture processes and the nature of seismicity. Through numerical simulations, we directly visualize how fault roughness controls rupture propagation by tracking the evolution of micro‐ruptures and associated stress states. On smoother faults, stress remains concentrated at nearly fixed locations throughout the slip process. In contrast, rougher faults exhibit multiple transient, spatially discrete stripes of stress concentration. Micro‐ruptures initiate at rough contacts and drive rapid localized fault slip, which is subsequently arrested by re‐interlocking at regional rough contacts. Consequently, more extensive ruptures occur on less rough faults with this nucleation potentially extending along the entire fault, favoring the formation of large, destructive earthquakes on relatively smooth fault in nature. Moreover, rougher fault surfaces produce larger b ‐value promoting energy dissipation through multiple small ruptures. These microseismic events cluster in time and indicate the initiation a self‐locking‐rupturing cycle, comparable to small, frequent microseismicity observed in active fault zones. Our findings establish a direct mechanistic link between fault topography, rupture process and microseismicity, advancing the understanding of the nucleation then propagation of earthquakes.

papers.t: How Large Are Marsquakes? Revisiting Magnitude Scaling and Implications for Marsquakes and Meteoroid Impacts
in: Imperial College London
Brown University
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
Université Paris Cité
tk: Recalibrated magnitude scaling relations for Mars show that marsquake magnitudes are ~0.5 lower than previously estimated, primarily controlled by shallow crustal structure.
重新标定的火星震震级平均偏低约0.5，且受浅部地壳控制。
papers.ab: Reliable estimates of seismic source size on Mars are critical for interpreting tectonic activity and impact processes, constraining the planet's interior evolution, and informing the design of future Martian seismic experiments. However, because InSight observations are limited to a single station, magnitude estimates cannot rely on empirical averaging of site and path effects as on Earth, and instead depend on comparisons between observed and modeled waveform amplitudes. Consequently, inferred magnitudes are sensitive to assumptions about interior structure, attenuation, and source parametrization. Existing Marsquake Service (MQS) magnitude‐scaling relations were calibrated using pre‐InSight interior models and tectonic source assumptions, potentially biasing magnitude estimates. Here, we reanalyze spectral amplitudes using InSight seismic data and investigate how post‐InSight interior models and source‐dependent parametrization influence inferred moment magnitudes. Using waveform simulations for a suite of 1‐D interior models, we quantify the effects of velocity structure, attenuation, three‐dimensional heterogeneity, and source physics on long‐period magnitude scaling. We introduce separate source representations and scaling relations for marsquakes and impacts. Across the tested post‐InSight models, the shallow crustal structure beneath InSight primarily controls scaling. Recalibrated marsquake magnitudes are lower by approximately 0.5 on average relative to MQS magnitudes, with the reduction varying across plausible shallow structures. Applying impact‐specific scaling brings seismic and crater‐derived estimates into closer agreement, although differences remain for large distant impacts, and the recalibrated magnitudes enable tentative matching of seismic detections to cataloged Martian impact craters. These relations provide site‐specific calibration for InSight observations and tighter constraints on Martian seismicity and impact processes.

papers.t: Prestack Diffraction Separation Using the Schrödinger Equation‐Based Adaptive Transformation
in: State Key Laboratory for Fine Exploration and Intelligent Development of Coal Resources Beijing China
College of Geoscience and Surveying Engineering China University of Mining & Technology (Beijing) Beijing China
tk: A prestack diffraction separation method using a Schrödinger equation-based adaptive transform effectively isolates weak diffractions from strong reflections.
利用薛定谔方程自适应变换实现叠前反射与衍射波分离。
papers.ab: Small‐scale subsurface geological discontinuities, such as caves and fractures, can provide storage space for oil and gas. High‐resolution imaging of these small‐scale geological discontinuities is important for the development of oil and gas reservoirs. These small‐scale subsurface discontinuous geological features are manifested as diffracted waves. Diffraction imaging can clearly delineate the spatial distribution of small‐scale structures. However, high‐energy reflections always mask diffractions. An essential prerequisite for diffraction imaging is the removal of strong reflection interference from seismic data. We propose a prestack diffraction separation method based on a Schrödinger equation–based adaptive transform. To extract diffractions from shot gathers, we first apply a normal moveout (NMO) operator to enhance the kinematic differences between diffracted and reflected waves. Subsequently, we apply an adaptive transformation method constructed within a quantum mechanical framework based on the Schrödinger equation. Unlike fixed‐basis transforms, this method employs data‐adaptive wave functions to characterize seismic data, enabling a more effective capture of the amplitude and frequency characteristics of both diffracted and reflected waves in NMO‐corrected shot gathers. Different wave functions, such as those representing the diffracted and reflected components, correspond to distinct components in the data. We reconstructed the reflections using the wave functions corresponding to the reflected components. Through the subtraction of reconstructed reflections from the shot gathers, the diffraction patterns were isolated. The proposed diffraction separation workflow based on the Schrödinger equation–based adaptive transform can effectively extract weak diffractions from seismic data, laying the foundation for subsequent high‐resolution diffraction imaging. Synthetic data tests validated that the method can effectively detect 5‐m karst caves and faults with the same throw. Nankai dataset applications show the capability of the separation workflow to successfully extract fracture‐related diffractions under complex geological conditions, thereby facilitating the detailed characterization of geological features such as fractures.

papers.t: Quantifying Ground-Motion Variability from Rupture Uncertainty: How Many Simulations Are Enough?
in: Physical Sciences and Engineering (PSE) Division, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Thuwal, Saudi Arabia
Computer, Electrical and Mathematical Science and Engineering (CEMSE) Division, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Thuwal, Saudi Arabia
tk: This study determines the number of physics-based simulations needed to characterize ground-motion variability and introduces a directivity parameter that reduces computational requirements by up to 80%.
本研究确定了表征地动变异性所需的物理模拟次数，并引入方向性参数减少了高达80%的计算量。
papers.ab: Probabilistic seismic hazard assessment (PSHA) increasingly leverages physics-based simulations (PBS) to improve the representation of source, site, and path effects, particularly in regions with limited observational data. Source parameters exert a strong influence on ground-motion intensity, underscoring the need for rigorous quantification of rupture-related uncertainty. By solving the seismic wave equation for predefined kinematic rupture models, PBS provides a physically consistent framework that circumvents the ergodic assumption inherent in traditional ground-motion estimation approaches. We evaluate the Castro-Cruz and Mai (2025; CM2025) rupture generator for its ability to produce statistically representative rupture scenarios and capture realistic median values of ground-motion intensity. In this article, the ground-motion variability produced by CM2025 ruptures is benchmarked against empirical ground-motion models (GMMs) across multiple earthquake scenarios. After validating CM2025’s capability to capture ground-motion variability, we address a fundamental question motivated by the substantial computational cost of PBS: How many simulations are required to robustly characterize the ground-motion variability from kinematic rupture models? To answer this question, we perform over 2000 simulations of Mw 6.5 strike-slip and dip-slip earthquakes and quantify confidence intervals for the median and logarithmic standard deviation of peak ground velocity (PGV). To improve efficiency, we introduce a new directivity parameter into the statistical characterization of ground motions. This innovation reduces the number of simulations required to achieve a target confidence interval by up to 80% for sites with strong rupture-directivity sensitivity. For example, stations aligned with strike-slip faults initially require over 200 simulations for accurate PGV estimation; our new method achieves equivalent confidence with only 35 simulations. Our findings are a step toward a scalable framework for optimizing computational resources, enabling more efficient and accurate seismic hazard assessments.

papers.t: Fine shear-wave velocity structure of the lithosphere in the Northern Tan-Lu fault zone from two- and three-station interferometry tomography
in: Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences
Chinese Academy of Sciences
Institute of Geology and Geophysics
State Key Laboratory of Lithospheric Evolution
tk: This study images the fine lithospheric shear-wave velocity structure of the Northern Tan-Lu fault zone using two- and three-station interferometry.
该研究利用双台和三台干涉成像技术获得了郯庐断裂带北段岩石圈精细速度结构。

papers.t: Experimental investigation of a deep organic carbon cycling promoted by carbonate reduction in subduction zones
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
Université Paris Cité
Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen
Sorbonne Université
Institut de Recherche pour le Développement
Austral University of Chile
tk: Piston-cylinder experiments demonstrate that oxygen fugacity controls the formation, ordering, and composition of abiotic graphitic carbon via carbonate reduction in subduction zones.
实验表明氧逸度控制俯冲带碳酸盐还原形成非生物石墨碳的结构。
papers.ab: Recent studies show that subduction zones host both biogenic and abiotic organic carbon. The latter can form under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions, yet the mechanisms and redox controls remain poorly constrained. We present piston-cylinder experiments at 700 °C and 3 GPa simulating carbonate reduction in the presence of antigorite over a wide oxygen fugacity range, from about ΔFMQ −4 to −1 relative to fayalite–magnetite–quartz (FMQ) buffer. Graphitic carbon forms under all investigated redox conditions, and is systematically associated with chlorite derived from antigorite breakdown. Raman spectroscopy, TOF- and Orbi- SIMS analyses indicate that under the most reducing conditions investigated i.e. , approaching those imposed by wüstite–magnetite buffer (ΔFMQ ≈ −4), abundant graphitic carbon forms and is highly ordered, hydrogen-poor and dominated by aromatic structures. In contrast, less reducing conditions (buffered at nickel–nickel oxide, ΔFMQ ≈ −1), yield smaller amounts of highly disordered, partially hydrogenated and oxygenated graphitic carbon. These differences, observed under identical pressure and temperature, primarily reflects the influence of oxygen fugacity, indicating a redox-driven formation pathway distinct from the thermal maturation and graphitization of biogenic organic matter. Such redox-driven precipitation of graphitic carbon may promote transient carbon storage, facilitate volatile transport into the deep mantle and contribute to the diversity of metastable carbon species involved in the deep carbon cycling.

papers.t: Frequency-Bessel surface-integration method to extract full set of dispersion spectrograms from seismic records of an earthquake event
tk: A new frequency-Bessel surface-integration method is proposed to extract a complete set of surface-wave dispersion spectrograms directly from earthquake seismic records.
提出了一种新的频率-贝塞尔面积分方法，用于直接从地震记录中提取完整的面波频散谱图。

papers.t: Earthquakes and the Metamorphic Sole of the Tinos Ophiolite, Cyclades, Greece
in: Department of Geosciences University of Nevada Las Vegas Las Vegas NV USA
Corresponding Author Philip England Department of Earth Sciences University of Oxford Oxford UK
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences University of Minnesota Minneapolis MN USA
Department of Geosciences Pennsylvania State University University Park PA USA
tk: Analyzes metamorphic sole rocks from Tinos, Greece, to identify coseismic melt veins recording ancient earthquakes and estimate shear stress and energy dissipation.
通过分析希腊天诺斯蛇绿岩变质底部的熔融脉，揭示了古板块边界的地震摩擦熔融与剪切应力特征。
papers.ab: We analyze deformation fabrics, compositions of melts, metamorphic temperatures, and paleopiezometric data beneath the Tsiknias Thrust, Tinos, Greece, which formed part of the plate boundary that, in Late‐Cretaceous time, absorbed convergence between Africa and Europe associated with final closure of the Vardar Ocean. Sedimentary and mafic rocks of the ocean floor beneath the Thrust experienced metamorphism at pressures of GPa, equivalent to a depth of about 30 km, and at ambient temperatures of °C. Subgrain‐size piezometry indicates that shear stress during this metamorphism was MPa, consistent with estimates of shear stress at comparable depths on present‐day convergent plate boundaries. In the meters immediately beneath the Tsiknias Thrust, apparent metamorphic temperatures vary between 600° and 800°C. In some locations the upper 10 m of the amphibolites are cut by veins, consisting almost entirely of plagioclase, whose compositions cannot be explained by partial melting of the host rock in that temperature range. They are, however, consistent with the products of laboratory experiments on frictional slip at seismic rates. We interpret these veins, and their deformed equivalents, as recording repeated episodes of coseismic melting followed by ductile shearing. Melt‐vein thicknesses of mm imply coseismic energy dissipation of J , which is comparable with seismological measurements of breakdown work in earthquakes on present‐day plate interfaces.

papers.t: The past, present, future and applications of Canada’s analog seismic data
in: Natural Resources Canada
Geological Survey of Canada
tk: Reviews the history, preservation status, digitization challenges, and scientific value of Canada's one million legacy analog seismograms.
综述了加拿大百万张历史模拟地震图的保存现状、数字化挑战及科学价值。
papers.ab: Canada has been seismologically instrumented for more than one hundred twenty-five years. Analog instruments were first deployed in Canada in 1897 and dominated seismic monitoring for almost a century until they were replaced by digital instruments, first deployed in the late 1970s in Canada. Although many analog seismograms have been lost, approximately one million remain. These records contain a wealth of data about earthquakes, explosions and many other phenomena. The analog seismogram collection is currently stored in a secure location and has legal protection. However, access is difficult and a path to scanning and digitizing the records remains elusive. Scanning and digitizing are necessary for modern analysis techniques to be used to unlock their secrets. Some of Canada’s largest, historical earthquakes have been analyzed using techniques of the 1980s and 1990s but science has progressed considerably in recent decades and all events would benefit from the application of newer analysis methods. There has been more success in converting textual records, such as station bulletins, to accessible, digital formats. This paper discusses the history of Canada’s legacy seismic data as well as challenges, successes and thoughts on moving forward.

papers.t: Fault‐Related Carbonates as Quaternary Seismotectonic and Paleoclimate Archives (Monte Marine Fault, Central Apennines)
in: Dipartimento di Scienze Università degli Studi Roma Tre Rome Italy
Archaeology, Environmental Changes, and Geo‐Chemistry Group Vrije Universiteit Brussel Brussels Belgium
Department of Stratigraphy and Paleontology University of Granada Granada Spain
EPOC UMR 5805 University of Bordeaux CNRS Pessac France
High‐Precision Mass Spectrometry and Environment Change Laboratory (HISPEC) Department of Geosciences National Taiwan University Taipei ROC
InGeo Department University of Chieti‐Pescara “G. D'Annunzio” Chieti Italy
Pacific Centre for Isotopic and Geochemical Research Department of Earth Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences University of British Columbia Vancouver BC Canada
tk: Integrates structural, geochemical, and geochronological analyses of fault-related carbonates along the Monte Marine Fault to reconstruct long-term seismogenic activity, fluid flow, and exhumation rates.
结合构造、地球化学和年代学分析，重建了蒙特马林断裂带的长期地震活动、流体循环及剥露历史。
papers.ab: Seismogenic faults shape continental landscapes, drive crustal deformation and influence fluid exchange between the lithosphere and atmosphere. Yet, quantitative links between fault activity, exhumation and near‐surface environmental evolution remain poorly understood. Here, structural (meso‐ and micro‐scale) investigations are integrated with carbonate geochemistry and geochronology to reconstruct the long‐term spatio‐temporal evolution of seismogenic faulting along the Monte Marine normal fault (MMNF) in the central Apennines, Italy. Field investigations and sampling of exhumed fault zones were complemented by analyses of faults exposed in paleoseismological trenches, together preserving carbonate mineralizations and cataclasites formed at different crustal depths and during successive stages of fault evolution. Carbon and oxygen stable isotope analyses (δ 13 C, δ 18 O), clumped isotope thermometry (Δ 47 ) and carbonate geochronology (U‐Th, 14 C dating) distinguish three structural and geochemical groups, spanning deeply exhumed fault zones, shallow fault‐related carbonates, and near‐surface carbonate concretions. Meteoric‐derived footwall mineralizations along the MMNF record structurally controlled fluid flow from at least ∼481 ka, up to the Holocene surface‐rupture record preserved in paleoseismological trenches (ca. 5.3–4.0 ka cal BC), pointing to long‐lived, spatially distributed seismogenic activity. These data also constrain a maximum average exhumation rate of ∼1.57 ± 0.30 mm/yr across the fault system since ∼0.5 Ma. By linking fault‐zone carbonate archives from exhumed structures with those exposed in paleoseismological trenches, this study provides a quantitative framework for reconstructing long‐term fluid circulation, seismogenic fault activity and paleoclimatic conditions, tracing the evolution of fault–fluid systems across structural levels, from deeply exhumed fault zones to active surface ruptures in extensional mountain belts.

papers.t: Single‐Crystal Elasticity of Lawsonite at High Pressure: Implications for High Poisson's Ratio and V P / V S Zones in Subduction Zones
in: Synergetic Extreme Condition High‐Pressure Science Center State Key Laboratory of High Pressure and Superhard Materials College of Physics, Jilin University Changchun China
GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences Potsdam Germany
College of Geoexploration Science and Technology Jilin University Changchun China
Beijing National Laboratory for Condensed Matter Physics and Institute of Physics Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
Geodynamics Research Center Ehime University Matsuyama Japan
tk: High-pressure elasticity experiments on lawsonite reveal exceptionally high Poisson's and Vp/Vs ratios, providing a non-fluid mineralogical explanation for seismic anomalies in subduction zones.
劳森石的高压弹性实验为俯冲带高泊松比异常提供了矿物学解释。
papers.ab: Conventional models attribute anomalously high Poisson's ratios in Earth's interior to the presence of fluids or melts. Here, we propose a fundamentally different mechanism, which is rooted in the unique crystal chemistry of lawsonite (CaAl 2 Si 2 O 7 (OH) 2 ·H 2 O). Our high‐pressure and room temperature experiments reveal anomalous changes in the elastic tensor of lawsonite at ∼4.5 and ∼9 GPa, which are linked to phase transitions involving hydrogen‐bond reorganization. Compared to typical mantle minerals, lawsonite exhibits moderately low P‐wave velocity ( V P ) and very low S‐wave velocity ( V S ). More notably, it is characterized by exceptionally high isotropic aggregate Poisson's ratio (0.32–0.38) and V P / V S ratio (1.92–2.27), which serve as diagnostic identifiers in the interpretation of seismic models. In hot subduction zones, such as Cascadia and Southwest Japan, lawsonite provides a key mineralogical mechanism for the high‐Poisson's‐ratio anomalies observed at 20–50 km depth, presenting a viable explanation distinct from conventional models that invoke overpressurized, fluid‐saturated oceanic crust. In colder subduction systems such as NE Japan, the presence of 20–40 vol.% lawsonite can account for the seismic anomalies observed at 50–90 km depth. Furthermore, lawsonite exhibits strong velocity anisotropy, which may help interpret the observed seismic anisotropy. The seismologically unique signature of lawsonite and its compatibility with seismic models underscore how this mineral could have a critical role in facilitating water transport into the deep mantle.

Millennium Institute of Oceanography
Geological Survey of Canada
University of Victoria
University of Chile
tk: Tsunami marigrams reveal that the 1971 Mw 7.8 La Ligua earthquake ruptured a deep section of the megathrust, downdip of its aftershock zone.
海啸模拟记录表明，1971年智利La Ligua Mw 7.8级地震破裂了余震区下倾方向的深部俯冲带。

papers.t: The Aurora Vent Field at the Transition From Magmatic Accretion to Tectonic Extension on Gakkel Ridge: Constraints From Microseismicity and Aeromagnetic Observations
in: Alfred Wegener Institute Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research Bremerhaven Germany
Faculty of Geosciences University of Bremen Bremen Germany
tk: Microseismicity and aeromagnetic data reveal a transition from magmatic to tectonic spreading at the Aurora Vent Field, Gakkel Ridge, with a localized intrusion likely heating the hydrothermal system.
微地震和航空磁测揭示了加克尔洋脊奥罗拉热液区的岩石圈构造演化及侵入体热源。
papers.ab: The Aurora hydrothermal vent field (AVF) is the first confirmed active vent system on the Arctic Ocean seafloor, located at the western end of the ultraslow spreading Gakkel Ridge. It marks a distinctive endmember among ridge‐axis hydrothermal systems, where volcanic construction and ultramafic influence co‐exist. The region's perennial ice cover and remoteness have left the crustal and lithospheric structure, including the underlying subseafloor processes, largely unconstrained. In 2023, the RV Polarstern PS137 expedition investigated how lithosphere forms in this region and how it interacts with the AVF's hydrothermal system. Here, we present results from a ∼11‐month passive seismic data set, recorded by a network of eight ice‐going ocean bottom seismometers and complemented by a coincident aeromagnetic survey. Together, these data reveal a transition from magmatic to non‐volcanic spreading between the Western Volcanic Zone and the Lena Trough. With the AVF located at its onset, seismicity and magnetic anomaly patterns are consistent with progressively thicker and colder lithosphere and reduced melt supply toward the Lena Trough. A localized and likely thermally controlled gap in seismicity may indicate a small gabbroic intrusion northeast of the AVF that could provide a heat source for the hydrothermal system. Abundant seismicity surrounding the AVF indicates that tectonic processes continuously influence the lithosphere, whereas evidence for transient magmatic activity near the vent field is limited. These findings suggest that the AVF represents a long‐lived hydrothermal system and provide new insights into the geological controls on hydrothermal systems at ultraslow spreading ridges.

papers.t: Multi-Modal Surface Wave Inversion using Physics Guided Variational Autoencoders
tk: A physics-guided multi-modal variational autoencoder (PG-VAE) is proposed for automated, scalable near-surface characterization using multi-modal Rayleigh-wave dispersion.
提出一种物理引导的多模态变分自编码器，用于自动、高效的近地表瑞雷面波多模态反演。
papers.ab: The growth in seismic acquisition techniques has led to large-scale surveys, making traditional manual dispersion analysis logistically and computationally prohibitive. While deep learning techniques can offer an automated alternative, standard convolutional neural networks (CNNs) often fail to account for the non-uniqueness of the inverse problem and can produce geologically unrealistic, smooth velocity models. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-guided multi-modal variational autoencoder (PG-VAE) for scalable near-surface characterization. Our framework introduces a multi-stream fusion strategy that maps independent latent features from both raw shot gathers and spectral-dispersion images by leveraging the physics of Rayleigh-wave dispersion. We implement a specialized decoder architecture with learned transposed convolutions and residual refinement to enforce a structural bias towards layered earth models. Physics guidance is incorporated via a differentiable surrogate network that serves as a forward-consistency regularizer, penalizing predictions that violate the physics of Rayleigh-wave dispersion. The network is trained on diverse synthetic data generated via elastic modeling, and then validated on unseen synthetic data, and subsequently evaluated on an ultra-high-density field dataset from the Devine test site in Texas. We also employ gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to examine the input features contributing to the network predictions. The proposed method could serve as a scalable tool for near-surface characterization and as an initial model-building tool for high-resolution elastic full-waveform inversion.

papers.t: Lithospheric Delamination of the Pamir Driven by the Underthrusting Indian Plate as Inferred From Seismic Observations
in: School of Earth Sciences Zhejiang University Hangzhou China
Division of Mathematical Sciences School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences Nanyang Technological University Singapore
tk: Receiver function analysis of the Pamir reveals crustal anisotropy and low Vp/Vs ratios supporting Indian-plate-driven lithospheric delamination over Asian slab subduction.
接收函数分析支持印度板块驱动的帕米尔岩石圈拆沉模式。
papers.ab: The tectonic evolution and deformation mechanisms of the Pamir remain controversial, partly because the crustal response to deep lithospheric geodynamic processes is insufficiently constrained. Two competing lithospheric tectonic models are under consideration: subduction of the Asian slab and delamination of Pamir lithosphere, each of which predicts distinct crustal anisotropic signatures. Here, we use shear‐wave splitting of Moho P‐to‐S converted‐phases from receiver functions recorded at 198 seismic stations to map crustal anisotropy across the Pamir and the surrounding regions, thereby providing direct constraints on crustal deformation styles. We further determine crustal thicknesses and Vp/Vs ratios using H‐κ‐c stacking. Crustal thickness correlates positively with surface elevation and negatively with Bouguer gravity anomalies, indicating that crustal thickening provides the dominant first‐order support for the high topography. More importantly, Pms splitting measurements reveal strong crustal anisotropy, with a mean delay time of ∼0.66 s, and a systematic rotation of fast‐polarization orientations across the intermediate‐depth seismicity belt. In the southern Pamir, convergence‐parallel fast directions record N‐S‐oriented basal shear imposed by the indented Indian lithospheric mantle, which has likely promoted Quaternary extension of southern Pamir. Conversely, to the north of this belt, orogen‐parallel fast‐directions signify pure‐shear thickening of the Pamir lithosphere. Together with low crustal Vp/Vs ratios of 1.60–1.72 beneath the southern Pamir, which are consistent with a felsic bulk crust and removal of mafic lower crust, these observations favor Indian‐lithosphere‐induced delamination of the Pamir lithosphere rather than a model dominated by uniform southward subduction of Asian lithosphere.

papers.t: Mantle Transition Zone Constraints on Slab Penetration and Slab‐Edge Mantle Flow Beneath the Kamchatka Peninsula
in: State Key Laboratory of Marine Geology Tongji University Shanghai China
Department of Geological Engineering Montana Technological University Butte MT USA
Research Institute of Exploration & Development PetroChina Xinjiang Oilfield Company Karamay China
Geology and Geophysics Program Missouri University of Science and Technology Rolla MO USA
tk: P-to-S receiver functions reveal a thickened mantle transition zone beneath southwestern Kamchatka and a thinned zone beneath northern Kamchatka, indicating semi-toroidal mantle flow around the slab edge.
P波到S波接收函数揭示堪察加半岛下方的地幔过渡带厚度变化，支持绕过板块边缘的半环形地幔流模型。
papers.ab: Numerous seismic studies have reported the absence of a resolvable subducted slab beneath parts of northern Kamchatka, though the mechanism for this anomaly remains debated. We utilize 1,696 P‐to‐S receiver functions to image the mantle transition zone (MTZ) beneath the Kamchatka Peninsula and surrounding areas. Beneath southwestern Kamchatka, the thickened MTZ and the pronounced 520‐km discontinuity support cold Cretaceous Pacific slab‐related material with possible hydration within the MTZ. In contrast, significant MTZ thinning is observed beneath northern Kamchatka, where previous tomography studies also show slab absence in the shallow upper mantle. This argues against the presence of a large cold detached slab remnant in the sampled MTZ. Combined with previous seismic anisotropy, tomography, and geodynamic constraints, our results support a model that thermally buoyant mantle material flows around the slab edge and ascends into the upper mantle, forming a semi‐toroidal mantle flow. The inferred slab‐edge mantle flow may extend to at least MTZ depths and provide a plausible setting for progressive modification and weakening of the slab margin beneath northern Kamchatka, while allowing slab penetration farther southwest. These observations highlight the first‐order role of slab–mantle interaction in controlling slab fate at convergent margins.

papers.t: Late Palaeozoic faulting and basin formation of the Loppa High area, Barents Sea
in: University of Oslo
University Centre in Svalbard
Aarhus University
Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland
tk: The paper reconstructs the late Paleozoic tectono-stratigraphic evolution of the Loppa High using 2D/3D seismic data, identifying three distinct extensional fault systems.
该研究利用二维和三维地震数据重建了巴伦支海Loppa高地的晚古生代构造演化。
papers.ab: This study reconstructs the Pennsylvanian–late Permian to Early Triassic tectono-stratigraphic evolution of the Loppa High, a long-lived structural high on the southwestern Barents Shelf. We integrate 2D and 3D seismic surveys and key wells across ~35,000 km 2 to map eight regionally correlatable horizons (H1–H8) tied to the Billefjorden, Gipsdalen, Bjarmeland, Tempelfjorden and Sassendalen groups. Two-way travel-time structure maps, time–stratigraphic thickness maps and detailed fault interpretation (>150 faults) reveal three discrete late Palaeozoic extensional fault systems and a multi-phase tectonic evolution of the Loppa High. An ENE–WSW-striking Carboniferous fault system (C) parallels the Asterias Fault Complex and is linked to regionally widespread late Mississippian–middle Pennsylvanian rifting and development of the northern Loppa High as an early Carboniferous basement high. A Pennsylvanian–early Permian NNE–SSW fault system (P), antithetic to the Bjørnøyrenna Fault Complex, segments the northwestern Loppa High into the Neiden, Børselv and Kråketind sub-highs and controls distribution of Ørn Formation carbonates and Fafner evaporites. The C and P fault systems, along with Pennsylvanian regional transgression, exerted important controls on the depositional architecture. The late Permian–Early Triassic N–S-striking fault system (T) is spatially associated with the West Selis Boundary Fault and records rift reorganization associated with tilting, uplift and erosion of the West Selis Boundary Fault footwall and the final drowning of the Polhem Sub-platform. The results demonstrate that the evolution of the Loppa High is tightly coupled to regional fault trends across the northwestern Barents Shelf and Spitsbergen and reflects structural inheritance relevant to the later opening of the Norwegian–Greenland Sea.

papers.t: Rapid urban land uplift enhanced by crustal faults during groundwater recovery
tk: Crustal faults in Osaka act as hydraulic barriers, compartmentalizing groundwater-recovery-induced land uplift up to 12 mm/year.
大阪的地壳断层充当了水力屏障，使地下水恢复引起的地表抬升呈现出受断层控制的分区特征。
papers.ab: Urban land subsidence driven by groundwater extraction is widespread, but the processes governing how groundwater recovery translates into spatially variable surface uplift remain poorly understood. We use satellite geodesy and multi-decadal groundwater observations to measure vertical land motion in Greater Osaka, Japan, where aquifers are intersected by a dense network of crustal faults. We observe widespread surface uplift at rates up to 12 mm/year, organized into distinct domains separated by sharp boundaries. Uplift rates vary abruptly across domain boundaries, which coincide with mapped faults. Where no faults are mapped, abrupt spatial changes in uplift rate suggest the presence of previously unrecognized buried faults. Uplift rates are positively correlated with groundwater-level rise in wells screened at depths up to 600 m, while deformation modelling indicates dominant uplift sources are shallower than 500 m. Our analysis suggests crustal faults act as hydraulic barriers to lateral groundwater flow, localising vertical land motion during aquifer recovery, with implications for groundwater management, infrastructure stability, and land-use planning in urban basins worldwide.

papers.t: Describing the uncertainty of earthquake focal mechanisms
tk: Introduces the Rotation Vector Distribution Matrix (RVDM) to represent 3D rotational uncertainty of earthquake focal mechanisms, improving tectonic stress inversions.
引入旋转向量分布矩阵（RVDM）表征震源机制不确定性，优化应力反演。
papers.ab: Uncertainty estimates on earthquake focal mechanism (FM) data are often simplified to a single, standard error angle or to a qualitative metric because a practical description of the full, 3D rotational uncertainty has not existed. We introduce the rotation vector distribution matrix (RVDM), a 3x3 matrix description of FM uncertainty. The RVDM is a multivariate normal probability distribution of rotation vectors that can easily be computed from a representation of the FM posterior probability distribution (PPD), usually obtained via a grid-search or Monte Carlo method. We investigate RVDM precision in describing synthetic FM PPDs, relying only on P-wave first-motion data, and find that it significantly improves PPD fits compared to simplified metrics. We further examine the impact of propagating the RVDM into synthetic tectonic stress inversions by comparing to inversions that incorporate only a standard (uniform) rotational uncertainty for each FM, as well as inversions that incorporate the full FM PPDs. Finally, we apply our proposed RVDM approach to Monte Carlo PPD samples of FMs, derived from P-wave first-motions, near the Yakutat microplate collision in Yukon, Canada. The results from both synthetic and real data suggest that using the RVDM model (or retaining the full PPD) in tectonic stress inversions can greatly reduce stress tensor uncertainties when the FMs are poorly constrained.

papers.t: A library for differentiable signal processing and machine learning on the sphere
tk: torch-harmonics is a differentiable PyTorch library for spherical signal processing and machine learning, enabling rotationally-aware learning in geophysics and planetary sciences.
torch-harmonics是一个用于球面信号处理和机器学习的可微PyTorch库，支持地球物理等领域的旋转感知学习。
papers.ab: The two-dimensional sphere embedded in three-dimensional Euclidean space S2, plays a central role in a variety of scientific and engineering domains, including geophysics, planetary science, geodesy, atmospheric physics, quantum chemistry, cosmology, and virtual reality, among many others. As machine learning increasingly permeates these fields, the demand grows for robust tools that process and model functions on the sphere, while respecting the inherent topological and symmetry properties of the domain. We present torch-harmonics, a comprehensive library that offers efficient, differentiable implementations of advanced signal processing and machine learning (ML) methods for spherical data. These include the spherical harmonic transform (SHT), the spherical analogue of the Fourier transform, vector spherical harmonics, discrete-continuous and spectral convolutions, as well as both global and neighborhood spherical attention mechanisms. Beyond traditional representations, torch-harmonics provides the building blocks for state-of-the-art spherical ML architectures such as spherical transformers in order to enable scalable, rotationally-aware learning and inference in modern scientific and engineering applications.

papers.t: Elasticity of polycrystalline davemaoite constrains its grain size in the lower mantle
tk: Machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations reveal that nanoscale grain-boundary disorder explains the discrepancy in davemaoite's shear modulus, constraining its minimum grain size in the lower mantle to ~100 nm.
机器学习分子动力学模拟表明纳米级晶界无序解释了毛钙石剪切模量偏差，并约束下地幔其晶粒尺寸不小于100 nm。
papers.ab: Earth's lower mantle hosts large low shear-velocity provinces (LLSVPs) beneath Africa and the Pacific, but their origin remains debated. Davemaoite, a major lower-mantle mineral, has been proposed as a contributor to these anomalies; however, its experimentally measured shear modulus is approximately 30% lower than first-principles predictions, a longstanding discrepancy between theory and experiment. Here, using million-atom machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations, we show that nanoscale grain-boundary disorder, invisible to conventional x-ray diffraction, can reconcile this gap. Introducing 5.8 vol% disordered regions reduces the shear and bulk moduli by 37% and 12%, respectively. This shear-selective softening can reproduce LLSVP-like seismic anomalies in basalt-rich assemblages, but only at disorder levels corresponding to grain sizes smaller than those expected in the lower mantle. Combining the disorder-elasticity relationship with seismic constraints, we derive a minimum davemaoite grain size of approximately 100 nm. This limit is consistent with mantle grain growth models and with attenuation-based evidence for coarse-grained LLSVPs.

papers.t: A limit theorem linking continuous plate models to the topology of the plate boundary network
tk: This paper mathematically proves a limit theorem connecting continuous plate models to discrete plate boundary networks using a signed-geodesic-distance construction.
本文证明了连接连续板块模型与离散板块边界网络的数学极限定理。
papers.ab: Plate tectonics is described in two registers: a discrete one, in which rigid plates tile the sphere and meet at trivalent junctions, and a continuous one, in which Bercovici and Wessel (1994) replace hard plate outlines by smooth shape functions of finite boundary half-width $δ^*$. We prove that the two registers are connected by a limit theorem. Generalizing the shape functions to a signed-geodesic-distance construction, we show that they converge almost everywhere, exponentially in $1/δ^*$, to the plate indicator functions; that the sharp plate mosaic is a finite regular trivalent CW decomposition of the sphere under an explicit structural hypothesis; and that a component-counted weighted Euler characteristic $χ_w^{δ^*}(τ)$, built from the super-level sets of the shape functions, equals $V-E+F=2$ for all $δ^*$ below an explicit threshold $δ_0(τ)$, with its face, edge and vertex terms converging separately to the numbers of plates, boundary arcs and triple junctions. The theorem is proved unconditionally on the signed-distance offset cover under positive-reach, separation and bounded-sector hypotheses, and transferred to the normalized partition-of-unity field for thresholds $τ<1/3$ by a comparison lemma whose junction-ball step, a planar single-crossing property, is certified numerically. The residual $|χ_w-2|$ defines a topological diffuseness index for diffuse plate boundaries. For the present-day PB2002 network the hypotheses are measured to be non-vacuous, with $δ_0(0.15)\approx2.8$ km. The theorem is the mathematical foundation of the topological audit of plate reconstructions presented in a companion paper (Kim, 2026, submitted to Geoscience Frontiers).

papers.t: Earthquake damage mapping from Sentinel-1 modeling against coherence damage proxy
tk: Supervised machine learning using Sentinel-1 coherence distributions outperforms the standard coherence damage proxy for mapping earthquake damage at the block scale.
基于Sentinel-1相干性分布的监督机器学习在街区尺度上优于传统地震损伤代理。
papers.ab: This paper tests whether a supervised model that uses the same Sentinel-1 signal as the coherence damage proxy can rank earthquake damage better than the proxy itself. Damage grades from Copernicus EMS for four earthquakes are joined to 783 635 OpenStreet- Map footprints over 28 assessed areas, and the coherence drop is aggregated to buildings, morphological blocks and cells of 50 m to 400 m. A ladder of models, from a logistic regression to gradient boosting, a random forest and an RBF SVM, is compared with the proxy on identical folds, using the held-out area as the replicate. Under leave-one-area-out validation, modeling improves on the proxy for blocks, where the two boosting models beat it in 13 and 15 of 15 areas, significant after correction for multiple testing. For buildings the best model gains in 12 of 15 areas, which is not significant after correction, and for cells no model improves on the proxy, with the flexible models tending to perform worse. The logistic model is the most reliable one. It is never significantly worse than the proxy and its gain changes little between validation schemes. Only 2 % to 7 % of its weight is on the mean coherence drop used by the proxy, while 79 % to 87 % is on the distribution of the drop inside the unit and on its neighbourhood. These results hold within one event. The cross-event gains depend on assumed negatives and should be read as upper bounds.

tk: PSInSAR and GNSS data are merged to construct a 3D velocity field of Hispaniola, revealing complex fault locking and identifying an overlooked regional hazard source.
结合PSInSAR与GNSS数据构建了伊斯帕尼奥拉岛三维速度场，揭示了复杂的断层锁定并确定了被忽视的区域灾害源。
papers.ab: The oblique convergence between the Caribbean and North American plates is accommodated, in Hispaniola, by left-lateral strike-slip on two major sinistral fault systems and by intra-arc shortening. We apply a Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSInSAR) approach to Sentinel-1 data using six tracks acquired between 2016 and 2023 to generate time series of interseismic velocities over the entire island. We merge the resulting ascending and descending tracks with GNSS–derived velocities to determine a spatially-continuous 3D velocity field that documents deformation gradients across large fault systems. The Enriquillo–Plantain Garden fault fits a single locked–fault model, while the Septentrional one potentially involves several sub–faults. Strain in southeastern Haiti and the southwestern Dominican Republic is well modeled by the Jérémie-Malpasse-Bahoruco oblique reverse fault-system, which represents a significant, but overlooked, regional hazard source.

papers.t: Rigorous vertical averaging for pseudo-3D modeling of precipitation obstructed fluid flow
tk: A pseudo-3D Stokes solver with a vertically averaged drag term is developed to efficiently compute permeability in porous media with changing pore morphology.
开发了一种具有垂直平均阻力项的伪三维Stokes求解器，用于高效计算孔隙结构变化介质的渗透率。
papers.ab: Computing effective hydraulic properties of porous materials with a dynamically changing pore morphology presents a complex and critical challenge in both theoretical and applied sciences. This paper presents a tool to effectively compute the intrinsic permeability k(x,t) for domains with both temporally and spatially varying pore structures, by utilizing a sample of snapshots of microfluidic experiments with calcium carbonate precipitation. To compute large domains at reasonable cost, a pseudo-3D Stokes solver with an additional viscous drag term is employed. In order to simulate the intricate domains with highly heterogeneous pore space, we derive vertically averaged governing equations including a vertically averaged drag term from scratch and without limiting assumptions. For exemplary precipitates (semi-spheres) of varying sizes within a rectangular channel with fixed solid boundaries, results are compared across multiple modeling approaches, each employing different drag force formulations. In addition, the performance of the derived models is examined for segments of an EICP experiment in terms of accuracy (comparison with 3D solvers) and computational efficiency. Finally, an entire experimental domain is used to demonstrate the capabilities offered by the solver thanks to its efficiency as well as accuracy and the permeability tensor k is computed and compared with experimental results. In all these applications, the vertically averaged drag term proves to be the optimal solution in terms of speed and accuracy, thus allowing for an efficient analysis of the non-uniformity of local fluid flow fluctuations resulting from alterations in the pore space.

papers.t: Sensitivity of neutrino oscillations to the Earth’s interior properties
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
Université Paris Cité

Institut Universitaire de France
Lyon 1 Université

University of Idaho
tk: This study evaluates the sensitivity of atmospheric neutrino oscillations to the Earth's electron density, demonstrating their potential for joint neutrino-seismic tomography of the mantle and core.
该研究评估了大气中微子振荡对地球电子密度的敏感性，为联合中微子-地震层析成像奠定了基础。
papers.ab: Understanding the Earth’s deep interior remains challenging, as traditional geophysical methods face ambiguities in linking seismic observations to temperature, composition, or mass density variations. Atmospheric neutrinos, produced by the constant flux of cosmic rays colliding with the upper atmosphere, offer a complementary probe: with energies of a few GeV, they traverse the Earth and experience flavor oscillations influenced by the planet’s electron density distribution, which depends on both its mass density and composition. Combining seismic observations with neutrino measurements in a joint inversion framework could provide complementary constraints on gross spatial and compositional variations in the deep Earth. We consider the next-generation neutrino detectors KM3NeT/ORCA, Hyper-Kamiokande, and DUNE, as well as an idealized hypothetical detector representing the intrinsic sensitivity of the method. The idealized detector is most sensitive to perturbations in the core, whereas realistic detector performance shifts the sensitivity toward the mantle, including the mantle transition zone, where hydrogen enrichment could produce detectable variations in electron density. These results establish the sensitivity of neutrino oscillations to the Earth’s electron density profile and provide a basis for future joint neutrino–seismic tomography.

tk: The TRANSFORM2 project aims to upgrade European Near-Fault Observatories (NFOs) through advanced sensors, machine learning workflows, and next-generation earthquake early warning systems.
TRANSFORM2项目旨在通过先进传感器、机器学习和下一代预警系统升级欧洲近断层观测站。
papers.ab: Near-Fault Observatories (NFOs) are natural laboratories situated at or near active faults experiencingcomplex geophysical processes, often close to densely populated urban areas. NFOs offer researchers from multiple disciplines access to rich, reusable datasets for generating scientificproducts. This facilitates improved understanding of the multi-scale physical and chemical processesdriving earthquake generation—a goal attainable only through continuous, long-term, high-resolutionmultidisciplinary data acquisition and consistent application of state-of-the-art processing techniques. Eight NFOs (and one under evaluation) in Europe have been identified by the European Plate ObservingSystem (EPOS) as long-term Research Infrastructures. NFOs target the enhanced understanding of themechanics of earthquakes to unravel the anatomy of complex seismogenic faults.The TRANSFORM² project has the ambitious goal to improve and transform the existing NFOs, paving theway for the next generation of NFOs across Europe. This will be achieved by: ● Evaluate state-of-the-art sensors.● Accelerate development of promising new sensors.● Develop ML-powered workflows for real-time detection, location, and characterization ofseismicity.● Create next-generation Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) paradigms and validate their societalimpact.● Strengthen stakeholder & decision-maker engagement.● Position existing NFOs as open, high-quality test-beds.● Identify sustainable funding pathways and provide recommendations to national authorities and theEuropean Commission for long-term RI support. Following the half time of the project, the design and testing of cutting-edge sensors, along with thedevelopment of automatic workflows for the detection, characterization of seismic events and sequences,and implementation of EEW systems, are actively being carried out and extended to a growing number ofNFOs. Concurrent deployment of the principal sensors, which are vital for supporting and enabling theadvancements, is already in progress. Finally, a ‘white book’ will be created to document how data, products and services from the nextgeneration Research Infrastructure (RI) can be exploited for the benefit of different target stakeholders.

papers.t: Structured-light three-dimensional surface scanning with deep learning-assisted N-bar localizer detection for stereotactic registration: a technical feasibility study in deep brain stimulation
tk: A feasibility study of a structured-light 3D surface scanning workflow with deep learning for stereotactic registration in deep brain stimulation.
一项利用深度学习辅助结构光三维表面扫描进行脑深部刺激立体定位配准的可行性研究。
papers.ab: Intraoperative computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for stereotactic registration in deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery, but it adds ionizing radiation, operative time, and workflow complexity. Whether an optical surface-scanning approach could ultimately support CT-independent stereotactic registration remains unknown. In this technical feasibility study, we developed a structured-light three-dimensional surface scanning (3DSS) workflow with deep learning (DL)-assisted N-bar localizer detection and quantified its agreement with conventional CT-based registration. Ten patients undergoing frame-based DBS for Parkinson’s disease or essential tremor underwent handheld craniofacial and N-bar scanning, completed in 1–3 min without interrupting surgery. CT-derived craniofacial surface models were co-registered with the surface scans using coarse-to-fine point-cloud registration with iterative closest point (ICP) refinement. A supervised DL object-detection model was used specifically to identify N-bar rod cross-sections from voxelized surface scans; and the detected localizer geometry was registered to the known N-bar model using deterministic point-to-line ICP to derive the 3DSS-based stereotactic transformation. Across the 10 independent patient registrations, CT–3DSS surface alignment reached a mean absolute error of 0.85 ± 0.10 mm, and the resulting 20 hemisphere-level comparisons showed a mean CT–3DSS target-coordinate deviation of 1.91 ± 0.87 mm and a mean trajectory angular deviation of 0.81° ± 0.60°. Despite these average levels of agreement, 10 of 20 target deviations exceeded 2 mm (maximum, 3.48 mm), underscoring the variability of the current approach. In addition, the present implementation remains CT-dependent because a CT-derived craniofacial surface is required to map the 3DSS data into the CT/DICOM world coordinate system, while CT-based stereotactic registration served as the comparison reference. Taken together, these preliminary single-center findings demonstrate technical feasibility while quantifying the performance gap that must be addressed through hardware and algorithmic refinements before radiation-free, CT-independent stereotactic registration can be considered for clinical use.

papers.t: Origin and geologic significance of Dual Seismic Discontinuities in the upper mantle
in: Yangtze University
Innovation Academy for Precision Measurement Science and Technology, CAS
University of Tasmania
Southern University of Science and Technology
International Institute for Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation
University of Twente
Zhejiang University
tk: Investigates the origin and geological implications of dual seismic discontinuities in the upper mantle, shedding light on mantle dynamics.
探讨了上地幔双地震不连续面的起源及其地质意义，揭示了地幔动力学特征。
papers.ab: Two negative seismic discontinuities are commonly imaged in the continental upper mantle. Beneath thick cratons they are generally interpreted as a mid-lithospheric discontinuity (MLD) and a deeper lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary (LAB). However, similar paired signals beneath tectonically active regions with thinner lithosphere have remained difficult to explain, leading to conflicting interpretations of lithospheric structure. Here we show that integrating thermal lithosphere thickness from multi-observable probabilistic inversions, S-wave receiver functions and melt extraction depths from young basalts resolves these ambiguities and identifies a previously unrecognized origin for paired seismic discontinuities in tectonically active regions. Using eastern China as a data-rich natural laboratory, and drawing on additional tests worldwide, we show that in stable cratons the base of the thermal lithosphere matches the deeper seismic discontinuity, consistent with the conventional interpretation. In thinned, intraplate volcanic regions, however, the shallow discontinuity aligns with both the thermal and geochemical LAB, whereas the deeper discontinuity lies within the asthenosphere. We infer that paired seismic discontinuities in these settings record distinct melt accumulation zones, with melt stored both near the LAB and deeper in the asthenosphere. This framework reconciles long-standing conflicts over lithosphere thickness and shows that integrated thermal, seismic and geochemical constraints can map how melt is stored and transferred through continents, linking upper-mantle structure to volcanism, lithospheric weakening and the long-term evolution of Earth’s interior.

papers.t: A self-adaptive fuzzy pitch control method for suppressing vibration of large-scale wind turbines under combined wind-seismic loading
tk: A self-adaptive fuzzy pitch control method is proposed to mitigate wind turbine vibrations and reduce failure probabilities under combined wind-seismic hazards.
提出一种自适应模糊变桨控制方法，用以抑制风电机组在风震联合作用下的振动。
papers.ab: For large-scale wind turbines subjected to sudden seismic excitation during operation, a self-adaptive fuzzy pitch (SFP) control method is proposed to mitigate the structural seismic response. The displacement and velocity of tower-top fore-aft (TTFA) are used as input variables for the fuzzy controller, and a self-adaptive proportional factor is established through an exponential function. The pitch angle adjustment is taken as the output variable, which is then superimposed on the pitch angle given by the baseline pitch controller to realize SFP control. Through co-simulation of OpenFAST and Simulink, the results demonstrate that compared with the traditional proportional–integral (PI) control, the proposed SFP strategy reduces the peak TTFA displacement and acceleration by approximately 25% and 31% on average, respectively, under various earthquake records. Seismic fragility analysis further shows that at a peak ground acceleration (PGA) of 1.0 g, SFP control reduces the failure probabilities corresponding to yield displacement and elastic limit displacement by 43.05% and 20.82%, respectively. These quantitative findings confirm that the proposed method significantly enhances the structural safety of wind turbines under combined wind-seismic loading, providing a practical and robust intelligent control solution for wind farms located in seismically active regions.

This will be achieved by: ● Evaluate state-of-the-art sensors.● Accelerate development of promising new sensors.● Develop ML-powered workflows for real-time detection, location, and characterization ofseismicity.● Create next-generation Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) paradigms and validate their societalimpact.● Strengthen stakeholder & decision-maker engagement.● Position existing NFOs as open, high-quality test-beds.● Identify sustainable funding pathways and provide recommendations to national authorities and theEuropean Commission for long-term RI support. Following the half time of the project, the design and testing of cutting-edge sensors, along with thedevelopment of automatic workflows for the detection, characterization of seismic events and sequences,and implementation of EEW systems, are actively being carried out and extended to a growing number ofNFOs. Concurrent deployment of the principal sensors, which are vital for supporting and enabling theadvancements, is already in progress. Finally, a ‘white book’ will be created to document how data, products and services from the nextgeneration Research Infrastructure (RI) can be exploited for the benefit of different target stakeholders.

papers.t: Iterative separation of coherent blended signals in common shot gathers using synchrosqueezed curvelet-Radon constraints
tk: A joint synchrosqueezed and Radon transform constraint iteratively separates blended seismic signals in common-shot gathers without relying on time-dithering coherence differences.
一种结合同步挤压与Radon变换的联合约束方法，无需依赖时间抖动即可在共炮点道集中迭代分离混叠地震信号。
papers.ab: Blended data acquired via simultaneous-source seismic exploration conventionally require post-acquisition deblending, which typically relies on the coherence differences introduced by firing time delays (time dithering). To reduce the dependency of the deblending process on these time dithers, a novel joint constraint based on the synchrosqueezed transform and the Radon transform is proposed, operating directly in the common-shot gather (CSG) domain. Specifically, by exploiting the differences in propagation directions of the blended signals within CSGs, the synchrosqueezed transform is first employed for an initial iterative separation to extract individual sources directly from the continuous records. Once the majority of the valid signals are separated, the Radon transform is subsequently applied in further iterations to suppress the residual blending interference, thereby preventing amplitude damage to the effective signals. Compared to conventional non-CSG deblending methods, this approach bypasses the reliance on time-delay coherence differences, thus enabling real-time quality monitoring of individual sources during field acquisition. Furthermore, compared to other existing CSG-based separation techniques, the proposed joint-constraint iterative framework demonstrates superior performance when handling complex data. Applications on both synthetic and field blended datasets demonstrate that high-fidelity data separation can be successfully achieved independently of the time-dithering constraints. Finally, because the proposed method operates completely independently across different CSG slices, it is highly amenable to parallel computing, facilitating the efficient processing of massive datasets within a short timeframe.
