Notably, the study captured the full pathological continuum: from nearly no coronary abnormality in P01 and early atheromatous plaque formation in P02, to advanced atherosclerosis in P03, and finally, in P04, severe fibrofatty atheroma, and myocardial infarction. Unlike conventional animal myocardial infarction models that rely on interventional triggers, the infarction in P04 occurred spontaneously, demonstrating the spontaneous cascade of plaque development and acute plaque rupture with thrombosis. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using streptozotocin-treated pigs to model key stages of diabetic coronary artery disease.

papers.t: Curvelet-Based Stochastic Noise Suppression for Downhole DAS Microseismic Data
in: SINOPEC Geophysical Research Institute Co., Ltd., Nanjing 211103, China
Nanjing Branch, National Technology Innovation Center for Oil & Gas Geophysical Exploration, Nanjing 211103, China
tk: This study evaluates curvelet-transform thresholding schemes for downhole DAS microseismic denoising, proposing Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) as the most robust, training-free default method.
本文评估了下井DAS微震去噪的Curvelet阈值方案，推荐MAD作为最稳健的默认方法。
papers.ab: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) converts fiber cables into dense strain-rate sensor arrays, capturing direct, reflected and guided seismic phases with ultra-fine spatial sampling. However, DAS interrogators suffer far stronger random noise than traditional geophones, limiting its microseismic imaging capacity. This work adopts curvelet-transform denoising to suppress noise. Curvelets partition the frequency–wavenumber plane into multiscale directional sectors; coherent wave energy concentrates in limited angular wedges, while stochastic noise disperses evenly across all transform coefficients, enabling noise-signal separation via wedge-wise thresholding. We test four default threshold schemes on synthetic downhole DAS microseismic data. Parameter tuning proves all methods deliver comparable performance, so we compare their out-of-box reliability for shale reservoir monitoring. Three noise-statistic-based strategies perform stably: median-absolute-deviation (MAD), quiet-window and empirical-cumulative-distribution-Function (ECDF percentile) thresholding. By contrast, the default knee-point algorithm from mainstream DAS toolboxes fails, as its preset threshold falls within noise components and barely removes interference. We propose MAD as a robust default for the tested downhole DAS microseismic setting for it estimates thresholds directly from noisy traces without blank reference windows and offers superior operational stability. Applied to field DAS records from a southwest China shale-gas horizontal monitor well, the MAD curvelet workflow greatly enhances microseismic arrivals with negligible spurious events. Benchmarks against standard 2D Daubechies-4 wavelet and adaptive Goldstein FK filtering verify curvelet denoising as a physically interpretable, efficient tool for DAS wavefields.

papers.t: Modeling Long-Term Postseismic Deformation Following the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos Earthquake Using Campaign and Continuous GNSS Observations
in: Vocational School of Information Technologies, Afyon Kocatepe University, 03200 Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye
Earthquake Implementation and Research Center, Afyon Kocatepe University, 03200 Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye
Department of Geomatics Engineering, Afyon Kocatepe University, 03200 Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye
Department of Geomatics Engineering, Aksaray University, 68100 Aksaray, Türkiye
Osmancık Ömer Derindere Vocational School, Hitit University, 19030 Çorum, Türkiye
Department of Geomatics, Gumushane University, 29830 Gumushane, Türkiye
Department of Geophysical Engineering, Ankara University, 06830 Ankara, Türkiye
MDSoft Informatics, Ankara University Technopolis, 06830 Ankara, Türkiye
Department of Geomatics Engineering, Gebze Technical University, 41400 Gebze, Türkiye
Çivril Atasay Kamer Vocational School, Pamukkale University, 20160 Denizli, Türkiye
Graduate School of Natural and Applied Sciences, Afyon Kocatepe University, 03200 Afyonkarahisar, Türkiye
Department of Computer Engineering, Atlas University, 34408 İstanbul, Türkiye
tk: This study models the long-term postseismic deformation of the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos earthquake using campaign and continuous GNSS data, revealing heterogeneous relaxation behaviors.
本研究利用野外和连续GNSS观测，模拟了2020年萨摩斯Mw 7.0地震的长期震后形变。
papers.ab: Postseismic deformation provides fundamental insights into earthquake-cycle processes, lithospheric rheology, and stress redistribution following large earthquakes. Although the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos earthquake has been extensively investigated in terms of coseismic deformation and early postseismic behavior, the long-term evolution of deformation following the event remains poorly constrained. This study characterizes the long-term spatiotemporal evolution of postseismic deformation associated with the 2020 Mw 7.0 Samos earthquake using combined campaign and continuous GNSS observations. A total of 18 GNSS stations were analyzed over an approximately 4.5-year period following the earthquake. Pre-earthquake GNSS velocities were incorporated as prior constraints, while postseismic deformation was modeled using linear, logarithmic, exponential, and combined logarithmic–exponential functions. The preferred model for each station component was identified using the corrected Akaike Information Criterion (AICc), and model-selection robustness was evaluated through 1000 Monte Carlo observation–perturbation simulations. The results reveal a spatially heterogeneous postseismic deformation field with station-dependent temporal behavior. Among the nonlinear solutions passing the Monte Carlo and goodness-of-fit criteria, the seven single-process LOG and EXP solutions yielded characteristic relaxation times ranging from 182.6 to 730.5 days, with a median of 438.3 days. The two LOGEXP solutions additionally contained a logarithmic timescale of 109.6 days and exponential timescales of 292.2–438.3 days. These findings demonstrate that campaign GNSS observations, when integrated with continuous GNSS data and an objective statistical framework, can provide meaningful constraints on the long-term evolution of postseismic deformation despite sparse temporal sampling. More broadly, the results emphasize the strongly time-dependent nature of postseismic deformation and the critical role of observation timing in capturing its spatiotemporal evolution.

papers.t: Provenance evolution of the Red River drainage system: new constraints on Ailaoshan-Red River fault zone kinematics
in: Ocean University of China, 238 Songling Road, Laoshan District, Qingdao City, Qingdao, Shandong, China [CN]
Shandong University of Science and Technology, Unknown, Qingdao, China [CN]
Ocean University of China, Unknown, Qingdao, China [CN]
Ocean University of China, Unknown, Qingdao, Shandong, China [CN]
Ocean University of China, No.238 Songling Road, Laoshan District, Qingdao, Shandong, China [CN]
tk: Sediment provenance analysis constrains the strike-slip reversal of the Ailao Shan-Red River Fault Zone to no later than 10.5 Ma.
沉积物物源分析将哀牢山-红河断裂带的走滑反转时间限制在不晚于10.5 Ma。
papers.ab: The strike-slip reversal of the Ailao Shan–Red River Fault Zone (ARRFZ) acted as a critical tectonic switch, triggering a shift in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau from lateral extrusion to vertical uplift and expansion. This transition reshaped regional topography and drainage systems, modulated local climate, and remotely governed sedimentation in the northwestern South China Sea. Treating the southeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau–Red River–Yinggehai Basin as a source-to-sink system, we characterize the lithologic features of the potential provenance regions in terms of their petrology, mineralogy, and thermochronology. To achieve this, we integrate petrographic thin-section analysis, heavy mineral assemblage characterization, and zircon U–Pb geochronology. The three potential source areas exhibit distinctive zircon age spectra and heavy mineral assemblages: the Simao Block is characterized by multi-peaked age spectra, a high ZTR index, and zircon-limonite assemblages; the ARRFZ features tripartite age spectra and low-ZTR magnetite-apatite assemblages; and the Sichuan–Yunnan Block displays multi-peaked age spectra with zircon-dominant assemblages. By integrating provenance datasets compiled from Vietnam, Hainan Island, and the Yinggehai Basin, we reconstruct the source-to-sink system linking the southeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau to the Yinggehai Basin. Prior to 10.5 Ma, sediments transported by the Red River were derived predominantly from the Simao Block. Afterward, at 10.5 Ma, the detrital contribution from the Sichuan–Yunnan Block through the Red River increased markedly. This lateral shift in sediment provenance documents the eastward propagation of tectono-geomorphic uplift and further constrains the inversion of the ARRFZ from left-lateral to right-lateral strike-slip motion to no later than 10.5 Ma.

papers.t: Azimuthal Anisotropy From Multimode Waveform Modeling Reveals Layering Within the Antarctica Craton
in: Planetary Science Institute
University of California, Los Angeles
UCLA Health
tk: Multi-mode Rayleigh waveform modeling reveals depth-dependent azimuthal anisotropy and lithospheric layering beneath the East Antarctic craton.
多阶瑞利波形建模揭示了东部南极克拉通的方位各向异性与分层。
papers.ab: The isotropic structure of the crust and upper mantle under Antarctica has been constrained by many studies. However, the depth dependence of seismic anisotropy, a powerful tool to characterize deformation and flow, is still poorly known. Here, we modeled three-dimensional (3-D) variations in azimuthal anisotropy under Antarctica using a multi-mode Rayleigh waveform fitting technique. We first searched the model space with a reversible-jump Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach to find path-averaged vertically polarized shear wave velocity profiles that fit fundamental and higher mode Rayleigh waveforms. We then inverted them to obtain a 3-D velocity and azimuthal anisotropy model across the region down to 600 km depth. Our results reveal that the east-west dichotomy found in other studies is not only characterized by different wave velocities but also by different anisotropy directions, likely reflecting the different deformation histories of the two blocks. Azimuthal anisotropy was found to be present in the top 300 km only and peaks at 100 - 200 km depth under the East Antarctica craton. Additionally, depth changes in fast direction were observed within the craton between 75 km and 150 km depth, suggesting layering is present. We speculate this layering relates to the formation history of the craton.

papers.t: Two-phase Temperature Reconstruction in Ice-Water Systems
tk: A physics-based data-assimilation method reconstructs two-phase temperature fields in ice-water systems using velocity data and boundary conditions.
一种基于物理的数据同化方法利用流速和边界条件重建冰水系统中的双相温度场。
papers.ab: What controls heat transport when liquid water interacts with ice? Answering this question is essential for understanding water bodies undergoing phase change. Yet experimental progress remains limited by the lack of a minimally invasive methodology for simultaneously resolving temperature fields in coupled liquid water and non-isothermal ice systems. Here, we introduce a physics-based data-assimilation method for reconstructing temperature fields in buoyancy-driven flows interacting with non-isothermal ice. Particle tracking velocimetry provides the liquid velocity field, while thermal and kinematic boundary conditions constrain the inverse problem. The method couples advection--diffusion in liquid water with conduction in ice to reconstruct simultaneous mean temperature fields and quantify heat transport across the water--ice interface, while remaining minimally invasive and compatible with free-surface systems. We demonstrate the method in laboratory experiments in which the temperature range across the liquid water in contact with ice drives cabbeling-induced convection. This framework enables investigation of coupled thermo-fluid dynamics in cryospheric aquatic systems, including heat exchange at the ice-water interface and liquid-phase energetics, with broader applications to phase-change processes in food and energy industries.

papers.t: DAS observations off-shore Chile and reconstruction inputs for the 2025 Kamchatka tsunami
in: Géoazur
Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Université Nice Sophia Antipolis
University of Chile
tk: This Zenodo archive provides processed offshore DAS data, synthetic waveforms, and Python code for converting DAS observations to water elevation and preparing inputs for tsunami reconstruction.
该Zenodo归档提供了智利近海DAS数据及海啸重建转换代码。
papers.ab: This archive contains two components: 1. Data (`data/`): processed DAS observations, synthetic waveforms, conversion inputs, and PCOMCOT reconstruction input files, including station coordinates, station weights, and time-reversal waveforms. 2. Code (`code/`): documented Python notebooks and supporting functions for (i) DAS preprocessing, (ii) DAS-to-water-elevation conversion and reconstruction-input preparation, and (iii) post-processing of observation-driven PCOMCOT reconstruction results. The archive also includes `environment.yml`, which defines the Python environment required to run the notebooks.

papers.t: Sub-slab Low-Velocity Anomalies: Observations, Origins, and Constraints on the Slab Pull Model
in: Independent Researcher
tk: Sub-slab low-velocity anomalies are dynamic wake effects of rapid slab advance, not universal evidence for slab pull.
板片下低速异常是快速板片推进的动态尾流效应，而非板片拉力的普遍证据。
papers.ab: Seismic tomography detects sub-slab low-velocity anomalies (LVAs) with velocity reductions of 1%–7% beneath circum-Pacific subduction zones such as Japan, South America, and the northwest Pacific, yet such features show prominent regional heterogeneity and are not globally ubiquitous. This study integrates seismic tomography, mineral physics experiments, and geodynamic simulations to systematically analyze the observational signatures, formation mechanisms, and geodynamic implications of sub-slab LVAs for the classic slab pull hypothesis. Centered on trench kinematics, we establish a three-category classification of subduction regimes based on net slab advance velocity (): trench-advancing, trench-retreating, and trench-stationary systems, each characterized by distinct sub-slab material states and asthenospheric circulation patterns. Our analysis demonstrates that well-developed sub-slab LVAs are not a common feature of all global subduction zones, but are restricted to the very few fast-advancing subduction zones that satisfy (where is the maximum asthenospheric creep backfilling velocity). In the majority of global subduction zones, although slabs continuously descend into the asthenosphere under gravitational forces, their horizontal net advance velocity relative to the mantle approaches zero—equivalent to "in situ subduction" (i.e., vertical descent without horizontal advance)—precluding the formation of persistent wake low-pressure zones. In trench-retreating subduction zones, which constitute approximately 62%–78% of global subduction zones, the advancing upper plate compresses the sub-slab asthenosphere, generating a high-pressure environment that suppresses melt accumulation. Only in the very few subduction zones where slabs substantially advance forward relative to the mantle (e.g., the northwest Pacific) can a wake low-pressure relaxation zone form beneath the slab, enabling melt to stably accumulate and produce seismic velocity anomalies. Sub-slab LVAs originate from dynamic wake effects induced by rapid slab advance, rather than serving as universal evidence for slab pull.

papers.t: Effects of Fault-Adjacent Topography on Supershear Rupture Behavior Along Strike-Slip Branch Fault Systems
in: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, University of California, Riverside, California, U.S.A.
tk: Topography slows down supershear rupture, causes asymmetric propagation, and can facilitate throughgoing rupture at branch intersections.
地形起伏会减缓并抑制超剪切破裂，但能促进分支断层的贯穿破裂。
papers.ab: Complex fault systems are often surrounded by topography. Although it is known that nearby topography can affect on-fault rupture dynamics, the particulars of its effect on supershear rupture and behavior at fault intersections have not been fully explored. In this study, we conduct 3D dynamic rupture simulations comparing the rupture behavior between a branch fault system with a flat free surface and one with asymmetric fault-adjacent topography. To isolate the effects of topography, we implement simplified uniform on-fault traction and illustrate that the fault-adjacent topography causes the free surface-induced supershear to propagate much more slowly and asymmetrically compared with the corresponding flat free surface case. As an example, for a right-lateral fault system along the x direction, the daughter crack is slightly faster in the positive x direction as opposed to the negative x direction. In addition, depending on the initial shear stress conditions, the normal stress perturbations introduced by the nearby topography can fully suppress the formation of the daughter crack in the slower direction, leading to a unilateral supershear rupture in the other direction. Furthermore, topography can facilitate throughgoing rupture onto secondary fault segments at fault intersections. The results from this simple dynamic modeling study suggest that topography can have significant implications for earthquake dynamics and may explain why some strike-slip earthquakes do not experience supershear rupture.

papers.t: Comment on egusphere-2026-3762
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
British Antarctic Survey
Institut Terre & Environnement de Strasbourg
Université de Strasbourg
Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung
ETH Zurich
University of Bremen
tk: Tests the feasibility of using ice-core break-off events during drilling as opportunistic seismic sources to estimate P-wave velocity and anisotropy in Greenland.
测试了利用冰芯断裂作为机会地震源来估算格陵兰冰盖P波速度和各向异性的可行性。
papers.ab: Ice-core drilling generates repeated mechanical disturbances within the ice column, raising the possibility that operational drilling signals could be used as opportunistic seismic sources. We test whether impulsive ice-core break-off events during the 2022 EastGRIP (Greenland) field season can be detected on surface-based, near-offset three-component geophones and used to estimate apparent P-wave velocity. A catalogue of 67 candidate core-break times was identified from drill-log load peaks, of which 37 had sufficient simultaneous near-offset seismic station coverage for assessment. Only three of these assessable events produced plausible impulsive arrivals. Automatic STA/LTA triggering was useful for identifying candidate windows, but did not reliably pick first arrivals. Where clear arrivals were identifiable above the background noise, manually picked arrivals gave apparent P-wave velocities consistent with firn/ice propagation, and showed a small across-flow faster-than-along-flow tendency, though this difference remains below the level of uncertainty required for robust anisotropy interpretation. These results show that ice-core break-off may provide a useful opportunistic seismic source, but only if future deployments include direct source-time measurement, quiet acquisition conditions, and receiver geometries designed for this purpose.

papers.t: Waveform-Prediction Augmentation and Deep Manifold Learning Enable Imbalanced Fault Diagnosis in Rotating Machinery
in: School of Mechanical and Electronic Engineering, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan 430070, China
Hubei Digital Manufacturing Key Laboratory, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan 430070, China
Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China
tk: A deep manifold learning and waveform-prediction augmentation framework is proposed to solve the imbalanced fault diagnosis problem in rotating machinery.
提出结合波形预测与深度流形学习的旋转机械不平衡故障诊断框架。
papers.ab: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery is essential for ensuring the reliable and safe operation of industrial equipment. However, imbalanced training data often bias intelligent diagnostic models toward majority classes, resulting in insufficient representation of minority faults. In addition, the high dimensionality and redundancy of vibration signals make it difficult to extract discriminative features and preserve meaningful neighborhood structures, thereby degrading diagnostic performance. To address these challenges, a waveform-prediction augmentation and deep manifold learning model for imbalanced fault diagnosis is proposed for rotating machinery. First, minority-class fault signals are augmented through time-series prediction using a nonlinear autoregressive neural network (NARNN), thereby alleviating the class imbalance at the data level. Subsequently, a deep manifold feature mapping (DMAP) is proposed to extract discriminative fault features. In DMAP, a stacked autoencoder (SAE) is employed to perform preliminary feature extraction on the training samples and obtain deep latent feature representations. The deep features extracted by the SAE are further processed using a dynamic time warping (DTW)-assisted manifold learning method for dimensionality reduction. In this process, DTW is used to calculate pairwise dissimilarities between deep representations and construct the neighborhood graph, thereby better preserving the local neighborhood relationships and topological structure of the deep features and producing more discriminative low-dimensional representations. Finally, a k-nearest neighbor classifier is adopted for fault classification. By integrating data augmentation, deep feature learning, and manifold dimensionality reduction, the proposed model effectively improves the fault diagnosis performance in imbalanced scenarios. Experiments on the bearing and planetary gearbox datasets demonstrate that, under an imbalance ratio of 0.1, the proposed method improves diagnostic accuracy by 10.2 and 1.6 percentage points, respectively. The comparative results further confirm its effectiveness in alleviating the diagnostic difficulties caused by class imbalance.

papers.t: Rupture Dynamics of Fast and Slow Earthquakes Controlled by Fluids
in: State Key Laboratory of Critical Earth Material Cycling and Mineral Deposits, School of Earth Sciences and Engineering
Nanjing University
tk: A new theoretical rupture-tip equation of motion incorporates fluid effects to explain the transition between fast and slow earthquakes controlled by fault-zone dilatancy.
该研究推导了包含流体效应的断层破裂动力学方程，揭示了剪切胀缩控制快慢地震转换的机制。
papers.ab: Fluids are ubiquitous in fault zones and can control rupture propagation through thermally induced pressurization and shear-induced dilatancy, which modulate pore pressure and thus fault strength. Among the mechanisms proposed for fast earthquakes and slow slip events, fault-zone fluids are particularly relevant to both behaviors. However, a theoretical rupture-tip equation of motion for elongated faults of finite width that quantitatively incorporates fluid effects remains lacking. Here we combine theoretical analysis with dynamic rupture simulations to investigate how thermal pressurization, shearinduced dilatancy, and fault-normal fluid diffusion interact with rupture mechanics on finite-width faults. We derive closed-form expressions for strength evolution, fracture energy, and energy release rate, as inputs to the fundamental rupture-tip equation of motion. The numerical simulations agree with the theoretical rupture-tip equation of motion and thus provide a numerical validation. In addition, both theoretical and numerical models suggest a critical dilatancy that delineates two rupture modes: when dilatancy falls below this critical value, ruptures accelerate toward the limiting speed, whereas when dilatancy exceeds it, ruptures sustain steady slow propagation. Spatial variations in fault-zone hydraulic and mechanical properties can explain the observed slow-to-fast rupture transitions in subduction zones. By explicitly incorporating fault-fluid processes into the theoretical framework, our model reconciles a broad spectrum of rupture speeds and slow-to-fast transitions, with potential implications for seismic hazard assessment.

papers.t: Topographic stress controls fissure segmentation and eruptive cone formation during the Laki and Eldgjá eruptions
in: University of Potsdam
GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
tk: Topographic stress gradients control the segmentation of eruptive fissures and inhibit the growth of large eruptive cones during major basaltic eruptions in Iceland.
地形应力梯度控制了冰岛喷发裂隙的分段，并抑制了大型喷发锥的发育。
papers.ab: Elongated dykes in tectonic rifts feed extensive basaltic fissure eruptions, yet surface eruption sites are highly discontinuous and unpredictable. Here we show that along-strike topographic variations, and the associated stress gradients, correlate with this localisation. We investigate eruptive cones at the two most productive historical basaltic eruptions in Iceland, Laki (1783–1784) and Eldgjá (~939–940). Morphological analyses of > 300 cones reveal volume variations (10 0 –10 7 m 3 ) and segmentation along ~ 100 km of fissures. Comparing cone distribution and volumes along the rift zone with pre-eruptive stress models, we demonstrate that high topographic stress gradients inhibit cone growth. We identify a critical stress gradient threshold predicting where larger cones are inhibited, while horizontal stress gradient peaks predict the location of fissure gaps. Our findings establish an empirical and physical link between topographic stress and volcanic morphologies, complementing previous models with a quantitative framework that aims at improving the forecasting of along-rift vent locations and development.

papers.t: Evidence for Hadean inheritance recorded in Mesoarchean granitoids from the Assean Lake Complex, Manitoba
in: University of Ottawa
Manitoba Geological Survey
tk: Sm-Nd isotopic analysis of Mesoarchean granitoids from Assean Lake reveals they inherited Hadean signatures through the reworking of older crustal precursors.
对Assean Lake中太古代花岗岩的钐-钕同位素分析表明，它们通过重塑更古老的地壳前体继承了冥古宙的特征。
papers.ab: Archean cratons represent the oldest preserved cores of continental crust, assembled through over two billion years of magmatism and crustal reworking. This protracted history obscures the nature of the progenitor materials that sourced the Neo- to Mesoarchean felsic rocks dominating most cratons. Although long-lived radiogenic isotopic systems provide insights into crustal evolution, they can be affected by post-magmatic processes, potentially leading to ambiguous interpretations, particularly when characterizing early crustal components absent in the geological record. The coupling of long-lived systems with short-lived isotopic tracers offers a more robust approach to resolving early crustal evolution. Here, we combine 147–146 Sm- 143–142 Nd isotopic systematics with whole-rock major and trace element geochemistry for ca. 3.2 Ga orthogneisses from the Assean Lake Complex (Manitoba, Canada) to constrain the age and origin of their crustal precursors. The 146 Sm- 142 Nd data indicate these Mesoarchean granitoids were derived from multiple crustal sources with distinct formation ages and composition. Sodic tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG) gneisses likely formed by partially melting a hydrated mafic crustal precursor (weighted mean µ 142 Nd ∼ -3.2) extracted from the mantle near the Hadean-Eoarchean transition. Conversely, coeval granitic gneisses were produced by reworking older TTG-like crust ultimately derived from a Hadean mafic reservoir (weighted mean µ 142 Nd ∼ -7.1). Together, these results provide direct evidence that the Assean Lake high-K granitoids inherited Hadean isotopic signatures through reworking of older crustal precursors ultimately derived from a Hadean mafic reservoir. They demonstrate that compositionally and temporally distinct crustal reservoirs, including ancient Hadean components, were mobilized and reworked contemporaneously during Mesoarchean magmatism, highlighting the dynamic, multi-source nature of early continental crust formation.

papers.t: Multistage warm-up seismic full-waveform inversion informed by electromagnetic data
in: Earth and Space Research
China National Offshore Oil Corporation (China)
State Key Laboratory of Oil and Gas Reservoir Geology and Exploitation
tk: A multi-stage FWI workflow uses electromagnetic resistivity inversion and clustering to build a robust initial velocity model, successfully mitigating cycle-skipping.
利用电磁反演和聚类构建初始模型，克服全波形反演周波跳跃。
papers.ab: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) provides high-resolution velocity models by exploiting the complete information embedded in seismic waveforms. However, the advantages of FWI come with cycle skipping when sufficient information is not available to build an accurate initial model. To integrate nonseismic data into seismic FWI, this study established a direct conversion method, leveraging the correlation between multiphysical models. The diffusive nature of electromagnetic (EM) data made it an independent, low-cost information source that complemented seismic low-frequency data. Unlike joint inversion approaches, the flexible FWI framework initialized FWI using EM resistivity inversion results. This novel approach extracted low-frequency skeleton structure from electromagnetic data to construct an initial FWI model. By design, it avoided strong assumptions about petrophysical correlation and structural alignment and did not require complex multiphysics objective functions, resulting in a straightforward implementation. The three-stage implementation began by inverting EM data to generate a blurred resistivity image. Pixels in this image were then clustered into models; each was assumed to have a constant velocity. To prevent cycle skipping, a preliminary FWI was performed to roughly fit seismic data by determining velocities for these models. Finally, a full-bandwidth FWI refined the preliminary velocity model, which had already incorporated EM and low-frequency seismic information, aiming for the highest possible resolution. Applied to the Marmousi model, the approach outperformed conventional seismic-only FWI methods in terms of data fitting and computational performance. Using EM to warm up FWI was theoretically similar to initializing FWI with a smoothed version of the true model because EM surveys could be regarded as a low-pass filter of the subsurface structure, as EM surveys physically averaged subsurface structures. The findings underscore the importance of incorporating nonseismic data in seismic imaging and offer a robust workflow for joint multiphysical data acquisition and analysis.

papers.t: The Distribution of Interseismic Locking on the Cascadia Subduction Zone Using Bayesian Methods
in: University of Washington
Earth and Space Research
Seattle University
tk: This study applies a Bayesian probabilistic framework to invert GNSS and leveling data, mapping the interseismic locking distribution and its uncertainties along the Cascadia Subduction Zone.
本研究采用贝叶斯概率框架反演GNSS和水准数据，绘制了卡斯卡迪亚俯冲带的震间锁死分布及其不确定性。
papers.ab: We use a Bayesian probabilistic framework to invert for the kinematic locking distribution on the Cascadia Subduction Zone, constrained by surface deformation data and a prior assumption of the locking pattern. Interseismic surface deformation observations include land and seafloor GNSS data, along with decades-averaged vertical rates from spirit leveling. Using a Bayesian inversion framework, we explore a range of priors, including different updip and downdip limits and along-strike heterogeneity in locking. Data corrections account for contemporary glacial isostatic adjustment and viscoelastic effects. The mean of the locking distributions suggests a highly coupled offshore zone, transitioning to creep at a depth that varies along strike, with sensitivity to the prior. The shape of the locking distributions varies along strike, with the highest means near the deformation front and in Central Oregon. Results suggest high probability of strong locking offshore and low locking deeper than 20 km depth, which can provide insight into associated hazards. This work also highlights the importance of tradeoffs among different deformation signals. We find that the combined influence of viscoelasticity and glacial isostatic adjustment is relatively small in Cascadia, on the order of a few mm/yr vertically, indicating that elastic strain accumulation dominates the contemporary crustal deformation.

papers.t: Comment on egusphere-2026-3474
in: RWTH Aachen University
ETH Zurich
Swiss Seismological Service
Trent University
Dalhousie University
Fraunhofer Research Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies IEG
Natural Resources Canada
University of Neuchâtel
University of Science and Technology of China
Géoazur
York University
tk: The PRECODE experiment at BedrettoLab investigates excavation damage zone evolution in crystalline rock using multidisciplinary monitoring, showing distinct fracturing behaviors between different excavation methods.
PRECODE实验通过多学科监测研究开挖损伤区演化及开挖方式影响。
papers.ab: The brittle damage around tunnels in the form of spalling is common in massive crystalline rocks subjected to high in-situ stresses. Understanding the short-term development and long-term evolution of the Excavation Damage Zone (EDZ) is particularly important for deep geological repositories (DGRs) for heat-generating nuclear waste, as the EDZ may provide preferential pathways for radionuclide migration. This paper presents an overview of the PRECODE mine-by experiment at BedrettoLab, a newly developed underground research laboratory (URL) in southern Switzerland designed to investigate brittle fracturing and EDZ evolution in crystalline rocks under repository-relevant conditions. The PRECODE tunnel was excavated in Rotondo Granite using both controlled drill-and-blast (D&B) and line-drilling and rock-breaking (LDRB) methods to evaluate the influence of excavation technique on EDZ characteristics. The experiment combines multidisciplinary in-situ monitoring including acoustic emission, distributed acoustic and strain sensing, hydraulic monitoring, electrical resistivity tomography, and terrestrial laser scanning with laboratory-based fracture mechanics and time-dependent testing under varying environmental conditions. The main objectives are to characterize short-term EDZ formation, investigate long-term crack growth and stress corrosion processes, quantify permeability evolution, and assess the interaction between excavation-induced damage and nearby fault zones. Preliminary results indicate clear differences in AE activity and EDZ development between excavation methods, while observations from the mature EDZ of the more than 40-year-old Bedretto Tunnel suggest ongoing time-dependent brittle fracturing. The coupled in-situ and laboratory datasets provide a unique basis for improving predictive models and long-term safety assessments for nuclear waste repositories in crystalline rocks.

papers.t: Krasheninnikov eruption facilitated by M8.8 Kamchatka earthquake and hidden critical state
tk: The 2025 Krasheninnikov eruption was triggered by dynamic stresses from a Mw 8.8 earthquake, which destabilized a volatile-rich magma reservoir in a hidden critical state.
2025年克拉舍宁尼科夫火山喷发由Mw 8.8地震的动态应力触发，该地震使处于隐秘临界状态的富含挥发分岩浆房失稳。
papers.ab: Large earthquakes can trigger volcanic eruptions, but the required conditions and mechanisms remain uncertain. Here, we investigate whether the August 2025 eruption of Krasheninnikov volcano, Russia, was facilitated by the July 29th, 2025, Mw 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. InSAR observations from 2016 to 2025 show no pre-earthquake inflation and satellite SO2 data indicate no detectable pre-eruptive degassing, suggesting apparent pre-earthquake, and pre-eruption, volcanic quiescence. Following the earthquake, InSAR data reveal a dyke intrusion beginning August 1st, shortly before eruption onset on August 2nd. Deformation modelling indicates a ~3.2x107 m3 dyke fed by a ~6-km-deep reservoir containing compressible, gas-rich magma. Stress modelling shows that static seismic stress and strain changes were small, mechanically mixed, and unlikely to have directly caused the dyke intrusion and eruption. Dynamic stresses were larger, reaching ~1.0±0.6 MPa, but still probably insufficient to trigger direct magma reservoir failure. Instead, the prolonged earthquake shaking likely promoted time-dependent volatile exsolution, bubble growth, and eventual reservoir destabilisation in a system already mechanically susceptible to failure. We show that apparently quiescent volcanoes may conceal hidden critical states prone to seismic perturbation, particularly in extensional arc settings with volatile-rich magmas exposed to repeated megathrust earthquakes.

papers.t: Dispersion equations of Scholte waves for an inclined multilayered seabed
in: Sinopec (China)
tk: This paper derives Scholte wave dispersion equations for inclined multi-layered seabeds, demonstrating that dipping angles and azimuths significantly affect dispersion characteristics.
本文推导了倾斜多层海底的Scholte波色散方程，揭示了倾角和方位角对色散特征的显著影响。
papers.ab: Scholte waves are surface waves that propagate along a fluid–solid interface and arise from the interference of P- and SV-waves. The conventional dispersion equations for surface waves are typically derived under the assumption of horizontal interfaces and cannot be applied to inclined strata. The presence of an inclined multilayered seabed introduces substantial mathematical challenges in deriving dispersion equations for Scholte waves. To address this, a natural stratum coordinate system and a seismic wave propagation coordinate system were established. Coordinate rotation transformation matrices were derived to convert the seismic wave equations and boundary conditions between these two coordinates. In this natural stratum coordinate system, the dispersion equations of Scholte waves were derived with the presence of an inclined multilayered seabed. In addition, the dispersion curves and wavefields of Scholte waves were calculated for theoretical models with several inclined interfaces. The numerical results demonstrated that the dipping angles and azimuths substantially influence the dispersion characteristics of Scholte waves. The effects of dipping angles on the dispersion curves were larger than those of azimuths. These derived equations can be further applied to high-precision inversion of dispersion curves and to predict the S-wave velocities, dipping angles, and azimuths of shallow seabeds with complex fluid–solid interfaces.

papers.t: Provenance of continental blocks in the southern Scotia Sea using detrital zircon UPb geochronology
in: British Antarctic Survey
University of Leicester
National Museum of Nature and Science
tk: Detrital zircon U-Pb geochronology of submerged banks in the southern Scotia Sea constrains their Gondwana paleo-Pacific margin origin prior to Cenozoic rifting.
利用碎屑锆石U-Pb年代学确定了南斯科舍海海底陆块在新生代裂解前源自冈瓦纳古太平洋边缘。
papers.ab: Reconstructions of the opening of the Scotia Sea and the Drake Passage oceanic gateway have traditionally been based on considerations of ocean spreading and rifting between crustal blocks, and geological correlations based on sequences on islands such as South Georgia and the South Orkney Islands. Detrital zircon U Pb geochronological data derived from dredged schists and sandstones from two submerged continental blocks in the southern Scotia Sea, Bruce Bank and Discovery Bank, provide further constraints on the origin and tectonic movement of the blocks and confirm the use of detrital geochronology for understanding the tectonic evolution of the Scotia Sea. Bruce Bank yielded greenschist facies schist with a Triassic maximum sedimentation age of 216.2 Ma, similar to schist dredged from the northern continental margin of the adjacent South Orkney microcontinent. Both schists are correlated with metamorphic rocks of an accretionary complex exposed on the South Orkney Islands. Sandstones with Permian to Triassic maximum sedimentation ages of 258–224 Ma were dredged from both the northern margin of the South Orkney microcontinent and Discovery Bank. A younger sedimentary unit with Cretaceous maximum sedimentation ages of 140–110 Ma has been recovered from both Bruce and Discovery banks. The new data are consistent with the interpretations that Bruce and Discovery banks were joined in mid-Cretaceous times and that both were proximal to the South Orkney Islands in a position on the paleo-Pacific margin of Gondwana before Late Cretaceous-Cenozoic rifting, translation of the crustal blocks, and formation of the Scotia Sea.

papers.t: A Unified Quadratic Scaling Relation Between Potency and Local Earthquake Magnitudes for-1.8 ≤ ML ≤ 7.5
in: Department of Earth and Space Sciences
Southern University of Science and Technology
Nevada Seismological Laboratory
University of Nevada
Department of Earth Sciences
University of Southern California
tk: Establishes a unified quadratic scaling relation between seismic potency and local magnitude down to -1.8 using Bayesian spectral inference and multi-scale datasets.
建立了低至-1.8级的地震功率与地方震级统一二次定标关系。
papers.ab: Quantifying earthquake size across scales requires linking physical source parameters to empirical magnitude measures, especially for microearthquakes where attenuation, scattering, and instrumental limitations complicate source characterization. We combine regional results with near-source observations from the Tony Creek dual Microseismic Experiment, dense nodal data from Ridgecrest, and regional broadband data from San Jacinto to extend potency–magnitude scaling to local-magnitude ML ≈ −1.8. Bayesian spectral inference yields robust potency estimates across seven potency magnitude MP units and nine ML units. The combined datasets follow a continuous quadratic relation MP = 0.040M2 L + 0.556ML + 1.133. Synthetic modeling shows that source scaling, attenuation, and the finite Wood–Anderson passband can produce similar nonlinearity, although rupturescaling differences may also contribute. Despite sensitivity to observational and regional factors, the independent datasets are broadly consistent with the established quadratic relation, supporting it as a general empirical scaling over the investigated size range. Plain Language Summary Local magnitude is a common measure of earthquake size based on recorded ground motion, whereas seismic potency measures permanent deformation at the source. Estimating potency for very small earthquakes is difficult because the relevant signals are weak and affected by attenuation and instrumental bandwidth. We combine close-range recordings of induced microearthquakes in western Canada with independent tectonic earthquake observations from Ridgecrest and the San Jacinto Fault in California, together with a regional catalog of larger earthquakes. The combined observations reveal a smooth, curved relation between local magnitude and potency across a broad range of earthquake sizes. Tests with synthetic waveforms show that much of this curvature can arise from wave attenuation and the limited frequency range used to measure local magnitude, even when the earthquake sources scale similarly. The derived relation provides a practical empirical conversion between commonly reported magnitude and physical source size, while the exact coefficients may vary among regions and observing systems.

papers.t: A re-classification of Marsquakes based on P-wave coda
in: F́ısica Aplicada, Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea (EHU, Escuela de Ingenieŕıa de Bilbao, Bilbao, Spain
Université
Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Planétologie, C.N.R.S.
Université de Toulouse
Institut de physique du globe de Paris
CNRS
University of Bristol
Imperial College London
tk: A clustering procedure based on P-wave coda decay and morphology classifies high-frequency Marsquakes into five sub-groups, revealing regional structural variations around the InSight landing site.
基于P波尾波衰减和波形特征的聚类方法将高频火星震分为五类，揭示了InSight着陆点周围的区域结构差异。
papers.ab: The seismic events recorded by the NASA InSight mission provide one of the best resources to probe the interior structure of Mars. At the same time, the identification of their source is crucial to understand the active geological processes taking place on Mars to this day. Here, we present a clustering procedure for the P-wave coda of high frequency seismic events on Mars. This group of events is the most numerous type of Martian event, however, their spatial distribution and generation mechanisms are not fully understood, as they are only located to an epicentral distance. Our clustering procedure identifies five sub-groups of event. This characterisation is based on the P-wave coda slope decay, which provides information on attenuation and scattering, and on newly identified Pwave morphologies in terms of delayed energy arrivals. We interpret the differences between event clusters as evidence for distinct wave propagation pathways, based on a comparison to events with known locations. These results reveal variations in the regional structure surrounding the InSight landing site and provide new constraints on the spatial distribution and possible origins of high frequency types marsquakes.

papers.t: Origin of the Hawaiian Islands: An Asthenospheric Material Body with Heat Retention Caused by Migration Lag
in: Independent Researcher, Unknown, Xuchang, Henan, China [CN]
tk: Proposes that the Hawaiian hotspot originates from an asthenospheric body with heat retention caused by migration lag, rather than a deep mantle plume.
提出夏威夷热点源于软流圈物质滞后运移导致的蓄热，而非深部地幔柱。
papers.ab: The Hawaiian-Emperor chain has been interpreted as a mantle plume trail, but seismic and geochemical evidence contradict this. This paper proposes two possible origins for Hawaii's thermal anomaly: one is a body moving with the asthenosphere, externally heated from depth; the other is a high-viscosity body migrating with lag, preventing heat dissipation and causing local accumulation. "Heat retention" reflects hindered dissipation, not spontaneous generation. Comparing asthenospheric flow (mass-conservation constrained) with hotspot kinematics, seismic tomography, surface heat flow, helium isotopes, age-distance, and thermal wake distribution, this paper excludes the first model. It proposes instead a semi-confined domain beneath the Pacific plate, migrating at ~0.1 v_L (0.8–1.0 cm/a), far slower than the ambient asthenosphere (2.5–4.0 cm/a). This lag retains heat for ~45–55 Ma, establishing ~200°C thermal equilibrium—this is not the body's total age, which is much older (at least 85 Ma). Heat accumulation triggers melting. Conduit inertia causes stepwise eruption-site migration, forming an age-progressive chain. Thermal budget: 69 GW conductive plus 13.7 GW magmatic totals 82.7 GW, with only 16.6% excess heat—inconsistent with a deep plume. Predictions: cone-shaped low-velocity anomaly, depth-rotating SKS fast axes, and global hotspots moving toward mid-ocean ridges. This model differs from the classical plume hypothesis: hotspots are not deep imprints, but products of heat retention from migration lag. It provides a unified framework for intraplate volcanism and continental rifts. All data are from published literature; numerical modeling is left for future work.

papers.t: Multimodal speckle and polarization fiber sensing for localized, broadband vibration monitoring
tk: A dual-modality fiber-optic sensing architecture combining speckle dynamic analysis and polarization interrogation achieves localized, high-bandwidth vibration monitoring up to 40 kHz.
结合散斑动态分析与偏振解调的双模态光纤传感架构实现了高达40 kHz的局部宽带振动监测。
papers.ab: High-bandwidth and multi-point acoustic and vibration sensing is a critical asset for real-time condition monitoring, maintenance, and surveillance applications. In the case of large scales and harsh environments, optical fiber distributed sensing has emerged as a compelling alternative to electronic transducers, featuring lower installation and maintenance costs, along with compact footprints and enhanced robustness. Yet, current distributed fiber-optic sensing solutions are typically costly and face a resolution-bandwidth tradeoff. This work addresses the current challenges of distributed fiber optic sensors by presenting a dual-modality architecture that combines speckle dynamic analysis and polarization interrogation. The implementation operates under a single-active-source assumption across four discrete points distributed on a 4-m length fiber and uses camera-based speckle analysis to localize the active position, while the polarization interrogation reconstructs the corresponding waveform from 100 Hz to 40 kHz with a 200 kHz acquisition rate, with 35 dB SNR. Overall, the work establishes a general and promising blueprint to harness multimodality in fiber sensing and break single-modality constraints.

papers.t: Evaluation of passive seismic imaging by comparison with active-source results in the Larsemann Hills, Antarctica
in: Polar Research Institute of China
tk: Direct comparison of passive and active-source seismic imaging in Antarctica validates passive methods for high-resolution ice-sheet and shallow bedrock characterization.
南极野外对比研究证实，被动源地震成像可有效替代主动源进行冰盖及浅部基岩高分辨率成像。
papers.ab: In Antarctica, more than 98% of the continent is covered by ice sheets. Seismic exploration is recognized as one of the most effective methods for high-resolution imaging of ice sheets and the underlying bedrock. However, conducting active-source seismic surveys remains highly challenging due to the extreme environmental conditions and limited logistical support. Passive seismic exploration, which does not require active sources, has therefore emerged as a promising approach for efficient seismic investigations on Antarctic ice sheets. However, its imaging capability under field conditions still requires direct validation against active-source results. This study provided a field-scale validation of passive seismic imaging by directly comparing passive results with co-located active-source results acquired along a survey line on the ice sheet in the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica. Two seismic processing workflows were developed for surface-wave and body-wave imaging. For surface waves, least-squares noise suppression and beamforming-based stationary-phase selection were used to improve the quality of reconstructed virtual shot gathers. Multichannel analysis of surface waves (MASW) was conducted on active and passive data sets, and the resulting dispersion characteristics and inverted shear-wave velocity models showed strong consistency. For body-wave imaging, conventional reflection processing techniques used for active-source data were adapted for virtual shot gathers retrieved from passive recordings. The stacked passive seismic profile reproduced the main reflection events observed in the active-source profile, particularly the ice–bed interface and shallow reflections within the bedrock. These comparative results demonstrated that, in the Larsemann Hills region of Antarctica, passive seismic methods provided an environmentally sustainable, cost-effective, and reliable alternative to active seismic surveys for large-scale imaging of ice sheets and shallow bedrock structures.

papers.t: Gravity Continuity Is Not Magmatic Connectivity: Blind Tests of Lunar Volcanic Systems at Marius and Rümker Hills
in: China University of Geosciences, Hubei Subsurface Multi-Scale Imaging Key Laboratory, School of Geophysics and Geomatics, China University of Geosciences, Wuhan 430074, China, Hubei, China, China [CN]
Research Institute No.270, Unknown, Nanchang, China [CN]
tk: Gravity data alone cannot uniquely resolve shallow magmatic conduits or connectivity beneath lunar volcanic complexes due to high false-connection rates.
月球重力数据由于高虚假连通率，无法唯一解析浅部岩浆通道。
papers.ab: Gravity inversions can map smooth density continuities beneath lunar volcanic complexes, but their resolution is rarely tested. We reconstruct the Marius Hills Bouguer field from GRGM1200B gravity and finite-amplitude topography, then compare two disconnected frusta with nested connected models while withholding the proposed connector corridor. A nominal 80 × 50 × 5 km connector at 3–8 km depth fails blind prediction across regional fields, boundary perturbations, and constant-to-quadratic density models. The withheld-corridor mean of +54.52 mGal in degrees 7–660 comprises +57.39 mGal from degrees 7–60 and −2.87 mGal from degrees 61–660. Among 1,000 disconnected-truth bootstraps searching 400 geometries, 0.6% reproduce the joint gain of a broader 12–32 km body (p = 0.0070), but that gain reverses with spectral band and regional background. A further 3,000 scale-conditioned replicates yield complete-field false-connection rates of 13.2%–17.6%, whereas local-band blind prediction remains negative. Across density laws, the broad body retains anomalous mass of 1.218–1.364 × 10¹⁶ kg while its centroid depth shifts from 22.0 to 27.8 km. At Rümker Hills, strict false-partition rates are 22.9%–35.4%, and no tested density condition reaches 80% power at the observed residual level. Lunar gravity supports regional excess mass and possible lateral heterogeneity but does not uniquely resolve a shallow conduit, full-crustal partition, or vertical-density profile. Connectivity interpretations should therefore require spectral separation, spatial prediction, and correlated-residual null and power tests.

papers.t: Generative model to improve the physical simulation of normalized seismic acceleration
in: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Université Paris-Saclay
CentraleSupélec
tk: A novel Conformer-based generative adversarial network improves physics-based strong ground motion simulations by synthesizing realistic broadband accelerograms from low-frequency inputs.
提出一种基于Conformer的生成对抗网络，通过低频物理模拟合成逼真的宽频地震动加速度图。
papers.ab: Earthquake physics-based simulations have revealed their accuracy limit in high-fidelity broadband strong ground motion scenario prediction. Earlier attempts leveraging AI tried to fill the gap between the low-frequency high-fidelity numerical simulation and the high-frequency accuracy and realism demanded in earthquake engineering. Our research is built on top of the SeismoALICE solution proposed by Gatti and Clouteau (2020), an AI generative approach that renders broadband (0-20 Hz) single-station accelerograms conditioned by low-frequency physics-based simulation outcomes. First, we developed a novel neural architecture based on Encoder, Decoder, and Discriminators that integrates Conformer's advanced attention techniques (Gulati et al., 2020), stabilising the training and producing realistic output for the generation. This novel architecture is trained according to Adversarial Learning Inference with Conditional Entropy (ALICE, Li et al., 2017). Second, our approach employs a similarity evaluation technique called Hyper-Spherical Loss (HSL) in the time domain and an adaptation of the Focal Frequency Loss (FFL) for time series. Our investigation demonstrates that Conformer architecture outperforms previous approaches in super-resolution of earthquake data, such as the STanford EArthquake Dataset (STEAD) Dataset (Mousavi et al., 2019). We finally showcase the enhanced strong motion synthesizer to predict the seismic response at the Cruas Nuclear Power Plant during the 2019 MW 4.9 Le Teil earthquake, providing insightful perspective for future large-scale applications as a downstream generative pipeline.

papers.t: Seismoacoustic recovery of the SpaceX CRS-32 Dragon re-entry with a proof-of-concept for automated detection
tk: Seismoacoustic data from open networks and Raspberry Shakes are used to recover the SpaceX CRS-32 re-entry trajectory, with a neural network demonstrating automated N-wave detection.
利用公开地震台网与树莓派设备重建了SpaceX CRS-32重返大气层轨迹，并利用神经网络实现了N波自动检测。
papers.ab: Atmospheric re-entries of human-made objects are increasing in frequency, yet detailed information on their trajectory, fragmentation, and debris footprint is rarely made publicly available. This creates an information asymmetry in which regulators, independent agencies, and the scientific community lack the means to verify that re-entries occurred as reported or to characterize their physical processes for future modeling. We address this gap by applying a seismoacoustic localization method to the 25 May 2025 re-entry of the SpaceX CRS-32 Cargo Dragon spacecraft which splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Southern California. Using openly available seismic waveform data from 5 networks, including 22 Raspberry Shake amateur instruments, we recover a re-entry trajectory consistent in trajectory with the operator's publicly communicated splashdown prediction and release the manually labeled CRS-32 labeled N-wave picks as a public dataset. As a preliminary step toward automation, we train a neural network on the manually picked dataset and demonstrate reliable onset detection with stable performance across a wide range of detection thresholds, showcasing promise for N-wave detection from a two-event training set. These results show that existing open seismic infrastructure can provide independent, continental-scale characterization of re-entry events: a capability increasingly needed as the rate and opacity of commercial re-entries continue to grow.

papers.t: Dense earthquake catalogs for sparse seismic networks
tk: This work develops methods to build dense, high-resolution earthquake catalogs using sparse seismic networks.
该研究开发了利用稀疏地震台网构建高密度地震目录的方法。

papers.t: Implications of thermal weakening and magma compressibility for volcano monitoring
tk: 3D thermomechanical modeling shows that thermal weakening and magma compressibility significantly reduce volcanic surface uplift, leading to potential underestimation of intrusion volumes.
三维热力学模拟表明，热软化和岩浆压缩性会显著减少火山地表隆起。
papers.ab: Magmatic intrusion and volcanic deformation are traditionally approximated with an inflating cavity in an elastic halfspace. Various analytical models predict surface displacement as a function of pressure or volume change, depth, and elastic crustal properties. While this approach allows for rapid inversion of monitoring data, it neglects important components such as the visco-elastic behavior of thermally weakened host rock, magma transport, and magma compressibility. Here, we use 3D thermomechanical models to investigate the temporal evolution of overpressure and surface deformation due to magma influx into a pre-existing reservoir. Instead of applying an internal source of pressure or volume in the magma body, we introduce a cylindrical feeding system which allows us to track the self-consistent development of overpressure and investigate the effects of magma compressibility. Our model reproduces analytical solutions for an elastic host rock and a visco-elastic shell. For thermally weakened, visco-elastic host rock, we observe two effects: (i) The same overpressure causes more deformation, and (ii) the same injected volume causes less overpressure. These effects partially cancel out, with a net uplift reduction due to thermal weakening. Considering magma compressibility further reduces the overpressure. Stacking all three effects results in up to 80 % less surface deformation in our models compared to the elastic assumption. Consequently, intrusion volumes derived from surface deformation may be significantly underestimated, especially in young/cold magmatic systems. In thermally mature systems, magma overpressure is significantly overestimated. We propose modifications to the elastic solutions which can capture thermal weakening effects to first order.

papers.t: Detection of Interannual and Fine‐Scale Plate Coupling Variations Using Intraplate Earthquakes and Geodetic Data: Application to the Tohoku‐Oki Plate Boundary
in: Geological Survey of Japan AIST Ibaraki Japan
Meteorological Research Institute Ibaraki Japan
Now at Geological Survey of Japan AIST Ibaraki Japan
tk: A new method integrates geodetic data and intraplate earthquake focal mechanisms to resolve fine-scale, interannual variations in subduction zone plate coupling.
该研究结合大地测量与内震震源机制，实现了俯冲带板间耦合的高分辨率时空演化监测。
papers.ab: We propose a method to infer detailed spatiotemporal variations in interplate coupling by integrating geodetic and seismic data. It examines whether focal mechanisms of intraplate earthquakes occurring near the plate interface align with the stressing rates caused by a geodetically derived slip‐deficit rate model, evaluating deviations from a steady coupling state. We apply this method to the Tohoku‐Oki plate boundary region over a quarter‐century period, including the 2011 M w 9.0 Tohoku‐Oki earthquake. The analysis successfully detects previously reported features, such as the partial decoupling of the plate interface in the large slip area of the Tohoku‐Oki earthquake in the years leading up to the event, and the decadal evolution of aseismic slip off the coast of central and southern Tohoku before the Tohoku‐Oki earthquake. Additionally, it reveals complex variations in the interplate coupling, including temporal fluctuations and fine‐scale spatial heterogeneities not clearly captured by geodetic data alone. These findings highlight the value of integrating focal mechanism and geodetic information for a refined understanding of the evolving coupling state along subduction zones. Our method allows detection of changes on interannual timescale and spatial variations at scales finer than those typically resolved by geodetic inversions. This provides a powerful new tool for monitoring interplate coupling evolution, offering potential improvements in seismic hazard assessment and early identification of anomalous coupling patterns that may precede large earthquakes.

papers.t: Multiscale Surface Wave Tomography of the Bhutan Himalaya: MHT Imaging and Evidence of Crustal Tear of the MHT Below Central Bhutan
in: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Bhopal India
Swiss Seismological Service ETH Zürich Zurich Switzerland
CSIR‐National Geophysical Research Institute Hyderabad India
tk: Multiscale surface wave tomography using ambient noise and teleseismic data reveals the flat-ramp geometry and a potential crustal tear of the Main Himalayan Thrust beneath Bhutan.
利用背景噪声和远震面波多尺度成像揭示了不丹喜马拉雅主逆冲断裂的平缓坡折结构及地壳撕裂。
papers.ab: The Bhutan Himalaya, within the India‐Eurasia collision zone, is characterized by active deformation and significant seismic hazard. We image the Main Himalayan Thrust (MHT), the primary structure accommodating convergence, using surface wave dispersion derived from ambient noise and teleseismic earthquake recordings from the GANSSER network. Ambient noise data constrain shear wave velocities in the upper crust, whereas teleseismic Rayleigh waves extend resolution to ∼50 km depth. The resultant shear‐wave velocity model reveals pronounced lateral heterogeneity in the upper crust, including high‐velocity domains ( V s > 3.6 km/s) consistent with quartzite‐dominated lithologies. The MHT is imaged as a laterally continuous low‐velocity layer (LVL) exhibiting a flat‐ramp geometry: in western Bhutan a ramp emerges at ∼10 km, whereas in eastern Bhutan, the structure dips more gently to ∼20 km. In central Bhutan, disruption of the LVL, together with a concave‐upward lower‐crustal anomaly, suggest possible tear or segmentation of the thrust system.

papers.t: Building the Andean Crust at ∼35°S: Arc Geochemistry Reveals Cretaceous Thinning and Rapid Neogene Thickening
in: Department of Geosciences The University of Arizona Tucson AZ USA
Department of Earth, Energy, and Environment University of Calgary Calgary AB Canada
Department of Environmental Sciences University of Montana Western Dillon MT USA
IANIGLA–CONICET Mendoza Argentina
Montana Bureau of Mines and Geology Butte MT USA
Faculty of Geology and Geophysics University of Bucharest Bucharest Romania
Geological Institute of Romania Bucharest Romania
tk: Whole-rock geochemistry and zircon petrochronology from the Chilean Andes reveal Cretaceous crustal thinning followed by rapid Neogene thickening driven by retroarc shortening.
智利安第斯山脉的地球化学与锆石年代学研究揭示了白垩纪地壳变薄及新近纪快速增厚过程。
papers.ab: Quantification of the timing and mechanisms of crustal thickening in Cordilleran orogenic hinterlands remains challenging. We address this in the Andes using whole‐rock geochemistry and zircon petrochronology from a >70 Myr volcanic record in the Tinguiririca valley of Chile (∼35S), which captures a pivotal transition from extensional to contractional deformation. Zircon (Sm, Gd, Dy)/Yb ratios generally track trends in whole‐rock geochemical crustal thickness (paleomohometry) models across this record, with Dy/Yb showing the most consistent correspondence. Our results indicate modest crustal thinning coeval with Late Cretaceous normal faulting and oblique plate convergence. Eocene and Early Miocene samples yield similar crustal thicknesses (∼35 km), suggesting limited local net attenuation during proposed intra‐arc rifting (Abanico basin). The crust then thickened by ∼10 km to near‐modern values (∼46 km) during the Neogene; Quaternary estimates match modern geophysical constraints, validating the paleomohometry approach. Thickening was most rapid between ca. 17 and 13 Ma, coinciding with accelerated retroarc shortening and plate convergence. Additional zircon geochronologic and geochemical proxies (Th/U, phosphorus content, and oxygen fugacity) indicate enhanced Miocene crustal melting and magmatic productivity. Along‐strike comparisons reveal north‐to‐south younging and decreasing magnitude of thickening, mirroring trends in retroarc shortening. These findings indicate that underthrusting of foreland lithosphere during retroarc shortening drove crustal thickening, magmatic flare‐up, and generation of orogenic topography in the southern Central Andes.

papers.t: Improved Half‐Space Cooling Model Reconciles Bathymetry and Thermal Evolution of the Southwest Subbasin, South China Sea
in: State Key Laboratory of Submarine Geoscience Second Institute of Oceanography Ministry of Natural Resources Hangzhou China
Donghai Laboratory Zhoushan China
School of Oceanography Shanghai Jiao Tong University Shanghai China
tk: An improved half-space cooling model resolves Southwest Subbasin bathymetry, revealing magma-supported shallowing during spreading and significant post-spreading subsidence.
改进的半空间冷却模型揭示了南海西南次海盆由岩浆支撑的浅水深及显著的扩张后沉降。
papers.ab: The bathymetry of marginal sea basins commonly deviates from depths calculated by classical lithospheric cooling models, yet the controlling mechanisms remain debated. Here, using 19 seismic profiles and corrected local heat‐flow data, we apply an improved half‐space cooling model within a two‐stage reconstruction to reassess thermal subsidence of the Southwest Subbasin (SWSB), South China Sea (SCS). By correcting for sediment and crustal loading, dynamic topography, sea‐level change, and post‐spreading cooling, we reconstruct paleobathymetry at seafloor spreading cessation (∼16 Ma) and isolate water‐loaded subsidence during active spreading. Paleobathymetric reconstructions yield mean depths of 2.70–2.86 km at ∼16 Ma, compared with a present‐day sediment‐corrected mean of 4.55 km, implying 1.69–1.85 km of integrated post‐spreading subsidence. We interpret this deepening primarily as cooling and contraction following the rapid cessation of magmatic heat input, potentially amplified by dense recycled mantle components. Removing post‐spreading effects restores cessation‐age bathymetry comparable to normal oceanic lithosphere. Syn‐spreading age–depth coefficients are ∼188–287 m/Ma 1/2 lower than open‐ocean reference values, indicating a pronounced subsidence deficit. We attribute this to enhanced magma supply linked to subduction‐driven mantle flow, which maintained thermal and dynamic support during spreading. Along‐strike variations reflect heterogeneous magma supply influenced by southern slab breakoff and westward spreading propagation over heterogeneous lithosphere. Our results reveal a two‐stage evolution linking magma‐supported shallow bathymetry during spreading to substantial post‐spreading subsidence. This framework provides new constraints on the coupled roles of mantle dynamics, magma supply, and lithospheric cooling in shaping SWSB bathymetry.
