papers.t: Fault Damage Zones Q Value Determination From Spectra Decay Analysis and Its Application to the 2019 Ridgecrest Aftershock Sequence
in: School of Earth and Space Sciences, Peking University, Beijing, China
Division of Geological and Planetary Sciences, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, California, U.S.A.
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting, Peking University, Beijing, China
tk: Proposes a spectral decay method for fault zone trapped waves to resolve fine-scale attenuation, revealing higher attenuation at the Ridgecrest horse-tail segment.
提出利用断层带陷波谱衰减分析反演介质Q值的新方法，并应用于脊冠地震断裂带。
papers.ab: An earthquake-hosting fault may present complicated geometry, which has relatively straight and simple segments to host major slips, and bifurcates into “horse tail” structures near ends. The “horse tails” play an important role in controlling the nucleation and termination behaviors of great earthquakes. Despite the obvious geometrical differences between the two structures, understanding the damage zones formed by multiple ruptures is also important in understanding their physical properties. The seismic attenuation parameter (Q) is important in understanding fault damage zones, which are commonly considered to be related to the damage intensity and rock fragmentation, and further implies the fault maturity and porosity. However, Q is not well resolved in damage zones by traditional methods because damage zones only span a few hundred meters in width. The emergence of dense portable seismic arrays and high-precision microseismic catalogs now provides a new opportunity to resolve fine-scale attenuation structures. In this study, we propose a new method to invert for the attenuation properties of seismic waves trapped in fault damage zones (fault zone trapped waves) through spectral decay analysis of amplitude ratios from events with varying propagation distances along the fault. First, we develop the trapped wave attenuation theory by analogy with Love waves. Second, we validate the feasibility of inverting attenuation curves by theoretical analysis and extracting the parameters from the attenuation curves. Furthermore, we adopt the inversion methods for two dense portable arrays (B2 and B4) deployed across the ruptured fault segments of the 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake. Our inverted results reveal markedly different attenuation structures for damage zones at different locations: the damage zone at the “horse tail” (along array B4) shows a Q value of ∼30–40 and a velocity reduction of ∼20–30%, whereas at the central fault (along B2 array) exhibits a Q of ∼50–70 and a velocity reduction of ∼10–15%. Overall, the “horse tail” faults may exhibit a more fragmented, fluid-rich, and compliant zone in comparison with the central segment. Our method provides a generalized framework to quantify near-fault attenuation from dense seismic observations. Our method is effective and can be generalized to invert attenuation parameters for other fault zone observations.

papers.t: Direct Detection of Hydrogen Reveals a New Macroscopic Crustal Water Reservoir on Early Mars
in: Department of Energy Conversion and Storage Technical University of Denmark Kgs. Lyngby Denmark
Department of Physics Technical University of Denmark Kgs. Lyngby Denmark
Centre for Star and Planet Formation Globe Institute University of Copenhagen Copenhagen Denmark
Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science Technical University of Denmark Kgs. Lyngby Denmark
Nanoscience Center Niels Bohr Institute University of Copenhagen Copenhagen Denmark
PSI Center for Neutron and Muon Sciences Paul Scherrer Institute Villigen Switzerland
European Synchrotron Radiation Facility Grenoble France
Danish Technological Institute Høje Taastrup Denmark
Department of Chemistry Aarhus University Aarhus Denmark
MAX IV Laboratory Lund University Lund Sweden
tk: Combined neutron and X-ray tomography of Martian meteorite NWA 7034 reveals hydrogen-rich iron oxyhydroxides, indicating a widespread ancient crustal water reservoir on Mars.
结合中子和X射线断层扫描技术，在火星陨石中发现了富氢铁氢氧化物，揭示了早期火星广泛存在的地壳水库。
papers.ab: The next great leap in Martian exploration is the return of samples to Earth. Maximizing their scientific value requires non‐destructive analytical techniques for early three‐dimensional characterization. Neutron computed tomography (CT), highly sensitive to hydrogen, complements conventional X‐ray CT and enables the detection of hydrous phases. The distribution and nature of hydrous phases are central to understanding the habitability, climatic and geological evolution, and potential biosignatures of Mars. Using the only Martian crustal material available on Earth, the NWA 7034 meteorite and its pairs, we demonstrate that combined neutron, X‐ray, and X‐ray diffraction CT enables non‐destructive, sample‐wide hydrogen mapping, revealing the distribution and petrographic contexts of hydrous phases. We identify hydrogen‐rich iron oxyhydroxides within ancient igneous clasts, representing a macroscopic mineralogical water reservoir. These alteration assemblages closely resemble those observed by the Perseverance rover in Jezero crater, indicating that such hydrated phases may constitute a widespread near‐surface water reservoir on early Mars.

papers.t: Abrupt Suppression of Tectonic Tremors Outside the Stress Shadow of Mendocino Earthquakes
in: ISTerre Université Grenoble Alpes CNRS Université Savoie Mont Blanc IRD Université Gustave Eiffel Grenoble France
Department of Earth and Planetary Science The University of Tokyo Tokyo Japan
School of Earth Sciences Yunnan University Kunming China
tk: Tectonic tremors near the Mendocino Triple Junction abruptly ceased after major earthquakes despite Coulomb stress increases, suggesting fluid-driven recovery processes.
门多西诺三联点附近的构造微震在大地震后骤然停止，表明流体过程主导了其恢复。
papers.ab: Tectonic tremor is a long‐duration noise‐like seismic signal associated with slow fault motion at major plate boundaries. Due to their remarkable sensitivity to stress perturbations, tremors serve as invaluable probes of the mechanical state and stress conditions deep within fault zones. Near the Mendocino Triple Junction, a tremor cluster ceased abruptly following each of three Mw 6.0+ earthquakes (2020–2024), including the 2024 Mw 7.0 Mendocino fault earthquake. Moment tensor inversion reveals a high‐angle, right‐lateral strike‐slip mechanism for this tremor cluster. Coulomb stress modeling indicates the tremor cluster is located in a region where Coulomb stress was increased by the mainshock. During the recovery phase of tremor activity, we observed a clear migration trend. Integrating these observations with tomography, we suggest that fluid‐related processes may have contributed to tremor suppression and recovery. Our results provide a broader framework for understanding how large earthquakes modulate slow fault slip beyond stress shadow effects.

papers.t: Amploc: A Complete Python Workflow for Amplitude-Based Locations
in: USGS Cascades Volcano Observatory, Vancouver, Washington, U.S.A.
tk: Amploc is an open-source Python workflow integrating amplitude-based location algorithms, station corrections, and an interactive GUI for real-time seismic monitoring.
Amploc是一个集成了振幅定位算法、台站校正和交互式GUI的开源Python实时地震监测工作流。
papers.ab: Amplitude-based locations are well suited for characterizing long-duration seismic sources that may migrate with time, such as debris flows, avalanches, rockfall, and volcanic tremor. Although amplitude-based location methods have existed for decades, their adoption in real-time monitoring systems remains limited. We present a complete Python-based workflow that includes station corrections, amplitude-based location algorithms, and interactive review tools that are appropriate for real-time use. The algorithms themselves are not new; however, Amploc integrates several previously published methods into a unified operational framework. The workflow also introduces a browser-based graphical interface that allows users to review real-time location results using formats familiar to many observatories. By integrating calibration, location algorithms, and visualization tools, Amploc lowers the barrier to operational use of amplitude-based locations and improves characterization of phenomena that inform hazard assessments such as long-period earthquakes, volcanic tremor, and debris flows.

papers.t: Atmosphere-groundwater modulated seismic velocity variations revealed by distributed acoustic sensing
tk: Hourly seismic velocity variations in Hefei, China, monitored via DAS and seismic interferometry, reveal environmental modulations driven by thermoelastic effects, groundwater, and barometric pressure.
利用DAS与地震干涉法监测合肥由气象和地下水调制的波速变化。
papers.ab: Monitoring seismic velocity variations in Earth’s critical zone (CZ) provides crucial information on Earth’s environmental changes. However, monitoring of urban near-surface environments at high temporal resolution is still challenging. Combining distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and seismic interferometry, we acquired hourly high-precision seismic velocity variations in downtown Hefei city, China, with amplitude up to 10 -3 . Velocity variations exhibit long-term and diurnal signals with amplitudes of ～10 -4 . Sub-daily signals are also presented with amplitudes one order smaller. The long-term and diurnal variations of seismic velocity are well explained by thermoelastic effect modeling, and transient signals (~ 0.05%) are well fitted by hydraulic force modeling from groundwater data and precipitation data. We also conclude that the semi-diurnal velocity variations are caused by the interaction of barometric pressure and the water table. This work demonstrates the capability of DAS to conduct hourly monitoring of Earth’s CZ in urban areas and cast insight into land-atmosphere coupling from a seismological perspective.

papers.t: Cascadia Slow Earthquake Behaviors Modulated by Tectonic and Environmental Forcings
in: Joint Institute for Regional Earth System Science and Engineering (JIFRESSE) University of California Los Angeles CA USA
Jet Propulsion Laboratory California Institute of Technology Pasadena CA USA
tk: Cascadia slow earthquake behaviors are modulated by stress variations from past slow slip events and long-term stress redistribution rather than just annual hydrological cycles.
卡斯卡迪亚慢地震受慢滑移应力及长期应力重新分布的调节。
papers.ab: Slow earthquakes, including episodic tremor and slip (ETS), are highly sensitive to small stress perturbations, yet their links to tectonic and non‐tectonic forcings remain unclear. Previous studies suggest that annual hydrological cycle dominates the tremor seasonal behavior in northern Cascadia. But over a longer time range, the tremor seasonal pattern seems significantly changed. Here, we systematically examine major stress perturbations toward influencing tremor and slow slip event (SSE) activities in Cascadia and identify two distinct patterns: an incongruent tremor seasonal variation that cannot be explained by hydrological forcing and a long‐term change in the locations where ETS events nucleate and their propagation directions. The tremor seasonality is better explained by stress variation due to SSEs, while the long‐term ETS evolution likely reflects spatiotemporal stress redistribution on subduction fault interface through stress feedback of past major ETS events and potential stress balancing along fault strike.

papers.t: Competing Effects of Elastic Heterogeneity and Viscous Flow on Interseismic Coupling at Cascadia
in: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Science Kiel Germany
Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences Indiana University Bloomington IN USA
United States Geological Survey Seattle WA USA
tk: Viscoelasticity offsets the deepening of inferred Cascadia coupling caused by elastic heterogeneity, improving fits to vertical deformation data.
粘弹性抵消了弹性非均匀性导致的卡斯卡迪亚锁固加深。
papers.ab: Interseismic coupling maps are important tools for estimating future earthquake hazard at subduction zones. Often interseismic coupling is estimated from surface velocities using a homogeneous elastic Earth model. However, inversions that incorporate viscoelastic mantle flow or elastic heterogeneity show that each can change the spatial distribution and magnitude of estimated coupling. We present here a Bayesian inversion of surface deformation for the boundaries of coupling zones at the Cascadia subduction zone that incorporates both elastic heterogeneity and a viscoelastic earthquake cycle model. We find that elastic heterogeneity deepens inferred coupling and worsens fit to surface deformation compared to homogeneous elastic models, but viscoelasticity partly offsets these effects and yields similar coupling and a better fit to the vertical data than homogeneous elastic models. We also find that, of all geometries and viscosities tested, downgoing plate thickness and oceanic mantle viscosity have the greatest impact on modeled displacements and coupling.

papers.t: Seismic Exploration for Magmatic Brine Lenses: An Example From Soufrière Hills Volcano, Montserrat
in: Department of Earth Sciences University of Oxford Oxford UK
School of Geosciences University of Witwatersrand Johannesburg South Africa
Montserrat Volcano Observatory Flemmings Montserrat
Seismic Research Centre The University of the West Indies St. Augustine Trinidad and Tobago
NORSAR Kjeller Norway
tk: Joint inversion of seismic travel times and earthquake parameters reveals a subvolcanic, fluid-saturated magmatic brine lens at 2–3 km depth beneath Soufrière Hills Volcano.
联合反演地震走时与震源参数，揭示了苏弗里埃尔火山下方2-3千米处的富金属盐水透镜体。
papers.ab: The majority of metallic ore deposits are related to processes associated with ancient or modern volcanic systems. Beyond geothermal energy production, volcanoes also represent a potential resource of critical metals, including those required for carbon‐neutral technologies. Geothermal metals occur in subsurface fluid reservoirs fed by surface and magmatic sources. Metals primarily derive from magmatic sources associated with hot, saline brine lenses. Imaging and characterizing such fluid bodies remains challenging. Here, we apply a joint inversion of P ‐, S ‐wave travel times and local earthquake parameters, to image the subsurface of Soufrière Hills Volcano, Montserrat. Analysis of seismic velocities, V P / V S ratio, and hypocenter distributions provide evidence for a subvolcanic, fluid‐saturated, and presumably metal‐rich lens at depths of ∼2–3 km. Our results also show evidence of previously‐confirmed hot and shallower geothermal systems. We discuss the implications of these results for the magmatic source region and the structure of the associated geothermal system.

papers.t: Crustal Density Differences Along Mars' Dichotomy Boundary From Gravity and Topography
in: Planetary Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Laboratory NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Greenbelt MD USA
Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratory NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Greenbelt MD USA
tk: Spacecraft tracking data analysis reveals Mars' northern crustal density is 2622 ± 42 kg/m³ and southern is 2492 ± 36 kg/m³, consistent with seismic constraints.
利用航天器跟踪数据测得火星北部壳密度为2622 kg/m³，南部为2492 kg/m³。
papers.ab: Seismic data for Mars has provided constraints on the thickness of its crust, but its density and how much it varies spatially, especially across the hemispherical dichotomy, is still undetermined. We apply a novel constraint in the analysis of spacecraft tracking data to determine Mars' gravity field that allows for the determination of the density of the north and south directly from the data. We find a density of kg for the north and kg for the south. This result is independent from the seismic results, and consistent with seismic constraints that indicate the difference between the north and south should not be greater than 200 kg . Accounting for the higher densities of volcanoes changes the difference slightly, still within the seismic constraint. Our density results provide additional, independent constraints for crustal thickness modeling and elucidating the origin of the dichotomy.

papers.t: Detailed Shallow Shear Velocity Structure in the Nankai Trough From Ambient Noise Differential Adjoint Tomography: Implications for Earthquake Generation Mechanisms
in: University of Hong Kong Hong Kong China
Japan Agency for Marine‐Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) Yokohama Japan
Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
tk: Ambient noise differential adjoint tomography reveals high-resolution shallow Vs structure in the Nankai Trough, highlighting how permeability and fluid migration control earthquake generation.
利用背景噪声差分伴随成像揭示南海海槽浅部高分辨率剪切波速度结构，阐明流体运移对地震产生机制的影响。
papers.ab: Seismic and aseismic slip has been reported in the Nankai Trough. In this study we apply ambient noise differential adjoint tomography to obtain a high‐resolution S‐wave velocity (Vs) model in the Nankai Trough. The Vs in the very shallow imbricate thrust zone is higher than that on both the seaward and landward sides. This region may prevent the upward migration of fluids from below, which may lead to an elevated pore fluid pressure beneath the region and facilitate slow earthquake occurrence. There is a large‐scale anomaly with low Vs and high P‐wave velocity (Vp)/Vs in the Kumano basin. This may be caused by the ascent of deep‐sourced fluids from the plate boundary and indicate that an impermeable condition is absent in the seismogenic zone. In subduction zones the permeability property above fluid‐source zones may be important for the strength of the plate interface and thus the types of earthquakes.

papers.t: Seismic Radial Anisotropy of the Southern Tibetan Rifts From Ambient Noise Adjoint Tomography: Basal Shear and Localized Crustal Weak Zones Promote Rifting
in: State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics and Forecasting School of Earth and Space Sciences Peking University Beijing China
Department of Ocean Science and Engineering Southern University of Science and Technology Shenzhen China
State Key Laboratory of Lithospheric and Environmental Coevolution Institute of Geology and Geophysics Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
tk: Ambient noise adjoint tomography reveals that deep basal shear focuses into localized mid-to-upper crustal weak zones beneath southern Tibetan rifts, promoting E-W extension.
背景噪声伴随成像揭示深部基底剪切聚焦于藏南裂谷中上地壳薄弱带并促进裂谷发育。
papers.ab: North–south‐trending rifts in southern Tibet record E–W extension within the Tibetan Plateau, closely linked to high gravitational potential energy from collisional thickening and northward underthrusting of the Indian lower crust. To reveal how basal shear is transmitted upward and controls rifting, we use ambient noise adjoint tomography with broadband temporary‐array data to construct crustal shear‐wave velocity and seismic radial anisotropy (RA) models beneath three rifts. Positive RA is pervasive in the mid‐to lower crust of the Lhasa Terrane (∼30–55 km), indicating ductile shear deformation related to Indian lower‐crustal underthrusting. In contrast, low velocities (equivalent to ∼3.7%–5.2% partial melt) and strong positive RA in the mid‐to upper crust (∼10–30 km) are mainly confined beneath rift axes. These results suggest that, during upward transmission, deep basal shear preferentially focuses into localized weak zones in the mid‐to upper crust, thereby promoting rifting above.

papers.t: The Pulsating Earth: A Unified Thermoelectric-Physical Model Resolving the Systemic Anomalies of Plate Tectonics
in: Independent researcher
tk: Proposes a pulsating Earth model driven by thermoelectric and electrochemical feedbacks in LLSVPs to explain global tectonic cycles.
提出一种由LLSVP热电和电化学反馈驱动的地球脉动模型，用以解释全球构造循环。
papers.ab: The plate tectonic paradigm, while successful in explaining first-order surface features, has accumulated 31 systemic observational contradictions—ranging from deep continental roots and the mechanical feasibility of large-scale plate motion to the episodic nature of orogenesis, complex magnetic anomaly patterns, and the antipodal distribution of continents—that increasingly demand ad‑hoc auxiliary assumptions to maintain internal consistency. This study presents a fundamentally reimagined geodynamic framework in which these contradictions are resolved through a cyclical pulsating Earth model driven by coupled thermoelectric, electrochemical, and thermodynamic feedback mechanisms operating within the Large Low Shear Velocity Provinces (LLSVPs) and their embedded Ultra‑Low Velocity Zones (ULSVPs) at the base of the lower mantle. The proposed physical engine operates as follows: thermal gradients between the iron‑rich LLSVPs and the surrounding silicate mantle generate thermoelectric voltages via the Seebeck effect (S ≈ 0.1–0.5 mV/K), which are augmented by electrochemical potentials arising from perovskite‑to‑post‑perovskite phase transitions and iron redox reactions (Fe2+ ⇌ Fe3+ + e-). These driving voltages produce electric currents that are amplified through three positive feedback loops: (1) Peltier heating at the LLSVP‑mantle boundary, (2) adiabatic compression under volumetric confinement, and (3) Arrhenius‑type increases in electrical conductivity (small polaron hopping, ionic conduction, and partial melt conduction). The resulting self‑sustaining heating and cooling cycles drive periodic radial expansion and contraction of the planet, generating extensional tectonics (seafloor spreading, continental rifting) during heating phases and compressional tectonics (subduction, orogenesis) during cooling phases. Quantitative validation demonstrates that the LLSVP‑ULSVP‑outer core system generates a total magnetic flux of 1.916 × 1025 flux lines—falling precisely at the algorithmic midpoint of the scientifically expected range (4.8 × 1024 to 4.8 × 1025 flux lines)—without requiring parameter tuning beyond established mineral‑physics constraints. Furthermore, the model yields a total radial expansion of 324.4 km over 20 million years; after deducting 11.4% for mechanical work (lithospheric uplift, faulting, deformation resistance and in exhausting the cooling wave in mantle from the previous stage), the net new crustal area corresponds to 287.3 km, exactly matching the observed oceanic crust production documented by Müller et al. (2008). The derived heating cycle duration of 45,000 years (natural range: 37,000–56,000 years) and peak surface velocities of approximately 19 mm/yr provide explicit, testable predictions for geodetic, paleomagnetic, and cosmogenic isotope records, including the interpretation of the Laschamp (~41 ka) and Mono Lake (~33–34 ka) geomagnetic excursions as LLSVP phase‑transition markers. This pulsating framework resolves all 31 tectonic problems cataloged by Pratt (2000) within a unified mechanical and thermodynamic ontology, eliminating the need for ad‑hoc secondary hypotheses. It provides a coherent explanation for the coexistence of extensional and compressional structures within the same tectonic provinces, the episodic nature of mountain building, the presence of continental fragments within ocean basins, the complex geometry of accretionary wedges, and the antipodal distribution of continents. By grounding the driving mechanism in experimentally verified thermoelectric and electrochemical properties of lower mantle minerals—the Seebeck and Peltier effects, redox chemistry, and solid‑state defect physics—the model advances a falsifiable, quantitatively robust alternative to conventional plate tectonics, inviting rigorous testing through continued space‑geodetic monitoring, high‑resolution seismic tomography, and spectral analysis of paleoclimatic and paleomagnetic archives. The Earth, it appears, breathes through cycles of thermal‑electrical pulsation; the tectonic features we observe are the surface expressions of this deep, rhythmic respiration.

papers.t: Differentiating the contribution of magma and gas to the current unrest at Campi Flegrei over space and time with modelling
in: Department of Physics and Astronomy
Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Sez., Napoli-Osservatorio Vesuviano
Bayerisches Geoinstitut
Universität Bayreuth
tk: This study compares numerical models to differentiate the contributions of deep magma and shallow gas to ground deformation at Campi Flegrei.
本研究利用数值模拟区分了坎皮佛莱格瑞岩浆与气体对形变的贡献。
papers.ab: Campi Flegrei caldera has experienced increasing rates of uplift over the past 20 years, paired with increased seismicity rates and magnitudes since 2005, becoming even more pronounced after 2018. While magma transport from depth is often invoked to explain deformation patterns, other studies highlight shallow fluid accumulation as the primary driver of deformation. Disentangling these processes is challenging, as no modelling framework currently reproduces both processes while considering geophysical, geochemical and petrological constraints on geometry and material properties. Here, we compare thermo-mechanical and thermo-poro-viscoelastic models to assess the relative contributions of deep magma migration and shallow reservoir pressurization. We first integrate seismic imaging, geodesy, and rock physics constraints into a three-dimensional thermo-mechanical model with viscoelasto-plastic rheologies. The model includes magma influx from 8 km depth feeding a reservoir whose top reaches 4.25 km, together with a weak tuff layer and hydrothermal system. We then model a thermo-poro-viscoelastic inclusion representing a shallow gas-rich reservoir with its top at 2 km depth. Comparison with InSAR and GNSS observations shows that magma migration reproduces the first-order deformation pattern but not its full amplitude and temporal evolution when independent constraints are considered. Gas accumulation and hydrothermal pressurization can instead recover the spatiotemporal deformation history, with some spatial discrepancies after the onset of seismic unrest. This approach provides insights into how much of the deformation history we can reproduce using competitive interpretations, the full interdisciplinary information available, and advanced modelling frameworks. Plain Language Summary Scientists at Campi Flegrei have conflicting opinions about whether deep magma or shallow gas and fluids are producing the ongoing ground deformation, started in the 2000s, and seismicity, which has been steadily rising since 2015. Advances in modelling allow testing these interpretations under a common modelling framework, including all evidence and data the volcano continuously produces. While the effect of magma progressively rising to surface can model part of the ground deformation, shallow gas and fluids are necessary to reproduce the 25-years deformation-history at the caldera, at least until the recent, more intense seismic unrest. These models show that coupling these two mechanisms is key to understanding the volcano, and likely necessary to forecast the next eruption.

papers.t: Foreshock productivity and rupture nucleation in injection-induced earthquakes in western Canada
in: Institute of Advanced Technology (Institute of Interdisciplinary Frontiers Science), School of Physics, Zhejiang University of Technology, Hangzhou, China.
Geological Survey of Canada, Natural Resources Canada (NRCan), Sidney, Canada.
School of Earth Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.
State Key Laboratory of Ocean Sensing, School of Physics, Institute of Quantum Precision Measurement, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.
State Key Laboratory of Earthquake Dynamics, Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration, Beijing, China.
tk: Analysis of 77 injection-induced earthquake sequences in western Canada reveals that 92% have foreshocks, highlighting three distinct fluid-driven nucleation models.
对加拿大西部77个诱发地震序列的研究表明，92%存在前震，并揭示了三种流体驱动的成核机制。
papers.ab: Foreshock activity is a key consideration in traffic-light protocol (TLP) to mitigate seismic risk from injection-induced earthquakes (IIEs). However, the seismogenic processes of IIE foreshocks remain poorly understood. Using an enhanced western Canada catalog (2014–2024), we analyzed 77 IIE sequences to statistically delineate foreshock patterns before local magnitude ( M L ) ≥ 3 mainshocks. We found that 92% are preceded by foreshocks and that foreshock productivity and spatiotemporal patterns reflect the interplay among fluid injection, the seismogenic index, and the fault stress state. Sequence-specific analyses elucidate three nucleation models: fluid-driven preslip with weakened source asperity, fluid-driven preslip with intact source asperity, and fluid-driven cascade, highlighting the central role of fluids in enabling aseismic slip and interevent stress transfer before mainshock rupture. These results imply that IIE monitoring strategies should be spatially conditioned according to foreshock productivity.

papers.t: Long-Term Spatiotemporal Distribution of Great Earthquakes and Its Physical Drivers: An Analysis Based on Thermal-Mechanical Coupling and Scale Invariance
tk: This study proposes a thermal-mechanical coupling framework to explain the global heterogeneity of great earthquakes, finding a strong negative correlation between crustal heat flow and earthquake density.
本研究提出了一个热-力耦合框架，揭示了地壳热流与大地震密度之间的显著负相关性。
papers.ab: Approximately 90% of global shallow great earthquakes (M≥7) are concentrated along the Circum-Pacific subduction zones and continental collision belts, while ancient cratons exhibit remarkably sparse strong earthquake records. This study proposes a thermal-mechanical coupling framework, based on the spatial correlation between radioactive element distribution, terrestrial heat flow, and seismic activity, to explain the pronounced heterogeneity in the global distribution of great earthquakes. We find a significant negative correlation between crustal heat flow and the density of M≥7 earthquakes (Pearson r = -0.68, p

papers.t: Physical Controls on the Shape of Earthquake Source Time Functions

tk: This study investigates the physical factors, such as frictional properties and stress state, that dictate the temporal shape of earthquake source time functions.
该研究探讨了决定地震震源时间函数时间特性的物理因素（如摩擦性质和应力状态）。

papers.t: DASView: A PyQt-Based Visualization and Processing Tool for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
in: School of Electrical Engineering and Automation, Hefei University of Technology, Hefei, China
School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
State Key Laboratory of Precision Geodesy, School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
Senseable City Laboratory, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, Massachusetts, U.S.A.
tk: DASView is an open-source, PyQt-based interactive visualization and processing tool designed to handle massive distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) datasets efficiently.
DASView是一款基于PyQt的开源交互式分布式声波传感（DAS）数据可视化与处理软件。
papers.ab: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) has emerged as a transformative geophysical sensing technology, with growing applications in seismic monitoring, intelligent traffic surveillance, and urban subsurface imaging, driven by its high spatial density, cost efficiency, and environmental robustness. However, DAS data are typically massive and ultradensely sampled, which fundamentally differs from conventional seismic records and presents significant challenges for data visualization and signal processing. To lower the technical barriers for DAS data analysis, we develop an interactive visualization and processing tool based on the PyQt framework. The tool integrates both classical seismic data processing workflows, such as data slicing, filtering, and spectral analysis, as well as DAS-specific functionalities, including denoising and channel attribute analysis. Core features include 2D waterfall visualization, interactive single-channel waveform and spectrum inspection, and flexible figure export. In addition, the platform supports modules for travel-time extraction and automated traffic signal tracking. We also provide openly accessible example datasets to facilitate method validation. This tool is intended to support DAS researchers and practitioners by offering an accessible and efficient platform for DAS data exploration, processing, and visualization, thereby contributing to the broader adoption and advancement of DAS-based sensing technologies.

papers.t: A Two-Interface Driving Model for Horizontal Asthenospheric Flow: A Unified Physical Framework
in: Independent Researcher, Unknown, Xuchang, Henan, China [CN]
tk: Proposes a two-interface driving model for asthenospheric flow that unifies different friction regimes and predicts seismic anisotropy.
提出软流圈双界面驱动模型，统一摩擦机制并预测各向异性。
papers.ab: The asthenosphere is a key layer between lithospheric plates and the deep mantle. Traditional models treat it as a passive viscous "conveyor belt" driven by overriding-plate drag. We propose a two-interface driving model based on an equivalent friction framework (μ∝v/H) and an interface-selection principle that selects optimal frictional interfaces. We apply these tools to asthenospheric kinematics. Our analysis predicts a continuous velocity profile: an upper drag layer (~30 km, velocity decreasing from v_L to zero), and a return-flow zone (~150 km) rising from zero to a broad peak of 0.6–0.8v_L before decaying to zero. At the LAB we obtain μ≈0.0067 (effective creep-layer thickness ~366 m); at the mantle-transition-zone top, μ≈0.3‰–0.8‰. Average return-flow velocity reaches ~0.5v_L, consistent with force-balance constraints and rheological inversions. Two key advances are reported. First, depth-dependent shear stress from vertical velocity gradients drives dislocation creep and olivine-lattice rotation, generating predictable 3‑D a‑axis tilting testable by SKS splitting, establishing a macroscopic-to-crystal causal link for LPO fabric. Second, shear-creep thickness is controlled by melt fraction via solid grain size: melt fraction → grain size → deformation thickness → friction. In the fully molten limit this reduces to fluid friction; in the solid limit it yields Byerlee-type friction, unifying fluid, partial-melt, and solid friction within one continuum. The asthenosphere thus behaves as an active layered domain: velocity structure follows interface selection, and return flow is governed by mass conservation.

papers.t: Interaction of water and supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) with rock and joints
in: University of Tehran
K. N. Toosi University of Technology
University of Kurdistan
tk: This study uses 2D fully coupled hydromechanical FDEM simulations to demonstrate that supercritical CO2 outperforms water in fracturing rock by lowering breakdown pressure.
本研究利用二维全耦合FDEM模拟，证明超临界二氧化碳在降低破裂压力方面优于水。
papers.ab: Reservoir stimulation by hydraulic fracturing has become a superior technique by injecting high-pressure fluid into deep rock to initiate fractures, creating new fluid paths to improve oil and gas extraction. Water is the primary fluid used in hydraulic fracturing and has demonstrated advantages over the decades in enhancing reservoir permeability. While water is the most common fluid used in hydraulic fracturing, its use presents several significant limitations. Chief among them is the intense demand on local freshwater supplies, which can exacerbate water scarcity and compete with agricultural and municipal needs in arid regions. Furthermore, the flowback of contaminated water -containing dissolved salts, heavy metals, and naturally occurring radioactive materials -poses serious risks of soil and groundwater pollution if not properly managed. Finally, the disposal of this produced water through deep-well injection has been conclusively linked to induced seismicity, or human-caused earthquakes, creating geological instability. These limitations encourage the search for alternative fluids, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO 2 ). This paper employed a 2D fully coupled hydromechanical finite-discrete element method (FDEM) to study the performance of water and ScCO 2 in intact and jointed rocks. Important factors, including flow rate, in-situ stress magnitude, and fluid viscosity, are assessed for both the fluid and the results, and the results are compared with respect to the fluid-driven fracture pattern and breakdown pressure. The results confirm the extraordinary performance of ScCO 2 compared to water. ScCO 2 penetrates easily into rock grains and joints, easily dilates them, and generates fracture branching and long fractures. Moreover, breakdown pressures are lower than those of water, making it a preferred alternative to enhance permeability with less fluid energy.

papers.t: Weakening mechanisms and the energy budget of simulated earthquakes in carbonates
in: The University of Texas at Austin, 2275 Speedway Stop C9000, Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Austin, United States [US]
The University of Texas at Austin, JGB 4.216G, 1 University Sta. C9000, Austin, United States [US]
University of Utah, Unknown, Salt Lake City, United States [US]
Universita degli studi di Padova Dipartimento di Geoscienze, Via Gradenigo 6, Padova, 35131, Italy [IT]
tk: Integrates infrared thermal imaging with numerical heat-conduction modeling to constrain fault-surface temperatures and weakening mechanisms in laboratory carbonate earthquakes.
结合红外热成像与数值热传导模拟，约束了实验室碳酸盐岩地震中的断层表面温度及弱化机制。
papers.ab: The coseismic temperature along faults is critical for evaluating earthquake energy budgets and thermally activated dynamic weakening mechanisms. However, coseismic temperatures cannot be measured directly during natural earthquakes and remain difficult to constrain in laboratory experiments, mainly because of technical limitations. Here, we develop a method that integrates infrared thermal imaging with numerical heat-conduction modeling to infer fault-surface temperatures during laboratory earthquakes. The approach explicitly accounts for the finite spatial resolution of the thermocamera, the geometry of the experimental setup, the distribution of heat sources, and the real-to-nominal contact area ratio (Ac/A). We apply this framework to a high-velocity rotary shear experiment on limestone exhibiting pronounced velocity weakening. By fitting time-dependent temperature fields extracted from thermal imagery, we constrain the distribution and magnitude of frictional heat sources along the slipping surface. For realistic real-to-nominal contact area ratios (0.2 We conclude that flash-heating-induced weakening mechanisms were absent in our experiment and that other processes, such as thermal softening or powder lubrication, must have caused the observed weakening. More broadly, our study provides constraints on earthquake energy budgets and the role of thermal processes during seismic slip.

papers.t: Carbon dioxide release from cooling magmatic underplate: Implications for the origin of CO2 emanations in the Cheb Basin, Western Ohře (Eger) Rift area, Bohemian Massif
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Charles University
Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Geophysics
Czech Geological Survey
tk: This study models CO2 release from a cooling magmatic underplate to explain the origin of CO2 emanations in the Cheb Basin.
热模型与相平衡计算表明，切布盆地CO2释放源于冷却岩浆底侵。
papers.ab: Geodynamic activity in the western Ohře (Eger) Rift area, Bohemian Massif, comprises seismic swarms, CO2 emanations, and Cenozoic volcanic activity, with relationships between individual phenomena remaining debated and largely unknown. Above that, seismic studies and petrological observations of mantle xenoliths in the area suggest a possibility of (sub)recent magma underplating and ponding at crust/mantle boundary. In this contribution, we integrate new and existing lithospheric thermal models with phase equilibria calculations and CO2 solubility models. By this approach, we determine the release dynamics of CO2 from crystallizing magmatic underplate, to shed light on a possible connection between CO2 emanations and underplating in the area. We show that CO2 flow rates estimated in the western Ohře Rift (order of 100 t/day) may be related to the underplate body, providing it is being actively filled with a new magma (ca. 0.001 km3/year), or the underplate is relatively recently emplaced (ca. <1 My). Long-term activity of CO2 degassing, as evidenced by local travertine occurrences, may thus be of magmatic origin providing it is episodic, in response to fluctuating magma generation or emplacement rates.

papers.t: SCMLPick: A SeisComP Module Implementing Machine Learning Phase Picking for Real-Time Seismic Monitoring
in: Bureau of Economic Geology, The University of Texas at Austin, Austin, Texas, U.S.A.
tk: SCMLPick is a new SeisComP module that enables real-time, low-latency deployment of machine learning-based phase pickers within operational seismic networks.
SCMLPick是一个新型SeisComP模块，可在地震网络中实现低延迟的实时机器学习震相拾取。
papers.ab: Rapid and accurate detection of seismic phases is essential for effective seismic monitoring. Although various detection methods exist, recent advances in machine learning (ML) algorithms have demonstrated superior performance in automatically identifying seismic phases. However, the real-time deployment of such models remains challenging due to substantial computational demands and limited feasibility of integration with operational workflows. Since 2023, the Texas Seismological Network (TexNet) has utilized an ML-based picker, increasing the detection rate of low-magnitude earthquakes (primarily M < 1.0) by a factor of 50 compared to the conventional short-term average to long-term average method. Nevertheless, the existing implementation operates in postprocessing mode, introducing latencies exceeding 10 min relative to phase onset. To overcome this limitation, we developed SCMLPick, a novel SeisComP module that enables the real-time application of ML-based phase pickers within operational seismic networks. SCMLPick bridges the gap between state-of-the-art ML algorithms and the stringent demands of real-time seismic processing. Its development focused on integrating ML-based pickers into the SeisComP framework, optimizing runtime performance, and tuning region-specific parameters. SCMLPick continuously processes real-time waveform data, achieving average phase-picking latencies of less than 60 s, a significant reduction from the 600–3000 s observed in the previous postprocessing implementation. A comparative evaluation against TexNet’s existing postprocessing implementation demonstrated strong agreement in pick and event detections, with over 98% matching of events for M ≥ 1.0 and high consistency in arrival time estimation. Region-specific tuning further enhanced the detection accuracy and operational reliability of SCMLPick.

papers.t: A probabilistic long-term health risk assessment framework for wildfires: the case of California
in: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
ETH Zurich
Institute of Energy and Process Engineering
tk: A probabilistic risk assessment framework evaluates long-term mortality from wildfire-induced PM2.5 exposure in California, finding it comparable to earthquake risks.
该研究构建了概率风险评估框架，评估加州野火PM2.5暴露的长期死亡率风险。
papers.ab: The increased wildfire activity across the Western United States in recent decades has amplified the health risk from wildfire smoke. Existing risk assessment frameworks, however, remain at the conceptual level or target immediate and direct economic and health consequences. Here, we develop a probabilistic risk assessment (PRA) framework to estimate the health impacts of wildfires in California, integrating (1) wildfire probability, (2) fire spread, (3) emissions, (4) PM 2.5 transport, and (5) long-term mortality from degraded air quality. The findings reveal that the frequency-mortality curve due to PM 2.5 exposure from wildfires follows a power law distribution with exponent \(\beta =1.44\) , emphasizing the dominant influence of extreme wildfire events. Wildfires originating in the northwestern parts of California are found to be the most significant contributor to mortality from PM 2.5 exposure, due to the high vegetation density as well as the dominant winds directing the emissions towards densely populated regions. Additionally, our results show that wildfire fatality risk is comparable to that of California earthquakes and significantly higher than the risk associated with nuclear energy generation in the state.

papers.t: Quantifying the effects of nickel on Earth's inner-core nucleation
tk: Atomistic simulations show that nickel enrichment, bcc phase nucleation, and chemical heterogeneity lower the nucleation barrier, helping resolve the Earth's inner-core nucleation paradox.
原子模拟表明，镍富集、bcc相成核和化学不均匀性降低了成核势垒，缓解了地核成核悖论。
papers.ab: The formation of Earth's solid inner core marks a major transition in the thermal and chemical evolution of the deep Earth, yet its origin remains paradoxical, as initial nucleation appears to require unrealistically large undercooling in the outer core. Here, we use atomistic simulations to quantify how Ni affects this process under inner-core conditions. While Fe-Ni alloys preserve strong thermodynamic competition between the hcp and bcc phases, the bcc phase consistently forms smaller critical nuclei and has lower nucleation barriers than hcp. Increasing Ni content in the melts further lowers the nucleation barrier and shortens the nucleation waiting time. Local chemical fluctuations also strongly affect the macroscopic nucleation rate. Combining these effects, bcc nucleation in Fe80Ni20 reaches about 250 K of undercooling, approaching geophysical constraints. We demonstrate that Ni enrichment, bcc nucleation, and chemical heterogeneity substantially narrow the inner-core nucleation paradox.

papers.t: Tidal tomography reveals a thermal anomaly beneath Mars’s crustal dichotomy
tk: Tidal tomography using spacecraft tracking data reveals a 200–400 °C thermal anomaly in Mars's mantle beneath the southern highlands, aligning with the crustal dichotomy.
潮汐断层成像揭示火星南部高地下方存在地幔热异常。
papers.ab: Mars undergoes seasonal tidal forcing as a result of its eccentric orbit and the tilt of its rotation axis relative to the Sun 1 . Response to this forcing produces temporal variations in the Martian gravity field and is sensitive to the internal structure of the planet 2–4 . Using tracking data from the Mars Global Surveyor (MGS), Mars Odyssey (ODY) and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) spacecraft 5–7 , we demonstrate that degree-3 components of the time-variable gravity field of Mars differ by up to 300% from predictions for a spherically symmetric planet 8–10 . These deviations can be explained if the effective shear modulus of the mantle varies by >20% over a roughly north–south pattern that closely aligns with the surface expression of the Martian crustal dichotomy 11 . On the basis of this correlation, we infer preservation of a 200–400 °C thermal anomaly in the present-day mantle below the southern highlands of Mars. This temperature variation could reflect regional mantle convection 12,13 or insulation by the thick southern highlands crust of Mars that has persisted over several billion years 14,15 .

papers.t: Gradient-Based Efficient Optimization Method for Surface Sensor Arrays in Microseismic Source Mechanism Inversion
in: School of Naval Architecture & Ocean Engineering, Jiangsu University of Science and Technology, Zhenjiang 212100, China
tk: Derives the analytical gradient of the response matrix condition number to efficiently optimize surface sensor arrays for microseismic moment tensor inversion.
首次推导了响应矩阵条件数的解析梯度，实现了微震台网的高效优化。
papers.ab: The accuracy of microseismic moment tensor inversion critically depends on the spatial configuration of surface sensor arrays, quantified by the condition number κ(G) of the dynamic response matrix. Existing optimization methods suffer from slow convergence and unreliability due to the fundamental lack of gradient information. In this specific context, the analytical gradient of κ(G) with respect to sensor positions via singular value perturbation theory and the chain rule of direction cosines are derived for the first time in this paper. Based on the analytical gradient, three optimization strategies are established: a BFGS quasi-Newton method with quadratic penalty (BP) for smoothly constrained regions; a sequential quadratic programming method (FMC/SQP) achieving the lowest condition numbers across all shapes with approximately 5000 evaluations; and a center-boundary parameterization method (CB) that exploits the structural regularity of optimal configurations to reduce variables from 2N to N−1, requiring only approximately 300 evaluations (1/16 of FMC). Systematic experiments on five region shapes and two complex constraint scenarios demonstrate that gradient methods achieve a 15–30% reduction in κ across 4 of 5 shapes and a 5–31-fold improvement in robustness, with FMC reducing the average condition number by 25% at 15.4-fold better robustness than the baseline. Synthetic inversion experiments confirm that reducing κ from approximately 1.5×104 to approximately 50 reduces moment tensor inversion error by approximately 50-fold. The analytical gradient framework is transferable to sensor placement problems across multiple disciplines, and the three-method toolchain offers a graduated accuracy–efficiency trade-off for practical deployment optimization.

papers.t: LitCurate: A Configuration-Driven AI-Assisted Framework for Scientific Database Construction with an Application to Lower-Mantle Equation-of-State Data
tk: LitCurate is an open-source, LLM-powered framework for building auditable scientific databases, demonstrated by constructing a lower-mantle mineral equation-of-state database.
LitCurate是一个开源且基于大语言模型的科学数据库构建框架，通过构建下地幔矿物状态方程数据库展示了其应用。
papers.ab: The growing scientific literature contains decades of experimental and computational results that could support data-driven and physics-based modeling, yet much of this infor- mation remains locked in publications and is not readily usable for large-scale analysis or sci- entific software. Building structured databases from the literature is particularly challenging whenrelevantstudiesmustfirstbediscoveredamonglargecollectionsofpapersandreported quantities must be extracted with enough scientific context to remain usable. We present LitCurate, an open-source framework for building scientific databases from the literature using large language models within an auditable, stage-wise curation workflow. LitCurate integratesliteraturediscovery, relevancescreening, full-textprocessing, andstructuredinfor- mation extraction while retaining intermediate results and provenance, allowing researchers to inspect and revise individual stages rather than treating automated curation as a black- box process. We apply LitCurate to construct an equation-of-state database of lower-mantle and lower-mantle-relevant high-pressure mineral phases from experimental and theoretical studies, comprising 1,334 entries from 205 papers. The resulting dataset links reported equation-of-state parameters to mineral phases, compositions, equation formulations, meth- ods, and parameter constraints, and labels values as source-reported or citation-reported when provenance can be determined. The records are available through a searchable web application. By connecting scientific literature to traceable, machine-readable data, LitCu- rate provides a reusable approach for transforming accumulated literature into resources for scientific analysis and computational modeling.

papers.t: Global Prevalence of Anti-similar Earthquakes at Intermediate Depth
tk: Anti-similar earthquakes with flipped waveforms are globally prevalent at intermediate depths, likely driven by conjugate or sub-parallel faulting.
反相似地震（波形相反）在深部中源地震中具有全球普适性，可能由共轭或次平行断层作用引起。
papers.ab: Anti-similar earthquakes, those with nearly identical but flipped waveforms, remain an uncommon observation. We document three locations where these events occur at intermediate depth. The first of these is Colombia, including the well-established source of anti-similar events in the Bucaramanga Nest, and new reports in other intermediate depth seismicity clusters in the Wadati-Benioff zones of Colombia. The second is the Alaska subduction zone, and the third is the Vrancea seismic nest in Romania. These new observations, combined with reports from Japan and Chile, provide mounting evidence that anti-similar earthquake sequences might be a common or characteristic process of intermediate-depth seismicity. Either conjugate faulting promoted by eclogitization induced stresses or sub-parallel faulting can explain their occurrence at these depths. Careful examination of seismicity in other productive intermediate depth seismicity zones might reveal an even more widespread geography for anti-similar earthquakes and place tighter constraints on their underlying mechanism.

papers.t: Permeability evolution during a viscous–brittle transition in crystal- and bubble-bearing magma
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Tohoku University
Tohoku History Museum
tk: Uniaxial compression experiments on rhyolite magma show that brittle failure increases permeability by two orders of magnitude, whereas viscous deformation slightly decreases it.
流纹岩岩浆的单轴压缩实验表明，脆性破裂使渗透率提高两个数量级，而粘性变形则使其略有降低。
papers.ab: The evolution of magma rheological behavior and permeability during the ascent determines the explosivity of volcanic eruptions. In this study, we investigated the evolution of magma permeability under viscous and brittle deformation. We performed uniaxial compression experiments for rhyolite magma at temperatures of 806–955 °C and strain rates of 10 –6.5 –10 –1.3 s −1 . We used rhyolite lava collected from Niijima Island (Japan) as the starting material, with 15–25 vol% phenocrysts and 20–35 vol% porosity. The gas permeabilities of samples were measured before and after deformation. Our experiments showed viscous deformation of rhyolite magma at Weissenberg number ( Wi ) of less than 10 –3.4 and brittle deformation at Wi greater than 10 –2.5 . During viscous deformation, the permeability did not change significantly at low strain, while it decreased slightly at large strain. On the other hand, the permeability increased strongly when the magma failed in the brittle regime, with larger strain (>0.08), originating from the formation of large cracks and their widening. These results imply that efficient outgassing occurred in the conduit with high Wi regions, corresponding to the shallow and outer parts of the conduit. Once wide fractures are formed, the permeability and outgassing rate increase by two orders of magnitude, which is significantly higher than that of the viscous magma beneath the fractured magma in the conduit. We propose that a zoned structure, consisting of a brittle plug with high permeability and porosity, and viscous vesicular magma, may have formed at the top of the volcanic conduit.

tk: Multi-temporal InSAR and differential deformation metrics are used to assess reservoir-induced fault reactivation at the Qarn Alam Field.

papers.t: Graphite lubricates Mercury’s global contraction
tk: Friction experiments and critical taper analysis show that graphite-rich crustal layers lubricated low-angle thrust faults during Mercury's global contraction, suggesting greater planetary shortening.
摩擦实验与临界楔分析表明，富石墨地壳层在水星收缩过程中起到了润滑低角度逆冲断层的作用。
papers.ab: Secular cooling of Mercury’s interior drove planetary contraction, forming widespread lobate scarps that are the surface expressions of thrust faults and fold-and-thrust belts. Despite their importance to Mercury’s global tectonics, the mechanics and rheology of these features remain poorly understood. Using Critical Taper analysis calibrated by friction experiments, we estimate the maximum basal friction (µ b ) from observed wedge geometry and show that the topography of large fold-and-thrust belts is consistent with weak graphite-bearing, low-angle fault zones. This finding indirectly supports models proposing a graphite flotation crust during Mercury’s early differentiation. We infer that remnants of this carbon-rich layer, heterogeneously distributed within Mercury’s crust because of early impacts, caused the weakening of large portions of the crust during later contraction, allowing the nucleation of weak, low-angle thrust faults. Since the gently dipping, frictionally weak thrusts require greater horizontal shortening to build the observed relief than steeper, stronger faults, Mercury’s cumulative radial contraction may exceed previous, more conservative estimates.

papers.t: Lab earthquakes confirm the theory of frictional slip pulses
tk: Laboratory earthquake experiments confirm the theoretical predictions of frictional slip pulses, demonstrating their unstable, slowly growing or decaying nature across various fault conditions.
实验室地震实验证实了摩擦滑动脉冲理论，展示了其不稳定的演化特征。
papers.ab: Large natural earthquakes are typically mediated by frictional pulse-like rupture, which features a finite slipping zone. Recently, a comprehensive two-dimensional theory of frictional slip pulses has been developed. It predicts that pulses are categorically unstable rupture modes, whose evolution is intrinsically slow. Unsteady pulses satisfy an equation of motion expressed in terms of discrete observables, which is inherently related to their steady-state counterparts. The theory also predicts a transition from decaying to slowly growing pulses. Here, we perform extensive lab earthquake experiments to test the theory. The experiments confirm the theoretical predictions for pulse-like lab earthquakes over a range of prestress levels, rupture nucleation conditions and small-scale fault roughness amplitudes. Specifically, the predicted time-dependent dynamics are tested in a plane defined by the evolving pulse size and peak slip rate, along with measurements of the dimensionless growth rate of pulses, demonstrating their intrinsically slow unsteady nature. The predicted transition between decaying and growing pulses is also experimentally demonstrated. These results constitute major progress in understanding a dominant earthquake rupture mode.

papers.t: A machine vision-based method for displacement monitoring under fog interference
in: Dalian Maritime University
Changsha University of Science and Technology
tk: A machine vision method using red-light active illumination and sub-pixel algorithms achieves high-accuracy bridge displacement monitoring under foggy conditions.
基于红光照明与亚像素算法的雾天桥梁位移高精度监测方法。
papers.ab: Accurate displacement monitoring of bridges in foggy environments remains a critical challenge for structural health monitoring. This study proposes a machine vision-based technique that integrates red-light active illumination with sub-pixel algorithms to address this issue. To mitigate the low signal-to-noise ratio caused by fog scattering, the core of our approach employs a high-brightness monochromatic red LED as an active source to provide a high-contrast target against scattered ambient noise. A sophisticated sub-pixel localization pipeline incorporating dynamic threshold searching, morphological denoising, and multi-algorithm fusion achieves a remarkable displacement resolution of 0.1 mm. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness of method across various fog conditions (light, moderate, and thick fog) with maximum RMSE below 0.0262 mm. Validation on a scaled cable-stayed bridge model shows strong agreement with laser displacement sensor measurements under dynamic loading. This research provides a cost-effective, reliable solution for bridge displacement monitoring in adverse weather conditions, advancing machine vision applications in infrastructure monitoring.

papers.t: Modeling Nonergodic Ground Motions Using Graph Neural Networks
in: Department of Earth and Environmental Science, Tulane University, New Orleans, Louisiana, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Geologic Hazards Science Center, Golden, Colorado, U.S.A.
U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Science Center, Moffett Field, California, U.S.A.
Department of Geophysics, Stanford University, Stanford, California, U.S.A.
tk: A graph neural network trained on CyberShake simulations successfully models nonergodic ground motions in southern California, capturing basin amplification and azimuthal variations.
利用图神经网络在CyberShake模拟数据上训练，成功构建了南加州非遍历地震动模型。
papers.ab: We develop a nonergodic ground-motion model (GMM) for southern California by training a graph neural network (GNN) on approximately 400,000 simulated earthquakes from CyberShake. Our analysis focuses on long-period responses at rupture distances of 200 km or less. Each rupture is modeled as a graph, with nodes representing CyberShake sites connected to their closest neighbors. The resulting nonergodic, or region-specific, GMM includes site conditions, source properties, and path properties, as well as absolute source and site locations (via latitude and longitude), relative source-to-site distances, and intersite distances. The GNN model predictions are residuals relative to an ergodic GMM. Using the graph structure, the GNN learns spatially correlated residual patterns, such as source-to-site and local site interactions. Consequently, the GNN captures site-specific and spatially varying features, such as basin amplification and azimuthal variations of ground motion with respect to the fault, features that are often missed by traditional ergodic GMMs. In addition, the GNN model maintains magnitude scaling and period-dependent trends that are consistent with empirical relations across sources in southern California. We select the 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake as a case study to evaluate the performance of the GNN. By leveraging the spatial and physical characteristics of CyberShake simulations, the GNN achieves lower mean residuals than ergodic GMMs at T = 5.0 s and shows comparable performance at other periods. GNN-based nonergodic GMMs offer a promising framework for ground-motion modeling and hazard analysis.

papers.t: Waned mantle upwelling contributes to a heavily deformed northern smooth plains on Mercury
tk: Waned mantle upwelling and dynamic topography variations beneath the Northern Rise drove elevated contractional deformation and long-standing tectonism in Mercury's northern smooth plains.
水星北部的地幔上涌减弱与动态地形变化导致了其北部平原强烈的收缩形变。
papers.ab: Recent advancements in mapping and interpretation have revealed both numerous contractional landforms and evidence that tectonic activity has persisted into geologically recent times in Mercury’s northern smooth plains (NSP). To investigate the mechanisms behind these observations, we conduct a comprehensive assessment of contractional strain across the NSP. Our analysis reveals that (1) the NSP exhibits higher strain than other terranes on Mercury, and (2) the surface deformation pattern is spatially correlated with the Northern Rise (NR) at the center of the NSP, suggesting an additional driving force. We propose that this elevated strain and its distribution result from waned mantle upwelling induced by deep mantle flow beneath the NR. Sustained variations in dynamic topography likely fueled the long-standing tectonism in the NSP. These findings provide a complementary perspective on Mercury’s evolutionary history and may help illuminate similar processes on other terrestrial planets.

papers.t: Analysis of legacy geophysical data to delineate geologic hydrogen occurrences in the Midcontinent Rift System, Iowa, USA
in: University of Iowa
Iowa Department of Natural Resources
Battelle
Colorado School of Mines
tk: Legacy seismic and petrophysical data from Iowa's Midcontinent Rift System are analyzed to delineate geologic hydrogen occurrences and migration pathways.
利用历史地震与测井数据圈定爱荷华州地质氢气赋存与通道。
papers.ab: Geologic hydrogen is among contemporary global interests to minimize carbon dioxide emissions. It is mainly produced by serpentinization of olivine within mafic rocks, which comprise the Midcontinent Rift System (MRS) of the midwestern United States. Exploration is active along the MRS in Iowa, where in 1969, a 96.3% hydrogen gas measurement was reported from a natural gas storage field near Vincent. Data useful to geologic hydrogen exploration in Iowa are limited to legacy petrophysical logs and seismic lines from early fossil energy exploration. Legacy data from the Vincent area were evaluated for evidence of subsurface hydrogen and system components. Hydrogen shows are indicated in multiple wells within the upper Eau Claire carbonate. Faults that would serve as migration pathways are evident in the MRS basalts and overlying sedimentary strata. The response of petrophysical logs in interpreted zones of hydrogen accumulation suggest the obsolete neutron-gamma logging tool is sensitive to the presence of geologic hydrogen, but ancillary resistivity, acoustic, and density logs are necessary for further interpretation. Pilot study natural gas injections may have displaced accumulated hydrogen to wells at the structure’s flanks, and some samples were likely from intervals outside the accumulation, which could be tested by reservoir modeling studies.

papers.t: Continually learning neural-operator surrogate for three-dimensional airborne electromagnetic Bayesian inversion
tk: A continually learning neural-operator surrogate accelerates 3D airborne electromagnetic Bayesian inversion, enabling survey-scale uncertainty quantification in seconds.
一种持续学习的神经算子代理模型加速了三维航空电磁贝叶斯反演。
papers.ab: Three-dimensional probabilistic inversion of time-domain airborne electromagnetic (AEM) data is limited by the cost of the forward solve. Even though one simulation takes only tens of seconds, a Bayesian inversion of a survey of millions of soundings requires of order $10^{10}$ forward evaluations. To address this, we develop a continually learning neural-operator surrogate of the three-dimensional AEM forward operator that replaces the solver inside the Bayesian inversion. We start from the point of view that regardless of what geological prior is specified, Maxwell's laws remain invariant. Secondly, we avoid the limitation of learning on a single prior by continual learning on consecutive priors, which means our surrogate becomes richer as it is applied in future case studies, either by the authors, or by the scientific community. We use a validity check built on ensemble disagreement to divert cases with measurements outside the training range to the solver. Driven by the surrogate, the identical Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler reproduces the full-solver posterior, and its credible intervals cover the truth within 2.6 percentage points. Applied to the 2013 Capricorn TEMPEST survey in Western Australia, the surrogate inverts over two million soundings in seconds, a computation infeasible for the solver. Testing the geological prior against the entire survey costs minutes. The framework delivers uncertainty-quantified conductivity imaging at survey scale, which we believe is essential to perform near real-time mineral-systems targeting with geophysics.

papers.t: Socio-economic value of data-driven eruption forecasts to balance false alarms against catastrophic loss
tk: A new Potential Economic Value framework shows that machine-learning volcano forecasts can reduce eruption losses by 30–90% by prioritizing precautionary warnings over false-alarm avoidance.
潜在经济价值框架表明，通过优先减少漏报，机器学习火山预测可减少30-90%的损失。
papers.ab: The adoption of new forecasting methods for volcanic eruptions typically emphasizes predictive accuracy, often overlooking their potential to reduce overall life and economic losses. We introduce a Potential Economic Value (PEV) framework that evaluates forecast utility by balancing precautionary actions against avoidable catastrophic losses (such as mass casualties). Using machine-learning forecasts from continuous seismic data at five volcanoes, we show that non-forecasted eruptions (missed) have disproportionate consequences, compared to false alarms, which generate recurring and manageable disruption. Retrospective analyses of the 2019 Whakaari (New Zealand) and 2014 Ontake (Japan) eruptions, along with three additional volcanoes, indicate that losses could have been reduced by 30–90%, despite generating numerous false alarms. Across all case studies, effective forecasting prioritizes reducing missed eruptions over maximizing accuracy. This supports the use of more precautionary warning thresholds, provided that the resulting increase in alert frequency is managed in ways that maintain public compliance and trust.

papers.t: Fluidized Gouge Injections Record Fluid Overpressure Transients and Seismic Slip in Clay-Rich Fault Zones
in: Dipartimento di Scienze Biologiche, Geologiche e Ambientali, Università di Bologna, Bologna, Italy
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia (INGV), Rome, Italy
Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra, Sapienza Università di Roma, Rome, Italy
School of Earth System Science, Institute of Surface-Earth System Science, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China
Dipartimento di Scienze Chimiche, della Vita e della Sostenibilità Ambientale, Università di Parma, Parma, Italy
tk: Fluidized gouge injections in clay-rich fault zones record transient fluid overpressure and extreme comminution, serving as geological markers of past seismic slip.
富黏土断裂带中的流体化断层泥侵入体记录了瞬态流体超压，可作为过去地震滑动的地质标志。
papers.ab: Identifying diagnostic signatures of coseismic slip in the geological record is essential for constraining fault rheology and earthquake dynamics, yet unambiguous geological markers of past seismic ruptures are still scarce. Among seismic slip indicators, solidified frictional melt is widely regarded as the most reliable; however, its restrictive formation conditions and poor preservation limit the geological record of seismic rupture. Here, we investigated fluidized fault gouge injections into host cataclasites preserved in the clay-rich fault zones of the Altyn Tagh fault (northern Tibetan Plateau) and Carboneras fault (southeast Spain), two structurally distinct strike-slip systems showing similar injection geometries and microstructures. The injections display elongate tips with pinch-out terminations and internal undulated foliation surfaces with irregular, lobate geometries, indicating flow within relatively more viscous, quartz-rich host cataclasites. The injected material embeds clasts derived from the host rock, and fractal dimensions of the clast size distribution exceeding 3 are consistent with extreme comminution comparable to that documented in faults accommodating coseismic slip. We interpret gouge fluidization and injection as resulting from transient fluid overpressure, a process that may play a key role in dynamic fault weakening. Therefore, such injections may represent reliable geological indicators of past earthquakes and provide constraints on rupture dynamics in structurally and rheologically complex fault zones.

papers.t: Global Prevalence of Anti-similar Earthquakes at Intermediate Depth
tk: Anti-similar earthquakes are widely prevalent at intermediate depths globally, suggesting conjugate or sub-parallel faulting mechanisms driven by eclogitization stresses.

The first of these is Colombia, including the well-established source of anti-similar events in the Bucaramanga Nest, and new reports in other intermediate depth seismicity clusters in the Wadati-Benioff zones of Colombia. The second is the Alaska subduction zone, and the third is the Vrancea seismic nest in Romania. These new observations, combined with reports from Japan and Chile, provide mounting evidence that anti-similar earthquake sequences might be a common or characteristic process of intermediate-depth seismicity. Either conjugate faulting promoted by eclogitization induced stresses or sub-parallel faulting can explain their occurrence at these depths. Careful examination of seismicity in other productive intermediate depth seismicity zones might reveal an even more widespread geography for anti-similar earthquakes and place tighter constraints on their underlying mechanism.
