papers.t: Comment on egusphere-2026-3474
in: RWTH Aachen University
ETH Zurich
Swiss Seismological Service
Trent University
Dalhousie University
Fraunhofer Research Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies IEG
Natural Resources Canada
University of Neuchâtel
University of Science and Technology of China
Géoazur
York University
tk: This paper presents the PRECODE mine-by experiment at BedrettoLab, investigating excavation damage zone evolution in crystalline rocks using multidisciplinary monitoring.
本文介绍了Bedretto实验室的PRECODE开挖实验及多学科监测成果。
papers.ab: The brittle damage around tunnels in the form of spalling is common in massive crystalline rocks subjected to high in-situ stresses. Understanding the short-term development and long-term evolution of the Excavation Damage Zone (EDZ) is particularly important for deep geological repositories (DGRs) for heat-generating nuclear waste, as the EDZ may provide preferential pathways for radionuclide migration. This paper presents an overview of the PRECODE mine-by experiment at BedrettoLab, a newly developed underground research laboratory (URL) in southern Switzerland designed to investigate brittle fracturing and EDZ evolution in crystalline rocks under repository-relevant conditions. The PRECODE tunnel was excavated in Rotondo Granite using both controlled drill-and-blast (D&B) and line-drilling and rock-breaking (LDRB) methods to evaluate the influence of excavation technique on EDZ characteristics. The experiment combines multidisciplinary in-situ monitoring including acoustic emission, distributed acoustic and strain sensing, hydraulic monitoring, electrical resistivity tomography, and terrestrial laser scanning with laboratory-based fracture mechanics and time-dependent testing under varying environmental conditions. The main objectives are to characterize short-term EDZ formation, investigate long-term crack growth and stress corrosion processes, quantify permeability evolution, and assess the interaction between excavation-induced damage and nearby fault zones. Preliminary results indicate clear differences in AE activity and EDZ development between excavation methods, while observations from the mature EDZ of the more than 40-year-old Bedretto Tunnel suggest ongoing time-dependent brittle fracturing. The coupled in-situ and laboratory datasets provide a unique basis for improving predictive models and long-term safety assessments for nuclear waste repositories in crystalline rocks.

papers.t: Seasonality and Characteristics of Hydrological Deformation of Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna River Basin Using GPS and GRACE: Is Semi-Annual Cycle a Processing Artefact or Geophysical Signal?
in: CSIR National Institute of Data Science and AI (CSIR-NIDSA), Erstwhile CSIR-Fourth Paradigm Institute (CSIR-4PI), Wind Tunnel Road, Bangalore, Karnataka, India, 560037
Department of Physics
B.N. College (Autonomous)
Divisional Support Branch, Regional Operations Division,
Office of the Surveyor General,Ministry of Natural Resources
Meteorological Research Institute
tk: GPS and GRACE observations reveal that the semi-annual cycle of vertical crustal deformation in the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin is a real geophysical signal driven by snow loading.
GPS和GRACE观测表明，恒河-布拉马普特拉-梅格纳流域垂直地壳形变的半载周期是由积雪载荷引起的真实地球物理信号。
papers.ab: Response of the crust to the prevailing complex hydrological regime of Ganges-Brahmaputra- Meghna river basin complicates the geodetic estimates of secular and transient vertical deformation associated with ongoing active tectonics. Estimates of the seasonal deformation using ~12 years of daily Global Positioning System (GPS) observations reveal hydrologically induced vertical deformation of 3.50 to 6.65 cm peak-to-peak across the geographical regions considered in this study. Weighted root mean square reduction by reducing Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) derived vertical seasonal deformation from the corresponding ones observed by Global Positioning System (GPS) is 41% in Brahmaputra-Meghna (BM) river basin and 47% in Nepal Himalayan region of the Ganges basin. Median Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency value of 0.68 has been obtained between GPS and GRACE seasonal deformation with 91% of the stations above the value of 0.50. Spectral analysis shows predominant annual cycles in both GPS and GRACE in addition to significant Semi-Annual Cycle (SAC) over Nepal Himalayan region of the Ganges basin. Comparison between spatial variability in the power of SAC and total precipitation simulated by a high resolution Japan Meteorological Research Institute’s atmospheric general circulation model reveals that the presence of SAC in GPS and GRACE observations is a robust geophysical signal associated with snow loading and cannot be attributed solely as processing artefact. Further, the comparison reveals that the spatial variations of vertical hydrological deformation correlates well with the East-West contrast in total precipitation.

papers.t: GeoFormer: Geometry-Aware Transformer and its application to 5D First-Arrival Picking
tk: GeoFormer integrates acquisition geometry into a Transformer architecture to achieve robust 5D first-arrival picking on prestack seismic data.
GeoFormer将采集几何信息融入Transformer架构，实现了鲁棒的五维震相初至拾取。
papers.ab: We propose GeoFormer, a Geometry-Aware Transformer architecture specifically designed for prestack seismic data. Unlike Vision Transformer, whose tokens are extracted from 2D patches and primarily encode visual patterns, GeoFormer is designed for prestack seismic data by explicitly incorporating acquisition geometry. Each seismic trace is represented by a 5D unit consisting of the waveform and four source-receiver coordinates, from which two geometric attributes are derived: offset and relative elevation, where relative elevation is the receiver elevation minus the source elevation. GeoFormer therefore performs trace-level tokenization, where each token combines the waveform with these geometric attributes. To exploit these geometric attributes, GeoFormer introduces three geometry injection mechanisms operating at different levels of the Transformer pipeline. At the token level, GeomMLP replaces the classification token with a per-trace geometric representation derived from offset and elevation. At the normalization level, GeomAdaLN replaces uniform layer normalization with geometry-conditioned feature modulation. At the attention level, GeomAttnBias injects a parameter-free physical prior that geometrically proximate traces should attend more to each other. We validate GeoFormer on first-arrival picking, a representative seismic processing task that relies heavily on acquisition geometry. Experiments on four field datasets demonstrate that GeoFormer outperforms Vision Transformer and two task-specific baselines. Crucially, GeoFormer maintains robust picking accuracy under strong noise because its trace-level tokens encode geometric attributes that provide a physical prior independent of waveform quality. Ablation studies confirm that GeomMLP, GeomAdaLN, and GeomAttnBias each contribute to GeoFormer's picking accuracy.

papers.t: Spatially Variable Attenuation and a Localized Deep Stress-Drop Anomaly in the 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule Aftershock Sequence
in: Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris, Université Paris Cité, 1 rue Jussieu, Paris, France, 75005
Université Gustave Eiffel, 5 bd Descartes, Champs-sur-Marne, France, 77420
GFZ
Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University, 116th and Broadway, New York, USA, 10027
Institut des Sciences de la Terre, Université Grenoble Alpes, 1381 Rue de la Piscine, Gières, France, 38610
tk: Spectral inversion of 7,452 Maule aftershocks reveals highly variable attenuation and a localized deep band of high stress-drop earthquakes in the subducting slab.
对智利茂莱余震序列的谱反演揭示了空间可变的衰减以及俯冲板块深部的高应力降异常。
papers.ab: We invert horizontal 𝑺-wave Fourier acceleration spectra between 0.5 and 25 Hz from 7,452 earthquakes in the 2010 𝑴𝐰 8.8 Maule aftershock sequence to estimate source, path, and site terms in south-central Chile using a nonparametric generalized inversion technique. The dataset contains 101,566 event-station records from 2,257 crustal and 5,195 slab-related earthquakes recorded by 114 stations during the first 10 months after the mainshock. To account for propagation heterogeneity, we perform separate inversions for spatially coherent event clusters within both seismotectonic regimes, assign cluster-specific shear-wave velocity from a 3D velocity model, and use 100 randomized clustering iterations to evaluate the variance of the recovered terms. We find that relative site responses remain stable between inversion strategies. At some stations, relative amplification approaches a factor of 10 at 2–3 Hz. Effective attenuation varies markedly across the rupture area, with 𝑸𝟎 values of approximately 30–160 and frequency exponents of 0.4–1.5. Crustal clusters generally have lower 𝑸𝟎 and stronger frequency dependence than slab-related clusters. We fit the recovered source spectra with an 𝝎𝟐 model. Stress-drop distributions overlap between crustal and slab-related earthquakes, with median values of 0.95 and 0.78 MPa, respectively. Source scaling is close to self-similar above approximately 𝑴𝐰 3.5, where the weak dependence of stress drop on seismic moment becomes nearly flat. A slab-related seismicity band between 42.5 and 52.5 km depth contains systematically higher stress-drop values, with a median value of 1.75 MPa. These results show that resolving spatially variable propagation is necessary for interpreting source variability. The resulting empirical model provides a basis for regional ground-motion characterization and for tracking postseismic fault evolution across the Maule rupture zone.

papers.t: An Open-Source XML Database-Based Implementation of the FDSN Station Webservice: exist-fdsn-station
in: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Rome, Italy
Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, Milan, Italy
tk: Presents exist-fdsn-station, an open-source, containerized XML database-based implementation of the FDSN station web service that extends the standard API for metadata interaction.
介绍了 exist-fdsn-station，一个基于 XML 数据库的开源、容器化 FDSN 台站服务实现。
papers.ab: The International Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks has established the fdsnws-station application programming interface (API) standard for read-only access to seismic station metadata, provided primarily in an extensible markup language (XML) format called StationXML. Here, we present an extension of the standard API that introduces controlled operations for interacting with the underlying metadata repository. The proposed interface is designed to support direct handling of StationXML documents within distributed service-oriented infrastructures. We implemented the extended API using a framework that provides a native XML database management system and an embedded application platform. This approach offers a design advantage because the schema-less database allows ingestion of metadata from heterogeneous sources while preserving the XML structure. The software implementation, exist-fdsn-station, is containerized and can be integrated as a reusable component within larger infrastructures. Performance tests show that the system scales predictably with the size of the returned data and can support large aggregated metadata collections. The software is currently used in operational environments at the Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia (INGV) data center, including the public fdsnws-station endpoint.

papers.t: Multi-Geometry InSAR Observations of the 2026 Mw 7.4 Chocó, Colombia Earthquake: NISAR and Sentinel-1 Coseismic Deformation, Decomposition, and Data-Quality Lessons
in: Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Carrera 30 No. 45-03, Edificio 500, Bogota, BOGOTA D.C., BOGOTA, Colombia [CO], 111321
tk: This study analyzes coseismic deformation from the 2026 Mw 7.4 Chocó earthquake using NISAR and Sentinel-1 InSAR, highlighting critical data-quality and orbit-ephemeris lessons.
本文利用NISAR和Sentinel-1观测了2026年哥伦比亚地震的同震形变。
papers.ab: We present coseismic deformation observations of the 10 August 2026 Mw 7.4 Chocó, Colombia earthquake from two independent L-band and C-band SAR missions: NASA-ISRO's newly operational NISAR and ESA's Sentinel-1. A NISAR ascending interferogram (24-day baseline) was initially degraded by an orbit-ephemeris mismatch between a Forecast Orbit Ephemeris (FOE) Urgent-Response product and a Medium-precision Orbit Ephemeris (MOE) reference scene, reducing mean coherence to 0.060; reprocessing with a MOE-orbit product recovered a usable, though still spatially limited, coseismic signal (mean coherence 0.145, largest phase-connected component covering ~11% of the scene). Sentinel-1 ascending and descending interferograms, processed via ASF's HyP3 on-demand service with 6-day baselines, achieved substantially higher coherence (mean 0.36-0.37, ~50% coverage) and physically plausible line-of-sight displacements of several centimeters. Decomposing the ascending and descending measurements into east-west and vertical components reveals up to ~9 cm of eastward motion and ~11 cm of uplift concentrated on the eastern side of the Cauca-Romeral fault system, spatially consistent with USGS's oblique reverse-left-lateral focal mechanism. A separate attempt to extend NISAR coverage southward, toward a secondary displacement signal near Tuluá, failed an overlap-consistency check against the validated result (mean offset -33 cm, correlation -0.09 to -0.54 depending on correction) and is reported here as a negative result and methodological caution rather than a geophysical finding. We cross-reference our results against an independent Copernicus EMSR916 Pléiades-derived building-damage grading product for Pereira (182 graded buildings) and discuss implications for rapid multi-sensor InSAR response to future events.

papers.t: Characterizing differences in seismicity clustering and background rates between Hawaii and California
in: University of Memphis
tk: This study compares three declustering methods to reveal that Hawaii's volcanic seismicity exhibits highly localized, non-Poissonian clustering compared to Southern California's more Poissonian tectonic background rates.
本文对比了三种地震去群集方法，揭示了夏威夷火山地震活动具有高度局域且非泊松分布的群集特征。
papers.ab: Summary The statistics of earthquake populations are governed by stress changes and event interactions at various scales which promote non-linear event cascades and seismicity clustering. Earthquake clustering in space and time is observed in both tectonic and volcanically dominated regions; however, notable differences exist for instance during eruptive sequences. Here, we characterize seismicity statistics in California and Hawaii and quantify differences in background rates and clustering. We compare three statistical approaches, i.e, i) Reasenberg declustering, ii) Gamma distribution fit, and iii) Nearest Neighbor Clustering which are applied to seismicity in Hawaii, southern California, and ETAS catalogs with known clustering characteristics. Tests with ETAS-catalogs suggest that background rate variations are more consistently resolvable using the Nearest Neighbor and Gamma distribution algorithm without requiring parameter adjustments to the specific study area. The Nearest Neighbor method tends to overestimate background rates, whereas the Gamma distribution algorithm shows systematic underestimation, suggesting that an ensemble model can improve the performance over any single method. Uncertainties in background rate estimates based on small magnitude events (e.g., M≥2.5) are high, in particular for the Reasenberg method, which overpredicts true rates by up to a factor of 4, and extrapolations to larger magnitudes need to be treated cautiously. Our analysis shows that the combination of the three approaches generates new insights into the processes that govern seismicity clustering. The analysis of southern California seismicity produces consistent results between the different methods, and the distribution of background seismicity rates is indistinguishable from Poissonian rates at magnitudes above 3.5. Conversely, the seismicity in Hawaii exhibits notable non-Poissonian background rate changes. Results from the Nearest Neighbor clustering analysis suggest notable differences between tectonic and volcano seismicity, including background rate changes and more pronounced spatiotemporal clustering around active volcanoes. Hawaiian seismicity is characterized by more localized spatial-temporal clustering, in particular during the 2018 eruption. This difference may be a result of magmatic, hydrothermal and eruptive processes, which make volcanic areas susceptible to stress perturbations and earthquake triggering at small scales.

papers.t: Time-compressed composite-earthquake inversion for multi-event rupture representation and rupture-growth-tendency analysis in the 2023 Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye sequence
in: Linyi University
Heilongjiang Earthquake Agency
China Earthquake Administration
Hubei Urban Construction Vocational and Technological College
ENN (China)
tk: Proposes a time-compressed composite-earthquake inversion method to represent multiple distinct earthquakes as a single complex event, successfully modeling the 2023 Kahramanmaraş sequence.
提出时间压缩复合地震反演方法，将多个独立地震统一表示并反演。
papers.ab: Regional tectonic loading on a connected fault system can often be treated, to first order, as a slowly varying background process. Here we test the feasibility of representing several distinct earthquakes on the same fault system as ordered source units of one complex composite event. The method compresses inter-event origin-time separations but does not time-warp the waveform samples within each event. For the proportional mapping, C1, C2, C34 and C5 are placed at 0, 6.94, 355.7 and 419 s, superposed and inverted on a common 600 × 200 km plane discretised into 30 × 10 subfaults of 20 × 20 km. Under the proportional temporal mapping, the direct C12345 composite inversion is compared with the time-shifted sum of the separately inverted C1, C2, C34 and C5 source models, yielding a source-time-function correlation of 0.865. A 19-case sensitivity suite gives a median spatial correlation of 0.710, a median source-time-function correlation of 0.965 and a median centroid shift of 7.49 km, indicating that local patch geometry is less stable than the first-order spatial and temporal organisation. A constrained convolutional image model, trained on the 0–700 s slip-image sequence and combined with adjacent-front, depth and increment caps, is then used to examine slip-increase and rupture-growth tendency over 700–1000 s. The resulting zones show partial retrospective proximity to later M ≥ 5.0 earthquakes. The present results support the feasibility of a unified time-compressed multi-event representation.

papers.t: Improved Local Magnitude Estimation of Induced Earthquakes in the Kiskatinaw Seismic Monitoring and Mitigation Area, British Columbia, Canada
in: Institute of Sustainable Earth and Environmental Dynamics (SEED), Pukyong National University, Busan, Republic of Korea
Institute of Basic Science, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea
Division of Earth Environmental System Science, Pukyong National University, Busan, Republic of Korea
School of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea
Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea
Department of Earth Science Education, Korea National University of Education, Chungbuk, Republic of Korea
Department of Energy Mines and Resources, Yukon Geological Survey, Whitehorse, Canada
Department of Earth, Energy and Environment, University of Calgary, Calgary, Canada
tk: A newly calibrated local magnitude scale for the Kiskatinaw area reduces magnitude estimates by 0.3 units on average, improving induced seismicity monitoring.
新校准的KSMMA地方震级标度平均降低0.3，提高了监测精度。
papers.ab: The Kiskatinaw Seismic Monitoring and Mitigation Area (KSMMA) in northeastern British Columbia, Canada, has experienced increasing induced seismicity from hydraulic fracturing and fluid injection, prompting regulatory measures requiring the suspension of industrial operations for earthquakes of local magnitude (ML) 3.0 or greater. Accurate magnitude estimation is therefore critical, yet a widely used regional ML scale may misestimate shallow, near-source events typical of KSMMA. To address this limitation, we developed a KSMMA-calibrated ML scale using continuous seismic records during 2020 from 15 stations of the Earth-System Observing Network–Réseau d’Observation du Système terrestrE (EON-ROSE) dense array and eight stations of the Geological Survey of Canada (GSC)–British Columbia Oil and Gas Commission (BCOGC; now BC Energy Regulator, BCER) Induced Seismicity Study network. Event information from an existing catalog was used to supplement the dataset, but waveforms were reprocessed and Wood–Anderson amplitudes were remeasured uniformly. Earthquakes were detected using the phase-picking, association, location, and matched-filter (PALM) algorithm, which combines the ratio of short-term to long-term average, kurtosis, association, and matched-filter methods. Hypocenters were located with both absolute (HYPOINVERSE-2000) and relative (hypoDD) methods. The ML was developed following Richter’s definition, with distance corrections referenced to 17 km. Station corrections and attenuation coefficients were derived through generalized linear inversion. Amplitudes were measured on vertical-component Wood–Anderson simulated seismograms using a 1 Hz high-pass filter. The final dataset consisted of 4043 earthquakes, with ML values ranging from −0.53 to 3.04. Compared with previously used scales, the new calibration systematically yielded magnitudes approximately 0.3 units lower on average. Application of a KSMMA-specific ML scale, together with station corrections, yielded more consistent network-wide ML estimates and reduced scatter in event–station magnitude residuals. This regionally tailored ML scale improves characterization of induced seismicity in the KSMMA and supports more reliable seismic hazard assessment and risk management.

papers.t: The Seismogenic Structure of the Seismically Active Samakhiali Basin and Its Surrounding Region of Kachchh Rift Basin, Gujarat
in: Institute of Seismological Research, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India
Indian Institute of Technology-Roorkee, Roorkee, Uttarakhand, India
tk: Bayesian inversion of receiver functions reveals a 42–45 km thick crust, underplating, and an undulating intracrustal low-velocity zone beneath the seismically active Samakhiali Basin, India.
接收函数贝叶斯反演揭示了印度萨马希亚利盆地下方42-45公里的厚地壳、底侵作用及中地壳低速带。
papers.ab: Receiver function data from 50 closely spaced seismic stations of the Kachchh array network, along with data from 17 nearby permanent stations, were analyzed to determine the 3D crustal structure of the seismic source zone in the Kachchh rift basin, Gujarat. The stations were located within the seismically active source zone of the catastrophic Mw 7.7 Bhuj earthquake (2001) and its surrounding tectonic features, including the Wagad uplift (WU), Samakhiali basin (SB), and Kachchh mainland uplift (KMU). We performed velocity–depth inversions for all sites using a Bayesian inversion technique, which provides estimates of crustal thickness, individual crustal layer thicknesses, corresponding S-wave velocities, and VP/VS ratio. To image the seismogenic layer, we generated common conversion point stacked sections both along and across the study area. Our results reveal a relatively thick crust (∼42 to 45 km) beneath the highly active SB, which is uplifted by ∼5 km toward the north (WU) and south (KMU). We infer the process of underplating for the thick crust beneath this area. In and around the seismically active SB, we identified a sedimentary layer 1.5–2.5 km thick, consistent with previous results from gravity, resistivity, and seismic studies indicating 1–3 km sedimentary thickness. This sedimentary layer is overlying a prominent high-velocity zone around 4.0 km in thickness, which appears consistently throughout the study region and is interpreted as a gneiss–granitic basement. A notable feature of the crustal structure is the presence of an undulating intracrustal low-velocity zone (LVZ) with a thickness of 5–8 km, occurring at depths between ∼18 and 26 km. Despite the existence of this LVZ, seismicity is distributed from the mid-crust to the lower crust, suggesting complex seismotectonic interactions and possible fluid or compositional heterogeneities within the crust beneath the SB and its associated seismicity.

papers.t: A Dual-Criteria Model for Earthquake Early Warning Based on P-Wave and S-Wave Identification
in: 独立研究者, Unknown, 商洛, 陕西, China [CN]
tk: A dual-criteria model using P- and S-wave arrival times and energy-attenuation ratios is proposed to improve earthquake early warning and precursor detection.
基于P-S波到时差与能量衰减比的双准则地震预警与前兆检测模型。
papers.ab: The critical bottleneck in earthquake early warning is no longer the precision of data acquisition. Modern high-sensitivity seismic sensors can already detect ground displacements at the nanometer scale. The real challenge is to distinguish pre-seismic precursor signals from the massive background of ambient noise. This paper proposes a signal-identification model based on two independent criteria using P-waves and S-waves. The first criterion is the arrival-time difference between P- and S-waves. This determines the distance from the source to the receiver. The second criterion is the energy-attenuation ratio between P- and S-waves. Because P-waves and S-waves attenuate at different rates as they propagate through rock, this ratio provides a physical signature that distinguishes seismic waves from non-seismic sources such as explosions, heavy traffic, and industrial machinery. Only when both criteria are satisfied does the system confirm that the incoming signal originates from an earthquake precursor. This model directly addresses three persistent obstacles in earthquake early warning. First, it enables the extraction of micro-fracture signals from ambient noise, potentially extending the warning window from the conventional tens of seconds before the main shock to hours or even days in advance. Second, the dual-criteria verification substantially reduces the false-alarm rate. Third, the system shifts from a passive waiting mode—listening for the main shock P-wave—to an active monitoring mode that continuously searches for precursor patterns.

papers.t: Advancing the Use of Simulated Ground Motions in Physics-Based Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Analysis from Research to Practice
in: GFZ Helmholtz Center for Geosciences, Potsdam, Germany
University of Potsdam, Potsdam, Germany
Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of California, Berkeley, California, U.S.A.
tk: This paper highlights the missing 'method aleatory variability' in physics-based PSHA and provides recommendations to bridge the gap between research and practice.
本文指出物理强震动模拟在地震危险性分析中缺失“方法偶然不确定性”，并提出了推动其走向实用的建议。
papers.ab: Physics-based probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA), in which 3D numerical simulations replace traditional ground-motion models, has been under development for several decades. The development of high-performance computing capabilities and techniques has enabled significant advancements, such as the inclusion of complex near-fault source and path effects, which allow the extrapolation of ground motion to that of rare events at close distances; however, a gap remains between research and practice. This article compares and contrasts traditional PSHA with current physics-based PSHA and shows that method aleatory variability, which is apparent aleatory variability due to simplifications in the simulation method, is missing from current physics-based PSHA calculations. We highlight the need for proper separation and quantification of apparent aleatory variability and epistemic uncertainty, as well as validation of the distribution of the simulated ground motions for a given scenario. We discuss how the standard deviation of the misfits from simulation validations often includes both method aleatory variability and parametric epistemic uncertainty in the median, which is from scientific uncertainty in simulation inputs that are not part of the traditional hazard calculation as part of the source model. The limitations of the simulation method are often difficult to estimate directly from the validation because it is challenging to separate its effects from those of incorrect inputs. We provide an overview of simulation simplifications that lead to method aleatory variability, methods of incorporating method aleatory variability, and a list of recommendations for advancing physics-based PSHA from research to practice.

papers.t: Insights into the Inflation of Axial Seamount from Horizontal Seafloor Geodesy
in: University of Washington, 4229 7th Ave NE, Seattle, WA, United States [US]
University of Washington, Box 357940, Seattle, WA, United States [US]
University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory, Applied Physics Lab, Seattle, WA, United States [US]
The University of Texas at Austin Institute for Geophysics, 10100 Burnet Road,, Austin,, TX, United States [US]
tk: Three years of horizontal seafloor acoustic ranging at Axial Seamount reveal 30 cm of asymmetric caldera extension, indicating volumetric inflation over fault-accommodated uplift.
海底水平测距显示轴向海山存在30厘米非对称扩张，主因为体积膨胀。
papers.ab: Axial Seamount, a hotspot volcano on the Juan de Fuca Ridge, has been monitored through three eruptions with vertical geodesy documenting cycles of inflation and deflation. However, vertical motions alone cannot fully discriminate between distributed volumetric inflation and fault-accommodated uplift. We present three years of horizontal acoustic ranging observations (2022-2025) across Axial caldera from seafloor transponders defining 1.8-, 1.6-, and 3.3-km baselines spanning the western and eastern sides of the caldera and its full width. We observe 30 cm of extension across the caldera that is asymmetric with 24 cm of extension on the eastern baseline. Modeling of horizontal and vertical geodetic observation demonstrates that the observed deformation is primarily from volumetric inflation rather than fault motion. The data is consistent with a deeper pressure source coincident with a stacked sill complex under the southern caldera and a smaller shallow source under the northeastern caldera where eruptions originate.

papers.t: ROMNet: a hybrid reduced order modeling and machine learning approach to waveform inversion
tk: ROMNet combines reduced order modeling and neural networks to accelerate and simplify wave speed estimation in waveform inversion, mitigating cycle skipping.
ROMNet结合降阶模型与神经网络，加速并简化波形反演，有效缓解周期跳跃。
papers.ab: Waveform inversion seeks to estimate the wave speed of a heterogeneous, inaccessible medium, from time-resolved measurements of the waves at user controlled sensors. We consider this inverse problem for acoustic waves and an active array of source/receiver sensors that emit probing signals and measure the generated pressure waves. The forward map, from the wave speed to the measurements, is nonlinear and oscillatory. The oscillations cause cycle skipping, the main impediment to using the standard, nonlinear least-squares data fitting formulation, known as full waveform inversion (FWI). A recently introduced alternative waveform inversion approach computes from the measurements an algebraic surrogate of the wave operator, a reduced order model (ROM) matrix, which is then used to estimate the wave speed. The mapping from the measurements to the ROM is nonlinear, but well understood. It is computed efficiently, in a non-iterative manner. The nonlinear mapping from the ROM to the wave speed is less understood, and its approximation involves time-consuming optimization. Our goal in this paper is to use a neural network to map the ROM matrix to a nearby one, that has a simpler and explicit dependence on the wave speed. This simplifies and reduces the computational cost of the ROM-based waveform inversion. We introduce the methodology, called ROMNet, and test it with numerical simulations, using two training data sets: The first set consists of random media with variations of the wave speed modeled by a superposition of Gaussians with random amplitudes and standard deviations. The second is the publicly available GeoFWI dataset introduced for benchmarking FWI using deep learning. We compare the performance of ROMNet with the direct ROM-based inversion and with two representative deep learning approaches to FWI: ``Fourier-DeepONet" and ``InversionNet".

papers.t: Magma as a carrier of non-stoichiometric oxygen linking Earth’s interior and atmosphere
in: Center for High Pressure Science and Technology Advanced Research , Beijing 100193 ,
Lin Earth and Planetary Laboratory, Center for High Pressure Science and Technology Advanced Research , Beijing 100193 ,
State Key Laboratory of Solidification Processing, International Centre for Materials Discovery, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Northwestern Polytechnical University , Xi’an 710072 ,
Faculty of Science Department of Earth Sciences, , Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam 1081 HV ,
Shanghai Advanced Research in Physical Sciences , Shanghai 201203 ,
tk: High-pressure experiments and simulations show silicate magma can incorporate excess oxygen, acting as a volatile carrier that oxidizes Earth's shallow interior upon ascent.
高压实验与模拟表明硅酸盐岩浆可容纳超量氧，并在上升时释放以氧化地球浅部。
papers.ab: Magma generation and transport governs planetary evolution. Although oxygen is the most abundant anion in Earth’s silicate interior, its role in magma is conventionally ignored, with magma oxygen contents assumed to be simply fixed by cation stoichiometry. Here we show, using high-pressure and high-temperature experiments supported by molecular dynamics simulations, that silicate magma can incorporate substantially more oxygen than permitted by traditional valence-state constraints. Excess oxygen acts as a previously unrecognized volatile component, increasing in concentration from near zero at 1 atmosphere to >∼5 wt.% above 5 GPa, more than five times the maximum oxygen increase attainable in Earth’s solid mantle through iron redox changes. As oxygen-rich magmas ascend and decompress, their capacity to retain excess oxygen decreases, driving the release of O2. This behaviour provides a direct mechanism with the potential to link mantle melting to oxidation of Earth’s shallow interior and atmosphere, and identifies magma as a dynamic reservoir in planetary oxygen cycles.

papers.t: Quantum observables as Fréchet sensitivity kernels
tk: This paper presents a variational-adjoint framework for quantum mechanics, interpreting quantum observables and Born probability as Fréchet sensitivity kernels.
本文将量子观测物理量与波恩概率解释为Fréchet敏感核。
papers.ab: We present a variational--adjoint interpretation of quantum mechanics in which the interaction between forward and adjoint wavefunctions defines a general sensitivity kernel of the system. This Fréchet interaction density quantifies how perturbations in the wavefunction (or system parameters) influence a chosen observable. The familiar Born probability density appears as a special case when the adjoint wavefunction is chosen as the complex conjugate of the forward wavefunction, for which the interaction density becomes real and non-negative. Within this framework, probability is a particular positive-definite form of sensitivity described by the Fréchet interaction density. In general, the variational--adjoint interpretation also produces Fréchet sensitivity kernels associated with other quantum observables, including momentum, energy, and spin. This suggests that the Born probability density belongs to a broader class of Fréchet sensitivity kernels associated with quantum observables. The proposed interpretation also provides a connection with time-symmetric interpretations of quantum mechanics and possible future applications in quantum control and quantum metrology.

papers.t: Slab thermal transitions in the Aeolian arc driven by sub-slab mantle upwelling in the early Pleistocene
in: Institute of Oceanology
Ocean University of China
University of Naples Federico II
Nanjing University
tk: Geochemical evidence from Stromboli volcano reveals a rapid cold-to-hot slab thermal transition driven by early Pleistocene slab tearing and mantle upwelling.
地球化学证据揭示了板块撕裂驱动的快速冷热板块热转变。
papers.ab: Slab tearing and associated asthenospheric upwelling can profoundly affect arc magmatism by heating subducting slabs, yet continuous temporal magmatic records for such slab thermal perturbations remain elusive. Here, we document a magmatic shift in Stromboli volcano, eastern Aeolian arc, where potassium-rich rocks emerged since ~ 13,000 years ago and show isotopic and elemental evidence for high-temperature sediment melting. In contrast, rocks with ages > 13,000 years across the arc record incorporation of bulk sediment without experiencing obvious melting, consistent with a cold subduction setting. These results evidence a transition from cold-slab to hot-slab, linked to a mantle upwelling induced by slab tearing occurred in the early Pleistocene. This tectono-magmatic coupling accounts for the southeastward progression of potassium-rich volcanism across the Italian Peninsula, which coincides with tomographically and topographically inferred slab-tearing propagation. Our results demonstrate rapid (<1-2 million years) magmatic response to sub-slab mantle upwelling and offer critical insights into the drivers of recent volcanism in southeastern Italy, including Mount Vesuvius.

papers.t: Crustal weakening before rupture at volcanoes after long repose
tk: Presents an energy-balance method tracking stored elastic energy to identify the onset of crustal fracture growth and eruption potential at reawakening volcanoes.
提出一种通过能量平衡追踪地壳弹性储能变化以识别火山破裂前兆的方法。
papers.ab: At volcanoes reawakening after prolonged quiescence, local seismicity commonly increases before eruption. The earthquakes occur as crust extends over a zone of pressurising fluid several kilometres underground. The deformation causes existing faults to slip and new fractures to open. An eruption is most likely when the fractures grow large enough to rupture the crust. Fracture growth coincides with a net decrease in the elastic energy stored in the crust. Here we present a method for following changes in stored energy through a balance between the energy supplied by the pressure source and lost by seismicity. We test the method against unrest sequences at two large calderas, Sierra Negra and Campi Flegrei. The results provide a practical procedure for identifying the onset of fracture growth and, hence, for recognising an increased potential for crustal rupture.

papers.t: Frequency- and Component-Dependent Topographic Effects in Alpine Valleys Using 3D Physics-Based Simulations
in: Swiss Seismological Service, ETH Zürich, Zürich, Switzerland
Univ. Grenoble Alpes, Univ. Savoie Mont Blanc, CNRS, IRD, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ISTerre, Grenoble, France
tk: 3D spectral-element simulations in the Swiss Rhône Valley reveal that Alpine topography systematically amplifies vertical ground motion while weakly deamplifying horizontal motion.
瑞士罗讷河谷的3D谱元件模拟表明，阿尔卑斯地形系统性地放大垂直地面运动，同时微弱减弱水平运动。
papers.ab: We present three-dimensional (3D) spectral-element simulations of seismic wave propagation in the Swiss Rhône Valley to quantify how realistic Alpine topography affects ground motion across frequency bands. The simulations incorporate a digital elevation model–based free surface topography representation, a 3D crustal velocity model, and geotechnically constrained near-surface layers. The simulations are performed for three local earthquakes (Mw 3.2–4.5) recorded in two different configurations: topographic and flat-surface with basin geometry preserved. Topo/flat spectral ratios reveal a systematic component asymmetry in the topographic response. At mountain sites sampled by a spatially uniform synthetic grid, horizontal motion is deamplified across the dominant low-to-intermediate frequency bands (median 0.80–0.97× at 0.05–0.50 Hz), whereas vertical motion is consistently amplified (1.16–2.32×). The real seismic network with preferential sites confirms the strong vertical amplification, whereas the horizontal regime yields weak deamplification (0.65–1.00×). Basin sites exhibit mixed horizontal response and strong vertical amplification, consistent with coupled topographic scattering and basin-wave interactions as well as excitation of the Rhône basin’s fundamental frequencies. The observed asymmetry is consistent with topography-induced mode conversion and constructive interference associated with Alpine ridge geometry. These results demonstrate that realistic surface topography can fundamentally redistribute seismic energy between motion components and that sparse observational networks may incompletely capture this behavior. Physics-based simulations with realistic relief and spatially unbiased receiver sampling therefore provide a complementary framework for seismic hazard assessment in mountainous terrain.

papers.t: An Evolving Cosmic Shoreline and Sandbar Bounding the Rocky Airless Valley
tk: A coupled atmosphere-interior model explains exoplanet atmosphere retention via two boundaries: an outgassing-regulated sandbar and an escape-regulated shoreline.
耦合大气-内部模型通过排气和逃逸双重边界解释系外行星大气的保留。
papers.ab: Recent JWST observations challenge the traditional 'cosmic shoreline' from both sides, revealing thick volatile atmospheres on the hottest close-in 'lava worlds,' where irradiation should drive the most extreme escape, and bare rocky surfaces on cooler terrestrial planets around M dwarfs, where atmospheres would be expected to survive. Using a coupled atmosphere-interior evolution model, we show that atmosphere retention is governed not by a single escape boundary but by two: a hot, outgassing-regulated 'cosmic sandbar' and a cooler, escape-regulated 'cosmic shoreline,' separated by an 'airless valley' that may mark a graveyard of stripped sub-Neptune cores. The sandbar arises because long-lived magma oceans, sustained further by tidal heating from secular eccentricity excitation in multi-planet systems, keep most volatiles dissolved and expose only a small atmospheric reservoir to escape, whereas cooler planets solidify, sequestering volatiles in the deep solid mantle while overexposing the rest to loss. This two-regime structure recasts the single cosmic shoreline as two boundaries set by distinct physics: outgassing and escape. We provide time-evolving fits for both boundaries across G, K, and M stellar types as a function of volatile inventory, planetary mass, age, and tidal heating. Lava worlds with thick atmospheres are unlikely around stars cooler than K-type unless sustained by extreme tidal and/or other interior heating. This framework links atmosphere survival from USP lava worlds to habitable zone planets, informing target selection and interpretation for TRAPPIST-1 and JWST DDT characterization.

papers.t: Coastal Altimetry Improves the Estimates of Coastal Sea Level Rise and Vertical Land Motion in Southeast Asia
in: Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China
tk: The study utilizes X-TRACK/ALES v3.0 coastal altimetry to improve coastal sea-level rise and vertical land motion estimates in Southeast Asia.
该研究利用X-TRACK/ALES v3.0沿海测高数据提高了东南亚沿海海平面上升和垂直陆地运动的估算精度。
papers.ab: Accurate assessment of coastal sea-level rise (SLR) and vertical land motion (VLM) are vital for Southeast Asia, a region highly vulnerable to intensified coastal flooding. However, conventional satellite altimetry products often become unreliable nearshore due to land-contaminated radar waveforms and inadequate geophysical corrections. Here, we present a pioneering regional application of the latest X-TRACK/ALES v3.0 coastal altimetry product. Validation against tide gauges and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) records demonstrates that dedicated coastal altimetry captures coastal SLR with higher fidelity than conventional gridded and along-track products, which systematically overestimate coastal SLR trends. Our results reveal a mean absolute SLR of 2.36 mm/yr over 2002–2021 along the Southeast Asian coast and provide a high-resolution VLM dataset for this region identifying highly localized, nonlinear subsidence hotspots, largely complementing existing GNSS records. Our findings underscore the critical importance of dedicated coastal altimetry product for accurate coastal risk assessment.

papers.t: A Unified Physical Model for Global Plate Motion Velocities: Quantitative Relationships Among Thrust, Force Transmission Loss, Dip Angle, and Resistance
in: Independent Researcher, Unknown, Xuchang, Henan, China [CN]
tk: A unified physical model explains global plate velocities through force balance between LAB horizontal thrust and velocity-proportional resistance, suggesting slab pull is secondary.
该研究建立了基于板块边界力学平衡的统一物理模型，定量解释了全球板块运动速度。
papers.ab: Global plate motion velocities vary significantly—from ~8.5 cm/a for the Nazca Plate to ~2 cm/a for the Antarctic Plate—a disparity that traditional "slab pull" models have difficulty explaining quantitatively. This paper establishes a unified quantitative model for plate velocities based on the force balance between horizontal thrust—generated by the solid-fluid pressure contrast at the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB)—and basal/side frictional resistance, which is proportional to velocity. The model incorporates four core parameters: thrust magnitude (determined by arc magma source depth or maximum plate thickness), force transmission loss (related to plate length and dip angle), trench friction (related to dip angle), and plate-type resistance coefficients (oceanic, mixed, and continental). Systematic calculations for 11 major plates show that the model predicts velocities with an average deviation of <5% for oceanic plates, ~22% for mixed plates, and deviations for complex continental plates attributable to local thrust cancellation or remote force transmission. The central conclusion is that plate velocity is inversely proportional to total resistance, which itself is proportional to velocity—i.e., R ∝ *v*—constituting the physical basis for plate motion stability. The primary driver is the distributed horizontal thrust, with slab pull playing a secondary role (<3% contribution). The model predictions are consistent with the LAB structure-velocity positive correlation observed by Yang et al. (2026), indicating that LAB slope (the rate of lithospheric thickness change from mid-ocean ridge to trench) is an effective geometric indicator of thrust—steeper slopes correspond to greater thrust density per unit area.

papers.t: Leveraging the Physics of Jerk: An Automated Framework for Recovering Permanent Displacement from Seismic Records
in: University of Emergency Management, Hebei, China
Key Laboratory of Building Collapse Mechanism and Disaster Prevention, China Earthquake Administration, China
Hebei Technology Innovation Center for Multi-Hazard Resilience and Emergency Handling of Engineering Structures, Hebei, China.
China National Machinery Industry Co., Ltd., Beijing, China
Central South University, Changsha, China
Hebei University of Technology, Tianjin, China
tk: An automated baseline correction framework for strong-motion records is developed by reformulating the problem using robot trajectory planning and physical jerk constraints.
基于机器人轨迹规划与Jerk约束，提出强震记录自动基线校正框架。
papers.ab: Coseismic permanent ground displacement is essential for understanding earthquake rupture mechanisms and assessing seismic hazards. However, traditional geodetic methods are often limited by sparse spatiotemporal coverage and high costs. Strong-motion records offer a valuable supplement but are frequently contaminated by baseline offsets. Existing baseline correction methods largely rely on visual inspection and empirical image-based judgments, lacking a clear physical foundation and sufficient robustness. As a result, they are ill-suited for the automated processing of large-scale strong-motion datasets, and the valuable displacement information contained in these records remains underutilized. This study breaks away from conventional approaches by reformulating baseline correction as an inverse problem in robot trajectory planning and proposing a fully automated correction framework based on jerk constraints. The method achieves fully automated processing and effectively handles challenging scenarios such as velocity pulses, complex waveform distortions, and nonideal instrument states. Its strong cross-event adaptability is validated using records from the Chi-Chi, Wenchuan, and Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. By providing a physical interpretation of baseline offsets, this work eliminates the dependence on empirical, image-based adjustments and offers a novel, physically grounded approach for strong-motion signal processing.

papers.t: Feasibility of moment tensor inversion using Distributed Acoustic Sensing during volcanic unrest on the Reykjanes Peninsula, Iceland
tk: This study evaluates moment tensor inversion using simulated DAS data in Iceland, finding that subsurface heterogeneity significantly degrades inversion reliability compared to conventional seismic methods.
本文评估了冰岛火山活动期间利用DAS数据进行矩张量反演的可行性，发现地下介质非均匀性严重降低了反演可靠性。
papers.ab: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) is an emerging seismic measurement technique that enables meter-scale sampling of strain along fiber-optic cables. Its applications in seismology have expanded rapidly, including studies of moment tensor estimation in controlled environments such as reservoir monitoring within boreholes. However, its performance in less controlled settings, such as volcanic unrest, remains poorly investigated. Here, we assess the feasibility of moment tensor inversion using DAS measurements during volcanic unrest on the Reykjanes Peninsula, Iceland. The inversion is based on simulated DAS measurements derived from simulated velocity waveforms generated by the MTUQ software. Previously calculated reference moment tensors were used as the basis for the forward modeling and to estimate amplitude coupling factors along the fiber optic cable. Moment tensor inversion is then performed using a Simulated Annealing (SA) approach. The resulting moment tensors exhibit poor waveform fits and complex mechanisms that are inconsistent with the expected tectonic setting of the region. The results indicate that DAS-derived moment tensor inversions do not reliably recover the true moment tensor compared to conventional seismic methods within highly heterogeneous environments. These findings suggest that the heterogeneity of the subsurface and its affects on the DAS measurements should be investigated and accounted for, to increase the reliability of solely DAS-derived moment tensor inversions within volcanic environments.

papers.t: Training-Free Structural Damage Localization Using Spatial-Correlation Sensor Networks: Full-Scale Validation on a Seven-Story Reinforced-Concrete Building
in: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Princeton University, Princeton, NJ 08544, USA
tk: A training-free, data-driven sensor network approach localizes structural damage in a seven-story building using spatial correlation of earthquake-induced responses.
利用空间相关性传感器网络，实现免训练的建筑结构损伤定位。
papers.ab: Damage identification in instrumented structures is often framed through modal-parameter changes, finite element updating, or supervised classifiers. These approaches are powerful, but they require an explicit structural model, identified modes, labeled damage cases, or expert choices about reference sensors. This paper introduces a new data-driven and training-free approach with limited physical priors, defining a sensor network where each sensor is a node and the edges are defined from the spatial correlation of sensor responses. The idea is to use each sensor time history as the measured structural dynamics feature while damage is localized from the edges, whose correlations change relative to a baseline. The method is demonstrated on a full-scale seven-story reinforced-concrete shear-wall building tested at UC San Diego, considering four progressive earthquake-induced damage states and one brace-modification state. The results are compared with those obtained from a previously published finite element model. The results reveal that this network-based approach localizes the damage states in agreement with previous studies with limited prior requirements and low computational cost. Beyond damage localization, this network representation provides sensor centrality, allowing informative sensors to be selected from data rather than chosen randomly or only from experimental intuitions. For the case study, using this sensor network, we find the most central sensors, those carrying the most information with reduced trial-and-error and reduced expert intervention, and use them to recover the first three natural frequencies as a secondary dynamic check. The results show that spatial correlation networks can screen for damage, localize affected regions, and guide modal parameter extraction without building an FE model. This study opens a research avenue in which network representations of multi-sensor structural dynamics complement traditional modal analysis for structural health monitoring, with dense or heterogeneous sensing systems.

papers.t: Spatially variable carbon transport pathways in a volcanic and geothermal environment, Menengai Caldera, Kenya
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: University of Auckland
GNS Science
Dedan Kimathi University of Technology
Geothermal Development Company
tk: This study uses CO2 flux and isotopic data to reveal multi-scale volcanic and tectonic controls on carbon degassing pathways in the Menengai Caldera, Kenya.
本研究利用二氧化碳通量和同位素数据，揭示了肯尼亚梅嫩加伊火山口多尺度火山与构造对碳排气路径的控制。
papers.ab: AbstractMagmatic volatiles in geothermal settings ascend through permeable pathways developed from various tectonic and volcanic processes, resulting in structurally complex fracture networks controlling emissions of CO₂ and other magmatic volatiles. To better understand these controls, we examine spatial patterns and isotopic signatures of fumaroles and diffusely degassing CO₂ in the Menengai Geothermal Field, Kenya. Sequential Gaussian simulation analyses support a total CO₂ emission likely exceeding 389.7 t d⁻¹, with heavier δ13C-CO2 values suggesting primarily mantle‑derived carbon contributions. Degassing pattens mimic major rift structures, including NNW‑ to NNE‑trending faults and secondary E‑ to ENE‑trending structures. Fumarole lineaments, however, exhibit substantial scattering, with some observed lineament patterns falling outside the typical rift‑related structural fabric. We suggest that the broad distribution of CO₂ degassing (10s of km2 scale) is influenced by a large, ≥6.5 km‑deep igneous body, while deep volcanic and tectonic structures allow the upward migration of volatiles when hydraulically linked to this source. Lineaments observed in CO₂ flux patterns (1000s of m2 scale) support shallow CO₂ transport along blind rift‑parallel faults that terminate within post‑caldera lavas. From this depth, volatiles likely ascend through a permeability network derived from volcanic structures developed in post‑caldera lava flows, governing the local‑scale (100s of m² scale) patterns of CO₂ degassing. We conclude that a range of tectonic‑ and volcanic‑related factors, operating and interacting across multiple scales, control the spatial patterns of CO₂ degassing at Menengai, with possible implications for other geothermal systems within the East African Rift System (EARS), particularly the Kenyan Rift.

papers.t: A scalable Bayesian framework for modern sea-level inference
tk: A scalable, infinite-dimensional Bayesian framework combining adjoint sea-level theory and randomized low-rank decompositions enables computationally efficient, physics-consistent sea-level inversions with rigorous uncertainty quantification.
提出一种结合伴随海平面理论与随机低秩分解的无限维贝叶斯反演框架，实现高效且物理一致的海平面不确定性量化。
papers.ab: This paper presents a scalable Bayesian framework for the inference of modern-day sea-level change and surface mass redistribution. To motivate this approach, we first review and quantify the performance of some standard methods for the analysis of satellite gravity and ocean altimetry observations. We find that these methods substantially underestimate uncertainties and are subject to systematic biases, deficiencies that stem from their incomplete treatment of sea-level physics and from uncertainty estimates based solely on the propagation of observational noise. To address these limitations, our approach combines three advances. First, we use recent developments in adjoint sea-level theory to embed the full physics into the forward and inverse modelling. Second, we formulate the Bayesian inverse problem in an infinite-dimensional setting, thereby avoiding discretisation artefacts and the underestimation of uncertainties inherent in truncated model spaces. Finally, our computational methods render such inversions tractable at full observational resolution while supporting joint model spaces and multiple data types. By employing a matrix-free approach with iterative solvers and randomised low-rank decompositions -- implemented in the linked open-source libraries pygeoinf and pyslfp -- basic calculations are possible on a single laptop, with the most intensive tasks parallelising trivially across available cores. We demonstrate the methodology through a series of synthetic experiments, culminating in a joint inversion of satellite gravity and ocean altimetry data that decomposes regionally averaged sea-level change into steric and manometric components with quantified uncertainties, including the degeneracies that remain.

papers.t: Revealing magma storage and underplating beneath tenerife island from receiver function analysis
tk: This study uses receiver function analysis to construct the first 3D model of the crust and upper mantle beneath Tenerife, revealing magma storage and underplating zones.
本研究利用接收函数分析构建了特内里费岛地壳与上地幔的首个三维模型，揭示了岩浆储集与底侵区域。

papers.t: Basin-Scale Modeling of Multiple Storage Projects in the Broom Creek Formation, North Dakota, USA: Unified Model and Uncertainty Quantification
tk: A unified basin-scale reservoir model quantifies significant inter-project interference and uncertainty for multiple CO2 storage projects in the Broom Creek Formation.
统一的盆地尺度储层模型量化了布鲁姆溪地层多个二氧化碳封存项目之间显著的相互干扰和不确定性。
papers.ab: Quantifying the interactions between neighboring projects will be essential as carbon storage operations expand in scale. However, many existing basin-scale studies are deterministic or rely on hypothetical scenarios. In addition, simulations that do not fully account for neighboring projects may suffice for initial permitting. In this study, we develop a unified basin-scale model for the Broom Creek Formation in North Dakota. The model includes a total of five (existing and planned) projects, involving 18~injection wells with a maximum potential injection rate of 30~MTPA. The unified model, constructed by integrating publicly available geological and project data, contains $44\times10^6$ cells and requires over two days to run. To enable faster simulations, we present a multilevel treatment that combines four-level nested local grid refinement, constructed through the solution of a constraint-satisfaction problem, with optimized power averaging for permeability in coarse regions. After demonstrating the accuracy of the coarse model, we use it to assess uncertainty in key quantities of interest (QoIs), including total CO$_2$ injected and plume area after 50~years, across a wide range of geological realizations and model parameters. In addition, we develop a deep learning surrogate model, which is used in global sensitivity analyses to identify dominant contributors to QoI variance. Comparisons between the unified model and standalone project simulations are presented to quantify inter-project interference. This can be substantial in some cases, e.g., for one project, the median total CO$_2$ injected decreases from 271~MT (standalone) to 192~MT (unified model).

papers.t: Noise Effects on Ordinal Pattern Statistics via Majorization
tk: This paper characterizes noise distortions in ordinal pattern statistics using majorization, providing a method to analyze noisy geophysical time series like paleomagnetic records.
本文利用主化理论刻画了序模式统计中的噪声畸变，为分析古地磁等噪声地球物理时间序列提供了方法。
papers.ab: The Bandt-Pompe permutation entropy framework, alongside the complexity-entropy causality plane, has become a standard tool for characterizing the dynamical properties of time series. However, observational noise distorts ordinal pattern probability distributions in ways that can systematically misplace time series within the causality plane, compromising dynamical classification. This effect is particularly relevant for geophysical signals, which are typically poorly and irregularly sampled, and have a low signal-to-noise level. In this work, we characterize the distortions on ordinal pattern statistics using the formalism of majorization. We provide theoretical results and propose corrective strategies that restore discriminability under realistic measurement conditions. To achieve this, we introduce methodology that allows the characterization of noisy dynamical series and further allows the quantification of observational noise without the need of a fitting procedure. Finally, we illustrate our methodology by analyzing paleomagnetic records to determine if the geological evolution of the Earth dipole is better described by a stochastic or chaotic system.

papers.t: Earthquake magnitude estimation using an optimized CNN-DNN-GRU model with binary differential evolution and firefly algorithm
tk: A hybrid CNN-DNN-GRU model optimized with binary differential evolution and firefly algorithm achieves highly accurate earthquake magnitude estimation using a massive seismic catalog dataset.
提出一种结合二进制差分进化与荧光虫算法优化的CNN-DNN-GRU混合深度学习模型，实现了高精度的地震震级评估。

papers.t: Tracing the Unlabeled Storm: Cross-Variable Transfer in a Lagrangian Atmospheric JEPA Framework
tk: A self-supervised Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (M-JEPA) is pretrained on continuous atmospheric proxies to improve daily monsoon precipitation forecasting without direct rainfall supervision.
该研究提出一种自监督联合嵌入预测架构，通过大气代理变量预训练提升季风降水预测精度。
papers.ab: Deep atmospheric convection governs South Asian monsoon variability, yet attempting to learn its latent world model directly from zero-inflated, heavy-tailed precipitation yields suboptimal predictive representations. Continuous atmospheric proxies, such as outgoing longwave radiation (OLR), express this convective organization far more coherently. We address this mismatch with \emph{cross-variable proxy learning}: M-JEPA, a multiscale Monsoon Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, is pretrained on five continuous proxy fields over Lagrangian patches tracking moving convective systems---without rainfall supervision at any point. The resulting frozen representation is transferred to daily precipitation forecasts through a shared decoder trunk featuring parallel probabilistic and deterministic branches. Because rainfall is strictly unobserved during pretraining, downstream skill directly measures the predictive information captured in the latent rollout. A frozen-backbone probing framework with two controls (an identical architecture trained on rainfall alone, and a randomly initialized backbone) attributes the transfer specifically to proxy pretraining: direct rainfall training exhibits $36\%$ higher CRPS error ($7.52$ vs.\ $5.54$\,mm/day). Against the 51-member operational ECMWF ensemble, the transferred model attains a statistically resolved CRPS advantage ($6.81$ vs.\ $6.89$\,mm/day) and higher Brier skill ($+0.05$ vs.\ $-0.04$) using $15.4$M parameters on a single consumer GPU, concentrated at heavy-rain thresholds and fine spatial scales, while the ensemble retains an advantage in neighborhood skill and deterministic references on point metrics. The result provides a competitive monsoon precipitation forecast grounded in intraseasonal dynamics and a diagnostic framework for evaluating transferred atmospheric representations.

papers.t: The spatial anatomy of urban wildfire vulnerability: a spatially validated GeoAI framework reveals the roles of building density and vegetation moisture in structure loss during the 2025 Palisades Fire
tk: A spatially validated GeoAI framework reveals that building density and neighborhood-scale vegetation moisture were key drivers of structure loss during the 2025 Palisades Fire.
空间验证的地理人工智能框架揭示了建筑密度和植被水分是2025年帕利塞兹火灾中房屋损毁的关键因素。
papers.ab: Urban wildfire resilience depends on interactions among built form, vegetation condition, and extreme fire weather, yet city-scale risk models often overlook whether predictive skill transfers across neighborhoods. We developed a spatially validated GeoAI workflow for the January 2025 Palisades Fire, linking 12,081 CAL FIRE damage inspections to pre-fire Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, Landsat surface temperature, LANDFIRE fuels, terrain, and OpenStreetMap buildings and roads. Among 9,883 inspected residential structures, 5,566 were destroyed. Random cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC 0.92 for the integrated XGBoost model, but 1 km spatial block validation reduced performance to 0.75; logistic regression performed similarly and was better calibrated. Building count within 100 m was the strongest predictor, with destruction odds increasing 4.12-fold per standard deviation. Vegetation moisture and greenness showed opposing conditional associations: NDMI at 100-300 m was protective (OR 0.52), whereas NDVI at 30-100 m was positively associated with destruction after accounting for moisture (OR 1.74). Predictive information was concentrated at the 100-300 m neighborhood scale. A separate post-fire track mapped burn severity and vegetation recovery without leakage. The results support neighborhood-scale susceptibility screening, moisture-aware vegetation management, and spatial block validation as a minimum standard for single-event urban wildfire modeling.

papers.t: The First Network of Ocean Bottom Seismometers around Jøtul Hydrothermal Vent Field, Knipovich Ridge
in: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung
Centre for Arctic Gas Hydrate, Environment and Climate
UiT The Arctic University of Norway
tk: Presents the first ocean bottom seismometer network around the Jøtul hydrothermal vent field, detailing data processing, clock drift correction, and ambient noise characteristics.
介绍了克尼波维奇脊Jøtul热液喷口区的首个海底地震仪网络及数据处理与噪声特征。
papers.ab: Ultraslow spreading ridges are a vital part of mid-ocean ridge systems, consisting of both magmatic and amagmatic spreading segments. Hydrothermal vents play a key role in the transfer of matter and heat from the lithosphere to the hydrosphere and biosphere. However, research on the relationship between magmatism, faulting, and hydrothermal circulation beneath vent fields on ultraslow spreading ridges is still limited. Here, we investigate Jøtul vent field, situated on a magmatic segment of Knipovich Ridge. We provide continuous passive seismic data recorded by a network of up to 15 broadband ocean bottom seismometers covering up to 50 km along-axis and the time from July 2023 to August 2024. We present our correction for nonlinear clock drift using ambient noise cross-correlation and sensor orientation from Rayleigh wave polarization analysis. Probabilistic power spectral density plots show a clear double-frequency microseismic noise peak. Noise bands at periods of 0.2-0.4 s are likely related to sediment layers and ocean currents. Vibrations of the radio beacon antenna produce noise at periods of 0.16 s. Despite this ambient seismic noise, transient signals of teleseismic, regional, and local earthquakes, and air-gun signals are clearly visible in the dataset enabling studies of seismicity and seismic structure.

papers.t: Simple data fusion from several ocean and atmosphere hindcast models improves surface drifter trajectory prediction
tk: Fusing multiple ocean and atmosphere hindcast models using simple linear regression significantly improves ocean surface drifter trajectory predictions.
利用简单的线性回归融合多个海洋与大气后报模型，可显著提高海洋表面漂流器轨迹预测的准确性。
papers.ab: Simulating the trajectory of surface drifters in the ocean matters for search and rescue, pollution tracking, oil and chemical spill response, and marine risk analysis. Accurate prediction remains difficult, as widely acknowledged in the literature, and also illustrated by the ``Forecasting Floats in Turbulence'' challenge issued by the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) in 2021, and which ultimately led to this paper. The main source of error usually comes from uncertain ocean currents, while errors in wind forcing and object drift properties are often smaller [Dagestad and Röhrs, 2019]. Here, we use an open one-year dataset of Sofar Spotter trajectories together with several ocean and atmospheric hindcast products to test data-driven drift models at scale. We compare three approaches: i) a standard (baseline) drifter trajectory simulation based on one ocean model and one atmospheric model, ii) linear regression (LR) models that fuse all available predictors, and iii) neural networks (NN) using similar inputs. A simple LR model that combines all predictors performs equally well as the NN. Because LR is simpler, cheaper, and more robust, we retain it as the preferred approach. In 2-day trajectory prediction, this improves the Liu-Weisberg skill score by around 40\% relative to the baseline. These findings apply to hindcast mode; applying this methodology for forecast mode remains for future work.

papers.t: Bayesian Joint Velocity and Impedance Inversion via Diffusion Models Conditioned on Common Image Gathers
tk: A score-based diffusion model conditioned on complementary common image gathers enables joint Bayesian inversion of velocity and impedance without empirical shortcuts.
该研究利用基于扩散模型的贝叶斯框架，实现了速度与阻抗的联合解耦反演。
papers.ab: We present a multi-parameter simulation-based inference framework for joint Bayesian recovery of subsurface velocity and acoustic impedance from seismic data. A score-based diffusion model is conditioned on two complementary Common Image Gathers (CIGs): an inverse-scattering CIG encoding reflectivity amplitude and an anti-ISIC CIG encoding kinematic velocity errors. The model simultaneously samples the posterior distributions of both parameters. Training labels are deliberately decoupled to prevent the model from exploiting the Gardner relationship: velocity targets are lightly smoothed to match the long-wavelength content of the anti-ISIC CIG, while impedance targets retain the unsmoothed ground truth. On the Compass benchmark the model achieves velocity SSIM of 0.967 (RMSE 0.050 km/s) and impedance SSIM 0.867 (RMSE 0.279 km/s g/cm^3), with velocity quality confirmed by CIG focusing.

papers.t: Viscosity of NaAlSi3O8−H2O fluids and implications for arc magmatism
in: Planetary Science Institute
University of California, Los Angeles
Princeton University
tk: Machine learning-driven molecular dynamics simulations reveal lower viscosity of supercritical NaAlSi3O8-H2O fluids, suggesting rapid fluid ascent (8000 years) in subduction zones.
机器学习模拟表明超临界流体粘度较低，俯冲带流体上升仅需八千年。
papers.ab: Water plays a crucial role in the transport properties of silicate liquids and is especially important in subduction-zone magma source regions where conditions promote complete miscibility between water and silicate melts. However, accurately tracing the movement of fluids and volatile-rich magmas is prevented by poor knowledge of the variation of viscosity across silicate- H 2 O joins at relevant pressure-temperature conditions. We used molecular dynamics driven by a machine learning potential of ab initio quality to investigate supercritical NaAlSi 3 O 8 − H 2 O fluids from 0 - 100 % H 2 O at 1200–3000 K (at 2 GPa) and 1–5 GPa (at 2500 K). Our results provide atomic-level insight into how H 2 O disrupts the silicate melt network to change viscosity. We find smaller fluid viscosity at a given pressure, temperature, and H 2 O content than obtained in previous models. We fit our results to an empirical viscosity model that allows application to transport in geologic settings. For model subduction zones, we find that the mean percolation velocity of fluids ascending by Darcian flow varies strongly with H 2 O content and that, at constant H 2 O , the fluids accelerate as they rise from slab source into the mantle wedge, and decelerate on further ascent. For plausible water contents, we find that ascent times from the slab to the Moho may be as little as 8000 years, satisfying constraints from U-Th disequilibria.

papers.t: Lithospheric boundaries of the São Francisco paleocontinental block revealed by multiple frequency seismic tomography
in: Institute of Physics
Universidade Federal de Ouro Preto
Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte
Observatoire de la Côte d’Azur
Géoazur
tk: Multiple-frequency seismic tomography reveals the lithospheric boundaries and subcrustal structures of the São Francisco Paleocontinental block down to upper mantle depths.
多频地震断层成像揭示了圣弗朗西斯科古陆块的岩石圈边界与深部结构。
papers.ab: Summary The São Francisco Paleocontinental block (SFPB) and the Congo Paleocontinental block (CPB) composed, prior to the Atlantic opening in the Cretaceous, the São Francisco-Congo Paleocontinent (SFCP). The SFCP was one of the landmasses involved in the Neoproterozoic Brasiliano-Pan African Orogeny and the assembly of Western Gondwana. Both the SFPB and CPB underwent reworking during the amalgamation of Western Gondwana, forming the orogenic belts that surround the preserved portions of the SFPB and CPB that are known today as the São Francisco and Congo cratons. Although the crustal portions in the outermost areas of these paleocontinents are no longer visible in the surface due to this reworking, the limits of these paleocontinents remain relatively intact at subcrustal depths. The objectives of this study are to delimit the SFPB and to image the structures beneath the Araçuaí belt at mantle lithosphere depths. We present the results of our study which were obtained by the multiple-frequency seismic tomography method for the SFPB and adjacent structures between depths of 68 and 587 km. Data were obtained by processing broadband seismograms recorded between 11-August-2023 and 31-July-2024 for P and PKIKP phases. The processed database comprised 9 254 residuals, which were added to the database of a previous regional study resulting in 97 150 traveltime delays. Checkerboard resolution tests using patterns with horizontal dimensions of 390×390 km reveal very good recovery between depths of 68 and 226 km, although the sharp vertical transition between the checkerboard layers is not fully recovered between the depths of 316 and 384 km. The checkerboard pattern with horizontal dimensions of 312×312 km reveals that the best recovery is observed in the southern and eastern portions of the São Francisco craton (SFCr) and in the Borborema province (BP) between depths of 68 and 226 km. Our results show a high-velocity anomaly with roughly NE-SW trend that extends from the Paranapanema block (PaBl), through the entire extension of the SFCr up to the southern BP. This anomaly contains two major segmentations, one in the southern Brasilia belt, marking the division of the PaBl with the SFPB, and the other dividing the eastern and western arms of the SFPB with a roughly NW-SE trend, interpreted as the Paramirim aulacogen. We also observe a high-velocity anomaly beneath the Araçuaí belt (ArBe) that dips with a SE direction. This anomaly starts at the northern end of the Abre Campo suture at a depth of 136 km, deepens to the south, and is interpreted as the foundered cratonic lithosphere that originated from the delamination of the SFCr due to the passage of the Trindade plume. To reinforce our interpretation, we tested several synthetic models with geometries that were based on our results and previous studies in the area. The synthetic model which presents the most resemblance to the real data model contains a high-velocity anomaly beneath the Araçuaí belt between depths of 226 and 384 km. A strong low-velocity anomaly beneath the Ribeira Belt is interpreted as material rising from the Nazca Slab dehydration.

papers.t: Contrasting mechanisms of present-day vertical deformation along the northeastern Tibetan Plateau: Insights from 3-D viscoelastic modeling
in: National Institute of Disaster Management
China Earthquake Administration
Institute of Geology, China Earthquake Administration
tk: 3-D viscoelastic modeling reveals that present-day vertical deformation in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau is controlled by both pure shear crustal shortening and localized mid-lower crustal flow.
三维粘弹性建模表明，青藏高原东北缘的现今垂直变形受地壳缩短和局部中下地壳流共同控制。
papers.ab: Summary The northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau exhibits pronounced spatial variations in present-day vertical crustal deformation, yet the mechanisms controlling these differences remain debated. In particular, contrasting uplift patterns are observed between the Liupanshan tectonic belt and the Maxianshan Fault, two key tectonic structures along the northeastern expansion front of the plateau. Here we develop two three-dimensional viscoelastic finite element models constrained by geological structures, seismic profiles, and GNSS observations to investigate the controls on vertical deformation. The modeling results show that when the mid–lower crustal viscosity is laterally uniform between the Longxi Basin and the Ordos Block, vertical deformation of ~2 mm/a is concentrated within a ~50 km-wide zone near the Liupanshan tectonic belt, consistent with leveling observations. This deformation pattern mainly reflects crustal shortening and thickening dominated by pure shear. In contrast, the observed ~4 mm/a uplift along the hanging wall of the Maxianshan Fault can only be reproduced when weak mid–lower crust and enhanced crustal flow are introduced beneath the Linxia Basin, indicating that northeastward mid–lower crustal flow is converted into vertical uplift along the fault. These results suggest that the Maxianshan Fault represents the northeastern termination of mid–lower crustal flow within the Qilian Block, whereas deformation in the Liupanshan tectonic belt is primarily accommodated by crustal shortening. Our findings highlight the fundamental role of lateral rheological heterogeneity in controlling vertical deformation and provide new insights into the mechanisms of present-day lateral growth of the northeastern Tibetan Plateau.

papers.t: Reproducibility of geodetic source modelling and implications for the unrest at Campi Flegrei caldera (Italy)
papers.j: Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research
in: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia
Universidad de Buenos Aires
